For a face $F$ of a tame retract $O$ (paracompact, being closed), the chart $\pi : F \to \pi(F)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChartInv⟧ is compatible with the sub-charts of $F$ built on the chart $\mathrm{id}$ of $O$, its transition maps being the sc-operators $\iota$ and $\pi$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart⟧; a chart compatible with all sub-charts built on one chart of $X$ is a chart of the induced structure, by locality of compatibility ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible⟧. Its model is the tame retract $(\pi(F), C', E')$, so $F$ is tame (a space all of whose points lie in tame charts is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart⟧), and the tame chart realizes the index: $d_F(x) = d_{C'}(\pi x) = d_C(x) - 1 = d_O(x) - 1$ (equation (14) twice). The text calls this last statement obvious.

**Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44), first sentence** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.proposition_2_5_16⟧. In a tame chart $\varphi$ around $x$: $\varphi(x)$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of the M-polyfold $O$ (Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42) with Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41)), and each face of $O$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold with $d_F + 1 = d_O$, where $d_O(\varphi x) = d_X(x)$.

*The corner as a model space.* For $\sigma \subseteq \{1, \dots, n\}$ list the coordinates outside $\sigma$ as $j \mapsto l_j$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIdx⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIdx_injective⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · exists_cornerIdx⟧. Deleting the coordinates in $\sigma$ and inserting zeros there ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertL⟧ are mutually inverse on $\{a : a_l = 0,\ l \in \sigma\}$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveL_cornerInsertL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertL_cornerRemoveL⟧; as sc-operators on $\mathbb R^{n} \oplus W$ and $\mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerInsertModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerRemoveModel⟧, composed with $T$, they give $\iota_\sigma : \mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W \to E$ onto the corner $f_\sigma = \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} f_i$ and $\pi_\sigma : E \to \mathbb R^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj⟧, with $\pi_\sigma\iota_\sigma = 1$ and $\iota_\sigma\pi_\sigma = 1$ on $f_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj_cornerIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl_cornerProj⟧, $\iota_\sigma(C') \subseteq C$ and $\pi_\sigma(C) \subseteq C'$ for $C' = [0, \infty)^{n - \#\sigma} \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerIncl_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerProj_mem⟧, and $d_C(y) = d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma$ on $f_\sigma$: the vanishing coordinates of $y$ are those of $\sigma$ together with the images $l_j$ of the vanishing coordinates of $\pi_\sigma y$, disjointly ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · degIndexWith_eq_quadrantDeg_cornerProj_add_card⟧. The sc-projection $P_\sigma = \iota_\sigma \circ \pi_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill⟧ sets the coordinates in $\sigma$ to zero ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_coord_mem⟧, fixes $f_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_eq_self⟧ and maps $C$ into $C$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · cornerKill_mem⟧. For $\sigma = \{i\}$ these are the $\iota$, $\pi$ and $P_i$ of Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43).

*The retraction onto a corner* ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_retraction⟧. Let $r$ be tame for $T$, $o \in O$ and $\sigma \subseteq I(o)$. For each $i \in \sigma$, Lemma 4.C at $o$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · local_face_structure⟧ gives a face $F_i$ of the retract with $o \in F_i \subseteq f_i$, containing a point with $d_C = 1$, and a ball around $o$ in which $r$ maps the points of $C \cap f_i$ into $F_i$. Distinct $i$ give distinct faces: a point $p \in F_i$ with $d_C(p) = 1$ has $I(p) = \{i\}$, so $F_i = F_j$ forces $i = j$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet_eq_singleton⟧. Take a ball $B$ around $o$ inside all these balls with $B \cap C \subseteq U$, an open $W_s$ with $W_s \cap U = r^{-1}(B) \cap U$ (continuity of $r$), and put $V := B \cap P_\sigma^{-1}(B \cap W_s)$, an open set containing $o$ (since $P_\sigma o = o = r(o)$). On $V \cap C$ the map $s := r \circ P_\sigma$ is sc-smooth by the chain rule. For $z \in V \cap C$, $P_\sigma z \in C \cap f_\sigma \cap B$, so $r(P_\sigma z) \in F_i \subseteq f_i$ for every $i \in \sigma$: $s(z) \in O \cap f_\sigma$. Moreover $s(z) \in B$ (as $P_\sigma z \in W_s$), $P_\sigma s(z) = s(z)$, and $s(z) \in W_s$ (as $r(s(z)) = s(z) \in B$); so $s$ maps $V \cap C$ into itself. On $f_\sigma \cap O$, $P_\sigma$ and $r$ are the identity, so $s \circ s = s$: $s$ is an sc-smooth retraction with retract $O \cap V \cap f_\sigma$, and this set equals $O \cap V \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i$ (a point of $O \cap V \cap f_\sigma$ is fixed by $r$, which maps it into each $F_i$; conversely $F_i \subseteq f_i$). The exposition proceeds by induction on $\#\sigma$, identifying the germ of $F_1 \cap F_2$ with a face of $F_1$; the formal proof removes all coordinates of $\sigma$ at once.

*The tame model of a corner* ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_tameModel⟧. Let $s$ be an sc-smooth retraction on $U_s \subseteq U$, equal to $r \circ P_\sigma$ there, with retract $F \subseteq O \cap f_\sigma$; write $U_s = W_0 \cap C$ with $W_0$ open, and put $U' := \iota_\sigma^{-1}(W_0) \cap C'$ and $r' := \pi_\sigma \circ r \circ \iota_\sigma$ on $U'$. For $z \in U'$, $r(\iota_\sigma z) = s(\iota_\sigma z) \in F$ (as $P_\sigma\iota_\sigma = \iota_\sigma$), so $r'$ maps $U'$ into $\pi_\sigma(F) \subseteq U'$; it is sc-smooth by the chain rule and idempotent because $\iota_\sigma\pi_\sigma = 1$ on $F$ and $r = 1$ on $F \subseteq O$; its retract is $\pi_\sigma(F)$. *Tameness (1):* $d_{C'}(r'z) + \#\sigma = d_C(r(\iota_\sigma z)) = d_C(\iota_\sigma z) = d_{C'}(z) + \#\sigma$ (the index formula on $f_\sigma$ twice, and tameness (1) of $r$) ⟦Chapter1/Degeneracy · degIndex_eq⟧. *Tameness (2):* at a smooth $x$ of the retract, $\iota_\sigma x$ is a smooth point of $O$, and $Dr'(x)v = \pi_\sigma(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v)$ by the chain rule between sc-domains ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · scDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScOperator.scDeriv_eq⟧; for $j$ with $x_j = 0$ the coordinate $l_j$ vanishes at $\iota_\sigma x$ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · coord_cornerIncl_idx⟧, and Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) gives $\lambda_{l_j}(Dr(\iota_\sigma x)\,\iota_\sigma v) = \lambda_{l_j}(\iota_\sigma v) = v_j$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧; so $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$ lies in $E'_x$ and is an sc-complement of $T_x\pi_\sigma(F)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. And $d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma y) + \#\sigma = d_C(y)$ for $y \in F$. This is the proof of the tame model of Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43) with $\sigma$ in place of $\{i\}$.

**Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44), second sentence** ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · MPolyfold.proposition_2_5_16_corner⟧. Let $X$ be tame and $x \in X$, and take a chart $\varphi : V \to O$ of the structure around $x$ with a tame retraction $r$ onto $O$, tame for a presentation $T$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart⟧. The face germs at $x$ are the faces $F_i$, $i \in I(\varphi x)$, of the retract (Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41): there are $d_X(x)$ of them), and $\sigma$ is a set of such indices. The retraction onto the corner gives the pairwise distinct faces $F_i \ni \varphi(x)$, $i \in \sigma$, an open $B \ni \varphi(x)$ and $s$ with retract $O \cap B \cap \bigcap_{i \in \sigma} F_i$. Put $A := \{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in B,\ \varphi(y) \in F_i\ \forall i \in \sigma\}$; its germ at $x$ is the germ $F^\sigma_x$. Since $\varphi(A)$ is the retract of $s$, $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold by the local criterion of Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45) ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local⟧ (paracompact as every subset ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype⟧). The chart $\pi_\sigma \circ \varphi$ of $A$ onto the retract $\pi_\sigma(\varphi(A))$ of $r'$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart⟧ is compatible with the sub-charts of $A$ built on $\varphi$, its transitions being $\iota_\sigma$ and $\pi_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.faceChart_compatible_subChart⟧, hence a chart of the induced structure ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isChart_subPolyfold_of_compatible⟧; its model is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame⟧, so $A$ is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isTame_of_forall_exists_chart⟧. Both tame charts realize the index ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith⟧, so for $a \in A$: $d_A(a) + \#\sigma = d_{C'}(\pi_\sigma\varphi(a)) + \#\sigma = d_C(\varphi(a)) = d_X(a)$; in particular $d_A(x) = d_X(x) - \#\sigma$, and the codimension, the number of quadrant coordinates removed in the tame model, is $\#\sigma$. The text states the proposition without proof.

**Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45).** *The interior of a face.* $F \cap \{d_X = 1\} = G$ for $F = \overline G$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.theorem_2_5_17_interior⟧: at $y \in F$ with $d_X(y) = 1$, in a tame chart with $I(\varphi y) = \{i\}$, all points of $\{d_X = 1\}$ near $y$ lie in $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F)$ for the single component $\hat F$ of Lemma 4.C at $\varphi(y)$, a connected subset of $\{d_X = 1\}$ containing $y$; it meets $G$ (as $y \in \overline G$), hence lies in $G$. *A local criterion for sub-M-polyfolds* ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local⟧: if near each $a \in A$, in a chart $\varphi$, $\varphi(A \cap V)$ agrees on an open $B \ni \varphi(a)$ with the retract of an sc-smooth retraction $s$ contained in $O$, then $A$ is a sub-M-polyfold, with the retraction $\varphi^{-1} \circ s \circ \varphi$ on $V' = \varphi^{-1}(B \cap W_0 \cap s^{-1}(B))$ — shrunk so that $s$ maps it into itself, a step the exposition's "transport by $\varphi^{-1}$" omits. *$G$ is a sub-M-polyfold* ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_5_17_isSubMPolyfold_interior⟧: at $y \in G$, the local face $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$ agrees with $\varphi(G)$ on the ball of Lemma 4.C (both consist of the points of $S$ there), and Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43) gives its retraction. *The face-structured case.* Near $x \in F$, in a tame chart, $\varphi(F)$ agrees on a ball with a face of the retract ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.exists_localFace_of_isFaceStructured⟧: the map $i \mapsto F_i$ (the closure of the component of $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_i)$) from $I(\varphi x)$ to the faces through $x$ is onto (as in Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42)), and since there are exactly $d_X(x) = \#I(\varphi x)$ faces through $x$, it is injective; so the points of $G$ near $x$ lie in $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_j)$ for the one $j$ with $F = F_j$. Hence $F$ is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_5_17_isSubMPolyfold_face⟧, and with the charts $\pi \circ \varphi$ onto the restrictions of the tame retractions $r'$ it is tame with $d_X(x) = d_F(x) + 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.theorem_2_5_17_isTame_face⟧. The local and global face counts of the theorem are Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42) and the definition of face-structured.

### II.17 Products and fibred products: Lemma 4.D and Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46)

*Products of partial quadrants.* For presentations $T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W$ and $T' : E' \cong \mathbb R^{n'} \oplus W'$ of $C$ and $C'$, concatenating the coordinates ($\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^{n'} \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · finAppendL⟧) gives a presentation $E \oplus E' \cong \mathbb R^{n+n'} \oplus (W \oplus W')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · prodPresentation⟧ of $C \times C'$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · prod_eq_prodPresentation⟧, so $C \times C'$ is a partial quadrant ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsPartialQuadrant.prod⟧ and $U \times U'$ is relatively open in it ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod⟧. The vanishing coordinates of $(x, x')$ are those of $x$ followed by those of $x'$, so $d_{C \times C'}(x, x') = d_C(x) + d_{C'}(x')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · degIndexWith_prodPresentation⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · degIndex_prod⟧, and the minimal subspace is $E_x \oplus E'_{x'}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · minimalSubspaceWith_prodPresentation⟧.

*Products of retractions.* $f \times f'$ is sc-smooth when $f$ and $f'$ are ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSmooth.prodMap⟧, with derivative $Df(x) \times Df'(x')$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · scDeriv_prodMap⟧; so $r \times r'$ is an sc-smooth retraction ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.prod⟧ with retract $O \times O'$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.prod_retract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScRetract.prod⟧, and products of sc-smooth maps between retracts are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSmoothRetractMap.prodMap⟧. Products of sc-subspaces and of sc-splittings are again such ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSubspace.prod⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · IsScSplitting.prod⟧; hence if $r$, $r'$ are tame for $T$, $T'$, then $r \times r'$ is tame for the product presentation ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.prod⟧: (1) is the additivity of the index, and for (2) the complement of $T_{(x, x')}(O \times O') = T_xO \oplus T_{x'}O'$ is $A \oplus A'$ inside $E_x \oplus E'_{x'}$.

**Lemma 4.D (the product M-polyfold).** $X \times Y$ is paracompact, being metrizable by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_prod⟧. The product charts ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.prod⟧ have the product retracts as models ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · LocalModel.prod⟧, their overlaps are products ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.overlap_prod⟧, and products of compatible charts are compatible ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MChart.Compatible.prod⟧; so they form an atlas of an M-polyfold structure on $X \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.prod⟧, in which products of charts of the factors are charts ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsChart.prod⟧. In a product chart the index is additive ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex_prod⟧; choosing charts that realize $d_X(x)$ and $d_Y(y)$ gives $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) \le d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le⟧. If $X$ and $Y$ are tame, products of tame charts are tame charts, so $X \times Y$ is tame, and since a tame chart realizes the index (§II.14), $d_{X \times Y}(x, y) = d_X(x) + d_Y(y)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isTame_prod⟧. The text's "$d_{X \times Y} = d_X + d_Y$" is thus a statement about tame spaces. The projections are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_fst⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_snd⟧ and so is the pairing $z \mapsto (f(z), g(z))$ of sc-smooth maps ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.prodMk⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46).** A *local sc-diffeomorphism* $f : X \to Z$ is read as: every point has an open neighbourhood $U$ that $f$ maps sc-diffeomorphically onto an open subset ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo⟧; such an $f$ is continuous and sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.continuous⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isScSmoothMap⟧. The fibred product $X {}_f\times_g Y = \{(x, y) : f(x) = g(y)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredProduct⟧ is closed in $X \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isClosed_fibredProduct⟧, hence paracompact, which the text does not mention. *Sub-M-polyfold.* Near $(x, y)$, with $f|_U : U \to W$ an sc-diffeomorphism and $V = g^{-1}(W)$, the map $R(x', y') = ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')$ on $U \times V$ is sc-smooth, idempotent, with image the fibred product near $(x, y)$; in a product chart it is an sc-smooth retraction ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredSubDataL⟧, and so the fibred product is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct⟧ (symmetrically when $g$ is the local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.fibredSubDataR⟧ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_fibredProduct'⟧). *$\pi_2$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism.* On the fibred product near $(x, y)$, $\pi_2$ is sc-smooth with inverse $y' \mapsto ((f|_U)^{-1}(g(y')), y')$, a pairing of sc-smooth maps with values in the fibred product, hence sc-smooth into the sub-M-polyfold by Proposition 2.3.19 (2) (preprint 2.21) ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_snd_fibredProduct⟧; symmetrically for $\pi_1$ when $g$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_fst_fibredProduct⟧. The exposition factors this inverse through $y' \mapsto (x, y')$, which is not sc-smooth unless $x$ is a smooth point (a constant map is sc⁰ only when its value lies in $X_\infty$); the formula above has the same values and avoids it. *The index.* Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24) along $\pi_2$ gives $d_{X {}_f\times_g Y}(x, y) = d_Y(y)$ for arbitrary $Y$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_snd⟧, and along $\pi_1$, when $g$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, $= d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_fibredProduct_eq_fst⟧. *Tameness.* If $Y$ is tame, the charts $\psi \circ \pi_2$, $\psi$ a tame chart of $Y$ restricted to $g^{-1}(W)$, are charts of the fibred product with tame models ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isTame_fibredProduct⟧. Together: Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46) ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.proposition_2_5_20⟧, and in its last statement $d = d_X = d_Y$ for arbitrary $X$, $Y$ and, for tame $X$, $Y$, $2d = d_{X \times Y}$ by Lemma 4.D ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.proposition_2_5_20_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧.

### II.18 Strong bundle retractions (Definitions 2.6.1–2.6.3 (preprint 2.47–2.49))

*$U \triangleleft F$.* The double filtration is $U_m \times F_k$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · doubleLevel⟧. $C \times F_0$ is a partial quadrant in $E \oplus F$, through $(\mathbb R^n \oplus W) \oplus F \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus (W \oplus F)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · prodQuadrantIso⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsPartialQuadrant.prod_univ⟧, and $U \times F_0$ is relatively open in it ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.prod_univ⟧ — so "sc-smooth on $(U \triangleleft F)[i] = U \oplus F^i$" makes sense (exposition Lemma 1.B of Chapter 1). Pairings of $\mathrm{sc}^k$ maps are $\mathrm{sc}^k$, with the tangent map rearranged by an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · scPair⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · tangentProdSwap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsSck.scPair⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsScSmooth.scPair⟧, and the projections and inclusions of products are sc-operators ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodFstOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodSndOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodInlOp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · ScBanach.prodShiftInclOp⟧.

**Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47).** A strong bundle map maps $U \times F_0$ into $U' \times F'_0$, has first component independent of $h$ and second linear in $h$, maps $U_m \times F_k$ into $U'_m \times F'_k$ for $k \le m + 1$, is sc-smooth on $U \times F_0$, and its fibre-lifted map on $U \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · shiftFiber⟧ is sc-smooth for $E \oplus F^1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleMap⟧; a strong bundle retraction is an idempotent one ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleRetraction⟧. *Lemma 5.A.* The base $r(u) = R(u, 0)_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleMap.base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.apply_fst⟧ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U$: sc-smooth as $R$ composed with $u \mapsto (u, 0)$ and the first projection, idempotent by the first component of $R \circ R = R$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.baseRetraction⟧. For $u \in O$, $R(u, h) = (u, \Gamma(u, h))$, so the second component of $R \circ R = R$ reads $\Gamma(u, \Gamma(u, h)) = \Gamma(u, h)$: $\Gamma(u, \cdot)$ is a projection ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.fiber_idem⟧. $R$ is an sc-smooth retraction on $U \times F_0$ in $C \times F_0$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetraction⟧ and, through the lift of the fibre component to $F_1$ (possible since $R$ preserves the double filtration at $(0, 1)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.snd_mem_range⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toBase_shiftFiber_snd⟧), on $U \times F_1$ for $E \oplus F^1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetractionOne⟧.

**Definition 2.6.2 (preprint 2.48).** $K$ is a local strong bundle retract if $K = R(U \times F_0)$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsStrongBundleRetract⟧, with $K_{m,k}$, $K[i]_m$ and $K[1] \subseteq E_0 \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongLevel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongLevelShift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongShiftOne⟧ and the projection $p$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · strongProj⟧. $K = \{(u, h) : u \in O, \Gamma(u, h) = h\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.mem_image_iff⟧. *Lemma 5.B.* $K[1]$ is the image of $R$ on $U \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetraction.toScRetractionOne_retract⟧, so $K$ and $K[1]$ are retracts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScRetract_one⟧; the base $p(K)$ is $O$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.base_eq⟧; and $p : K[i] \to O$ is sc-smooth, because $p \circ R = r \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ is ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst_one⟧, as is the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_shiftIncl⟧.

**Definition 2.6.3 (preprint 2.49).** An sc-smooth section is sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ into $(K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)$ with $f(x)_1 = x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScSmoothSection⟧; an sc⁺-section is sc-smooth into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScPlusSection⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsScPlusSection.mem⟧. Composed with the inclusion $K[1] \to K[0]$ (Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8)), an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsScPlusSection.isScSmoothSection⟧.

### II.19 Strong bundles over M-polyfolds (Definitions 2.6.4–2.6.7 (preprint 2.50–2.53))

**Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50).** For $P : Y \to X$ with linear structures on the fibres, a strong bundle chart is a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ (of the structure — the text says only "a homeomorphism onto $O$"), a strong bundle retraction $R$ on $U \subseteq C$ with base retract $O$, and a homeomorphism $\Phi : P^{-1}(V) \to K$ with $\Phi(y)_1 = \varphi(P(y))$, linear on fibres ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.K⟧. $K$ is a local strong bundle retract and a retract on $[0]$ and $[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isStrongBundleRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.model⟧, the source $P^{-1}(V)$ is open ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.isOpen_source⟧, $\Phi(P^{-1}(V)) = K$ and $p(K) = O$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.image_source⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.base_K⟧. "Bounded on the fibres" needs no hypothesis: the restriction of the continuous $\Phi$ to a fibre is continuous ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.continuous_fiber⟧. Two charts are compatible if the transitions $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.overlap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.transition⟧ and back are sc-smooth between the overlaps on $[0]$ and, fibre-lifted, on $[1]$, and carry fibre components in $F_1$ to $F'_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.symm⟧; the last condition, implicit in the text, is what makes $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ the restriction of $\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1}$. Atlases and their equivalence ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleAtlas⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv⟧, an equivalence relation (§II.45) ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleAtlas.equivalence⟧; Banachable fibres ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsBanachable⟧.

**Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51).** A strong bundle is a continuous surjection with Banachable fibres and a strong bundle atlas, $Y$ Hausdorff paracompact ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle⟧. Each $\Phi$ is a chart of $Y$ with model $(K, C \times F_0, E \oplus F)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.toMChart⟧, compatibility of strong bundle charts on $[0]$ is compatibility of these charts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.toMChart⟧, and they form the atlas of the M-polyfold $Y[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.atlas0⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.toMPolyfold0⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.isChart_toMChart⟧. $P : Y[0] \to X$ is sc-smooth: in the charts $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ it is $p : K \to O$ (Lemma 5.B), and one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj⟧. The double filtration $Y_{m,k}$ is defined through all the charts of the atlas around a point ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.doubleLevel⟧.

*$Y_{m,k}$ does not depend on the chart* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff⟧. Let $y$ lie in the domain of a chart $\Phi$ of the atlas with $\Phi(y) \in E_m \times F_k$, $k \le m + 1$, and let $\Phi'$ be another chart around $y$; then $\Phi'(y) = (\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})(\Phi(y))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.transition_apply⟧. *The base component:* $\Phi'(y)_1 = \varphi'(\varphi^{-1}(\Phi(y)_1))$, and the base transition, sc-smooth and so $\mathrm{sc}^0$, maps points of level $m$ to points of level $m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.transition_apply⟧. *The fibre component, $k \le m$:* $\Phi(y)$ lies on level $k$ of $E \oplus F$ (levels decrease ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.range_toBase_mono⟧), and the $[0]$-transition, $\mathrm{sc}^0$ on the overlap retract ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap⟧, keeps it on level $k$. *The case $k = m + 1$:* the fibre component of $\Phi(y)$ lies in $F_1$, so its lift $\Phi(y)[1]$ to $E_0 \times F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.toBase_liftOne⟧ is a point of level $m$ of $E \oplus F^1$ (level $m$ of $F^1$ is $F_{m+1}$ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScBanach.shiftScale_toBase⟧); the $[1]$-transition, $\mathrm{sc}^0$ for $E \oplus F^1$ on the overlap ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap_one⟧, keeps it on level $m$, and its value is the lift $\Phi'(y)[1]$, because the $F_1$-condition of compatibility puts the fibre component of $\Phi'(y)$ in $F'_1$. So $\Phi'(y) \in E'_m \times F'_{m+1}$. The case $k \le m$ uses the $[0]$-transition only; the case $k = m + 1$ uses exactly the $F_1$-condition made explicit in Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50).

*The set $Y[1]$ and its topology.* $Y_{0,1}$ is the set of points whose fibre component lies in $F_1$ in every chart of the atlas around them ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneSet⟧; by the $F_1$-condition one chart suffices ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff⟧. $Y[1]$ is $Y_{0,1}$ as a type ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.One⟧ with the topology generated by the sets $\{y \in \operatorname{dom}\Phi : \Phi(y)[1] \in W\}$, $W$ open in $E_0 \times F_1$, as for $X_m$ in §2.3 (preprint §2.2) ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isOpen_one_basic⟧. The inclusion $Y[1] \to Y$ is continuous ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.continuous_oneVal⟧: inside the domain of a chart $\Phi$, an open subset of $Y$ is the preimage under $\Phi$ of an open $W \subseteq E_0 \times F_0$ ($\Phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $K$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.exists_isOpen_image_eq⟧), and its points in $Y[1]$ form the basic set of $(1 \times \iota)^{-1}(W)$. A continuous injection into the Hausdorff space $Y$ makes $Y[1]$ Hausdorff ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Separation/Hausdorff · T2Space.of_injective_continuous⟧.

*The charts $\Phi[1]$* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart⟧. $y \mapsto \Phi(y)[1]$ maps $P^{-1}(V) \cap Y[1]$ into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundleChart.liftOne_mem⟧, with inverse $z \mapsto \Phi^{-1}(z_1, \iota z_2)$, a point of $Y_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.symm_mem_oneSet⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChartInv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.liftOne_symm⟧. It is continuous by the definition of the topology. Its inverse is continuous: a basic open set $\{\Phi'(y)[1] \in W\}$ pulls back to the set of $z \in K[1]$ in the $[1]$-part of the overlap with $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1](z) \in W$; the overlap is $K \cap W_0$ for an open $W_0$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.overlap_eq_inter⟧ and the $[1]$-transition is continuous on it, so this set is open in $K[1]$. The overlap of $\Phi[1]$ and $\Phi'[1]$ is the $[1]$-part of the overlap of $\Phi$ and $\Phi'$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_overlap⟧, and their transition map is the $[1]$-transition $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_transition⟧, sc-smooth in both directions by Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50); so the charts $\Phi[1]$ are compatible ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.oneChart_compatible⟧ and form an atlas of $Y[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.atlas1⟧. $Y[1]$ is metrizable: $P$ restricted to $Y[1]$ is continuous into the paracompact Hausdorff $X$, and over the domain $V$ of a chart of $X$ its preimage is the source of a chart $\Phi[1]$, homeomorphic to a retract and so metrizable ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MChart.metrizableSpace_source⟧; the pull-back form of Smirnov's theorem applies ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.metrizableSpace_one⟧. Hence $Y[1]$ is paracompact ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.paracompactSpace_one⟧, which an M-polyfold must be and the text does not mention, and **$Y[1]$ is an M-polyfold** ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.toMPolyfold1⟧ whose charts include the $\Phi[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isChart_oneChart⟧.

*$P[1]$ and the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$.* In the charts $\Phi[1]$ and $\varphi$, $P[1]$ is the projection $K[1] \to O$ of Lemma 5.B ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_fst_one⟧, and one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts⟧; so **$P[1] : Y[1] \to X$ is sc-smooth** ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_proj1⟧. In the charts $\Phi[1]$ and $\Phi$ the inclusion $Y[1] \to Y[0]$ is $(u, h) \mapsto (u, \iota h)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsStrongBundleRetract.isScSmoothRetractMap_shiftIncl⟧, so it is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScSmoothMap_oneVal⟧ (not stated in the text; it gives that an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section).

**Definition 2.6.6 (preprint 2.52).** A section has $P \circ f = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · IsSection⟧; it is sc-smooth if sc-smooth into $Y[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection⟧, and an sc⁺-section if in every chart its fibre values lie in $F_1$ and its fibre-lifted representative ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.localRepOne⟧ is sc-smooth into $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection⟧. *This is the text's definition* ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_iff⟧: $f$ is an sc⁺-section iff it is a section and $f = \iota \circ g$ for an sc-smooth $g : X \to Y[1]$, $\iota$ the inclusion. Forward: the values of $f$ lie in $Y_{0,1}$ (one chart suffices), which defines $g$; on the domain of a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ under a strong bundle chart $\Phi$, $g = \Phi[1]^{-1} \circ (\text{the local representative}) \circ \varphi$, which gives the continuity of $g$, and the representative of $g$ in the charts $\varphi$, $\Phi[1]$ is the chart-wise representative, sc-smooth by hypothesis. Backward: the fibre values lie in $F_1$ because $g$ takes values in $Y_{0,1}$, and the chart-wise representative is the representative of $g$ in $\varphi$, $\Phi[1]$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) (a chart with empty domain is handled separately).

**Definition 2.6.7 (preprint 2.53).** $f^*Y = \{(z, y) : P(y) = f(z)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackSpace⟧ with the projections ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackProj'⟧, $P \circ P' = f \circ P_f$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_comm⟧; $P_f$ is continuous and $f^*Y$ closed in $Z \times Y$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · continuous_pullbackProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isClosed_pullbackSpace⟧.

### II.20 Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54): the pull-back strong bundle

*The pulled-back retraction.* For a retraction $r'$ on $U'$ and $g : O' \to O$ sc-smooth between retracts, $R_g(w, h) := (r'(w), \Gamma(g(r'(w)), h))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullbackRetraction⟧, where $g(r'(w)) \in O \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_mem_O⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_mem_U⟧. It is a strong bundle retraction ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isStrongBundleRetraction_pullback⟧: it maps $U' \times F_0$ into itself; its first component does not depend on $h$ and its second is linear in $h$; it preserves the double filtration ($r'$ and $g \circ r'$ preserve levels, and $R$ preserves the double filtration); on $[0]$ it is the pairing of $r' \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ with the second component of $R \circ ((g \circ r') \circ \mathrm{pr}_1, \mathrm{pr}_2)$, sc-smooth by the chain rule and the pairing lemma, and likewise on $[1]$; and $R_g \circ R_g = R_g$ because $r' \circ r' = r'$ and $\Gamma(o, \cdot)$ is a projection for $o = g(r'(w)) \in O$ (Lemma 5.A). Its image is $K_g = \{(w, h) : w \in O', (g(w), h) \in K\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · pullback_image⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · isStrongBundleRetract_pullback⟧.

*The fibres.* $P_f^{-1}(z) \to P^{-1}(f(z))$, $(z, y) \mapsto y$, is a bijection ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiberEquiv⟧; transporting the linear structure along it ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiber_addCommGroup⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiber_module⟧ makes it a linear homeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackFiberCLE⟧, so the fibres of $f^*Y$ are Banachable.

*The charts.* The data: a strong bundle chart $c$ of $Y$, a chart $\psi$ of $Z$ with $f(\operatorname{dom}\psi) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$, a retraction $r_Z$ onto the model of $\psi$, and the sc-smoothness of $g = \varphi \circ f \circ \psi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g_smooth⟧. The chart $\Phi_f(z, y) = (\psi(z), \mathrm{pr}_F\Phi(y))$ maps $P_f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)$ into $K_g$ — because $\Phi(y) = (g(\psi(z)), \cdot) \in K$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.g_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.mem_Kg⟧ — with inverse $(w, h) \mapsto (\psi^{-1}(w), \Phi^{-1}(g(w), h))$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.symm_mem_pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.invFun⟧; both are continuous, it covers $\psi$ and is linear on fibres, so it is a strong bundle chart of $f^*Y$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.toChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.image_eq_Kg⟧.

*Compatibility.* Sc-operators and pairings are sc-smooth between retracts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · ScOperator.isScSmoothRetractMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · IsScSmoothRetractMap.scPair⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · isScRetract_univ⟧, and overlaps of strong bundle charts are retracts on $[0]$ and $[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · StrongBundleChart.isScRetract_overlap_one⟧. On the overlap of two pulled-back charts the transition map is
$$(w, h) \mapsto \big(\psi_2\psi_1^{-1}(w),\ \mathrm{pr}_F(\Phi_2\Phi_1^{-1})(g_1(w), h)\big)$$
⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transitionFormula⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transition_eqOn⟧: its first component is the transition of $Z$ composed with the projection, its second the fibre component of the transition of $Y$ composed with $(w, h) \mapsto (g_1(w), h)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.gPair⟧, which maps the overlap into the overlap of $Y$'s charts ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.gPair_mem⟧. Each factor is sc-smooth between retracts, and Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) and the pairing lemma give the sc-smoothness on $[0]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transition_isScSmooth⟧; the same with $F^1$ on $[1]$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transitionOne_eqOn⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transitionOne_isScSmooth⟧; fibre components in $F_1$ go to $F_1$ because the transitions of $Y$ have this property ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.transition_snd_mem_range⟧. So any two pulled-back charts are compatible ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · PullbackChartData.compatible_toChart⟧.

**Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54).** $f^*Y$ is paracompact: $Z$ and $Y[0]$ are metrizable (Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16)), so $Z \times Y$ and its subspace $f^*Y$ are metrizable, hence paracompact ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · paracompactSpace_pullbackSpace⟧ — a requirement of Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) that the text does not mention. The pulled-back charts, built around every point from a chart of $Y$'s atlas and a chart of $Z$ restricted to $f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi)$, cover $f^*Y$ and form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · pullbackAtlas⟧. With the continuous surjection $P_f$ and its Banachable fibres this is a strong bundle structure on $f^*Y \to Z$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · proposition_2_6_8⟧ ("the easy proof is left to the reader").

### II.21 What the formalization taught us

- **Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) needs no added hypothesis, and not the text's route.** The text's proof applies Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) to $X_m$ without checking that $X_m$ is regular. A partition of unity of $X$, pulled back along the continuous inclusion, metrizes $X_m$ directly ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧, and the same lemma proves Smirnov's theorem ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_locally⟧, Proposition 2.3.15 (3) (preprint 2.19) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_3_15_three⟧ and the paracompactness of $f^*Y$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundlePullback · paracompactSpace_pullbackSpace⟧. With it every paracompactness hypothesis carried by the constructions is discharged ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype⟧.
- **Compatibility is local, and the text needs it.** That the charts compatible with an atlas are compatible with each other is not in the text; it is the chain rule plus the locality of sc-smoothness ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.compatible_of_locally⟧, and every chart-independence claim of §2.3 (preprint §2.2) rests on it.
- **$TO$ is a fixed-point set.** Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4) and Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6) are one-line consequences of $p \in Tr(TU) \iff Tr(p) = p$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff⟧, which the text's proofs use without stating.
- **The tangent bundle needs the locality of $Tf$.** That Definition 2.3.12's (preprint 2.17) relation is an equivalence relation needs the chain rule on the triple overlap and the agreement of $Tf$ computed on an open subset with $Tf$ computed on the whole retract ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangentMap_inter_isOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_transport⟧.
- **Level $1$ suffices for §2.4 (preprint §2.3).** Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30), Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31) and Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32) hold at points on level $1$ and for sc¹ germs ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · proposition_2_4_10_reduced⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · theorem_2_4_12⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · corollary_2_4_13⟧; the text's "closure of $(T^R_xO)_\infty$" is the density of level-$1$ points in the kernel of a finite-rank map ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · ScBanach.subset_closure_ker_inter_range_toBase⟧.
- **Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) needs only tameness (2), and Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40) needs (2) through it.** $Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$ holds for every retraction ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧; that the retraction keeps points of a face in that face is the ray lemma ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ray_zeroSet⟧, which uses Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35).
- **Three slips in the exposition.** "$|P_1 z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0$" in the exposition's proof of Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43) is false for a general norm on $E_0$; the formal neighbourhood intersects balls with their $P_i$-preimages ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_15⟧. The "transport by $\varphi^{-1}$" in Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45) needs a shrinking so that the retraction maps its domain into itself ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_local⟧. In Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46) the inverse of $\pi_2$ cannot be factored through the constant-in-$x$ map $y' \mapsto (x, y')$, which is not sc-smooth at a non-smooth $x$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_snd_fibredProduct⟧.
- **Tameness is needed only for the additivity of the index under products.** $d_{X \times Y} \le d_X + d_Y$ in general ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le⟧, with equality for tame factors ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.isTame_prod⟧; the identities $d = d_X = d_Y$ of Proposition 2.5.20 (preprint 2.46) hold without tameness ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.proposition_2_5_20_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧.
- **Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) needs two explicit conditions.** The base homeomorphism of a strong bundle chart must be a chart of $X$, and the $[1]$-transition must preserve fibre components in $F_1$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundle · StrongBundleChart.Compatible⟧. The second condition is exactly what makes $Y_{0,1}$, and so the M-polyfold $Y[1]$, independent of the chart ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_oneSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleOne · StrongBundle.mem_doubleLevel_iff⟧.
- **Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36) does not need the equality case of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31).** For a tame retraction the smooth vectors of the splitting are $Dr(x)T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)$, dual to the coordinates by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35), and $T^R_xO$ is an sc-subspace because $Dr(x)$ preserves $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · proposition_2_5_6_partialCone⟧.
- **Corners at once, not by induction.** The intersections $F^\sigma_x$ of Proposition 2.5.16 (preprint 2.44) are retracts of $r \circ P_\sigma$, by Lemma 4.C for each $i \in \sigma$; no identification of the germ of $F_1 \cap F_2$ with a face of $F_1$ is needed ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_retraction⟧.
- **$C_xO$ is always a partial quadrant.** The second sentence of Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28) does not hold as we read it. At every smooth point of every sc-smooth retract, $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · remark_2_4_8_isPartialQuadrant⟧. The reason is finite-dimensional: $Dr(x)$ induces a nonnegative idempotent matrix on $E/E_x$, and the cone of such a matrix is simplicial (Flor) ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · flor_nonnegRange_simplicial⟧. What tameness adds is only that the quadrant has the full dimension $d_C(x)$. The second statement of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31) needs no hypothesis.
- **The linear structure of $T_xX$ is chart independent because the fibre transitions are restrictions of derivatives.** Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18) adds in one chart and does not check independence. It holds because $T\psi \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$ is the restriction of $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(\varphi(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.exists_transition_clm⟧. At a smooth point this restriction is an sc-isomorphism of the models, which makes the sc-structure of $T_xX$ chart independent too ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.tangentFiberScIso⟧.
- **The openness of $\mathrm{pr}_1 : TO \to O_1$ has a one-line proof.** Appendix 2.7.3 states it without proof. The section $o' \mapsto Tr(o', h)$ through a given tangent vector is continuous because $Tr$ is $\mathrm{sc}^0$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · ScRetraction.exists_isOpen_tangent_section⟧.
- **Michael's lemma needs a shrinking.** The closures of a locally finite open refinement lie in members of the cover only after the cover is shrunk by regularity ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.exists_closed_refinement⟧. The converse direction needs no separation at all ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.paracompactSpace_of_closed_refinement⟧.
- **Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2) is a conjugation.** $\varphi(y) = P(r(y) - x) + (1 - P)(y - r(y))$ has derivative $1$ at $x$ and satisfies $\varphi \circ r = P \circ \varphi$, so the inverse function theorem replaces the remainder estimates of Appendix 2.7.1 ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.retractChart_comp⟧.
- **"An equivalence class of atlases" needs transitivity, which rests on the locality of compatibility.** The text does not check this, for M-polyfolds or for strong bundles ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · MAtlas.Equiv.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv.trans⟧.

### II.22 The 2021 edition: Proposition 2.1.13 and local completeness (§2.1)

The Springer edition (2021) adds to §2.1 a theory of *local completeness*: Proposition 2.1.4, Definition 2.1.5, Remark 2.1.6, Corollary 2.1.7, Proposition 2.1.8, Lemma 2.1.9 and Proposition 2.1.10, pp. 22–25. It also changes one statement, Proposition 2.1.13.

**Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), the 2021 statement.** For sc-smooth retractions $r$, $s$ onto the same retract $O$, a retraction $\rho$ onto $O'$, and $f$ with $f(O) \subseteq O'$, three things hold ⟦Chapter2/Book2021 · proposition_2_1_13⟧:
- (1) $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth iff $f \circ s$ is;
- (2) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r) = T(f \circ s)$ on $TO$;
- (3) if $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth, $T(f \circ r)$ maps $TO$ into $TO'$.

The 2021 statement of (3) carries the hypothesis "$f \circ r$ sc-smooth", without which $T(f \circ r)$ is not defined. The formal statement of §II.3 had read (3) this way from the start ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_three⟧, so the 2021 theorem is the conjunction of the three earlier ones. The first is used in both directions ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_two⟧.

**Complete metrics on a subspace.** "$W$ admits a metric $d$ defining its topology for which $K$ is complete" is a metric structure on $W$ whose topology is the given one, with $K$ complete for it ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · AdmitsCompleteMetricOn⟧. A metric space admits its own metric ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · admitsCompleteMetricOn_of_isComplete⟧, and such a $W$ is metrizable ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.metrizableSpace⟧. The property passes to smaller sets ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.mono⟧ and along embeddings: an embedding $j : T' \to T$ pulls the metric back, and a closed subset of a complete set is complete ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isComplete_inter_of_isClosed⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · AdmitsCompleteMetricOn.of_isEmbedding⟧.

**Definition 2.1.5.** $X$ is *locally complete* if every $x$ has open $V \ni x$ and $W$ with $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ such that $W$ admits a metric defining its topology for which $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ is complete ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete⟧. The text's $V(x) \subseteq W(x)$ follows from $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$. The text also assumes $X$ Hausdorff; the formal definition does not, because it follows.
- *$W$ arbitrarily small* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.exists_subset⟧. Given a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$, take a metric ball $V'$ around $x$ in $W$ whose closure in $W$ lies in $W \cap N$. Replace $W$ by the open $W \cap \operatorname{int} N$ and $V$ by $V \cap V'$; the metric restricts.
- *Regular* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.regularSpace⟧. A neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ contains the closed neighbourhood $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ for a $W \subseteq N$; this is where the global condition $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ enters.
- *$T_1$* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.t1Space⟧. Points are closed in the metrizable $W$. For $y \ne x$, a neighbourhood of $x$ missing $y$ comes from $W$ when $y \in W$; otherwise $W$ itself serves.
- *Hausdorff* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.t2Space⟧: regular and $T_1$.

Witnesses: a complete metric space ($W = V = X$) ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isLocallyComplete_of_completeSpace⟧, $\mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isLocallyComplete_real⟧, and a metric space whose points have open $V \subseteq W$ with $\mathrm{cl}(V) \subseteq W$ and $\mathrm{cl}(V)$ complete for the given metric ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isLocallyComplete_of_metric⟧.

**Remark 2.1.6.** If $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$, the closure of $V$ in the subspace $W$ is $\mathrm{cl}_X(V)$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · remark_2_1_6⟧. The modified notion asks only $V \subseteq W$, with completeness of $\mathrm{cl}_W(V)$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyCompleteRel⟧. Local completeness implies it, by the identity just proved ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.isLocallyCompleteRel⟧. The remark's "weaker" is formalized as this implication; that the modified notion is *strictly* weaker is §II.31 (gap G.76, closed).

**Proposition 2.1.4.** Let $O = r(U)$ be a retract with the metric of $E_0$. *Closed pieces of $O$:* for $\varepsilon$ small, $O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ is closed in $E_0$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScRetraction.exists_isClosed_retract_inter_closedBall⟧. Choose $\delta$ with $\bar B_\delta(x) \cap C \subseteq U$ ($U$ is relatively open in the closed $C$). A limit $v$ of points $v_k \in O \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x)$ lies in $C \cap \bar B_\varepsilon(x) \subseteq U$, and $v_k = r(v_k) \to r(v)$ by continuity of $r$ on $U$, so $v = r(v) \in O$. *The neighbourhoods* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsScRetract.exists_isComplete_closure⟧: $V$ the open $\varepsilon/2$-ball and $W$ the open $\varepsilon$-ball in $O$, inside any given neighbourhood. The closure of $V$ in $O$ lies in $O \cap \bar B_{\varepsilon/2}(x)$, closed in the Banach space $E_0$ and therefore complete. This proves the proposition ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_4⟧. The text's set $V'$ with $r(V') \subseteq V'$ is not needed, because the closed balls already give closed pieces of $O$.

**Corollary 2.1.7.** By Proposition 2.1.4, with the metric $d_O$ restricted to $W$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isLocallyComplete_of_metric⟧, a retract is locally complete ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · corollary_2_1_7⟧. So is $E_0$, the retract of the identity ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isLocallyComplete_univ_retract⟧.

**Proposition 2.1.8.** *Embeddings with locally closed image* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.of_isEmbedding⟧. Let $j : Y \to X$ be an embedding with $j(Y) = U \cap Z$, $U$ open and $Z$ closed. For $y \in Y$, take $W$, $V$ around $j(y)$ with $W \subseteq U$. The preimages $j^{-1}(W)$ and $j^{-1}(V)$ serve for $y$, for two reasons. First, the closure of $j^{-1}(V)$ corresponds to $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \cap j(Y)$, and $j(Y) \cap W = Z \cap W$ is closed in $W$. Second, the embedding $j^{-1}(W) \to W$ has closed image, so the metric of $W$ pulls back with the completeness of the closure. Parts (1)–(3) follow:
- (1) a locally closed subspace ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_8_1⟧;
- (2) a homeomorphic space, the image being everything ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_8_2⟧;
- (3) an open subspace ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_8_3⟧.

*The open-cover statement* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_8_4⟧. Let $y \in Y_i$, with $U \ni y$ open, $U \subseteq Y_i$ and $\mathrm{cl}_Y(U) \subseteq Y_i$ (condition (b)), and $W'$, $V'$ for $y$ in the locally complete $Y_i$. Put $V = V' \cap U$ and $W = W'$, both open in $Y$ because $Y_i$ is. Then $\mathrm{cl}_Y(V) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_Y(U) \subseteq Y_i$ by (b), so $\mathrm{cl}_Y(V)$ is the closure of $V$ in $Y_i$ and lies in $W$. The metric of $W' \subseteq Y_i$ is transported to $W \subseteq Y$, the identity being a homeomorphism. No Hausdorff hypothesis is used anywhere.

**Lemma 2.1.9 and Proposition 2.1.10.** *First countable* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_1_9⟧: the neighbourhood filter of $x$ in $X$ is the image of that of $x$ in the open, metrizable $W$, and the latter is countably generated. *Completely regular* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.completelyRegularSpace⟧. For $x$ outside a closed $A$, take $W \subseteq X \setminus A$ (arbitrarily small $W$). In the metrizable $W$, a continuous $g : W \to [0, 1]$ has $g(x) = 0$ and $g = 1$ off $V$. Extended by $1$ on $X \setminus \mathrm{cl}_X(V)$, it is continuous on the two open sets $W$ and $X \setminus \mathrm{cl}_X(V)$, which cover $X$ because $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$. Mathlib's complete regularity uses this normalization ($f(x) = 0$, $f = 1$ on $A$); the text's $\beta$ is $1 - f$. With Hausdorff, the space is $T_{3\frac12}$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_1_10⟧. The text argues continuity with sequences; the formal proof works with filters and open covers, so first countability is not needed for it.

### II.23 The 2021 edition: local path-connectedness and local contractibility (§2.2)

§2.2 of the 2021 edition, pp. 30–33, is new.

**Lemma 2.2.1.** Let $U$ be relatively open in a partial quadrant $C$ and connected. For $k \in \mathbb N$, $U_k = U \cap E_k$ carries the topology of $E_k$ ⟦Chapter1/ScSmooth · ScBanach.lvlSet⟧. For $k = \infty$ the text does not say which topology $U_\infty$ carries. The formalization takes the topology of all the norms: $U_\infty$ is the set of compatible sequences $(v_m) \in \prod_m E_m$ with $v_0 \in U$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.lvlSetInfty⟧, with the product topology. A smooth point $x$ gives its sequence of lifts ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.smoothSeq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.toBase_smoothSeq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.smoothSeq_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.smoothSeq_zero⟧. The image of $U_\infty$ in $E_0$ is $U \cap E_\infty$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.image_lvlSetInfty⟧.

The proof uses three facts:
- two points of $U_\infty$ whose base points span a segment inside $U$ are joined in $U_\infty$ by the segment, which is continuous into every level ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · ScBanach.joinedIn_lvlSetInfty_of_segment⟧;
- smooth points are dense in every level $C_m$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsPartialQuadrant.exists_smooth_near⟧, the text's "$U_\infty$ is dense in every $U_k$";
- every $z \in U$ has a ball with $B_\varepsilon(z) \cap C \subseteq U$, a convex set ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.exists_ball_inter_subset⟧.

*The case $k = \infty$* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_2_1_infty⟧. Fix a point $a$ of $U_\infty$, and say that $z \in U$ is good if near $z$ every point of $U_\infty$ is joined to $a$. Joining propagates inside a convex $B_\varepsilon(z) \cap C \subseteq U$ by segments, and smooth points are dense, so the set of good points is open and closed in $U$. It is nonempty, so it is all of $U$ because $U$ is connected. *The case $k \in \mathbb N$* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_2_1⟧: project the path-connected $U_\infty$ to $U_k$ and join points of $U_k$ to nearby smooth points by segments. The text's proof replaces a path in $U_0$ by a polygon through smooth points, using compactness of the path; the clopen argument avoids both the path and the polygon.

**Lemma 2.2.2.** For $x \in O$ and $V = V' \cap U$ with $V' \ni x$ open in $E_0$, the set $W = V \cap r^{-1}(V)$ has these properties ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_2_2⟧:
- it is relatively open in $C$, by continuity of $r$ on $U$;
- it contains $x$, since $r(x) = x$;
- $W \cap O = V \cap O$, because points of $O$ are fixed;
- $r(W) \subseteq W$, since $r(r(y)) = r(y) \in V$;
- $r(W) = O \cap V$.

**Definition 2.2.3 and Theorem 2.2.4.** Mathlib's local path-connectedness is the text's: every open neighbourhood contains a path-connected open neighbourhood ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · definition_2_2_3⟧. A retract is locally path-connected ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · theorem_2_2_4⟧. This was proved earlier for Chapter 7 (2017, p. 183, recalls it without proof) ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace⟧: points $o, p$ of $O$ near each other are joined in $O$ by $\tau \mapsto r(o + \tau(p - o))$, the segment lying in a convex piece of $U$. The text goes through Lemma 2.2.2 and the component of $W(x)$ containing $x$.

**Definition 2.2.5 and Proposition 2.2.6.** *Almost locally contractible* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsAlmostLocallyContractible⟧: for $z$ and open $V \ni z$, an open $W$ with $z \in W \subseteq V$ and a continuous $\Phi : [0, 1] \times W \to Z$ with values in $V$, $\Phi(0, \cdot) = \mathrm{id}$, $\Phi(t, z) = z$ and $\Phi(1, \cdot) \equiv z$. For a retract ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_2_6⟧, choose $\varepsilon$ with $B_\varepsilon(z) \cap C \subseteq U$ and $r(B_\varepsilon(z) \cap C) \subseteq V$, by continuity of $r$ at $z = r(z)$. Then $\Phi(t, y) = r((1 - t)y + tz)$ on $W = B_\varepsilon(z) \cap O$ is the text's homotopy: the segment stays in the convex $B_\varepsilon(z) \cap C$, and $r$ fixes $y$ and $z$. The model $E_0$ itself is a witness ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isAlmostLocallyContractible_univ⟧.

### II.24 The 2021 edition: paracompactness and M-polyfolds (§2.3, Appendix 2.7.2)

**The footnote to Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13).** The 2021 footnote says that paracompactness does not include the Hausdorff property; it asks only that every open cover have a locally finite open refinement. In the formalization, this paracompactness* is defined with covers as sets of open sets ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyFiniteSetFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsParacompactStar⟧ and coincides with Mathlib's paracompactness, which does not include the Hausdorff property either ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isParacompactStar_iff⟧. So "Hausdorff paracompact*" is exactly the hypothesis of the M-polyfold structure (§II.5) ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · definition_2_3_4⟧, and $\mathbb R$ is paracompact* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isParacompactStar_real⟧. The footnote changes nothing for M-polyfolds, whose Hausdorff property is required separately.

*The convention of Appendix 2.7.2.* The appendix (p. 72; 2017 Appendix 2.6.2, p. 51) states the convention with a locally finite open *subcovering* ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsParacompactBySubcover⟧. Read literally, it excludes $\mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · not_isParacompactBySubcover_real⟧. The cover by the intervals $(-n-1, n+1)$ has no locally finite subcover: a subcover is infinite, since $\mathbb R$ is unbounded, and the infinitely many intervals of it all contain $0$. So the wording does not hold as we read it, and we read it as "refinement", as in the footnote (possible misprint).

**Lemmas 2.7.2 and 2.3.5.** In a regular space every open $U \ni x$ contains an open $V \ni x$ with $\mathrm{cl}(V) \subseteq U$, because closed neighbourhoods form a basis ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_7_2⟧. The text states this for regular Hausdorff spaces. A Hausdorff paracompact space is normal, hence regular, and the shrinking can be done inside any given neighbourhood ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · exists_isOpen_closure_subset_of_paracompact⟧. This is Lemma 2.3.5 for M-polyfolds, $V(x)$ "arbitrarily small" ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_3_5⟧.

**Proposition 2.3.6.** A chart domain is homeomorphic to a retract, hence locally complete by Corollary 2.1.7 and Proposition 2.1.8 (2) ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · MChart.isLocallyComplete_source⟧. The chart domains form an open cover of the M-polyfold $X$, and condition (b) of the open-cover part of Proposition 2.1.8 holds by Lemma 2.3.5. So $X$ is locally complete ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · MPolyfold.isLocallyComplete⟧, with $W(x)$ arbitrarily small ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_3_6⟧. The text argues directly in a chart, with Proposition 2.1.4 and Lemma 2.3.5. "The topology on level $0$" in the text is the topology of $X$.

**Proposition 2.3.7.** Every M-polyfold is locally path-connected ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · proposition_2_3_7⟧. As for Theorem 2.2.4, this was already proved for Chapter 7 ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace⟧, by transporting the local path-connectedness of retracts through charts.

### II.25 The 2021 edition: tame sub-M-polyfolds (Definitions 2.5.18, 2.5.19)

**Definition 2.5.18.** The structure induced on a sub-M-polyfold $Y$ (§II.10) is *tame* if the M-polyfold $Y$, paracompact as a subspace, is tame ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.HasTameInducedStructure⟧.

**Definition 2.5.19.** Condition (3) asks for an sc-complement of $T_yY$ in $T_yX$ inside the reduced tangent space $T^R_yX$. Here (3) is stated in a chart; with the linear structure of $T_yX$ (gap G.7, closed, §II.39) it is restated in $T_yX$ in §II.47. For retracts $Q \subseteq O$ in $C$, a presentation $T$ of $C$, and a level-$1$ point $z$ of $Q$, there must be an sc-subspace $A$ of $E$ with $A \subseteq T_zO \cap E_z$ and $(T_zO)_m = (T_zQ)_m \oplus A_m$ on every level ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.HasReducedComplementAt⟧. ($E_z$ is the subspace of §II.12 and $T_zO \cap E_z$ the reduced tangent space of Definition 2.4.7 (preprint 2.27).) This is literally Chapter 4's general-position condition, restated so that Chapter 2 does not import Chapter 4. $A = 0$ serves for $Q = O$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.hasReducedComplementAt_self⟧.

The data at a point consist of sub-M-polyfold data $(V, r)$, so that $r(V) = Y \cap V$, together with two conditions ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.TameSubData⟧:
- $d_X(r(x)) = d_X(x)$ on $V$;
- at every smooth $y \in Y \cap V$, the chart form of (3) for some chart around $y$, with $Q$ the chart image of $Y$ near $y$.

$Y$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold of the tame $X$ if every point of $Y$ has such data ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold⟧; it is then a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold⟧. Satisfiability: in a tame $X$, $Y = X$ with $r = \mathrm{id}$ has tame induced structure, the sub-charts built on tame charts having the same tame models ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_univ⟧. It is a tame sub-M-polyfold, with $Q = O$ and $A = 0$ in every chart ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.isTameSubMPolyfold_univ⟧. The independence of (3) of the chart, the remark that a tame sub-M-polyfold is tame, and the two examples in $[0, \infty)^2 \times \mathbb R$ are §II.35 (gap G.77, closed).

### II.26 The 2021 edition: faces of open sets and the corner axioms (§2.7.4, Propositions 2.7.5, 2.7.7)

Appendix §2.7.4 is new in the 2021 edition. It builds from a tame M-polyfold $X$ a space $bX$ of "points with a chosen face" and a map $B : bX \to X$. The formalization proves all of it for an abstract $d : X \to \mathbb N$ satisfying *corner axioms*, then specializes to the degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold. The same proofs serve for the object spaces of tame ep-groupoids in 2021 §7.6.5.

**Faces of open sets.** For an open $V$ and $p \in V$ with $d(p) = 1$, the face of $V$ through $p$ is the closure in $V$ of the connected component of $V \cap \{d = 1\}$ through $p$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceAt⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsFaceIn⟧. $F_X(y, V)$ is the set of faces of $V$ through $y$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.facesThrough⟧. For an M-polyfold the faces of $X$ itself are those of Definition 2.5.10 (preprint 2.39) ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.isFaceIn_univ_iff⟧. The text's faces of $V$ are those of $V$ with its induced structure, whose degeneracy index is $d_X|V$ (2021 Proposition 2.4.4), so defining them from $d_X$ is the same thing.

**The corner axioms** ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsCornerIndex⟧. First, $d$ is upper semicontinuous (Lemma 2.4.3 (preprint 2.23)). Second, every $x$ has an open $D$ such that every $y \in D$ has *local pieces* in arbitrarily small neighbourhoods $N$: an open $B \ni y$ in $N$ and $d(y)$ preconnected sets $\ell_i \subseteq N \cap \{d = 1\}$ accumulating at $y$ and covering $B \cap \{d = 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.LocalPieces⟧. Third, the pieces are separated in $D$: no preconnected subset of $D \cap \{d = 1\}$ meets two of them. In a tame chart the pieces are the images under $r$ of the sets $\{z \in C : |z - \varphi(y)| < \varepsilon,\ I(z) = \{i\}\}$, $i \in I(\varphi(y))$, from the local face structure of §II.15 ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.exists_localPieces_chart⟧. So the degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold satisfies the axioms ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.isCornerIndex_degIndex⟧, and $d \equiv 0$ does trivially ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.isCornerIndex_zero⟧. Faces of nested opens are compatible: a face of $V$ meets an open $U \subseteq V$ in a union of faces of $U$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceAt_inter_eq⟧. A face $\theta$ of $U$ lies in a unique face of $V$, the union $\theta'$ of the faces of $V$ containing it ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceExt⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceExt_unique⟧. Every face of $V$ through a point of $U$ comes from a face of $U$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.exists_faceExt_eq⟧.

**Proposition 2.7.5.** *Face-structured neighbourhoods exist* ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.exists_nbhd_forall_isFaceStructuredOpen⟧. Take $D$ from the axioms. For an open $V \subseteq D$ and $y \in V$, the local pieces of $y$ inside $V$ lie on faces of $V$, and every face through $y$ contains a piece. Distinct pieces lie on distinct faces: a face through two pieces would give a preconnected subset of $D \cap \{d = 1\}$ meeting both, which separation forbids. So $y$ lies on exactly $d(y)$ faces of $V$. Then $V = D \cap \{d \le d(x)\}$, open by semicontinuity, gives (1) and (2). For (3), on any open $V \ni x$, take the set $B$ of the local pieces of $x$ inside $V$: a face of $V$ through a point of $B$ contains one of the pieces of $x$, which accumulate at $x$, and faces are closed in $V$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.exists_nbhd_faces_mem⟧. Together these prove the proposition ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_5⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_5⟧.

**Definition 2.7.6 and Proposition 2.7.7.** The definitions:
- an open $V$ is *face-structured* if every $y \in V$ lies on exactly $d(y)$ faces of $V$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsFaceStructuredOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceStructuredOpens⟧;
- $N_X$ is the set of the nonempty face-structured $V$ with $d|V$ bounded ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhds⟧;
- $N_{X,x}$ is the set of those $V \in N_X$ with $x \in V$ and $d \le d(x)$ on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhdsAt⟧.

$N_X = \bigcup_x N_{X,x}$, because a $V \in N_X$ contains a point where the bounded $d|V$ is maximal ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhds_eq_iUnion⟧. An open subset of a face-structured set is face-structured: its faces through a point are the traces of those of the larger set, by the local pieces ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsFaceStructuredOpen.mono⟧. Hence Proposition 2.7.7:
- $N_{X,x}$ is nonempty (Proposition 2.7.5) ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceStructuredNbhdsAt_nonempty⟧, so $N_X$ covers $X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.sUnion_faceStructuredNbhds⟧;
- nonempty open subsets of members of $N_X$ are in $N_X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.mem_faceStructuredNbhds_of_subset⟧;
- nonempty intersections of members of $N_X$ are in $N_X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.inter_mem_faceStructuredNbhds⟧;
- $N_{X,x}$ is closed under intersections ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.inter_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt⟧.

For tame M-polyfolds this is ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_7⟧.

*Quadrants.* In $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $d$ counts the vanishing half-line coordinates ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.dq_eq⟧. $\{d = 1\}$ is the union of the strata $\{p_k = 0,\ p_l > 0\ (l \ne k)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.part⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.dq_eq_one_iff⟧. A preconnected subset of $\{d = 1\}$ lies in one stratum ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.subset_part⟧, so a face through a point of the $k$-th stratum lies in $\{p_k = 0\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.faceAt_subset_coord_eq_zero⟧. A point of an open $V$ with $y_k = 0$ lies on the face of $V$ through a nearby point of the $k$-th stratum ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.exists_part_mem_faceAt⟧. Hence every open subset of a quadrant is face-structured ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.isFaceStructuredOpen_quadrant⟧.

### II.27 The 2021 edition: $L_X$, $F_X$, $bX$ and $U(x, V, \theta)$ (Definitions 2.7.8–2.7.11)

**Definition 2.7.8.** There is a morphism $(x, V) \to (y, W)$ iff $V \subseteq W$, $x$ lies on $d(x)$ faces of $W$, and each of them contains $y$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsMor⟧. The objects are the pairs $(x, V)$ with $d(x) \ge 1$ and $V \in N_{X,x}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.LObj⟧. There is at most one morphism between two objects, so $L_X$ is a preorder, a thin category. *Composition* ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsMor.trans⟧ follows the text's argument. Given $(x, V) \to (y, W) \to (z, Q)$, every face $\gamma$ of $Q$ through $x$ extends a face $\theta$ of $W$ through $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.exists_faceExt_eq⟧. That face contains $y$, so $y \in \gamma$, and then $z \in \gamma$.

**Definition 2.7.9.** The functor sends $(x, V)$ to $F_X(x, V)$ and a morphism to $\theta \mapsto \theta'$, the face of $W$ containing $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.LocalBoundaryCategory⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.boundaryStructureFunctor⟧. It is the text's "face $\theta'$ of $W$ through $x$ and $y$ with $\theta \cap \theta'$ open in $\theta$" ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.faceExt_unique⟧. Identities and composition hold because extending twice is extending once. $F_X(\varphi)$ is injective, the text's injection (2.43) ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor_map_injective⟧. It is bijective when the point does not change, since both sets have $d(x)$ elements ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.boundaryFunctor_map_bijective⟧.

**Definition 2.7.10.** An admissible triple is an object $(x, V)$ with a face $\theta \in F_X(x, V)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BTriple⟧. $(x, V, \theta) \sim (x', V', \theta')$ iff $x = x'$ and some $V'' \in N_{X,x}$, $V'' \subseteq V \cap V'$, has a face through $x$ sent to $\theta$ and to $\theta'$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BRel⟧. Reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity hold ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BRel.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BRel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BRel.trans⟧; for transitivity, intersect the two $V''$ and use the bijectivity at a fixed point. $bX$ is the quotient ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.bSetoid⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.BSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.TameBoundarySpace⟧, and $B[x, V, \theta] = x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.bMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryMap⟧. The image of $B$ is $\{d \ge 1\} = \partial X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.range_bMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.range_tameBoundaryMap⟧. *Fibres.* $B^{-1}(x)$ has exactly $d(x)$ points ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.encard_bMap_preimage⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.encard_tameBoundaryMap_preimage⟧: for a fixed $V \in N_{X,x}$, the classes over $x$ correspond to the $d(x)$ faces of $V$ through $x$, because every triple over $x$ is equivalent to one with this $V$ and distinct faces give distinct classes. This is the set-level content of Theorem 2.7.13 (4).

**Definition 2.7.11.** $U(x, V, \theta)$ is the set of classes with a representative $(y, V', \theta')$ such that $y \in \theta$, there is a morphism $(y, V') \to (x, V)$, and it sends $\theta'$ to $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.uSet⟧. The formalization reads membership as "for some representative". $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is $B$ restricted to it, with values in $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.phi⟧. It is injective: two classes over the same $y$ in $U(x, V, \theta)$ are sent to the same face $\theta$ of $V$, and $F_X$ of the morphism to $(x, V)$ is injective ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.phi_injective⟧.

*The image.* Put $V^x = \{y \in V : \text{every face of } V \text{ through } y \text{ contains } x\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.reach⟧, an open set ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.isOpen_reach⟧. For $y \in V$ there is a morphism $(y, V') \to (x, V)$ exactly when $y \in V^x$. So the image of $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is $\theta \cap V^x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.bMap_image_uSet⟧. If $V$ is centred at $x$, i.e. every face of $V$ contains $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsCenteredAt⟧, then $V^x = V$ and $\Phi$ is a bijection onto $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.phi_bijective_of_isCenteredAt⟧. $V^x$ is itself centred at $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.isCenteredAt_reach⟧ and lies in $N_{X,x}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.reach_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt⟧. So the centred neighbourhoods are cofinal, which is what the text's "take $V$ sufficiently small" (p. 85) provides. The text calls $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ a canonical bijection for every triple (2.44); §II.28 shows that some such restriction is needed.

### II.28 The 2021 edition: (2.44) and an example in $[0, \infty)^3$

Let $X = [0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$, $W$ any sc-Banach space; the trivial $W$ gives the setting $[0, \infty)^3$. Its degeneracy index satisfies the corner axioms ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.dq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.isCornerIndex_dq⟧. Take:
- $x = (0, 0, 1)$, a corner point with $d(x) = 2$;
- $V = \{p_0 < 1/2,\ 1/2 < p_1 + p_2 < 3/2\}$, a convex open slab around the segment from $x$ to $(0, 1, 0)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.slab⟧.

On $V$, $d \le 2$. $V$ is face-structured, like every open subset of a quadrant (§II.26), so $V \in N_{X,x}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.slab_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt⟧. The open segment $\{(0, t, 1 - t)\}$ lies in $\{d = 1\}$, and the face $\theta$ of $V$ through it contains its endpoints $x$ and $(0, 1, 0)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.slabFace⟧. $(x, V, \theta)$ is an admissible triple ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.counterTriple⟧. The point $(0, 1, 0)$ also lies on the face of $V$ through the nearby points of the stratum $\{p_2 = 0\}$. That face lies in $\{p_2 = 0\}$, so it misses $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.exists_face_not_mem⟧. Hence $(0, 1, 0) \notin V^x$, and $(0, 1, 0) \in \theta$ is not in the image $\theta \cap V^x$ of $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.pt_010_not_mem_image⟧. So $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is not onto $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.phi_not_surjective⟧, and not every $\Phi$ is a bijection ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.not_forall_bijective_phi⟧. As we read it, (2.44) does not hold for every $V \in N_{X,x}$. It holds for centred $V$ (§II.27). The example does not depend on reading membership in $U(x, V, \theta)$ as "for some representative", because $\Phi$ misses $(0, 1, 0)$ already on the level of points.

### II.29 The 2021 edition: the topology of $bX$ (Lemma 2.7.15, Propositions 2.7.12, 2.7.16, Theorem 2.7.13 (1))

**The topology.** $\mathcal U \subseteq bX$ is in $T_{bX}$ if every class $p \in \mathcal U$ has a representative $(x, V, \theta)$ and a set $O \ni p$, $O \subseteq \mathcal U \cap U(x, V, \theta)$, with $B(O)$ open in $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.IsBOpen⟧. We read $O$ as containing $p$: otherwise $O = \emptyset$ would make every set open. Two tools:
- a triple can be shrunk into any open $N \ni x$, keeping its class and shrinking its $U$-set ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.BTriple.exists_shrink⟧;
- equivalent triples have a common refinement whose $U$-set lies in both ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.BRel.exists_common⟧.

If two triples with the same $V$ have meeting $U$-sets, their faces agree ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.eq_of_mem_uSet⟧. These give the alternative characterization: $\mathcal U \in T_{bX}$ iff every $p \in \mathcal U$ has a representative with $U(x, V, \theta) \subseteq \mathcal U$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isBOpen_iff⟧. In that form the axioms of a topology are immediate. For intersections, two representatives of $p$ have a common refinement with $U$-set inside both ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.bTopology⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isOpen_iff_isBOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isOpen_iff_forall_uSet⟧. This proves Lemma 2.7.15 ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.lemma_2_7_15⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · MPolyfold.lemma_2_7_15⟧. The text's proof of the intersection axiom uses the sc-smoothness of transition maps; this one uses only faces.

**Proposition 2.7.12, topological part.** The sets $U(x, V, \theta)$ are open ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isOpen_uSet⟧ and form a basis ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isTopologicalBasis_uSet⟧, and $B$ is continuous ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.continuous_bMap⟧. *The germ of a face:* if $\theta$ is a face of $U \subseteq V$ through $y$, then near $y$ the extended face $\theta'$ of $V$ coincides with $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.exists_nbhd_faceExt_inter_subset⟧. Hence $\Phi$ is open: $B(\mathcal U \cap U(x, V, \theta))$ is open in $\theta$ for open $\mathcal U$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.exists_isOpen_bMap_image⟧. With injectivity and continuity, every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an open embedding into $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.isOpenEmbedding_phi⟧, and a homeomorphism onto $\theta$ for $V$ centred at $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.phiHomeomorph⟧. For two triples, the image of $U(x, V, \theta) \cap U(x', V', \theta')$ is open in $\theta$ and in $\theta'$, and the transition map is the identity on points of $X$, both maps being restrictions of $B$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_12⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12⟧. Not part of this section: the sc-diffeomorphism half of Proposition 2.7.12.
