For centred representatives it is proved with the M-polyfold structure of $bX$ (§II.36), for every representative in §II.37 (gap G.78, closed).

**Proposition 2.7.16.** *Hausdorff.* Two classes over different points of the Hausdorff $X$ are separated by preimages under the continuous $B$. Two classes over the same $x$ have representatives with a common centred $V$ and different faces, and their $U$-sets are disjoint (Hausdorff instance in `Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology.lean`). *Metrizable* ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.proposition_2_7_16⟧. For $x \in \partial X$ and a centred $W \in N_{X,x}$, write $(x, W, \theta)$ for the triple of a face $\theta$ of $W$ through $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.tripleOf⟧. The sets $U(x, W, \theta)$ cover $B^{-1}(W)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.exists_mem_uSet_tripleOf⟧; they are open, pairwise disjoint and metrizable through $\Phi$. So $B^{-1}(W)$ embeds into $X \times \mathbb R^{F_X(x, W)}$ by $B$ and the indicators of these clopen pieces, and is metrizable ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.metrizableSpace_preimage⟧. The pull-back form of Smirnov's theorem along $B$ (§II.7) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧ then metrizes $bX$. For tame M-polyfolds, $bX$ is Hausdorff and metrizable ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_16⟧. The text's route instead builds a locally finite refinement from one of the cover $(V_x)$ of $\partial X$, proves paracompactness, and applies Nagata–Smirnov.

**Theorem 2.7.13 (1) and the topological characterization.** A topology in which every $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open, and every $\Phi$ maps open sets to relatively open subsets of $\theta$, is $T_{bX}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.eq_of_isOpen_uSet⟧. With the results above this gives the topological part of the theorem ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.theorem_2_7_13_topology⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13⟧:
- $bX$ is metrizable;
- the $U$-sets are open and the $\Phi$ are open embeddings;
- $T_{bX}$ is unique with these properties;
- $B$ is continuous, with image $\partial X$ and fibres of $d_X(x)$ points.

The tame boundary of Definition 2.7.14, as a continuous map, is $B$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · MPolyfold.tameBoundary⟧. Parts (2)–(4) (the tame M-polyfold structure, $B$ sc-smooth, $d_{bX}$) and the iterated boundaries are §II.36. *Witness.* The quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$ is a tame M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_isTame⟧. Its corner has exactly $n$ preimages in $bX$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_encard_preimage⟧, so $bX \ne \emptyset$ for $n \ge 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_tameBoundarySpace_nonempty⟧. It is a tame sub-M-polyfold of itself ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_univ⟧.

### II.30 What the 2021 additions taught us

- **Local completeness needs no Hausdorff hypothesis.** The global condition $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ gives regularity, and the metrizable $W$ gives $T_1$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.t2Space⟧. Proposition 2.1.8, Lemma 2.1.9 and complete regularity hold without it.
- **One permanence lemma.** Parts (1)–(3) of Proposition 2.1.8 are one statement about embeddings with locally closed image ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · IsLocallyComplete.of_isEmbedding⟧. Proposition 2.3.6 is then the open-cover part applied to chart domains.
- **"Subcovering" in Appendix 2.7.2 does not hold as we read it.** With it, $\mathbb R$ would not be paracompact ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · not_isParacompactBySubcover_real⟧. The footnote to Definition 2.3.4 has "refinement", which is Mathlib's notion ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · isParacompactStar_iff⟧ (possible misprint).
- **$U_\infty$ needs a topology.** Lemma 2.2.1 for $k = \infty$ is proved for the topology of all the norms ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopology · lemma_2_2_1_infty⟧, by a clopen argument rather than polygons.
- **§2.7.4 is combinatorics of $d$.** Every statement of the appendix about faces, $L_X$, $bX$ and its topology follows from the upper semicontinuity of $d$ and separated local pieces ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.IsCornerIndex⟧, which is why it applies to ep-groupoids as well.
- **(2.44) needs $V$ centred.** $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ has image $\theta \cap V^x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.bMap_image_uSet⟧, and in $[0, \infty)^3$ it is not onto for a thin slab ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryExample · TameBoundaryExample.phi_not_surjective⟧. Centred neighbourhoods are cofinal ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundary · TameBoundary.reach_mem_faceStructuredNbhdsAt⟧.
- **The topology of $bX$ needs no sc-calculus.** Lemma 2.7.15 and Proposition 2.7.16 are proved from faces and the pull-back form of Smirnov's theorem ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryTopology · TameBoundary.metrizableSpace_preimage⟧. The text uses the sc-smoothness of transition maps and a paracompactness argument.

### II.31 The 2021 edition, continued: Remark 2.1.6 is strict (the K-topology)

§II.22 proved the implication of Remark 2.1.6. That the modified notion is *strictly* weaker needs an example, which the text does not give.

**A criterion.** If every point has an open neighbourhood $W$ that is completely metrizable, the modified definition holds with $V = W$, the closure of $W$ in itself being $W$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · isLocallyCompleteRel_of_forall_isCompletelyMetrizable⟧. A space embedded in $\mathbb R$ onto the complement of a sequence $(a_n)$ is completely metrizable: $y \mapsto (y, ((y - a_n)^{-1})_n)$ is a closed embedding into $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$, with image $\{(u, z) : z_n(u - a_n) = 1 \text{ for all } n\}$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · isCompletelyMetrizableSpace_of_isEmbedding_compl_range⟧. This replaces the theorem that $G_\delta$ subsets of complete metric spaces are completely metrizable, which Mathlib lacks.

**The K-topology.** Let $K = \{1/(n+1)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · kSeq⟧ and give $\mathbb R$ the topology generated by the usual open sets and $\mathbb R \setminus K$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · kTop⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · RealKTop⟧. It is finer than the usual topology, so Hausdorff. The open sets $\mathbb R \setminus K$ and $\mathbb R \setminus \{0\}$ cover it, carry the usual subspace topology, and are complements of sequences; by the criterion the modified definition holds ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · RealKTop.isLocallyCompleteRel⟧. But $0$ and the closed set $K$ cannot be separated: every closed neighbourhood of $0$ contains irrational points arbitrarily close to some $1/(n+1)$, hence meets $K$ ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · RealKTop.not_regularSpace⟧. A locally complete space is regular (§II.22), so this one is not locally complete ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · RealKTop.not_isLocallyComplete⟧.

**Remark 2.1.6, strictness.** Some Hausdorff space satisfies the modified definition and not Definition 2.1.5 ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · remark_2_1_6_strict⟧. So the remark holds as we read it, and the example shows that the global condition $\mathrm{cl}_X(V) \subseteq W$ is what makes a locally complete space regular.

### II.32 The 2021 edition: bundle retractions and the levels of $X^1$ (Definition 2.1.16, after Definition 2.3.8)

**Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9).** A retraction $R$ of $E \oplus F$ is a bundle retraction covering the retraction $r$ of $E$ if its domain is $U \oplus F$, $U$ the domain of $r$, and $R(u, v) = (r(u), \rho(u)v)$ there, with $\rho(u)$ a continuous linear map ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · ScRetraction.IsBundleRetractionOver⟧. A map $\Phi$ is a bundle map on $B$ covering $a$ if $\Phi(u, v) = (a(u), \phi(u)v)$ on $B$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · IsBundleMapOn⟧; then the first component of $\Phi$ is $a$ of the first component ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · IsBundleMapOn.fst_eq⟧. The text writes "$p' \circ \Phi = p$", which we read as $p' \circ \Phi = a \circ p$ (possible misprint). Sc-smoothness and $R \circ R = R$ are part of the data, as for every retraction (§II.2). The tangent retraction is a bundle retraction covering the level-$1$ retraction $r^1$: $Tr(u, h) = (r(u), Dr(u)h)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · ScRetraction.tangentRetraction_isBundleRetractionOver⟧. The tangent map of an sc-smooth map between retracts is a bundle map covering $f^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · IsScSmoothRetractMap.retractTangentMap_isBundleMapOn⟧. The categories $\mathcal R$ and $\mathcal{BR}$ and their forgetful functors only name these objects and maps; they are not formalized. The category $\mathcal{SBR}$ of §2.6 is (§II.45).

**The levels of $X^1$ (gap G.6).** §II.6 built the M-polyfold $X^1$ on $X_1$; its levels are those of $X$ shifted by one as sets. Their topologies agree too. In a chart, the level-$m$ lift of a point is moved to another chart by the level-$m$ map of the transition map ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.levelLift_transition⟧, and the level-$m$ lift of the level chart $\varphi^1$ of $X^1$ is the level-$(m+1)$ lift of $\varphi$, since $(E^1)_m = E_{m+1}$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.levelLift_levelChart⟧. The identity of points is therefore continuous from $(X^1)_m$ to $X_{m+1}$ and back, chart by chart, for an arbitrary chart of $X^1$ through level maps of transition maps ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.shiftLevelMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.continuous_shiftLevelMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.shiftLevelInv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.continuous_shiftLevelInv⟧. So $(X^1)_m \cong X_{m+1}$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph⟧, with the charts of $X_{m+1}$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.shift_level_eq⟧. Composing these homeomorphisms, each iterate $(X^1)^1 \cdots$ is $X_m$ with its topology and charts, which is the text's statement after Definition 2.3.8.

### II.33 The 2021 edition: Theorem 2.3.16 and Proposition 2.3.17, $T(X^i) \equiv (TX)^i$

**In a local model.** For an sc¹ map $f$, the tangent map of the level-$1$ map $f^1$ is the level-$1$ map of $Tf$ on $T(U^1) = (TU)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · tangentMap_levelMap_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · toBase_tangentMap_levelMap_one⟧. For a retract, $T(O^1) = (TO)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · retractTangent_shift_of_isScRetract⟧, and for sc-smooth maps between retracts $T(f^1)$ is again the level-$1$ map of $Tf$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · toBase_retractTangentMap_shift⟧.

**Theorem 2.3.16, bundle form.** For an M-polyfold $X$, the tangent charts belong to the structure of $TX$ (§II.8), $p : TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth, and in a tangent chart $p$ is the first projection onto the level chart $\varphi^1$. Every model $(TO, TC, TE)$ is a bundle retract, $Tr$ covering $r^1$, and the transition map of two tangent charts is a bundle map covering the level-$1$ map of the transition map of the charts ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · theorem_2_3_16⟧. "M-polyfold bundle" is read through the models and transition maps; the linear structure of the fibres $T_xX$ and the linearity of $Tf$ on them are §II.39 (gap G.7, closed).

**Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$.** A tangent vector $q$ of $X^1$ at $x \in (X^1)_1 = X_2$, read in the level chart $\varphi^1$ of a chosen chart $\varphi$ of $X$ around $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.someChart⟧, is $(\varphi^1(x), h')$ with $h' \in E_1$; it gives the tuple $(x, \varphi, h')$ of $TX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.TangentPre.lower⟧. Read in any chart $\psi$ of $X$, this tuple is the inclusion of $q$ read in $\psi^1$, because $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $(TO)^1$ is the tangent map of $(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_lower⟧. So it defines an inclusion $\iota : T(X^1) \to TX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentLower⟧. Its values lie on level $1$ of $TX$, giving $\Phi : T(X^1) \to (TX)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentShiftMap⟧, a bijection ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentShiftEquiv⟧ and a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentShiftHomeomorph⟧. In every chart $\psi$ around the base point, $T\psi(\Phi(\alpha))$ is the inclusion of $T(\psi^1)(\alpha)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_tangentLower⟧, so $\Phi$ does not depend on the chosen chart; in the charts $T(\varphi^1)$ and $(T\varphi)^1$ it is the identity of $T(O^1) = (TO)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.levelChart_tangentShiftMap⟧. Hence $\Phi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentShiftEquiv_isScDiffeoOn⟧, it covers the identity of $(X^1)^1$, and the level-$1$ map $p^1 : (TX)^1 \to (X^1)^1$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentProjShift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · proposition_2_3_17⟧.

**$i = 2$.** A bijection of M-polyfolds sc-smooth in both directions raises to an sc-diffeomorphism of the lifts ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.levelOneEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.levelOneEquiv_isScDiffeoOn⟧. Composing $\Phi$ for $X^1$ with the raise of $\Phi^{-1}$ gives $T(X^2) \cong (TX)^2$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentShiftEquivTwo⟧, covering the identity of $(X^1)^2 = (X^2)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.tangentProjShiftTwo⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · proposition_2_3_17_two⟧.

**Every $i$.** To speak of $X^i$ as a function of $i$, an M-polyfold is bundled with its space ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold⟧; then $X^0 = X$, $X^{i+1} = (X^i)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.lift⟧, and $TX$ is again bundled ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangent⟧. Sc-diffeomorphisms and sc-smooth maps are packaged with their index raises ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.ScEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.ScEquiv.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.ScMap⟧, with $\Phi$ and $p$ as instances ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.tangentShiftScEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.tangentProjScMap⟧. By recursion, $\Phi_0 = \mathrm{id}$ and $\Phi_{i+1} = (\Phi_i)^1 \circ \Phi$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv⟧; likewise $J_i : (X^1)^i \to (X^i)^1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.shiftLiftEquiv⟧ and $p^i$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentProjLift⟧. The inclusions $X^i \to X$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.incl⟧ are injective, and $T(X^i) \to TX$ is the composite of the inclusions $\iota$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentIncl⟧. With these, $\Phi_i$ and $J_i$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, the projections are sc-smooth, $J_i \circ p^i \circ \Phi_i = p$, $\Phi_i$ commutes with the inclusions into $TX$ and with those of the two towers $T(X^{i+1}) \to T(X^i)$ and $(TX)^{i+1} \to (TX)^i$, $J_i$ is the identity on points, and these properties determine $\Phi_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv_unique⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · proposition_2_3_17_all⟧. $\Phi_1$ is the $\Phi$ above ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv_one⟧. Because $\iota \circ T(f^1) = Tf \circ \iota$ for every sc-smooth $f$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · MPolyfold.tangentLower_tangentMap⟧, $\Phi_i$ is natural in $X$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.tangentLiftEquiv_natural⟧. A bundled M-polyfold exists, the half-line ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · BundledMPolyfold.nonempty⟧. Linearity of $\Phi_i$ on the fibres is not stated; in charts $\Phi_i$ is a composite of index raises of identities. The linear structure of $T_xX$ in which it could be stated is §II.39. Lemma 4.4.4 for every $i$ uses this identification (Chapter 4).

### II.34 The 2021 edition: Remark 2.4.2, the diagonal half-line

The text's example is $\Delta = \{(s, s, s) : s \ge 0\}$ in $C = [0, \infty)^3$; here $C = [0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$ for any sc-Banach space $W$, with $W = 0$ the text's case. The constant linear maps between $\mathbb R$ and $\mathbb R^3$ are sc-operators ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · ScOperator.ofConst⟧, and replacing the three coordinates by their average ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalAverage⟧ is an sc-smooth retraction of $C$ onto $\Delta \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalRetraction⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · mem_diagonalRetraction_retract_iff⟧, the orthogonal projection onto the diagonal; the text gives no retraction. Its retract is a local model ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalModel⟧ and an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalPolyfold⟧.

$(s, w) \mapsto ((s, s, s), w)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalEmbed⟧, with inverse the first coordinate ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalProject⟧, is an sc-diffeomorphism from the half-line M-polyfold $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ onto $\Delta \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalEmbed_isScDiffeoOn⟧. In $C$, $d_C((s, s, s), w)$ is $3$ at $s = 0$ and $0$ otherwise ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · degIndex_diagonal_quadrant⟧; on the M-polyfold, $d_\Delta$ is $1$ at $s = 0$ and $0$ otherwise, by the invariance of the index under sc-diffeomorphisms (Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24), §II.11) applied to the half-line ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalPolyfold_degIndex⟧. One chart, defined on all of $\Delta \oplus W$, has the model $[0, \infty) \oplus W$, and in it the chart index is $d_\Delta$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalHalfLineChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · diagonalHalfLineChart_spec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · remark_2_4_2⟧. So the defining chart realizes $d_C$, the more economical one $d_\Delta$, as the remark says.

### II.35 The 2021 edition: tame sub-M-polyfolds, continued (Definition 2.5.19 and the text after it)

§II.25 stated condition (3) of Definition 2.5.19 in one chart around each smooth point, with one presentation of its partial quadrant.

**Chart independence.** A point is smooth iff its image in one chart is a smooth point of the model ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.mem_smoothSet_iff_of_isChart⟧. Condition (3) in a chart is the general-position condition of Chapter 4 for the retraction of the model and the chart image of $Y$, word for word. Chapter 4's chart change for that condition (`MPolyfold.isGeneralPositionRetractAt_chart_change`, Chapter 4) moves it to every chart $\varphi \ni y$, every presentation of the partial quadrant of $\varphi$, every level-$1$ representative, and the chart image of any other sub-M-polyfold retraction onto $Y$ near $y$ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.TameSubData.hasReducedComplementAt_of_isChart⟧, in particular of the same one ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.TameSubData.complement_forall_charts⟧. (3) is a statement in charts here; its form in $T_yX$, equivalent to it, is §II.47.

**A tame sub-M-polyfold is tame.** Sc-splittings compose: if $E = M \oplus B$ is an sc-splitting and $M_m = N_m \oplus A_m$ on every level for sc-subspaces $N, A \subseteq M$, then $E = N \oplus (A \oplus B)$ is one ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · ScBanach.levelSub_sup_of_le_of_isScSplitting⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · ScBanach.isScSplitting_sup_of_complementIn⟧. In a chart $\varphi$ with a tame model, whose tame retraction is $t$, the chart image $\varphi(W \cap Y)$ is the retract of $(\varphi r \varphi^{-1}) \circ t$. That retraction is tame: the index condition comes from (2) of Definition 2.5.19 and $d_X = d_C \circ \varphi$ in a tame chart; the sc-complement of the tangent space of $\varphi(W \cap Y)$ inside $E_x$ is $A \oplus B$, with $A$ from (3) in the chart $\varphi$ (chart independence) and $B$ the complement of $T_xO$ from the tameness of $t$ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.TameSubData.isTameRetract_image⟧. So the sub-charts of $Y$ built on tame charts of $X$ have tame models, and $Y$ has a tame induced structure (Definition 2.5.18) ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure⟧. The text calls this not difficult to see and gives no proof.

**The examples.** In $X = [0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, the fixed set of an idempotent sc-operator $L$ mapping the quadrant into itself ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.fixSet⟧ is a sub-M-polyfold, $L$ restricted to the quadrant being a retraction ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.isSubMPolyfold_fixSet⟧; if $L$ keeps the $\mathbb R^n$-component, $L$ preserves $d_X$ (condition (2)) and (3) holds in the identity chart, so the fixed set is a tame sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.isTameSubMPolyfold_fixSet⟧. For $n = 2$, $A = \{(x, y, 0)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.setA⟧ is the case $L(a, w) = (a, 0)$: a tame sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.isTameSubMPolyfold_setA⟧ with tame induced structure ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.hasTameInducedStructure_setA⟧. $B = \{(x, x, 0)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.setB⟧ is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.isSubMPolyfold_setB⟧. No retraction onto $B$ with (1) and (2) is defined near the corner: for small $t > 0$ the point $(t, 0, 0)$ has $d_X = 1$, while $d_X$ takes only the values $0$ and $2$ on $B$ ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.not_mem_tameSubData_setB⟧. So $B$ is not a tame sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.not_isTameSubMPolyfold_setB⟧, and (3) plays no role. Yet $t \mapsto (t, t, 0)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism from the half-line onto $B$ with its induced structure ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.halfLineToB_isScDiffeoOn⟧, which is therefore tame ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.hasTameInducedStructure_setB⟧. For $W = \mathbb R$ these are the text's statements ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · TameSubExample.examples_A_B⟧.

### II.36 The 2021 edition: the tame M-polyfold $bX$ (Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4), Definition 2.7.14, (2.45)–(2.47))

**Local faces in a tame chart.** Every point of a tame M-polyfold has tame charts with domain inside a given neighbourhood ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.exists_tame_chart_subset⟧, and near a point of a face $\theta$ of a face-structured open $V$ the face is, in such a chart, the zero set of one coordinate, as in Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45) (§II.16) ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.exists_localFace_of_faceIn⟧.

**Chart data.** A chart datum consists of a triple $(x, V, \theta)$ with $V$ centred at $x$ (§II.27), a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, an open $V_1$ inside its domain, an sc-isomorphism $T$ of its model space with $\mathbb R^{k+1} \oplus W$ and a coordinate $i$ vanishing on $T\varphi(\theta \cap V_1)$, such that the face projection $\pi$ of Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43) maps $\varphi(\theta \cap V_1)$ onto a tame retract of $[0, \infty)^k \oplus W$, and $d_X = d \circ \pi \circ \varphi + 1$ on $\theta \cap V_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.BChartData⟧. Its chart is $p \mapsto \pi(\varphi(B(p)))$ on $U(x, V, \theta) \cap B^{-1}(V_1)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.BChartData.chart⟧. Two such charts have the transition map $\pi' \circ (\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ \iota$, $\iota$ the face inclusion, which is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.BChartData.chart_transition_isScSmooth⟧, so they are compatible ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.BChartData.chart_compatible⟧. By the local faces, every point of $\theta$ lies in the $V_1$ of a datum with the triple $(x, V, \theta)$, and every class has a centred representative ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · TameBoundary.BSpace.exists_centred_rep⟧; so the charts cover $bX$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.exists_bChartData⟧ and form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.bAtlas⟧.

**Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4).** $T_{bX}$ is metrizable (§II.29), hence paracompact ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_tameBoundarySpace⟧, and with the atlas $bX$ is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold⟧, tame because the models are tame retracts ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_isTame⟧ (2). In these charts $B$ is the face inclusion $\iota$ followed by $\varphi^{-1}$, so $B$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryMap_isScSmooth⟧ (3). The index of the face model is one less than that of the quadrant: $d_X(B(p)) = d_{bX}(p) + 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap⟧, which is (4) as printed ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap_sub_one⟧.

**The characterization, centred representatives.** A face $\theta$ of a face-structured open $V$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_isFaceIn⟧, which we take as "the structure induced from $V$" ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.facePolyfold⟧. For $V$ centred at $x$, $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.phiTot⟧ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto $\theta$, because in the charts above it is the face inclusion ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.phi_isScDiffeoOn⟧. Every M-polyfold structure on $bX$ with the topology $T_{bX}$ for which all these $\Phi$ are sc-diffeomorphisms is equivalent to this one ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique⟧, which has the property ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_satisfies⟧. The sc-half of Proposition 2.7.12 for centred representatives follows ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo⟧, and one statement collects (2)–(4), the characterization and its uniqueness ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13_structure⟧.

**Definition 2.7.14 and the iterated boundaries.** The tame boundary is $bX$ with this structure and the sc-smooth $B$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.definition_2_7_14⟧. To iterate $b$, a tame M-polyfold is bundled with its space ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle⟧, so that $bX$ is again such a bundle ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.b⟧. Then $b^0X = X$, $b^{k+1}X = b^k(bX)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iter⟧, and $B^0 = \mathrm{id}$, $B^{k+1} = B_X \circ B^k_{bX}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iterMap⟧, which unwinds to the text's $B^k = B_X \circ B_{bX} \circ \cdots \circ B_{b^{k-1}X}$. By (3) and (4) and induction, $B^k$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.iterMap_isScSmooth⟧, $d_X(B^k(p)) = d_{b^kX}(p) + k$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.degIndex_iterMap⟧, and the image of $B^k$ is $\{d_X \ge k\}$, by induction from the image $\partial X$ of $B$ (§II.29) and the index formula ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.TameMPolyfoldBundle.range_iterMap⟧.

*Witness.* For the tame quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n \ge 1$, chart data exist ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_bChartData_nonempty⟧, and the $n$ points of $bX$ over the corner have $d_{bX} = n - 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.quadrantPolyfold_degIndex_tameBoundary⟧.

### II.37 The 2021 edition: Proposition 2.7.12 and the characterization for every representative

**Centred refinements.** Every triple $s$ has an equivalent triple $s'$ centred at its point with $U(s') \subseteq U(s)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · TameBoundary.BTriple.exists_centred_subset⟧: replace $V$ by $V^x$ (§II.27). On the image $\theta \cap V^x$ of $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.reachSet⟧, an open subset of $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.isOpen_reachSet⟧ equal to $\theta$ for centred $V$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.reachSet_eq_univ_of_isCenteredAt⟧, the inverse is a total map ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · TameBoundary.phiInv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · TameBoundary.phiInv_spec⟧.

**Sc-smoothness.** $\Phi$ is sc-smooth on $U(x, V, \theta)$, as $B$ followed by the inclusion into the sub-M-polyfold $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.phiTot_isScSmoothOn⟧. Near each point $y$ of $\theta \cap V^x$, $\Phi^{-1}$ is $\Phi_{s'}^{-1}$ for a centred refinement $s'$ at $y$, composed with the inclusion of an open piece of $\theta$ into the face of $s'$; that inclusion is sc-smooth because a map into a sub-M-polyfold is sc-smooth as soon as it is sc-smooth into $X$. This replaces the open sc-embeddings of faces in the text's argument ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.phiInv_isScSmoothOn⟧. So $\Phi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto the open set $\theta \cap V^x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.phi_isScDiffeoOn_nonCentred⟧.

**Proposition 2.7.12 as printed.** For every pair of representatives, the images of $U \cap U'$ lie in $\theta \cap V^x$ and $\theta' \cap V'^{x'}$ and are open there, and the transition map is the composite of an inverse and a forward map, hence an sc-diffeomorphism, with inverse the reverse transition map and the identity on points of $X$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12_scDiffeo_nonCentred⟧.

**The characterization.** An M-polyfold structure on $bX$ in which every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta \cap V^x$ is equivalent to that of §II.36 ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique_allReps⟧, which has the property ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_satisfies_allReps⟧. With "onto $\theta$" it does not hold as we read it for every representative: for the slab triple of §II.28, $\Phi$ does not map $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.not_surjOn_phiTot⟧. The strongest version that holds is the one onto $\theta \cap V^x$, which for centred $V$ is the printed statement (§II.36).

**What these additions taught us.**
- **"Weaker" is strict**, through a classical non-regular space ⟦Chapter2/LocalTopologyExample · remark_2_1_6_strict⟧; the global condition of Definition 2.1.5 is what gives regularity.
- **The levels of $X^1$ are those of $X$**, chart by chart ⟦Chapter2/TangentLift · MPolyfold.shiftLevelHomeomorph⟧, so the iterates realize the $X_m$ of the text.
- **$T(X^i) \equiv (TX)^i$ is one statement for all $i$** once M-polyfolds are bundled with their spaces ⟦Chapter2/TangentLiftAll · proposition_2_3_17_all⟧; fibre linearity of $Tf$ is §II.39.
- **Condition (3) of Definition 2.5.19 is Chapter 4's general-position condition**, and its chart change is Chapter 4's ⟦Chapter2/TameSub · MPolyfold.TameSubData.hasReducedComplementAt_of_isChart⟧.
- **$bX$ is built from face charts of centred triples** ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold⟧; non-centred representatives need the image $\theta \cap V^x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.phi_isScDiffeoOn_nonCentred⟧.

### II.38 Proposition 2.1.2 (preprint 2.2): classical smooth retractions have submanifold images

**Statement.** Let $r : U \to U$ be a $C^\infty$ retraction of an open subset $U$ of a Banach space $E$, $O = r(U)$ and $x \in O$. With $P = Dr(x)$, $R = \operatorname{range}P$ and $N = \ker P$, the space splits as $E = R \oplus N$ into closed subspaces. There are open $V \ni x$, $W \ni 0$ and a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $\psi : V \to W$ with $\psi(x) = 0$ and $\psi(O \cap V) = R \cap W$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.proposition_2_1_2⟧. The text prints the normalization as $\psi(0) = x$ for a map $\psi : V \to W$; we read it as $\psi(x) = 0$.

*Proof.* The text estimates remainders in Appendix 2.7.1. The formal proof conjugates $r$ to the linear projection $P$ instead.
- *$P$ is a projection.* From $r \circ r = r$ near $x$ and $r(x) = x$, the chain rule gives $P^2 = P$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.isIdempotentElem_fderiv⟧. So $R$ and $N$ are closed and complementary.
- *The conjugating map.* Put
$$\varphi(y) = P\bigl(r(y) - x\bigr) + (1 - P)\bigl(y - r(y)\bigr)$$
⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.retractChart⟧. It is $C^\infty$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.contDiffOn_retractChart⟧, with $\varphi(x) = 0$. Its derivative at $x$ is $P\cdot P + (1 - P)(1 - P) = P + (1 - P) = 1$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.hasFDerivAt_retractChart⟧.
- *Conjugation.* $\varphi(r(y)) = P(r(y) - x)$, because $r(r(y)) = r(y)$, and $P\varphi(y) = P(r(y) - x)$, because $P(1 - P) = 0$. So $\varphi \circ r = P \circ \varphi$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothRetractImage · GapP1Prop212.retractChart_comp⟧.
- *Inverse function theorem.* Mathlib's inverse function theorem makes $\varphi$ a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism from an open $V_0 \ni x$ onto an open set. Shrink $V_0$ to the open set $V$ of points $y \in V_0$ with $r(y) \in V_0$ at which $D\varphi(y)$ is invertible, and let $\psi = \varphi|_V$ and $W = \psi(V)$.
- *The image of $O$.* If $y \in O \cap V$, then $\psi(y) = \varphi(r(y)) = P\varphi(y) \in R$. Conversely, if $\psi(y) \in R$, then $\varphi(r(y)) = P\varphi(y) = \varphi(y)$; both $y$ and $r(y)$ lie in $V_0$, where $\varphi$ is injective, so $r(y) = y$ and $y \in O$.

### II.39 Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18), Proposition 2.3.19 (3)–(4) (preprint 2.21) and Theorem 2.3.16: the linear structure of $T_xX$

Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18) makes $T_xX$ a vector space by adding representatives in one chart, and the text says after it that $T_xX$ inherits the Banach structure of $T_{\varphi(x)}O$, and the sc-structure at a smooth $x$. That the result does not depend on the chart is not argued. It holds because the fibre transitions are linear.

**The models.** For a retract $O$ and $a \in O_1$, the tangent space $T_aO = Dr(a)E_0$ is a closed subspace, the range of a continuous projection ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · tangentSubmodule⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · isClosed_tangentSubmodule⟧. For a chart $\varphi$ around $x \in X_1$, the model of the fibre is $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberModel⟧, and $T\varphi$ restricts to a bijection $T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ with inverse $h \mapsto [(x, \varphi, h)]$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberEquiv⟧.

**The transitions are linear.** For two charts $\varphi$, $\psi$ around $x$, the fibre transition $T\psi \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$ is the restriction to $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ of the bounded operator $D(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(\varphi(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.exists_transition_clm⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.transitionCLM⟧. This comes from the description of the tangent map of a map between retracts, $(a, h) \mapsto (g(a), Dg(a)h)$ (Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8), §II.3). The transitions in the two directions are inverse to each other on the models ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberTransition_transition⟧.

**The vector space.** Transport the vector space structure of $T_{\varphi_0(x)}O$ along $T\varphi_0$ for one chosen chart $\varphi_0$ around $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.fiberChart⟧. For every other chart $\varphi$, $T\varphi = (\text{transition}) \circ T\varphi_0$ is then linear, so $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is a linear isomorphism for every chart ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberLinearEquiv⟧. This is the chart independence of the definition. The text's formula $\lambda[(x, \varphi, h_1)] + \mu[(x, \varphi, h_2)] = [(x, \varphi, \lambda h_1 + \mu h_2)]$ holds in every chart ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.definition_2_3_14⟧.

**The Banach space.** Give $T_xX$ the subspace topology of $TX$. Then $T\varphi$ is a homeomorphism onto $T_{\varphi(x)}O$, since the tangent charts are homeomorphisms (§II.8) ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.continuous_tangentFiberEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.continuous_tangentFiberEquiv_symm⟧. So it is a topological linear isomorphism onto a Banach space ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberContinuousLinearEquiv⟧. The norm pulled back through a chart induces the topology and is complete ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberNormedAddCommGroup⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.completeSpace_tangentFiber⟧. Two charts give equivalent norms, because the transition is an isomorphism of Banach spaces ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberTransitionEquiv⟧.

**The sc-structure at a smooth point.** If $x$ is smooth, so is $\varphi(x)$, and $Dr(\varphi(x))$ is an sc-projection. Its range $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ is therefore an sc-subspace of $E$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.isScSubspace_tangentFiberModel⟧. The transition operator is an sc-operator at a smooth point ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.isScOperator_transitionCLM⟧ and maps level $m$ of one model into level $m$ of the other ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.transitionCLM_mem_range_toBase⟧. With its inverse, it restricts to an sc-isomorphism of the models ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.tangentFiberScIso⟧ (§II.44). So the sc-structures through two charts agree.

**Tangent maps are linear on the fibres (Theorem 2.3.16).** For $f$ sc-smooth near $x$, $Tf$ restricted to $T_xX \to T_{f(x)}Y$ is, in charts $\varphi$ and $\psi$, the bounded operator $D(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(\varphi(x))$, and this operator is an sc-operator if $x$ is smooth ⟦Chapter2/TangentMapLinear · MPolyfold.exists_clm_tangentMapOnFiber⟧. Hence $Tf$ is continuous and linear on the fibres ⟦Chapter2/TangentMapLinear · MPolyfold.tangentMapOnCLM⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMapLinear · MPolyfold.tangentMapOnCLM_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMapLinear · MPolyfold.tangentMapCLM⟧. Together with §II.33 this is Theorem 2.3.16 with fibre linearity ⟦Chapter2/TangentMapLinear · MPolyfold.theorem_2_3_16_linear⟧. The text leaves this implicit in "$Tf$ is a bundle map".

**Proposition 2.3.19 (3)–(4) (preprint 2.21) in $T_aX$.** Let $A \subseteq X$ be a sub-M-polyfold, $a \in A_1$, and $r : V \to V$ an sc-smooth retraction with $r(V) = A \cap V$. The tangent of the inclusion, $Ti : T_aA \to T_aX$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.subInclusionCLM⟧, and the tangent of $i^{-1} \circ r$, $T_aX \to T_aA$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.subRetractionCLM⟧, are continuous linear maps. Since $i^{-1} \circ r \circ i = \mathrm{id}$ near $a$, the chain rule gives $T(i^{-1} \circ r) \circ Ti = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.subRetractionCLM_subInclusionCLM⟧. So $Ti$ is injective, $Ti \circ T(i^{-1} \circ r)$ is a continuous projection of $T_aX$, and
$$T_aX = Ti(T_aA) \oplus \ker T(i^{-1} \circ r)$$
is a splitting into closed subspaces ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_3_linear⟧. The projection is $Tr(a)$, so its range is $Tr(a)T_aX = Ti(T_aA)$, and $T(i^{-1} \circ r)$ is onto: this is (4) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_4⟧. At a smooth $a$ the splitting is an sc-splitting. In a chart, the images of the two summands are the ranges of the idempotent sc-operators $L \circ Dr(a)$ and $Dr(a) - L \circ Dr(a)$, where $L$ is the chart representative of $Tr(a)$. Both are sc-subspaces, complementary on every level of $T_{\varphi(a)}O$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangentSc · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_3_sc⟧. This is the text's proof, which writes $Dt(a)$ for $L \circ Dr(a)$, carried to $T_aX$. The chart statements of §II.10 remain.

### II.40 Proposition 2.3.15 (2) (preprint 2.19): $p : TX \to X_1$ is open

**Statement.** For every M-polyfold, the projection $p : TX \to X^1$ is open ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · MPolyfold.isOpenMap_tangentProj⟧. With the continuity of §II.8 this is (2) in full ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · proposition_2_3_15_two⟧. Appendix 2.7.3 reduces it to the openness of $\mathrm{pr}_1 : TO \to O_1$ and states that without proof.

*The local step* ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · ScRetraction.exists_isOpen_tangent_section⟧. Let $O = r(U)$, $(o, h) \in TO$, and $W$ open in $E_1 \times E_0$ with $(o, h) \in W$. The map $o' \mapsto Tr(o', h) = (r(o'), Dr(o')h)$ is continuous on $U_1$, because $Tr$ is $\mathrm{sc}^0$. At a point $o' \in O_1$ it equals $(o', Dr(o')h)$, a point of $TO$, because $r(o') = o'$ and $Dr(o')h \in T_{o'}O$. At $o$ it equals $(o, h)$, because $Dr(o)$ is the identity on $T_oO$. By continuity there is an open $N \ni o$ in $E_1$ such that every $o' \in N \cap O_1$ carries the vector $Dr(o')h$ with $(o', Dr(o')h) \in TO \cap W$. So $\mathrm{pr}_1(TO \cap W) \supseteq N \cap O_1$.

*The global step.* An open $S \subseteq TX$ around a class $\alpha$ is, in the tangent chart $T\varphi$ of a representative of $\alpha$, a set $TO \cap W$. The open set $N$ of the local step gives the basic open set $\{y \in V : \varphi(y) \in N\}$ of $X^1$ (§II.6), which contains $p(\alpha)$ and lies in $p(S)$. This makes the hypothesis "$p$ open" of Chapter 7's smooth regularity, and of the results of §§7.4 and 8.1 that assume it, a theorem.

### II.41 Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28) and Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), second statement: $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant

**Statement.** Let $r$ be an sc-smooth retraction with retract $O$ in a partial quadrant $C = T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)$, and $x \in O$ smooth. Then $T_xO$ and $T^R_xO$ are sc-subspaces of $E$, and $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant in the sc-Banach space $T_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · remark_2_4_8_isPartialQuadrant⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · remark_2_4_8_partialConeWith⟧. Its dimension is $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_C(x)$. No tameness is assumed. The remark's second sentence, that in general $C_xO$ is not a partial quadrant, therefore does not hold as we read it; the text gives no example, and by this theorem none exists. Under the hypothesis of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x)$, and the theorem's second statement follows, without the hypothesis being needed for the quadrant. What tameness adds is only the equality of the dimension with $d_C(x)$ (§II.14).

*Notation.* Let $I(x) = \{i : \lambda_i(x) = 0\}$, $E_x$ and $C_x$ as in §II.12, and $P = Dr(x)$, so that $T_xO = PE$. Let $\Lambda : E \to \mathbb R^{I(x)}$, $\Lambda v = (\lambda_i v)_{i \in I(x)}$, with kernel $E_x$, and $\sigma : \mathbb R^{I(x)} \to E$, $\sigma a = T^{-1}(\tilde a, 0)$ with $\tilde a$ the extension by zero, a right inverse of $\Lambda$.

*Step 1: $C_xO = P(C_x)$.* The two sign arguments of §II.12, applied to $r$ itself at $x = r(x)$, give $PE_x \subseteq E_x$ and $PC_x \subseteq C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_partialQuadrant⟧. As $P$ is the identity on $T_xO$, $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x = P(C_x)$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · partialConeWith_eq_image_scDeriv⟧.

*Step 2: a nonnegative idempotent matrix.* Let $M = \Lambda P \sigma$ on $\mathbb R^{I(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · coneMatrix⟧. Since $v - \sigma\Lambda v \in E_x$ and $P$ maps $E_x$ into $\ker\Lambda$, $\Lambda P = M\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · coordMapL_scDeriv⟧. Hence $M^2 = \Lambda P\sigma\Lambda P\sigma = \Lambda P P\sigma = M$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · coneMatrix_idem⟧. And $M$ maps the orthant into itself, since $\sigma$ maps it into $C_x$ and $P C_x \subseteq C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · coneMatrix_mapsTo_orthant⟧. Moreover $\Lambda(T_xO) = \operatorname{range}M$, and a $v \in T_xO$ lies in $C_x$ exactly when $\Lambda v \ge 0$.

*Step 3: Flor's theorem, in the case needed.* For a nonnegative idempotent matrix $M$, the cone $K = \operatorname{range}M \cap [0, \infty)^\iota$, which equals $M([0, \infty)^\iota)$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · image_orthant_eq_nonnegRange⟧, is simplicial: it is the set of nonnegative combinations of linearly independent columns $c_1, \dots, c_s$ of $M$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · flor_nonnegRange_simplicial⟧. Write $B(j)$ for the support of column $j$.
- From $M^2 = M \ge 0$, $M_{im} \ge M_{ij}M_{jm}$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · matEntry_mul_le⟧. So $m \in B(j)$ implies $B(m) \subseteq B(j)$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · colSupp_subset⟧.
- Call $j$ *minimal* if $B(j)$ is nonempty and minimal among the nonempty column supports. A minimal column has a private index, one that lies in no other minimal support except an equal one ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · IsMinCol.exists_private⟧. Pick $i \in B(j)$. Then $M_{ij} = \sum_m M_{im}M_{mj} > 0$ gives $m \in B(j)$ with $i \in B(m) \subseteq B(j)$, so $B(m) = B(j)$ by minimality, and $m$ is private.
- *Generation.* Every $y \in K$ is a nonnegative combination of minimal columns, one per minimal support. The proof is by induction on the size of the support of $y$. From $y = My$, a coordinate $y_i > 0$ yields $m$ with $y_m > 0$, $i \in B(m)$ and $B(m) \subseteq \operatorname{supp}y$, and then a minimal $j$ with $B(j) \subseteq B(m)$. With $t = \min_{l \in B(j)} y_l/M_{lj}$, the vector $y - t\,c_j$ is nonnegative, lies in $\operatorname{range}M$, and has smaller support ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · exists_nonneg_comb_coneGen⟧.
- *Independence.* Evaluating a vanishing combination at the private indices shows that the chosen columns are linearly independent ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · linearIndependent_coneGen⟧.

So $\Lambda(C_xO) \cong C_xO/T^R_xO$ is a simplicial cone, at every $x \in O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · remark_2_4_8_quotient_simplicial⟧.

*Step 4: the quadrant.* At a smooth $x$, $T^R_xO$ is an sc-subspace, because the sc-projection $P$ preserves $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · ScRetraction.isScSubspace_reducedTangentSpaceWith⟧. This is the argument of Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36) in §II.14, which did not use tameness. The vectors $\hat e_s = P\sigma(c_s) \in T_xO$ are smooth, with $\Lambda\hat e_s = c_s$. With a linear left inverse $\rho$ of $t \mapsto \sum_s t_sc_s$, the functionals $\ell_s = (\rho \circ \Lambda)_s$ satisfy $\ell_s(\hat e_t) = \delta_{st}$, and $T^R_xO = T_xO \cap \bigcap_s \ker\ell_s$. For $v \in T_xO$: $v \in C_x \iff \Lambda v \in K \iff \ell_s(v) \ge 0$ for all $s$. The sc-isomorphism $T_xO \cong \mathbb R^s \oplus T^R_xO$ of §II.14 ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitIso⟧ therefore carries $C_xO$ onto $[0, \infty)^s \oplus T^R_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · isPartialQuadrant_ofSubspace⟧.

The quadrant has dimension $s = \operatorname{rank}M = \dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$. For a tame retraction $M$ is the identity (Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35)), so $s = d_C(x)$.

### II.42 Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29): $T^R_xO$ and $C_xO$ through sc-smooth paths

**Statement.** Let $x \in O$ be smooth. (1) $T^R_xO$ is the closure of the set of derivatives $\dot\alpha(0)$ of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : (-\varepsilon, \varepsilon) \to O$ with $\alpha(0) = x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.lemma_2_4_9_reduced⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.twoSidedPathDerivs⟧. (2) $C_xO$ is the closure of the set of derivatives of sc-smooth paths $\alpha : [0, \varepsilon) \to O$ with $\alpha(0) = x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.lemma_2_4_9_cone⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.oneSidedPathDerivs⟧. (3) $T_xO = C_xO - C_xO$, at every $x \in O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.lemma_2_4_9_tangent⟧. The proof is the text's.

*Paths.* The intervals $(-\varepsilon, \varepsilon)$ and $[0, \varepsilon)$ are sc-domains in $\mathbb R$ with the constant structure ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.isScDomain_Ioo⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.isScDomain_Ico⟧. The derivative $\dot\alpha(0)$ is $D\alpha(0)1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.pathDeriv⟧, the classical two-sided or one-sided derivative ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.hasDerivWithinAt_pathDeriv⟧.

*Derivatives of paths lie in the cones.* From $r \circ \alpha = \alpha$ the chain rule gives $Dr(x)\dot\alpha(0) = \dot\alpha(0)$, so $\dot\alpha(0) \in T_xO$. For $i \in I(x)$ the coordinate $\lambda_i\alpha(t) \ge 0$ vanishes at $t = 0$. For a two-sided path it has a local minimum there, so its derivative is $0$, and $\dot\alpha(0) \in E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.pathDeriv_mem_minimalSubspaceWith⟧. For a one-sided path the derivative from the right is $\ge 0$, and $\dot\alpha(0) \in C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.pathDeriv_mem_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧. Both cones are closed, so the closures lie in them.

*Paths through every smooth vector.* For a smooth $v$, the path $\alpha(t) = r(x + tv)$ is sc-smooth for $t$ small, lies in $O$, starts at $x$, and has $\dot\alpha(0) = Dr(x)v$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.path_retract_segment⟧. If $v \in T^R_xO$ is smooth, $x + tv$ stays in $C$ for small $|t|$, since $v \in E_x$, and $Dr(x)v = v$. If $v \in C_xO$ is smooth, $x + tv \in C$ for small $t \ge 0$. So every smooth vector of $T^R_xO$, respectively $C_xO$, is a path derivative.

*Density.* The smooth vectors of $C_xO$ are dense in $C_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConePaths · GapP1Lemma249.partialConeWith_subset_closure⟧. Write $v = Pu \in C_xO$ and let $a$ be the $\mathbb R^n$-component of $T(Pu)$. The map $w' \mapsto P\,T^{-1}(a, w')$ on $W_0$ is continuous. It sends smooth points of $W$ to smooth points of $C_xO$, because $P$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point $x$ and $T^{-1}(a, w')$ lies in $C_x$. It sends the $W$-component of $T(Pu)$ to $P^2u = v$. Smooth points of $W$ are dense, so $v$ is a limit of smooth points of $C_xO$. For $T^R_xO$ the density is that of the smooth points of an sc-subspace, since $T^R_xO$ is one (§II.41) ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · ScRetraction.isScSubspace_reducedTangentSpaceWith⟧. With the two previous steps this proves (1) and (2).

*(3).* Let $Pk \in T_xO$, and let $a$ be the $\mathbb R^n$-component of $T k$. Put $k^- = T^{-1}(\max(-a, 0), 0)$, coordinatewise. Then $k + k^-$ and $k^-$ have all coordinates $\lambda_i \ge 0$, so $P(k + k^-)$ and $Pk^-$ lie in $C_xO$ by the one-sided sign argument, and $Pk = P(k + k^-) - Pk^-$. The converse inclusion holds because $C_xO \subseteq T_xO$. Smoothness of $x$ is not used.

### II.43 The extended faces of a partial quadrant, intrinsically (§2.5 before Definition 2.5.1 (preprint §2.4 before Definition 2.33))

The text defines the extended faces of a partial quadrant $C \cong [0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ from $C$ alone, through the components of $\{d_C = 1\}$. The library works with a presentation $T$, $C = T^{-1}([0, \infty)^n \oplus W)$, and the coordinate hyperplanes $f_i = \{\lambda_i = 0\}$. This subsection proves that the two agree, so the presentation enters the proofs only.

**The components of $\{d_C = 1\}$.** The set $\{e \in C : d_C(e) = 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.stratumOne⟧ is the disjoint union of the sets $A_i = \{\lambda_i = 0,\ \lambda_j > 0 \text{ for } j \ne i\}$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.faceOpen⟧. Each $A_i$ is convex, hence connected ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.convex_faceOpen⟧, and relatively open in $\{d_C = 1\}$, since the conditions $\lambda_j > 0$ are open. So the connected component of a point of $A_i$ is $A_i$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.connectedComponentIn_eq⟧, and the components are exactly the $A_i$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.faceComponents_eq⟧. The $A_i$ are distinct and nonempty: the point with $\lambda_i = 0$, the other coordinates equal to $1$ and $W$-component $0$ lies in $A_i$ only ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.facePoint_mem⟧. So there are exactly $n$ components ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.ncard_faceComponents⟧.

**Extended faces and half-spaces.** The span of $A_i$ is $f_i$, since $A_i$ is a nonempty relatively open subset of $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.span_faceOpen⟧. So the extended faces are the $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.extendedFaces_eq⟧, and there are exactly $n$ of them ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.ncard_extendedFaces⟧. The closed half-space containing $C$ with boundary $f_i$ is $C + f_i = \{\lambda_i \ge 0\}$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.add_coordFace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.isClosed_add_coordFace⟧. For $e \in C$, the faces containing $e$ are the $f_i$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$, so $d_C(e) = \#\mathcal F(e)$ ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.ncard_facesAt⟧. And $\bigcap_{f \in \mathcal F(e)}(C + f) = C_e$, the partial quadrant of Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33) as the library defines it ⟦Chapter2/ExtendedFaces · GapP1ExtendedFaces.iInter_facesAt⟧.

### II.44 Definition 2.5.8 (preprint 2.38): $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ inside $T_xX$

**Statement.** For a chart $\varphi$ around $x \in X_1$ and a presentation of its quadrant, $T^R_xX$ and $C_xX$ are the preimages of $T^R_{\varphi(x)}O$ and $C_{\varphi(x)}O$ under $T\varphi : T_xX \to T_{\varphi(x)}O$ ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.fiberCoord⟧ ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.reducedTangentFiber⟧ ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.partialConeFiber⟧. They do not depend on the chart or the presentation ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.reducedTangentFiber_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.partialConeFiber_eq⟧. At a smooth $x$, $C_xX$ is a partial quadrant in $T_xX$, and $d_{C_xX}(0_x) = \dim(T_xX/T^R_xX)$. In a tame chart both equal $d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · MPolyfold.definition_2_5_8_degIndex⟧. The sc-structure of $T_xX$ and the quadrant do not depend on the chart ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.definition_2_5_8_scStructure⟧.

*Chart independence.* For two charts, the transition maps form a germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between the overlap retracts ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.exists_isDiffeoGerm_transition⟧. Its derivative at $\varphi(x)$ is the fibre transition of §II.39. Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30) (§II.13) says that this derivative maps $T^R$ onto $T^R$ and $C$ onto $C$. So the preimages agree. This holds at every point on level $1$, not only at smooth points. The quotient dimension in a tame chart at a smooth point is $d_X(x)$ by Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36) ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.finrank_quotient_reducedTangentFiber_eq_degIndex⟧.

*The quadrant and its degree.* For a partial quadrant $C$ in an sc-Banach space $F$, $d_C(0) = \dim(F_0/(C \cap -C))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · degIndex_zero_eq_finrank_quotient⟧. The degree at the apex therefore depends only on the set. Inside $T_xX$, $T^R_xX = C_xX \cap -C_xX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · MPolyfold.mem_reducedTangentFiber_iff_lineality⟧, because $E_x = C_x \cap -C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · mem_minimalSubspaceWith_iff_lineality⟧. At a smooth $x$, in any chart, tame or not, the image of $C_xX$ in $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · MPolyfold.partialConeFiberModel⟧ is a partial quadrant, by §II.41 ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · MPolyfold.isPartialQuadrant_partialConeFiberModel⟧. Its degree at $0$ is $\dim(T_xX/T^R_xX)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentConeQuadrant · MPolyfold.degIndex_partialConeFiberModel_eq_finrank⟧.

*The sc-structure through two charts.* An sc-operator with an sc-operator inverse between sc-subspaces restricts to an sc-isomorphism of them ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · ScBanach.subspaceIso⟧. Applied to the fibre transition and its inverse, which preserve levels at a smooth point (§II.39), this gives an sc-isomorphism $T_{\varphi(x)}O \cong T_{\psi(x)}O'$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.tangentFiberScIso⟧. It carries $T\varphi(\alpha)$ to $T\psi(\alpha)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.tangentFiberScIso_comp⟧ and the model of $C_xX$ in $\varphi$ onto the model in $\psi$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceChartIndependent · MPolyfold.tangentFiberScIso_image_partialConeFiberModel⟧. So the identity of $T_xX$ is an sc-isomorphism between the two transported structures, and it preserves $C_xX$.

### II.45 Strong bundles: atlas equivalence, restriction, the maximal atlas, isomorphisms and $\mathcal{SBR}$ (Definitions 2.3.3, 2.6.1, 2.6.3–2.6.5 (preprint 2.12, 2.47, 2.49–2.51))

**Atlas equivalence is an equivalence relation.** The text speaks of "an equivalence class" of atlases, for M-polyfolds (Definition 2.3.3 (preprint 2.12)) and for strong bundles (Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51)), without checking transitivity. It holds by the locality of compatibility (§II.1). If $\mathcal A \sim \mathcal A'$ and $\mathcal A' \sim \mathcal A''$, a chart of $\mathcal A$ and a chart of $\mathcal A''$ are compatible near each point of their overlap, through a chart of $\mathcal A'$ there, and so they are compatible ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · MAtlas.Equiv.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · MAtlas.equivalence⟧. For strong bundles the same argument runs on $[0]$ and on $[1]$. The condition that the $[1]$-transition preserves fibre components in $F_1$ (§II.21) passes through the factorization ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.compatible_of_locally⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleAtlas.equiv_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleAtlas.Equiv.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleAtlas.equivalence⟧.

**Restriction of a strong bundle chart.** Let $s$ be open in the domain of the base chart $\varphi$, with $\varphi(s) = O \cap W$ for an open $W$. The chart restricts over $\varphi|_s$, with the strong bundle retraction restricted to $(U \cap r^{-1}(W)) \triangleleft F$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · IsStrongBundleRetraction.restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.restrict⟧. Its retract is $\{(u, h) \in K : u \in \varphi(s)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.restrict_K⟧, and its domain $\{u \in U : r(u) \in \varphi(s)\}$ does not depend on $W$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.restrict_U⟧. Compatibility passes to restrictions ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.restrict⟧. The overlaps are $\Phi(P^{-1}(t)) = K \cap (W \times F)$ ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · StrongBundleChart.image_preimage_eq⟧, open in $K$ through the base chart, so continuity of $P$ is never used.

**The maximal atlas.** The later chapters speak of "a strong bundle chart of $P$". Two such charts are compatible ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.IsChart.compatible⟧. All of them form an atlas equivalent to the given one ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.maximalAtlas⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.maximalAtlas_equiv⟧. A chart of $P$ is a chart of some atlas of the class ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.isChart_iff_exists_equiv⟧, and the charts depend only on the class ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.isChart_congr⟧. Restrictions of charts of $P$ are charts of $P$ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleMaximalAtlas · StrongBundle.IsChart.restrict⟧.

**Strong bundle isomorphisms and $\mathcal{SBR}$ (Definition 2.6.1 (preprint 2.47), pp. 66–67).** Strong bundle isomorphisms between the $U \triangleleft F$ contain the identity and are closed under inverse and composition ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · IsStrongBundleIso.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · IsStrongBundleIso.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · IsStrongBundleIso.trans⟧. In the text's wording, they are the invertible strong bundle maps with a strong bundle inverse ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · exists_isStrongBundleIso_iff⟧. The category $\mathcal{SBR}$ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR⟧ has as objects the local strong bundle retracts $(K, C \triangleleft F, E \triangleleft F)$. Its morphisms are the maps $K \to K'$ that extend to a map $\Phi : E \triangleleft F \to E' \triangleleft F'$ which is linear on the fibres, preserves the double filtration, and has $\Phi[0]$ and $\Phi[1]$ sc-smooth between the retracts ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.IsHom⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.Hom⟧. These are closed under identity and composition ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.IsHom.id⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.IsHom.comp⟧. Equality of morphisms is equality on $K$, so the category laws are those of maps. A strong bundle map of Definition 2.6.1 is a morphism ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · IsStrongBundleMap.isHom⟧, and a strong bundle isomorphism is an isomorphism ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · IsStrongBundleIso.toIso⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.isoOfInverse⟧. The forgetful functors $\mathrm{forget}[i] : K \mapsto K[i]$, $\Phi \mapsto \Phi[i]$ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.forget0⟧ ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · SBR.forget1⟧ land in the category of sc-smooth retracts ⟦Chapter3/StrongBundleIsoSBR · ScRetr⟧. The text has them land in $\mathcal{BR}$, which is only named (§II.32), so $K[i]$ is recorded without its bundle structure.

### II.46 Lemma 2.7.3 and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.56 and 2.57): closed locally finite refinements

**Statement.** A regular Hausdorff space is paracompact if and only if every open cover has a locally finite refinement by closed sets ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.lemma_2_7_3⟧. A regular Hausdorff space covered by a locally finite family of closed paracompact subspaces is paracompact ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.proposition_2_7_4⟧. Both hold as printed, with Mathlib's paracompactness (locally finite open refinements).

*Paracompact implies closed refinements* ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.exists_closed_refinement⟧. The text takes the closures of a locally finite open refinement. Such a closure need not lie in a member of the cover, so first shrink: by regularity each $x$ has an open $W_x$ with $\overline{W_x}$ inside a member $U_{i(x)}$. Take a locally finite open refinement $(V_j)$ of $(W_x)$. Its closures are locally finite and each lies in some $\overline{W_x} \subseteq U_{i(x)}$.

*Closed refinements imply paracompact* ⟦Chapter2/MichaelRefinement · GapP1Michael.paracompactSpace_of_closed_refinement⟧. This direction holds in every topological space, without separation. Let $(U_i)$ be an open cover. Take a locally finite closed refinement $(A_b)$, with $A_b \subseteq U_{i(b)}$. For each $x$ let $B(x)$ be the complement of the union of the $A_b$ not containing $x$ (open, by local finiteness), intersected with the $U_{i(b)}$ for the finitely many $A_b \ni x$. Take a locally finite closed refinement $(C_k)$ of $(B(x))_x$, and put $A'_b = X \setminus \bigcup\{C_k : C_k \cap A_b = \emptyset\}$. Then $A'_b$ is open, contains $A_b$, and $A'_b \cap U_{i(b)}$ is an open refinement. It is locally finite: a neighbourhood of $x$ meets only finitely many $C_k$, and each $C_k \subseteq B(x_k)$ meets only the $A_b$ with $x_k \in A_b$, finitely many.

*Proposition 2.7.4.* Given the closed paracompact $Y_i$ and an open cover, refine the cover on each $Y_i$ by a locally finite closed family $(C^i_b)$, using the lemma in the subspace $Y_i$. The family of all $C^i_b$, indexed by pairs $(i, b)$ instead of the text's unions $\bigcup_i C^i_b$, is a locally finite closed refinement of the cover, and the lemma applies.

The library's proof of Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) still goes around these results (§II.7), since the text applies Proposition 2.7.4 to $X_m$ without checking that $X_m$ is regular.

### II.47 The 2021 statements in book form: Remark 2.1.6, Definitions 2.5.18–2.5.19, Proposition 2.7.12, Theorem 2.7.13

For four 2021 statements, the earlier subsections proved the parts separately. Each is now one theorem in the book's shape.

**Remark 2.1.6.** The closure identity, the implication from local completeness to the modified notion, and its strictness (the K-topology, §II.31) together ⟦Chapter2/BookFormLocalCompleteness2021 · remark_2_1_6_book⟧. The text does not say whether "weaker" means strictly weaker, so both readings are included.

**Definitions 2.5.18–2.5.19 with (3) in $T_yX$.** With the linear structure of §II.39 and $T^R_yX$ of §II.44, condition (3) can be stated as the text states it. $T_yY \subseteq T_yX$ is read as the image of $Ti$ ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.subTangentRange⟧. In a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ and the sub-chart of $Y$ built on it, $T\varphi \circ Ti$ is the chart map of the sub-chart ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.fiberCoord_subInclusionCLM⟧. So $T\varphi$ maps $T_yY$ onto the tangent space of the chart image of $Y$ ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.coe_map_range_subInclusionCLM⟧. Condition (3) in $T_yX$ asks for a subspace $A \subseteq T^R_yX$ with $T_yX = T_yY \oplus A$ whose chart image is an sc-subspace complementary on every level ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.HasReducedScComplement⟧. It is equivalent to the chart form of §II.25 ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.hasReducedScComplement_iff⟧. Definition 2.5.19 with this (3) ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.TameSubData2021⟧ ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.IsTameSubMPolyfold2021⟧ is therefore the chart definition ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.isTameSubMPolyfold2021_iff⟧. It implies the tame induced structure of Definition 2.5.18, and $Y = X$ satisfies it ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameSub2021 · MPolyfold.definition_2_5_19_book⟧. Through the equivalence, the two examples of §II.35 apply to it.

**Proposition 2.7.12 and Theorem 2.7.13.** Proposition 2.7.12 as printed, for every pair of representatives ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameBoundary2021 · MPolyfold.proposition_2_7_12_book⟧. Theorem 2.7.13 (1)–(4) with the characterization, the uniqueness of topology and structure, and $\operatorname{range}B = \partial X$ of Definition 2.7.14, in one statement ⟦Chapter2/BookFormTameBoundary2021 · MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13_book⟧. In the characterization the image of $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is $\theta \cap V^x$, which is $\theta$ for centred $V$, as described in the opening of this part.

### II.48 §2.2 in M-polyfolds: smooth points of connected open sets are path-connected

Lemma 2.2.1 proves that the levels $U_k$, $k \le \infty$, of a connected relatively open $U \subseteq C$ are path-connected. Chapters 6 and 7 use the M-polyfold version without proof: for $U \subseteq X$ open and connected, $U \cap X_\infty$ is connected. It is proved here in two steps.
- *Local.* Every $u \in U$ has an open neighbourhood $N \subseteq U$ in which any two smooth points are joined in $U \cap X_\infty$ by a path continuous for the topology of $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothPaths · MPolyfold.exists_nhds_joinedIn_smooth⟧. The path is the retracted segment $t \mapsto \varphi^{-1}(r(\varphi(x) + \rho(t)(\varphi(y) - \varphi(x))))$ in a small ball, which is an sc-smooth path.
- *Global.* For $U$ open and connected, $U \cap X_\infty$ is path-connected in $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter2/SmoothPaths · MPolyfold.isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage⟧. Fix a smooth $x_0 \in U$. The set of points of $U$ all of whose nearby smooth points are joined to $x_0$ is open. By the local step and the density of $X_\infty$, it is also closed in $U$, so it is $U$.

## Part III. Sc-Fredholm theory and the implicit function theorem (HWZ Chapter 3, §§3.1–3.8)

Chapter 3 is the reason for the first two chapters: it defines the sections of strong bundles to which an implicit function theorem applies, the *sc-Fredholm sections*, and proves that theorem. The engine is a fixed point problem with finitely many parameters, $w = B(a, w)$, $a \in \widetilde C \subseteq \mathbb R^n$, $w \in W$, where $B(a, \cdot)$ contracts with an arbitrarily small constant near $0$ *on every level* $W_m$ of the scale. Its solution $w = \delta(a)$ is the *solution germ*; the germ implicit function theorem (Theorem 3.3.6 (preprint 3.33)) says that $\delta$ is as regular as $B$. Around it the chapter builds: germs and their calculus (§III.1), sections of strong bundles in charts (§III.2), fillers (§§III.3–III.4), basic germs and their linearization (§III.5), sc-Fredholm germs and sections with the stability theorem 3.15 (§III.6); the germ implicit function theorem itself (§§III.7–III.11); local regularity and compactness, Theorems 3.5.1 and 3.1.13 (preprint 3.40 and 3.12) (§§III.12–III.13); the finite-dimensional geometry of good position and the inverse and implicit function theorems in partial quadrants, which the formalization proved first and the rest uses (§§III.14–III.17); the basic class and local solvability (§§III.18–III.20); the linearization of an sc-Fredholm section at a zero, good position, and the graph description of the solution set of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) (§§III.21–III.23); the tangent germ property, its invariance, and the manifold structure of solution sets (§III.24); and Lemmas 3.7.2–3.7.4 (preprint 3.59–3.61) of the basic germ criterion (§III.25). Sections III.27–III.39 were added after the part was first assembled, for the Lean written since: tameness under sc-diffeomorphisms (§III.27), Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39) (§III.28), good complements whose projection maps the quadrant into itself and local solvability with such a complement (§III.29), the index in Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) (§III.30), the linearization at a zero in charts and its chart independence (§III.31), Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) at the nearby zeros (§§III.32–III.33), Theorem 3.6.8 (2) (preprint 3.54) (§§III.34–III.36), the implicit function theorems 3.54, 3.23, 3.19, 3.24, 3.56, 3.57 assembled (§III.37), the basic germ criterion, Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) (§III.38), and what this addendum taught us (§III.39). Sections III.40–III.46 were added in a second addendum: Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) (§III.40); Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) with the text's hypotheses, by an implicit function theorem at the nearby zero (§§III.41–III.43); the dimension of the solution set as the Fredholm index and its local constancy (§III.44); the kernel as tangent space, good position at interior zeros, and the filler condition of §III.33 as a theorem (§III.45); and what the second addendum taught us (§III.46). Section III.47 repairs a tameness hypothesis, and §III.48 records the switch of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) to the text's germ reading; the passages above that use the filling or the sc⁺-section have been rewritten for it. Section III.49 proves Definition 6.2.1 and Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.1 and 6.2), and §§III.50–III.55 compare the part with the 2021 edition. Sections III.56–III.66 were added with the waves of November 2026, which closed the remaining gaps of the chapter: Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27) under the tangent germ property alone (§III.56); the implicit function theorems with the 2021 definitions (§III.57); Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36) (§III.58); the extreme-ray lemmas of the appendix (§III.59); Definition 3.8.14, Lemmas 3.8.20 and 3.8.21 (preprint 3.71, 3.76, 3.77) (§III.60); Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) in a general presentation and $d_M = d_X$ (§III.61); the intrinsic linearization and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ (§III.62); Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58) for a general sc-splitting (§III.63); an sc-smooth family of projections whose rank jumps (§III.64); Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) with untamed 2021 germ data, a counterexample (§III.65); and what is left and what was learnt (§III.66).

**What is proved, and what is not.** All of Chapter 3 is now formalized. The sixteen gaps the comparison listed for the chapter (G.16–G.30 and G.79) are closed, G.79 by a counterexample, and no hypothesis remains that the text neither states nor takes in its proof.

*The germ implicit function theorem.* It is proved with the text's hypotheses (Theorems 3.3.2–3.3.7 (preprint 3.29–3.34) and Theorem 3.35 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)), and in the quantitative form of Remark 3.3.8 (preprint 3.36) (§III.58, G.19). What the formalization adds is precision about *where* the solution germ is regular. A germ is formalized as a fixed sequence of sets, and $\delta$ is sc$^k$ on the germ shifted by $s_k = 2^k - 1$ levels. So "if $f$ is sc-smooth so is its solution germ" holds for every $k$ on a germ depending on $k$ (§III.11).

*Germs, sections and their linearization.*
- Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) is formalized as the text writes it, with the filling and the sc⁺-section sc-smooth *germs* (§§III.6, III.48).
- Proposition 3.1.10 (preprint 3.10) holds on every level (§III.5, G.21).
- Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) gives an sc-Fredholm operator in every chart (§§III.30, III.57, G.22).
- Corollary 3.4.3 (preprint 3.39) is §III.28 (G.20), and Theorem 3.1.21 (preprint 3.18) is §III.40 (G.16).

*Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27)* is proved under the tangent germ property alone (§III.56). The two regularity conditions with which it was first proved (§III.24) are theorems: re-graphing over a projecting good complement gives the one, re-centring the other. The closedness of the good complement in Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25) and Lemma 3.6.9 (preprint 3.55), once listed as an added hypothesis, follows from the text's sc-complement. Two steps of the text's proof do not hold as we read it, each with a Lean counterexample (§III.56).

*The implicit function theorems.* Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) is proved with the text's hypotheses (§§III.41–III.43, G.23). With it come Theorems 3.1.22 and 3.1.26 (preprint 3.19 and 3.23), Corollary 3.1.27 (preprint 3.24) and Theorems 3.6.10 and 3.6.11 (preprint 3.56 and 3.57) (§§III.37, III.43, G.17, G.18). The dimension of the solution set is the Fredholm index (§III.44), and $\ker f'(y) = T_yS$ holds in $T_yX$ for the intrinsic linearization (§III.62, G.30). All of these are also stated in the book's form with the 2021 definitions (§III.57).

*"Tame strong bundle".* The phrase is read as germ data and good position in a tame chart (§III.47). This is the wording of the 2017 text and the preprint, and the chart the 2021 proof takes on p. 137; it is not derived from the 2021 text as printed. The reading is needed: with the 2021 germ data as printed, in any compatible chart, Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it. The witness is a tame strong bundle over $\mathbb R$ whose solution set near a zero in good position is a closed half-line (§III.65, G.79). The reading is satisfiable: the graph section of a smooth map of a trivial bundle has tame germ data (§III.47).

*The basic germ criterion*, Theorem 3.7.1 (preprint 3.58), is proved as printed, for a general sc-splitting (§III.63, G.24). The proof reduces it to the coordinates of the text's proof (§III.38).

*The appendix.*
- Lemmas 3.8.1–3.8.3 and 3.8.9–3.8.11 (preprint 3.62–3.64 and 3.66–3.68) are §III.59 (G.25, G.26).
- Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71) agrees with the $C^k$ the formalization uses (§III.60, G.27).
- Lemma 3.8.20 (preprint 3.76) is proved with Lemma 3.8.21 (preprint 3.77) in the general form its use needs (§III.60, G.28).
- Lemma 3.8.13 (preprint 3.70) and Proposition 3.8.12 (preprint 3.69) hold for a general presentation of the partial quadrant, which gives $d_M = d_X$ in Theorem 3.2.3 (§III.61, G.29).

*From Chapter 6.* Definition 6.2.1 and Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.1 and 6.2) are proved with the text's hypotheses for paths on $\mathbb R$ (§III.49).

*The four narrower rows.* Four comparison rows are narrower than the text. In each, the printed statement does not hold as we read it, and a Lean counterexample shows it:
- V3.73: the re-centring step in the proof of Theorem 3.2.3, for every pair of data. The lemma is proved with the first graph map $C^1$ on its whole domain (§§III.35, III.56).
- V3.120: Lemma 3.8.6 (2) at $N = 0$ (§III.54).
- V3.123: Lemma 3.8.1 at $P = \{0\}$ (§III.59).
- V3.130: Theorem 3.6.8 with the 2021 germ data as printed (§III.65).

**Seven structural choices.** (1) Germs are fixed sequences of sets, and the calculus the text uses on them silently is proved (§III.1). (2) Contraction germs carry explicit contraction regions instead of the text's balls, because the regions of the iterated germ $f^{(1)}$ must be unbounded in the tangent directions (§III.7). (3) "A strong bundle chart" in the definitions of §3.1 is a chart *compatible* with the atlas (§III.2). (4) Tameness, which the text assumes throughout, is used only in Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54), where it cannot be dropped (§III.65), and only for the chart of the germ data at the zero: through Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35), $(1 - Dr(0))E \subseteq E_0$, and through the tameness of the model of the chart $\psi \circ \varphi$ (§III.27). The theorems assume germ data and good position in tame charts, as Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4 and 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51 and 3.53) do; the first formalization assumed every compatible chart tame, which cannot be met (§III.47). (5) The coordinate change of Theorem 3.4.2 (preprint 3.38) is linear, which makes the transport of solution sets in §3.5 linear algebra. (6) Classical regularity in the appendix is Mathlib's $C^k$ within a set, and the iterations of the text's Lemmas 3.8.20 and 3.8.26 (preprint 3.76 and 3.82) are replaced by bootstrapping a derivative formula; the text's Definition 3.8.14 (preprint 3.71) is shown to be this notion, and Lemma 3.8.20 and Lemma 3.8.21 in the general form its use needs are proved as well (§III.60). (7) In Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) the filling $g$ and the sc⁺-section $s$ are germs on germs of neighbourhoods of their own, and the basic germ is shrunk to the germ $G''$ of the points that $\psi^{-1}$ sends into both, so that the nearby zeros produced by the implicit function theorem are points where $g$ and $s$ are sc¹ (§§III.6, III.48).

Throughout, $P$ and $Q$ are finite-dimensional normed spaces with the constant sc-structure (the text's $\mathbb R^n$ and $\mathbb R^N$), $\widetilde C \subseteq P$ a set containing $0$, convex, with nonempty interior (the text's $[0, \infty)^k \oplus \mathbb R^{n-k}$), $W$ an sc-Banach space, $E = P \oplus W$ with levels $P \times W_m$ ⟦Chapter3/ContractionGerm · ScBanach.paramProd⟧. Because all levels of $P$ coincide, the condition "$\widetilde C \times W$ is quadrant-like" is just "$0 \in \widetilde C$, convex, nonempty interior" ⟦Chapter3/ContractionGerm · isQuadrantLike_const_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter3/ContractionGerm · IsQuadrantLike.paramProd⟧.

### III.1 Germs and their calculus (Definitions 3.1.1, 3.1.2 (preprint 3.1, 3.2))

**Definition 3.1.1 (preprint 3.1).** An *sc-germ of neighbourhoods* around $0 \in C$ is a family of sets $U_m \subseteq E_m$, each of the form $O \cap C_m$ with $O$ open in $E_m$, containing $0$, and nested along the inclusions: $\iota U_{m+1} \subseteq U_m$ ⟦Chapter3/Germ · ScNbhdGerm⟧. Its *tangent germ* has levels $U_{m+1} \times E_m$ ⟦Chapter3/Germ · ScNbhdGerm.tangent⟧. The text's example, a relatively open $U \ni 0$ with $U_m = U \cap E_m$, is `ofSet` ⟦Chapter3/Germ · ScNbhdGerm.ofSet⟧. The germ calculus needs one property of $C$: every level $C_m$ is convex with nonempty interior and $0 \in C$ ("quadrant-like") ⟦Chapter3/Germ · IsQuadrantLike⟧. Partial quadrants have it ⟦Chapter3/Germ · IsPartialQuadrant.isQuadrantLike⟧, and it passes to $TC$ ⟦Chapter3/Germ · IsQuadrantLike.tangentSet⟧. It makes every $U_m$ a set of unique differentiability ⟦Chapter3/Germ · ScNbhdGerm.uniqueDiffWithinAt⟧, the intersection of an open and a convex set ⟦Chapter3/Germ · ScNbhdGerm.relOpenConvex⟧.

A germ is a *fixed* sequence of sets. The text says "the size of the sets $U_m$ does not matter", i.e. it reads germs up to shrinking; the formalization cannot, and must say on which sequence each statement holds. One trivial remark becomes important in §III.9: the re-indexed sequence $(U_{m+1})_m$ is in general not a germ, since $U_{m+1}$ is relatively open in $C_{m+1}$ and not in $C_m$; it is one when all levels coincide, i.e. for germs in the finite-dimensional parameter space $P$.

**Definition 3.1.2 (preprint 3.2).** $f$ is an *sc⁰-germ* on $G = (U_m)$ if $f(U_m) \subseteq F_m$ and the level map $f_m : U_m \to F_m$ is continuous for every $m$ ⟦Chapter3/Germ · IsSc0Germ⟧.
