The proofs use an equivalent *sheet form* ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · IsScSmoothCompSheet⟧: for every sc-diffeomorphism $s : \mathbf W \to V$ with inverse $\sigma$, the map $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t\psi), \psi)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$. *Step 1.* The graph of $\sigma \circ t$ over $t^{-1}(V)$ is an open piece of the fibred product, and the second projection is an sc-diffeomorphism from it onto $t^{-1}(V)$, with inverse $\psi \mapsto (\sigma(t\psi), \psi)$. *Step 2.* So the literal (4) gives the sheet form by composition, and conversely the fibred product is covered by such graphs ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet⟧. Every ep-groupoid satisfies the sheet form ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet⟧. The "for every $\sigma$" of the sheet form carries no vacuity risk, being equivalent to the literal condition (Findings, Chapter 7, item 4).

**Properness in sequential form** (V7.4). The text uses properness through sequences: in Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7), Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11), Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13) and Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8). For a continuous map between metrizable spaces, properness is equivalent to: every sequence whose images converge has a convergent subsequence ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq⟧. *Step 1, from properness.* The images and their limit form a compact set, whose preimage is compact, hence sequentially compact ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · exists_tendsto_subseq_of_isProperMap⟧. *Step 2, to properness.* Preimages of compact sets are sequentially compact, hence compact in a metrizable space, and a continuous map with compact fibres of compacta into a compactly generated space is proper (Mathlib's characterization) ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_of_exists_tendsto_subseq⟧. For the restriction of $t$ to $s^{-1}(Q)$ the criterion reads: every sequence with $s(\varphi_k) \in Q$ and $t(\varphi_k)$ convergent has a subsequence converging to a morphism over $Q$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_domRestrict_iff⟧, over $\mathrm{cl}\,Q$ when $Q$ is closed ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff⟧, and it is the compactness of $s^{-1}(Q) \cap t^{-1}(K)$ for compact $K$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · MPolyfold.isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_isCompact_preimage⟧. Three consequences recur. Properness passes to smaller closures, so any open $V' \subseteq V(x)$ around $x$ will do ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_domRestrict_closure_mono⟧; the image $t(s^{-1}(Q))$ is closed for closed $Q$, a proper map being closed ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isClosed_image_preimage_of_isProperMap_domRestrict⟧; and the fibres over points are finite when $t$ is locally injective ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · finite_setOf_of_isProperMap_domRestrict⟧. If $t$ is proper over $s^{-1}(Q)$ and the units exist, $Q$ is closed: a limit $x$ of $x_n \in Q$ is the source of a limit of a subsequence of the units $1_{x_n}$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isClosed_of_isProperMap_domRestrict⟧. The hidden hypothesis is metrizability, which M-polyfolds have (Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2), §II.7) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 3).

### VII.3 Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), the levels, Definitions 7.1.5 and 7.1.6 (2017: 7.5 and 7.6)

**Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4)** (V7.5). For a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ the text takes open $\mathbf U(\varphi)$, $U(x)$, $U(y)$ with $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(x)$ and $t : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(y)$ sc-diffeomorphisms and sets $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} : U(x) \to U(y)$. Such a sheet exists at every morphism ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Sheet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.exists_sheet⟧: (1) gives open neighbourhoods of $\varphi$ on which $s$, resp. $t$, is an sc-diffeomorphism onto an open set, and on their intersection both are, an sc-diffeomorphism restricting to one on every open subset. A sheet is chosen at every morphism ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.sheetAt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.mem_sheetAt⟧, and $\hat\varphi$ is defined from it ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Sheet.hat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hat⟧: an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Sheet.isScDiffeoOn_hat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_hat⟧, a composite of sc-diffeomorphisms, with $\hat\varphi(x) = y$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hat_src⟧. It depends on the sheet only as a germ. $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(x)$ is read through the chain rule as $Tt \circ (Ts|_{T_\varphi\mathbf X})^{-1}$ with Part I's tangent maps ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.tangentMor⟧; that it equals $T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$, is a bounded linear isomorphism on level $0$ for $\varphi$ on level $1$, and an sc-isomorphism for smooth $\varphi$, is proved in §VII.44, with the linear structure of $T_xX$ that Part I now provides (gaps G.7, G.70, closed). The display "$\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ U(x) \to U(y)$" is read with $:$ for the last $\circ$, and "$T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}$" with the missing $X$ (possible misprints; Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110) (2017 p. 227).

**The levels and the degeneracy index** (V7.6). A local sc-diffeomorphism preserves the levels and the degeneracy index: in a sheet it is an sc-diffeomorphism, and Part I's Proposition 2.4.4 (2017: 2.7) (§II.11) applies ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.mem_levelSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.degIndex_eq⟧. Hence $\varphi \in \mathbf X_m$ iff $s(\varphi) \in X_m$ iff $t(\varphi) \in X_m$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_src_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.mem_levelSet_tgt_iff⟧, and $d_X(s\varphi) = d_{\mathbf X}(\varphi) = d_X(t\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.degIndex_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.degIndex_tgt⟧. The text's $ml(x)$, the largest $m$ with $x \in X_m$, is the maximal level ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.maxLevel⟧, preserved too ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.maxLevel_eq⟧. $|X_k| = \pi(X_k)$ is defined ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.orbitLevel⟧; the set $|X_\infty|$, the identity $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k|X_k|$ and the density of $X_\infty$ in $X_k$ are §VII.44 (gaps G.72, G.73, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, items 6, 112, 116, 153) (pp. 289–291 (2017 pp. 227–228)).

**Definition 7.1.5 (2017: 7.5)** (V7.7). $d_{|X|}(|x|) = d_X(x)$ is well defined by the previous paragraph ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit_π⟧ (2017 p. 228).

**Definition 7.1.6 (2017: 7.6)** (V7.8). $X$ is tame if the object M-polyfold is tame ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsTame⟧, "tame" being the existence of an equivalent tame atlas (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19), §II.14) ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsTame⟧ — not "every chart is tame", which would be unsatisfiable. *Then $\mathbf X$ is tame.* At a morphism, a sheet $s : \mathbf W \to V$ composed with a tame chart of $X$ around $s(\varphi)$ is a tame chart of $\mathbf X$, since tameness is carried by sc-diffeomorphisms (§III.27) ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.exists_tame_chart⟧; these charts are compatible with the atlas of $\mathbf X$ and form a tame atlas ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame⟧; conversely a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism transfers tameness down ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isTame_iff_of_surjective⟧. The witnesses are the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial_rn⟧ and the reflection groupoid of §VII.30 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 7, 106) (2017 p. 228).

### VII.4 Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7), and the remark after it

**Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)** (V7.9). A functor between groupoids is a pair of maps commuting with $s$, $t$, $m$ on composable pairs and $u$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor⟧; it commutes with $\iota$, by the uniqueness of inverses ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor.mor_inv⟧, has identities and composites ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor.id⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor.comp⟧, a Mathlib functor ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor⟧ and a map of orbit spaces ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidFunctor.orbitMap⟧. An ep-functor is sc-smooth on objects and on morphisms ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpFunctor.id⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpFunctor.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpFunctor.ext⟧, and $\mathcal{EP}$ is the category of bundled ep-groupoids and ep-functors ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EP⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 8) (2017 p. 228).

**The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)** (V7.10). The text says that it suffices to ask sc-smoothness between the object spaces, because near $\varphi$ one has $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ for $\gamma$ in a neighbourhood $\mathbf U(\varphi)$ with $f(\mathbf U(\varphi)) \subseteq \mathbf U(\psi)$, $\psi = f(\varphi)$. Choosing that neighbourhood uses the continuity of $f$ on morphisms, and without it the claim does not hold as we read it. *The counterexample.* On the trivial action of $\mathbb Z/3$ on $\mathbb R$ (objects $\mathbb R$, morphisms $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R$, $s = t$ the projection), let $f$ be the identity on objects and $(g, y) \mapsto (g, y)$ for $y \le 0$, $(g, y) \mapsto (g^2, y)$ for $y > 0$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.remarkFunctor⟧. Since $g \mapsto g^2$ is an automorphism of $\mathbb Z/3$, this is a functor; it is sc-smooth on objects ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isScSmoothMap_remarkFunctor_obj⟧ but not continuous on morphisms, jumping at $(g, 0)$ for $g \ne 1$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.not_continuous_remarkFunctor_mor⟧, hence not sc-smooth there ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.not_isScSmoothMap_remarkFunctor_mor⟧, and no ep-functor has these components ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.not_exists_epFunctor_remarkFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.remark_definition_7_1_7_counterexample⟧. *The remark for functors continuous on morphisms.* Take a sheet $\mathbf U(\psi)$ of $s$ at $\psi = f(\varphi)$, with inverse $\sigma$, and $\mathbf U(\varphi) = f^{-1}(\mathbf U(\psi))$, open by continuity. For $\gamma \in \mathbf U(\varphi)$, $f(\gamma)$ lies in $\mathbf U(\psi)$ and has source $f(s\gamma)$, so $f(\gamma) = \sigma(f(s\gamma))$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.mor_eq_srcInv_obj_src⟧, a composite of sc-smooth maps ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_of_continuous⟧. The sheet at $\varphi$ and the neighbourhoods $U(s\varphi)$, $U(s\psi)$ of the text are not used. Since every ep-functor is continuous on morphisms ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpFunctor.continuous_mor⟧, the remark becomes an equivalence for functors sc-smooth on objects ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_mor_iff_continuous⟧, and a functor sc-smooth on objects and continuous on morphisms is an ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpFunctor.ofContinuous⟧. *The 2021 sentence* (p. 291) asks continuity on level $0$ between the morphism spaces, which is the hypothesis of the form just proved, so the 2021 remark holds as we read it (§VII.33); the counterexample concerns the 2017 sentence only ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_definition_7_1_7_counterexample⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 9, 104) (pp. 290–292 (2017 pp. 228–229)).

### VII.5 Propositions 7.1.8–7.1.10 (2017: 7.1–7.3): the topology of $|X|$

**Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1)** (V7.11) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8⟧. *$\pi$ is open.* $|X|$ carries the quotient topology, so $\pi$ is continuous ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.continuous_π⟧, and $\pi(U)$ is open iff its saturation $\pi^{-1}(\pi(U))$ is. *Step 1.* The saturation of $U$ is $t(s^{-1}(U))$: $y \cong x \in U$ iff some $\varphi$ has $s\varphi \in U$ and $t\varphi = y$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.preimage_π_image_eq⟧. *Step 2.* $s^{-1}(U)$ is open since $s$ is continuous, and $t$ is an open map, being a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isOpenMap⟧. The text argues with the sheets $V(\varphi)$, which is the openness of $t$ unpacked. So $\pi$ is an open quotient map ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_isOpenQuotientMap⟧ and carries neighbourhood filters to neighbourhood filters ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8_map_nhds⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 10) (2017 p. 229).

**Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2)** (V7.12) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9⟧. *Every $z \in |X|$ has a countable basis of open neighbourhoods, chosen monotone.* $X$ is metrizable (Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2)); for $z = \pi(x)$ the images of the balls $B(x, 1/(k + 1))$ are open by Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) and decreasing, and they form a basis because $\pi$ maps the neighbourhood filter of $x$ onto that of $z$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_of_hasAntitoneBasis⟧. The statement is Mathlib's antitone basis indexed by $\mathbb N$ (radii $1/(k + 1)$, the index starting at $0$), and $|X|$ is first countable ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_9_firstCountableTopology⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 10) (2017 p. 229).

**Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3)** (V7.13) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10⟧. *Every $x$ has an open $U$ with $\pi(\mathrm{cl}_XA) = \mathrm{cl}_{|X|}\pi(A)$ for every $A \subseteq U$.* The text proves "$\supseteq$" with a sequence $\varphi_k : a_k \to b_k$, $b_k \to b$, $a_k \in A$, of which properness extracts a convergent subsequence. The formalization proves more, for every $U$ with $t$ proper over $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_XU)$ and every $A \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XU$, and without sequences ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_10_of_isProperMap⟧. *Step 1.* Since $\pi$ is open and continuous, $\pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,\pi(A)) = \mathrm{cl}\,\pi^{-1}(\pi(A)) = \mathrm{cl}\,t(s^{-1}(A))$. *Step 2.* $t(s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}A))$ is closed, as the image of the closed $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}A) \subseteq s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}U)$ under a proper, hence closed, map (§VII.2), and contains $t(s^{-1}(A))$; so $\mathrm{cl}\,\pi(A) \subseteq \pi(t(s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}A))) = \pi(\mathrm{cl}A)$. *Step 3.* "$\subseteq$" is the continuity of $\pi$. "For every $z$ and every representative $x$" is "for every $x$" (Findings, Chapter 7, item 11) (pp. 291–293 (2017 pp. 229–230)).

### VII.6 Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1), Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4), and the conjugation $G_x \cong G_y$

**Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1)** (V7.14) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11⟧. *If $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_XU(x_0)) \to X$ is proper, only finitely many $\psi$ have $s(\psi) = x$ and $t(\psi) \in U(x_0)$.* **The text's proof** argues by contradiction with distinct $\psi_n : s(\psi_n) \to x$, $s(\psi_n) \in U(x_0)$; properness gives a convergent subsequence, $t$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism near the limit, and $t(\psi_n) = t(\psi_m) = x$ forces $\psi_n = \psi_m$. The proof thus treats the inverses of the morphisms of the statement, with $s$ and $t$ exchanged, and writes "$t : V(\psi) \to V(y)$" for $V(x)$ and "$s(\psi) \in s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(U(x_0)))$"; parentheses are unbalanced in the statement and the proof (possible misprints; Findings, Chapter 7, items 12, 96). **The formalized proof** does the proof's form first and has no sequences. *Step 1.* The fibre of the proper restriction of $t$ over $x$ is compact. *Step 2.* It is discrete, $t$ being locally injective as a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isLocallyInjective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · IsLocallyInjective.isDiscrete_preimage_singleton⟧. *Step 3.* A compact discrete set is finite ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · IsProperMap.finite_preimage_singleton_of_isLocallyInjective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · finite_setOf_mem_of_isProperMap_domRestrict⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · MPolyfold.finite_setOf_mem_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧. This gives the finiteness of $\{\psi \mid s\psi \in \mathrm{cl}_XU(x_0),\ t\psi = x\}$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap_of_isProperMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_swap⟧. *Step 4.* The statement's form follows by $\iota$, which exchanges $s$ and $t$ and is injective, and holds even for targets in $\mathrm{cl}_XU(x_0)$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_11_of_isProperMap⟧. The openness of $U(x_0)$ and $x_0 \in U(x_0)$ are kept as hypotheses but not used (2017 p. 230).

**Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4)** (V7.15) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_12⟧. *$G_x$ is finite.* Lemma 7.1.11 (2017: 7.1) with $x_0 = x$ and $U(x_0) = V(x)$ of Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3): $G_x$ is contained in the finite set of morphisms with source $x$ and target in $V(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · MPolyfold.finite_isotropy_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧. The proposition is an instance, so the cardinality of $G_x$ is its order as a finite group (Findings, Chapter 7, item 13) (2017 p. 230).

**The conjugation** (V7.16). For $\varphi : x \to y$, $g \mapsto \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is an isomorphism $G_x \to G_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.isotropyConj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.isotropyConj_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.conjIsotropy_val⟧, so isomorphic objects have isomorphic isotropy groups of the same order ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.nonempty_isotropy_mulEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.nat_card_isotropy_eq⟧. "There is no canonical identification" is given its content: two choices $\varphi, \varphi'$ give isomorphisms that differ by conjugation with $\varphi'\varphi^{-1} \in G_y$, an inner automorphism ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_eq_isotropyConj_conj⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 13) (2017 p. 230).

### VII.7 Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1), and local path connectedness

**Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)** (V7.17) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_1_13⟧. *For every object $x$ and every open $V \ni x$ there are an open neighbourhood $U \subseteq V$ of $x$, a homomorphism $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U)$ and an sc-smooth $\Gamma : G_x \times U \to \mathbf X$ with (1) $\Gamma(g, x) = g$, (2) $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$ and $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$, (3) every morphism $h : y \to z$ between points of $U$ is $\Gamma(g, y)$ for a unique $g$.* The data form a *natural representation* at $x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep⟧: $U$ open, connected and containing $x$; $\Phi(g)$ an sc-diffeomorphism of $U$ with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$ and $\Phi(gh) = \Phi(g) \circ \Phi(h)$ on $U$; $\Gamma$ sc-smooth on each slice $\{g\} \times U$, which is sc-smoothness on $G_x \times U$ (§VII.8), with (1)–(3). The first consequences: $\Phi(g)$ maps $U$ into $U$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ⟧, $\Phi(1)$ is the identity on $U$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_one⟧, every $\Phi(g)$ fixes $x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_self⟧, $\Gamma(g, y)$ is a morphism between points of $U$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_morOn⟧, $\Phi(g^{-1})\Phi(g) = 1$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_inv_Φ⟧, and (3) is a bijection $G_x \times U \to \mathbf U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.bijOn_Γ⟧. The action $g \ast y = \Phi(g)(y)$ is a group action on $U$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.smul_val⟧. The proof is the text's Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) in the appendix (§VII.26). *Hidden hypothesis:* $U$ connected. The text chooses "the connected open neighborhood $U(x)$" on p. 293 (2017 p. 231) but does not put it into the statement; as we read it, the homomorphism property of $\Phi$, the functoriality of $\Gamma$ and the uniqueness of $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ all need it (Findings, Chapter 7, item 20) (2017 p. 231).

**Local path connectedness** (V7.18). Connected neighbourhoods exist because M-polyfolds are locally path connected, which the text uses without statement (2017 p. 231, Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9), Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2)). *Step 1, a retract.* For $o \in O = r(U)$, $U$ open in a partial quadrant $C$, and a neighbourhood $W$ of $o$, there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that every $p \in O$ with $\|p - o\| < \varepsilon$ is joined to $o$ inside $O \cap W$ by the path $\tau \mapsto r(o + \tau(p - o))$: the segment lies in the convex set $B_\varepsilon(o) \cap C \subseteq U$, $r$ is continuous on level $0$ and fixes $o$ and $p$ ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · ScRetraction.exists_ball_joinedIn⟧. So an sc-smooth retract is locally path connected ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · IsScRetract.locallyPathConnectedSpace⟧. *Step 2, an M-polyfold.* Through any chart around a point, path components of open sets are neighbourhoods ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MChart.pathComponentIn_mem_nhds⟧, and $X$ is locally path connected ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace⟧, hence locally connected ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.locallyConnectedSpace⟧. *Step 3, consequences.* Open connected neighbourhoods form a basis ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.hasBasis_isOpen_isConnected⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.hasBasis_isOpen_isPathConnected⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.exists_isOpen_isConnected_subset⟧; components, also of open sets, are open ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponent⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.isOpen_connectedComponentIn⟧; an open set is connected iff path connected ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.isConnected_iff_isPathConnected⟧; every quotient of $X$, in particular $|X|$, is locally path connected ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · MPolyfold.locallyPathConnectedSpace_quotient⟧; and finitely many points of a Hausdorff locally connected space have pairwise disjoint connected open neighbourhoods inside a given open set ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · exists_pairwiseDisjoint_isOpen_isConnected⟧. *Step 4, the tool for connectedness.* Two continuous sections of a locally injective map into a Hausdorff space that agree at one point of a preconnected set agree on all of it ⟦Chapter7/LocConnected · eqOn_sections_of_isPreconnected⟧, by Mathlib's statement for separated maps ⟦Mathlib/Topology/SeparatedMap · eqOn_of_comp_eqOn⟧. For $s$ this says that a local inverse of $s$ on a connected $U$ is determined by one value; it is what makes $\Phi$ a homomorphism (§VII.26) and $\Gamma$ a functor (§VII.8). The paths are continuous on level $0$; sc-smooth paths between smooth points are Chapter 6's (§VI.18). This is the first fact of gap G.56 of Part I, now formalized (Findings, Chapter 7, items 21, 114).

### VII.8 Pages 231–233: the sheets $\mathbf U(g)$, $G_x \ltimes U(x)$, the functor $\Gamma$, and $\hat\Phi$

Everything on these pages is derived from one natural representation $(U, \Phi, \Gamma)$; the text's "using the proof of Theorem 7.1 one verifies" is not needed. No possible misprint was found on pp. 293–297 (2017 pp. 231–233) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 22).

**The splitting $\mathbf U(x) = \bigsqcup_g \mathbf U(g)$** (V7.19). Put $\mathbf U(g) = \Gamma(g, U)$. *Step 1, open.* The image of a continuous section of a local homeomorphism over an open set is open ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · isOpen_image_of_section⟧; $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ is a section of $s$ by (2) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_image_Γ⟧, containing $\Gamma(g, y)$ for every $y \in U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_image⟧. *Step 2, connected, disjoint, covering.* $\mathbf U(g)$ is connected as a continuous image of $U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_image_Γ⟧; two sheets are disjoint by the uniqueness in (3) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_inj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Γ⟧; they cover $\mathbf U(x)$ by the existence in (3) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.iUnion_image_Γ⟧, which is therefore open ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_morOn⟧. *Step 3, components.* Open, connected, disjoint and covering, they are the connected components of $\mathbf U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.connectedComponentIn_morOn⟧, and there are $\#G_x$ of them ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.injective_image_Γ⟧. *Step 4.* $s, t : \mathbf U(g) \to U$ are sc-diffeomorphisms, with inverses $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ and $\Gamma(g, \cdot) \circ \Phi(g)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_src_image⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_image⟧. Every $\varphi \in \mathbf U(x)$ has a sheet index $h$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.index⟧ with $\varphi = \Gamma(h, s\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_index⟧ and $t\varphi = \Phi(h)(s\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tgt_eq_Φ_index⟧, locally constant on $\mathbf U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_index_eq⟧. Once $U$ is connected, the text's "choose $U(x)$ so small that $\mathbf U(x)$ splits into $\#G_x$-many components" needs no shrinking. "$\mathbf U(x)$ fits into an arbitrarily small open neighbourhood of $G_x$" belongs to the construction: Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) holds for arbitrary open $N_g \ni g$ (§VII.26) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_2⟧ (2017 p. 231).

**The M-polyfold $G \times U$** (V7.20). "A natural M-polyfold structure as the finite disjoint union of copies of $U$" is the product with a discrete M-polyfold. *Step 1.* A discrete space is an M-polyfold with the charts $\{g\} \to \mathbb R^0$ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · discreteChart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · discretePolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isChart_discreteChart⟧, pairwise compatible because their transitions are the identity of the one-point space or the empty map ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · discreteChart_compatible⟧; every point is smooth ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · discretePolyfold_smoothSet⟧, and a map into it is sc-smooth iff continuous ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScSmoothMap_discrete_iff⟧. *Step 2.* In $G \times X$ the slices $\{g\} \times X$ are open ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isOpen_sheet⟧, $x \mapsto (g, x)$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScSmoothMap_sheet⟧ and the projection of a slice is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScDiffeoOn_snd_sheet⟧, with $d_{G \times X}(g, x) = d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · degIndex_prod_discrete⟧. *Step 3.* Hence a map on $G \times U$ is sc-smooth iff it is on each slice ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScSmoothOn_prod_discrete_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScSmoothOn_univ_prod_discrete_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Discrete · isScSmoothMap_prod_discrete_iff⟧, the text's sheet-by-sheet reading of "$\Gamma$ sc-smooth on $G \times U$". For a natural representation the objects are the open-subset M-polyfold $U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.objPolyfold⟧, the morphisms $G_x \times U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.morPolyfold⟧, and $(g, y) \mapsto g \ast y$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothMap_smul⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 23) (2017 p. 232).

**The translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ is an ep-groupoid** (V7.21). The groupoid has objects $U$, morphisms $G \times U$, $s(g, y) = y$, $t(g, y) = g \ast y$, $(g, h \ast z) \circ (h, z) = (gh, z)$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.translation⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationGroupoid⟧. *(1).* $s$ is the projection, a local sc-diffeomorphism by Step 2 above ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_src⟧; $t$ is the projection after the shear $(g, y) \mapsto (g, g \ast y)$, an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $(g, y) \mapsto (g, g^{-1} \ast y)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.shearHomeomorph⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isLocalScDiffeo_tgt⟧. *(3), for every $V$.* $t$ is the shear followed by the projection $G \times U \to U$, proper because $G_x$ is finite ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isProperMap⟧. *(4), sheet form.* For a local inverse $\sigma$ of $s$, $\sigma(t\psi) \circ \psi = (k(\psi)\psi_1, \psi_2)$ with $k$ locally constant, sc-smooth on each slice ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translation_isScSmoothCompSheet⟧. So $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.translationEpGroupoid⟧, built from $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ alone (2017 p. 232).

**The functor $\Gamma : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$** (V7.22). *Step 1, composition.* $y \mapsto \Gamma(g, h \ast y) \circ \Gamma(h, y)$ and $y \mapsto \Gamma(gh, y)$ are continuous sections of $s$ over $U$ — the first by (4) in the sheet form, for the sheet $\mathbf U(g)$ — with the same value $g \circ h$ at $x$ by (1); on the connected $U$ they agree (§VII.7) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mul⟧. *Step 2.* In the same way $\Gamma(1, y) = 1_y$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_one⟧, and $\Gamma(g^{-1}, g \ast y) = \Gamma(g, y)^{-1}$ by the uniqueness of inverses ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_inv⟧. *Step 3.* So $\Gamma$, the inclusion on objects, is a functor ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.functor⟧, full and faithful by (3) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.full⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.faithful⟧, onto the full subcategory on $U$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.fullSub⟧, and an ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.epFunctor⟧. *Hidden hypothesis:* $U$ connected, without which the sheet index of $\Gamma(g, h \ast y) \circ \Gamma(h, y)$ is only locally constant (2017 p. 232).

**The action $\hat\Phi$ on $\mathbf U(x)$** (V7.23). The text defines $\hat\Phi(g)(\varphi) = \Gamma(ghg^{-1}, g \ast s(\varphi))$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf U(h)$. The formalization defines the total map $\hat\Phi(g)(\varphi) = \Gamma(g, t\varphi) \circ \varphi \circ \Gamma(g, s\varphi)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat⟧ and recovers the text's formula from $\Gamma_{\mathrm{mul}}$ and $\Gamma_{\mathrm{inv}}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_Γ⟧, together with $\Phi(g)\Phi(h)\Phi(g)^{-1} = \Phi(ghg^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_conj⟧. Then $\hat\Phi(g)$ maps $\mathbf U(h)$ onto $\mathbf U(ghg^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_mem_image⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.image_Φhat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.index_Φhat⟧; the two diagrams are $s \circ \hat\Phi(g) = \Phi(g) \circ s$ and $t \circ \hat\Phi(g) = \Phi(g) \circ t$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.src_Φhat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tgt_Φhat⟧; $\hat\Phi(1) = 1$ and $\hat\Phi(gh) = \hat\Phi(g)\hat\Phi(h)$ on $\mathbf U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_one⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φhat_mul⟧; and $\hat\Phi(g)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $\mathbf U(x)$ with inverse $\hat\Phi(g^{-1})$, sc-smooth by (4) in the sheet form and the sc-smoothness of $\iota$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_Φhat⟧ (pp. 294–297 (2017 pp. 232–233)).

### VII.9 Uniqueness and restriction of natural representations

(V7.24.) The text uses without statement that natural representations can be shrunk and compared: "adapting the corresponding restrictions" (Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3)), "$U(x)$ can be chosen so small" ($T_x$, 2017 p. 241). Let $R = (U, \Phi, \Gamma)$ and $R' = (U', \Phi', \Gamma')$ be natural representations at $x$ and $C$ the connected component of $x$ in $U \cap U'$, open and connected (§VII.7) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpen_connectedComponentIn_inter⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isConnected_connectedComponentIn_inter⟧. *Step 1.* $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ and $\Gamma'(g, \cdot)$ are continuous sections of $s$ over $C$ with the value $g$ at $x$, so they agree on $C$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn⟧; applying $t$, $\Phi(g) = \Phi'(g)$ on $C$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn⟧. *Step 2.* $C$ is invariant: $\Phi(g)(C)$ is connected, contains $x$ and lies in $U \cap U'$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_connectedComponentIn⟧. *Step 3.* So a natural representation restricts to every invariant connected open neighbourhood of $x$ inside $U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_restrict⟧, in particular to $C$, where the restrictions of $R$ and $R'$ coincide ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.restrictInter⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.restrictInter_eq⟧, and natural representations exist inside every open $V \ni x$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_shrink⟧. *Step 4.* If $\Phi(g) = 1$ for one natural representation, then $\Phi'(g) = 1$ near $x$ for every one ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_of_actsTrivially⟧. Uniqueness holds on the component $C$; $U \cap U'$ itself need not be connected (Findings, Chapter 7, item 24).

### VII.10 Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) and Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8): the star construction

**Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5)** (V7.25) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15_2017⟧. *Let $Y$ be a finite set of mutually isomorphic objects and $V$ a neighbourhood of $Y$. There is a functor $f$ assigning to every $y \in Y$ a connected open $U(y) \subseteq V$, mutually disjoint, and to every $\psi : y \to y'$ between points of $Y$ an sc-diffeomorphism $f(\psi) : U(y) \to U(y')$, such that the morphisms between points of $\bigcup U(y)$ split into components $\mathbf U(\psi)$ with (1) the natural action of $G_y$ on $U(y)$, (2) $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$, $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y')$ sc-diffeomorphisms, (3) $f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$.* The datum is a structure ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite⟧ (Definition 7.1.18 (2017: 7.8), V7.26), "decomposes into the connected components" being read as: the $\mathbf U(\psi)$ are open, connected, pairwise disjoint and cover; they are then the components ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.connectedComponentIn_morOn⟧ (pp. 295–305 (2017 pp. 233–236)).

**The text's proof** (pp. 297–305 (2017 pp. 234–236)) is an induction on $\#Y$. $\#Y = 1$ is Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1). For $Y = \{y_1, y_2\}$ it fixes $\gamma_1 : y_1 \to y_2$ with a sheet and $\hat\gamma_1 = t \circ (s|\cdot)^{-1}$, takes a $G_{y_1}$-invariant connected $U(y_1)$ with $\hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$ inside a $G_{y_2}$-invariant $W(y_2)$, puts $U(y_2) = \hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$ and shows it invariant; the other morphisms $y_1 \to y_2$ are $g \circ \gamma_1$, $g \in G_{y_2}$, with components $\Phi_g(\mathbf U(\gamma_1))$, $\Phi_g(\varphi) = \Gamma(g, t\varphi) \circ \varphi$, and the morphisms $y_2 \to y_1$ get the inverse components. For $Y = Y' \cup \{y_{k+1}\}$ it fixes $\delta_j : y_{k+1} \to y_j$, shrinks as in the case of two objects, and adjusts the components of the morphisms of $Y'$ to $(s|\mathbf U'(\gamma))^{-1}(U(y_i))$, showing $t(\mathbf U(\gamma)) = U(y_j)$.

**The formalized proof** (V7.25) is a *star*: everything is transported from one base object, and nothing is shrunk afterwards. *Step 1, transport along a sheet.* Let $R = (U, \Phi, \Gamma)$ be a natural representation at $x$ and $\mathbf S_1, \mathbf S_2$ sheets of morphisms out of $x$ with local inverses $a_i = (s|\mathbf S_i)^{-1}$ and $U \subseteq s(\mathbf S_i)$, $\hat\gamma_i = t \circ a_i$. The images $\hat\gamma_i(U)$ are open and connected ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isOpen_transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isConnected_transportSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_hat_transportSet⟧, $\hat\gamma_i^{-1}$ is the inverse there ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.back⟧, and the conjugates $\hat\gamma_2 \circ \Phi(g) \circ \hat\gamma_1^{-1}$ are sc-diffeomorphisms compatible with composition ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap_conjMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.conjMap_one⟧. The transported morphisms are $\Theta_g(z) = a_2(\Phi(g)u) \circ \Gamma(g, u) \circ a_1(u)^{-1}$, $u = \hat\gamma_1^{-1}(z)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport⟧, with source $z$ and target $\hat\gamma_2(\Phi(g)u)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.src_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.tgt_transport⟧, equal to $\gamma_2 \circ g \circ \gamma_1^{-1}$, $\gamma_i = a_i(x)$, at the point $\hat\gamma_1(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport_hat_self⟧, sc-smooth by (4) in the sheet form, used twice, and the sc-smoothness of $\iota$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScSmoothOn_transport⟧. *Step 2, the bijection.* A morphism $k$ from $\hat\gamma_1(U)$ to $\hat\gamma_2(U)$ pulls back to the morphism $a_2(\cdot)^{-1} \circ k \circ a_1(\cdot)$ between points of $U$, which is $\Gamma(g, u)$ for a unique $g$ by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1); so $k = \Theta_g(sk)$ for a unique $g$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.existsUnique_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transport_injective⟧. *Step 3, a natural representation at $y$.* For $\gamma : x \to y$, $h \mapsto \gamma^{-1}h\gamma$ is an isomorphism $G_y \to G_x$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportConj⟧, and $U(y) = \hat\gamma(U)$, $\Phi_y(h) = \hat\gamma \circ \Phi(\gamma^{-1}h\gamma) \circ \hat\gamma^{-1}$, $\Gamma_y(h, \cdot) = \Theta_{\gamma^{-1}h\gamma}$ is a natural representation at $y$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_U⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_Φ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.transportRep_Γ⟧, after shrinking $R$ (same $\Phi$, $\Gamma$) into $s$ of a sheet of $\gamma$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.exists_spoke⟧. *Step 4, the star.* Fix one $x$ isomorphic to all of $Y$, morphisms $\gamma_y : x \to y$ with sheets $\mathbf K_y$, and by Hausdorff separation of the finite $Y$ pairwise disjoint open $W_y \ni y$; take $U_0 = \bigcap_y (s(\mathbf K_y) \cap \hat\gamma_y^{-1}(W_y \cap V))$ and a natural representation inside $U_0$ (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.exists_star⟧. Then $U(y) = \hat\gamma_y(U(x)) \subseteq W_y \cap V$ are pairwise disjoint. *Step 5, the functor.* $\psi \mapsto g_\psi = \gamma_{y'}^{-1} \circ \psi \circ \gamma_y \in G_x$ is a bijection from the morphisms $y \to y'$ onto $G_x$ compatible with composition, units and inverses ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_inv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.g_isotropy⟧; $f(\psi) = \hat\gamma_{y'} \circ \Phi(g_\psi) \circ \hat\gamma_y^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F⟧ is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.isScDiffeoOn_F⟧ and a functor, since $\psi \mapsto g_\psi$ is one and $\Phi$ is a homomorphism ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.F_unit⟧. *Step 6, the components.* $\mathbf U(\psi) = \Theta_{g_\psi}(U(y))$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.Θ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.sheet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.mem_sheet⟧ are pairwise disjoint ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.pairwiseDisjoint_sheet⟧ and cover the morphisms between points of $\bigcup U(y)$, by Step 2 ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.morOn_eq⟧; $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms on them, as images of sections ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_src_image_of_section⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_tgt_image_of_section⟧, and $t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1} = f(\psi)$. *Step 7, (1).* The natural representation of $G_y$ on $U(y)$ is the transported one of Step 3, whose $\Phi_y$ is $f$ on $G_y$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.Star.toNaturalRepFinite⟧; by §VII.9 it agrees near $y$ with every other one. The text instead chooses $U(y)$ invariant under a natural representation of $G_y$ given beforehand. The text's case of two objects already has this form ($U(y_2) = \hat\gamma_1(U(y_1))$); the adjustment of the components of $Y'$ in the inductive step has no counterpart. "A neighbourhood $V$ of $Y$" is a neighbourhood of the set ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15_of_mem_nhdsSet⟧, reduced to an open one; $Y = \emptyset$ is allowed ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.emptyNaturalRepFinite⟧, and enlarging $V$ keeps a datum ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRepFinite · EpGroupoid.NatRepFinite.mono⟧. "Mutually isomorphic" is used only through one $x$ isomorphic to all of $Y$. Among the possible misprints of the proof (Findings, Chapter 7, item 26): "$\Phi_g$" for $g \in G_{y_1}$ where $t(\varphi) \in U(y_2)$ requires $G_{y_2}$; "$\mathbf U(\gamma_g) := \Psi_g(\mathbf U(\gamma_1))$" for $\Phi_g$; the induction step "let $k \ge 3$", which must start at $k \ge 2$ to reach $\#Y = 3$; "$\varphi = \Gamma(g, s(\varphi)) \circ \psi$" for $\Gamma(g, t(\psi)) \circ \psi$; "$y : \mathbf U(\delta_j) \to U(y_j)$" for $t$; and "$g \in G_{y_i}$" for $G_{y_j}$ on 2017 p. 236 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 25, 26).

### VII.11 Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6) and Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9): $|U(x)| = G_x\backslash U(x)$, local uniformizers

**Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6)** (V7.27) ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19⟧. *For a natural representation at $x$, $\tau : G_x\backslash U(x) \to |U(x)| = \pi(U(x))$, $G_x \ast y \mapsto |y|$, is a homeomorphism.* $G_x\backslash U(x)$ is the orbit space of the action $g \ast y$ with the quotient topology. **The text's proof**: $\tau$ is well defined and onto; it is injective because a morphism $\varphi : y \to y'$ is $\Gamma(g, y)$ by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1), so $y' = g \ast y$; $|U(x)|$ is open by Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1); and $\tau \circ \sigma = \pi|U(x)$ for the open quotient map $\sigma$, so $\tau$ is continuous and open. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* $|y| = |y'|$ iff $y' = g \ast y$ for some $g$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_eq_π_iff_exists_smul⟧. *Step 2.* $\tau$ as a map into $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.orbitQuotientMap⟧ is continuous by the quotient topology and injective by Step 1. *Step 3, open.* The image of an open $Q$ is $\pi(\sigma^{-1}(Q))$, and $\sigma^{-1}(Q)$ is open in the open $U(x)$, so Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) applies; the openness of $\sigma$ is not needed. So $\tau$ is an open embedding into $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_orbitQuotientMap⟧ with range $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_orbitQuotientMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19_apply_mk⟧. *The second form.* The functor $G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$ of §VII.8 is fully faithful ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19_fullyFaithful⟧, and the same argument for the orbit space of the translation groupoid, whose classes are the same orbits, gives an open embedding with range $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_orbitMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_functor_orbitMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_19_orbitMap⟧, with $|U(x)|_{G_x \ltimes U(x)} \cong G_x\backslash U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.translationOrbitHomeomorph⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 27) (pp. 299–306 (2017 pp. 236–237)).

**Definition 7.1.20 (2017: 7.9)** (V7.28). A local uniformizer around $x$ is a fully faithful functor $\Psi_x : G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$, the inclusion on objects, inducing a homeomorphism of $|U(x)|_{G_x \ltimes U(x)}$ onto the open $\pi(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer⟧. "Embedding" is not a separate field: the injectivity on objects and morphisms, which the text notes after the definition, follows from the inclusion on objects and faithfulness ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_obj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.injective_mor⟧; for the uniformizers built from natural representations it is also topological, $\Psi_x$ being an open embedding on objects and on morphisms ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_obj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_functor_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_functor_mor⟧. "There exists a local uniformizer around every object": every natural representation is one ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.toLocalUniformizer⟧, and one exists inside every open $V \ni x$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.exists_localUniformizer⟧; its orbit map is a homeomorphism onto the open $|U(x)|$ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.isOpen_image⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Uniformizer · EpGroupoid.LocalUniformizer.orbitHomeomorph⟧. "$\Psi_x \circ G_x \ltimes U(x) \to X$" is read with $:$, and "a a local uniformizer" has a doubled article (possible misprints; Findings, Chapter 7, item 28) (2017 p. 237).

### VII.12 Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10), the M-polyfold $\mathbf A$, and Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7)

**Definition 7.1.21 (2017: 7.10)** (V7.29). An ep-subgroupoid is the full subcategory on a set $A$ of objects which is a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.3.18 (2017: 2.12), §II.10) and saturated ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsEpSubgroupoid⟧. Witnesses: $X$ itself ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_univ⟧, every saturated open set ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_of_isOpen⟧, the saturation of every open set, open by Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_saturation⟧, and every sub-M-polyfold of a trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_trivial⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 40, 105) (2017 p. 237).

**The facts (1)–(4) on $A$** (V7.30). By Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (2017: 2.6) (§II.10), $A$ has an M-polyfold structure ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subObjPolyfold⟧ with (1) the inclusion sc-smooth and a homeomorphism onto its image ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subObj⟧ and (2) $i^{-1} \circ r$ sc-smooth for every sc-smooth retraction $r$ onto $A \cap V$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subObj⟧. The tangent facts (3), (4) — $T_aA$ a closed, sc-complemented subspace of $T_aX$, and $T_aA = Tr(a)T_aX$ — are proved in §VII.44 with the linear structure of tangent spaces ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.fact_4_subObj⟧; in a chart they are Part I's ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_3_19_three⟧, and nothing below uses them (gap G.70, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, items 40, 154) (2017 pp. 237–238).

**$\mathbf A$ is a sub-M-polyfold** (V7.31). The text takes, for $\varphi \in \mathbf A$ with $a = s(\varphi)$, a sheet $s : \mathbf U(\varphi) \to U(a)$ and a retraction $r$ of $U(a)$ onto $U(a) \cap A$, and shows that $\mathbf r = (s|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1} \circ r \circ s$ retracts $\mathbf U(\varphi)$ onto $\mathbf U(\varphi) \cap \mathbf A$. *Step 1, saturation.* For saturated $A$, $t(\varphi) \in A$ iff $s(\varphi) \in A$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.src_mem_of_tgt_mem_of_isSaturated⟧, so $\mathbf A = s^{-1}(A) = t^{-1}(A)$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.morOn_eq_preimage_tgt⟧. *Step 2, a more general statement.* The preimage of a sub-M-polyfold under a local sc-diffeomorphism is one: the retraction is pulled back along a sheet, after shrinking $U(a)$ to $(V \cap V_0) \cap r^{-1}(V \cap V_0)$ so that $r$ maps it into itself ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · isSubMPolyfold_preimage_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_preimage_tgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_morOn⟧. So $\mathbf A$ is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subMorPolyfold⟧ with facts (1), (2) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_val_subMor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_retractInto_subMor⟧; its paracompactness, which the project's M-polyfolds need, is that of a subspace of a metrizable space. The text's "$s(\mathbf r(\psi)) = r(s(\psi)) \in A$ and $t(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in U(a)$" is not used: the second claim does not hold in general as we read it, $t(\mathbf r(\psi))$ lying near $t(\varphi)$ rather than near $a$, and $s(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in A$ with saturation gives $t(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in A$ (possible misprint or extraction artefact for $s(\mathbf r(\psi)) \in U(a)$; Findings, Chapter 7, item 41) (2017 p. 238).

**Proposition 7.1.22 (2017: 7.7)** (V7.32) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_22⟧. *For a saturated sub-M-polyfold $A$, the full subcategory on $A$ is an ep-groupoid; $A$ and $\mathbf A$ are sub-M-polyfolds, and all structure maps are the restrictions of those of $X$.* The text checks the conditions of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) in a few lines; the formalization supplies the unstated step that *a map into a sub-M-polyfold which is sc-smooth into the ambient M-polyfold is sc-smooth into the sub-M-polyfold*: near a point it is $(i^{-1} \circ r) \circ i \circ f$, by fact (2) ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · isScSmoothOn_subPolyfold_of_val⟧. *(1).* A sheet of $s$ maps $\mathbf U(\varphi) \cap \mathbf A$ onto $U(a) \cap A$; with the unstated step, $s$ and $t$ restrict to local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_fullSub_tgt⟧. *(2).* $u$ and $\iota$ are restrictions ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_fullSub_inv⟧. *(3).* The text uses a $U(a)$ with the natural $G_a$-action and $t$ proper over $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_XU(a))$ and notes that $U(a) \cap A$ is invariant; the invariance is not used, and any $V(a)$ of Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) works with $V(a) \cap A$: a sequence with sources in $\mathrm{cl}_A(V(a) \cap A) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XV(a)$ and convergent targets in $A$ has a subsequence converging in $\mathbf X$ (§VII.2), whose source lies in $A$ by saturation and in $\mathrm{cl}_A(V(a) \cap A)$ since this set is closed in $A$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_fullSub⟧. *(4), literally.* The inclusion $\mathbf A\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf A \to \mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X$ is sc-smooth between the fibred products of Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15), by the unstated step applied twice, and $m$ of $A$ is $m$ of $X$ composed with it ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.fullSub_comp_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_fullSub⟧. So the full subcategory is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid⟧ whose structure maps are the restrictions ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_src_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpGroupoid_comp_val⟧, and the inclusion is a full and faithful ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_full⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoid · EpGroupoid.subEpFunctor_faithful⟧, which the text does not state. *Hidden hypotheses:* none; the paracompactness of $A$ and $\mathbf A$ is proved (Findings, Chapter 7, item 42) (pp. 306–308 (2017 pp. 238–239)).

### VII.13 Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11), Lemmas 7.2.2 and 7.2.3 (2017: 7.2 and 7.3)

**Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11)** (V7.33). $X$ is *effective* if for every $x$, every $g \in G_x \setminus \{1_x\}$ and every open neighbourhood $\mathbf U(g)$ there is $\psi \in \mathbf U(g)$ with $s(\psi) \ne t(\psi)$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsEffective⟧; $x$ is *regular* if $G_x = \{1_x\}$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.IsRegular⟧, and $X_{reg}$ is the set of regular objects ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.regularSet⟧. "If $s(\varphi)$ is regular, so is $t(\varphi)$": conjugation with $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of isotropy groups (§VII.6) ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.isRegular_tgt_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isRegular_tgt_of_isRegular_src⟧, so $X_{reg}$ is saturated ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_regularSet⟧. The definition is satisfiable non-vacuously, by $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $\mathbb R$ by reflection (§VII.30) ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isEffective_reflection_nonvacuous⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 50, 101) (2017 p. 239).

**Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2)** (V7.34) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_2⟧. *$X_{reg}$ is open.* For regular $x$ and a natural representation at $x$, every morphism $\varphi : a \to b$ between points of $U(x)$ is $\Gamma(1_x, a)$ by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1), and $\Gamma(1_x, a) = 1_a$ (§VII.8); so $b = a$, $\varphi = 1_a$, and $G_a$ is trivial. The formalization proves the stronger statement that $U(x) \subseteq X_{reg}$ for *every* natural representation at a regular $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.subset_regularSet⟧. *Hidden hypothesis:* $\Gamma(1, a) = 1_a$, which needs $U(x)$ connected. "Examples show that the regular set can be empty" is the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action (§VII.30) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 51) (p. 308 (2017 p. 239)).

**Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3)** (V7.35) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_3⟧. *Equivalent: (1) $X$ is effective; (2) every open $V(x)$ contains a natural representation with $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x))$ injective.* Injectivity is read as "$\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on $U$ only for $g = 1$" ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.injective_Φ_iff⟧, the triviality of the kernel of $G_x \to \mathrm{Perm}(U)$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_kerΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_bot_iff_injective⟧. **The text's proof.** (1) ⇒ (2) by contradiction: if $\Phi(h) = 1$ with $h \ne 1$, effectiveness gives $\varphi_k \to h$ with $s(\varphi_k) \ne t(\varphi_k)$; $\varphi_k = \Gamma(h_k, s\varphi_k)$ with $h_k \ne h$, after a subsequence $h_k = g$, and in the limit $h = \Gamma(g, x) = g$. (2) ⇒ (1): $\Phi(g) \ne 1$ gives $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$, and $\Gamma(g, a)$ has $s \ne t$; "by taking smaller and smaller neighborhoods $U(x)$ and adapting the corresponding restrictions of $\Gamma$" one finds such morphisms converging to $g$. **The formalized proof.** *(1) ⇒ (2), for every natural representation, without sequences* ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.IsEffective.eq_one⟧. If $\Phi(h) = 1$ on $U$, the sheet $\Gamma(h, U)$ is an open neighbourhood of $h$ on which $s = t$, since $t(\Gamma(h, y)) = \Phi(h)(y) = y$; effectiveness forces $h = 1$. So effectiveness is the injectivity of every natural representation ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_forall_naturalRep⟧, and natural representations exist inside every $V(x)$ (§VII.9). *(2) ⇒ (1).* Fix one natural representation $R_0 = (U_0, \Phi_0, \Gamma_0)$, $g \ne 1$ and an open $\mathbf U(g)$. *Step 1.* Apply (2) once, to $V = \{y \in U_0 \mid \Gamma_0(g, y) \in \mathbf U(g)\}$, open and containing $x$. *Step 2.* The natural representation $R$ that (2) gives inside $V$ has $\Phi(g) \ne 1$, so some $a \in U$ has $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$. *Step 3.* $R$ need not be a restriction of $R_0$, as we read "adapting the corresponding restrictions"; it agrees with $R_0$ on the component of $x$ in $U \cap U_0 = U$, i.e. on $U$ (§VII.9) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_eqOn_of_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_eqOn_of_subset⟧. *Step 4.* So $\Gamma_0(g, a) = \Gamma(g, a) \in \mathbf U(g)$ has source $a$ and target $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$. One application of (2) suffices (Findings, Chapter 7, item 52) (pp. 307–309 (2017 pp. 239–240)).

### VII.14 Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8)

**Proposition 7.2.4 (2017: 7.8)** (V7.36) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_4⟧. *If $X$ is effective, $X_{reg}$ is open and dense.* **The text's proof**: in a $U(x_0)$ take $x$ with $\#G_x$ minimal; if $\#G_x > 1$, Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3) gives $U(x) \subseteq U(x_0)$ with $\Phi$ injective and, for $g \ne 1$, a point $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$; $G_a$ is isomorphic to $H = \{h \in G_x \mid \Phi(h)(a) = a\}$, so $\#G_x \le \#G_a = \#H \le \#G_x$, $H = G_x$, a contradiction. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* For a natural representation at $x$ and $a \in U$, $h \mapsto \Gamma(h, a)$ is an isomorphism from the stabilizer of $a$ onto $G_a$, by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1) and the functoriality of $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy⟧. *Step 2.* Given a nonempty open $O$, take $x \in O$ minimizing $\#G_x$ over $O$ itself, so the text's $U(x_0)$ is not needed. *Step 3.* If $G_x \ne 1$, take a natural representation inside $O$ (§VII.9), injective by Lemma 7.2.3 (2017: 7.3), $g \ne 1$ and $a \in U$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$; then $\#G_a = \#\mathrm{Stab}(a) < \#G_x$, contradicting minimality. So $O$ meets $X_{reg}$; openness is Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2). Only $\#G_a < \#G_x$ is used. *The converse* holds too, and is not in the text ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_of_dense_regularSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_dense_regularSet⟧: if $X_{reg}$ is dense and $g \ne 1$, a regular $a$ near $x$ with $\Gamma(g, a)$ in a given $\mathbf U(g)$ has $\Gamma(g, a) \ne 1_a = \Gamma(1, a)$, so $s \ne t$ there (Findings, Chapter 7, item 53) (pp. 308–311 (2017 pp. 240–241)).

### VII.15 The subgroups $T_x$, and Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12)

**$T_x$** (V7.37). $g \in G_x$ *acts trivially* if $\Phi(g) = 1$ for some natural representation ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ActsTrivially⟧, and $T_x$ is the set of such $g$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivialSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.one_mem_trivialSet⟧. The text: since $G_x$ is finite, $U(x)$ can be chosen so small that the kernel of $\Phi$ is $T_x$, a normal subgroup as a kernel. Since sc-smooth maps are not analytic, $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ does not give $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on a connected $U(x)$, so the kernel can depend on $U(x)$; the text's "small" is made precise in three statements. *Step 1, for every representation.* $g \in T_x$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$, for any given natural representation (§VII.9, Step 4) ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.actsTrivially_iff⟧. *Step 2, intrinsically.* $g \in T_x$ iff $s = t$ on a neighbourhood of $g$ in $\mathbf X$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_iff_eventually⟧: one direction is the sheet $\Gamma(g, U)$; for the other, a continuous section of $s$ through $g$ along which $s = t$ near $x$ gives $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSet_of_section⟧. *Step 3, small neighbourhoods.* For one $R_0$, the common fixed set in $U_0$ of the finitely many elements of $T_x$ is a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$, and $\ker\Phi = T_x$ for *every* natural representation inside $N$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_mem_nhds_trivialSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_trivialSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_kerΦ_eq⟧. *Step 4.* So $T_x$ is a kernel, a normal subgroup ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.mem_trivialSubgroup⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_normal⟧, its own normal closure ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.normalClosure_trivialSet⟧, and by Step 2 Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) says exactly $T_x = \{1_x\}$ for all $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_iff_trivialSubgroup_eq_bot⟧. *At nearby points.* For $g \in \ker\Phi$, $\Gamma(g, y) \in T_y$ for $y \in U$, which the proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) uses ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_trivialSet_of_val_eq_Γ⟧. *Along a morphism, not stated in the text.* For $\varphi : x \to y$ and $g \in T_x$, $z \mapsto \theta(z) \circ \Gamma(g, s\theta(z)) \circ \theta(z)^{-1}$, $\theta = (t|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$, is a continuous section of $s$ through $\varphi g \varphi^{-1}$ — by (4) in the sheet form, twice — along which $s = t$ near $y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.exists_conj_section⟧; by Step 2, $\varphi g\varphi^{-1} \in T_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet_iff⟧, and $\varphi T_x\varphi^{-1} = T_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.map_isotropyConj_trivialSubgroup⟧. This is what the descent of the composition to $\mathbf X^R$ needs. "$\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x)$" lacks a parenthesis (possible misprint or extraction artefact). Witnesses: $T_x = 1$ for the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroup_trivial⟧ and the reflection, $T_x = G_x \cong \mathbb Z/3$ for the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action (§VII.30) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 54) (2017 p. 241).

**Definition 7.2.7 (2017: 7.12)** (V7.38). $\mathbf X^T = \bigcup_x T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart⟧; $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $s(\varphi) = s(\varphi') = x$ and $\varphi = \varphi' \circ g$ with $g \in T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel⟧; $\mathbf X^R$ is the set of classes ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.ReducedMor⟧. *Step 1, $\mathbf X^T$ intrinsically.* By §VII.15 Step 2, $\mathbf X^T$ is the interior of $\{\varphi \mid s\varphi = t\varphi\}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_interior⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.val_mem_nonEffectivePart_iff⟧, open ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpen_nonEffectivePart⟧ and closed under units, inverses, composition and conjugation ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.unit_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.inv_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.comp_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.conj_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧. So $\varphi \sim \varphi'$ iff $\varphi = \varphi' \circ k$ with $k \in \mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff⟧, a form without dependent types. *Step 2, an equivalence relation,* because $T_x$ is a subgroup ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_refl⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedSetoid⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedMor_eq_quotient⟧. *Step 3, the left form.* By the conjugation $\varphi T_x\varphi^{-1} = T_y$, $\varphi \sim \psi$ iff $\varphi = k \circ \psi$ with $k \in T_{t\psi}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.exists_comp_left⟧; the relation respects $s$, $t$, $\iota$ and composition on both sides ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.src_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.tgt_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.inv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ReducedRel.comp_right⟧. "The subset $\mathbf X^R$ of reduced morphisms" is a quotient, as the next sentence of the text says (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 55) (2017 p. 241).

### VII.16 Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9): the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$

**Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9)** (V7.39) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10⟧. *$\mathbf X^R$ has a natural M-polyfold structure.* **The text's proof**: $\mathbf X^R$ carries the quotient topology; on a sheet $s : U(\varphi_0) \to U(s\varphi_0)$ the projection $\pi'$ is continuous and injective; its image $U([\varphi_0])$ is open, by the map $\delta(\psi') = \psi' \circ \Gamma(g, s\psi')$ near an equivalent $\psi$, with $U(s\psi)$ chosen with $\ker\Phi = T_{s\psi}$; the same argument shows $\Psi_{\varphi_0} : U(\varphi_0) \to U([\varphi_0])$ open; and the transitions are, near $\varphi$ with $\psi = \varphi \circ g$, the sc-smooth $\delta$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the topology.* The projection $\pi^R : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedπ_eq_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedπ⟧ is a quotient map ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isQuotientMap_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.continuous_reducedπ⟧. *Step 2, $\pi^R$ is open* ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ⟧. The text's $\delta$ composes on the right with a section of $s$; its continuity holds by (4) applied to inverses. The left form is used instead: for $\varphi \sim \psi$, $\varphi = \Gamma(g, t\psi) \circ \psi$ near $\psi$ with $g \in T_{t\psi}$ and a natural representation with $\ker\Phi = T_{t\psi}$ (§VII.15); $\delta(\psi') = \Gamma(g, t\psi') \circ \psi'$ is sc-smooth by (4) in the sheet form ⟦Chapter7/NaturalAction · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScSmoothOn_comp_Γ_tgt⟧ and $\psi' \sim \delta(\psi')$ since $\Gamma(g, t\psi') \in T_{t\psi'}$. So the saturation of an open set is open. *Step 3, sheets.* On every sheet $s : \mathbf W \to V$, $\pi^R$ is injective — equivalent morphisms have the same source — and hence an open embedding ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.injOn_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ_image_Γ⟧; "small" sheets are not needed. *Step 4, charts.* For a chart $\psi$ of $\mathbf X$ with domain in a sheet $\mathbf W$, $\sigma = (s|\mathbf W)^{-1}$, the chart of $\mathbf X^R$ is $[\varphi'] \mapsto \psi(\sigma(s[\varphi']))$ on $\pi^R(\mathrm{dom}\,\psi)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart⟧; every point lies in one ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.exists_chart_sheet⟧. *Step 5, transitions.* On an overlap, an element of the second sheet equivalent to $\varphi'$ has the source $s(\varphi')$, so the text's $\delta$ equals $\sigma_2 \circ s$ and the transition is $\psi_2 \circ \sigma_2 \circ s \circ \psi_1^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart_transition⟧, sc-smooth; what needs the text's argument is that the overlap is open, i.e. Step 2 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.overlap_reducedChart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedChart_compatible⟧. The charts form an atlas ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedCharts⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedAtlas⟧, all without hypotheses. *Step 6, Hausdorff and paracompact.* An M-polyfold is a Hausdorff paracompact space (Definition 2.3.4 (2017: 2.8)). The proof gives neither as we read it, and $\mathbf X^R$ need not be Hausdorff (the example at the end of this paragraph, formalized); so the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$ is built under the hypothesis that $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff, the 2021 text's hypothesis on $T_R$ (§VII.34); paracompactness, a second hypothesis in the first reading, is now an instance, proved for every ep-groupoid as Proposition 7.2.12 ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isChart_reducedChart⟧, and then $\pi^R$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, with inverse $\sigma \circ s$ on $\pi^R(\mathbf W)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedπ⟧ (gap G.71, closed, §§VII.34, VII.48). Steps 1–5 are the 2021 Proposition 7.2.10, with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNaturalCharts · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10_natural_charts⟧. *The hypotheses are satisfiable.* For effective $X$, $\sim$ is equality ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedRel_iff_eq_of_isEffective⟧, $\pi^R$ a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedHomeomorph⟧, and $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff, paracompact and regular ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t3Space_reducedMor_of_isEffective⟧; this covers the trivial ep-groupoid of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_trivial⟧. Paracompactness also follows from regularity of $\mathbf X^R$ when $\mathbf X$ is second countable ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor_of_t3⟧; these partial results of the first reading are superseded by Proposition 7.2.12, which needs no hypothesis. Four possible misprints of the proof: "$\psi' = (s|U(\psi))^{-1}(s(\psi))$" for $s(\psi')$, "$U(\varphi) \subset \Psi_{\varphi_0}(U([\varphi_0]) \cap U([\psi_0]))$" for $\Psi_{\varphi_0}^{-1}$, "$T_x$ agrees with the kernel of the $G_{s(\varphi)}$-action" for $T_{s(\varphi)}$, and a garbled sentence on the smoothness of the source and target maps (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 57, 60, 111) (2017 pp. 242–243). *The Hausdorff hypothesis cannot be dropped* ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.exists_not_t2Space_reducedMor⟧. Let $\mathbb Z/2$ act by $(t, z) \mapsto (t, \pm z)$ on the retract $O$ of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3) example, a point over each $t \le 0$ and a line over each $t > 0$; the action is the restriction of an sc-operator ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.isScSmoothMap_smul⟧. Over $t < 0$ both elements act trivially, so $(-1, (t, 0)) \in \mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.mem_nonEffectivePart⟧; at $(0, 0)$ points of $O$ with $t > 0$ tend to $0$ and are moved by $-1$, so $(-1, (0, 0)) \notin \mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧. The classes of $(\pm 1, (-1/(n+1), 0))$ coincide and converge to both $[(-1, 0)] \ne [(1, 0)]$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_t2Space_reducedMor⟧. So Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017), for every ep-groupoid, do not hold as we read them; the 2021 text takes the Hausdorff hypothesis (Findings, Chapter 7, item 107; found on paper while reading, proved in the round-trip audit).

### VII.17 The reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$, Proposition 7.10 (2017), Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13)

**$X_R$** (V7.40). Objects $X$, morphisms $\mathbf X^R$, $s([\varphi]) = s(\varphi)$, $t([\varphi]) = t(\varphi)$, with unit, inverse and composition descended by §VII.15 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedTgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedInv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedComp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedComp_π⟧, $s$ and $t$ onto ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedTgt⟧, a groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedGroupoidStr⟧; the composition of a non-composable pair is a junk value, as in §VII.1 (2017 p. 243).

**Proposition 7.10 (2017)** (V7.40) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_10_2017⟧. *Under the hypotheses of §VII.16, $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid, and it is effective.* *(1).* For a sheet $\mathbf W$ of Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4), $s, t : \pi^R(\mathbf W) \to X$ are $s \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$ and $t \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$, the text's $s(\Psi_\varphi(\varphi')) = s(\varphi')$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedTgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedTgt⟧. *(2).* $u = \pi^R \circ u_X$ and $\iota = \pi^R \circ \iota_X \circ (\pi^R|\mathbf W)^{-1}$ on $\pi^R(\mathbf W)$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedInv⟧. *(3), "proved similarly".* For the same $V(x)$, $t \circ \pi^R = t_X$ on $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}V(x))$, with $\pi^R$ a continuous surjection onto the corresponding set of $\mathbf X^R$; a map whose composite with a continuous surjection is proper is proper (Mathlib) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_reduced⟧. *(4), "reduced by our local charts",* in the sheet form: for an sc-diffeomorphism $s : \mathbf W' \to V'$ of $\mathbf X^R$ with inverse $\sigma'$, $\kappa = \sigma_2 \circ s \circ \sigma'$ is the inverse of $s$ on an open set of $\mathbf X$ — a step the text leaves implicit — and $m(\sigma'(t\psi), \psi) = \pi^R(m(\kappa(t\psi), \psi))$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_reduced⟧. So $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid⟧ and $X \to X_R$ an ep-functor ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionFunctor⟧. *Effective.* The text's point $a$ with $\Phi(g)(a) \ne a$ is replaced by the intrinsic form of $T_x$: if $s = t$ near $[g]$ in $\mathbf X^R$, then $s = t$ near $g$ in $\mathbf X$, $\pi^R$ being continuous, so $g \in T_x$ and $[g] = [1_x]$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid⟧. For effective $X$, $X_R \cong X$ in $\mathcal{EP}$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionInv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reductionIso⟧. In the 2021 form, Theorem 7.2.14 with Proposition 7.2.16, only the Hausdorff hypothesis remains ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNaturalCharts · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14_reduced⟧ (§VII.48) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 58, 60) (2017 p. 244).

**The isotropy of $X_R$, and Definition 7.2.15 (2017: 7.13)** (V7.41). $g \mapsto [g]$ is a surjective homomorphism from $G_x$ onto the isotropy of $x$ in $X_R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedIsotropyHom⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.surjective_reducedIsotropyHom⟧ with kernel $T_x$ — the text's "$[1_x] = T_x$" ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.ker_reducedIsotropyHom⟧ — so that isotropy is $G_x/T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.quotientTrivialSubgroupEquiv⟧. The effective isotropy group $G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = G_x/T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.EffIsotropy⟧ is defined as the quotient by the normal closure of $T_x$, which is $G_x/T_x$ by §VII.15 ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquiv⟧, and it is the isotropy group of $X_R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.effIsotropyEquivReduced⟧. "For and object" (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 59) (2017 p. 244).

### VII.18 Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2), Lemmas 7.3.2 and 7.3.3 (2017: 7.4 and 7.5)

**Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2)** (V7.42) ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1⟧. *$|X|$ is locally metrizable, regular and Hausdorff; if $|X|$ is paracompact, it is metrizable.* "Locally metrizable" is read as: every point has an open neighbourhood which is metrizable in the subspace topology. The three properties are Lemmas 7.3.2, 7.3.5 and 7.3.4 (2017: 7.4, 7.7 and 7.6). The metrizability ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_3_1_metrizable⟧ is the text's "Nagata/Smirnov" in Part I's form (§II.7): a paracompact Hausdorff locally metrizable space is metrizable ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_locally⟧. The hypothesis "$|X|$ paracompact" is satisfiable, by the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 70) (2017 p. 244).

**Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4)** (V7.43) ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2⟧. *Every $z \in |X|$ has an open metrizable neighbourhood; one can take $|U(x)|$ for a natural representation at $x$.* **The text's proof**: $U$ is metrizable with a metric $d$; $\rho(y, y') = \max_g d(g \ast y, g \ast y')$ is an equivalent $G_x$-invariant metric; $\hat\rho([y], [y']) = \min\{\rho(g \ast y, h \ast y') \mid g, h \in G_x\}$ defines the quotient topology on $G_x\backslash U$; and Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6) carries it to $|U|$. **The formalized proof** follows it, for any finite group acting by homeomorphisms on a metrizable space ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient⟧. *Step 1.* $\rho$ is the maximum over the finite $G_x$ ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · maxDist⟧, invariant ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · maxDist_smul⟧, and $d \le \rho$. *Step 2.* $\hat\rho$ is computed as $\min_h\rho(y, h \ast y')$, the same number by invariance ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · quotDist⟧ ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · quotDist_mk⟧; it is symmetric and satisfies the triangle inequality by invariance, and $\hat\rho([y], [y']) = 0$ forces $y' \in G_x \ast y$, orbits of a finite group being closed. *Step 3, the topology.* A set of $G_x\backslash U$ is open in the quotient topology iff it contains a $\hat\rho$-ball around each of its points: $\{y' \mid \rho(y, y') < \varepsilon\} = \bigcap_g g^{-1}(B_d(g \ast y, \varepsilon))$ is open, and $d \le \rho$ gives the converse. This is Mathlib's construction of a metric space with a prescribed topology; $\rho$ itself is never installed as a metric on $U$. So $G_x\backslash U(x)$ is metrizable ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_naturalRep⟧ and so is $|U(x)|$, its homeomorphic image (§VII.11) ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_2_naturalRep⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 71) (pp. 319–325 (2017 pp. 244–245)).

**Lemma 7.3.3 (2017: 7.5)** (V7.44) ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_3_3⟧. *Every point of $|X|$ has a monotone countable basis of open neighbourhoods.* This is Proposition 7.1.9 (2017: 7.2) (§VII.5), proved there from the metrizability of $X$ and the openness of $\pi$; the text derives it from Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 72) (2017 p. 245).

### VII.19 Lemmas 7.3.4 and 7.3.5 (2017: 7.6 and 7.7), Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1), subsets of $|X|$

The text proves Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6) before Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7); the formalization proves Lemma 7.3.5 (2017: 7.7) first and derives Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6) from it (Findings, Chapter 7, item 72).
