The text takes $\beta_1$, $\beta_2$ with prescribed signs, the graphs $G_1$, $G_2$ with weight $1$, and $\Theta(p) = \#\{i \mid p \in G_i\}$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.thetaGraphs_eq⟧, and says that the graphs of $\gamma_1 = 0$ and of some $\gamma_2$ positive off $0$ describe $\Theta$ too. *Step 1.* The sign conditions are the structure `Remark913Hyp` ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp⟧, satisfied by $\beta_1(s) = e(s)$, $\beta_2(s) = e(-s)$ with Mathlib's `expNegInvGlue` $e$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.remark913Hyp_expNegInvGlue⟧. *Step 2.* For the second structure to describe the same $\Theta$, $\gamma_2$ must be $\beta_1 + \beta_2$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.eq_add_of_thetaGraphs_eq⟧, which is smooth and positive off $0$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.γ₂_pos⟧. The two structures are ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureβ⟧ and ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.structureγ⟧. *Step 3.* "Not unique, even close to $x$" is read as: no sheet of the first structure agrees with a sheet of the second on any neighbourhood of the origin, since each of $\beta_1$, $\beta_2$ differs from $0$ and from $\beta_1 + \beta_2$ at points arbitrarily close to $0$.

**Lemma 9.1.5 (2017: 9.1)** (V9.5) ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_5⟧. *$|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is locally closed in $|X|$.* **The text's proof** takes a neighbourhood with the natural $G_x$-action, the properness property and a local branching structure, and shows that the image of $\bigcup_i M_i$ is closed in the image of $U(x)$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* For a functor the support is saturated, $\pi^{-1}(|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|) = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.preimage_π_orbitSupp⟧. *Step 2.* On $U(x)$ the support is $\bigcup_i M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_supp_iff⟧, a finite union of sets closed in $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_M⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isClosed_preimage_val_supp⟧, so $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is locally closed in $X$ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.isLocallyClosed_supp⟧. *Step 3.* $\pi$ is open (Chapter 7), and the image of the locally closed saturated set is locally closed. The properness property of the text is not used.

**Definitions 9.1.6 and 9.1.8 (2017: 9.2 and 9.3)** (V9.6, V9.8) are read literally ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.IsClosedBranched⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.IsCompactBranched⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.IsOrbifoldType⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.IsManifoldType⟧; the indicator of a point is compact and of manifold type ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.isCompactBranched_indicator⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Basic · EpGroupoid.isManifoldType_indicator⟧. Proposition 9.1.9 and Remark 9.1.10 (natural manifold and orbifold structures on $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$) and Remark 9.1.4 (metrizability, the compactness criterion) are proved in §IX.26 (gaps G.94, G.95, closed).

### IX.3 The restriction remark, and Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2)

**The restriction** (V9.7). Before Lemma 9.1.7 the text replaces $M_i$ by $N_i = M_i \cap V(x_0)$ for $V(x_0) \subseteq U(x)$ and notes that some $N_i$ may be empty. Definition 9.1.2 asks $x \in M_i$, which the $N_i$ need not satisfy at $x_0$; the remark is formalized for an open $V \subseteq U(x)$ containing $x$ itself, which is the case the symmetrization uses ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.restrict⟧. The $N_i$ are submanifolds ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.inter_isOpen⟧, and they are properly embedded in $V$ because they are closed in $U(x)$.

**Lemma 9.1.7 (2017: 9.2)** (V9.7) ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_1_7'⟧. *At $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ there is a local branching structure on the domain of a natural representation of $G_x$, with a $G_x$-action on the index set, $g * M_i = M_{g(i)}$ and $\sigma_{g(i)} = \sigma_i$; it can be found inside every open $V \ni x$.* **The text's proof** sets $J = I \times G_x$, $M_{(i,g)} = g * M_i$, $\sigma_{(i,g)} = \sigma_i / |G_x|$ and computes $\sum_{y \in g * M_i} \sigma_{(i,g)} = \frac{1}{|G_x|} \sum_g \Theta(g^{-1} * y) = \Theta(y)$ by functoriality. **The formalized proof** follows it ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.symmetrize⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure⟧. *Step 1.* Restrict the given structure to the domain $U \subseteq V \cap U(x)$ of a natural representation (Theorem 7.1.13, §VII.4). *Step 2.* $\Phi(g)(M_i \cap U)$ is a submanifold properly embedded in $U$ through $x$, since $\Phi(g)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U$ fixing $x$ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.image_of_isScDiffeoOn⟧; the text uses this without saying so. *Step 3.* The weights: $\Theta(\Phi(g)(y)) = \Theta(y)$ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.apply_Φ⟧ and $y \in \Phi(g)(A) \iff \Phi(g)^{-1}(y) \in A$ ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_image_Φ_iff⟧ turn the text's computation into a sum over $G_x$ with $|G_x|$ = `Nat.card` of the finite group. *Step 4.* $G_x$ acts on $J$ by left multiplication on the second factor ⟦Chapter9/Symmetric · EpGroupoid.mulActionProdLeft⟧.

### IX.4 Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2): the local construction, and the uniqueness

**Proposition 9.1.11 (2017: 9.2)** (V9.9) ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_11⟧. *A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid determines a unique sequence $\Theta_0, \Theta_1, \ldots$ of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids with $\Theta_k$ $k$-dimensional and $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$, locally finite.* The formal statement: for every branched $\Theta$ there is exactly one family $(\Theta_k)$ with `IsDimDecomposition` ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.IsDimDecomposition⟧, every $\Theta_k$ branched and $k$-dimensional, at each object finitely many nonzero and $\Theta$ their sum, and every such family is locally finite ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.IsLocallyFiniteFamily⟧.

**The local construction.** The text splits the indices of a symmetric structure by the dimension of $M_i$ and puts $\Theta_k(y) = \sum_{i \in I_k, y \in M_i} \sigma_i$. Formally, for a labelling $\mathrm{dim}$, $\Theta_k$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart⟧ has the $k$-dimensional local branching structure $(M_i)_{\mathrm{dim}\,i = k}$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartStructure_isOfDim⟧ and $\Theta = \sum_k \Theta_k$ on $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.eq_sum_dimPart⟧; $\Theta_k = 0$ if no sheet has dimension $k$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_eq_zero⟧, and $\Theta_n = \Theta$ for an $n$-dimensional structure ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_eq_of_isOfDim⟧. For a symmetric structure $G_x$ preserves dimension, since $\Phi(g)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dim_smul⟧, so $\Theta_k$ is $G_x$-invariant ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.SymmetricBranchingStructure.dimPart_Φ⟧. That the local $\Theta_k$ does not depend on the structure is Proposition 9.1.12 (§IX.5).

**The uniqueness, as we read it, does not hold** ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.not_proposition_9_1_11_rn⟧. On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^2$, let $L$ be the $x$-axis ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.axis2⟧ and $\Theta = 1_L$. *Family A:* $\Theta_0 = 1_{\{0\}}$, $\Theta_1 = 1_{L \setminus \{0\}}$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.decompA⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.decompA_isDimDecomposition⟧. *Family B:* $\Theta_0 = 0$, $\Theta_1 = 1_L$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.decompB⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.decompB_isDimDecomposition⟧. In family A, $L \setminus \{0\}$ is a $1$-dimensional submanifold properly embedded in the open set $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{0\}$, which is all Definition 9.1.2 asks at its points, and $1_{\{0\}}$ is $0$-dimensional; both families satisfy (1) and (2). The proof of the text constructs family B.

**The repaired uniqueness.** Call a decomposition *local* if near every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ its $\Theta_k$ is the $k$-dimensional part of a local branching structure of $\Theta$, which is what the text's proof produces ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionUnique · IsLocalDimDecomposition⟧. Family B is local and family A is not ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionUnique · decompB_isLocalDimDecomposition⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionUnique · decompA_not_isLocalDimDecomposition⟧. Two local decompositions are equal: near a point of the support both are dimensional parts of structures there, which agree near the point by Proposition 9.1.12, and off the support both vanish ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionUnique · isDimDecomposition_unique⟧. Proposition 9.1.12 now holds on every ep-groupoid (§IX.5), so the uniqueness among local decompositions has no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_11_unique⟧.

**The global decomposition** (gap G.96, closed). *Step 1, the definition.* $\Theta_k(y)$ is the sum of the weights of the $k$-dimensional sheets of a chosen labelled structure at $y$, and $0$ if there is none ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · HasLabelledBranchingAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · dimComponent⟧. Every sheet passes through its base point, so this is the value at $y$ of the local $\Theta_k$ at $y$. *Step 2, independence and locality.* By Proposition 9.1.12, $\Theta_k(x)$ is the same for every labelled structure at $x$ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · dimComponent_eq_self⟧, and on all of $U(x)$ it is the $k$-dimensional part of any labelled structure at $x$, restricted to $y$ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · dimComponent_eq_of_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · dimPart_restrictAt⟧. *Step 3, functoriality.* Along a morphism $\varphi$, a labelled structure at $s(\varphi)$ is transported to $t(\varphi)$, preserving dimensions ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · isSubmanifoldOfDim_transport⟧, and Step 2 at the target gives $\Theta_k(s(\varphi)) = \Theta_k(t(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · isFunctorial_dimComponent⟧; the text's symmetric structures are not needed. *Step 4, paracompactness*, which the text does not discuss: $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta_k)|$ is closed in $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · isClosed_orbitSupp_dimComponent⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_dimComponent⟧. *Step 5.* So each $\Theta_k$ is a $k$-dimensional branched ep⁺-subgroupoid ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_dimComponent⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · isNDimensional_dimComponent⟧, the family is a local decomposition ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · isLocalDimDecomposition_dimComponent_general⟧, and for every ep-groupoid there is exactly one local decomposition ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general⟧. *Step 6, local finiteness.* At the points of the support only finitely many $\Theta_k$ are nonzero nearby, those of the sheets of one structure ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · dimComponent_locallyFinite_of_mem_general⟧. At points of the closure of the support outside it, the formalization needs a bound on the dimensions of the submanifolds of $X$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_11_local_of_le⟧, which holds on $\mathbb R^m$ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · rn_hasDimAt_le⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · proposition_9_1_11_local_rn⟧. For the line $L$ the construction gives family B ⟦Chapter9/DimDecompositionExists · dimComponent_axis2⟧. Row V9.9 is narrower for these two reasons: "uniquely" is read among local decompositions, and local finiteness off the support uses the bound.

### IX.5 Proposition 9.1.12: the statement and its cases

**Proposition 9.1.12** (V9.10) ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.Proposition_9_1_12⟧, new in the 2021 edition. *For two local branching structures of $\Theta$ on $U(x)$ there is an open $G_x$-invariant $V(x) \subseteq U(x)$ on which the dimensional decompositions agree.* The formal conclusion is `DimPartsAgreeNear`: an open $V \ni x$ in both domains on which $\Theta_k = \Theta'_k$ for every $k$ ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear⟧. "$G_x$-invariant, with the usual properties" is obtained by shrinking $V$ to the domain of a natural representation ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.DimPartsAgreeNear.exists_naturalRep⟧. *The equidimensional case* is immediate, since then $\Theta_n = \Theta$ for both ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_isOfDim⟧. The general case is proved in Appendix §9.6.1 (§§IX.21–IX.22): under the hypothesis `TopMultiplicity` ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity⟧, under the graph representation ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧, without hypothesis on every ep-groupoid over $\mathbb R^m$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn⟧, and now without hypothesis on every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_12⟧: `TopMultiplicity` holds on every M-polyfold, by the slice argument of §IX.22 run with one cone per tangent space (§IX.27) ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicity⟧. Mixed structures exist: $\Theta = 1 + \delta_0$ on $\mathbb R^1$ has sheets of dimensions $0$ and $1$ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · exists_mixed_rn_one⟧, and on $\mathbb R^2$ two labelled structures of one $\Theta$ with sheets of dimensions $1$ and $0$ have different sheets and agreeing dimensional parts ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_mixed_rn_two⟧.

### IX.6 The category $\mathrm{Gr}(X)$, and the tangent spaces $T_yM$

**$T_yM$** (V9.12). Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (preprint: 4.14) defines $T_yM = Tr(y)(T_yX)$ for an sc⁺-retraction $r$ with image $M$ near $y$. Here $T_yM$ is the set of tangent vectors at $y$ fixed by the tangent of $r$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent⟧. *Step 1.* It does not depend on the retraction ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldTangent_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_congr⟧, lies in the fibre over $y$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_subset_tangentFiber⟧, is local ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_inter_isOpen⟧, and is mapped onto $T_{f(y)}f(M)$ by an sc-diffeomorphism $f$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_image⟧. *Step 2, the chart form.* In a chart the second components of the images of $T_yM$ form a set ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.chartTangent⟧ equal to the tangent space of the chart model of $M$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.chartTangent_eq⟧, a linear subspace ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.exists_submodule_chartTangent⟧ of dimension $\dim_yM$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.finrank_chartTangent⟧; a chart change acts on it by a continuous linear map ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.exists_clm_tangentChartMap_snd⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.chartTangent_chart_change⟧, a linear isomorphism ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.exists_linearEquiv_chartTangent⟧. So the generators $T_xM_i$ of $T_\Theta(x)$ are linear subspaces in every chart ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_submodule_of_mem_support⟧, which is what the text means by "finite-dimensional linear subspaces of $T_xX$".

**$\mathrm{Gr}(X)$** (V9.11). $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ is the additive group of finitely supported $\mathbb Q$-valued functions on subsets of $T_xX$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.Gr⟧, a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ acts by the image under its tangent $T\varphi$ (Chapter 7) ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grPush⟧, with $T1_x = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_unit_of_eq⟧ and $T\varphi$ injective on the fibre ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_injOn⟧; the push-forward is functorial ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grPush_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grPush_unit⟧. The objects $(x, a)$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.GrObj⟧ form a category over the full subcategory $X^\infty$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.SmoothCat⟧ with the projection $\pi$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grProj⟧.

### IX.7 Good points: Definitions 9.2.2 and 9.2.6 (2017: 9.4 and 9.5), Lemmas 9.2.3 and 9.2.5 (2017: 9.3 and 9.4), Remark 9.2.4 (2017: 9.4)

**Definition 9.2.2 (2017: 9.4)** (V9.15) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsGoodPoint⟧. $y \in M_U$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.MU⟧ is good if there is an open $V(y) \subseteq U(x)$ on which all sheets through $y$ coincide. The text states this for equidimensional $\Theta$; no proof below uses equidimensionality, so the definition and Lemmas 9.2.3 and 9.2.5 are stated for every $\Theta$ with a local branching structure.

**The intrinsic form** ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isGoodPoint_iff⟧. *For $y \in U(x)$: $y$ is good iff $y \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $\Theta$ is constant on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ near $y$.* *Step 1.* Near $y$ take $V$ in the complement of the sheets not through $y$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.nbhdAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isOpen_nbhdAt⟧; there $\Theta(z) \le \Theta(y)$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.le_of_mem_nbhdAt⟧, with equality iff $z$ lies on all sheets through $y$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.eq_iff_of_mem_nbhdAt⟧. *Step 2.* If all sheets through $y$ coincide on $V$, $\Theta$ is $\Theta(y)$ on $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap V$; conversely, if $\Theta$ is constant on the support near $y$, every point of a sheet through $y$ near $y$ lies on all of them, by Step 1.

**Lemma 9.2.3 (2017: 9.3)** (V9.16) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_2_3⟧ follows at once, for any two structures, at possibly different points, whose domains contain $y$: the intrinsic form does not mention the structure. This is the text's argument, in which $Q(z) = V(y) \cap W(y)$ is presumably $Q(y)$.

**Remark 9.2.4 (2017: 9.4)** (V9.17). (a) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_a⟧ is Lemma 9.2.3 with the good set of Definition 9.2.6 ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.mem_goodSet_iff⟧. (b) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.remark_9_2_4_b⟧: near a good $y$, $\Theta = \Theta(y) \cdot 1_M$ with $M = M_i \cap V(y)$ for any $i \in I_y$, properly embedded in $V(y)$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.restrictAt⟧.

**Lemma 9.2.5 (2017: 9.4)** (V9.18) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_5⟧. *$s(\varphi)$ is good iff $t(\varphi)$ is good.* The text transports local branching structures along morphisms. The formal proof uses the intrinsic form and the sheet of $\varphi$: on a sheet $\mathbf W$ of $s$ around $\varphi$, $\hat\varphi = t \circ (s|\mathbf W)^{-1}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism between open neighbourhoods of $s(\varphi)$ and $t(\varphi)$ with $\Theta \circ \hat\varphi = \Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.Sheet.apply_hat⟧, so "$\Theta$ constant on the support near the point" passes from one to the other ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.src_mem_goodSet_of_tgt⟧.

**Definition 9.2.6 (2017: 9.5)** (V9.19) ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.goodSet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.badSet⟧. Both sets are saturated ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.preimage_π_image_goodSet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.preimage_π_image_badSet⟧, by Lemma 9.2.5. The text cites "Remark 9.2.4 (c)" here; the remark has (a) and (b), and Lemma 9.2.5 is what the descent to $|X|$ uses.

### IX.8 Lemma 9.2.7 (2017: 9.5): good points are dense and accumulate on every sheet

**Lemma 9.2.7 (1) (2017: 9.5 (1))** (V9.20). The openness of the good set in $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is the definition ⟦Chapter9/GoodPoints · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1⟧. **The text** derives the density from (2). **The formalized proof** needs neither (2) nor equidimensionality ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_1_dense⟧. *Step 1.* Given an open $W \subseteq U(x)$ meeting the support, shrink $W$ one sheet at a time so that $M_U \cap W$ either lies in $M_j$ or misses it ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · exists_isOpen_subset_inter_eq_empty_or_subset⟧: if $M_U \cap W \not\subseteq M_j$, a point of $M_U \cap W$ off the closed set $M_j$ has a neighbourhood in $W$ missing $M_j$, and the sheets already decided stay decided. *Step 2.* On the final $W$ every sheet through a point of $M_U \cap W$ contains $M_U \cap W$, so all sheets through it agree on $W$ and it is good. So the good set is dense ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.dense_goodSet⟧ and the bad set nowhere dense ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.isNowhereDense_badSet⟧.

**Lemma 9.2.7 (2) (2017: 9.5 (2))** (V9.21) ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2⟧. *For an $n$-dimensional structure at $x$ and every $i$, good points of $M_i$ converge to $x$.* **The text's proof** fixes $i_0$, sets $\Sigma_i = M_i \cap M_{i_0} \cap D_k(x)$ and either finds a point of $M_{i_0} \cap D_k(x)$ off all $\Sigma_i$ or moves a point off the boundaries of those $\Sigma_i$ with interior; such a point is "clearly" good. **The formalized proof** does this with Step 1 above applied inside $M_{i_0}$. The point found is good only if $M_{i_0} \subseteq M_i$ near it forces $M_{i_0} = M_i$ near it, which is invariance of domain for submanifolds of equal dimension. It was first the hypothesis `HasDomainInvarianceAt` ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · MPolyfold.HasDomainInvarianceAt⟧, proved on $\mathbb R^m$ by the inverse function theorem ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · MPolyfold.hasDomainInvarianceAt_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_2_7_2_rn⟧. It now holds on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasDomainInvarianceAt⟧: in a chart both submanifolds are the ranges of chart sc⁺-retractions, and two such retracts with the same tangent space at the point, one inside the other, agree near it ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · eq_of_range_eq⟧ (§IX.27). So Lemma 9.2.7 (2) holds for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_2_7_2_general⟧ (gap G.98, closed). The statement holds at every $x$, not only at bad points. In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the origin is bad ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.zero_mem_badSet⟧ and is approached by good points on each graph ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.exists_seq_goodSet_structureβ⟧.

### IX.9 Proposition 9.2.8 and Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: 9.3 and 9.6–9.8): graph charts and tangent slices

**The text.** At a bad point $x$ the indices with the same $T_xM_i = L$ form a class $\Xi$. Locally, $x = 0$ in a partial quadrant $C$; $L \cap C$ has interior in $L$ (Lemma 9.2.9); the $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, are graphs $a + B_i(a)$ over a cone around a unit $h_0$ in that interior, with an sc-complement $Z$ of $L$ (Lemma 9.2.10), through the inversion of a map $\Phi$ on the cone (Lemma 9.2.11). Proposition 9.2.8 then splits $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$ with sequences of good points $x^e_k \to x$ lying on $M_i$ exactly for $i \in I^e$, and the proof of Theorem 9.2.1 counts $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i = \sum_e \Theta(x^e_k)$.

**What the count needs.** One finite set $F$ near $x$ that meets each $M_i$, $i \in \Xi$, exactly once and misses the other sheets, so that $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i = \sum_{y \in F} \Theta(y)$: a *tangent slice* ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · MPolyfold.HasTangentSlicesAt⟧. The sequences of Proposition 9.2.8 are one way to produce such sets; a slice needs only one good direction $h_0 \in L$, off the finitely many other tangent spaces. So Proposition 9.2.8 is formalized in this slice form (V9.22).

**The graph representation, first as a hypothesis.** Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 rest on sc-calculus at level $0$ inside a partial quadrant (sc-complements, the mean value formula for sc⁺-retractions, an inverse function theorem on a cone). In the first version of this part their content in a chart was the hypothesis `IsGraphChartAt`, which is now proved on every M-polyfold (§IX.27; gap G.97, closed): every $n$-dimensional submanifold through $x$ is, along each admissible ray $t h$ of its tangent space, met by the affine fibre through $t h$, with secants uniformly approximated by $T_xM$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.IsGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.HasGraphChartsAt⟧. Rays replace the cones of Lemma 9.2.10, and the admissible directions play the role of $C$. *From graphs to slices* ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_of_hasGraphChartsAt⟧: with $Q$ a projection onto $L$, the slice is $\{y \mid Q(\varphi y - \varphi x) = t h_0,\ \|\varphi y - \varphi x - t h_0\| < \varepsilon t\}$ for small $t$; it meets each sheet of the class once, by the graph property, and misses the other sheets, since their tangent spaces do not contain $h_0$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · exists_mem_ball_forall_not_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesBasic · eq_zero_of_proj_eq_zero⟧. *On $\mathbb R^m$* the graph representation holds at every point and in every dimension ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · MPolyfold.isGraphChartAt_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · MPolyfold.hasGraphChartsAt_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · MPolyfold.hasTangentSlicesAt_rn⟧: a submanifold is near $x$ the image of a smooth retraction $s$, and the inverse function theorem for $Q \circ s$ restricted to $L$ gives the graph ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · exists_mem_graph_of_hasStrictFDerivAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · MPolyfold.rn_exists_retraction⟧.

**One chart for all dimensions.** For Proposition 9.6.5 and the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 without equidimensionality, the sheets of all dimensions through $x$ must be compared in one chart: `HasGraphChartAt` asks one chart and one set of admissible directions for all of them ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.HasGraphChartAt.hasGraphChartsAt⟧, which holds on $\mathbb R^m$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.hasGraphChartAt_rn⟧. In it, every class has slices inside every neighbourhood ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.exists_slice_of_isGraphChartAt⟧, which can be chosen to miss finitely many given submanifolds of smaller dimension ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.exists_generic_slice⟧. For Lemma 9.3.4 good points must be found near the slice, which a ray does not provide; the ball form `HasGraphBallAt` asks the graph property over a ball of foot points ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.HasGraphBallAt.hasGraphChartsAt⟧, again true on $\mathbb R^m$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · hasGraphBallAt_rn⟧. On a general M-polyfold, one cone of admissible directions for all submanifolds through a boundary point is more than the slice arguments use: they need a cone for each tangent space separately, `HasClassGraphChartAt` ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · HasClassGraphChartAt⟧, which holds at every point ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasClassGraphChartAt⟧; the stronger `HasGraphChartAt` and `HasGraphBallAt` hold at interior points ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasGraphChartAt_of_mem_interior⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior⟧ (§IX.27).

### IX.10 Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1): the section $T_\Theta$

**Theorem 9.2.1 (2017: 9.1)** (V9.13) ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_2_1⟧. *There is a section functor $T_\Theta : X^\infty \to \mathrm{Gr}(X)$, $\pi \circ T_\Theta = \mathrm{Id}$, with $T_\Theta(x) = \sum_i \sigma_i T_xM_i$ for every local branching structure at $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, the zero sum off the support, and $T_\Theta(\varphi) = (T_\Theta(s(\varphi)), \varphi)$.* The theorem is proved in two parts. *Part 1, the section, given the independence.* Write $\sum_i \sigma_i T_xM_i$ as an element of $\mathrm{Gr}(x)$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum⟧. If any two structures at $x$ give the same sum ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.HasIndependentTangentSums⟧, $T_\Theta(x)$ is that sum for a chosen structure, and $0$ off the support ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentValue⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentValue_eq⟧. For a morphism $\varphi$, a structure at $s(\varphi)$ is transported to $t(\varphi)$ by $\hat\varphi$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.transport⟧, which maps the sheets' tangent sets by $T\varphi$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat⟧; by the independence $T\varphi_*(T_\Theta(s(\varphi))) = T_\Theta(t(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grPush_tangentValue⟧, which makes $T_\Theta$ a functor ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentSection⟧.

**Part 2, the independence** (V9.14). *At a good point* there is no hypothesis: near it all sheets through it coincide, so the sum is $\Theta(y) \cdot T_yM$ for every structure ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_eq_of_isGoodPoint⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_subset_goodSet⟧. *Equidimensional structures* ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_isOfDim⟧: group the sheets of both structures through $x$ by tangent set; for each class $L$, a tangent slice $F$ (§IX.9) meeting each sheet of either structure with tangent space $L$ once gives $\sum_{T_xM_i = L} \sigma_i = \sum_{y \in F} \Theta(y) = \sum_{T_xM'_j = L} \sigma'_j$. With sheets of one dimension a slice for one structure is one for the other. *In general* the text reduces to the equidimensional case through the dimensional decomposition, and so does the formalization: if the dimensional parts of two structures agree near $x$ (Proposition 9.1.12), their tangent sums agree dimension by dimension ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_eq_sum_dimPartStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentSum_eq_of_dimPartsAgreeNear⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_dimPartsAgreeNear⟧. With one graph chart for all dimensions and the local constancy of the dimension, which supplies the labellings, the independence follows ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_of_hasGraphChartAt_of_hasLocallyConstantDimAt⟧; restricting a structure to a neighbourhood where the dimensions are constant is ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_restrict_labelled⟧. On every ep-groupoid over $\mathbb R^m$ both hypotheses hold, so $T_\Theta$ exists for every branched $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn⟧. Now Proposition 9.1.12 holds on every ep-groupoid and labelled structures exist at every point (§IX.27), so the independence, and with it Theorem 9.2.1, holds for every branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · hasIndependentTangentSums⟧; the tangent slices of the equidimensional case exist at every point too ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · hasTangentSlicesAt⟧. In Remark 9.1.3 (b) the two structures have the same tangent sum at the bad origin ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlicesRn · EpGroupoid.Remark913Hyp.tangentSum_structureβ_eq_structureγ⟧. The text writes "it suffices to prove the proposition" (p. 410) for the theorem and closes with "This completes the proof of Theorem 9.2.8" (p. 418), presumably Theorem 9.2.1; in $\sum_{i \in I \mid y \in M_j} \sigma_i T_yM_i$ (p. 418) the index is presumably $i$.

### IX.11 Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6): the tangent $T\Theta$

**Definition 9.2.12 (2017: 9.6)** (V9.23) ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentTheta⟧. $T\Theta(h) = 0$ over the complement of the support and $T\Theta(h) = \sum_{h \in TM_i} \sigma_i$ over $U(x)$, with $h \in TM_i$ read as $h \in T_{p(h)}M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentSubmanifold⟧. The formal definition evaluates $T_\Theta(p(h))$ at the tangent sets containing $h$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.grEval⟧, so it does not depend on a structure by construction; that it agrees with the text's local formula for every structure ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_eq⟧ is the text's "the local definitions fit together", and comes from the independence through the identity $\sum_{h \in T_yM_i} \sigma_i = \sum_{h \in T_yM'_j} \sigma'_j$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.sum_tangent_eq_sum_tangent⟧. $T\Theta \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentTheta_nonneg⟧ and it is a functor on the tangent ep-groupoid of Chapter 8 ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_tangentTheta⟧.

**Is $T\Theta$ a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid?** The text says so without discussion. It needs that the $TM_i$ are smooth submanifolds of $TX$ of smooth points, closed in $TU(x)$, and that $|\mathrm{supp}(T\Theta)|$ is paracompact; these are the fields of `TangentBranchingHyp` ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.TangentBranchingHyp⟧, under which the theorem holds ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingStructure⟧. *Closedness* is proved ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.isClosed_tangentSubmanifold⟧. *Paracompactness* follows from that of $|X|$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_tangentTheta⟧. So only the smoothness of the $TM_i$ remains ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_of_isSmoothSubmanifold⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSlices · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_of_isSmoothSubmanifold⟧. $TM_i$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $TX$, the image of the retraction $Ts$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSubMPolyfold_tangent⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isSubMPolyfold_tangentSubmanifold⟧. *That $Ts$ is an sc⁺-retraction of $TX$* (gap G.99, closed): for the sc⁺-retraction $s$ presenting a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold, $g = 1_0^1 \circ s$ is sc-smooth into $X^1$ and $Ts = T\iota \circ Tg$ for the inclusion $\iota : X^1 \to X$. The tangent of $\iota$ is the natural inclusion $T(X^1) \to TX$ of Proposition 2.3.17, in a chart the tangent of the sc-operator $E^1 \to E$, which is itself ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · retractTangentMap_shiftIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · tangentLower_tangentMapOn_one⟧. Hence $Ts$ maps into $(TX)_1$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · tmap_mem_levelSet⟧, and $1_0^1 \circ Ts$ is $Tg$ followed by the sc-diffeomorphism $T(X^1) \cong (TX)^1$, so $Ts$ is an sc⁺-retraction of $TX$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · isScPlusRetractionOn_tmap⟧. So $TA$ is a smooth submanifold of $TX$ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · IsSmoothSubmanifold.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangent⟧, the field holds for every local branching structure ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · LocalBranchingStructure.isSmoothSubmanifold_tangentSubmanifold⟧, and for $|X|$ paracompact $T\Theta$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $TX$ on every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · tangentBranchingHyp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TangentSubmanifoldSmooth · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_general⟧. On $\mathbb R^m$ this was proved first with the field as the only hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_rn⟧; the tangent of a line in $\mathbb R^2$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $T\mathbb R^2$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · rnPolyfold_isSubMPolyfold_tangent_graph2⟧. The full hypothesis has the zero functor as witness ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentBranchingHyp_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_tangentTheta_zero⟧. The text's introduction (p. 408) calls $T\Theta$ a "branched ep-subgroupoid", Definition 9.2.12 an ep⁺-subgroupoid.

### IX.12 Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9) and Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5): the position of $M$ relative to $\partial X$

**Reduced tangent position in a chart** (V9.24). $T^R_xX$ is not a subspace of a vector space in the project; in a chart $\varphi$ with $\varphi(x) = z$ in a partial quadrant, "$T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$" is the inclusion of the chart image of $T_xM$ in the reduced tangent space $E_z$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · IsReducedTangentAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_reduced⟧, equivalently in the partial quadrant or the partial cone at $z$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialQuadrant⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · isReducedTangentAt_iff_subset_partialCone⟧. It does not depend on the chart ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.isReducedTangentAt_chart_change⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.isTangentReducedAt_iff_forall⟧, and defines `IsTangentReducedAt` ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.IsTangentReducedAt⟧. $d_M(x)$ is the degeneracy index of the induced M-polyfold structure ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.subDegIndex⟧, at most $d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_le⟧.

**Lemma 9.2.13 (2017: 9.9).** *For $x \in M$: (1) $x \in \partial X$ and $d_M(x) = 0$ iff (2) $T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$.* **As printed (2) ⇒ (1) does not hold at interior points**: for a point $p$ of $\mathbb R^n$, $\{p\}$ is in reduced tangent position at $p$ and $p \notin \partial\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.not_lemma_9_2_13_two_one⟧. The lemma is about $x \in M \cap \partial X$, where the text uses it, and is formalized there. *(1) ⇒ (2)* ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_chart⟧: if $d_M(x) = 0$, Part I's Theorem 2.5.? (preprint: 2.31) gives a chart of $M$ without boundary near $x$, whose tangent space lies in the reduced tangent space of $X$; the boundary hypothesis is not used, and the implication holds off $\partial X$ too ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_of_not_mem_boundary⟧. *(2) ⇒ (1)* ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_two_one⟧. **The text's proof** builds a complement $Y$ and a map $F$ and asserts that the image is $M$ near $0$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* In a chart, $M$ is the image of an sc⁺-retraction $s$ near $z$, with $T_zM \subseteq E_z$. *Step 2,* "the image is $M$ near $0$", which the text does not spell out: the projection $p$ onto $T_zM$ along a complement is injective on $M$ near $z$, by a level-1 contraction with the mean value inequality ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_injOn_proj⟧. *Step 3.* By Mathlib's inverse function theorem for $p \circ s$ on $T_zM$, $\chi = p(\cdot - z)$ is a chart of $M \cap G$ onto an open subset of $T_zM \subseteq E_z$, with inverse $s \circ (z + \cdot) \circ \Psi^{-1}$, a model without boundary ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · ScRetraction.IsScPlus.exists_flat⟧. *Step 4.* So $d_M(x) = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_zero_of_isTangentReducedAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_zero_of_isReducedTangentAt⟧. The complement $Y$ and the map $F$ are not needed. Together: the equivalence at $x \in \partial X$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.lemma_9_2_13_iff⟧, and at every $x \in M$: $d_M(x) = 0 \iff T_xM \subseteq T^R_xX$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_zero_iff⟧. The witness is a point of $\mathbb R^n$; a witness at a boundary point needs a submanifold API for quadrants, not yet available.

**Remark 9.2.14 (2017: 9.5)** (V9.25). $\partial M$ is the boundary of the induced M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.mem_boundary_subPolyfold_iff⟧. *$x \in \partial M$ iff $x \in \partial X$ and $T_xM \not\subseteq T^R_xX$* ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_iff⟧: ⇐ with $d_M(x) \ge 1$ from Lemma 9.2.13 ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14⟧; ⇒ since $\partial M \subseteq \partial X$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_mem_boundary⟧ and a point of $M$ in reduced position has $d_M = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_isTangentReducedAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPositionConverse · MPolyfold.remark_9_2_14_not_mem_boundary_iff⟧.

### IX.13 Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4), Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7) and Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6): the boundary $\partial\Theta$

**The boundary of a sheet.** $y \in \partial M$ is characterized through $T_yM$ (Remark 9.2.14), so the set of $y$ with $y \in \partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldBoundary_iff⟧ is read off the tangent sets: $y \in \partial M$ iff $y \in \partial X$ and $T_yM$ is not in reduced position ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.IsReducedTangentSet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.isReducedTangentSet_iff⟧. It is local and invariant under sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldBoundary_inter_isOpen_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.mem_submanifoldBoundary_image_iff⟧.

**Proposition 9.2.15 (2017: 9.4)** (V9.26). *(1)* The boundary weight $\sum_{y \in \partial M_i} \sigma_i$ is the part of $T_\Theta(y)$ on tangent sets not in reduced position ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryPart⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.filter_tangentValue_eq⟧; so, under the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, it is the same for any two structures whose domains contain $y$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_1⟧. *(2)* If $d_X(y) = 0$, no tangent set is out of reduced position, so the weight and the formal sum vanish for every structure, with no independence ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_2⟧. *(3)* $\partial\Theta$, $0$ off $\partial X$ and the boundary part of $T_\Theta$ on it ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta⟧, is a functor ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_boundaryTheta⟧, nonnegative, supported in $\partial X$ and given by the local formula on every structure ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_2_15_3⟧. (1) and (2) need neither $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap \partial X$ nor that $\Theta$ be branched.

**Definition 9.2.16 (2017: 9.7)** (V9.27). *$\partial\Theta$ is uniquely characterized by (1) $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \subseteq \partial X$ and (2) the local formula at points of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$* ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.IsBoundaryCharacterized⟧. $\partial\Theta$ has (1) and (2) ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.isBoundaryCharacterized_boundaryTheta⟧. **The uniqueness, as we read it, does not hold**: (2) is asked only on $\mathrm{supp}(F)$, so $F = 0$ has (1) and (2) for every $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.isBoundaryCharacterized_zero⟧, and for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, where $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · boundaryTheta_halfLine_one⟧, both $0$ and $\partial\Theta$ do ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · not_unique_isBoundaryCharacterized_halfLine⟧. With (2) asked at the points of $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ and $F = 0$ off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$, $F = \partial\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.eq_boundaryTheta⟧. **A reading with the printed (2)** ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCharacterization · definition_9_2_16_existsUnique⟧: among the $F \ge 0$ vanishing off $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ with (1) and (2), there is exactly one whose support contains the supports of all the others, and it is $\partial\Theta$. *Step 1.* Such an $F$ agrees with $\partial\Theta$ on its own support, by (2) and the local formula for $\partial\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCharacterization · IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_on⟧, so its support lies in $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCharacterization · IsBoundaryCharacterized.supp_subset⟧. *Step 2.* Hence $F = \partial\Theta$ iff its support contains $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCharacterization · IsBoundaryCharacterized.eq_boundaryTheta_iff⟧, and $\partial\Theta$ itself has (1) and (2). Row V9.27 is narrower for this reason. Before the definition the text writes "In view of Proposition 9.2.13" (2017: "Proposition 9.9", the number of Lemma 9.2.13 there), presumably Proposition 9.2.15, and in it "branched ep⁺-groupoid".

**Remark 9.2.17 (2017: 9.6)** (V9.28). $\partial\Theta \le \Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_le⟧, and $\partial\Theta$ is not $\Theta$ restricted to $\partial X$: for the indicator of the corner $0$ of $[0, \infty)$, $\Theta(0) = 1$ and $\partial\Theta(0) = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · boundaryTheta_halfLineCorner⟧, while for $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, whose sheet is all of $[0, \infty)$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.HasCornerStructure.isSmoothSubmanifold_univ⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_one⟧, $\partial\Theta(0) = 1$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_one⟧. For the indicator of an interior point $\partial\Theta = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryTheta_indicator_of_mem⟧. The witnesses satisfy the independence ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_indicator_of_mem⟧. The remark's "In Section 9.5, Definition 9.3.6" refers to §9.3.

### IX.14 Orientations: $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(X)$, Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8) and Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8)

**Oriented tangent sets** (V9.29). An orientation of a finite-dimensional vector space is a class of bases; for a tangent set it is a set of frames, lists of vectors of the set, whose chart images ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.chartVec⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.chartVec_injOn⟧ are the positive bases of an orientation of the chart image ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.OrTangent⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.chartFrames⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.IsChartOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt⟧. A chart change acts linearly ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.exists_clm_chartVec⟧, so this does not depend on the chart ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.isChartOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_iff_forall⟧; every tangent set with linear chart image has exactly two orientations ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.exists_two_orientations⟧, and sc-diffeomorphisms and morphisms push them forward ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.OrTangent.push⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · MPolyfold.IsOrientedAt.push_tangentMapOn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.isOrientedAt_push_tangentMor⟧. $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}(x)$ is generated by oriented tangent sets ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.GrHat⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grHatPush⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.GrHatObj⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grHatProj⟧, and forgetting the orientation is a functor over $X^\infty$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grForget⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grForgetFunctor_comp_grProj⟧, adding the two orientations of a set to the set ⟦Chapter9/OrientationTangent · EpGroupoid.grForget_single_add_single⟧. Remark 9.3.1 (2017: 9.7), on an earlier notion of orientation, has no formal content.

**Definition 9.3.2 (2017: 9.8)** (V9.30) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.IsOrientation⟧. An orientation of a submanifold is a continuous choice of orientations of its tangent sets ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation⟧, continuity being local constancy of the chart frames; an oriented local branching structure carries one per sheet ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure⟧, with oriented sum $\sum_{y \in M_i} \sigma_i T_y(M_i, o_i)$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.orientedSum⟧ forgetting to the tangent sum ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.grForget_orientedSum⟧. An orientation of $\Theta$ assigns to each smooth object an element of $\widehat{\mathrm{Gr}}$, naturally in morphisms, forgetting to $T_\Theta$, and locally an oriented sum; the "lifts $T_\Theta$" clause uses $T_\Theta$, hence the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.IsOrientation.mk'⟧, which on $\mathbb R^m$ is free ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_trivial_rn⟧. It defines a section functor ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.orientedSection⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grHatProj⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.orientedSection_comp_grForgetFunctor_obj⟧. Witnesses: $\Theta = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.isOrientation_zero⟧, and finite weighted sums of oriented closed submanifolds of $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.isOrientation_sum_rn⟧.

**Remark 9.3.3 (2017: 9.8)** (V9.31) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBasic · EpGroupoid.remark_9_3_3⟧. For the indicator of a point $p$, $T_q = q \cdot (\{p\}, +) + (1 - q) \cdot (\{p\}, -)$, $q \in (0, 1) \cap \mathbb Q$, are pairwise distinct orientations: a $0$-dimensional tangent set has two orientations, and any split of the weight $1$ between them is an orientation.

### IX.15 Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10) and Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)

**Lemma 9.3.4 (2017: 9.10)** (V9.32). *Two orientations of $\Theta$ that agree at good points are the same.* **Without equidimensionality, as we read it, the lemma does not hold** ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · lemma_9_3_4_mixed_dim⟧: on $\mathbb R^2$ let $\Theta = 1_{\mathbb R \times 0} + 1_{(0,0)}$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · mixedTheta⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · mixedTheta_isBranched⟧. The origin is bad ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · zero_not_mem_goodSet_mixed⟧, the good points are the other points of the line, and two orientations that orient the line the same way and the point $\{0\}$ oppositely agree at all good points and differ at the origin. The lemma is formalized for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · EpGroupoid.IsOrientationOfDim⟧.

**The text's proof** takes, at a bad $x$, the sequences of good points of Proposition 9.2.8 for the first structure and compares the orientations of the two structures along them. As we read it, this needs that the same sequences serve the second structure, which the text does not show, and that frames of different sheets can be compared along a sequence. **The formalized proof** ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4⟧. *Step 1.* Its hypothesis `HasOrientedGoodPointsAt` ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · MPolyfold.HasOrientedGoodPointsAt⟧ asks, for each class of sheets of both structures with one tangent set at $x$, good points near $x$ on every sheet of the class, on which the orientations of the sheets can be compared; this is Proposition 9.2.8 applied to both families together. Under it, the oriented sums at $x$ agree class by class, which is the lemma. *Step 2,* from the ball graph representation (§IX.9) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_of_hasGraphBallAt⟧: over a ball of foot points in the class tangent space each sheet of the class is a graph, the good points are dense in it (Lemma 9.2.7 (1)), and the relative orientations of the sheets are locally constant. *Step 3,* local constancy: the relative orientation of two frame fields is the sign of a determinant ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · frameDet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · orientation_eq_iff_frameDet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.frames_eq_iff_frameDet⟧, continuous if the chart frames are continuous on level 1 ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.continuousOn_chartVec_of_continuousOn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff⟧. This continuity was first the hypothesis `HasContinuousLevelOneOn` ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.HasContinuousLevelOneOn⟧, true on $\mathbb R^m$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · hasContinuousLevelOneOn_rn⟧, and ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt⟧ holds under the two hypotheses, on every ep-groupoid over $\mathbb R^m$ without them ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_3_4_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn⟧; witness in dimension $0$: ⟦Chapter9/OrientationUniqueness · hasOrientedGoodPointsAt_rn_zero⟧. *Step 4, no hypothesis* (gap G.100, closed). The level-1 continuity holds along every smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasContinuousLevelOneOn⟧: on the submanifold the level-1 lift of the chart is $1_0^1 \circ t$ composed with the chart, for the chart sc⁺-retraction $t$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · levelLift_eq_plusLift⟧, continuous since $t$ is sc⁺. The ball graph representation holds at interior points, which gave the lemma for $\Theta$ supported where $d_X = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_3_4_of_hasGraphBallAt'⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_3_4_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧. At boundary points a ball of foot points is not available, but it is not needed: the good direction $h_0$ off the other tangent spaces is chosen near an admissible direction $h_1$, so that every $h$ near $h_0$ is admissible with one radius and one factor ⟦Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints · exists_small_cone⟧, and the tangent sheets are graphs over a small ball $\{u \in T \mid \|u - t h_0\| < \tau t\}$ for $t$ below a uniform bound ⟦Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints · exists_graph_unif_chart⟧. So the good-point input holds at every point ⟦Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints · hasOrientedGoodPointsAt⟧, and Lemma 9.3.4 holds for every $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ of every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints · lemma_9_3_4_general⟧, every orientation of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ being $n$-dimensional ⟦Chapter9/OrientationAnyDim · IsOrientation.isOrientationOfDim⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationAnyDim · lemma_9_3_4_of_isNDimensional⟧. Row V9.32 stays narrower only because of the mixed-dimensional counterexample above.

**Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1)** (V9.33) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · example_9_3_5_rn⟧. Take $\beta^{++}(s) = e(s) + e(-s)$ with $e$ = `expNegInvGlue`, $\beta^{--} = -\beta^{++}$, $\beta^{+-}$ equal to $\beta^{++}$ for $s \le 0$ and to $\beta^{--}$ for $s > 0$, and $\beta^{-+}$ the other way ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · betaPP⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · betaMM⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · betaPM⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · betaMP⟧. The two pairs of graphs cover each point equally often ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5_count⟧, which defines $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example935Theta⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example935Theta_isBranched⟧. Orienting the graphs by $\pm(1, \beta')$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · graphOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · chartVec_image_graph2⟧ gives $\hat T^1$ from $G^{++}, G^{--}$ and $\hat T^2$ from $G^{+-}, G^{-+}$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · exampleT1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · exampleT2⟧. Verified as stated: they coincide at the origin ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5_eq_origin⟧, differ at $(s, \beta^{++}(s))$ for $s > 0$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5_ne_of_pos⟧, and no signs for the second structure reproduce $\hat T^1$ near the origin ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5_cannot_coincide⟧. **Two claims do not hold as we read them.** "Otherwise different": they also coincide wherever $x < 0$, where $G^{+-} = G^{++}$ and $G^{-+} = G^{--}$ with the same orientations ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · example_9_3_5_eq_of_neg⟧. "Four possibilities to orient": the four sign choices for the first structure give four different orientations ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · orientedLift1_injective⟧, and $\hat T^2$ is none of them ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExample · exampleT2_ne_orientedLift1⟧. Counting both structures, the sign choices give exactly six orientations, the two structures sharing the two constant choices ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSigns · orientedLift1_eq_orientedLift2_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSigns · orientedLift2_injective⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSigns · ncard_signOrientations⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSigns · example_9_3_5_six⟧, and with fractional weights there are infinitely many, as in Remark 9.3.3. So "four possibilities" holds for each structure and, for $\Theta$, does not hold as we read it; the full classification is §IX.29 (gap G.101, closed). The good points distinguish $\hat T^1$ from $\hat T^2$, in line with Lemma 9.3.4 ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · exists_goodSet_exampleT1_ne_exampleT2⟧.

### IX.16 Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10), Lemma 9.3.7, and the boundary orientation ((9.11), Definition 9.3.8, Proposition 9.3.9, Definition 9.3.10)

**Definition 9.3.6 (2017: 9.10)** (V9.34) ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · EpGroupoid.IsTameBranched⟧. A tame structure has a natural representation on its domain, the properness property, and sheets with tame induced structures in the sense of Part I's Definition 2.5.18. Witnesses: $\Theta = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_zero⟧ and a point of $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · EpGroupoid.isTameBranched_indicator⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.hasTameInducedStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧. "In particular every $M_i$ has an equivalent structure of a manifold with boundary with corners" (gap G.102, closed): for a tame structure with $n$-dimensional sheets, each $M_i$ with the subspace topology is a Mathlib manifold with corners modelled on $[0, \infty)^n$ ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · TameBranchingStructure.hasCornerStructureOfDim⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · TameBranchingStructure.isManifold⟧. *Step 1.* A tame induced structure gives corner coordinates near each point, charts onto relatively open subsets of partial quadrants of $\mathbb R^n$ with smooth transitions ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · CornerCoords⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · IsSubmanifoldOfDim.hasCornerStructureOfDim_of_hasTameInducedStructure⟧. *Step 2.* A Mathlib manifold has one model, so each partial quadrant is moved into the full quadrant by a linear isomorphism ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · exists_cle_partialQuadrant⟧, which gives a charted space ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · cornerChartedSpace⟧ with smooth transitions ⟦Chapter9/MathlibManifoldBridge · isManifold_cornerChartedSpace⟧. The same bridge serves Part I's solution sets.

**Lemma 9.3.7** (V9.35) ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.lemma_9_3_7⟧, new in the 2021 edition. *For tame $Y$ and submanifolds $M_1$, $M_2$ of one dimension with tame induced structures, $T_yM_1 = T_yM_2$ implies $d_{M_1}(y) = d_{M_2}(y)$.* **The text's proof** describes $T_yM$ in a tame chart of $M$ by the cone $C_yM$ and shows that $T_0O \cap C$ is the reduced tangent space. **The formalized proof.** For a submanifold with tame induced structure, $d_M(y)$ is the codimension of the reduced part of the chart image of $T_yM$, which depends only on that linear space and on the partial quadrant of the chart of $Y$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_of_hasTameInducedStructure⟧ (Remark 2.5.9 in every chart). So equal tangent spaces give equal indices ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryPosition · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_tangentSpace_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq⟧, with neither "$Y$ tame" nor "of the same dimension". The text's "$T_0O \cap C = T^R_0O$" (a cone against a subspace) is read through the linearity of the chart image of $T_0M$.

**Definition 9.3.8 (2017: 9.9)** (V9.36) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.boundaryFrames⟧. *For an oriented $(M, o)$, $y \in \partial M$ with $d_M(y) = 1$: a basis $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $T_y\partial M$ is positive iff $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ is positive, $e$ outward.* Linear algebra first: the convention orients a hyperplane $K$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · exists_boundary_orientation⟧, by the determinant criterion ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · exists_basis_orientation_iff_det_pos⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · det_cons_smul_add⟧. In a tangent set: for $K \subseteq T_yM$ with $(m-1)$-dimensional chart image and $e \notin K$, the frames orient $K$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.isOrientedAt_boundaryFrames⟧, and $e \mapsto ce + k$, $c > 0$, $k \in K$, does not change them ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.boundaryFrames_eq⟧; both orientations occur, on a graph ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · exists_boundaryFrames_graph⟧. $T_y\partial M$ and $e$ are data in this definition. That $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ and the outward half-space are determined by $M$ through the cones $C_yM$, and that the resulting orientation is continuous along the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$, is proved in §IX.30 (gap G.103, closed); row V9.36 is now explicit.

**(9.11) and Proposition 9.3.9** (V9.37), new in the 2021 edition. Split the oriented sum at $y$ by $\ell = d_{M_i}(y)$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · EpGroupoid.degreePart⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · EpGroupoid.degreePart_orientedSum⟧; by Lemma 9.3.7 tangent sets of different degree never coincide ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.HasSubDegree⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.hasSubDegree_tangent_iff⟧, so two oriented structures with the same oriented sum at $y$ have the same degree-$\ell$ parts for every $\ell$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · EpGroupoid.eq_9_11⟧. Applying a boundary operation $T_y(M, o) \mapsto T_y(\partial M, o_{\partial M})$, a function `bd` of the oriented tangent set, to the degree-$1$ part gives (9.12), which therefore does not depend on the structure ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9⟧. **Definition 9.3.10 (2017: 9.11)** (V9.38) is (9.12) with $0$ off the support ⟦Chapter9/OrientationBoundary · EpGroupoid.boundaryLift⟧; the condition $y \in \partial M_i$ is implied by $d_{M_i}(y) = 1$. The operation `bd` is now built from the sheet, and (9.12) and Proposition 9.3.9 hold with it ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · EpGroupoid.boundaryOrientation⟧; the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$ along $\partial M$ and its extension to the faces (Figure 9.1) are §IX.30. Remark 9.3.11, on the non-tame case, has no formal content.

### IX.17 §9.4: essential points and sets of measure zero (Definitions 9.4.1, 9.4.5, 9.4.7, Lemmas 9.4.2–9.4.8 (2017: 9.12–9.14, 9.11–9.15))

**For Mathlib manifolds.** Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.5 are about a smooth finite-dimensional manifold $M$ with boundary and corners, formalized for Mathlib manifolds with corners. *Definition 9.4.1 (1)* (V9.39): $T^K_zM$ is the span of the unit limits $\varphi(z_k)/|\varphi(z_k)|$, $z_k \to z$ in $K \setminus \{z\}$, in a chart $\varphi$ centred at $z$. In a chart it is the span of Mathlib's tangent cone of the chart image of $K$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · chartImage⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · span_tangentConeAt_chartImage_eq_map⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryMeasure · span_unitDirections⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryMeasure · unitDirections⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · relTangent⟧, and a chart change maps it by the derivative ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · relTangent_eq_map⟧, which is the text's "independent of the choice of $\varphi$". *Definition 9.4.1 (2)*: $z$ is essential if it is a limit of points of $K$ where $T^K M$ is everything ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · relTangent_eq_top_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · fullSet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · essentialSet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · essentialSet_eq⟧. For two crossing lines in $\mathbb R^2$ the essential set is $\{0\}$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · crossLines⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · essentialSet_crossLines⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · nonEssential_crossLines⟧. *Lemma 9.4.2 (2017: 9.11)* (V9.40), "obvious from the definition": $K^e$ is a closure taken in $K$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · lemma_9_4_2⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · lemma_9_4_2_open⟧. *Definition 9.4.5 (2017: 9.13)* (V9.43) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · IsMeasureZero⟧: null in every chart; countable unions ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · isMeasureZero_iUnion⟧, a chart cover suffices ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · isMeasureZero_of_forall_mem⟧, and $\mathbb R^2$ is not null ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · not_isMeasureZero_univ⟧. *Lemma 9.4.6 (2017: 9.14)* (V9.44) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · lemma_9_4_6⟧, "proved similarly as Lemma 2.8 in [57]": *Step 1.* At a point where $T^K_zM \ne T_zM$ there is a unit direction $v$ off the span, and points of $K$ near $z$ lie outside a cone around $v$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryMeasure · eventually_abs_le_of_tangentConeAt⟧. *Step 2.* A cone has positive density at its vertex ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryMeasure · exists_pos_measure_cone_lt⟧, so $z$ is not a Lebesgue density point of $K$; by Lebesgue's density theorem the set of such $z$ is null ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryMeasure · addHaar_setOf_span_tangentConeAt_ne_top⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometryManifold · isMeasureZero_setOf_relTangent_ne_top⟧. *Step 3.* A non-essential point has a neighbourhood in $K$ of such points, by Lemma 9.4.2. The statement holds for every $K$, not only for $K(i, i')$.

**For sheets in an M-polyfold.** The sheets $M_i$ are submanifolds of an M-polyfold, which in general carry no Mathlib manifold structure (a tame sheet does, §IX.16). So the essential points and null sets of the sheets are the data of a `SheetGeometry` ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry⟧, with Lemma 9.4.4 (`ess_comm`), Lemma 9.4.6 (`isNull_diff_ess`) and the note of Definition 9.4.7 (`submanifoldTangent_eq`) as fields; it was first witnessed by pieces of graphs in $\mathbb R^2$, with the essential sets and null sets of the Mathlib part read in the chart $z \mapsto z_0$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · graphSheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · graphSheetGeometry⟧. It is now built on the $n$-dimensional submanifolds of every M-polyfold with no hypothesis, Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.5 being read in the M-polyfold charts as in the text's proof of Lemma 9.4.4 ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · sheetGeometry⟧ (§IX.28; gap G.105, closed). So Lemma 9.4.8 and Propositions 9.4.9, 9.4.10 hold for every $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ with no sheet-geometry hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/SheetGeometryFree · lemma_9_4_8_of_isNDimensional⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetGeometryFree · proposition_9_4_9_of_isNDimensional⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetGeometryFree · proposition_9_4_10_of_isNDimensional⟧.

**Lemma 9.4.4 (2017: 9.13)** (V9.42). *Essential for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_i$ iff for $K(i, i') \subseteq M_{i'}$*, "left to the reader". **As we read it, it needs sheets of one dimension** ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · lemma_9_4_4_mixed_dim⟧: $\mathbb R \times 0$ as a subset of $\mathbb R$ is essential at every point, as a subset of $\mathbb R^2$ nowhere, since its relative tangent space is a line. For an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ the text's reduction to $T^D_0N$ in a chart applies, and is now proved for $n$-dimensional submanifolds of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · lemma_9_4_4_chart⟧ and for the sheets of every structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lemma_9_4_4_of_isNDimensional⟧ (§IX.28).

**Definition 9.4.7 (2017: 9.14)** (V9.45). $i \sim_y i'$ through a chain of links $y \in K(i_{p-1}, i_p)^e$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsLink⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.YEquiv⟧ is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.equivalence_yEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.ySetoid⟧; equivalent sheets have the same tangent set at $y$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.submanifoldTangent_eq_of_yEquiv⟧; $\#P_y$ is ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.numClasses⟧.

**Lemma 9.4.8 (2017: 9.15)** (V9.46) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.lemma_9_4_8⟧. *$\{y \in M_U \mid \#P_y \ge 2\}$ is null.* "Null in $M_U$" is null in every sheet through the point ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.IsNullIn⟧. The text decomposes $M_U$ by $(I_y, P_y)$ and concludes that the bad part lies in $\bigcup_{j, j'} K(j, j')^{ne}$. As we read it, $K(j, j')^{ne}$ is null only in $M_j$ and $M_{j'}$; inside a sheet $M_i$ through $y$ the proof uses $K(i, j)^{ne}$ for $j$ not $y$-equivalent to $i$: if $y$ had two classes, the class of $i$ omits some $j \in I_y$, so $y \in K(i, j)$ is not essential. Hence $M_U \setminus M^*_U$ is null ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.MStar⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.isNullIn_diff_MStar⟧.

### IX.18 Property (T), Propositions 9.4.9 and 9.4.10 (2017: 9.5 and 9.6)

**Property (T)** (V9.41) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.PropertyT⟧: the orientation relation of two sheets with the same tangent space is the same at every common point with the same tangent space; the first structure of Example 9.3.5 has it ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · propertyT_example935B1⟧. Under (T) the sign map $K(i, i')^e \to \{\pm1\}$ is constant ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · EpGroupoid.tangent_eq_iff_of_mem_ess⟧. **Lemma 9.4.3** (V9.41) ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · lemma_9_4_3⟧ ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · lemma_9_4_3_propertyT⟧. *Every oriented local branching structure has Property (T) after restriction to a smaller open $U'(x)$* (gap G.104, closed). **The text's proof** argues along sequences of points converging to $x$. **The formalized proof** finds, for each of the finitely many pairs $(i, i')$, an open neighbourhood of $x$ on which the pair satisfies (T), and intersects ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_pairT⟧ ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · propertyT_restrict_iff⟧. *Case 1, different dimensions:* two submanifolds with the same tangent set at a point have the same dimension there ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · HasDimAt.eq_of_submanifoldTangent_eq⟧, so (T) asks nothing of such a pair. *Case 2, dimension $0$:* a point where a submanifold is $0$-dimensional is isolated in it, by the chord estimate with vanishing derivative ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · HasDimAt.exists_isOpen_eq_of_mem⟧. *Case 3, equal tangent spaces at $x$:* where the tangent spaces agree, the relative orientation is the sign of a frame determinant, locally constant by the level-1 continuity (§IX.15) ⟦Chapter9/OrientationRn · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_iff⟧. *Case 4, different tangent spaces at $x$:* they stay different nearby, since a continuous frame field of one, written in the chart, has a nonzero minor against the other ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · exists_chartTangent_field⟧ ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · exists_frameDet_ne_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/PropertyTShrinking2021 · exists_isOpen_submanifoldTangent_ne⟧, so after shrinking (T) is empty for the pair.

**Proposition 9.4.9 (2017: 9.5)** (V9.47) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_9⟧. *Off a null set $M_U = M^*_U = \bigsqcup_J M^J_U$, and on $M^J_U$: $\Theta = \sigma_J$, $T_\Theta = \sigma_J T^J$, $\hat T_\Theta = a_J(T^J, o^a_J) + b_J(T^J, o^b_J)$, $a_J + b_J = \sigma_J$, $o^a_J = -o^b_J$.* *Step 1.* The null set is Lemma 9.4.8; the pieces are the level sets of $y \mapsto I_y$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.SheetGeometry.MStarPart⟧. *Step 2.* On $M^J_U$ all sheets of $J$ are $y$-equivalent, so they have one tangent set $T^J$ and $T_\Theta(y) = \sigma_J T^J$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.tangentValue_eq_sum⟧, which uses the independence of Theorem 9.2.1. *Step 3.* By (T) the orientations of the sheets of $J$ at $y$ fall into two opposite classes; $o^a_J = -o^b_J$ is "$o^a_J \ne o^b_J$ on the same tangent set", since it has exactly two orientations ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.OrTangent.eq_or_eq_or_eq_of_isOrientedAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · MPolyfold.exists_ne_isOrientedAt⟧; if one class is empty its orientation is the other one. The footnote's "measure zero" in $M_U$ refers forward to Definition 9.5.1 and Lemma 9.5.2 (p. 437), consistently as we read it.

**Proposition 9.4.10 (2017: 9.6)** (V9.48) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_4_10⟧. *Two oriented structures on $U(x)$ with (a) the same weight sums and (b) the same oriented sums agree off a null set, piece by piece, as in (1)–(5).* **The text** takes the union $B''$ of the two structures, which describes $2\Theta$, applies Proposition 9.4.9 to $B$, $B'$, $B''$ and intersects. **The formalized proof** takes $M^\dagger_U = M''^*_U$ for the union only, not intersected with $M^*_U$ and $M'^*_U$, which (1)–(5) do not need. The pieces $A_p$ are cut out by the finitely many values of $y \mapsto (I_y, I'_y, J_+(y), J'_+(y))$, with $J_\pm(y)$ the two orientation classes at $y$, so Property (T) is not used. The two structures of Example 9.3.5, all signs $+$, satisfy (a) and (b) ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · example935B1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · example935B2⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · example935_hypotheses_9_4_10⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · example935_MU_eq⟧; at the origin $G^{++}$ and $G^{--}$ are tangent but not $0$-equivalent, so the set of Lemma 9.4.8 is not empty ⟦Chapter9/BranchingGeometry · example935_two_le_numClasses⟧.

### IX.19 §9.5: sets of measure zero and the σ-algebras $L(S)$, $L(\partial S)$ (Definitions 9.5.1, 9.5.3, 9.5.14, Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: Definitions 9.15–9.17, Lemma 9.16))

**The setting of §9.5.** $\Theta$ is oriented, tame, compact and $n$-dimensional, and $S = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$. Measure zero in a sheet $M_i$ is that of Definition 9.4.5, which the project first had for Mathlib manifolds only (§IX.17). So, as in §9.4, the null sets of the sheets are data, now instantiated on every M-polyfold by the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the chart images (§IX.28; gap G.106, closed): a system `SheetNullSets` on a class $\mathcal S$ of sheets ⟦Chapter9/Measure · SheetNullSets⟧, with null sets closed under subsets, countable unions ⟦Chapter9/Measure · SheetNullSets.isNull_iUnion_countable⟧ and finite unions ⟦Chapter9/Measure · SheetNullSets.isNull_union⟧, local, induced alike by two sheets of $\mathcal S$ on their overlap (`isNull_transfer`), and a nonempty sheet not null in itself. A §9.4 sheet geometry with these properties is a `SheetMeasureGeometry` ⟦Chapter9/Measure · MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · MPolyfold.SheetMeasureGeometry.toSheetNullSets⟧, and then null preimages are §9.4's "null in $M_U$" ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.hasNullPreimages_iff_isNullIn⟧. *The covering criterion* ⟦Chapter9/Measure · SheetNullSets.isNull_of_cover⟧: a subset $C$ of a sheet $N \in \mathcal S$ is null in $N$ if near each of its points it is covered by finitely many sheets of $\mathcal S$ in which it is null; by locality and the transfer property.

**Definition 9.5.1 (2017: 9.15)** (V9.49) ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSupp⟧. $A \subseteq |X|$ has measure zero if every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ has a tame local branching structure (Definition 9.3.6, the text's "suitable $U(x)$") with sheets in $\mathcal S$ whose preimages $M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ are null in $M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.HasNullPreimages⟧. The variants ask this of some local branching structure ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAny⟧, or of every structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroSuppAll⟧; the standing assumption is that tame structures with sheets in $\mathcal S$ exist ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.HasTameSheetsIn⟧. Compactness and orientation are not used.

**Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16)** (V9.50) ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.lemma_9_5_2⟧. *The notion does not depend on the choice of the local branching structures.* **The text** cites the literature, without proof. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the core* ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAll_of_any⟧. Suppose some structure at every point has null preimages of $A$, and let $B'$ be any structure with sheets in $\mathcal S$ and $M'_j$ one of its sheets. Each $z \in M'_j \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ lies in the support, so a structure $B$ at $z$ with null preimages exists. Near $z$, $M'_j \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U_B = \bigcup_i M_i$, so $M'_j \cap \pi^{-1}(A)$ is covered near $z$ by the finitely many $M_i$, in which it is null. The covering criterion gives that it is null in $M'_j$. *Step 2.* A tame structure is a structure ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroSuppAny_of_isMeasureZeroSupp⟧, and under the standing assumption every point has a tame one with sheets in $\mathcal S$; the three notions agree. *Step 3.* The sets of measure zero form a σ-ideal ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSuppAll⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroSupp⟧, and $S \ne \emptyset$ is not null, since a sheet through a point of the support is not null in itself ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSuppAny_orbitSupp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.not_isMeasureZeroSupp_orbitSupp⟧.

**The transfer property, as we read it, needs one dimension** ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isNull_transfer_mixed_dim⟧. Step 1 uses that a set null in the sheets $M_i$ is null in $M'_j$ on their overlap. For sheets of different dimensions this does not hold: the axis $\mathbb R \times 0$ has Lebesgue measure zero in the sheet $\mathbb R^2$ and is not null in itself, a $1$-dimensional sheet; so no single system contains the planar null sets and those of graphs. The lemma is therefore proved for structures whose sheets lie in one class, as do the $n$-dimensional structures of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$. That *every* structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets is now proved on every ep-groupoid, from the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · isOfDim_of_isNDimensional⟧, so for $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ Lemma 9.5.2 holds as printed (§IX.28; row V9.50 explicit). With the Hausdorff null sets the transfer across dimensions does not hold as we read it either: the axis of $\mathbb R^2$ has $2$-dimensional and not $1$-dimensional measure zero ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · isHNull_mixed_dim⟧.
