**Definition 9.5.3 (2017: 9.16) and the remark after it** (V9.51). *Step 1, a general fact.* For a family $\mathcal N$ of subsets, the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets and $\mathcal N$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · borelNullSigma⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · borel_le_borelNullSigma⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · measurableSet_borelNullSigma_of_mem⟧ is, if $\mathcal N$ is a σ-ideal ⟦Chapter9/Measure · IsSigmaIdeal⟧, the family $\{A \mid A \,\Delta\, B \in \mathcal N$ for a Borel $B\}$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · borelNullCompletion⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · measurableSet_borelNullSigma_iff⟧: that family is a σ-algebra, by $\bigcup_k A_k \,\Delta\, \bigcup_k B_k \subseteq \bigcup_k (A_k \,\Delta\, B_k)$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · symmDiff_iUnion_subset⟧, contains the Borel sets and $\mathcal N$, and lies in every σ-algebra containing both. *Step 2.* $L(S)$ is this σ-algebra on the subspace $S$ for the sets of measure zero ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.measureZeroSets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigma⟧, a σ-ideal under the standing assumption ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isSigmaIdeal_measureZeroSets⟧. *Step 3.* The text's remark that $L(S)$ is obtained by adding the sets of measure zero is read as the completion: $K \in L(S)$ iff $K \,\Delta\, B$ has measure zero for a Borel $B$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.remark_9_5_3⟧; sets of measure zero belong to $L(S)$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.measurableSet_lebesgueSigma_of_isMeasureZeroSupp⟧. The form $K = B \cup N$ would need Borel null hulls of null sets, which an abstract system does not provide.

**Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) and the paragraph before it** (V9.52). $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)| \subseteq S$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.orbitSupp_boundaryTheta_subset⟧. $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in the boundaries $\partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary⟧ is a second system on a class of boundaries, and $K$ has measure zero in $\partial S$ if at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has boundary preimages null in the $\partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundaryAll⟧. *"A well-defined notion"* ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundaryAll_of⟧: the proof of Lemma 9.5.2 applies to the boundaries. By the local formula for $\partial\Theta$ (Proposition 9.2.15), which holds for every structure given the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, a point of $\partial M'_j$ lies in $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$, and a point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ lies in some $\partial M_i$ of any structure at it, a positive sum having a nonzero term ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.exists_mem_of_sum_pos⟧; so the boundary preimage in $\partial M'_j$ is covered near each point by the $\partial M_i$ of a structure with null boundary preimages. $L(\partial S)$ is the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets of $\partial S$ and these sets ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasureZeroSets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundary⟧. The $(n-1)$-dimensional null sets themselves, a witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ and the σ-algebra $L(\partial S)$ built with them are §IX.34 (gap G.108, closed).

**Witnesses** (V9.53). *Tools.* Measure zero of Definition 9.4.5 is local ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_image_of_local⟧, holds for subsingletons ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_of_subsingleton⟧, and on $\mathbb R^2$ is Lebesgue measure zero ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_rn2_iff⟧. On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ every local branching structure restricts to a tame one, on the domain of a natural representation ⟦Chapter9/Measure · exists_tameBranchingStructure_trivial_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_trivial_rn⟧, and $\pi$ is injective ⟦Chapter9/Measure · injective_π_trivial_rn⟧. *Example 9.3.5.* The graph sheets of §9.4 carry a `SheetMeasureGeometry` ⟦Chapter9/Measure · graphSheetMeasureGeometry⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · graphNull⟧; for the $\Theta$ of the two graphs $G^{++}$, $G^{--}$, which touch at $0$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · zero_mem_supp_theta935⟧, the point $|0|$ has measure zero ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935_zero⟧, $S$ does not ⟦Chapter9/Measure · not_isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935⟧, and both are in $L(S)$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · lebesgueSigma_theta935⟧. *The plane.* For $\Theta = 1$ on $\mathbb R^2$, with the open subsets of $\mathbb R^2$ as sheets and Lebesgue null sets ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeSheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeNull⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeSheet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isSmoothSubmanifold_univ_rn2⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · mem_supp_thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_thetaPlane⟧, some member of $L(S)$ is not Borel ⟦Chapter9/Measure · exists_mem_lebesgueSigma_not_borel_thetaPlane⟧: every subset of the null axis is in $L(S)$, there are $2^{\mathfrak c}$ of them, and only $\mathfrak c$ Borel sets.

### IX.20 §9.5: the isotropy factors (Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (2017: Lemmas 9.18, 9.19))

The measures $\mu_\omega$ of Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 are local weighted integrals of a form over the sheets, divided by $\#G_x$ or $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$. This subsection gives what the proofs of Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 rest on, the orders of the isotropy groups and the decompositions of the preimages; the measure identities themselves are stated and proved in §IX.31 (Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11, Proposition 9.5.13 (1)) and §IX.33 (Proposition 9.5.13 (2)), and rows V9.54–V9.56 are explicit.

**Lemma 9.5.9 (2017: 9.18)** (V9.54). **The text's proof** identifies $H = \{g \mid g * y = y\}$ with $G_y$, writes $G = \bigcup_{r \in R} rH$, chooses $V(y)$ invariant under $H$ and disjoint from its other translates, notes that $\tilde M_j = V \cap M_j$ is a branching structure on $V$, decomposes the preimage of $K$ as $\bigcup_r \varphi_r(\tilde K)$, and uses $\#R = \#G/\#H$. **The formalized part.** *Step 1, $\#R \cdot \#G_y = \#G_x$* ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_quotient_stabilizer_mul_card_isotropy⟧: the stabilizer $H$ of $y$ for the action of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ is isomorphic to $G_y$ by the natural representation (Chapter 7) ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_stabilizer_iff_Φ⟧, and $R$ is `Quotient.out` on $G_x/H$. *Step 2, the slice* ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_slice⟧: inside any neighbourhood of $y$ there is an open $V$ with $\varphi_g(V) = V$ for $g \in H$ and $\varphi_g(V) \cap V = \emptyset$ for $g \notin H$: separate $y$ from $\varphi_g(y) \ne y$ for the finitely many $g \notin H$, and make the neighbourhood $H$-invariant. *Step 3, the preimage.* $|\varphi_g(z)| = |z|$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_Φ⟧, so $\varphi_g$ maps $M_U = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U$ to itself, $\Theta$ being a functor ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_MU⟧; for $K \subseteq |M_U \cap V|$, $M_U \cap \pi^{-1}(K) = \bigcup_{g} \varphi_g(M_U \cap V \cap \pi^{-1}(K))$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion⟧, the same with $g$ running over the representatives $r$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion_quotient⟧, and the union over $R$ is disjoint ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Φ_out⟧. The restriction $\tilde M_j$ is §IX.3's `restrictAt`: the project's structures pass through their base point, so at $y$ the sheets through $y$ are kept.

**Lemma 9.5.10** (V9.55), new in the 2021 edition. *Step 1.* $\#T_x \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$ for the subgroup $T_x$ acting trivially near $x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_mul_card_trivialSubgroup⟧. *Step 2.* Under LUC for the given $U(x)$ (Definition 7.2.18, `NaturalRep.HasLUC`), $T_x$ is the kernel of the representation ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_trivialSubgroup⟧, hence lies in every stabilizer ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_le_stabilizer⟧, and corresponds to $T_y$ under $H \cong G_y$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy_mem_trivialSubgroup_iff⟧, so $\#T_y = \#T_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_trivialSubgroup_eq⟧. *Step 3, (9.23).* Dividing Step 1 of Lemma 9.5.9 by $\#T_x = \#T_y$ gives $\#R \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_y = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_quotient_stabilizer_mul_card_effIsotropy⟧.

**Lemma 9.5.11 (2017: 9.19)** (V9.56). The orders $\#G_x$ and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ are invariant along morphisms, by conjugation with $\varphi$ (Lemma 7.2.6) ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_isotropy_eq_of_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_of_mor⟧. A functor is constant on orbits ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.eq_of_π_eq⟧, so for structures on $U$, $U'$ and any map $\hat\varphi$ of $U$ onto $U'$ with $|\hat\varphi(z)| = |z|$, $|M_U| = |M_{U'}|$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.image_π_MU_eq⟧; the maps $\varphi_g$ of a natural representation are such maps ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_hyps⟧. The "change of variables" in the integrals is the invariance of the sheet integration under the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, and gives Lemma 9.5.11 as a measure identity in §IX.31.

**Proposition 9.5.13** (V9.57), new in the 2021 edition. *(1)* For effective $X$, $T_x = \{1\}$, so $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_of_isEffective⟧ and the normalizing factors of the two integrals agree. *(2)* The reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$ (Chapter 7) has the object M-polyfold of $X$, with Hausdorff and paracompact morphism space as instances (Hausdorff under LUC); functors ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_reduced_iff⟧ and local branching structures ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.toReduced⟧ of $X$ and $X_R$ coincide, and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G^R_x = \#(G^R_x)^{\mathrm{eff}}$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_reduced⟧. The identity of the integrals, $\oint_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \int_{\hat\Theta_R}\omega$, is §IX.33 (row V9.57 restated).

### IX.21 Appendix §9.6.1: Lemmas 9.6.1 and 9.6.2, Definition 9.6.3 and Lemma 9.6.4

**In place of "measure zero."** The text's proofs of Lemmas 9.6.1, 9.6.2 and 9.6.4 remove sets of smaller dimension or not containing a sheet near the point, "of measure zero", and move a point slightly. The formalization uses a topological covering lemma instead, with no Lebesgue measure and no Baire category. *Step 1.* If $A \cap W \subseteq N$ for an open $W \ni a$, then $\dim_aA \le \dim_aN$, by the inclusion of the chart tangent spaces ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.HasDimAt.le_of_inter_subset⟧. *Step 2,* the covering lemma ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.exists_mem_forall_notMem⟧: a nonempty open piece of a $k$-dimensional submanifold is not covered by finitely many submanifolds of smaller dimension closed in an open set, by induction on the family: removing one closed set of smaller dimension leaves a nonempty open piece, by Step 1. *Step 3,* "moving $z$ slightly": a point of the piece off all the given sets ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsGeneric⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_isGeneric⟧.

**Lemma 9.6.1** (V9.58) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_1⟧. *Two structures at $x$ have the same top dimension* ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.topDim⟧. If the first has top dimension $k$ and the second $\ell < k$, a generic point of a $k$-dimensional sheet of the first has $\Theta > 0$ by the first structure and $\Theta = 0$ by the second. So $\dim_\Theta(x)$ is well defined ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq⟧, $-\infty$ off the support ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq_bot⟧.

**Lemma 9.6.2** (V9.59) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_2⟧. *The unions $M^k_U$ of the top-dimensional sheets agree on $U \cap U'$* ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.topUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_topUnion_iff_of_mem⟧: a generic point of $M^k_U \setminus M'^k_{U'}$ would have $\Theta > 0$ by the first structure and, off the lower-dimensional sheets of the second, $\Theta = 0$.

**Definition 9.6.3** (V9.60) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopGoodPoint⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopBadPoint⟧, as in the text. At points top-good for both structures the top parts agree, with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_isTopGoodPoint⟧: near such a point the top part is $\sigma \cdot 1_M$ for both, and $\sigma$ is read off $\Theta$ at a generic point of $M$.

**Lemma 9.6.4** (V9.61). *Top-goodness does not depend on the structure.* **The text's proof**: near a top-good $z$, $\Theta = \sigma \cdot \delta_M + \Theta_0 + \cdots + \Theta_{k-1}$; a point of $M$ near $z$ off the lower-dimensional sets has $\Theta = \sigma$, and "similarly as good points", $z$ is top-good for the second structure. **As we read it, this needs that the top weight of the second structure at $y$ is $\sigma$**, an argument the text does not give: the second structure could a priori have, through $y$, several top-dimensional sheets with tangent spaces that differ. **The formalized proof** makes this step the hypothesis `TopMultiplicity` ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.TopMultiplicity⟧: at a point where $\Theta$ equals $\sigma$ on generic points of a $k$-dimensional sheet, the top weight of any structure is $\sigma$. Under it the lemma holds ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_4⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isTopBadPoint_iff⟧, the top parts agree on $U \cap U'$ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_topMultiplicity⟧, and Proposition 9.1.12 follows by the descending induction of p. 454: subtract the top parts ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.subOn⟧ and repeat ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_topMultiplicity⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity⟧. Witnesses: $k = 0$ on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_zero⟧, and $k \ge n$ on $\mathbb R^n$, where an $n$-dimensional submanifold is a neighbourhood of each of its points ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · rnPolyfold_mem_nhds_of_hasDimAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · topMultiplicity_rn_of_le⟧; so Proposition 9.1.12 holds on $\mathbb R^0$ and $\mathbb R^1$ unconditionally ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · proposition_9_1_12_rn_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · proposition_9_1_12_rn_one⟧. The step itself is proved from the graph representation in §IX.22 ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicityAt_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_4_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧, and now on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicityAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicity⟧, so Lemma 9.6.4 holds for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_6_4_general⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · isTopBadPoint_iff_general⟧. In the proof the top-good point is called $z$ and then $y$.

### IX.22 Proposition 9.6.5, the formula on p. 457, and the proof of Proposition 9.1.12

**Proposition 9.6.5** (V9.62) ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.proposition_9_6_5⟧. *At a top-bad $x$, a class $\Xi$ of top-dimensional indices with one tangent space splits as $I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$ with sequences of top-good points $x^e_j \to x$ lying on $M_i$ exactly for $i \in I^e$.* In (1) the text writes "$I_k = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$"; the $I^e$ being subsets of $\Xi$, it reads as $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$. **The slice form.** Under `HasGraphChartAt` at $x$, for every class and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite top slice in $W$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopSlice⟧: it meets each sheet of the class once, misses the other top-dimensional sheets and all lower-dimensional ones, using a generic slice (§IX.9). Top slices in every $W$ replace the top-good sequences.

**The formula on p. 457** ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_sum_slices⟧. $\Theta_k(x) = \sum_\Xi \sum_{y \in \text{slice}} \Theta(y)$; for one class the slice gives $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_sum_of_isTopSlice⟧. The text's $\Theta_k(x^k_e)$ uses points $x^k_e$ not introduced, presumably points $x^e_j$ of the sequences. **The independence of the right-hand side**, which the text asserts while $\Xi$, $I^e$ and $x^e$ come from the first structure, is an argument the text does not give. It is proved by choosing one slice for the sheets of both structures, off all lower-dimensional sets of both, so that both class weights are the same sum of values of $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧. The same grouping proves `TopMultiplicityAt` ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.TopMultiplicityAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧, on $\mathbb R^m$ in all dimensions ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_rn⟧. A per-dimension graph representation is not enough here: the lower-dimensional sheets through $y$ must be avoided in the chart in which the top sheets are graphs, which is why one chart for all dimensions was asked. One cone per tangent space in that chart suffices, since the slice for a class only uses the cone of that class; with this change the slices exist at every point of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_slice_of_classGraphChart⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_generic_slice_general⟧, and Proposition 9.6.5 and the formula on p. 457 hold for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_6_5_general⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · sum_class_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · dimPart_topDim_eq⟧.

**The proof of Proposition 9.1.12.** With the top parts agreeing near $x$, subtract them from both structures and repeat in lower dimensions ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧; on $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn⟧, and on every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_12⟧. "This completes the proof of Proposition 9.6.5" (p. 457) refers to Proposition 9.1.12, Proposition 9.6.5 being stated without proof.

### IX.24 What is not formalized

Gaps G.93–G.109 are closed, G.110 is formalized in part, for Remark 9.5.20 only, and no gap of the chapter is open.

- **G.110 (in part), Remark 9.5.20.** Formalized: the M-polyfold $X \subseteq \mathbb R \times \mathbb C$, $\partial X = \{(\pm 1, 0)\}$, $\mathbb Z_3 \ltimes X$ with the local unique continuation property, $\partial X$ as a sub-ep-groupoid, and the effective isotropy at a point of $\partial X$, three read in $X$ and one read in $\partial X$ (§IX.39). Not formalized: $\Theta(t, z) = \delta_0(z)$ with its orientation, $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df = \frac13(\phi(1) - \phi(-1))$ and the two boundary integrals, estimated at 2,340–3,790 lines; the main risks are sc-smooth partitions of unity on the $c_0$ scale of the example and the tameness of $M$ at the infinite-dimensional ends. Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 themselves are proved as printed for every $n \ge 1$ (§§IX.36–IX.38).
- **Closed: G.109**, Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 as printed for every $n \ge 1$ (§§IX.36–IX.38), and with it the Theorems 9.5.17, 9.5.18 part of G.110.
- **Left inside closed gaps.** Local finiteness of the decomposition of Proposition 9.1.11 off the support without a bound on the dimensions (G.96). The form $f \cdot \omega$ for a non-constant sc-smooth $f$, read through the evaluation (G.107); in dimension $0$ the integration is the abstract one ⟦Chapter9/PointIntegration · pointIntegration⟧. The orientations of the faces of the faces, the last sentence of the caption of Figure 9.1 (G.103). The comparison of the face-by-face null sets with those taken in the ambient charts (G.108), and of the essential points in M-polyfold charts with those in corner charts (G.105), which no statement needs. A witness of Lemma 9.2.13 at a boundary point.
- **Nothing to formalize.** Remarks 9.3.1, 9.3.11 and 9.5.8 (the last has no content beyond Lemma 9.5.11); Remarks 9.5.12 and 9.5.19 and §§9.6.2–9.6.3 discuss open questions.

### IX.25 What the formalization taught us

The definition of a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid is local and says nothing about how the local pictures fit together, and three statements that read as uniqueness claims, Proposition 9.1.11, Definition 9.2.16 and Lemma 9.3.4, turned out to depend on exactly that: an indicator can be split into a point and a punctured line, a characterization asked only on its own support is met by zero, and a lower-dimensional sheet through a bad point escapes the good points. In each case the repair is a condition that ties the object to the local branching structures of $\Theta$ (local decompositions, the largest support, equidimensionality). The analytic heart of §9.2, the graph representation of tangent sheets near a bad point, is a statement about one chart in which sheets of all dimensions are graphs; separated from the counting it serves, it became a single hypothesis, true on $\mathbb R^m$ by the inverse function theorem, from which Proposition 9.1.12, Theorem 9.2.1, Lemma 9.6.4 and Proposition 9.6.5 follow. Two steps the text leaves to "similarly" (Lemma 9.6.4) or asserts (the independence on p. 457) needed that both structures be compared on one common slice. Finally, "measure zero" in §9.6.1 is not needed: the arguments only use that a piece of a $k$-dimensional submanifold is not covered by finitely many thinner ones, which is topology. In §9.5 the opposite happens: the measure-theoretic part needs only that the null sets of the sheets form a local σ-ideal compatible on overlaps, and that compatibility is exactly where dimensions must agree; and of the isotropy computations that normalize the integrals, everything except the integrals themselves is finite group theory.

The second round of work taught more. *The level-0 hypotheses were one fact.* Every level-0 statement of §9.2 (the cone, the graphs, invariance of domain, the local constancy of rank, the level-1 continuity of frames) follows from one observation: the lift $1_0^1 \circ r$ of an sc⁺-retraction to level $1$ is $C^1$ on the retract, so that Mathlib's inverse function theorem applies on level $1$ and the conclusions descend through the inclusion. The project's first hypothesis, one cone for all submanifolds through a boundary point, was more than the text uses; one cone per tangent space is enough, and holds everywhere (§IX.27). *A tacit finiteness in §9.5.* The text integrates $\omega$ over measurable subsets of the sheets, which presupposes $\int|\omega| < \infty$. For the sheets themselves this follows from compactness and the properness of $\mathrm{cl}\,U(x)$ (§IX.32); for the boundary sheets $\partial_1 M_i$ it was first an added hypothesis of Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 (§§IX.34–IX.35), and it follows from the continuity of Part I's chart forms up to the corners and, toward the frontier of $U(x)$, from a comparison of tangent spaces with other structures, in which $\{d = 1\}$ depends on the tangent space alone (§§IX.36–IX.37). The same proof needs facts the text does not state: that the sheets are Lindelöf, so that countably many neighbourhoods suffice in Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5; that $M_i \cap \mathrm{supp}\,\beta_k$ is compact in the proof of Stokes' theorem; that chart changes are differentiable along a finite-dimensional submanifold for the level-0 norms, which makes Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.5 chart independent; and, for Proposition 9.5.13 (2), a natural action of $G^R_x$ built from that of $G_x$ under the local unique continuation property. *Some hypotheses are not used.* Proposition 9.1.9 does not use the paracompactness of $|X|$, the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$ needs no tameness, only reduced codimension $1$, and the effective clause of Lemma 9.5.11 needs no local unique continuation. *Examples are more rigid than they look.* In Example 9.3.5 every one-dimensional submanifold inside the support through the origin has tangent $\mathbb R(1,0)$ and meets every vertical line, and this rigidity determines all orientations: a three-parameter family, of which six have integer weights (§IX.29). *Paracompactness through metrizability.* In Remark 9.1.4 the step from a paracompact neighbourhood to a component compact set goes through metrizability, since a subspace of a paracompact space need not be paracompact (§IX.26).

*Remark 9.5.20 needs infinite dimensions.* In finite dimensions a finite group that fixes a boundary point and acts trivially on the face acts trivially on the inward normal as well, so the effective isotropy of a boundary point is the same read in $X$ and in $\partial X$. The remark's example has to be an M-polyfold whose local dimension jumps at its boundary, $0 \to 3 \to 0$ (§IX.39).

### IX.26 Remark 9.1.4, Proposition 9.1.9 (2017: 9.1) and Remark 9.1.10 (2017: 9.2)

**Remark 9.1.4** (V9.63), new in the 2021 edition ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_4⟧. *A paracompact $L \subseteq |X|$ is metrizable, and if $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is component compact, the paracompactness in Definition 9.1.2 (1) is automatic.* **The text's argument**, followed exactly. *Step 1.* $|X|$ is locally metrizable, regular and Hausdorff (Theorem 7.3.1), so a paracompact subspace is metrizable by Smirnov's theorem ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_4_metrizable⟧. *Step 2.* A component compact $K$ has an open paracompact neighbourhood $U$ (Corollary 7.3.8), metrizable by Step 1 ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_4_exists_nhds⟧. *Step 3,* which the text does not spell out: $K$ is paracompact. A subspace of a paracompact space need not be paracompact, but a subspace of the metrizable $U$ is metrizable, hence paracompact ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_of_isComponentCompact⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_4_paracompactSpace⟧. *Step 4.* So a functor with the other properties of Definition 9.1.2 and component compact $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_of_isComponentCompact⟧, compact supports in particular ⟦Chapter9/OrbitSubsetMetrizable · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_of_isCompact⟧.

**Proposition 9.1.9 (2)** (V9.64), *for $\Theta$ of orbifold type, $X$ induces a natural orbifold structure on $Z = |\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$*. **The text's proof.** Near $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ all sheets coincide, $\Theta = 1_{M_x}$; the groupoid with objects $\bigsqcup_x M_x$ and morphisms $\bigsqcup M(x, x')$ is étale and proper, the functor $\beta : M \to Z$ induces a homeomorphism $|\beta|$, and other choices give an equivalent structure. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, one sheet.* $\Theta$ takes only the values $0$ and $1$, so a sheet missing a point of the support near $x$ would make $0 < \Theta < 1$ there; hence $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U(x) = M_i$ for every $i$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportOrbifold · EpGroupoid.supp_inter_eq_of_isOrbifoldType⟧. *Step 2.* So $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $X$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportOrbifold · EpGroupoid.isSmoothSubmanifold_supp_of_isOrbifoldType⟧, saturated, hence an ep-subgroupoid, whose full subcategory is an ep-groupoid (Proposition 7.1.22) ⟦Chapter9/SupportOrbifold · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_supp_of_isOrbifoldType⟧. *Step 3.* For a saturated $A$, the map $|A| \to \pi(A)$ induced by the inclusion is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/SupportOrbifold · EpGroupoid.orbitSuppHomeomorph⟧. This gives a choice-free form ⟦Chapter9/SupportOrbifold · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_9_two⟧. *Step 4, the text's groupoid.* For a choice of local branching structures at all points of the support ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · SheetChoice⟧, the sets $M_x = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U(x)$ form an open cover ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · sheetCover⟧, and the text's $M$ is the refinement of Proposition 10.1.3 of the full ep-subgroupoid along it ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · textGroupoid⟧: objects $(x, y)$ with $y \in M_x$, morphisms $((x, x'), \varphi)$ with $s(\varphi) \in M_x$, $t(\varphi) \in M_{x'}$. It is an ep-groupoid, $|\beta|$ is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · textOrbitHomeomorph⟧, and $M \to \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ is an equivalence over $Z$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · proposition_9_1_9_two_text⟧. *Step 5, independence.* A refinement of covers gives an equivalence of refinements ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · OpenCover.isEquivalence_refineFunctor⟧; for two choices $c$, $c'$ the common refinement by the $M_x \cap M'_{x'}$ gives $M_c \leftarrow M_{c,c'} \to M_{c'}$, a generalized isomorphism of Chapter 10 (Theorem 10.3.10) compatible with the homeomorphisms to $Z$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · proposition_9_1_9_two_independent⟧. "Equivalent orbifold structure" is read as this generalized isomorphism. The construction assumes $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \ne \emptyset$; for $\Theta = 0$ there is nothing to construct.

**Proposition 9.1.9 (1)**, *for $\Theta$ of manifold type, a natural manifold structure on $Z$*. *Step 1.* Between two objects of the support there is at most one morphism, so the isotropy of the ep-subgroupoid is trivial ⟦Chapter9/SupportManifold · EpGroupoid.subsingleton_isotropy_of_isManifoldType⟧, and $\pi$ is injective on the domain of a natural representation ⟦Chapter9/SupportManifold · EpGroupoid.injOn_π_of_subsingleton_isotropy⟧, the text's "$\Psi_x$ is injective". *Step 2, descent.* A general lemma: a continuous, open, surjective, locally injective map $p$ from an M-polyfold to a Hausdorff paracompact space, such that $p(a) = p(b)$ is realized near $a$ by an sc-smooth $f$ with $f(a) = b$ and $p \circ f = p$ ⟦Chapter9/DescentPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsDescentMap⟧, pushes the charts forward ⟦Chapter9/DescentPolyfold · MPolyfold.descChart⟧ to compatible charts, an M-polyfold structure on the target ⟦Chapter9/DescentPolyfold · MPolyfold.descend⟧ for which $p$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/DescentPolyfold · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_descend⟧. *Step 3.* The orbit map $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \to Z$ is such a map, with $f = t \circ (s|U(\varphi))^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportManifold · EpGroupoid.isDescentMap_orbitSupp⟧, which gives the structure ⟦Chapter9/SupportManifold · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_9_one⟧. *Step 4, "natural"* is read as uniqueness: any two M-polyfold structures on $Z$ for which the orbit map is a local sc-diffeomorphism agree ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidNaturality · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_9_one_unique⟧. The paracompactness of $|X|$, a hypothesis of the proposition, is not used.

**Remark 9.1.10** (V9.65, narrower). *For $\Theta$ $n$-dimensional with $d_{|X|} = 0$ on $Z$, the structures are classical.* *Step 1.* The support is an $n$-dimensional submanifold of degeneracy index $0$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportClassicalStructures · EpGroupoid.isSubmanifoldOfDim_supp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SupportClassicalStructures · EpGroupoid.degIndex_eq_zero_of_mem_supp⟧, so it has a corner structure of dimension $n$ (§IX.16), which a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism carries to $Z$ ⟦Chapter9/SupportClassicalStructures · MPolyfold.HasCornerStructureOfDim.of_isLocalScDiffeo_surjective⟧. *Step 2.* In case (1) $Z$ is a Mathlib manifold, `IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞` ⟦Chapter9/SupportClassicalStructures · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_10_manifold⟧, and the orbit map is a Mathlib local diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidEtale · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_10_manifold_proj⟧. *Step 3.* In case (2), for every choice, the object and morphism spaces of $M$ are Mathlib $n$-manifolds ⟦Chapter9/SupportClassicalStructures · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_10_orbifold⟧, and source, target, unit, inverse and the equivalence to the support are Mathlib local diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidEtale · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_10_orbifold_etale⟧, since a local sc-diffeomorphism between such corner structures of degeneracy index $0$ is a Mathlib local diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/SupportGroupoidEtale · MPolyfold.isLocalDiffeomorph_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧. The row is narrower for two reasons: the dimension $n$ is fixed, a Mathlib manifold having one model space while the text's $Z$ may have components of different dimensions; and the composition of $M$ is sc-smooth, as for every ep-groupoid, but not stated as Mathlib-smooth, Mathlib having no notion of an orbifold. Witness: the $x$-axis of $\mathbb R^2$ ⟦Chapter9/XAxisWitness · EpGroupoid.remark_9_1_10_hypotheses_axis⟧.

### IX.27 The level-0 facts on every M-polyfold: Remark 9.1.1 (2017: 9.1), Lemmas 9.2.9–9.2.11 (2017: 9.6–9.8), invariance of domain, and the level-1 continuity

These are the facts the first version of this part took as hypotheses (gaps G.93, G.97, G.98, G.100, all closed). **The text** works at level $0$ in a chart, with $x = 0$ in a partial quadrant $C$ and $M$ the image of an sc⁺-retraction: $L = T_0M$ meets $C$ in a set with interior in $L$ (Lemma 9.2.9); $M$ is a graph $a + B(a)$ over a cone in $L \cap C$ with $DB(0) = 0$ (Lemma 9.2.10), by inverting $\Phi(a) = a + PB(a)$ (Lemma 9.2.11); $\dim T_mM$ is locally constant (Remark 9.1.1); a point in the interior of the sets it meets is "clearly" good (Lemma 9.2.7 (2)). The text treats $B$ as $C^1$ at level $0$, while the retraction is only sc-smooth.

**The level-1 calculus of an sc⁺-retraction.** *Step 1.* For an sc⁺-retraction $r$ the lift $1_0^1 \circ r$ into level $1$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · plusLift⟧ is $C^1$ on level $1$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasFDerivWithinAt_plusLift⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · continuousOn_plusDeriv⟧, strictly differentiable ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_strict_plusLift⟧, and its derivative brought down by the inclusion $\iota$ is $Dr$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · toBase_plusDeriv⟧. All estimates are proved on level $1$ and brought down by $\iota$; on the finite-dimensional $T = \mathrm{range}\,Dr(z)$ the two norms are equivalent. *Step 2, the chord estimate* ($DB(0) = 0$): chords of the retract are close to $T$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_approx⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_strict_range⟧. *Step 3, Lemma 9.2.9:* $Dr$ maps into the cone of the quadrant ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · nonneg_scDeriv⟧, so a closed ball of $T$ around an admissible direction $h_1$, scaled by small $s$, stays in $C$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · ScRetraction.exists_cone⟧. *Step 4, Lemmas 9.2.10 and 9.2.11:* the projection of the retract onto $T$ approximates the identity of $T$ on small balls, so Mathlib's surjectivity theorem for maps approximating a linear map (`ApproximatesLinearOn`) inverts it over a cone, uniformly in the foot point ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_graph_unif⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_graph⟧, and over a ball of $T$ at interior points ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_graph_ball⟧. *Step 5, invariance of domain:* if two sc⁺-retractions $r_1$, $r_2$ have the same tangent space at $z$, every point $b$ of the first retract near $z$ with $r_2(b)$ in the first retract is fixed by $r_2$. On level $1$, with $u$ the difference of the lifts of $r_2(b)$ and $b$, the chord estimate for both retractions gives $\|u\|_1 \le c\eta\|u\|_1$ with $c\eta < 1$, so $u = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · eq_of_range_eq⟧. *Step 6, local constancy of the rank:* the idempotents $Dr(z)$, read on level $1$, depend continuously on the point in the operator norm, and an idempotent at distance $< 1$ from another has rank at most that of the other ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · finrank_range_le_of_norm_sub_lt⟧; applied both ways, the rank is locally constant along the retract ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · eventually_finrank_eq⟧.

**In an M-polyfold.** *Step 7.* A submanifold $A$ is, in a chart, the range of a chart sc⁺-retraction $t$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_plusRetraction⟧, whose derivative has range the chart tangent space ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · chartTangent_eq_range⟧, and on $A$ the level-1 lift of the chart is $1_0^1 \circ t$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · levelLift_eq_plusLift⟧; so the dimension is the rank of $Dt$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasDimAt_finrank⟧. *Step 8, consequences.* Remark 9.1.1 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · MPolyfold.hasLocallyConstantDimAt⟧ (Step 6), invariance of domain ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasDomainInvarianceAt⟧ (Step 5), the level-1 continuity along submanifolds ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasContinuousLevelOneOn⟧ (Step 7). *Step 9, the graph representation.* Each tangent space $T_xA$ has its admissible cone of directions ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · goodDirections⟧, and every submanifold through $x$ is a graph over it ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · isGraphChartAt_goodDirections⟧. This is the class form `HasClassGraphChartAt`, one cone per tangent space, at every point ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasClassGraphChartAt⟧; at interior points one cone and the ball form serve all submanifolds ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · exists_chart_mem_interior_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · isGraphBallAt_of_mem_interior⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralLevelZero · hasGraphChartAt_of_mem_interior⟧.

**What follows** ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_slice_of_classGraphChart⟧. The slice arguments of §§IX.9–IX.10 and IX.21–IX.22 only use the cone of the class at hand, so they run with the class form: tangent slices at every point ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · hasTangentSlicesAt⟧, generic slices missing finitely many thinner sets ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_generic_slice_general⟧, `TopMultiplicity` ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicity⟧, Proposition 9.1.12 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_12⟧, Lemma 9.6.4 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_6_4_general⟧, Proposition 9.6.5 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_6_5_general⟧, the independence of Theorem 9.2.1 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · hasIndependentTangentSums⟧, Lemma 9.2.7 (2) ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_2_7_2_general⟧, Proposition 9.1.11 in the reading of §IX.4 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · existsUnique_localDimDecomposition_general⟧, and, with the boundary argument of §IX.15, Lemma 9.3.4 ⟦Chapter9/GeneralBoundaryPoints · lemma_9_3_4_general⟧. Proposition 9.2.8 itself stays in slice form (V9.22).

### IX.28 Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 (2017: 9.13, 9.14) for the sheets of an M-polyfold, and Lemma 9.5.2 (2017: 9.16) with Lebesgue null sets

The sheets of an M-polyfold carry no manifold charts of their own, so Definitions 9.4.1 and 9.4.5 are read in the M-polyfold charts $\psi$ of the ambient space, as the text itself does in the proof of Lemma 9.4.4 (gaps G.105, G.106, closed).

**Definition 9.4.1 in M-polyfold charts.** $T^K_zM$ is the span of Mathlib's tangent cone of $\psi(K)$ at $\psi(z)$ in $E_0$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · chartRelTangent⟧, and $z$ is essential if it is a limit of points where $T^K M = TM$ in every chart ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · IsRelTangentFull⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · chartEssentialSet⟧. *Step 1.* For $K \subseteq M$, $T^K_zM \subseteq T_zM$, since chords of the chart retract are approximated by its tangent space (§IX.27, Step 2) ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · chartRelTangent_le⟧. *Step 2.* Conversely $T_zM \subseteq T^M_zM$: for level-1 directions $p$ into the quadrant, $Dr(z)p$ is a limit direction of the retract, and these span the range of $Dr(z)$ since $E_1$ is dense in $E_0$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · ScRetraction.range_scDeriv_subset_span_tangentConeAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · chartTangent_subset_chartRelTangent⟧. So every point of $M$ is essential for $M \subseteq M$ and the reading is not degenerate ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · chartEssentialSet_self⟧. *Step 3, chart independence.* On level $0$ a chart change is only continuous, but along a finite-dimensional submanifold it is differentiable for the level-0 norms: the points of the chart image lie on level $1$ with level-1 distance controlled by level-0 distance, because the chart retraction is sc⁺ ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · ScRetraction.exists_lift_lipschitz⟧, and an sc¹ map is differentiable from level $1$ to level $0$ (Proposition 1.2.1) ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · ScRetraction.hasFDerivWithinAt_of_isSc1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · exists_hasFDerivWithinAt_transition⟧. The derivative maps tangent cones to tangent cones ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · exists_clm_tangentCone_chart_change⟧, so "$T^K_zM = T_zM$" in one chart gives it in all ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · isRelTangentFull_of_chart⟧.

**Lemma 9.4.4** (V9.42, narrower) ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · lemma_9_4_4_chart⟧. *For $n$-dimensional $M$, $M'$, $K = M \cap M'$ has the same essential points in $M$ and in $M'$.* The text's reduction to $T^D_0N$ is the pointwise statement, which holds in each chart separately: $T^K_zM = T_zM$ iff $T^K_zM' = T_zM'$, both tangent spaces being $n$-dimensional and containing $T^K_z$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · isRelTangentFull_iff⟧. At essential points $T_zM = T_zM'$, the note in Definition 9.4.7 ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssentialChart2021 · submanifoldTangent_eq_of_mem_chartEssentialSet⟧. For different dimensions the lemma does not hold as we read it (§IX.17).

**Definition 9.4.5 in M-polyfold charts.** *Step 1.* `HNull d s`: the $d$-dimensional Hausdorff measure of $s$ vanishes ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · HNull⟧. A subset $C$ of a sheet has $n$-dimensional measure zero if its separable pieces have $n$-null chart images in every chart ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · IsHNull⟧; $E_0$ need not be separable, and a non-separable set has infinite Hausdorff measure, but the sheets are locally separable, so nothing is lost. It is a local σ-ideal ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · isHNull_iUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · isHNull_of_local⟧. *Step 2, why these are Lebesgue null sets.* Near a point of a sheet the tangent projection $p$ onto $T_xM$ satisfies $\|(\psi a - \psi b) - p(\psi a - \psi b)\| \le \frac12\|\psi a - \psi b\|$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · exists_half_approx⟧, so it is bi-Lipschitz there, and on $\mathbb R^n$ the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure is Lebesgue measure ⟦Chapter9/SheetNullBridge · hNull_iff_volume_euclidean⟧. On a tame sheet these are exactly the null sets of Definition 9.4.5 in the smooth charts of the manifold with corners of §IX.16 ⟦Chapter9/SheetNullBridge · isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_cornerChartedSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetNullBridge · isHNull_iff_isMeasureZero_sheet⟧. *Step 3, chart independence:* a map Lipschitz at each point sends separable null sets to null sets ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · hNull_image_of_pointwise_lipschitz⟧, which with Step 3 above gives ⟦Chapter9/SheetChartChange · isHNull_of_forall_exists_chart⟧. *Step 4, positivity:* an $n$-dimensional sheet is not null in itself, its tangent projection containing a ball of $T_xM$ (§IX.27, the graph over a cone) ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · not_isHNull_of_hasDimAt⟧. *Step 5.* So the null sets form a `SheetNullSets` on the $n$-dimensional submanifolds with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/SheetNull · sheetNullSets⟧; the transfer property is immediate, since the definition does not mention the sheet.

**Lemma 9.4.6** (V9.44) ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · lemma_9_4_6_chart⟧. *For $K \subseteq M$, $M$ $n$-dimensional, $K \setminus K^e$ has measure zero.* The proof of §IX.17 transported through the tangent projection: every limit direction of $p(\psi(A))$ is the projection of a limit direction of $\psi(A)$, chords of $M$ being close to the finite-dimensional tangent space ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · exists_mem_tangentConeAt_proj⟧; the points of $K$ where $T^K \ne T$ project to points of $p(\psi(K))$ where the tangent cone does not span, a Lebesgue null set by the density theorem ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · exists_hNull_chart_not_isRelTangentFull⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · isHNull_setOf_not_isRelTangentFull⟧. The $n$-dimensional submanifolds carry the `SheetGeometry` and `SheetMeasureGeometry` of §§IX.17, IX.19 with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · sheetGeometry⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetEssential · sheetMeasureGeometry⟧.

**For $n$-dimensional $\Theta$, and Lemma 9.5.2** (V9.50, explicit). *Step 1.* Every local branching structure of an $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ has $n$-dimensional sheets ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · isOfDim_of_isNDimensional⟧: at a point of the support, a structure with $n$-dimensional sheets and any other structure have the same tangent sum (Theorem 9.2.1), so each sheet of the second has the tangent space of a sheet of the first. *Step 2.* So Lemmas 9.4.4 and 9.4.6 hold for the sheets of every structure of $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lemma_9_4_4_of_isNDimensional⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lemma_9_4_6_of_isNDimensional⟧, and Lemma 9.4.8, Propositions 9.4.9, 9.4.10 follow (§IX.17). *Step 3.* Definition 9.5.1 with these null sets ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · IsMeasureZeroH⟧, and Lemma 9.5.2 as printed: null preimages for some choice of structures iff for every structure ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lemma_9_5_2_of_isNDimensional⟧, and for tame $\Theta$ iff for a choice of tame structures ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lemma_9_5_2_tame⟧; the proof is that of §IX.19 with one class of sheets. *Step 4.* The sets of measure zero form a σ-ideal ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · isSigmaIdeal_isMeasureZeroH⟧, $S$ is not one of them ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · not_isMeasureZeroH_orbitSupp⟧, and $L(S)$ is the completion of §IX.19 ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · remark_9_5_3_H⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · lebesgueSigmaH_eq⟧. Across dimensions the transfer does not hold as we read it ⟦Chapter9/SheetMeasure · isHNull_mixed_dim⟧.

### IX.29 Example 9.3.5 (2017: 9.1): all orientations of $\Theta$

**The text** says that $\Theta$ has "four different possibilities to orient". With the first claim of §IX.15 settled, the question is what all orientations of $\Theta$ are (gap G.101, closed; V9.33, narrower). The support is $G^{++} \cup G^{--}$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.supp_example935Theta⟧, and $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \setminus \{0\}$ consists of four open arcs, $G^{++}$ and $G^{--}$ over $s > 0$ and over $s < 0$; $\Theta = 1$ on the arcs and $\Theta(0) = 2$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.example935Theta_eq_one⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.example935Theta_zero⟧.

**The sheets inside the support.** Every sheet of a local branching structure of $\Theta$ lies in the support and is $1$-dimensional (§IX.28). *Step 1, velocities.* A curve in the support through a point $z$ of $G_b$ has velocity in $\mathbb R(1, \beta_b'(z_0))$: off the origin it runs in $G_b$; at the origin $|\gamma_1| = \beta^{++}(\gamma_0)$ is $o(t)$ since $\beta^{++}$ is flat, so the velocity is horizontal ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.hasDerivAt_snd_eq_of_mem_Z⟧. Hence every $1$-dimensional submanifold inside the support has, at $z \in G_b$, the tangent space of $G_b$, and at the origin the tangent $\mathbb R(1, 0)$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.submanifoldTangent_eq_of_subset_Z⟧. *Step 2, signs.* Its orientation is one of $\pm(1, \beta')$ at every point ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.tangent_eq_orTan_or⟧, with a locally constant sign ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.exists_isOpen_tangent_eq_orTan_iff⟧. *Step 3, vertical lines.* A sheet through the origin meets every vertical line $\{s\} \times \mathbb R$ for small $|s|$, by the ball graph representation over $T_0M = \mathbb R \times 0$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleSheets · Ex935.exists_mem_fst_eq⟧.

**The classification** ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · example_9_3_5_classification⟧. *Step 1, normal form.* At a point $y$ of the support an orientation is $c \cdot (1, \beta') + (\Theta(y) - c)\cdot(-(1, \beta'))$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.eq_single_add_single⟧. *Step 2, constancy along arcs.* Near a point of an arc every sheet of a structure is the arc with a locally constant sign (Step 2 above), so the coefficient $a$ is constant along each arc, $0 \le a \le 1$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.coef_pt_eq_of_pos⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.coef_pt_eq_of_neg⟧. *Step 3, the origin.* Every sheet of a structure at $0$ meets each vertical line near $0$ (Step 3 above), and the count $\Theta(s, \beta^{++}(s)) + \Theta(s, \beta^{--}(s)) = 2 = \Theta(0)$ forces it to meet it exactly once. With the constancy of the signs, the weight $A$ of $(1, 0)$ at the origin is $a(+, G^{++}) + a(+, G^{--})$, and also $a(-, G^{++}) + a(-, G^{--})$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.coef_zero_eq⟧. *Step 4, the family.* So every orientation is a member of the family $\mathrm{classOrient}(a)$, $a$ indexed by side and branch, with the two sums equal ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.classOrient⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.eq_classOrient⟧, and different $a$ give different orientations ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.classOrient_injective⟧. *Step 5, the converse.* Each member is an orientation: it is the oriented sum of the four graphs $G^{++}, G^{--}, G^{+-}, G^{-+}$, each with both orientations, with weights solving a $2 \times 2$ transport problem between the sides $s > 0$ and $s < 0$ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.exists_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · Ex935.isOrientation_classOrient⟧.

**Consequences.** $\Theta$ has infinitely many orientations, a three-parameter family ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · example_9_3_5_infinite⟧; those with integer weights are exactly the six sign choices of §IX.15 ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · example_9_3_5_integral⟧ ⟦Chapter9/OrientationExampleClasses · example_9_3_5_integral_ncard⟧. So "four different possibilities" holds for each of the two structures, and for $\Theta$ it does not hold as we read it.

### IX.30 The boundary operation, the continuity of $o_{\partial M}$, the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ and Figure 9.1 (Definitions 9.3.8 and 9.3.10 (2017: 9.9 and 9.11))

**The text.** For a tame $M$ the points with $d_M(y) = 1$ form an open dense part of $\partial M$ with a manifold structure; for $(M, o)$ oriented, a basis $(a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ of $T_y\partial M$ is positive iff $(e, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1})$ is positive, $e$ outward; these orientations "fit continuously together", and the orientation of the interior of a face extends to the closed face (Figure 9.1). §IX.16 formalized the linear algebra with $T_y\partial M$ and $e$ as data. Here they are built from $M$ (gap G.103, closed; V9.36–V9.38 explicit).

**The boundary operation** (`Chapter9/BoundaryOperation`). *Step 1, presented charts.* $T^R_yX$ and $C_yX$ are read in a chart with a presentation of its partial quadrant ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.PresentedChart⟧; a chart change acts on chart vectors over $y$ by a continuous linear map carrying reduced space to reduced space and cone to cone ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.PresentedChart.exists_clm⟧, so "reduced", "inward" and the reduced codimension $\dim(L / L \cap T^R_yX)$ are chart independent ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.isReducedVec_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.isInwardVec_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.hasReducedCodim_iff⟧. *Step 2.* For tame $M$, $d_M(y)$ is the reduced codimension of $T_yM$, the content of Lemma 9.3.7's proof ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.subDegIndex_eq_quotDim_span⟧. *Step 3, the cone spans.* Every vector of $T_yM$ is a difference of two vectors of $C_yM = T_yM \cap C_yX$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.exists_sub_eq_vec_submanifoldTangent⟧; so if $T_yM$ has reduced codimension $1$, $C_yM$ is a half-space of $T_yM$ bounded by $T^R_yM$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · exists_coeff_halfSpace⟧, outward vectors exist ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.IsBoundaryAdmissible.exists_outward⟧, and two of them satisfy $e' = c e + k$ with $c > 0$, $k \in T^R_yM$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.IsBoundaryAdmissible.exists_pos⟧. *Step 4, the operation.* $T_y(M, o) \mapsto (T^R_yM, o_\partial)$, with the frames $a$ such that $(e, a)$ is positive for every outward $e$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.boundaryOp⟧, a function of the oriented tangent set with no choice; by Step 3 and §IX.16 it is Definition 9.3.8 for any single outward $e$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.boundaryOp_eq⟧. *Step 5, identification.* The chart image of its carrier is the reduced tangent space of the induced chart of $M$, $T_y\partial M = T^R_yM$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.chartVec_image_boundaryCarrier⟧, and "outward" means "not in the partial cone of $M$" ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.isOutward_iff_not_mem_partialCone⟧. *Step 6.* With it, $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ is the oriented sum filtered by reduced codimension $1$, which needs no quantifier over submanifolds ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · EpGroupoid.boundaryOrientation⟧; it agrees with Definition 9.3.10 for tame orientations ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · EpGroupoid.boundaryLift_boundaryOp_eq_boundaryOrientation⟧, and Proposition 9.3.9 holds ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_3_9_boundaryOrientation⟧. The situation occurs at the corner of $[0, \infty)$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOperation · MPolyfold.exists_isBoundaryAdmissible_halfLine⟧.

**Continuity of $o_{\partial M}$** ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.exists_continuous_boundaryFrames⟧. The text says the orientations fit together "by definition". *Step 1.* The boundary stratum is the set of points where $T_yA$ has reduced codimension $1$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · MPolyfold.boundaryStratum⟧, $\{d_A = 1\}$ for tame $A$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · MPolyfold.boundaryStratum_eq_of_tame⟧. *Step 2.* Let $r$ be the chart sc⁺-retraction at $y_0$, $w$ a positive frame of $o_{\partial A}$ at $y_0$, $s \in C_{y_0}A$ off $T_{y_0}\partial A$. For $z$ in the stratum near $y_0$, $Dr(z)$ maps the partial quadrant and the reduced space at $y_0$ into those at $z$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mem_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mem_minimalSubspaceWith⟧, so $Dr(z)w$ is a basis of $T_z\partial A$ by a dimension count, and $-Dr(z)s$ is outward. *Step 3.* The sign of $(-Dr(z)s, Dr(z)w)$ against a continuous positive frame of $o$ is a frame determinant, locally constant (§IX.15). So $o_{\partial M}$ is an orientation along the stratum ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · MPolyfold.OrientationAlong⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.boundaryOrientation⟧, for every oriented submanifold: tameness is not used, only the reduced codimension $1$. Every oriented structure gives one on each sheet ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientationContinuity2021 · EpGroupoid.OrientedBranchingStructure.exists_boundaryOrientation⟧.

**The stratum.** *Step 1, open and dense.* $\{d_Q = 1\} = \partial Q \cap \{d_Q \le 1\}$ is open in $\partial Q$ for every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryStratumDense · MPolyfold.setOf_degIndex_eq_one⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryStratumDense · MPolyfold.isOpen_degIndex_le_one⟧, and dense in $\partial Q$ for a corner structure, since in corner coordinates a point with vanishing coordinates is a limit of points with exactly one of them vanishing ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryStratumDense · MPolyfold.HasCornerStructureOfDim.boundary_subset_closure_degIndex_eq_one⟧; so for a tame sheet the stratum is open and dense in $\partial M$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryStratumDense · MPolyfold.exists_isOpen_boundaryStratum_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryStratumDense · MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary_subset_closure_boundaryStratum⟧. *Step 2, a submanifold.* In corner coordinates $\kappa$, on the open piece where all coordinates but $y_i$ are positive ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.CornerCoords.facePiece⟧, the map $\kappa^{-1} \circ (y_i \mapsto 0) \circ \kappa$ is an sc-smooth retraction onto the points with $d = 1$ ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.CornerCoords.faceRet⟧. With $s$ the sc⁺-retraction of $M$, $\iota \circ \kappa^{-1} \circ (y_i \mapsto 0) \circ \kappa \circ s$ is an sc⁺-retraction of an open subset of $X$ onto the stratum, the sc⁺ property coming from $r = s \circ r$ ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.exists_stratum_coords⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.exists_isScPlusRetractionOn_stratumOne⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_stratumOne⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StratumRetraction · MPolyfold.stratumOne_eq_boundaryStratum⟧. *Step 3, dimension and tangent spaces.* In a chart the image of $T_y\partial_1M$ is the image of the hyperplane $\{v_i = 0\}$ under the derivative of the inclusion ⟦Chapter9/StratumTangent · MPolyfold.chartTangent_stratumOne_eq⟧, so $\partial_1M$ is $(n-1)$-dimensional ⟦Chapter9/StratumTangent · MPolyfold.isSubmanifoldOfDim_stratumOne⟧ with $T_y\partial_1 M = T^R_yM$ ⟦Chapter9/StratumTangent · MPolyfold.submanifoldTangent_stratumOne⟧. *Step 4, oriented.* $o_{\partial M}$ is an orientation of the submanifold $\partial_1M$ in the sense of Definition 9.3.2's sheets ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientation · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.stratumOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientation · MPolyfold.SubmanifoldOrientation.stratumOrientation_tangent⟧. In corner coordinates where only $y_i$ vanishes, $T\iota(v) \in C_yM$ iff $v_i \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientation · MPolyfold.isInwardVec_incFrame_iff⟧, so $T\iota(-e_i)$ is outward, and a frame $T\iota(v_1), \ldots, T\iota(v_m)$ of $\{v_i = 0\}$ is positive for $o_{\partial M}$ iff $(T\iota(-e_i), T\iota(v_1), \ldots)$ is positive for $o$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryOrientation · MPolyfold.incFrame_mem_boundaryFramesAt_iff⟧: "outward normal first", Part I's rule for the faces of a manifold with corners.

**Figure 9.1** ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · MPolyfold.figure_9_1_existsUnique_faceOrientation⟧. For a face-structured tame sheet, Part I reads the closed faces as manifolds with corners ⟦Chapter9/StokesFaceSum · MPolyfold.faceChartedSpace⟧ with the induced orientation, outward normal first ⟦Chapter9/StokesFaceSum · MPolyfold.faceOrientation⟧. *Step 1, linear algebra.* $\det(-e_i, \iota_i v_1, \ldots, \iota_i v_m) = (-1)^{i+1} \det v$ for the face embedding $\iota_i$ ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · det_cons_neg_stdFrame_faceEmbedding⟧, and the basis $(-e_i, \iota_i b)$ ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · consFaceBasis⟧ has a given orientation iff $b$ has the one Part I's rule assigns ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · orientation_consFaceBasis_eq_iff⟧. *Step 2, agreement.* At every point of a face with $d_M = 1$, a basis $b$ of a face chart is positive for Part I's face orientation iff the frame $T\iota(\iota_i b_1), \ldots, T\iota(\iota_i b_m)$ is positive for $o_{\partial M}$ ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · MPolyfold.faceOrientation_eq_iff_mem_stratumOrientation_pair⟧. *Step 3, extension.* The points with $d_M = 1$ are dense in each closed face ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · MPolyfold.dense_faceStratum⟧, and two continuous tangent orientations agreeing on a dense set are equal ⟦Chapter9/FaceOrientation · TangentOrientation.eq_of_eqOn_dense⟧. So the orientation of the open face extends to exactly one continuous orientation of the closed face, Part I's face orientation. The text's "interiors of the faces" are read as the points with $d_M = 1$, and "extends" as the unique continuous extension. The orientations of the faces of the faces (the caption's last sentence) are not formalized.

### IX.31 Branched integration for an abstract sheet integration: (9.20), Lemma 9.5.7 (2017: 9.17), (9.21), Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 (2017: 9.18, 9.19), Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 (2017: 9.2, 9.3), Definition 9.5.6 and Proposition 9.5.13 (1)

**The text.** For an oriented local branching structure $(M_i, o_i)$, $(\sigma_i)$ on $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and a measurable $K \subseteq |M_U|$ with preimages $K_i \subseteq M_i$, the local measures are $\mu^U_\omega(K) = \frac{1}{\#G_x}\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{K_i}\omega|(M_i, o_i)$ and $\mu^{\mathrm{eff},U}_\omega$ with $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ (9.21). They do not depend on the structure (Lemma 9.5.7, via (9.20)), on shrinking $U$ (Lemmas 9.5.9, 9.5.10) or on moving along a morphism (Lemma 9.5.11); covering $S$ by finitely many $|M_{U_p}|$ and summing gives a unique linear $\omega \mapsto \mu_\omega$ into the signed measures on $(S, L(S))$ with the local formula (Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5), and $\int_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \mu_\omega(S)$, $\oint_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \mu^{\mathrm{eff}}_\omega(S)$ (Definition 9.5.6). Rows V9.54–V9.57 and V9.66 are explicit or restated (gap G.107, closed).

**The integration as a structure.** *Step 1.* The measurable subsets of a sheet $N$ are the sets whose trace differs from a Borel trace by a null set of $N$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · SheetNullSets.IsMeasIn⟧; two sheets induce the same measurable subsets of their intersection ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · SheetNullSets.IsMeasIn.transfer⟧. *Step 2.* A `SheetIntegration` gives numbers $\int_A \omega|(N, o)$ for the forms $\omega$ of a real vector space $\Omega$, the oriented sheets $N$ of a class, and measurable $A \subseteq N$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration⟧, with the properties the text uses: linearity in $\omega$, countable additivity, vanishing on null sets, equal (opposite) integrals over a common subset of two sheets where their oriented tangent spaces agree (are opposite), invariance under the sc-diffeomorphisms whose tangent maps are those of morphisms ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.IsMorTangentOn⟧, Lindelöf sheets, and Lemma 9.4.6 with the note of Definition 9.4.7. It is built for sc-forms in §IX.32.

**(9.20) and Lemma 9.5.7** ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.sum_integ_eq_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.sum_integ_eq_sum_integ⟧. *A finite family of oriented sheets with weights whose weighted sum of oriented tangent spaces vanishes at every point of $K$ has $\sum_k w_k \int_{K \cap N_k}\omega|(N_k, o_k) = 0$.* **The text's proof** removes a null set and compares on the pieces of Proposition 9.4.10. **The formalized proof** redoes that decomposition for measurable pieces. *Step 1.* The points where two sheets through a point have different tangent spaces form a null set in every sheet ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.isNull_tangentBad⟧. *Step 2.* The rest of $K$ is cut into the finitely many measurable pieces on which the set of sheets through $y$ and the pairs with equal oriented tangent space are constant ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.piece⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.isMeasIn_piece⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.pairwise_disjoint_piece⟧. *Step 3.* On a piece all the integrals are $\pm$ the integral over one sheet, and the signed sum of the weights vanishes because a tangent space has two orientations ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationAbstract · EpGroupoid.SheetIntegration.sum_sign_weight_eq_zero⟧. The families need not pass through one point. For two oriented tame structures describing $\hat T_\Theta$ this gives Lemma 9.5.7 ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · lemma_9_5_7⟧.

**(9.21) and Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11.** *The local measures.* An oriented tame structure is a tame structure (natural representation, properness, tame sheets) with $n$-dimensional oriented sheets ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · OrientedTameStructure⟧; it describes $\hat T_\Theta$ if its oriented sum is $\hat T_\Theta$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · Represents⟧. The weighted sum $\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{A \cap M_i}\omega|(M_i, o_i)$ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · sheetSum⟧ divided by $\#G_x$ or $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ is $\mu^U_\omega$, $\mu^{\mathrm{eff},U}_\omega$ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · localMeasure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · localMeasureEff⟧, linear in $\omega$ and additive in the set ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · sheetSum_hasSum⟧. *Lemma 9.5.9* ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · lemma_9_5_9⟧: with the slice $V$ of §IX.20 and the decomposition $M_U \cap \pi^{-1}(K) = \bigsqcup_{r \in R}\varphi_r(M_U \cap V \cap \pi^{-1}(K))$, each $\varphi_r$ preserves the integrals, its tangent maps being those of morphisms ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · NaturalRep.isMorTangentOn_Φ⟧ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · sheetSum_image⟧, so the sum over $U$ is $\#R$ times the sum over $V$ ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · sheetSum_preimage_eq_card_mul_slice⟧; with $\#R \cdot \#G_y = \#G_x$ the normalized measures agree. The text takes the restricted structure on $V$; by Lemma 9.5.7 any structure at $y$ describing $\hat T_\Theta$ serves, and the text's proof uses Lemma 9.5.7 and the naturality of $\hat T_\Theta$ here. *Lemma 9.5.10* ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · lemma_9_5_10⟧: the same with (9.23), $\#R \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_y = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ under the local unique continuation property. *Lemma 9.5.11* ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · lemma_9_5_11⟧: the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi : U \to U'$ of a morphism has, at each point, the tangent map of a morphism, so it carries the structure on $U$ to one on $U'$ with the same sums ⟦Chapter9/LocalMeasure · sheetSum_preimage_eq_of_morDiffeo⟧, and $\#G_x = \#G_{x'}$ (§IX.20). The effective clause holds without the local unique continuation property, only $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_{x'}$ being used. Remark 9.5.8 has no content beyond Lemma 9.5.11.

**Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5** ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · theorem_9_5_4⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · theorem_9_5_5⟧. *Step 1, measurability.* The local sc-diffeomorphism $t \circ (s|U(\varphi))^{-1}$ of a morphism has the tangent maps of the morphisms of its sheet ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · isMorTangentOn_hat⟧, and the preimage of $K \in L(S)$ has measurable traces on the sheets, by Lemma 9.5.2 ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · OrientedTameStructure.isMeas_preimage⟧. *Step 2, overlaps.* Near two points $z \in U$, $z' \in U'$ over one point of $|X|$ the two local measures agree, combining Lemmas 9.5.9 and 9.5.11 ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · exists_slice_pair⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · exists_local_agreement⟧; since the sheets are Lindelöf, countably many such neighbourhoods cover a measurable $K \subseteq |M_U| \cap |M_{U'}|$, and the two structures give the same measure of $K$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · overlap⟧. The text does not mention that countably many pieces suffice. *Step 3, gluing.* Each structure gives a signed measure on $(S, L(S))$, linear in $\omega$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · localSignedMeasure⟧. On a compact space with a σ-algebra containing the Borel sets, linear local expressions on the members of an open cover that agree on overlaps glue to exactly one linear map into signed measures: cut $K$ into the pieces $W_k \setminus \bigcup_{j<k} W_j$ of a finite subcover and add ⟦Chapter9/MeasureGlue · existsUnique_linearMap_signedMeasure_of_local⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureGlue · existsUnique_linearMap_signedMeasure_of_openCover⟧. This is the text's "defines our desired signed measure". *Step 4.* Hence exactly one linear $\omega \mapsto \mu_\omega$ with the local formula for every oriented tame structure with sheets in the class describing $\hat T_\Theta$ and every measurable $K \subseteq |U(x)|$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · existsUnique_branchedMeasure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · branchedMeasure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · branchedMeasureEff⟧, given such a structure at every point of the support (`hcov` in this abstract form, the class condition of the integration). *Definition 9.5.6* ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · branchedIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · branchedIntegralEff⟧, and the identity after Theorem 9.5.5, $\mu^{\mathrm{eff},U} = (\#G_x / \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x)\,\mu^U$ ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · OrientedTameStructure.localMeasureEff_eq⟧. *Proposition 9.5.13 (1)*: for effective $X$ the two integrals agree ⟦Chapter9/BranchedIntegral · proposition_9_5_13_1⟧. A witness in dimension $0$: points as sheets, the integral the signed value of an invariant function ⟦Chapter9/PointIntegration · pointIntegration⟧.

### IX.32 The integral of sc-differential forms over oriented sheets, and Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 as printed

**The text** integrates "$\omega|(M_i, o_i)$" over measurable subsets of the sheets without constructing the integral; the sheets are manifolds with boundary and corners and $\omega$ an sc-differential form on the ep-groupoid (Definition 8.2.1). Here the integral is built for $n \ge 1$ and shown to be a `SheetIntegration` of §IX.31, first on sheets in one chart, then on sheets covered by countably many charts (gap G.107, closed).

**Evaluating forms.** *Step 1.* An evaluation of forms is a real vector space $\Omega$ with values $\omega(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_n)$ on tangent vectors, linear in $\omega$, alternating and multilinear on the tangent space of a submanifold (stated through determinants), invariant under the tangent maps of morphisms, and continuous along continuous frame fields ⟦Chapter9/GraphChart · FormEval⟧. *Step 2.* The forms $\Omega^n_{ep}(X)$ of Definition 8.2.1 are one: the chart expression of $\omega$ is sc-smooth, hence continuous along level-1 lifts, which are continuous along a submanifold since the chart retraction is sc⁺ ⟦Chapter9/FormEvalEp · MPolyfold.continuousWithinAt_levelLift⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FormEvalEp · epFormEval⟧. *Step 3.* The direct limit $\Omega^n_{ep,\infty}(X)$ of Definition 8.2.2 is one too: a submanifold of $X$ in $X_\infty$ is one of every level $X^i$ with the same tangent spaces and continuous frame fields, so the forms of $X^i$ are evaluated on lifted tangent vectors, compatibly with the steps of the limit ⟦Chapter9/FormEvalInfty · IsSmoothSubmanifold.levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FormEvalInfty · epFormsInftyEval⟧.

**Graph charts.** *Step 1.* A graph chart of an $n$-dimensional submanifold $N$ is a chart $\varphi$ of the M-polyfold containing $N$ and a continuous linear $p : E_0 \to \mathbb R^n$, injective on $\varphi(N)$, whose inverse is differentiable within $p(\varphi(N))$ with derivative a linear isomorphism onto the chart image of $T_yN$, continuous in $y$ ⟦Chapter9/GraphChart · MPolyfold.GraphChart⟧. No corner structure of $N$ is used, and derivatives are taken within a set that need not be open. *Step 2.* Near every point of an $n$-dimensional submanifold there is one: the tangent projection of §IX.28 is bi-Lipschitz on $N$ near the point, and its image is closed ⟦Chapter9/GraphChartExists · ScRetraction.exists_graphData⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GraphChartExists · exists_graphChart⟧. *Step 3, the integral in a chart.* The density is $\pm\omega(\partial_1, \ldots, \partial_n)$ for the coordinate frame, with sign $+$ where the frame is positive for the orientation ⟦Chapter9/ChartIntegral · density⟧, and $\int_A$ is its Lebesgue integral over the coordinate image of $A \cap N$ ⟦Chapter9/ChartIntegral · chartInteg⟧; the sign is locally constant on $N$ ⟦Chapter9/FrameSign · GraphChart.exists_isOpen_isPos⟧. *Step 4, the comparison of two charts.* At a common point of two sheets with $T_yN = T_yN'$ the coordinate change is differentiable within the coordinate image of $N \cap N'$, with derivative expressing one frame in the other ⟦Chapter9/GraphChartTransition · GraphChart.exists_transition⟧; the change of variables for maps differentiable on a measurable set ⟦Chapter9/GraphChart · integral_image_eq_of_det⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GraphChartTransition · GraphChart.setIntegral_coord_image_eq⟧ gives equal integrals where the oriented tangent spaces agree and opposite ones where they are opposite ⟦Chapter9/ChartIntegral · FormEval.chartInteg_congr⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ChartIntegral · FormEval.chartInteg_neg⟧. With $N = N'$ this is the independence of the graph chart; no smoothness of $N \cap N'$ is needed. This is how the proof of Lemma 9.5.7 compares sheets. *Step 5.* Invariance under the sc-diffeomorphisms whose tangent maps are those of morphisms ⟦Chapter9/ChartIntegral · FormEval.chartInteg_mapDiffeo⟧.

**The one-chart integration** ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.sheetIntegration⟧. The class consists of the $n$-dimensional submanifolds in one graph chart on which every form is absolutely integrable ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.sheets⟧, the null sets are the $n$-dimensional Hausdorff null sets ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.sheetNull⟧, and the integral is that of Step 3 ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.integ⟧; all fields of a `SheetIntegration` hold, among them the Lindelöf property, through the coordinate homeomorphism ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.hereditarilyLindelofSpace⟧, and the integral vanishes where $\omega$ vanishes on the sheet ⟦Chapter9/SheetIntegrationConcrete · FormEval.integ_eq_zero_of_ev_eq_zero⟧. With it, §IX.31 gives Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 for structures whose sheets lie in one graph chart ⟦Chapter9/TameOpen · theorem_9_5_4_tame⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TameOpen · theorem_9_5_5_tame⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TameOpen · tameBranchedIntegral⟧; such structures exist near every point of the support once some oriented tame structure does, by restriction to a smaller domain ⟦Chapter9/IntegralCovering · exists_restrict_mem_sheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TameOpen · HasTameInducedStructure.inter_isOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter9/TameOpen · hcov_of_loc⟧.

**Several charts.** *Step 1, $\int|\omega|$.* In a graph chart, $\int_A|\omega|$ bounds $|\int_A\omega|$, does not depend on the chart, is invariant under morphisms and countably additive ⟦Chapter9/ChartAbsIntegral · abs_chartInteg_le⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ChartAbsIntegral · chartAbs_congr⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ChartAbsIntegral · chartAbs_mapDiffeo⟧. *Step 2.* A sheet covered by countably many open $V_k$ with $N \cap V_k$ in the one-chart class has the disjoint Borel pieces $P_k = N \cap V_k \setminus \bigcup_{j<k}V_j$ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · ChartCover⟧; the cover is finite in the sense $\sum_k \int_{P_k}|\omega| < \infty$ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · ChartCover.IsFinite⟧, and then $\int_A \omega = \sum_k \int_{A \cap P_k}\omega$ converges absolutely ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · ChartCover.gInteg⟧. *Step 3, independence.* Two covers, or two sheets over a common set where their oriented tangent spaces agree or are opposite, give equal or opposite sums, by a double series over the pieces of the two covers ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · hasSum_of_double⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · ChartCover.gInteg_eq_of⟧. *Step 4.* The class of sheets with a finite cover ⟦Chapter9/MultiChart · FormEval.msheets⟧ carries a `SheetIntegration` ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartIntegration · FormEval.msInteg⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartIntegration · FormEval.msheetIntegration⟧ that contains the one-chart class and agrees with it there ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartIntegration · FormEval.sheets_subset_msheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartIntegration · FormEval.msInteg_eq_integ⟧; Theorems 9.5.4, 9.5.5 follow for structures with sheets in this class ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartTheorem · theorem_9_5_4_multi⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartTheorem · theorem_9_5_5_multi⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartTheorem · multiBranchedIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartTheorem · multiBranchedIntegralEff⟧. Compact sheets are in it ⟦Chapter9/MultiChartCompact · msheets_of_isCompact⟧.

**The finiteness the text uses tacitly** ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · msheets_of_orientedTameStructure⟧. The text integrates over measurable subsets of the sheets, which presupposes $\int|\omega| < \infty$. For the sheets of an oriented tame structure of a compact $n$-dimensional $\Theta$ it holds. *Step 1.* The support is locally compact, being locally a finite union of finite-dimensional submanifolds; a compact $K' \subseteq \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ meets every orbit of the support since $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ is compact; and $\mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U \subseteq s(\{\varphi \mid s(\varphi) \in \mathrm{cl}\,U,\ t(\varphi) \in K'\})$, compact by the properness of $\mathrm{cl}\,U$ (Definition 7.5.8) ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · exists_isCompact_supp_inter⟧. *Step 2.* An $n$-dimensional submanifold inside a compact part of the support is covered by finitely many one-chart sheets of structures at points of it ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · msheets_of_subset_isCompact⟧, and $\int|\omega|$ over it is dominated by the finitely many one-chart integrals ⟦Chapter9/FiniteDominated · chartAbs_eq_of_borel⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FiniteDominated · isFinite_of_dominated⟧. *Step 3, Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 as printed* ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · theorem_9_5_4_full⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · theorem_9_5_5_full⟧: there is exactly one linear $\omega \mapsto \mu_\omega$ into the signed measures on $(S, L(S))$ with $\mu_\omega(K) = \mu^U_\omega(K)$ for every oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ and every measurable $K \subseteq |U(x)|$; the $n$-dimensionality of $\Theta$ follows from the hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheorem · isNDimensional_of_loc⟧.

**The reading `hloc` of "oriented, tame".** The theorems take as hypothesis that every point of the support has an oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$. Without boundary it follows from the text's hypotheses ⟦Chapter9/CoveringFromText · hloc_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧: the oriented structure of Definition 9.3.2 has $n$-dimensional sheets, and restricted to the domain of a natural representation inside an open set with the properness property it is tame, every submanifold having a tame induced structure when $d_X = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/CoveringFromText · exists_orientedTameStructure_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheoremText · theorem_9_5_4_full_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧. With boundary, Definition 9.3.6 gives tame sheets of *some* structure and Definition 9.3.2 oriented sheets of *another*; that the oriented structure can be taken tame is the reading of "tame".

**Part I's integral, and a witness.** Over a tame sheet the integral equals Part I's manifold integral of the restricted form for the corresponding tangent orientation ⟦Chapter9/ManifoldBridge · bridgeOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ManifoldBridge · isContinuous_bridgeOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ManifoldIntegralBridge · FormEval.integ_eq_manifoldIntegral⟧, chart by chart of a partition of unity by the change of variables between graph and corner coordinates ⟦Chapter9/ManifoldBridge · FormEval.chartInteg_eq_setIntegral_corner⟧; for classes of $\Omega^n_{ep,\infty}(X)$ represented on any level see ⟦Chapter9/LevelRestrict · epFormsInftyEval_integ_eq_integral⟧.
