The unit circle in $\mathbb R^2$, the image of the radial retraction $r \mapsto r/|r|$ of $\mathbb R^2 \setminus \{0\}$, oriented counter-clockwise ⟦Chapter9/CircleWitness · rnPolyfold_isSubmanifoldOfDim_unitCircle2⟧ ⟦Chapter9/CircleWitness · circleOrientation⟧, satisfies all hypotheses with compact nonempty support ⟦Chapter9/CircleWitness · circle_witness⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FiniteTheoremText · circle_theorem_9_5_4_full⟧, and with $U(x) = \mathbb R^2$ and the whole circle as one sheet $\int_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \int_{S^1}\omega$ ⟦Chapter9/CircleOneSheet · circle_multiBranchedIntegral⟧.

### IX.33 (9.22) and Proposition 9.5.13 (2)

**(9.22)** (V9.69, explicit). *If $\tau = f \cdot \omega$, then $d\mu_\tau = \bar f\,d\mu_\omega$, with $\bar f \circ \pi = f$.* **Reading.** $f \cdot \omega$ is read through the evaluation, $\tau(\alpha) = f(y)\,\omega(\alpha)$ on the frames of the tangent spaces $T_yN$ of the sheets ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · IsMul⟧, witnessed for constant $f$ ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · isMul_smul⟧; the form $f \cdot \omega$ for a non-constant sc-smooth $f$ is not built. *Step 1, local, exact.* In a graph chart, $\int_A\tau$ is the integral of $f$ times the density of $\omega$ ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · integ_eq_setIntegral_mul⟧, so $\mu^U_\tau(K)$ is (9.21) for $\omega$ with $f$ inserted in the integrands ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · OrientedTameStructure.localMeasure_eq_sum_setIntegral_mul⟧. *Step 2, the estimate.* If $|\bar f - a| \le \varepsilon$ on $K$, then $|\mu_\tau(K) - a\,\mu_\omega(K)| \le \varepsilon\,M_\omega(K)$ with $M_\omega(K) = \frac{1}{\#G_x}\sum\sigma_i\int_{K_i}|\omega|$, additive in $K$ ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · OrientedTameStructure.abs_localMeasure_sub_le⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DensityLocal · abs_branchedMeasure_sub_le⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DensitySignedMeasure · OrientedTameStructure.absSheetSum_union⟧. *Step 3, integrals against a signed measure.* Mathlib's integral against a vector measure is, for a signed measure $s$, $\int_K g\,ds^+ - \int_K g\,ds^-$ for the Jordan decomposition ⟦Chapter9/SignedMeasureIntegrals · SignedDensity.setIntegral_eq_jordan⟧. If a second signed measure $t$ satisfies the estimate of Step 2 against $s$ on the measurable subsets of a set, then $t(K) = \int_K g\,ds$, by Riemann–Stieltjes sums over the partition of $K$ by the values of $g$ and $\varepsilon \to 0$ ⟦Chapter9/SignedMeasureIntegrals · SignedDensity.eq_setIntegral_of_estimate⟧; on a compact space, estimates near every point suffice ⟦Chapter9/SignedMeasureIntegrals · SignedDensity.eq_setIntegral_of_local_estimate⟧. *Step 4.* So for $\bar f$ bounded and $L(S)$-measurable, continuous for instance, $\mu_\tau(K) = \int_K \bar f\,d\mu_\omega$ for every $K \in L(S)$, and the same for the effective measures ⟦Chapter9/DensitySignedMeasure · eq_setIntegral_of_sheetSum⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DensitySignedMeasure · branchedMeasure_eq_setIntegral_mul⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DensitySignedMeasure · branchedMeasureEff_eq_setIntegral_mul⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DensitySignedMeasure · branchedMeasure_eq_jordan⟧.

**Proposition 9.5.13 (2)** (V9.57, restated). *Under the local unique continuation property, $\oint_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \int_{\hat\Theta'}\omega'$ on the reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$.* **The text's proof**: $X$ and $X_R$ have the same object M-polyfold, $\Theta' = \Theta$, "we can take the same local branching structure", and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G'_x$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the natural action of $G^R_x$*, which "the same local branching structure" needs and the text does not construct. For a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ with the property of Definition 7.2.18, $\Phi^R([g]) = \Phi(g)$ and $\Gamma^R([g], y) = [\Gamma(g, y)]$ define one of $G^R_x = G_x/T_x$ on the same $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · NaturalRep.toReduced⟧: $\Phi$ descends because $T_x = \ker\Phi$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · Φ_eq_of_reducedIsotropyHom_eq⟧, $\Gamma$ because $\Gamma(gk, y) = \Gamma(g, y)\circ\Gamma(k, y)$ with $\Gamma(k, y)$ trivial in $X_R$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · reducedπ_Γ_eq_of_reducedIsotropyHom_eq⟧, and the uniqueness in Theorem 7.1.13 (3) holds because $[\Gamma(a, y)] = [\Gamma(b, y)]$ forces $a = bc$ with $\Phi(c) = \mathrm{id}$ near $y$, and the local unique continuation property gives $c \in T_x$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · reducedIsotropyHom_eq_of_reducedπ_Γ_eq⟧. *Step 2, the same structures.* The properness property, tame and oriented tame structures carry over with the same $U$, sheets, weights and orientations ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · HasPropernessProperty.toReduced⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · OrientedTameStructure.toReduced⟧, and $\#G^R_x = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · card_isotropy_reduced_eq_card_effIsotropy⟧. *Step 3, the same integrals.* The tangent map of $[\varphi]$ is that of $\varphi$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · tangentMor_reducedπ⟧, so a form of $X$ is one of $X_R$ and a sheet integration on $X$ is one on $X_R$ with the same integrals ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · SheetIntegration.toReduced⟧; the orientation carries over ⟦Chapter9/ReducedRep · IsOrientation.toReduced⟧. *Step 4, the same σ-algebra.* $|X| \cong |X_R|$ and $|\mathrm{supp}(\Theta)|$ in both are identified ⟦Chapter9/ReducedIntegral · orbitHomeomorphReduced⟧ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedIntegral · orbitSuppHomeomorphReduced⟧, carrying $L(S)$ to $L(S)$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedIntegral · measurableSet_image_orbitSuppHomeomorphReduced⟧. *Step 5.* By the uniqueness in Theorem 9.5.4 on $X_R$, $\mu^{\mathrm{eff}}_{\hat\Theta,\omega}(K) = \mu_{\hat\Theta',\omega'}(K)$ for $K \in L(S)$ ⟦Chapter9/ReducedIntegral · proposition_9_5_13_2_measure⟧, and with $K = S$ the proposition ⟦Chapter9/ReducedIntegral · proposition_9_5_13_2⟧. The local unique continuation property also makes the morphism space of $X_R$ Hausdorff, so that $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid. No hypothesis is added. Witness: the circle ⟦Chapter9/ReducedCircle · circle_proposition_9_5_13_2⟧.

### IX.34 Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) with $(n-1)$-dimensional null sets, and Theorems 9.5.15, 9.5.16 (2017: 9.4, 9.5): the boundary measures

**The text.** For $K \subseteq |\partial M_U|$ the preimages lie in the $\partial M_i$, manifolds with boundary and corners, and measure zero is $(n-1)$-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero in every boundary face (p. 448). Then (Theorem 9.5.15) there is a linear map $\omega \mapsto \mu^\partial_\omega$ into the signed measures on $(\partial S, L(\partial S))$, "uniquely characterized" by $\mu^\partial_\omega(K) = \frac{1}{\#G_x}\sum_i\sigma_i\int_{K_i}\omega|(\partial M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$, and Theorem 9.5.16 the same with $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ under the local unique continuation property; the proof is "using the same techniques" as Theorem 9.5.4.

**The null sets of the boundaries** (gap G.108, closed; V9.52, V9.53). *Step 1.* As for the sheets (§IX.28), $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero is read in the M-polyfold charts with the $(n-1)$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. *Step 2, positivity.* In corner coordinates of dimension $m + 1$, near a point whose only vanishing coordinate is $y_i$, the chart image of $\{y_i = 0\}$ is an open piece of a coordinate hyperplane, not $m$-null ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNotNull · MPolyfold.CornerCoords.not_hNull_chart_coord_eq_zero⟧; so a nonempty $\partial M$ of a tame $n$-dimensional sheet is not $(n-1)$-null ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNotNull · MPolyfold.HasCornerStructureOfDim.not_isHNull_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNotNull · MPolyfold.not_isHNull_submanifoldBoundary⟧. *Step 3.* These null sets form a null-set system on the class of the boundaries of tame sheets with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · MPolyfold.tameBoundaries⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · MPolyfold.boundaryNullSets⟧; for $n = 1$ they are the counting null sets ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · MPolyfold.boundaryNullSets_one_isNull_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · SheetNullSets.point⟧. *Step 4, well defined.* For $n$-dimensional $\Theta$, $K$ has measure zero in $\partial S$ iff near each point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has $\partial M_i \cap \pi^{-1}(K)$ null for all $i$, and then every tame structure has ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundary_boundaryNullSets_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · EpGroupoid.isHNull_boundary_of_isMeasureZeroBoundary⟧; Definition 9.5.14 is ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundaryH⟧. *Step 5, the corners.* A codimension-2 coordinate subspace of $\mathbb R^n$ is $(n-1)$-null, so the points with $d_M \ge 2$ are $(n-1)$-null ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · MPolyfold.isHNull_two_le_subDegIndex⟧ and $\partial M$ minus the stratum $\{d_M = 1\}$ is null ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryNullSigmaAlgebra · MPolyfold.isHNull_submanifoldBoundary_diff_boundaryStratum⟧: the boundary integral lives on the stratum. *Face by face.* The text's notion for a face-structured sheet is formalized as a proper σ-ideal ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · MPolyfold.IsFaceNull⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · MPolyfold.not_isFaceNull_face⟧; its comparison with the ambient reading is not formalized, and no statement needs it. *Witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$:* $\Theta = 1$ on $[0, \infty)$, tame and $1$-dimensional ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · halfLineTame⟧, with $|0| \in \partial S$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · halfLine_orbitSupp_boundary_nonempty⟧ and $L(\partial S)$ the Borel sets ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFaceNullSets · halfLine_lebesgueSigmaBoundary⟧.

**The boundary sheets.** *Step 1.* For an oriented tame structure of dimension $m + 1$, $\partial_1M_i = \{d_{M_i} = 1\}$ is an $m$-dimensional submanifold (§IX.30) with the orientation $o_{\partial M_i}$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundarySheets · OrientedTameStructure.boundarySheet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundarySheets · OrientedTameStructure.boundaryOrient⟧. *Step 2, (9.12) with the stratum.* If the structure describes $\hat T_\Theta$, then $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}(y) = \sum_{y \in \partial_1M_i}\sigma_i T_y(\partial_1M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundarySheets · OrientedTameStructure.boundaryOrientation_eq_sum⟧; the left side depends on $\hat T_\Theta$ only. *Step 3.* Near each of its points a boundary sheet lies in the one-chart class for $m$-forms ⟦Chapter9/BoundarySheets · OrientedTameStructure.exists_boundarySheet_mem_sheets⟧. *Step 4, the traces.* For $K \in L(\partial S)$ the trace of $\pi^{-1}(K)$ on $\partial_1M_i$ is measurable, by induction over the generators of $L(\partial S)$: Borel generators have Borel traces, null generators null traces by Step 4 above and $\partial_1M_i \subseteq \partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · OrientedTameStructure.isMeasIn_boundarySheet⟧.

**The machinery of §IX.31 for sheet families.** The boundary sheets are not the sheets of a branching structure, so (9.20), (9.21) and Lemmas 9.5.7–9.5.11 are proved again for an oriented sheet family: a natural representation on $U(x)$ and finitely many $m$-dimensional oriented submanifolds with rational weights whose union is $D \cap U(x)$ for a fixed set $D$ closed under morphisms ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · IsMorSaturated⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · OrientedSheetFamily⟧, described by a field $T'$ carried along by morphisms ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · IsNaturalOn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · OrientedSheetFamily.lemma_9_5_7⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · OrientedSheetFamily.lemma_9_5_9⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · OrientedSheetFamily.lemma_9_5_11⟧. An oriented tame structure is the instance $D = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta)$ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · OrientedTameStructure.toFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter9/SheetFamily · isNaturalOn_of_isOrientation⟧. The overlaps and the gluing go as in §IX.31 ⟦Chapter9/FamilyMeasure · OrientedSheetFamily.overlap⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FamilyMeasure · existsUnique_familyMeasure⟧. *The boundary family.* $D$ is the set of points of the support where $\hat T_\Theta$ has a term of reduced codimension $1$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFamily · boundaryStratumSet⟧, closed under morphisms ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFamily · isMorSaturated_boundaryStratumSet⟧ since tangent maps of morphisms preserve the reduced codimension; for a structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ it is the union of the $\partial_1M_i$ in $U(x)$, the weights being positive. $\hat T_{\partial\Theta}$ is natural ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFamily · isNaturalOn_boundaryOrientation⟧, and the $(\partial_1M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$, $(\sigma_i)$ form a family describing it ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFamily · OrientedTameStructure.boundaryFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryFamily · OrientedTameStructure.represents_boundaryFamily⟧.

**Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16, first form** (V9.67; the form with the text's hypotheses is in §§IX.36–IX.38) ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · theorem_9_5_15_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · theorem_9_5_16_hyp⟧. *For every sheet integration whose null sets are the $m$-dimensional ones, $n = m + 1$, $m \ge 1$, there is exactly one linear $\omega \mapsto \mu^\partial_\omega$ into the signed measures on $(\partial S, L(\partial S))$ with the printed local formula*, and for the integration over countably many graph charts ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · theorem_9_5_15_msheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · theorem_9_5_16_msheets⟧. $\partial S$ is compact, being closed in $S$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureGlue · EpGroupoid.isCompact_orbitSupp_boundaryTheta⟧, and the gluing is ⟦Chapter9/MeasureGlue · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_5_15_of_overlap⟧. The sum runs over the nonempty $\partial_1M_i$, the empty set need not belong to the class ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · OrientedSheetFamily.nonemptyPart⟧, and $n$-dimensionality is stated explicitly. **Added hypothesis `hcov`**, not derived from the text: at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ an oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ whose nonempty boundary sheets lie in the class of the integration. For the multi-chart class this is the finiteness of $\int|\omega|$ over $\partial_1M_i$ near the corners of $M_i$, which the text uses tacitly; the difficulty lies where $\partial_1M_i$ approaches the corners, and compact boundary sheets satisfy it ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · OrientedTameStructure.boundarySheet_mem_msheets_of_isCompact⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · hcov_msheets_of_isCompact⟧. Witnesses: $\Theta = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasure · hcov_zero⟧, and with $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \ne \emptyset$ the closed upper hemisphere of §IX.35 ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_hcov⟧. `hcov` is derived from the text's hypotheses (§§IX.36–IX.37), and the case $m = 0$ is §IX.38 (gap G.109, closed).

### IX.35 Theorems 9.5.17, 9.5.18 (2017: 9.6, 9.7): Stokes' theorem, and the hemisphere

**The text, paraphrased (pp. 449–451).** For $X$ with sc-smooth partitions of unity, $\Theta$ tame, oriented and compact of dimension $n$, and $\omega$ an sc-differential form of degree $n-1$, $\int_{\hat\Theta} d\omega = \mu^{\partial}_\omega(\partial S)$; the effective version asks in addition for the local unique continuation property. The proof covers $S$ by finitely many $|U(x_k)|$ carrying oriented branching structures $(M_i, o_i)_{i \in I_k}$, takes an sc-smooth partition of unity $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_\ell$ constant on the orbits and subordinate to the saturations $U_k^*$ and a further saturated $U_0^*$, puts $\omega_k = \beta_k\omega$, applies the classical Stokes theorem on each sheet, and sums: $\mu_{d\omega}(S) = \sum_k c_k \sum_{i \in I_k} \sigma_i \int_{(M_i,o_i)} d\omega_k = \sum_k c_k \sum_{i \in I_k} \sigma_i \int_{\partial(M_i,o_i)} \omega_k = \sum_k \mu^{\partial}_{\omega_k}(\partial S) = \mu^{\partial}_\omega(\partial S)$, with $c_k = 1/\sharp G_{x_k}$ or $1/\sharp G^{\mathrm{eff}}_{x_k}$.

**The Lean proof, step by step.**

*Step 1 (the cover and the partition of unity).* From the sc-smooth partitions of unity of Definition 7.5.5 and the compactness of $S$ one gets finitely many structures and $\beta_0, \dots, \beta_\ell$ as in the text, with $U_0^* = \pi^{-1}(|X| \setminus S)$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.exists_stokes_partition⟧. The product $\beta\omega$ is a form of $\Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$ ⟦Chapter9/FunctionTimesForm · EP.epFormsInftySmul⟧, and the restriction to a level commutes with the evaluation used by the integral ⟦Chapter9/LevelRestrict · formsInftyRestrict_epFormsInftyToObj⟧ ⟦Chapter9/LevelRestrict · epFormsInftyEval_integ_eq_integral⟧.

*Step 2 (Stokes on one sheet).* The sheets $M_i$ need not be compact. What makes the classical theorem applicable is that $M_i \cap \mathrm{supp}\,\beta_k$ is compact, which the text does not state; it follows from the properness of $U(x) \to |U(x)|$ and the compactness of $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesLocalFormulas · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_ultrafilter_le_nhds⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesLocalFormulas · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.isCompact_inter⟧. Then $\int_M (d\omega)|_M = \int_{\partial M} \omega|_M$ on a σ-compact oriented sheet with corners when the restriction has compact support ⟦Chapter9/StokesLocalFormulas · MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict_of_isCompact⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesLocalFormulas · MPolyfold.OrientedSheet.stokes⟧. A sheet of an oriented tame structure is such a sheet, with the tangent orientation of $o_i$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheet · OrientedTameStructure.orientedSheet⟧, so $\int_{(M_i,o_i)} d(\beta\omega) = \int_{\partial(M_i,o_i)} \beta\omega$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheet · EP.integ_d_smul_eq_boundaryIntegral⟧, and on one structure $\Phi(d(\beta\omega))(S) = c(x)\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{\partial(M_i,o_i)} \beta\omega$ for every $\Phi$ with the local formula of Theorem 9.5.4 or 9.5.5 ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheet · EP.stokes_one_structure⟧ (the second and third equalities of the display). The term $k = 0$ vanishes ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheet · EP.stokes_off_support⟧.

*Step 3 (the sum).* Summing over $k$ gives the first three equalities of the display ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.stokes_of_partition⟧, hence Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 with the right-hand side written as the sum of boundary integrals ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.theorem_9_5_17_boundary_sum⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.theorem_9_5_18_boundary_sum⟧. The measure $\mu_{d\omega}$ is local: it vanishes on sets above which the integrals vanish ⟦Chapter9/MeasureWholeSheets · measure_eq_zero_of_integ_eq_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureWholeSheets · measure_univ_eq_of_integ_eq_zero⟧. The last two equalities of the display are two properties of $\omega \mapsto \mu^\partial_\omega(\partial S)$: the local formula for $\beta\omega$ with $\mathrm{supp}\,\beta \subseteq U(x)^*$, and vanishing when $\mathrm{supp}\,\beta$ misses $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$. Every linear functional with these two properties satisfies Stokes' theorem ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.theorem_9_5_17_of_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.theorem_9_5_18_of_boundary⟧, and such a functional exists ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartition · EP.exists_boundary_functional⟧.

*Step 4 (every dimension $n \ge 1$).* The statements of Step 3 were first proved for $n \ge 2$, because in degree $0$ the evaluation on frames is cut off. The product rule $(\beta\omega)|_N = \beta\,(\omega|_N)$ is proved in every degree ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheetAllDegrees · EP.formsInftyRestrict_epFormsInftySmul_all⟧, and the statements hold for $n = 1$ as well ⟦Chapter9/StokesSheetAllDegrees · EP.stokes_one_structure_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartitionAllDegrees · EP.stokes_of_partition_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartitionAllDegrees · EP.theorem_9_5_17_boundary_sum_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartitionAllDegrees · EP.theorem_9_5_18_boundary_sum_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesPartitionAllDegrees · EP.exists_boundary_functional_all⟧.

*Step 5 (the classical boundary integral is the integral over the stratum).* The text's $\int_{\partial(M_i,o_i)}$ is Part I's integral over the faces $\{y_l = 0\}$ of corner charts with signs; $\mu^\partial$ of §IX.34 integrates over the stratum $\partial_1M_i = \{d_{M_i} = 1\}$ with the boundary orientation $o_{\partial M_i}$ of Definition 9.3.8. The text identifies the two without comment. The face frame $T\iota(\iota_l e_1), \dots, T\iota(\iota_l e_m)$ is positive for $o_{\partial M}$ exactly when the sign of the face matches the reading of $o$ in the chart ⟦Chapter9/FaceFrame · MPolyfold.faceFrame_mem_stratumOrientation_iff⟧; the change of variables on a face is ⟦Chapter9/FaceChange · FormEval.face_change⟧; the open face piece and the face domain differ by a null set, the corners ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryIntegralFaces · CornerCoords.faceSet_ae_eq⟧; one term of Part I's integral is an integral over a face piece ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryIntegralFaces · FormEval.face_term_eq⟧, and a weighted integral over the stratum splits over the faces ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryIntegralFaces · FormEval.integral_density_eq_sum_face⟧. Hence $\int_{\partial(M_i,o_i)} a = \int_{\partial_1M_i} a|(\partial_1M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ when the nonempty boundary sheet lies in the multi-chart class ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryIntegralStratum · EP.boundaryIntegral_eq_msInteg⟧.

*Step 6 (the boundary measures are local).* $\mu^\partial_\omega(D) = 0$ when the integrals of $\omega$ over the boundary sheets above $D$ vanish ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryLocal · boundaryMeasure_eq_zero_of_integ_eq_zero⟧, and $\mu^\partial_\omega(\partial S) = c(x)\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{\partial_1M_i} \omega$ for one structure when the integrals vanish off a closed saturated subset of $U(x)^*$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryLocal · boundaryMeasure_univ_eq⟧. For structures at points off $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ the structure is first restricted into a neighbourhood that avoids $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryLocal · OrientedTameStructure.exists_restrict_subset⟧, and both sides vanish.

*Step 7 (the theorems).* Steps 5 and 6 give the two properties of Step 3 for $\omega \mapsto \mu^\partial_\omega(\partial S)$. The generic statement is ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.stokes_of_boundaryMeasure⟧; for every functional with the local formula of Theorem 9.5.15 or 9.5.16 it is ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.theorem_9_5_17_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.theorem_9_5_18_hyp⟧; with the boundary measures themselves ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureEff⟧ it reads $\int_{\hat\Theta} d\omega = \mu^{\partial}_\omega(\partial S)$ and $\oint_{\hat\Theta} d\omega = \oint_{\partial S} \omega\, d\mu^{\partial}$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.theorem_9_5_17_msheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.theorem_9_5_18_msheets⟧, for $\omega \in \Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$ with $m \ge 1$. **Added hypothesis `hcovS`**, not derived from the text: at every point of $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$ an oriented tame structure describing $\hat T_\Theta$ whose sheets lie in one graph chart and whose nonempty boundary sheets lie in the multi-chart class; it gives the `hcov` of §IX.34 ⟦Chapter9/StokesBoundaryMeasure · EP.hcovB_of_hcovS⟧. It is derived from the text's hypotheses in §IX.36. For Theorem 9.5.18 the hypotheses of Theorem 9.5.5 are kept as in §IX.32.

**The witness.** $X$ is the trivial ep-groupoid of the half-space $[0,\infty) \times \mathbb R^2$, and $\Theta = 1$ on the closed upper hemisphere $\{|p| = 1\}$, a compact $2$-dimensional tame sheet whose boundary stratum is the equator ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereSheet · hemi⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereSheet · isSubmanifoldOfDim_hemi⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereSheet · boundaryStratum_hemi⟧, with its orientation and $\hat T_\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · thetaH⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · hemiOrientation⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · TH⟧. $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_hasScPartitionsOfUnity⟧, $\hat T_\Theta$ is an orientation ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_isOrientation⟧, `hcov` and `hcovS` hold ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_hcov⟧, and $\partial S \neq \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_boundary_nonempty⟧; together ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereWitness · e8w_stokes_hypotheses⟧. So Theorem 9.5.17 applies with a nonempty boundary ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereStokes · E8W.e8_hemisphere_stokes⟧. The witness has $m = 1$ and no corners, branching or isotropy. As a trivial ep-groupoid it has the local unique continuation property, so it is a witness for Theorem 9.5.18 as well (§IX.38).

**With the text's hypotheses.** `hcovS` is derived (§IX.36), the case $m = 0$ holds with $\mu^\partial$ (§IX.38), and the effective version has the witness of §IX.38; row V9.68 is restated. What remains of gap G.110 is Remark 9.5.20 (§IX.39).

### IX.36 The class conditions derived: the corner estimate, and Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 for $n \ge 2$

The first proofs of §§IX.34–IX.35 assume `hcov` and `hcovS`: the nonempty boundary sheets $\partial_1 M_i$ of the structures lie in the multi-chart class, so that $\int|\omega|$ over them is finite. Both follow from the text's hypotheses. The earlier estimate for this (800–1,200 lines) assumed that the closed faces of a sheet would be built as submanifolds; the route taken needs none.

*Step 1, forms are continuous up to the corners.* On a tame sheet $M$, Part I's chart form of $\omega \in \Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$ is a $C^\infty$ form on the Mathlib manifold with corners $M$, read in its corner charts, which lie in the maximal atlas (§IX.30).

*Step 2, the face change of variables with absolute values.* The change of variables of §IX.35, Step 5, is redone with absolute values and lower integrals: on a face set of a corner chart $\kappa$, $|\omega|$ on the graph-chart frame is $|\det|$ times the absolute value of the face pull-back ⟦Chapter9/CornerFinite · EpGroupoid.FormEval.abs_ev_faceFrame⟧. On the preimage of a compact subset of the chart domain the face pull-back is a continuous function on a compact set, so it is integrable ⟦Chapter9/CornerFinite · EpGroupoid.integrableOn_facePullback_of_isCompact⟧.

*Step 3, the corner estimate* ⟦Chapter9/CornerFinite · EpGroupoid.FormEval.boundaryStratum_inter_mem_msheets⟧. If $\partial_1 M \cap V \subseteq K \subseteq M$ with $K$ compact, then $\partial_1 M \cap V$ is in the multi-chart class. Finitely many corner charts, each with a compact piece of its domain, cover $K$. $\partial_1 M \cap V$ is a countable union of face images, so it is Lindelöf and has a cover by countably many graph charts ⟦Chapter9/CornerFinite · EpGroupoid.FormEval.exists_chartCover_of_isLindelof⟧. Each piece of that cover is split by corner chart and pulled back by Step 2. For a fixed corner chart the pieces are disjoint and lie in one compact set of face parameters, so the sum of the integrals of $|\omega|$ is at most a finite sum of integrals over compact sets.

*Step 4, shrinking a structure.* Every oriented tame structure at $x$ restricts to one with the same natural representation, describing the same $\hat T_\Theta$, whose $U(x)$ lies in the interior of a closed neighbourhood $t$ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.exists_restrict_eq⟧. Then $\partial_1 M_i \subseteq M_i \cap t \cap K$, where $K$ is the compact set containing $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta \cap U(x)$ given by the properness property, and $M_i$ meets a compact subset of $U(x)$ in a compact set because $M_i \to U(x)$ is proper ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isCompact_M_inter⟧. Step 3 applies ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.boundaryStratum_inter_mem_msheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.exists_restrict_boundary_mem_msheets⟧. The natural representation is kept, and with it the local unique continuation property.

*Step 5, the theorems.* So `hcov` and `hcovS` follow from `hloc`, the reading (d) of "oriented, tame" (§IX.23) ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.hcov_of_loc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.hcov_of_loc_isLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.hcovS_of_loc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryCover · EP.hcovS_of_loc_isLUC⟧. Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 hold with the local formula for the structures whose nonempty boundary sheets are in the class ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.theorem_9_5_15_class⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.theorem_9_5_16_class⟧; such structures exist at every point and every structure restricts to one, so the uniqueness is the text's. The canonical measures are ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.boundaryMeasure⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.boundaryMeasureEff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.boundaryMeasure_spec⟧. **Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 as printed, $m \ge 1$** (V9.68) ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.theorem_9_5_17⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.theorem_9_5_18⟧. *For $X$ with sc-smooth partitions of unity, $\Theta$ compact, branched, with an orientation $\hat T_\Theta$ and `hloc`, and $\omega \in \Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$: $\int_{\hat\Theta} d\omega = \mu^\partial_\omega(\partial S)$, with the measure of Theorem 9.5.15; with the local unique continuation property of $X$, the same for $\oint$ and the measure of Theorem 9.5.16* ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · EP.hloc_hasLUC⟧. The hemisphere of §IX.35 satisfies these hypotheses with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereBoundaryMeasure · E8W.k1_hemisphere_stokes⟧.

### IX.37 The local formula for every oriented tame structure

The text states the formula of Theorem 9.5.15 for every structure. Step 4 of §IX.36 handles a structure after shrinking it; toward the frontier of $U(x)$ the corner charts of $M_i$ give no uniform bound. The formula holds for every structure all the same, by comparison with other structures.

*Step 1, a finite cover.* $\partial_1 M_i$ lies in a compact subset of $\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, by the properness property. Cover it by finitely many $U(p)'$ of structures as in §IX.36, whose nonempty boundary sheets are in the class.

*Step 2, a common tangent space* ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · MPolyfold.k1_exists_tangent_eq⟧. At $z \in \partial_1 M_i \cap U(p)'$ some sheet $M'_k$ of the other structure passes through $z$ with $T_zM'_k = T_zM_i$. Otherwise there is an open $O \ni z$ on which, at every common point, the tangent spaces of $M_i$ and of each $M'_k$ differ. Since $M_i \subseteq \mathrm{supp}\,\Theta$, every point of $M_i \cap O$ lies on some $M'_k$, and there the relative tangent space of $M_i \cap M'_k$ is not full. Such points form an $(m+1)$-null set, by the argument of Lemma 9.4.6 (§IX.28), while an open piece of an $(m+1)$-dimensional submanifold is not null.

*Step 3, the same stratum.* $\{d = 1\}$ is defined through the tangent space alone, so $z \in \partial_1 M'_k$ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · MPolyfold.k1_mem_boundaryStratum_of_tangent_eq⟧. Whether $d_{M_i} = d_X$, which the tame induced structure does not give, does not matter.

*Step 4, domination.* $\partial_1 M_i$ lies in the union of finitely many sheets of the class, and a submanifold covered by finitely many sheets of the class is in the class ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · EpGroupoid.FormEval.k1_msheets_of_subset_list⟧. So every nonempty boundary sheet of every oriented tame structure is in the class ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · EP.boundarySheet_mem_msheets_of_loc⟧.

**Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 as printed, $m \ge 1$** (V9.67, restated) ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · EP.theorem_9_5_15⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · EP.theorem_9_5_16⟧. *For $n = m + 1$ with $m \ge 1$, $\Theta$ compact, branched, with an orientation $\hat T_\Theta$ and `hloc`, there is exactly one linear $\omega \mapsto \mu^\partial_\omega$ from $\Omega^m_{ep,\infty}(X)$ to the signed measures on $(\partial S, L(\partial S))$ with $\mu^\partial_\omega(K) = \frac{1}{\sharp G_x}\sum_i \sigma_i \int_{K_i} \omega|(\partial_1 M_i, o_{\partial M_i})$ for every $x \in \mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$, every oriented tame structure at $x$ describing $\hat T_\Theta$ and every measurable $K$ with $|K| \subseteq |U(x)|$*; with $\sharp G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ when $X$ has the local unique continuation property. The canonical measure has the formula for every structure ⟦Chapter9/AllStructures · EP.boundaryMeasure_apply_all⟧. The sum runs over the nonempty $\partial_1 M_i$, which contribute nothing in the text when empty, and $n$-dimensionality follows from `hloc`.

### IX.38 Dimension one: 0-forms, finite sets of boundary points, and the half-circle

For $n = 1$ the boundary sheets are $0$-dimensional and $\omega \in \Omega^0_{ep,\infty}(X)$; the multi-chart class of §IX.34 needs $m > 0$.

*Step 1, 0-forms as functions.* A 0-form is read as a function on objects, its level-0 value at a smooth point, invariant under morphisms ⟦Chapter9/ZeroFormValues · EP.zeroFormEval⟧; its restriction to a sheet is this value ⟦Chapter9/ZeroFormValues · EP.formsInftyRestrict_zero_eq⟧. The integral over an oriented point $p$ is $\pm\omega(p)$, the sign from the orientation: the point integration of §IX.31 through this evaluation ⟦Chapter9/ZeroFormValues · EP.zeroFormIntegration⟧.

*Step 2, finite sets of oriented points* ⟦Chapter9/FinitePointIntegration · EpGroupoid.finPointIntegration⟧. For a finite set $N$ of smooth points, $\int_A \omega = \sum_{p \in N \cap A} \pm\omega(p)$. This is a sheet integration in the sense of §IX.31 for the class of finite sets ⟦Chapter9/FinitePointIntegration · EpGroupoid.finPointSheets⟧, with the null sets of dimension $0$: the tangent space of a finite set at one of its points is that of the point ⟦Chapter9/FinitePointIntegration · EpGroupoid.submanifoldTangent_finite_eq⟧, and every subset of a finite set is measurable. On sets with at most one point it is the point integration ⟦Chapter9/FinitePointIntegration · EpGroupoid.finPointInteg_eq_pointInteg⟧. For 0-forms: ⟦Chapter9/FinitePointIntegration · EP.finZeroFormIntegration⟧.

*Step 3, the boundary sheets are finite.* In a corner chart with values in $[0, \infty)$ the face is one point, so near every point a 1-dimensional tame sheet has at most one point of its boundary stratum ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · MPolyfold.exists_isOpen_boundaryStratum_subsingleton⟧. Every oriented tame structure restricts to one whose boundary sheets have at most one point ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.exists_boundarySheet_subsingleton⟧, and the class conditions follow from `hloc` ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · EpGroupoid.hcov_dim1_of_loc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · EpGroupoid.hcovEff_dim1_of_loc⟧. The covering argument of §IX.37 then shows that every $\partial_1 M_i$ is finite ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.boundarySheet_finite_of_loc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.boundarySheet_mem_finPointSheets_of_loc⟧.

*Step 4, Part I's boundary integral.* For a 1-dimensional sheet with one boundary point $p$, Part I's $\int_{\partial M} \omega$ is $\pm\omega(p)$: the Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb R^0$ is a Dirac measure, and the face sign is that of §IX.35, Step 5, at $m = 0$ ⟦Chapter9/FaceIntegralDimOne · EpGroupoid.boundaryIntegral_eq_pointInteg⟧ ⟦Chapter9/FaceIntegralDimOne · EP.boundaryIntegral_eq_zeroFormIntegration⟧.

*Step 5, Stokes.* The locality argument of §IX.35, Step 6, is redone for any sheet integration ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasure_univ_eqI⟧ and combined with the boundary-sum form of §IX.35, Step 4 ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EP.stokes_of_boundaryMeasure_dim1⟧.

**The theorems for $n = 1$** (V9.67, V9.68). Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 with the formula for every oriented tame structure, $\int_{K_i} \omega|(\partial_1 M_i, o) = \sum_{p \in K_i} \pm\omega(p)$ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_15_dim1_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_16_dim1_all⟧, first proved for the structures whose boundary sheets are points ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_15_dim1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/BoundaryMeasureDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_16_dim1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/EffectiveDimOneLUC · EP.theorem_9_5_16_dim1_isLUC⟧. Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18: $\int_{\hat\Theta} d\omega = \mu^\partial_\omega(\partial S)$ ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_17_dim1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EP.theorem_9_5_18_dim1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/EffectiveDimOneLUC · EP.theorem_9_5_18_dim1_isLUC⟧, with the measures ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureDim1⟧ ⟦Chapter9/StokesDimOne · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureEffDim1⟧, which are those of the $n = 1$ Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureDim1_apply_all⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AllStructuresDimOne · EP.boundaryBranchedMeasureEffDim1_apply_all⟧. The hypotheses are the text's.

**Witnesses with nonempty boundary.** *$n = 1$.* $X = [0, \infty) \times \mathbb R$ as a trivial ep-groupoid, and $\Theta = 1$ on the closed half-circle $\{|p| = 1\}$, the image of the sc⁺-retraction $p \mapsto p/|p|$ of $X \setminus \{0\}$: a compact, tame, 1-dimensional submanifold ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleSheet · K2Arc.isSubmanifoldOfDim_arc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleSheet · K2Arc.isTameSubMPolyfold_arc⟧ whose boundary stratum is its two end points on $\{0\} \times \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleSheet · K2Arc.boundaryStratum_arc⟧, oriented by a field that is a unit tangent on the circle ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.arcOrientation⟧. All hypotheses of Theorems 9.5.15–9.5.18 for $n = 1$ hold, with $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta) \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.arc_hloc⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.arc_isLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.k2_arc_hypotheses⟧, and Stokes' theorem applies ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.k2_arc_stokes⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HalfCircleWitness · K2Arc.k2_arc_stokes_eff⟧. *$n = 2$, the effective version.* Every natural representation of a trivial ep-groupoid has the local unique continuation property ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereStokesEffective · E8W.hasLUC_trivial⟧, so the hemisphere of §IX.35 has it ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereStokesLUC · E8W.e8w_isLUC⟧, and Theorem 9.5.18 applies with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereStokesLUC · E8W.k2_hemisphere_stokes_eff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/HemisphereStokesEffective · E8W.e8_hemisphere_stokes_eff⟧. Neither witness has corners, branching or nontrivial isotropy; Remark 9.5.20 is about the last (§IX.39).

### IX.39 Remark 9.5.20 (2021 pp. 451–452): the example, in part

**The text.** $X = \{(-1, 0)\} \cup ((-1, 1) \times B) \cup \{(1, 0)\} \subseteq \mathbb R \times \mathbb C$ with an M-polyfold structure, $\mathbb Z_3$ rotating the $\mathbb C$-factor, $M = [-1, 1] \times \{0\}$, $\Theta(t, z) = \delta_0(z)$ oriented by $[-1, 1]$, and $f(t, z) = \phi(t)$. The remark computes $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df = \frac13(\phi(1) - \phi(-1))$ and observes that $\partial X = \{(\pm 1, 0)\}$ is a sub-ep-groupoid whose points have trivial effective isotropy, while in $X$ it is $\mathbb Z_3$: the boundary integral of $f$ is $\frac13(\phi(1) - \phi(-1))$ read in $X$, in accordance with Stokes' theorem, and $\phi(1) - \phi(-1)$ read in $\partial X$.

**The M-polyfold** ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpPolyfold · K3.P⟧. The text says only that $X$ can be given an M-polyfold structure. It is given one with one chart, onto an sc-smooth retract of the partial quadrant $[0, \infty)^2 \times (c_0 \oplus c_0)$ in $E = \mathbb R^2 \oplus c_0 \oplus c_0$, with the weighted scale of Remark 4.1.3's example (§IV.27). The retraction is $R(p, a, b) = (2p/|p|, \pi_{\tau(p)}a, \pi_{\tau(p)}b)$ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpRetract · K3.Rt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpRetract · K3.mem_O_iff⟧, with Remark 4.1.3's family $\pi_\tau$ (rank one for $\tau > 0$, zero for $\tau \le 0$) composed with $\tau(p) = p_0p_1$ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpRetract · IsLossFamily.comp_contDiff⟧ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpRetract · IsLossFamily.diag⟧. Its retract is the quarter circle of radius $2$ carrying a plane over each interior point and a point over each end. The chart is $\psi(t, z) = (2(\cos\theta, \sin\theta), \mathrm{Re}\,w\,\beta_\tau, \mathrm{Im}\,w\,\beta_\tau)$ with $\theta = \pi(1 + t)/4$ and $w = z/\sqrt{1 - |z|^2}$ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpPolyfold · K3.chart⟧. The degeneracy index is $1$ at $(\pm 1, 0)$ and $0$ elsewhere ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpPolyfold · K3.degIndex_eq⟧; the lower bound at the ends is Theorem 2.4.12, from an inward vector in the tangent space of the retract ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpPolyfold · K3.scDeriv_end⟧. So $\partial X = \{(-1, 0), (1, 0)\}$ ⟦Chapter9/DimensionJumpPolyfold · K3.boundary_eq⟧.

**The groupoid** ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.ε⟧. $\mathbb Z_3$ acts by $k \cdot (t, z) = (t, \omega^k z)$, sc-smoothly, since in the chart it is the restriction of the rotation of $(a, b)$, an sc-operator commuting with $R$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.isScSmoothMap_smul⟧. Its non-effective part is $\{1\} \times X$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.nonEffectivePart_ε⟧, which is closed, so $\varepsilon = \mathbb Z_3 \ltimes X$ has the local unique continuation property ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.isLUC_ε⟧. The effective isotropy has three elements on $M$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.card_effIsotropy_of_snd_eq_zero⟧ and one off $M$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.card_effIsotropy_of_snd_ne_zero⟧. $\partial X$ is a saturated sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.isEpSubgroupoid_boundary⟧, and $\varepsilon_B$ is the sub-ep-groupoid of Proposition 7.1.22 on it ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.εB⟧. At a point of $\partial X$ the isotropy group has three elements in $\varepsilon$ and in $\varepsilon_B$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.card_isotropy_εB⟧, and the effective isotropy has three in $\varepsilon$ and one in $\varepsilon_B$ ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.card_effIsotropy_εB⟧: every morphism of $\varepsilon_B$ acts trivially near its points. Collected: ⟦Chapter9/CyclicGroupoidIsotropy · K3.remark_9_5_20_effIsotropy⟧.

**Not formalized** (gap G.110, in part). $\Theta$ with its orientation and `hloc` at the infinite-dimensional ends; sc-smooth partitions of unity of $\varepsilon$ (Corollary 7.6.6 asks for a Hilbert space on level $0$, and here $E_0$ contains $c_0$); $f$ as a 0-form; $\oint_{\hat\Theta} df = \frac13(\phi(1) - \phi(-1))$, by the $n = 1$ theorems of §IX.38 and the local formula at the two ends; the integral of $f$ over $\partial\Theta$ in $\varepsilon_B$; and that $\partial X$ is a smooth submanifold, shown at each of its two points only. Estimated at 2,340–3,790 lines (Findings, Chapter 9, item 120).

## Part X. Equivalences and localization (HWZ Chapter 10, §§10.1–10.5 and Appendix §§10.6.1–10.6.3 (2017 §§10.1–10.5))

Chapter 10 continues Part II; its numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021, pp. 461–520), with the 2017 text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 333–374). It studies the sc-smooth functors between ep-groupoids that should become invertible once ep-groupoids are taken as models of polyfolds. §10.1 defines equivalences (Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1)), characterizes them as the equivalences of categories that are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects (Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1)), builds the refinement along an open covering (Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1)), shows that natural equivalence, the two-out-of-three property and the tangent functor respect equivalences (Definition 10.1.4, Propositions 10.1.5, 10.1.6, Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.2, 10.2, 10.3, 10.1)) and, mostly new in 2021, that the properties of Chapter 7 are invariant (Remarks 10.1.8, 10.1.11, 10.1.12, Propositions 10.1.9, 10.1.10, 10.1.13, 10.1.14, 10.1.16–10.1.19, Example 10.1.15). §10.2 constructs the weak fibred product (Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3), Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2), Remark 10.2.3 (2017: 10.2)). §10.4 carries all this to strong bundles: strong bundle equivalences (Definition 10.4.1 (2017: 10.10)), the pull-back and push-forward of section functors (Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4, Theorem 10.4.5 (2017: 10.7–10.9, 10.8)), natural transformations of strong bundle functors (Definitions 10.4.8, 10.4.10, Remark 10.4.9 (2017: 10.11, 10.12, 10.4)) and the category $\mathcal{SEP}$ (Definition 10.4.11 (2017: 10.13)). §10.3, treated here after §10.4 in the order of the verified edition, inverts the equivalences: diagrams $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ with $F$ an equivalence, their refinement and equivalence (Definitions 10.3.1, 10.3.3, 10.3.5, Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4, 10.3.6, Definition 10.3.7 (2017: 10.4–10.7, 10.3–10.5)), the composition of classes (Theorem 10.3.8 (2017: 10.3), Appendix §10.6.1), generalized isomorphisms (Definition 10.3.9, Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.8, 10.4), Appendix §10.6.2), the category $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ with the functors $i$ and $|\cdot|$ (Proposition 10.3.11, Definition 10.3.12, Theorems 10.3.14, 10.3.15 (2017: 10.6, 10.9, 10.5, 10.6)) and the invariance of the properties of Chapter 7 under generalized isomorphisms (Propositions 10.3.16, 10.3.17, Remark 10.3.18, Theorem 10.3.19, Definition 10.3.20, Theorem 10.3.21). §10.5, treated after §10.3, repeats the localization for strong bundles: diagrams $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} W'' \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ with $\Phi$ a strong bundle equivalence, their classes, the maps $[d]$, $|[D]|$ and the homomorphisms $\gamma$ (pp. 504–506), the category $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ and generalized strong bundle isomorphisms (Definitions 10.5.1, 10.5.2 (2017: 10.14, 10.15), Remark 10.5.3), the push-forward of section functors (Theorem 10.5.4 (2017: 10.9), Remark 10.5.5) and the local regularity property (Proposition 10.5.6, Theorem 10.5.7 (2017: 10.10)). Appendix §10.6.3, new in 2021, gives the example behind Remark 10.1.8 on a weighted Sobolev scale; §10.1 also introduces the full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ (p. 461) and §10.4 the strong bundle versions of Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10 (Propositions 10.4.6, 10.4.7).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Every gap of Chapter 10 is closed (G.111–G.127): each statement of the chapter is proved, and two, Theorems 10.3.19 and 10.5.7, do not hold as we read them and are proved for an effective target. Nothing in the chapter is open or formalized only in part. *§10.1.* All definitions are formalized. Lemma 10.1.2 (with its converse), Propositions 10.1.3, 10.1.5, 10.1.6, 10.1.13, 10.1.14, 10.1.16–10.1.19, Theorem 10.1.7, Remarks 10.1.11 and 10.1.12 and Example 10.1.15 are proved, several in a stronger form. Proposition 10.1.9 is proved, and Proposition 10.1.10 with (LR) on one side only (§§X.5, X.7; G.113–G.115). The subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ is §X.27 (G.111). Remark 10.1.8 with the example of Appendix §10.6.3, on the weighted Sobolev scale as printed, is §X.28 (G.112). Two results the text quotes or leaves to the reader are proved: Proposition 10.1.5, and the fullness and faithfulness of $TF$ in Theorem 10.1.7. *§10.2.* All claims of Theorem 10.2.2 are proved, including that the structures are those induced from the triple products (§X.29; G.116), and so is Remark 10.2.3. *§10.4.* All definitions are formalized, and Propositions 10.4.2–10.4.4, Remark 10.4.9 and the equivalence of Definitions 10.4.8 and 10.4.10 are proved. Theorem 10.4.5 is proved with its Fred part (§X.31; G.121); the sc-smoothness of the push-forward, "easily verified" in the text, is proved too. Propositions 10.4.6 and 10.4.7 are §X.32 (G.122), with Definition 8.4.2 read for strong bundle isomorphisms of $W|U(x)$; Proposition 10.4.7 is proved with the property for the target only. *§10.3.* All definitions are formalized, with the proofs of the appendix. Proved: (E1)–(E3), Lemmas 10.3.2, 10.3.4, 10.3.6, Theorems 10.3.8, 10.3.10, 10.3.14, 10.3.15, Propositions 10.3.11, 10.3.16, 10.3.17, Remark 10.3.18 and Theorem 10.3.21 (§§X.16–X.20; G.118 closed by §X.20, G.119 by §X.23). The universal property of the localization (G.117) is §X.30. Theorem 10.3.19 does not hold as we read it, and holds for an effective target (§X.20; G.120, settled). *§10.5.* Formalized: the diagrams, their refinements and classes, $[d]$, $|[D]|$, the square $|\mathscr D|$, $\gamma$, Definitions 10.5.1 and 10.5.2, and $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ as a category through the weak fibred product of strong bundles (§§X.21, X.22). (10.24) with generalized vertical maps and the local expressions $q$, $Q$ are §X.33 (G.124). Proved: Remark 10.5.3, with both directions of the strong bundle Theorem 10.3.10 (§§X.22, X.34; G.123); Theorem 10.5.4 with its Fred part and as a linear isomorphism (§§X.23, X.31; G.125); Remark 10.5.5, with an example; and Proposition 10.5.6 (§§X.23, X.32; G.126). Theorem 10.5.7 does not hold as we read it, and holds over an effective base of the target (§X.23; G.127, settled). Remark 10.3.13 and the sentences on "smaller models" in Remark 10.2.3 have no formal content. *The narrower row.* There is one: V10.66, Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target. The effectiveness of $Y$ is an added hypothesis, not derived from the text; without it the theorem does not hold as we read it (`not_theorem_10_3_19`). Its satisfiability witness is the point (§X.20). The strong bundle analogue is part of the restated row V10.67, with the same reason: Theorem 10.5.7 over an effective base of the target, with (LR) of a base or the local regularity property of the target bundle (§X.23).

**Six structural choices.** (1) *Equivalences as a structure.* `EpFunctor.IsEquivalence` has the four conditions of Definition 10.1.1 as fields, with full and faithful stated on the sets of morphisms; Mathlib's `Functor.IsEquivalence` of the underlying functor is derived (§X.1). (2) *Indexed coverings.* The refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$ takes a family $(U_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of open sets; objects and morphisms are open subsets of products with the discrete $\iota$ (§X.2). (3) *Iterated fibred products.* The weak fibred product is built from Part I's fibred products, twice, so that its M-polyfold structures come with their universal properties; the admissibility, $F$ or $G$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, is all that the construction uses (§X.9). (4) *Total pull-backs and push-forwards.* $\Phi^*$ and $\Phi_*$ are defined on all maps, by the zero of the fibre where needed, and the push-forward with one choice of $x$ and $\sigma$ made for all; all statements are about section functors, where the choice does not matter (§X.12). (5) *Diagrams one universe up.* A diagram contains its middle ep-groupoid as an object of $\mathcal{EP}$, so the classes of diagrams form a type in the universe of the objects of $\mathcal{EP}$ and $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ is a large category like $\mathcal{EP}$; compositions are written in Mathlib's order, $d.\mathrm{comp}\,e$ for the text's $[e] \circ [d]$ (§X.16). (6) *The weak fibred product of strong bundles as a pull-back.* The text leaves it to the reader; it is the pull-back of $W''$ along $\pi_Z$, so that one projection is a strong bundle equivalence by construction and the squares in the proofs of the composition commute strictly, by the fibrewise injectivity of strong bundle equivalences; the generalized strong bundle maps, defined as the classes of the equivalence relation generated by having a common refinement, are the text's classes by the transitivity (§§X.21, X.22).

Throughout, $X = (X, \mathbf X)$, $Y$, $Z$ are ep-groupoids as in Part VII, $s, t$ the source and target, $|X|$ the orbit space and $|F| : |X| \to |Y|$ the induced map, $G_x$ the isotropy group, $T_x$ its subgroup acting trivially near $x$ and $\mathbf X^T$ the non-effective part (§VII.3). Functors are sc-smooth functors (`EpFunctor`), and natural transformations those of Chapter 8 (`EpNatTrans`).

### X.1 Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1) and Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1)

**Definition 10.1.1 (2017: 10.1)** (V10.1) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EP.equivalences⟧. The four fields are fullness and faithfulness on the sets of morphisms, $|F|$ a homeomorphism, and $F$ a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects. Fullness and faithfulness are those of Mathlib for the underlying functor ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.full_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.faithful_iff⟧, and so is essential surjectivity ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.essSurj_iff⟧. *Step 1, essential surjectivity.* For $y \in Y$, $|F|$ is onto, so $[y] = [F(x)]$ for some $x$, that is a morphism $F(x) \to y$ exists ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.essSurj⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_iso⟧. *Step 2, the morphism sets.* Every $\psi : F(x) \to F(x')$ is $F(\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_mor_eq⟧ and $F$ is injective on morphisms with the same ends ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.mor_injective⟧. *Step 3, the class $E$.* The identity is an equivalence ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.id⟧, composites are ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.comp⟧ (the composite of homeomorphisms and of local sc-diffeomorphisms, with $|G \circ F| = |G| \circ |F|$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.toFunctor_comp⟧), so `EP.equivalences` is a multiplicative class. Witness: the functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ (one morphism between any two integers) to the point ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpGroupoid.Examples.pairToPoint⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_pairToPoint⟧, a local sc-diffeomorphism because $\mathbb Z$ is discrete ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpGroupoid.Examples.isLocalScDiffeo_discrete⟧.

**Local sc-diffeomorphisms at a point.** The local property of Definition 10.1.1 (3) is localized ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_iff_forall⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.at⟧, with the rules used below: composition ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.comp⟧, agreement near the point ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.congr⟧, and the two cancellation rules: if $g \circ f$ and $g$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms at $x$ and $f(x)$, so is $f$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_left⟧; if $g \circ f$ and $f$ are, so is $g$ at $f(x)$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeoAt.of_comp_right⟧.

**Lemma 10.1.2 (2017: 10.1)** (V10.2) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.lemma_10_1_2⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.isEquivalence_iff⟧. *Step 1, $|F|$ is bijective.* For a functor of groupoids, $|F|$ is injective when $F$ is full ($F(x) \cong F(x')$ lifts to $x \cong x'$) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.injective_orbitMap_of_full⟧, surjective exactly when $F$ is essentially surjective ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.surjective_orbitMap_iff⟧, hence bijective for an equivalence of categories ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · GroupoidFunctor.bijective_orbitMap_of_isEquivalence⟧. *Step 2, $|F|$ is a homeomorphism.* $|F|$ is continuous by the universal property of the quotient ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.continuous_orbitMap⟧; it is open because $F$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, hence open, on objects and the orbit maps are open (Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1)) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.isOpenMap_orbitMap⟧. *Step 3, the converse.* An equivalence is full, faithful and essentially surjective (§X.1), so an equivalence of categories ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEquivalence_toFunctor⟧. *Not invertible.* The functor $\mathbb Z \to \mathrm{pt}$ above has no left inverse on objects ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpGroupoid.Examples.not_exists_leftInverse_pairToPoint⟧.

### X.2 Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1): the refinement $X_{\mathcal U}$

**The construction** ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.groupoidStr⟧. A covering is a family of open sets $U_i$ with every object in some $U_i$; the trivial covering by $X$ is one ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.univ⟧. The text indexes the covering by itself and writes $(U, x)$; the index type is the formal reading. The objects $(i, x)$, $x \in U_i$, form an open subset of $\iota \times X$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · isOpen_of_discrete_left⟧, the morphisms $(i, \varphi, j)$ one of $(\iota \times \iota) \times \mathbf X$, and both get the open-subset M-polyfold structures ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.objPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.morPolyfold⟧, which need a nonempty set: the object set of $X$ is assumed nonempty (for an empty $X$ there is nothing to prove). Products with a discrete space keep the paracompactness and metrizability ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · paracompactSpace_discrete_prod⟧.

**$X_{\mathcal U}$ is an ep-groupoid** ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.epGroupoid⟧. *Step 1, local sc-diffeomorphisms.* On a product with a discrete factor a map that is a local sc-diffeomorphism on each sheet is one ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · isLocalScDiffeo_sheet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · isLocalScDiffeo_snd_discrete⟧; $s(i, \varphi, j) = (i, s(\varphi))$ and $t(i, \varphi, j) = (j, t(\varphi))$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_src⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt⟧, through the restriction rules for open subsets ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_restrictOpen_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeoAt_restrict⟧. *Step 2, unit, inverse, multiplication.* They are those of $X$ on each sheet, sc-smooth by the continuity on the discrete factor ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · isScSmoothOn_discrete_of_continuousOn⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isScSmoothMap_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isScSmoothMap_inv⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.isScSmoothCompSheet⟧. *Step 3, properness.* At $(i, x)$ take a neighbourhood $V_0$ of $x$ with the properness property of $X$ and an open $V(x)$ with $\mathrm{cl}\,V(x) \subseteq U_i \cap V_0$; then $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}(\{i\} \times V(x)))$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.exists_isProperMap⟧. The proof uses ultrafilters in place of the text's sequences; the index $j$ of a limit is determined by the sheet, which is clopen.

**Proposition 10.1.3 (2017: 10.1)** (V10.3) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.proposition_10_1_3⟧. $F(i, x) = x$, $F(i, \varphi, j) = \varphi$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.OpenCover.functor⟧ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, faithful because a morphism of $X_{\mathcal U}$ is determined by its ends and its $\varphi$, full because $\psi : x \to x'$ lifts to $(i, \psi, j)$, and essentially surjective because every $x$ lies in some $U_i$; Lemma 10.1.2 applies. The text writes the morphism as $(U, \varphi, v)$ in the formula for $F$; we read $(U, \varphi, V)$ (possible misprint). *Witness.* The covering $\{x > -1\}$, $\{x < 1\}$ of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.Examples.reflectionCover⟧ gives an equivalence ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.Examples.isEquivalence_reflectionCover⟧ that is not injective on objects ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceRefinement · EpGroupoid.Examples.not_injective_reflectionCover_obj⟧.

### X.3 Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2), Propositions 10.1.5 and 10.1.6 (2017: 10.2 and 10.3)

**Definition 10.1.4 (2017: 10.2)** (V10.4) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · definition_10_1_4⟧. The definition is Chapter 8's Definition 8.1.13 ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpNatTrans⟧ ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent⟧; the claims after it, that $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation and compatible with composition, are Chapter 8's ⟦Chapter8/NatTrans · EpFunctor.naturallyEquivalent_equivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter8/NatTrans · EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter8/NatTrans · EpFunctor.NaturallyEquivalent.comp_right⟧. A natural transformation of ep-groupoids is a natural isomorphism of the underlying functors, every morphism being invertible ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpNatTrans.toNatIso⟧.

**Proposition 10.1.5 (2017: 10.2)** (V10.5) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_5⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.of_natTrans⟧. The text quotes it from the literature. *Step 1.* $\tau : X \to \mathbf X'$ is continuous ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpNatTrans.continuous_app⟧ and, since $s \circ \tau = F$ with $F$ and $s$ local sc-diffeomorphisms, a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_app⟧. *Step 2.* $G = t \circ \tau$ is a composite of local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpNatTrans.isLocalScDiffeo_obj⟧. *Step 3.* The underlying functors are naturally isomorphic, so $G$ is an equivalence of categories with $F$, and Lemma 10.1.2 applies. The symmetric statement follows from the symmetry of $\simeq$.

**Proposition 10.1.6 (2017: 10.3)** (V10.6) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_6⟧. *Step 1, categories.* $\Phi$ is an equivalence of categories since $F$ and $\Phi \circ F$ are (Mathlib's two-out-of-three). *Step 2, objects in the image.* At $F(x)$, $\Phi \circ F$ and $F$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms at $x$, so $\Phi$ is one at $F(x)$ (the right cancellation rule). *Step 3, transport.* The text's argument stops here; an arbitrary $y$ receives a morphism $\sigma : F(x) \to y$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_iso⟧, and the local sc-diffeomorphism property of a functor passes from $s(\sigma)$ to $t(\sigma)$ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_obj_tgt⟧: near $\sigma$, $t \circ \tau = \Phi \circ t \circ \ldots$ is written with a local inverse $\tau$ of $s$, and on morphisms $\Phi$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism where it is one on objects ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeoAt_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.isLocalScDiffeo_mor⟧. *Step 4.* Lemma 10.1.2. The text's $|\Phi| : |X| \to |Y|$ in the proof is read $|\Phi| : |Y| \to |Z|$ (possible misprint).

### X.4 Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1): the tangent of an equivalence

**Theorem 10.1.7 (2017: 10.1)** (V10.7) ⟦Chapter10/Equivalence · EpFunctor.theorem_10_1_7⟧. $TF$ is Chapter 8's tangent functor ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpFunctor.tangent⟧; the text proves the homeomorphism and the local sc-diffeomorphism property and leaves full and faithful to the reader. Here all goes through Lemma 10.1.2. *Step 1, local sc-diffeomorphism.* The tangent of a local sc-diffeomorphism is one (Part I). *Step 2, faithful.* A tangent morphism $(\varphi, v)$ is determined by $\varphi$ and its source vector ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tangent_ext⟧, and $F$ is faithful. *Step 3, full.* For $(\psi, w) : TF(x, a) \to TF(x', a')$, $\psi = F(\varphi)$ by fullness of $F$; $\varphi$ lifts to a tangent morphism with source $(x, a)$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.exists_tSrc_eq'⟧, whose image under $TF$ has the same source as $(\psi, w)$, and the targets agree since $TF$ is injective on the tangent fibre at $x'$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.injOn_tangentFiber⟧. *Step 4, essentially surjective.* For $(y, b)$ take $\psi : F(x) \to y$, lift $\psi^{-1}$ with source $(y, b)$ and use that $TF$ maps $T_xX$ onto $T_{F(x)}Y$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.tangentFiber_subset_image⟧, then invert ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tInv⟧.

### X.5 Remarks 10.1.8 and 10.1.11 (2017: 10.1), Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4)

**Also formalized.** The full subcategory $\mathcal{EP}_{lreg}$ of p. 461 (G.111) is §X.27. Remark 10.1.8 (new in the 2021 edition), with the example of Appendix §10.6.3 on its weighted Sobolev sc-retract (G.112), is §X.28. Propositions 10.1.9 and 10.1.10 (G.113, G.114) are the next two paragraphs.

**Proposition 10.1.9** (V10.62) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_9⟧, for (LR) as in Definition 7.4.19 ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.IsLR⟧. *The transport chart* ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.exists_transportChart⟧: for $\psi : F(x) \to y$, $Q = \hat\psi \circ F$ with $\hat\psi = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of a neighbourhood of $x$ onto one of $y$, with morphisms $\psi_u : F(u) \to Q(u)$. *The isomorphism* $g \mapsto \psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$, $G_x \to G_y$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.conj⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.bijective_conj⟧; on p. 469 its second factor $\sigma \mapsto \psi \circ \sigma \circ \psi^{-1}$ is printed with target $U(y)$, read $G_y$ (possible misprint). The equivariance (10.2)–(10.3), $Q(g * z) = (\psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1}) * Q(z)$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.Q_Φ⟧, comes from the uniqueness of $\Gamma$ on connected sets ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Γ⟧. *The step the text takes for granted*, $U(y) = Q(U(x))$ "with the natural action": a natural representation at $y$ (Theorem 7.1.13) restricted to $Q(U(x))$ is one, invariant under $G_y$ by the equivariance and the surjectivity of the isomorphism ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_push⟧; the converse direction restricts one at $x$ to $Q^{-1}(U(y))$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_naturalRep_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_Φ⟧. *The conjugation.* The condition of (LR) on one $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLR⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpGroupoid.isLR_iff_hasLR⟧ passes both ways along an equivariant sc-diffeomorphism over a surjection of the groups: $\beta = Q^{-1} \circ \gamma \circ Q = \hat g$ gives $\gamma = (\psi \circ F(g) \circ \psi^{-1})^\wedge$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.hasLR_iff_of_equivariant⟧. *Witness* ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EquivalenceLRExamples.nonempty_transportChart_pointEP⟧.

**Proposition 10.1.10 (2017: 10.4)** (V10.63) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_one⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_one_of_isLR_right⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_10_two⟧. Only (LR) for $X$ is used; with (LR) for $Y$, Proposition 10.1.9 supplies it. ### X.6 Remark 10.1.12, Propositions 10.1.13 and 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5), Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1)

**Remark 10.1.12** (V10.9) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.remark_10_1_12⟧. *Step 1.* $g \mapsto F(g)$ is a homomorphism $G_x \to G_{F(x)}$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.isotropyHom⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.isotropyHom_val⟧, bijective for an equivalence (fullness and faithfulness at $(x, x)$) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijective_isotropyHom⟧. *Step 2.* $g \in T_x$ iff $F(g) \in T_{F(x)}$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.isotropyHom_mem_trivialSet_iff⟧, since $F$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects and on morphisms, and the local actions correspond. *Step 3.* Conjugation by $\psi : F(x) \to y$ ⟦Chapter7/Groupoid · GroupoidStr.isotropyConj⟧ maps $T_{F(x)}$ onto $T_y$ ⟦Chapter7/Effective · EpGroupoid.isotropyConj_mem_trivialSet_iff⟧. The text's $G_x \to Y_y$ is read $G_x \to G_y$ (possible misprint).

**Proposition 10.1.13** (V10.10) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_13⟧. *Step 1, $\mathbf X^T$ along $F$.* For a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, $\varphi \in \mathbf X^T$ iff $F(\varphi) \in \mathbf Y^T$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.mor_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.mem_nonEffectivePart_of_mor⟧, that is $\mathbf X^T = F^{-1}(\mathbf Y^T) \cap \{s = t\}$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.nonEffectivePart_eq⟧. *Step 2, (1).* So $F_R$ is well defined ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.reducedMap⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.reducedMap_π⟧, continuous ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.continuous_reducedMap⟧ and open, $F$ being open on morphisms and the quotient maps open ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.isOpenMap_reducedMap⟧; only the local sc-diffeomorphism property of $F$ is used. *Step 3, closedness.* For an equivalence, $\mathbf X^T$ is closed iff $\mathbf Y^T$ is ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_iff⟧. From $Y$ to $X$: $\mathbf X^T$ is the preimage of a closed set intersected with a closed set. From $X$ to $Y$: a $\psi \in \mathrm{cl}(\mathbf Y^T)$ at $y$ is conjugated, by a local inverse of $t$ at a morphism $\sigma : F(x) \to y$, into a morphism at $F(x)$ in $\mathrm{cl}(F(\mathbf X^T))$, with the continuity of the composition at a point ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpGroupoid.continuousAt_comp⟧; closures replace the text's sequences. *Step 4, (2).* Theorem 7.2.22 says $\mathbf X^R$ is Hausdorff iff $\mathbf X^T$ is closed ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22⟧; with Step 3 this gives (2), the route of the text.

**Proposition 10.1.14 (2017: 10.5)** (V10.11) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.proposition_10_1_14⟧. With both reduced morphism spaces Hausdorff the reduced ep-groupoids of Chapter 7 exist ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid⟧. $F_R$ is $F$ on objects and $F_R$ of Step 2 on morphisms ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.reducedGroupoidFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.reduced⟧; it is a functor since $[\cdot]$ is ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceReduced · EpFunctor.reducedπ_eq_of_mor⟧, sc-smooth since the M-polyfold structure of $\mathbf X^R$ is the one for which the quotient map is a local sc-diffeomorphism, full and faithful by Remark 10.1.12, and $|F_R| = |F|$. By Proposition 10.1.13 (2) either Hausdorff hypothesis implies the other; both are kept, as in the text.

**Example 10.1.15 (2017: 10.1)** (V10.12) ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example_10_1_15⟧. $X = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R$ with $1, 3$ acting by $-1$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.z4LineAction⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X⟧, $Y = \mathbb Z/4 \ltimes \mathbb R^2$ by quarter turns ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.z4PlaneAction⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y⟧, $\Phi$ to the origin ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Functor⟧. *Step 1.* $2$ acts trivially on $\mathbb R$, not on $\mathbb R^2$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_two_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_two_not_mem_nonEffectivePart⟧. *Step 2.* Hence $(1, x)$ and $(3, x) = (2, x) \circ (1, x)$ have the same class ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015X_reducedπ_one_eq_three⟧, their images not ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceExamples · EpGroupoid.Examples.example1015Y_reducedπ_one_ne_three⟧, so no map of sets $f$ with $f([\varphi]) = [\Phi(\varphi)]$ exists. The text speaks of an induced map of the reduced ep-groupoids; the statement here needs no topology.

### X.8 Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3): the weak fibred product

**Definition 10.2.1 (2017: 10.3)** (V10.17) ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.groupoid⟧. *Objects.* $\{(\phi, z) \mid t(\phi) = G(z)\} \subseteq \mathbf Y \times Z$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.objRight⟧, then $\{(x, (\phi, z)) \mid F(x) = s(\phi)\}$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.objSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.Obj⟧, with projections and extensionality ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.Obj.ext⟧. *Morphisms.* The same with $\mathbf X$, $\mathbf Z$ and $F \circ s$, $G \circ s$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.morRight⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.morSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.Mor⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.Mor.ext⟧. *Structure maps.* The conjugate $G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj⟧ has the ends $F(t(h))$, $G(t(k))$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.src_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.tgt_conj⟧; it is the target's middle entry ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.tgt⟧, $s$ keeps $\phi$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.src⟧, the unit is $(1_x, \phi, 1_z)$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.unit⟧ and the inverse $(h^{-1}, \mathrm{conj}, k^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.inv⟧. The text prints $\iota(h, \psi, k) = (h^{-1}, G(k) \circ \phi \circ F(h)^{-1}, k^{-1})$; we read $\psi = \phi$ (possible misprint). The product of a composable pair is $(h \circ h', \phi', k \circ k')$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.compOf⟧, extended to a total map that returns its first argument off composable pairs ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.comp⟧. *Groupoid laws.* By the rules $\mathrm{conj}(h \circ h', \phi', k \circ k') = \mathrm{conj}(h, \mathrm{conj}(h', \phi', k'), k)$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj_comp⟧, $\mathrm{conj}$ of units ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj_unit⟧ and of inverses ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj_inv⟧, with $\phi$ recovered from the target ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj_recover⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.conj_comp_mor⟧; a morphism is a loop iff its ends agree ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.src_eq_tgt_iff⟧.

### X.9 Theorem 10.2.2 (2017: 10.2): $X \times_Y Z$ is an ep-groupoid

**The admissibility** ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.Admissible⟧. The construction uses of $F$ (or of $G$) only that it is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, which every equivalence is ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProductTheorem · WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_left⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProductTheorem · WeakFibredProduct.Admissible.of_isEquivalence_right⟧. *Step 1, sub-M-polyfolds.* Part I's fibred product of an sc-smooth map with a local sc-diffeomorphism is a sub-M-polyfold (Proposition 2.5.20); $t : \mathbf Y \to Y$ is one, so $\mathbf Y \,{}_t\!\times_G Z$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $\mathbf Y \times Z$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objRight⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.PA⟧, and its projection to $Z$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_snd_fibredProduct⟧; then the second fibred product with $F$ or with that projection ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_objSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.PObj⟧, and the same for morphisms ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morRight⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isSubMPolyfold_morSet⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.PB⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.PMor⟧. The text says the sets are sub-M-polyfolds of the triple products. They are, and the iterated structures are the induced ones (§X.29; G.116); the construction here does not use it. *Step 2, the projections.* $x$, $\phi$, $z$, $h$, $\phi$, $k$ are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_x⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_z⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_k⟧, and a map into $X \times_Y Z$ is sc-smooth when its entries are ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothOn_obj_of⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothOn_mor_of⟧. For $F$ admissible, $(x, \phi, z) \mapsto z$ and $(h, \phi, k) \mapsto k$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms ((10.9), (10.10)) ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_z⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_k⟧; for $G$ admissible the projections to $X$ and $\mathbf X$ are ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_x⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_h⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_fst_fibredProduct⟧. *Step 3, $s$ and $t$.* $\pi_Z \circ s = s_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\pi_Z \circ t = t_Z \circ \pi_{\mathbf Z}$ with three local sc-diffeomorphisms make $s$, $t$ ones ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.of_comm⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_src⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isLocalScDiffeo_tgt⟧; their sc-smoothness uses that of the conjugate ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_src⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_tgt⟧. *Step 4, unit, inverse, multiplication* ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothMap_inv⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.isScSmoothComp⟧: entries are multiplications of $X$ and $Z$ and projections, sc-smooth on the composable pairs ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_comp_of⟧. *Step 5, properness.* For open $U \ni x$, $V \ni z$ with the properness property in $X$ and $Z$, $W = \{x' \in U, z' \in V\}$ has $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,W)$ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.exists_isProperMap⟧: subsequences of $h_n$, then of $k_n$, converge, and $\phi_n = G(k_n)^{-1} \circ (G(k_n) \circ \phi_n \circ F(h_n)^{-1}) \circ F(h_n)$ converges by continuity of the multiplication ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · EpGroupoid.tendsto_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter10/WeakFibredProduct · WeakFibredProduct.continuous_conj⟧. The text writes $t : s^{-1}(U) \to X$; Definition 7.1.3 (3) asks for the closure, which is the reading.
