## Part XII. Sc-Fredholm sections on ep-groupoids (HWZ Chapter 12, §§12.1–12.5)

Chapter 12 opens Part III of the book (Springer 2021, pp. 569–597; the numbers below are the 2021 ones, with the 2017 text's in parentheses). It carries the Fredholm package of Part I (Chapters 5 and 6) from strong bundles over M-polyfolds to strong bundles $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over ep-groupoids. Everything in Part I lives on one M-polyfold; an ep-groupoid has two, the objects and the morphisms, and a strong bundle over it is a strong bundle over the objects together with an action $\mu$ of the morphisms on the fibres. The chapter asks of every Part I notion whether it can be made compatible with the morphisms, and answers by one construction, repeated: build the object on a neighbourhood $U(x)$ carrying the natural representation of the isotropy group $G_x$, average it over $G_x$, carry it to the saturation of $U(x)$ by morphisms, and glue the pieces with a partition of unity of the orbit space $|X|$. §12.1 defines sc-Fredholm section functors (Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1)). §12.2 builds auxiliary norms (Definition 12.2.1, Theorem 12.2.2, Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4, Proposition 12.2.5, Theorems 12.2.6, 12.2.7 (2017: Definition 12.2, Theorem 12.1, Definitions 12.3, 12.4, Proposition 12.1, Theorems 12.2, 12.3)) and their reflexive variant (Definitions 12.2.8, 12.2.10, Remarks 12.2.9, 12.2.12, Theorems 12.2.11, 12.2.13 (2017: Definitions 12.5, 12.6, Remarks 12.1, 12.2, Theorems 12.4, 12.5)). §12.3 supplies sc⁺-section functors (Definition 12.3.1, Theorems 12.3.2, 12.3.3, Remarks 12.3.4, 12.3.5, Definition 12.3.6, Proposition 12.3.7, Corollary 12.3.8, Theorem 12.3.9 (2017: Definition 12.7, Theorems 12.6, 12.7, Remarks 12.3, 12.4, Definition 12.8, Proposition 12.2, Corollary 12.1, Theorem 12.8)). §12.4 treats compactness (Definition 12.4.1, Theorem 12.4.2, Definition 12.4.3, Lemma 12.4.4, Proposition 12.4.5, Theorem 12.4.6 (2017: Definition 12.9, Theorem 12.9, Definition 12.10, Lemma 12.1, Proposition 12.3, Theorem 12.10)), and §12.5 the orientation bundle $O_f$ (Lemma 12.5.1, Definition 12.5.2, Theorem 12.5.3, Definition 12.5.4, Remark 12.5.5, Proposition 12.5.6, Theorem 12.5.7 (2017: Lemma 12.2, Definition 12.11, Theorem 12.11, Definition 12.12, Remark 12.5, Proposition 12.4, Theorem 12.12)). The sections of this Part follow the book: §XII.1 is §12.1; §§XII.2–XII.9 are §12.2; §§XII.10–XII.13 are §12.3; §§XII.14–XII.15 are §12.4; §§XII.16–XII.22 are §12.5; §XII.23 collects the hypotheses and their witnesses, §XII.24 what is not formalized and §XII.25 what the formalization taught us.

**What is proved, and what is not.** Every numbered item of Chapter 12 is formalized, and no statement of Chapter 12 was found not to hold as we read it. What remains open is §12.5's inheritance of Part I's hypotheses (gap G.140) and Theorem 12.5.7 restated for Chapter 10's classes of diagrams (gap G.192).

*§12.1.* Definition 12.1.1 and the remark after it (regularizing on objects and on morphisms, sc-Fredholm germs) are formalized as printed (§XII.1).

*§12.2.* Definition 12.2.1 is Definition 8.3.5, and Theorem 12.2.2, Definitions 12.2.3 and 12.2.4 with the remark between them, Proposition 12.2.5 and the good neighbourhood Theorem 12.2.6 are proved as printed (§§XII.2–XII.5). Theorem 12.2.7, the extension of an auxiliary norm from $\partial X$, is proved as printed for every tame $X$ with paracompact $|X|$ (§XII.6): its global part is the averaging–transport–gluing construction, and its local step is the norm $N'(w) = N(\text{transport of } w \text{ to } \rho(P w)) + \|h - A(u)h\|_{F_1}$ built from a continuous retraction $\rho$ onto the boundary. Definitions 12.2.8 and 12.2.10 are formalized, Remark 12.2.9 is proved in a stronger form (morphisms preserve mixed convergence) (§XII.7); Theorem 12.2.11 is proved as printed with its three clauses, and Remark 12.2.12 as printed, its clause (3) in a stronger form (§XII.8). Theorem 12.2.13 is proved with the text's hypotheses and with the paracompactness of $|X|$ that its proof takes from Theorem 12.2.11 made explicit; the local step the text settles by inspection is a lemma on the lower semicontinuity of $N'$ under mixed convergence (§XII.9).

*§12.3.* Definition 12.3.1 is formalized as printed and in a pointwise reading. Theorem 12.3.2 (1) is proved in each of the two consistent readings, Theorem 12.3.2 (2) in the pointwise reading (§XII.10); Theorem 12.3.3 in the pointwise reading, Remarks 12.3.4 and 12.3.5 in explicit forms (§XII.11). Pairing Definition 12.3.1 as printed with Part I's pointwise bump functions would need Part I's open weak-to-pointwise question; this is a reading, not formalization work. Definition 12.3.6 is formalized in its local form and its ep-groupoid form, Proposition 12.3.7 in a stronger form (only the face germs at the point are used) and Corollary 12.3.8 explicitly (§XII.12). Theorem 12.3.9, the extension of sc⁺-section functors from $\partial X$ with the bound $N(\tilde s) \le \delta$, is proved as printed (§XII.13).

*§12.4.* Definition 12.4.1, Theorem 12.4.2 and Lemma 12.4.4 are proved (§XII.14). Definition 12.4.3 is formalized, and Proposition 12.4.5 and Theorem 12.4.6 are proved in stronger forms, several of the text's hypotheses being unused (§XII.15).

*§12.5.* The action of a morphism on linearizations goes through a local strong bundle isomorphism built from its sheet (§XII.16). Lemma 12.5.1 and the action $\varphi_*$ on orientations are proved with §12.5's standing hypothesis, inherited from Part I, that sc⁺-sections pass through smooth fibre points (§XII.17). Definition 12.5.2 is Part I's $O_f$ (§XII.18). Theorem 12.5.3 is proved under Part I's hypotheses (tame $X$, bump functions on the objects, tame germ data), including its last sentence: the local isomorphism of a morphism carries a continuous local orientation near $x$ to one near $x'$, with value $\sigma_*o_x$ at $x'$ (§XII.19). Definition 12.5.4 is formalized, and its continuity clause, read for the topology of $O_f$, agrees with Part I's continuity of orientations along paths (§XII.20). Remark 12.5.5 is prose. Proposition 12.5.6 is proved in both directions, (⇐) with the continuity of the orientation (§XII.21). Theorem 12.5.7 is proved for one representative $W \leftarrow V \rightarrow W'$ of a generalized strong bundle isomorphism: (1) with homeomorphisms $|O_f| \to |O_{f'}|$ over $|X_\infty| \to |X'_\infty|$, and (2) with continuity in the sense of Definition 12.5.4; its independence of the representative and its functoriality, which the text leaves to the reader, are proved for the data of the diagrams with no further hypothesis (§XII.22).

*Narrower items, and why.* Theorems 12.3.2 (2) and 12.3.3: the pointwise reading of bump functions, the project's reading of Part I's Definition 5.3.1. Theorem 12.3.2 (1) is restated as two equivalences, one per reading. Theorem 12.5.3, Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐), Theorem 12.5.7: Part I's hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.17 and the hypothesis that sc⁺-sections pass through smooth fibre points, both inherited (G.140); Theorem 12.5.7 also by being stated for the data of one diagram rather than for Chapter 10's classes (G.192).

*Open gaps.* G.140 (Part I's hypotheses carried by §12.5) and G.192 (Theorem 12.5.7 for `SDiagram` and `GenSBMap`), with estimates in §XII.24.

**Decisions that shape the chapter.**

(1) *Part I on the object M-polyfold.* An sc-Fredholm section functor is an sc-smooth section functor that is a Part I sc-Fredholm section of the object bundle $W \to X$; an auxiliary norm is a Part I auxiliary norm invariant under $\mu$ (Definition 8.3.5, Part VIII). Every Part I theorem applies to the objects without restatement, and the chapter's work is the passage through the morphisms.

(2) *Norms are built from Part I norms, and completeness is automatic.* The local norms the text takes from a chart are Part I auxiliary norms (Proposition 5.1.3, Part V). Completeness of a glued fibre norm is not checked by hand: a Part I lemma shows that a continuous fibrewise seminorm satisfying condition (2) of an auxiliary norm is an auxiliary norm (§XII.2). This lemma is used in Theorems 12.2.2, 12.2.7, 12.2.11 and 12.2.13.

(3) *Bump functions in two readings.* Definition 12.3.1 asks for an sc-smooth function "not identically" zero; Part I's Definition 5.3.1 is read pointwise in this project (Part V). Both readings are kept for ep-groupoids and related (§XII.10); the theorems that need a function nonzero at a given point use the pointwise one.

(4) *Orientations live in chart points.* $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ are Part I's, read in a chosen chart point at $x$. A morphism $\varphi$ acts through a local strong bundle isomorphism built from the sheet of $\varphi$ (`morIso`, the inverse of the text's $\hat\Phi$), along which chart points are pulled back and compared (§XII.16). A strong bundle equivalence acts in the same way, through the local isomorphisms it is near each object (§XII.22).

(5) *Continuity of an orientation in two readings.* Part I defines continuity of an orientation section over an open set by propagation along sc-smooth paths (`IsContOrOn`); Definition 12.5.4 asks continuity of $x \mapsto (x, o_x)$ for the topology of $O_f$. The proofs of §12.5 use the first, and the two are shown to agree (§XII.20), so the statements are given in the text's form.

(6) *Theorem 12.5.7 for the data of diagrams.* A generalized strong bundle isomorphism is a class of diagrams $W \leftarrow V \rightarrow W'$ of strong bundle equivalences (Chapter 10, Part X). The theorem is proved for one representative, with the independence of the representative stated through common refinements (Chapter 10's equivalence of diagrams) and the functoriality through the shape of Chapter 10's weak fibred product.

(7) *Hypotheses of Part I are inherited, not added.* Where §12.5 rests on Part I's Theorem 6.6.17, it carries that theorem's hypotheses; they are listed once, in §XII.23, with witnesses.

**Notation.** Throughout, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ is a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid $X$ with source and target maps $s$, $t$; $B$ is the underlying Part I strong bundle on objects, $W_{0,1}$ its level-$(0,1)$ part, $\pi : X \to |X|$ the orbit map, $G_x$ the isotropy group, and a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ is the one of Theorem 7.1.13 ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · theorem_7_1_13⟧: a group homomorphism $\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U(x))$ and a map $\Gamma : G_x \times U(x) \to \mathbf X$ with $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$, $t(\Gamma(g, y)) = \Phi(g)(y)$, such that every morphism between points of $U(x)$ is $\Gamma(g, y)$ for exactly one $g$. The saturation of a set $A$ of objects is the set of objects joined by a morphism to a point of $A$; $A$ is saturated if it equals its saturation. $\partial X$ is the set of objects of degeneracy index at least $1$; it is saturated, since morphisms are local sc-diffeomorphisms and keep the degeneracy index.

### XII.1 Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1) and the remark after it

**Definition 12.1.1** (same) ⟦Chapter12/CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_1_1⟧, p. 569. Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid. An sc-smooth section functor $f$ (an sc-smooth section of the object bundle with $f(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, f(s(\varphi)))$ for every morphism $\varphi$) is *sc-Fredholm* when it is an sc-Fredholm section of the object bundle in Part I's sense (Definition 3.4.17 as read in Part III): regularizing, and with an sc-Fredholm germ at every smooth point. The Lean declaration is the definition unfolded: it states that the project's predicate `IsScFredholmSectionFunctor` is the conjunction of the section functor property and Part I's sc-Fredholm property for the bundle $B$. Nothing is added; the text's phrase "for the strong bundle $W \to X$" is the object bundle, since the morphisms carry no further bundle.

**The remark after Definition 12.1.1** (explicit), p. 569. The text observes, without proof, that the regularizing property holds on objects and on morphisms, and that the germs are sc-Fredholm. Each is a separate statement.

*On objects* ⟦Chapter12/CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_obj⟧. If $x \in X_m$ and $f(x) \in W_{m,m+1}$, then $x \in X_{m+1}$. This is Part I's regularizing property of $f$ on the object bundle, read off the definition.

*On morphisms* ⟦Chapter12/CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_mor⟧. The text writes $f(\varphi)$ for a morphism $\varphi$. A section functor gives no vector over a morphism directly; the formal statement reads $f(\varphi)$ as the section $\varphi \mapsto (\varphi, f(s(\varphi)))$ of the pull-back bundle $\mathbf X\,{}_s\!\times_P W \to \mathbf X$, the bundle over the morphism space whose fibre over $\varphi$ is $W_{s(\varphi)}$. The statement: if $\varphi \in \mathbf X_m$ and $f(\varphi)$ lies on level $(m, m+1)$ of the pull-back bundle, then $\varphi \in \mathbf X_{m+1}$. *Step 1.* The projection of the pull-back bundle to $W$ is a strong bundle map, so it keeps the bi-levels; $f(s(\varphi))$ lies in $W_{m,m+1}$. *Step 2.* By the regularizing property on objects, $s(\varphi) \in X_{m+1}$. *Step 3.* The levels of the morphism M-polyfold are those of the sources, since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism; so $\varphi \in \mathbf X_{m+1}$.

*Germs* ⟦Chapter12/CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_germ⟧. At a smooth object $x$, the germ of $f$ at $x$ is an sc-Fredholm germ. This is the second clause of Part I's definition, read at $x$.

No hypothesis is added. The definition has a witness in every Part I sc-Fredholm section of a trivial ep-groupoid (an M-polyfold with only identity morphisms), where the functor property is empty.

### XII.2 Definition 12.2.1 (2017: 12.2): auxiliary norms, and completeness for free

**Definition 12.2.1** (same) ⟦Chapter8/Book2021 · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm⟧, p. 570. The text recalls Definition 8.3.5, and the formalization uses that declaration unchanged: an auxiliary norm is a Part I auxiliary norm $N : W_{0,1} \to [0, \infty)$ of the object bundle (Definition 5.1.1, Part V: continuous, a complete norm on each fibre, and condition (2): if $P(h_k) \to x$ in $X$ and $N(h_k) \to 0$, then $h_k \to 0_x$ in $W_{0,1}$) with $N(\mu(\varphi, k)) = N(k)$ for every morphism $\varphi$ and every $k \in W_{0,1}$ over $s(\varphi)$. In the project $N$ is a function on all of $W$, and "$N(k) \le C$" is Part I's relation, which fails off $W_{0,1}$ (equivalently, $N = \infty$ there).

**Completeness is automatic** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_of_tendsto⟧. The text asserts, of each glued norm it builds, that it is complete on the fibres. The formal proof replaces these assertions by one lemma about Part I's Definition 5.1.1. Call $N : W \to [0, \infty)$ a *fibre seminorm* if its restriction to each fibre $W_{0,1}|_x$ is a seminorm ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.IsFiberSeminorm⟧, and say it satisfies *condition (2)* if $P(h_k) \to x$, $N(h_k) \to 0$ imply $h_k \to 0_x$ in $W_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.TendstoZeroOne⟧. The lemma: a continuous fibre seminorm on $W_{0,1}$ satisfying condition (2) is an auxiliary norm.

*Proof.* Fix $x$ and a strong bundle chart $\Phi$ around $x$ with fibre $F$, and write $|w|_1 = \|\mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w)\|_{F_1}$ for $w$ over points near $x$; on each fibre this is a complete norm, because $\Phi[1]$ is a linear isomorphism of the fibre onto a closed subspace (the image of the fibre projection $A(u)$) of $F_1$.

*Step 1, an upper bound.* By continuity of $N$ at $0_x$ there is $\delta > 0$ and a neighbourhood $O$ of $x$ with $N(w) \le 1$ when $P(w) \in O$ and $|w|_1 \le \delta$. By homogeneity, $N(w) \le \delta^{-1}|w|_1$ for $P(w) \in O$. (In Lean: `StrongBundle.exists_le_mul_norm_liftOne`.)

*Step 2, a lower bound* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.exists_norm_liftOne_le_of_tendsto⟧. Suppose no $c > 0$ and neighbourhood of $x$ satisfy $|w|_1 \le c\,N(w)$. Then there are $w_k$ over points $P(w_k) \to x$ with $|w_k|_1 > k\,N(w_k)$; rescale so that $|w_k|_1 = 1$. Then $N(w_k) < 1/k \to 0$, and condition (2) gives $w_k \to 0_x$ in $W_{0,1}$, hence $|w_k|_1 \to 0$ by continuity of the chart on level $1$, against $|w_k|_1 = 1$.

*Step 3, positivity and completeness.* By Step 2, $N(w) = 0$ forces $|w|_1 = 0$, so $N$ is a norm on each fibre. By Steps 1 and 2 it is equivalent on each fibre near $x$ to the complete norm $|\cdot|_1$, hence complete (`complete_of_bounds`). The other two clauses of Definition 5.1.1, continuity and condition (2), are hypotheses. $\square$

The same lemma in local form: a *local auxiliary norm* on an open $U$ asks continuity on $W_{0,1}|U$, the seminorm property over $U$ and condition (2) for limits $x \in U$ only ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.IsLocalAuxNorm⟧. The local norms of all constructions below are local auxiliary norms, and the glued norms are proved to be auxiliary norms by the lemma. The step is a strengthening of Part I's toolkit: it applies equally to Part I's Proposition 5.1.3, though Part I proves that proposition directly.

### XII.3 Theorem 12.2.2 (2017: 12.1): auxiliary norms exist

**Theorem 12.2.2** (same) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_2⟧, p. 570: every strong bundle $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space $|X|$ admits an auxiliary norm. The same for a bundled object of the category $\mathcal{SEP}$ of strong bundles over ep-groupoids ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · SEP.theorem_12_2_2⟧, a one-line wrapper. The hypotheses are the text's; the conclusion is Definition 12.2.1 in full.

The proof follows the text's three steps, average, transport, glue; the formal construction is a chain of definitions in `AuxNormEp`, each with its lemma.

**Step 0: the lifted action on $W_{0,1}$.** The strong bundle action $\mu$ is defined on the pull-back $\mathbf X\,{}_s\!\times_P W$. For a function $\alpha$ from objects to morphisms with $s(\alpha(y)) = y$, define $\alpha * w = \mu(\alpha(P(w)), w)$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actOne⟧. When $\alpha$ is sc-smooth on an open set, $\alpha *$ is an sc-smooth map of $W[1]$ there, so it preserves $W_{0,1}$ and is continuous on it. Along a natural representation, $g * w = \mu(\Gamma(g, P(w)), w)$ is a group action of $G_x$ on $W|U(x)$: $1 * w = w$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actOne_Γ_one⟧ because $\Gamma(1, y) = 1_y$, and $(gh) * w = g * (h * w)$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actOne_Γ_mul⟧ because $\Gamma(gh, y) = \Gamma(g, \Phi(h)y) \circ \Gamma(h, y)$ by the uniqueness clause of Theorem 7.1.13 and $\mu$ respects composition. Restricted to one fibre, $g *$ is the linear map $\mu(\Gamma(g, y), \cdot) : W_y \to W_{\Phi(g)y}$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actFiber⟧.

**Step 1: average.** Fix $x$, a natural representation on $U(x)$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $U(x)$. Put
$$\bar M(w) = \frac{1}{|G_x|}\sum_{g \in G_x}M(g * w)$$
⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.avgNorm⟧. *Invariance* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.avgNorm_actOne⟧: $\bar M(h * w) = \bar M(w)$, by reindexing the sum through $g \mapsto gh$ and Step 0. *A local auxiliary norm* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_avgNorm⟧. Continuity: each term $M \circ (g *)$ is continuous, as a composite of continuous maps over $U(x)$, and $\Phi(g)$ maps $U(x)$ into itself. Seminorm: each term is a seminorm composed with a linear fibre map. Condition (2): if $P(w_k) \to y \in U(x)$ and $\bar M(w_k) \to 0$, then the term with $g = 1$ satisfies $M(w_k) \le |G_x|\,\bar M(w_k) \to 0$, since all terms are nonnegative, and condition (2) for $M$ gives $w_k \to 0_y$.

**Step 2: transport to the saturation.** Let $S = \mathrm{sat}(U(x))$ be the set of objects $y$ admitting a morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = y$ and $t(\varphi) \in U(x)$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.satSet⟧. Choose one such morphism $\varphi_y$ for every $y \in S$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.selMor⟧ (a choice function; no regularity is asked) and put
$$T(w) = \bar M(\mu(\varphi_{P(w)}, w)) \text{ for } P(w) \in S, \qquad T(w) = 0 \text{ otherwise}$$
⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm⟧.

*Independence of the choice* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm_eq_of⟧. If $\psi$ is another morphism from $y$ into $U(x)$, then $\psi \circ \varphi_y^{-1}$ is a morphism between points of $U(x)$, hence equals $\Gamma(g, t(\varphi_y))$ for a unique $g \in G_x$; so $\mu(\psi, w) = g * \mu(\varphi_y, w)$ and $\bar M(\mu(\psi, w)) = \bar M(\mu(\varphi_y, w))$ by invariance. At this point the text invokes the good neighbourhood property (5) of Theorem 12.2.6; the invariance of $\bar M$ makes it unnecessary, because what has to be compared are two morphisms into $U(x)$, and any two differ by an element of $G_x$.

*Continuity* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.continuousOn_transNorm⟧. Fix $w_0$ over $y_0 \in S$ and its chosen morphism $\varphi_0$. Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, there is a local inverse $\rho$ of $s$ on a neighbourhood $O$ of $y_0$ with $\rho(y_0) = \varphi_0$ (`X.isLocalScDiffeo_src`); shrinking $O$, $t(\rho(y)) \in U(x)$ for $y \in O$, so $O \subset S$. For $w$ over $O$, $\rho(P(w))$ is a morphism from $P(w)$ into $U(x)$, so by independence of the choice $T(w) = \bar M(\rho * w)$ near $w_0$, and this is continuous by Step 0.

*Condition (2)* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.tendsto_transNorm⟧. Let $P(w_k) \to y_0 \in S$ and $T(w_k) \to 0$. With $\rho$ as above, $v_k = \rho * w_k$ lies over $t(\rho(P(w_k))) \to t(\varphi_0) \in U(x)$ and $\bar M(v_k) = T(w_k) \to 0$ eventually; condition (2) for $\bar M$ gives $v_k \to 0$. To bring this back, let $\tau$ be a local inverse of $t$ near $\varphi_0$, and $\alpha' = \mathrm{inv} \circ \tau$, an sc-smooth local section of $s$ near $t(\varphi_0)$; then $w_k = \alpha' * v_k$ eventually, by `μ_inv_μ` and the identity $\tau(t(\rho(y))) = \rho(y)$, and $\alpha' *$ is continuous with $\alpha' * 0 = 0$. So $w_k \to 0_{y_0}$.

*Seminorm* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isFiberSeminorm_transNorm⟧: on the fibre over $y \in S$, $T$ is the seminorm $\bar M$ composed with the linear map $\mu(\varphi_y, \cdot)$; off $S$ it is $0$. So $T$ is a local auxiliary norm on $S$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_transNorm⟧, and it is *invariant under every morphism* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm_μ⟧: for $\psi : y \to y'$, $y \in S$ iff $y' \in S$, and $\varphi_{y'} \circ \psi$ is a morphism from $y$ into $U(x)$, so $T(\mu(\psi, w)) = \bar M(\mu(\varphi_{y'} \circ \psi, w)) = T(w)$ by independence of the choice.

**Step 3: glue.** *Partitions of unity of $X$* (Definition 12.2.3, §XII.4) are pulled back from $|X|$. For each object $x$ the set $\pi(S_x)$, $S_x = \mathrm{sat}(U(x))$, is open in $|X|$ because $\pi$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8), and these sets cover $|X|$. Since $|X|$ is paracompact and Hausdorff, there is a partition of unity $(\beta_i)_{i \in I}$ of $|X|$ subordinate to a subcover $(\pi(S_{x_i}))$. Put
$$N(w) = \sum_{i \in I}\beta_i(\pi(P(w)))\,T_i(w)$$
⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.glueNorm⟧, a locally finite sum. A term vanishes where $\pi(P(w)) \notin \operatorname{supp}\beta_i$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.partition_eq_zero_of_not_mem⟧ and all terms are nonnegative ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.glue_term_nonneg⟧.

*$N$ is an auxiliary norm* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isAuxNorm_glueNorm⟧. By the lemma of §XII.2 three things must be checked, and invariance.

- *Continuity.* Near any $w_0$, only finitely many $\beta_i \circ \pi \circ P$ are nonzero (local finiteness, pulled back through the continuous $\pi \circ P$), so $N$ is a finite sum there (`continuous_finsum`). Each term is continuous: where $\pi(P(w)) \in \operatorname{supp}\beta_i \subset \pi(S_{x_i})$, $P(w)$ lies in the open saturated $S_{x_i}$, on which $T_i$ is continuous; outside the closed set $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\beta_i)$ the term is identically $0$ nearby.
- *Seminorm.* A nonnegative combination of seminorms on each fibre.
- *Condition (2).* Let $P(w_k) \to y$ and $N(w_k) \to 0$. Choose $i$ with $\beta_i(\pi(y)) > 0$. Then $\beta_i(\pi(P(w_k))) \ge \beta_i(\pi(y))/2$ eventually, so $T_i(w_k) \le 2N(w_k)/\beta_i(\pi(y)) \to 0$, the term being squeezed below the sum by nonnegativity. Since $\pi(y) \in \operatorname{supp}\beta_i \subset \pi(S_{x_i})$, $y \in S_{x_i}$, and condition (2) for $T_i$ gives $w_k \to 0_y$.
- *Invariance.* $\beta_i \circ \pi$ is constant along morphisms (`π_src_eq_π_tgt`), and each $T_i$ is invariant.

*The ingredients* are all prior results. The local norms $M_i$ are the restrictions to $U(x_i)$ of one Part I auxiliary norm of the object bundle ⟦Chapter5/AuxNorm · proposition_5_1_3_exists⟧, which Part I provides on the object M-polyfold. The natural representations come from Theorem 7.1.13 at every object, with $U(x)$ inside $X$. The partition of unity exists because $|X|$ is paracompact (the hypothesis) and Hausdorff (Proposition 7.1.8; `PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`); Theorem 7.3.1 ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · theorem_7_3_1_metrizable⟧ supplies the regularity that the subordinate partition needs. $\square$

*Where the formal proof departs from the text.* (a) The text takes the local norm in a strong bundle chart as $\|\mathrm{pr}_2\Psi(\cdot)\|_{F_1}$; a Part I auxiliary norm restricted to $U(x)$ serves equally and comes with condition (2). (b) Completeness of $\bar M$, $T$ and $N$ is not checked separately; the lemma of §XII.2 gives it. (c) Property (5) of Theorem 12.2.6 is not used; invariance under $G_x$ replaces it. (d) The text's "$N$ is continuous since the sum is locally finite" needs that each term is continuous where its coefficient is nonzero, which is the continuity of $T_i$ on the open saturation; this is proved through local inverses of $s$.

### XII.4 Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4 (2017: 12.3, 12.4) and Proposition 12.2.5 (2017: 12.1): partitions of unity

**Definition 12.2.3** (same) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity⟧, p. 570. A continuous partition of unity of the ep-groupoid $X$, indexed by $\Lambda$, is a family of continuous functions $\beta_\lambda : X \to [0, 1]$ on the objects with (1) $\beta_\lambda(s(\varphi)) = \beta_\lambda(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$; (2) local finiteness through saturated sets: every object has a saturated open neighbourhood meeting the supports of only finitely many $\beta_\lambda$; (3) $\sum_\lambda\beta_\lambda = 1$. Supports are closures in $X$. The text's preamble has $|X|$ paracompact; the definition does not use it, and it is not a field, but a hypothesis of Proposition 12.2.5.

**The remark after Definition 12.2.3** (same), p. 570, has two directions.

*From $|X|$ to $X$* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.isContPartitionOfUnity_comp_π⟧. If $(\hat\beta_\lambda)$ is a continuous partition of unity of $|X|$, then $\beta_\lambda = \hat\beta_\lambda \circ \pi$ is one of $X$. (1) holds because $\pi(s(\varphi)) = \pi(t(\varphi))$. Continuity: $\pi$ is continuous. (2): a point $\pi(x)$ has an open $O$ meeting finitely many $\operatorname{supp}\hat\beta_\lambda$; $\pi^{-1}(O)$ is open and saturated, and $\operatorname{supp}(\hat\beta_\lambda \circ \pi) \subset \pi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\hat\beta_\lambda)$, so it meets finitely many supports. (3) is pointwise.

*From $X$ to $|X|$* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.descend⟧. A continuous partition of unity of $X$ descends: by (1) each $\beta_\lambda$ is constant on orbits, so $\beta_\lambda = \hat\beta_\lambda \circ \pi$ for a unique $\hat\beta_\lambda$ on $|X|$. Continuity of $\hat\beta_\lambda$ holds because $\pi$ is an open surjection, hence a quotient map. Local finiteness on $|X|$: for a saturated open $U$ meeting finitely many supports, $\pi(U)$ is open, by openness of $\pi$ (Proposition 7.1.8), and $\pi(U)$ meets $\operatorname{supp}\hat\beta_\lambda$ only if $U$ meets $\operatorname{supp}\beta_\lambda$; for the latter, a point of $\pi(U) \cap \{\hat\beta_\lambda \ne 0\}$ lifts into $U$ because $U$ is saturated, and $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}\{\hat\beta_\lambda \neq 0\}) = \operatorname{cl}\pi^{-1}\{\hat\beta_\lambda \neq 0\}$ for the open map $\pi$.

**Definition 12.2.4** (same) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.IsSubordinate⟧, p. 571. For a family $(U_\lambda)$ of saturated open sets covering $X$, a continuous partition of unity $(\beta_\lambda)$ is subordinate if $\operatorname{supp}\beta_\lambda \subset U_\lambda$ for every $\lambda$, the supports taken in $X$.

**Proposition 12.2.5** (same) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.proposition_12_2_5⟧, p. 571. If $|X|$ is paracompact, every cover $(U_\lambda)$ of $X$ by saturated open sets has a subordinate continuous partition of unity, indexed by the same $\Lambda$.

*Proof*, the text's. *Step 1.* The sets $\pi(U_\lambda)$ are open in $|X|$ because $\pi$ is open, and cover $|X|$ because $\pi$ is surjective. *Step 2.* $|X|$ is Hausdorff (Proposition 7.1.8) and paracompact, hence normal, and admits a partition of unity $(\hat\beta_\lambda)$ subordinate to $(\pi(U_\lambda))$, with the same index set (`PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate`). *Step 3.* By the first direction of the remark, $\beta_\lambda = \hat\beta_\lambda \circ \pi$ is a continuous partition of unity of $X$. *Step 4, subordination* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.isSubordinate_comp_π⟧: $\operatorname{supp}\beta_\lambda \subset \pi^{-1}(\operatorname{supp}\hat\beta_\lambda) \subset \pi^{-1}(\pi(U_\lambda)) = U_\lambda$, the last equality because $U_\lambda$ is saturated, and the first because $\pi^{-1}$ of a closed set is closed and contains $\{\beta_\lambda \ne 0\}$. $\square$

No hypothesis is added, and nothing in the text's argument is replaced. The construction of §XII.3 uses Proposition 12.2.5 in the form of Steps 1–4 directly, with $U_\lambda$ the saturations $\mathrm{sat}(U(x))$.

### XII.5 Theorem 12.2.6 (2017: 12.2): good neighbourhoods

**Theorem 12.2.6** (same) ⟦Chapter12/GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_2_6⟧, pp. 571–572. Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid and $x$ an object. There are open sets $U'(x) \subset U''(x)$ containing $x$ and a natural representation $R$ of $G_x$ with domain $U''(x)$ such that:

1. $\overline{U'(x)} \subset U''(x)$;
2. $U'(x)$ is invariant under the natural representation: $\Phi(g)(U'(x)) = U'(x)$ for all $g \in G_x$;
3. $U''(x)$ lies in the base of one strong bundle chart of the atlas, which restricted to $P^{-1}(U''(x))$ is a strong bundle isomorphism onto a local model;
4. for every sequence of morphisms $\varphi_k$ with $s(\varphi_k) \in \overline{U''(x)}$ and $t(\varphi_k) \to z$, a subsequence converges to a morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \overline{U''(x)}$ and $t(\varphi) = z$;
5. $(\pi^{-1}(\pi(U'(x))) \setminus U'(x)) \cap \overline{U''(x)} = \emptyset$: a point of $\overline{U''(x)}$ in the saturation of $U'(x)$ lies in $U'(x)$.

The text proves the theorem by pointing to Chapter 7; the formal proof assembles it in four steps.

*Step 1, properness.* Since $X$ is an ep-groupoid, $x$ has an open neighbourhood $V_0$ such that $t : s^{-1}(\overline{V_0}) \to X$ is proper (`X.exists_isProperMap`, the properness clause of the definition of an ep-groupoid). A strong bundle chart $c$ of the atlas contains $x$ in its base. Theorem 7.1.13 gives a natural representation $R_0$ of $G_x$ on a domain inside $V_0 \cap \operatorname{dom}c$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · theorem_7_1_13⟧.

*Step 2, two shrinkings.* Choose a closed neighbourhood $t_1$ of $x$ inside $R_0.U$, and shrink the natural representation to an invariant domain inside the interior of $t_1$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · exists_naturalRep_shrink⟧; this is $R_1$, with domain $U''(x) = R_1.U$ and $\overline{R_1.U} \subset t_1 \subset R_0.U$. Repeat with $R_1$ in place of $R_0$ to get $R_2$ with $\overline{R_2.U} \subset R_1.U$, and put $U'(x) = R_2.U$. The shrinking lemma keeps the group homomorphism $\Phi$ (restricted), so $\Phi_2(g) = \Phi_1(g)|U'$ and (1) holds. *(2).* $U'(x)$ is the domain of the natural representation $R_2$, which is invariant under its own $\Phi$; the image of the domain under $\Phi(g)$ is the domain ⟦Chapter12/GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.image_Φ_eq⟧, because $\Phi(g)$ maps the domain into itself and so does $\Phi(g^{-1}) = \Phi(g)^{-1}$. *(3).* $U''(x) \subset R_0.U \subset \operatorname{dom}c$; the chart is a member of the atlas, so its restriction is a strong bundle isomorphism onto its local model.

*Step 3, (4)* ⟦Chapter12/GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.exists_subseq_of_isProperMap⟧. The general lemma: if $t : s^{-1}(\overline{V_0}) \to X$ is proper, $A \subset \overline{V_0}$ is closed, $s(\varphi_k) \in A$ and $t(\varphi_k) \to z$, then some subsequence $\varphi_{\sigma(k)}$ converges to a $\psi$ with $s(\psi) \in A$, $t(\psi) = z$. *Proof.* $K = \{z\} \cup \{t(\varphi_k)\}$ is compact, as a convergent sequence with its limit; its preimage under the proper map is compact and contains every $\varphi_k$. The morphism space is metrizable, so compact sets are sequentially compact, and a subsequence converges to some $\psi$ in the preimage. Continuity of $s$ and closedness of $A$ give $s(\psi) \in A$; continuity of $t$ and uniqueness of limits give $t(\psi) = z$. Applied with $A = \overline{U''(x)} \subset \overline{V_0}$, this is (4).

*Step 4, (5).* Let $y \in \overline{U''(x)}$ with $\pi(y) = \pi(z)$ for some $z \in U'(x)$. There is a morphism $\varphi : z \to y$. Both $z \in U'(x) \subset R_0.U$ and $y \in \overline{U''(x)} \subset R_0.U$, so by the uniqueness clause of Theorem 7.1.13, $\varphi = \Gamma(g, z)$ for a unique $g \in G_x$, and $y = t(\varphi) = \Phi(g)(z)$. By (2), $\Phi(g)(z) \in U'(x)$. So $y \in U'(x)$. $\square$

The first shrinking serves (5): it puts $\overline{U''(x)}$ inside the domain $R_0.U$ of a natural representation, on which every morphism is a $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$. No hypothesis is added. Property (5) is not used in the construction of §XII.3 (§XII.3, Step 2); Theorem 12.2.6 is used through (3) and (4) in the compactness arguments of §§XII.14–XII.15 and in later chapters.

### XII.6 Theorem 12.2.7 (2017: 12.3): extension of auxiliary norms from the boundary

**Theorem 12.2.7** (same) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7⟧, pp. 574–575. Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid $X$ with paracompact $|X|$, and $N$ an auxiliary norm of $W_{0,1}|\partial X$ (Definition 12.2.1 over $\partial X$). Then there is an auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. The hypotheses are the text's.

**Auxiliary norms over a subset.** For a set $A$ of objects, *an auxiliary norm over $A$* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNormOn⟧ is a function $N$ on $W_{0,1}$ that is continuous on $W_{0,1}|A$, a complete norm on each fibre over $A$, satisfies condition (2) for sequences $w_k$ over $A$ whose base points converge to a point of $A$, and is invariant where defined: $N(\mu(\varphi, k)) = N(k)$ when $P(k) = s(\varphi) \in A$. The text's $N$ is a function on $W_{0,1}|\partial X$; a function on all of $W_{0,1}$ with conditions over $\partial X$ only is the same datum, its values off $\partial X$ being irrelevant. A global auxiliary norm restricts to one over any $A$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.isAuxNormOn⟧. Morphisms preserve $\partial X$ in both directions: $t(\varphi) \in \partial X$ iff $s(\varphi) \in \partial X$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpGroupoid.tgt_mem_boundary_iff⟧, because $t \circ (s|_{\text{sheet}})^{-1}$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism and keeps the degeneracy index; so $X \setminus \partial X$ is open ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpGroupoid.isOpen_compl_boundary⟧ (the degeneracy index is upper semicontinuous) and saturated.

The proof has two parts: a global part, the construction of §XII.3 with local extensions near the boundary as input, and a local step that constructs those local extensions.

#### The global part

*The local extensions* ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasLocalExtensions⟧: say $N$ *has local extensions* if every $x \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$ (§XII.2) with $M = N$ on $W_{0,1}|(V \cap \partial X)$.

**The global part** ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp⟧: if $|X|$ is paracompact and $N$ is an auxiliary norm over $\partial X$ with local extensions, then there is an auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. Tameness is not used here.

*Step 1, data at each point.* For every object $x$ choose a natural representation $R_x$ and a local auxiliary norm $M_x$ on its domain:
- if $x \in \partial X$: the local extension $M$ on $V \ni x$, and $R_x$ from Theorem 7.1.13 with domain inside $V$; $M_x = M$ restricted ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · StrongBundle.IsLocalAuxNorm.mono⟧, still equal to $N$ over $R_x.U \cap \partial X$;
- if $x \notin \partial X$: $R_x$ with domain inside the open set $X \setminus \partial X$, and $M_x = N_0$, the restriction of a fixed Part I auxiliary norm $N_0$ of the object bundle (Proposition 5.1.3).

*Step 2, average and transport,* as in §XII.3: $\bar M_x$ is $G_x$-invariant on $R_x.U$, and $T_x = \mathrm{transNorm}(R_x, \bar M_x)$ is a local auxiliary norm on $S_x = \mathrm{sat}(R_x.U)$, invariant under morphisms.

*Step 3, glue.* A partition of unity $(\beta_x)$ of $|X|$ subordinate to $(\pi(S_x))_x$, which cover $|X|$ (every $\pi(y)$ lies in $\pi(S_y)$), and $\tilde N = \sum_x(\beta_x \circ \pi \circ P)\,T_x$. By §XII.3, $\tilde N$ is an auxiliary norm of $W$.

*Step 4, $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$.* Fix $w$ over $y \in \partial X$. The claim is that every term is $\beta_x(\pi(y))\,N(w)$; then $\tilde N(w) = (\sum_x\beta_x(\pi(y)))N(w) = N(w)$. If $\beta_x(\pi(y)) = 0$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise $\pi(y) \in \operatorname{supp}\beta_x \subset \pi(S_x)$, so $y \in S_x$ ($S_x$ is saturated), and there is a morphism $\varphi : y \to y'$ with $y' \in R_x.U$.
- *$x$ is a boundary point.* Otherwise $R_x.U \subset X \setminus \partial X$, but $y' = t(\varphi) \in \partial X$ because $y \in \partial X$; contradiction.
- *The transported vector.* $T_x(w) = \bar M_x(v)$ with $v = \mu(\varphi_y, w)$ for the selected morphism $\varphi_y$; $v$ lies over a point of $R_x.U \cap \partial X$, and $N(v) = N(w)$ by the invariance of $N$ over $\partial X$.
- *Each term of the average is $N(w)$.* For $g \in G_x$, $g * v$ lies over $\Phi(g)(P(v)) \in R_x.U$, again in $\partial X$; there $M_x = N$, so $M_x(g * v) = N(g * v) = N(v) = N(w)$, by invariance of $N$ under the morphism $\Gamma(g, P(v))$.
- *The average of constants.* $\bar M_x(v) = |G_x|^{-1}\cdot|G_x|\cdot N(w) = N(w)$; $G_x$ is finite and nonempty.

So $\beta_x(\pi(y))T_x(w) = \beta_x(\pi(y))N(w)$ for every $x$, and $\tilde N(w) = N(w)$. $\square$

The text's argument for Step 4 is the same in substance: its local norms near boundary points restrict to $N$, and its interior pieces are supported away from $\partial X$. The formal proof records why interior pieces do not reach $\partial X$: their saturations miss $\partial X$ because $\partial X$ is saturated.

*A property of this Lean statement.* The global part takes the local extensions as the hypothesis `HasLocalExtensions`; it is valid as stated and serves as the global half of Theorem 12.2.7, the hypothesis being discharged below for every tame $X$. Its own satisfiability witness ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness⟧: over every ep-groupoid with paracompact $|X|$ some $N$ satisfies both hypotheses, the restriction of a norm of Theorem 12.2.2, since a global auxiliary norm has itself as local extension ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasLocalExtensions_of_isAuxNorm⟧. This witness is a consistency check only: in it the extension problem is solved by the global norm itself.

#### The local step

The local step is a statement about one strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold, the object bundle; it does not see the morphisms. The text takes a tame local strong bundle model $K = R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$ at a boundary point, the tame retraction $r$ of its base, and defines on $K|O$ a norm by the formula $N(rq(u), A(rq(u))w) + \|w - A(rq(u))w\|_{F_1}$, with $q$ a shift onto the boundary. The formal proof splits this into a retraction onto the boundary, which lives in a tame chart of the base, and a norm formula, which can be evaluated in any strong bundle chart.

**The retraction onto the boundary** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · MPolyfold.exists_retraction_boundary⟧. Let $X$ be a tame M-polyfold and $x_0 \in \partial X$. There are an open $V \ni x_0$ and a map $\rho : X \to X$, continuous on $V$, with $\rho(V) \subset \partial X$ and $\rho(y) = y$ for $y \in V \cap \partial X$.

*The coordinates.* Let $C$ be a partial quadrant with a presentation $T : C \cong [0, \infty)^n \oplus H$ (a linear isomorphism of the ambient space carrying $C$ onto the standard partial quadrant), and write points as $(t, h)$, $t \in [0, \infty)^n$. Define
$$\tau(t, h) = \min(t_1, \dots, t_n), \qquad q(t, h) = (t, h) - \tau(t, h)\,(1, \dots, 1, 0)$$
⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · minCoord⟧ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · boundaryShift⟧, read through $T$, for $n \ge 1$. The properties:
- $\tau$ and $q$ are continuous ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · continuous_minCoord⟧ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · continuous_boundaryShift⟧, as a minimum of finitely many coordinates and an affine expression in it;
- the coordinates of $q$ are $t_i - \tau$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · coord_boundaryShift⟧, and $\tau \le t_i$ for all $i$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · minCoord_le⟧, so $q$ takes values in $C$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · mem_quadrant_boundaryShift⟧;
- the minimum is attained at some $i$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · exists_coord_eq_minCoord⟧, where the coordinate of $q$ is $0$, so $q$ takes values in $\partial C$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · exists_coord_boundaryShift_eq_zero⟧;
- if some $t_i = 0$, the minimum is $0$ and $q$ is the identity ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · boundaryShift_eq_self⟧.

A point of $C$ has degeneracy index at least $1$ iff some half-line coordinate vanishes ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · one_le_degIndexWith_iff⟧.

*The retraction.* By tameness, $x_0$ lies in a tame chart $\psi$ (`IsTame.exists_chart`) whose model is a tame retract $O = r(U)$, $U \subset C$ relatively open, $r$ a tame sc-smooth retraction. Choose a presentation $T$ of $C$. *(a) The degeneracy index is read in the chart.* Because $r$ is tame, the degeneracy index of $X$ at $z \in \operatorname{dom}\psi$ equals that of $C$ at $\psi(z)$ (`degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith`). So $z \in \partial X$ iff some coordinate $t_i$ of $T\psi(z)$ vanishes. *(b) $n \ge 1$*: $x_0 \in \partial X$ forces a vanishing coordinate. *(c) The domain.* $U = V_0 \cap C$ for an open $V_0$ of the ambient space; put $V = \operatorname{dom}\psi \cap \psi^{-1}(q^{-1}(V_0))$, open by continuity of $\psi$ and $q$. It contains $x_0$: $q(\psi(x_0)) = \psi(x_0) \in O \subset U \subset V_0$ by (a) and the last property of $q$. *(d) The map.* $\rho = \psi^{-1} \circ r \circ q \circ \psi$ on $V$. For $y \in V$, $q(\psi(y)) \in V_0 \cap C = U$, so $r$ applies and $r(q(\psi(y))) \in O$, the image of the chart. *(e) Continuity* on $V$: a composite of continuous maps, $r$ being continuous on level $0$ since it is sc-smooth. *(f) Values in $\partial X$.* Tameness of $r$ means $r$ keeps the degeneracy index: $d_C(r(p)) = d_C(p)$ for $p \in U$ (`degIndex_apply`); $q(\psi(y)) \in \partial C$, so $r(q(\psi(y))) \in \partial C$, and by (a) $\rho(y) \in \partial X$. *(g) The identity on $V \cap \partial X$.* For $y \in V \cap \partial X$, $q(\psi(y)) = \psi(y)$ by (a) and the last property of $q$; $\psi(y) \in O$ and $r$ is the identity on its image (`apply_eq_self_of_mem_retract`); so $\rho(y) = y$. $\square$

The text takes $x_0 = (0, h_0)$ in the chart. This is not needed: $q$ maps into $\partial C$ and fixes $\partial C$ whatever the coordinates of $x_0$.

**The norm $N'$** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm⟧. Fix a strong bundle chart $c$ of the atlas, with base chart $\varphi$, model $K = R(U \triangleleft F)$, and its level-$1$ form $\Phi[1] : W_{0,1}|\operatorname{dom}\varphi \to (U \triangleleft F)[1]$. The fibre part of the retraction $R$ of the chart at a base point $u$ is a map $A(u) : F_1 \to F_1$, $h \mapsto \mathrm{pr}_2R(u, h)$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.chartFibMap⟧. Its properties:
- $A(u)$ is linear in $h$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isLinearMap_chartFibMap⟧, since $R$ is a strong bundle retraction, linear on fibres;
- for $u \in O$, $(u, A(u)h) \in K[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.mem_K_chartFibMap⟧ and $A(u)h = h$ when $(u, h) \in K[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.chartFibMap_of_mem⟧, since $R$ is a retraction onto $K$; points of $O$ lie in $U$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.mem_U_of_mem_O⟧;
- $A(u)h$ is the fibre part of the shifted retraction $R[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.shiftFiber_eq_chartFibMap⟧, and $(u, h) \mapsto R[1](u, h)$ is continuous on $U \oplus F_1$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.continuousOn_shiftFiber_R⟧, as level $0$ of the sc-smooth map $R : (U \triangleleft F)[1] \to (U \triangleleft F)[1]$.

The chart $\Phi[1]$ reads $W_{0,1}$ over the chart domain: projections commute with it ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.proj_oneChartOf_symm⟧ and it agrees with the level-$1$ lift of the chart ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.oneChartOf_toOne⟧. For a vector $w$ over $y$ with chart coordinates $(u, h) = \Phi[1](w)$ and a map $\rho$ with $\rho(y)$ in the chart domain, the *transport* of $w$ to the fibre over $\rho(y)$ is
$$\Phi[1]^{-1}\big(\varphi(\rho(y)),\ A(\varphi(\rho(y)))h\big),$$
a linear map of fibres $W_y \to W_{\rho(y)}$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractTransport⟧, compatible with the level-$1$ lift ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.liftOneFiber_retractTransport⟧. Then
$$N'(w) = N(\text{transport of } w) + \|h - A(\varphi(\rho(y)))h\|_{F_1},$$
the text's formula read in $\Phi[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm_toOne⟧. It is a fibre seminorm over each $y$ in the chart domain with $\rho(y)$ in the chart domain and $N$ a seminorm over $\rho(y)$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isFiberSeminorm_retractNorm⟧: the first term is a seminorm composed with a linear map, the second the norm of a linear expression in $h$.

**$N'$ is a local auxiliary norm** ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_retractNorm⟧. The lemma is stated for a general set $A$ of base points (not only $\partial X$), a function $N$ that is continuous on $W_{0,1}|A$, a seminorm on the fibres over $A$ and satisfies condition (2) for sequences over $A$ converging to points of $A$, and a map $\rho$ continuous on an open $V$ inside the chart domain, with $\rho(V) \subset A \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$. Then $N'$ is a local auxiliary norm on $V$. By §XII.2, three checks.

Write $S = W_{0,1}|V$, $u(w) = \varphi(\rho(P(w)))$, $z(w) = (u(w), A(u(w))\,\mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w)) \in K[1]$ and $T(w) = \Phi[1]^{-1}(z(w))$, which lies over $\rho(P(w))$.

*Continuity.* $\Phi[1]$ is continuous on $S$; $u$ is continuous on $S$ (continuity of $\rho$ on $V$ and of $\varphi$); $z$ is continuous as $R[1]$ applied to $(u(w), \mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w))$; $T$ is continuous as $\Phi[1]^{-1}$ after $z$, whose values lie in $K[1]$. Then $N \circ T$ is continuous on $S$ because $N$ is continuous on $W_{0,1}|A$ and $T(w)$ lies over $\rho(P(w)) \in A$; the second term is continuous as a norm of a difference of continuous maps.

*Seminorm.* Over $y \in V$: the lemma above, with $\rho(y) \in A$.

*Condition (2).* Let $P(w_k) \to y \in V$ and $N'(w_k) \to 0$. Eventually $w_k \in S$.
- Both terms are nonnegative and bounded by $N'(w_k)$, so $N(T(w_k)) \to 0$ and $\|h_k - A(u_k)h_k\| \to 0$, where $h_k = \mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w_k)$, $u_k = u(w_k)$.
- $T(w_k)$ lies over $\rho(P(w_k)) \in A$, which converges to $\rho(y) \in A$ by continuity of $\rho$. Condition (2) for $N$, applied to the tail of the sequence that lies over $V$, gives $T(w_k) \to 0_{\rho(y)}$ in $W_{0,1}$.
- Reading this in the chart, $\Phi[1](T(w_k)) = z(w_k) \to (\varphi(\rho(y)), 0)$, so $A(u_k)h_k \to 0$ in $F_1$.
- Then $h_k = (h_k - A(u_k)h_k) + A(u_k)h_k \to 0$ in $F_1$, and the base coordinates $\varphi(P(w_k)) \to \varphi(y)$.
- Convergence in the chart gives convergence in $W_{0,1}$: $w_k \to 0_y$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · MChart.tendsto_of_tendsto_apply⟧. $\square$

**$N' = N$ where $\rho$ is the identity** ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm_eq⟧: if $y \in V \cap A$ and $\rho(y) = y$, then $N'(w) = N(w)$ for $w$ over $y$. Indeed $\Phi[1](w) = (\varphi(y), h)$ lies in $K[1]$, so $A(\varphi(y))h = h$; the transport is $\Phi[1]^{-1}(\varphi(y), h) = w$, and the second term is $\|h - h\| = 0$ ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm_eq_of_fix⟧.

**The local step** ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_localExtension_of_isTame⟧. Let $X$ be a tame M-polyfold, and $N$ continuous on $W_{0,1}|\partial X$, a seminorm on the fibres over $\partial X$, with condition (2) for sequences over $\partial X$. Every $x_0 \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x_0$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$ with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$.

*Proof.* Take $\rho$ and $V_1$ from the retraction lemma, a strong bundle chart $c$ of the atlas at $x_0$, and
$$V = V_1 \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap \rho^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi),$$
open because $\rho$ is continuous on the open $V_1 \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$; it contains $x_0$ because $\rho(x_0) = x_0$. On $V$, $\rho$ is continuous with values in $\partial X \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$. Put $M = N'$ with $A = \partial X$. By the lemma, $M$ is a local auxiliary norm on $V$; by the identity clause of the retraction lemma, $\rho(y) = y$ on $V \cap \partial X$, so $M = N$ there. $\square$

For an ep-groupoid, the local step applied to the object M-polyfold, which is tame when $X$ is, discharges the hypothesis of the global part ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧: an auxiliary norm over $\partial X$ in the sense above is continuous, a seminorm and satisfies condition (2) over $\partial X$, which is what the local step asks.

**Theorem 12.2.7** is then one line: the global part with the local step ⟦Chapter12/AuxNormLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7⟧.

*Where the formal proof departs from the text.* (a) The text works in a tame local strong bundle model, a strong bundle chart whose base retraction is tame. The formal proof places the retraction onto the boundary in a tame chart of the base, which tameness of $X$ provides, and evaluates the norm formula in an arbitrary strong bundle chart of the atlas. Only the continuity of $\rho$ and its two properties enter the norm formula, so no tame strong bundle chart is needed; the result is the text's statement under the text's hypotheses. (b) The text's formula composes $A$ with $rq(u)$ in the same chart where the fibre lives; the formal $N'$ composes with $\varphi(\rho(y))$, which is the same expression read through $\psi$ and $\varphi$. (c) The invariance of $N$ under morphisms is not used in the local step; it enters through Step 4 of the global part, where each term of the average over $G_x$ is identified with $N$. (d) Tameness is used once, in the retraction lemma, to read the degeneracy index in the chart and to keep it under $r$.

### XII.7 Definition 12.2.8 (2017: 12.5) and Remark 12.2.9 (2017: 12.1): mixed convergence

The second half of §12.2 repeats the first for *reflexive* auxiliary norms, the norms of Part I's Definition 5.1.7 (Part V), which are lower semicontinuous along sequences that converge on the base and weakly on the fibres. They are needed in Chapter 15 for compactness in the presence of perturbations. The new ingredient is one fact: morphisms preserve mixed convergence (Remark 12.2.9 in the stronger form below). With it, every step of §XII.3 carries lower semicontinuity.

**Reflexive $1$-fibres** (restated) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveFibers⟧, p. 576. The text's standing assumption before Definition 12.2.8 is that the strong bundle has reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres. The formalization reads it on the object bundle in the sense of Part I's Definition 5.1.4: every object lies in the base of a strong bundle chart of the atlas whose fibre $F$ has $F_1$ reflexive.

**Definition 12.2.8** (same) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.MixedTendsto⟧ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_2_8⟧, p. 576. A sequence $w_k \in W_{0,1}$ converges *mixed* to $w \in W_{0,1}$ if $P(w_k) \to P(w)$ in $X$ and, in some strong bundle chart around $P(w)$ with reflexive $F_1$, the fibre coordinates $\mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w_k)$ converge weakly in $F_1$ to $\mathrm{pr}_2\Phi[1](w)$. It is Part I's mixed convergence on the object bundle; the declaration `definition_12_2_8` records the unfolding.

**Remark 12.2.9** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_9⟧, pp. 576–577. The text remarks that mixed convergence does not depend on the chart and is compatible with the morphisms. The formal statement has three clauses: for $w_k \to w$ mixed,

- (i) in *every* chart of the atlas around $P(w)$ with reflexive $F_1$ the fibre coordinates converge weakly;
- (ii) $w_k \to w$ in $W$ (on level $0$);
- (iii) for every sc-smooth local section $\alpha$ of the source map on an open $S \ni P(w)$ ($s(\alpha(y)) = y$ for $y \in S$), $\alpha * w_k \to \alpha * w$ mixed ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedTendsto_actOne⟧.

(i) is Part I's Lemma 5.1.5 (Part V), and (ii) Part I's observation that weak convergence in $F_1$ implies convergence in $F_0$ by the compactness of $F_1 \to F_0$. Clause (iii) is the stronger part: the text states compatibility with morphisms; the formal statement gives it along any sc-smooth family of morphisms, which is what the averaging and transport of §XII.3 need. Through a given morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = P(w)$ one takes for $\alpha$ the local inverse of $s$ on the sheet of $\varphi$, and gets $\mu(\alpha(P(w_k)), w_k) \to \mu(\varphi, w)$ mixed ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.exists_mixedTendsto_μ⟧.

*Proof of (iii).* The text's argument for chart independence uses that a transition map is bounded on the fibres and continuous on level $0$. The formal proof applies the same argument to the fibre maps of $\mu$.

*Step 1, level $0$.* The map $w \mapsto \alpha * w$ is sc-smooth on $W|S$ (`isScSmoothOn_sectionAct`), hence continuous on level $0$; by (ii), $\alpha * w_k \to \alpha * w$ in $W$.

*Step 2, a bound.* Fix a Part I auxiliary norm $N_0$ of the object bundle. Near any point, two auxiliary norms are comparable: if $N$, $N'$ are a local auxiliary norm and a continuous fibre seminorm, there are a neighbourhood $V$ and $C > 0$ with $N'(v) \le C\,N(v)$ over $V$ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.exists_le_mul_auxNorm⟧. (This is Part I's Lemma 5.1.2, in local form, proved through the upper and lower bounds of §XII.2.) Applied to $N_0$ and $N_0 \circ (\alpha *)$, which is a continuous fibre seminorm near $P(w)$: $N_0(\alpha * v) \le C\,N_0(v)$ for $P(v)$ near $P(w)$. A mixed convergent sequence is eventually bounded in $N_0$ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedTendsto.exists_eventually_le⟧: its fibre coordinates converge weakly, hence are bounded in $F_1$ by the uniform boundedness principle, and $N_0$ is bounded by a multiple of the chart norm near $P(w)$. So $N_0(\alpha * w_k)$ is eventually bounded.

*Step 3, bounded and convergent on level $0$ implies mixed* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedTendsto_of_bounded⟧. Let $v_k \to v$ in $W$ with $N_0(v_k) \le r$ eventually. Take a chart around $P(v)$ with reflexive $F_1$ (reflexive fibres). Near $P(v)$, $N_0$ dominates a multiple of the chart norm (the lower bound of §XII.2, `exists_bounds`), so the fibre coordinates are eventually bounded in $F_1$. A bounded sequence in a reflexive space whose limit on level $0$ is known converges weakly to that limit (`weakTendsto_liftOneSnd_of_tendsto`, Part I): every subsequence has a weakly convergent subsequence (weak sequential compactness in reflexive spaces, Part V), its weak limit equals the level-$0$ limit because $F_1 \to F_0$ is continuous and limits in $F_0$ are unique, so all subsequential weak limits agree, and the whole sequence converges weakly. Hence $v_k \to v$ mixed.

Steps 1–3 give (iii). $\square$

**Lower semicontinuity along mixed convergence** (extra) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt⟧. A function $M$ on $W_{0,1}$ is *mixed lower semicontinuous at* $w$ if for every sequence $w_k \to w$ mixed and every $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $M(w) - \varepsilon < M(w_k)$. This implies $M(w) \le \liminf_k M(w_k)$ in the extended reals ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.le_liminf⟧, the form in Definition 12.2.10. The pointwise $\varepsilon$-form is used because it composes well:

- *sums*: if $M_1$, $M_2$ are mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$, so is $M_1 + M_2$, with $\varepsilon/2$ for each ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.add⟧, and so are finite sums ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_finset_sum⟧;
- *nonnegative constants*: $cM$ for $c \ge 0$, with $\varepsilon/c$ (trivially for $c = 0$) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.const_mul⟧;
- *products with functions of the base point* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.mul_comp⟧: if $g \ge 0$ is continuous at $P(w)$ and $M \ge 0$ over an open $V \ni P(w)$, then $w \mapsto g(P(w))M(w)$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$. With $a = g(P(w))$, $b = M(w)$ and $\delta = \varepsilon/(a + b + 1)$: eventually $g(P(w_k)) > a - \delta$ (continuity of $g$ along $P(w_k) \to P(w)$), $M(w_k) > b - \delta$, and both are nonnegative; then $g(P(w_k))M(w_k) \ge ab - \delta(a + b) > ab - \varepsilon$;
- *functions that vanish at the point* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_of_nonpos⟧: if $M(w) \le 0$ and $M \ge 0$ everywhere, $M$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$;
- *local agreement* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.congr⟧: if $M = M'$ over an open $V \ni P(w)$, the property passes, because $P(w_k) \in V$ eventually;
- *constants* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_const⟧;
- *through morphisms* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_comp_actOne⟧: if $M$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $\alpha * w$, then $M \circ (\alpha *)$ is at $w$, by (iii) of Remark 12.2.9.

### XII.8 Definition 12.2.10, Theorem 12.2.11 and Remark 12.2.12 (2017: Definition 12.6, Theorem 12.4, Remark 12.2): reflexive auxiliary norms exist

**Definition 12.2.10** (same) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm⟧, p. 577. A reflexive auxiliary norm is an auxiliary norm $N$ (Definition 12.2.1: continuous, invariant under morphisms, a complete norm on each fibre, condition (2)) with the additional property (3): $N(w) \le \liminf_k N(w_k)$ whenever $w_k \to w$ mixed, the liminf taken in the extended reals. The text prints the liminf as $k \to 0$; it is presumably $k \to \infty$, as in Part I's Definition 5.1.7 (Part V), and is read so. A reflexive auxiliary norm of the ep-groupoid is one of Part I's on the object bundle ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.toStrong⟧, and it is mixed lower semicontinuous at every point ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.mixedLscAt⟧ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.mixedLscAt⟧ (the liminf inequality gives the $\varepsilon$-form). Conversely, an auxiliary norm that is mixed lower semicontinuous at every point is reflexive ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_of_mixedLscAt⟧. The constructions below prove the $\varepsilon$-form and convert at the end.

**Theorem 12.2.11** (same) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11⟧, p. 577. Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid with paracompact $|X|$ and reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres. Then (1) reflexive auxiliary norms exist; (2) if $N$ is one and $f : X \to (0, \infty)$ is continuous and constant along morphisms, then $h \mapsto f(P(h))N(h)$ is one; (3) for every auxiliary norm $N'$ there are reflexive auxiliary norms $N_1 \le N' \le N_2$. The hypotheses are the text's; the formal statement is the conjunction of the three clauses.

**(1) Existence** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_exists⟧. The construction is that of Theorem 12.2.2 (§XII.3), with lower semicontinuity carried through each step.

*The local norms.* The text takes on $U(x)$ the norm $\|\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \Psi(g * h)\|_{F_1}$ in a chart with reflexive $F_1$. The formal proof takes the restriction of one reflexive auxiliary norm $N_0$ of the object bundle, which Part I's Proposition 5.1.8 (Part V) provides under reflexive fibres; it is mixed lower semicontinuous everywhere.

*Average* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_avgNorm⟧. Each term $M(g * w)$ of $\bar M(w) = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_gM(g * w)$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$ over $U(x)$: $g *$ is the action of the sc-smooth family of morphisms $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$, so the property passes through it; the finite sum and the factor $|G_x|^{-1}$ keep it.

*Transport* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_transNorm⟧. Near a point $w_0$ over the saturation, §XII.3 showed $T = \bar M \circ (\rho *)$ for a local inverse $\rho$ of $s$; this is an sc-smooth local section of $s$, so the property passes through $\rho *$, and $T$ agrees with $\bar M \circ (\rho *)$ on a neighbourhood, so it passes to $T$ by local agreement.

*Glue* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_glueNorm⟧. Fix $w$ over $y$. By local finiteness, $\pi(y)$ has a neighbourhood $n$ in $|X|$ meeting only finitely many supports; on $O = \pi^{-1}(\operatorname{int} n)$, open and containing $y$, $\tilde N = \sum_{i \in F}(\beta_i \circ \pi \circ P)T_i$ for a finite set $F$. For $i \in F$:
- if $y \in S_i$ (the saturation carrying $T_i$): $T_i$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$ and nonnegative over the open $S_i$, and $\beta_i \circ \pi$ is continuous and nonnegative, so the product rule applies;
- if $y \notin S_i$: then $\beta_i(\pi(y)) = 0$, since $\operatorname{supp}\beta_i \subset \pi(S_i)$; the term vanishes at $w$ and is nonnegative, so it is mixed lower semicontinuous at $w$.

The finite sum is mixed lower semicontinuous, and so is $\tilde N$ by local agreement on $O$. The text's argument for (3) at this point is "since the sum is locally finite"; the formal proof shows that this suffices, the terms with vanishing coefficient at the limit being harmless because they are nonnegative.

*Conclusion* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_glueNorm⟧: $\tilde N$ is an auxiliary norm by §XII.3 and mixed lower semicontinuous everywhere, hence reflexive.

**(2) Scaling** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_mul⟧, which is **Remark 12.2.12 (1)** (same) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_1⟧, p. 577. Let $N$ be a reflexive auxiliary norm and $f > 0$ continuous with $f(s(\varphi)) = f(t(\varphi))$. Then $(f \circ P)N$ is: continuous as a product; a complete norm on each fibre, being a positive multiple of one; condition (2): if $P(h_k) \to x$ and $f(P(h_k))N(h_k) \to 0$, then $N(h_k) \to 0$ because $f(P(h_k)) \to f(x) > 0$; invariant because $f$ is constant along morphisms and $N$ invariant; and mixed lower semicontinuous by the product rule.

**Remark 12.2.12 (2)** (same) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_2⟧, p. 577. For auxiliary norms $N_1$, $N_2$ and paracompact $|X|$ (which the remark's context has), there is a continuous $f : X \to (0, \infty)$, constant along morphisms, with $N_1 \le (f \circ P)N_2$.

*Step 1, local constants.* For every object $y$, the local comparison lemma of §XII.7 gives an open $V_y \ni y$ and $C_y > 0$ with $N_1(w) \le C_y N_2(w)$ over $V_y$.

*Step 2, saturation.* The bound holds over $\mathrm{sat}(V_y)$: for $w$ over $z$ with a morphism $\varphi : z \to z'$, $z' \in V_y$, the vector $k = \mu(\varphi, w)$ ⟦Chapter8/Book2021 · EpStrongBundle.exists_oneVal_eq_μ⟧ lies over $V_y$, and $N_i(w) = N_i(k)$ by invariance of both norms.

*Step 3, glue the constants.* Let $(\beta_y)$ be a partition of unity of $|X|$ subordinate to the open cover $(\pi(\mathrm{sat}(V_y)))_y$, and $g = \sum_y\beta_yC_y$ on $|X|$, continuous by local finiteness and positive because at each point some $\beta_y > 0$. Put $f = g \circ \pi$, continuous and constant along morphisms.

*Step 4, the estimate.* For $w$ over $z$ with $\pi(z) = \zeta$:
$$N_1(w) = \sum_y\beta_y(\zeta)N_1(w) \le \sum_y\beta_y(\zeta)C_yN_2(w) = f(z)N_2(w),$$
the inequality termwise: where $\beta_y(\zeta) \ne 0$, $z \in \mathrm{sat}(V_y)$ by subordination and Step 2 applies. $\square$

**Remark 12.2.12 (3)** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_3⟧, p. 578. The text: for a saturated open $U$, a function $N \ge 0$ on $W_{0,1}|U$ satisfying the liminf inequality there, and a continuous functorial $f \ge 0$ with support in $U$, the function $\tilde N = f \cdot N$ on $U$, $0$ off $U$, satisfies the liminf inequality on all of $W_{0,1}$. The formal statement drops what the estimate does not use: $U$ open (not necessarily saturated), $N \ge 0$ and mixed lower semicontinuous over $U$, $f \ge 0$ continuous (not necessarily functorial or supported in $U$). *Proof.* Fix $w_k \to w$ mixed. If $P(w) \in U$: the product rule gives lower semicontinuity of $(f \circ P)N$ at $w$, and $\tilde N$ agrees with it over the open $U$, so local agreement applies. If $P(w) \notin U$: $\tilde N(w) = 0$ and $\tilde N \ge 0$ everywhere. In both cases the liminf inequality follows. $\square$ The saturation of $U$, the functoriality of $f$ and $\operatorname{supp}f \subset U$ serve the continuity and the invariance of $\tilde N$, which the text uses when it applies the remark, not the estimate.

**(3) The sandwich** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_sandwich⟧. Given an auxiliary norm $N'$, take a reflexive $N$ from (1). Remark 12.2.12 (2), applied twice, gives functorial continuous $f, g > 0$ with $N \le (f \circ P)N'$ and $N' \le (g \circ P)N$. Put $N_1 = (f \circ P)^{-1}N$ and $N_2 = (g \circ P)N$; both are reflexive by (2) (with $1/f$ and $g$), and $N_1 \le N' \le N_2$. $\square$

### XII.9 Theorem 12.2.13 (2017: 12.5): extension of reflexive auxiliary norms

**Theorem 12.2.13** (explicit) ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13⟧, p. 578. Let $X$ be a tame ep-groupoid with $|X|$ paracompact, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ a strong bundle with reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres, and $N$ a reflexive auxiliary norm of $W_{0,1}|\partial X$. Then there is a reflexive auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$.

*Explicit*: the paracompactness of $|X|$ is not printed in the statement. The proof refers to "partitions of unity, as in Theorem 12.2.11", which takes it from Theorem 12.2.11; Theorem 12.2.7, whose construction is reused, states it. *A reading*: a reflexive auxiliary norm "for $W_{0,1}|\partial X$" asks the liminf inequality only for mixed convergent sequences over $\partial X$. The proof needs no more, because the first term of the local norm $N'$ is evaluated over $\rho(\cdot) \in \partial X$.

The proof has the two parts of §XII.6, each with lower semicontinuity added.

**Reflexive norms over a subset** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNormOn⟧: an auxiliary norm over $A$ (§XII.6) with $N(w) \le \liminf N(w_k)$ for mixed convergent sequences over $A$ with limit over $A$. A global reflexive norm restricts ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.isReflexiveAuxNormOn⟧.

#### The global part

*Reflexive local extensions* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveLocalExtensions⟧: every $x \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$, mixed lower semicontinuous at every vector over $V$, with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$. They are in particular local extensions in the sense of §XII.6 ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveLocalExtensions.hasLocalExtensions⟧.

**The global part** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13_hyp⟧: for paracompact $|X|$, reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres and a reflexive auxiliary norm $N$ over $\partial X$ with reflexive local extensions, there is a reflexive auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. *Proof.* Steps 1–4 of §XII.6, with these choices: at boundary points the reflexive local extensions; at interior points the restriction of a reflexive auxiliary norm $N_0$ of the object bundle (Part I's Proposition 5.1.8). The result is an auxiliary norm equal to $N$ over $\partial X$ by §XII.6. Its lower semicontinuity: the averages, transports and the glued sum keep mixed lower semicontinuity by the three lemmas of §XII.8 (`mixedLscAt_avgNorm`, `mixedLscAt_transNorm`, `mixedLscAt_glueNorm`), which hold for any local norms that are mixed lower semicontinuous. So $\tilde N$ is reflexive. $\square$

*A property of this Lean statement.* The global part takes the reflexive local extensions as a hypothesis; it is valid as stated and serves as the global half of Theorem 12.2.13, the hypothesis being discharged below for every tame $X$. Its satisfiability witnesses: the restriction of a global reflexive norm has reflexive local extensions ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isReflexiveAuxNorm⟧, so every bundle with reflexive fibres and paracompact $|X|$ satisfies all hypotheses of the global part ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13_hyp_witness⟧; concretely the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ over the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · TrivialBundle.epBundle_reflexive_witness⟧. These are consistency checks: in the first the extension is the global norm itself, and in the second $\mathbb R^n$ is modelled on all of $\mathbb R^n$ with a single chart, so $\partial X = \emptyset$ and the boundary condition is empty.

#### The local step: the inspection

The text says that the local extension $N'$ of Theorem 12.2.7 is well behaved under mixed convergence "by inspection". The formal proof supplies the inspection, in three lemmas.

*The setting.* Near $x_0 \in \partial X$, in a tame chart of the base with the retraction $\rho$ onto $\partial X$ (§XII.6), and in a strong bundle chart $\Phi$ with fibre $F$, $F_1$ reflexive (which reflexive fibres provide around every point), write $u(w) = \varphi(\rho(P(w)))$ and $A(u)$ for the fibre map of the retraction of the chart; then
$$N'(w) = N\big(\Phi[1]^{-1}(u, A(u)h)\big) + \|h - A(u)h\|_{F_1},$$
where $h$ is the fibre coordinate of $w$.

**Two facts about the fibre maps.**

*A uniform bound* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_norm_chartFibMap_le⟧: near a point $u_0$ of the chart domain, $\|A(u)\|_{L(F_1)} \le C$ uniformly in $u$. *Proof.* $(u, h) \mapsto A(u)h$ is continuous at $(u_0, 0)$ on level $1$ (§XII.6), so for $u$ near $u_0$ and $\|h\| \le \delta$, $\|A(u)h\| \le 1$; by linearity $\|A(u)\| \le 1/\delta$.

*Weak convergence* ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.weakTendsto_chartFibMap⟧: if $u_k \to u$ and $h_k \rightharpoonup h$ in the reflexive $F_1$, then $A(u_k)h_k \rightharpoonup A(u)h$. *Proof.* (a) $h_k$ is bounded (uniform boundedness), so $A(u_k)h_k$ is bounded by the uniform bound. (b) The inclusion $F_1 \to F_0$ is compact, so $h_k \to h$ in $F_0$; the retraction is continuous on level $0$, so $A(u_k)h_k \to A(u)h$ in $F_0$. (c) A bounded sequence in the reflexive $F_1$ that converges in $F_0$ converges weakly in $F_1$ to the same limit, as in Step 3 of Remark 12.2.9. The fibre map lies over the base point ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.toBase_chartFibMap⟧, and weak limits are compatible with differences ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · WeakTendsto.sub⟧.

**The inspection** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_retractNorm⟧: let $N$ be mixed lower semicontinuous at the vectors over a set $A$ containing $\rho(V)$; then $N'$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at every $w$ with $P(w) \in V$. *Proof.* Let $w_k \to w$ mixed, and read in the chart with reflexive $F_1$: $u_k = u(w_k) \to u(w)$ by continuity of $\rho$, and $h_k \rightharpoonup h$ in $F_1$ (Remark 12.2.9 (i), for this chart).
- *Second term.* By the weak convergence fact, $h_k - A(u_k)h_k \rightharpoonup h - A(u)h$; the norm of a Banach space is weakly lower semicontinuous, so $\|h - A(u)h\| \le \liminf\|h_k - A(u_k)h_k\|$.
- *First term.* The vectors $T(w_k) = \Phi[1]^{-1}(u_k, A(u_k)h_k)$ lie over $\rho(P(w_k)) \in A$; their base points converge to $\rho(P(w))$ and their fibre coordinates converge weakly in $F_1$ by the same fact. So $T(w_k) \to T(w)$ mixed (Definition 12.2.8 in this chart), and $N(T(w)) \le \liminf N(T(w_k))$ by the hypothesis on $N$.
- The $\varepsilon$-form for the sum follows from those of the two terms.

The set $A$ is a parameter, so the lemma serves any extension step from a closed subset with a continuous retraction, not only $A = \partial X$. $\square$

**The local step** ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_reflexiveLocalExtension_of_isTame⟧: on a tame M-polyfold with a strong bundle with reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres, a function $N$ that is continuous over $\partial X$, a fibre seminorm over $\partial X$, satisfies condition (2) for sequences over $\partial X$ and is mixed lower semicontinuous at vectors over $\partial X$ for sequences over $\partial X$ has, at every $x_0 \in \partial X$, a local auxiliary norm $M$ on an open $V \ni x_0$, mixed lower semicontinuous at every vector over $V$, with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$. *Proof.* Choose the strong bundle chart of §XII.6 among those with reflexive $F_1$. Then $M = N'$; that it is a local auxiliary norm equal to $N$ on the boundary is §XII.6, and its lower semicontinuity is the inspection with $A = \partial X$; the mixed convergent sequences that the inspection feeds to $N$ lie over $\rho(V) \subset \partial X$, so the hypothesis on $N$ over $\partial X$ suffices. $\square$ Tameness enters only through the retraction onto the boundary.

On the ep-groupoid, the local step in the object M-polyfold discharges the hypothesis of the global part for every tame $X$ ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧, and Theorem 12.2.13 is the global part with this hypothesis discharged.

**Witness.** The hypotheses together are satisfiable ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · TrivialBundle.theorem_12_2_13_witness⟧: the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ over the tame trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$, with a reflexive auxiliary norm over its boundary. This witness is degenerate: the M-polyfold $\mathbb R^n$ of the project (`rnPolyfold`) has the single chart onto all of $\mathbb R^n$, so $\partial X = \emptyset$ and the boundary data are vacuous. Since Theorem 12.2.13 adds no hypothesis beyond the text's (paracompactness of $|X|$ being explicit), the witness checks only that the hypotheses are consistent; a non-degenerate case would take a tame ep-groupoid with boundary, such as the quadrant witness of Proposition 12.3.7 (§XII.12) seen as a trivial ep-groupoid, and a reflexive norm over its boundary, restricted from a global one by Theorem 12.2.11.

### XII.10 Definition 12.3.1 (2017: 12.7) and Theorem 12.3.2 (2017: 12.6): bump functions

§12.3 supplies sc⁺-section functors, the perturbations of the later chapters. A section functor must commute with the morphisms; the sc⁺-sections of Part I, built with bump functions in charts, do not. The remedy is the pattern of §12.2 once more: bump functions and sections are built near a point with the natural action, averaged over the isotropy group and extended to the saturation by the morphisms.

**Definition 12.3.1, as printed** (same) ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctions⟧, p. 579. An ep-groupoid $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions if for every object $x$ and every saturated open $U \ni x$ there is an sc-smooth $f : X \to \mathbb R$ on the object M-polyfold, not identically $0$, with $\operatorname{supp}f \subset U$ and $f(s(\varphi)) = f(t(\varphi))$ for every morphism $\varphi$.

**The pointwise reading** ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise⟧ asks $f(x) \ne 0$ instead of $f \ne 0$. It is the project's reading of Part I's Definition 5.3.1 (Part V), where the bump function at $x$ is read as nonzero at $x$. The pointwise reading implies the printed one ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise.weak⟧. The two readings are kept side by side because Part I has a matching pair: `MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions` (pointwise) and `MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak` (not identically zero), and whether the second implies the first is Part I's open weak-to-pointwise question (Part V).

**Tools on saturations.** The saturation of an open set is open ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.isOpen_saturation_of_isOpen⟧, because $\mathrm{sat}(V) = t(s^{-1}(V))$ and $t$ is a local homeomorphism, hence open. The saturation is saturated ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_saturation⟧, and is contained in any saturated set containing $V$ ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.saturation_subset_of_isSaturated⟧. Two objects with the same orbit are joined by a morphism ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.eq_of_π_eq⟧. Around every $x$ in an open $U$ there are a natural representation $R$ of $G_x$ with $R.U \subset U$ and an open $V \ni x$ invariant under $R$ with $\overline V \subset R.U$ and $\overline V$ proper (Chapter 7, `exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen`); "proper" is Chapter 7's notion: the restriction of $t$ to $s^{-1}(\overline V)$ is proper, so the saturation of a closed subset of $\overline V$ is closed ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · isClosed_saturation_of_isProperSubset⟧.

**Averaging a function** ⟦Chapter12/BumpEp · EpGroupoid.exists_natAverage⟧. Let $R$ be a natural representation on $U(x)$, $V$ invariant with $\overline V \subset U(x)$, and $g$ sc-smooth with $\operatorname{supp}g \subset V$.
