4. *Conclusion* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hyp⟧: for any sc⁺-sections $\sigma_i$ on $V(x)$ with $\sigma_i = s_i$ on $U(x)$, the averages are sc⁺, equivariant, and equal to $s_i$ on $U(x)$, by 3 with $B = U(x)$, which is invariant (§XIV.1) and on which the $s_i$ are equivariant by Definition 14.1.3 (2). For the zero structure the zero sections are such $\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hyp_witness⟧.

The text averages over the stabilizer of one index of each orbit and transports along the orbit; averaging over all of $G_x$ produces the same symmetry and needs no choice of orbit representatives. Two variants are proved on the way: the extension to any $V' \le V(x)$ with the same action and $\operatorname{cl}V' \subset V(x)$, from step 2 alone ⟦Chapter14/LocalExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_of_closure⟧, and the extension to a good $V'(x) \le V(x)$ with $\operatorname{cl}V'(x) \subset V(x)$ provided by Lemma 14.2.1 ⟦Chapter14/LocalExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4⟧.

### XIV.4 Definition 14.1.5 and Theorem 14.1.6 (2017: Definition 14.3, Theorem 14.1): good systems for $\partial X$

**Definition 14.1.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem⟧, p. 643. A *good system for $\partial X$* assigns to every $x \in \partial X$ a good neighbourhood $V(x)$ with its natural action (Definition 14.1.2) such that for all $x, x' \in \partial X$ and every connected component $\Sigma$ of $V(x, x') = \mathcal U(V(x), V(x'))$, the maps $s : \Sigma \to V(x)$ and $t : \Sigma \to V(x')$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto open subsets. It carries $U(x) = V(x) \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.U⟧ and the boundary morphism sets $\mathcal U(x, x') = \mathcal U(U(x), U(x'))$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.mor⟧. *Restated*: the text says that for all $x, x'$ "there exist" good $V(x)$, $V(x')$ restricting to $U(x)$, $U(x')$ with the component condition; one $V(x)$ per point is fixed, which is how the proof of Theorem 14.1.6 chooses them and how every later use takes them. The component condition passes to open subsets ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.isDiffeoComponent_of_subset⟧: a component of the smaller morphism set lies in a component of the larger one, on which $s$ and $t$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto open sets, and their restrictions to an open subset remain so. *Refinement* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.exists_refinement⟧: for tame $X$ and open $W(x) \ni x$, a good system has a refinement inside the $W(x)$ whose neighbourhoods carry the same natural actions; at each $x$, Proposition 14.1.1 in its relative form (§XIV.1) shrinks $V(x)$ inside $W(x)$ keeping the action, and the component condition passes to the smaller sets. This is the boundary analogue of Proposition 13.1.3.

**Theorem 14.1.6** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.theorem_14_1_6_hyp⟧, p. 643. *Statement as formalized*: let $X$ be tame with $|X|$ paracompact, and let $O(x) \ni x$ be open in $X$ for $x \in \partial X$. There is a good system for $\partial X$ with $V(x) \subset O(x)$, so $U(x) \subset O(x) \cap \partial X$. A cover of $\partial X$ by sets open in $\partial X$ is written $(O(x) \cap \partial X)$ with $O(x)$ open in $X$.

*Proof*, the text's. 1. Put $W(y) = O(y)$ for $y \in \partial X$ and $W(y) = X$ otherwise, and apply Theorem 13.1.8 to $X$ (Part XIII) ⟦Chapter13/GoodSystemExistence · theorem_13_1_8⟧: there is a good system of $X$, with neighbourhoods $N(y) \subset W(y)$ carrying the natural action, $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}N(y))$, and the component condition. 2. At each $x \in \partial X$, Proposition 14.1.1 in its relative form shrinks $N(x)$ to a good $V(x) \subset N(x)$ with the same action (§XIV.1). 3. The component condition passes from the $N(x)$ to the smaller open $V(x)$, as above. *Explicit*: the text assumes $|\partial X|$ paracompact; its proof applies Theorem 13.1.8 to $X$, which needs $|X|$ paracompact, and Proposition 14.1.1, which needs $X$ tame. Both are standing assumptions of the chapter, and the formal statement takes them; whether paracompactness of $|\partial X|$ alone suffices is not examined. *Witness*: the trivial ep-groupoid of a tame quadrant ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEp · EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_witness⟧, whose orbit space is paracompact ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial⟧, and the half-space ep-groupoid of §XIV.26.

### XIV.5 Definition 14.1.7 (2017: Definition 14.4): structured sc⁺-multisections over $\partial X$

**Decorations and correspondences.** A *decoration* of $\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration⟧ is a good system $\mathcal U$ for $\partial X$ (Definition 14.1.7 (1)) with a symmetric sc⁺-section structure $S_x = (I_x, (s^x_i))$ for $\Lambda$ on each $U(x)$ (Definition 14.1.7 (3)). For $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in U(x)$, $t(\varphi) \in U(x')$ and indices $i \in I_x$, $j \in I_{x'}$, the identity of (4) is $s^{x'}_j(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, s^x_i(s(\varphi)))$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.Compat⟧. *Correspondences* for a decoration ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.Tau⟧, p. 645, are maps $\tau_{x,x'} : \mathcal U(x, x') \to J(x, x')$, $x, x' \in \partial X$, with (2) $\tau_{x,x'}$ locally constant on $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with finitely many values; (a) $\tau_{x',x}(\varphi^{-1}) = \tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)^\sharp$; (b) $\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, z)) = [I_x \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_x \xrightarrow{g} I_x]$; (c) $\tau_{x,x'}(g' * \varphi * g) = g' * \tau_{x,x'}(\varphi) * g$ for the bi-action of $G_{x'} \times G_x$; and (4) the identity above for every pair $(i, j)$ of $\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)$. Condition (4) is read pointwise on $\mathcal U(x, x')$, as printed; Definition 13.3.4 asks it along the component of $\varphi$, and on all of $\mathcal U(x, x')$ the two are the same. A *structured tuple* is $(\Lambda, \mathcal U, S, \tau)$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple⟧ with $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection functor over $\partial X$ (Definition 14.1.3, whose structures are those of the decoration).

**Definition 14.1.7** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredMultisection⟧, p. 644. A *structured sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$* is an equivalence class of structured tuples; $\Lambda$ is *structurable over $\partial X$* if some class lies over it ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryStructurable⟧. The text defines the equivalence as "similar to the $X$-case" (Definition 13.3.8). *The equivalence as formalized* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.Equiv⟧: $T \sim T'$ if $\Lambda = \Lambda'$ over $\partial X$, and there are open $O(x) \ni x$ with $O(x) \cap \partial X \subset U(x) \cap U'(x)$, $I_x = I'_x$, and $\tau_{x,x'} = \tau'_{x,x'}$, transported along these equalities, on the morphisms from $O(x) \cap \partial X$ to $O(x') \cap \partial X$. It is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.setoid⟧: transitivity intersects the open sets, which needs no tameness. *Agreement with the literal analogue* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equiv_iff_goodSystem⟧: for $X$ tame, $T \sim T'$ iff $\Lambda = \Lambda'$ over $\partial X$ and some good system $\mathcal U''$ for $\partial X$ with $U''(x) \subset U(x) \cap U'(x)$ carries equal index sets and equal correspondences. One direction takes $O(x) = V''(x)$; the other refines the good system of $T$ inside the $O(x)$ (§XIV.4), whose boundary traces lie in $O(x) \cap \partial X \subset U(x) \cap U'(x)$. The underlying functor of a class ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredMultisection.forget⟧ is well defined over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredMultisection.forget_mk⟧, and $\Lambda$ is structurable iff it is the functor of a structured tuple ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_iff⟧. *Restated*: as in Definition 14.1.3, the paracompactness of $|X|$ is not part of the definition. *Witness*: for $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact, the zero multisection is structurable over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_zero⟧, on a good system from Theorem 14.1.6, with the zero structures and $\tau \equiv [\{*\} \leftarrow \{*\} \to \{*\}]$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.zeroTau⟧. A non-degenerate witness is the multisection of a constant non-zero section on the half-space bundle (§XIV.26).

### XIV.6 Proposition 14.1.8 (2017: Proposition 14.1): generalized strong bundle isomorphisms

**Proposition 14.1.8** (stronger), p. 645. *The text*: a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\bar f : W \to W'$ between strong bundles over tame ep-groupoids carries structurable sc⁺-multisections to structurable ones, on the whole bundle and over the boundary; the proof is "similar to" those of Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3, for a representative $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} V \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ by strong bundle equivalences with $V$ over a tame ep-groupoid: first pull back along $\Phi$, then push forward along $\Psi$.

*The interior case* (same). For sc⁺-multisections of the whole bundle, the push-forward and the pull-back along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism preserve structurability ⟦Chapter13/MultisectionPushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pushMult⟧ ⟦Chapter13/MultisectionPushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pullMult⟧; this is Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3 composed along a representative, proved in Part XIII. Nothing in it is specific to the boundary.

*The boundary case.* For $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ (Definition 14.1.7), $\bar f_*\Lambda$ is structurable over $\partial X'$, and for $\Lambda'$ structurable over $\partial X'$, $\bar f^*\Lambda'$ is structurable over $\partial X$: for a representative with tame middle and tame target ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8⟧ ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pullMult⟧; for a representative between tame ep-groupoids, the middle being then tame ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_tame⟧ ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pullMult_tame⟧; and at the level of classes ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.proposition_14_1_8⟧ ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.proposition_14_1_8_pullMult⟧, through the chosen representative of the class (Part X), the pull-back needing only $X$ tame. *Stronger*: the paracompactness of the orbit spaces is not used, and the two steps hold for every pull map (strong bundle equivalences and proper strong bundle coverings) and every strong bundle equivalence.

*Proof.* The construction is Part XIII's for Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3, carried out over the boundary; what is new is that the transported sections stay sc⁺ on the faces, which the text takes for granted.

1. *Boundaries correspond.* A pull map $F$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, so it preserves the degeneracy index (Proposition 2.4.4) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.degIndex_obj⟧ and $F^{-1}(\partial X') = \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.mem_boundary_iff⟧; $F$ restricts to a map of boundary points ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryObj⟧. The index is also invariant along morphisms ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.mem_boundary_src_iff_fm⟧, so isomorphic points of $W$ lie over $\partial X$ together ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.mem_boundary_of_π_eq_fm⟧, and Part XIII's transport charts $x \mapsto y$ of an equivalence preserve the boundary ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.transportChart_mem_boundary_iff_fm⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.Q_mem_boundary_iff_fm⟧.
2. *The functors.* A functor over $\partial X$ takes equal values on isomorphic points over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryWFunctor.eq_of_π_eq_fm⟧. Hence $\Phi^*\Lambda'$ is a functor over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.isBoundaryWFunctor_pull⟧, and $\Phi_*\Lambda(w') = \Lambda(w)$ whenever $w$ lies over $\partial X$ and $\Phi(w) \cong w'$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.pushMult_eq_bdry_fm⟧, so $\Phi_*\Lambda$ is a functor over $\partial X'$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.isBoundaryWFunctor_pushMult_fm⟧: Lemma 11.5.2 over the boundary, where only values over $\partial X$ enter.
3. *Pull-back.* For a good system $\mathcal U'$ for $\partial X'$, Part XIII's adapted neighbourhoods $N(x)$ (with $F(N(x)) \subset N'(F(x))$ and $\Phi$ a local strong bundle isomorphism over $N(x)$) map $U(x)$ into $U'(F(x))$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.IsPullNbhd.mapsTo_bdry⟧, and the component condition is carried back ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.isDiffeoComponent_of_isPull_fm⟧. Shrinking each $N(x)$ to a good neighbourhood with the same action by Proposition 14.1.1 gives a good system for $\partial X$ adapted to $\mathcal U'$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.BdryPullData⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.exists_bdryPullData⟧, for $X$ tame. On it, the pulled-back structure has $I_x = I'_{F(x)}$, the action through $F : G_x \to G_{F(x)}$, and sections defined by $\Phi(s^x_i(z)) = s'^{F(x)}_i(F(z))$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullStructure⟧; the decoration ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullDecoration⟧ and correspondences $\tau_{x,y}(\varphi) = \tau'_{F(x),F(y)}(F(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullTau⟧ form a structured tuple ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullTuple⟧; a functor over $\partial X$ with a decoration is an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.isBoundaryScPlusMultisection_fm⟧. Conditions (2)–(4) and (a)–(c) are Part XIII's arguments; condition (1) of Definition 14.1.3 for the pulled-back sections is the transport property `FacePull_hyp` ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.FacePull_hyp⟧: for open $O$, $O'$ with $F(O) \subset O'$, a section face-wise sc⁺ on $O' \cap \partial X'$ pulls back to one face-wise sc⁺ on $O \cap \partial X$. The pull-back step is proved under this property ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.isBoundaryStructurable_pull_hyp⟧, for equivalences in particular ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pull_hyp⟧, and the property is a theorem (step 5).
4. *Push-forward.* For an equivalence $F : W \to W'$ with $X'$ tame and a decoration of $\Lambda$, Part XIII's push neighbourhoods $N'(y)$ around a transport chart $x_y \mapsto y$ are shrunk to good neighbourhoods with the same action ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.exists_isPushNbhd_bdry_fm⟧; the inverse of the chart maps $U'(y)$ into $U(x_y)$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · Qinv_mem_bdry_fm⟧, and the component condition is carried forward ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · isDiffeoComponent_push_fm⟧. With the chosen point $x_y$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryX⟧ and neighbourhood ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushNbhd⟧ this is a good system for $\partial X'$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushGood⟧. The pushed structure has $I'_y = I_{x_y}$ and sections $s'_i(z) = \mu(\psi_u, \Phi(s_i(u)))$, $u = Q^{-1}(z)$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushStructure⟧, by Part XIII's pointwise formulas with the section property needed only at the points used ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · P_obj_fm⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · pushSec_eq_fm⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · pushSec_compat_fm⟧; the correspondences are $\tau'_{y,y'}(\varphi') = \tau_{x_y, x_{y'}}(\tilde\varphi)$ for the lift $\tilde\varphi$ of $\varphi'$, which maps boundary morphisms to boundary morphisms ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · liftMor_mem_bdry_fm⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushDecoration⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushTau⟧. Condition (1) for the pushed sections is the property `FacePush_hyp` ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.FacePush_hyp⟧; the push step is proved under it ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_pushMult_hyp⟧, and so is the proposition for a representative ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pullMult_hyp⟧.
5. *The transport of face-wise sc⁺ sections* ⟦Chapter14/FaceTransport · SBLocalization.isFaceScPlusSectionOn_of_localIso⟧, the key lemma. Let $L : W|U \to W'|U'$ be a local strong bundle isomorphism over $\phi : U \to U'$ with fibre map $\Psi$, $G \subset U$ open around $x \in \partial X$, and $s = \Psi \circ s' \circ \phi$ on $G \cap \partial X$. If $s'$ is face-wise sc⁺ at $\phi(x)$, then $s$ is at $x$. *Proof*: given a tame strong bundle chart $c$ of $W$ at $x$, restrict it to $\operatorname{dom}\varphi \cap G$; the restriction is again a tame chart, and its retract is $O \cap N$ for an open $N$. Transport the restricted chart along $L^{-1}$: the result is a tame strong bundle chart of $W'$ with the same model, by Part I's lemma on charts transported along local strong bundle isomorphisms ⟦Chapter3/FredholmPullbackIso · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isChart_transportChart⟧ ⟦Chapter3/FredholmPullbackIso · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isTameChart_transportChart⟧, proved for Theorem 3.6.8. In these two charts the local representatives of $s$ and of $s'$ agree at every point of a local face, since such points are mapped into $\partial X$, where $s = \Psi \circ s' \circ \phi$. The face condition for $s'$ at $\phi(x)$ in the transported chart is therefore the face condition for $s$ at $x$ in the restricted chart, and a face germ on the smaller retract $O \cap N$ is one on $O$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceTransport · IsScPlusOnFaceNear.of_restrict_p6⟧. Since the condition is pointwise ⟦Chapter14/FaceTransport · SBLocalization.isFaceScPlusSectionOn_iff_singleton⟧, this proves it on sets.
6. *Both transport properties hold.* `FacePull_hyp` holds for every pull map ⟦Chapter14/FaceTransport · SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp⟧: near every $x$ the pulled-back section is $\Psi \circ s' \circ F$ for the local strong bundle isomorphism of $\Phi$ at $x$, and step 5 applies. `FacePush_hyp` holds for every strong bundle equivalence ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.facePush_hyp_of_equivalence⟧: near $z_0 = Q(u_0)$ the pushed section $z \mapsto \mu(\psi_u, \Phi(s(u)))$ is $\Psi_2 \circ s_1 \circ \phi_2$, where $s_1 = \Phi \circ s \circ F^{-1}$ is $s$ transported along the local strong bundle isomorphism of $\Phi$ at $u_0$, and $(\phi_2, \Psi_2)$ is the action of the morphisms $\psi_u$ near $\sigma = \psi_{u_0}$, itself a local strong bundle isomorphism with an explicit formula: on an open $\mathcal T \ni \sigma$ of morphisms, $\phi_2(t\psi) = s\psi$ and $\Psi_2 = \mu(\psi, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.exists_localIso_act_p6⟧ (Part X's local isomorphism of a morphism, with its formula exposed). Step 5 applies twice. Two direct checks of the pull property, superseded by this general one, remain in the formalization: it holds for the identity of every strong bundle ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp_id⟧, and vacuously when $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧; the push property holds vacuously when $\partial X' = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.facePush_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧.
7. *Assembly.* Pull-backs along every pull map ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.PullMap.isBoundaryStructurable_pull⟧ and push-forwards along every equivalence ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_pushMult⟧ preserve structurability over the boundary; composing them along $W \xleftarrow{\Phi} V \xrightarrow{\Psi} W'$ gives $\bar f_* = \Psi_*\Phi^*$ and $\bar f^* = \Phi_*\Psi^*$. The middle $V$ is tame when $X$ is ⟦Chapter14/FacePush · SBLocalization.SDiagram.isTame_B_p6⟧, because $\Phi$ covers an equivalence of ep-groupoids and an ep-groupoid equivalent to a tame one is tame (Part X).

### XIV.7 Theorem 14.1.9 and Remark 14.1.10 (2017: Theorem 14.2, Remark 14.3): the ∂-extension theorem

**The boundary domain support** ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp⟧: Definition 13.2.14 read over $\partial X$, the closure of the set of $x \in \partial X$ over which $\Lambda$ charges a non-zero point, $\Lambda(w) > 0$ for some $w \ne 0_x$. It is saturated ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isSaturated_boundaryDomSupp⟧, and empty for the zero multisection ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_zero⟧.

**Theorem 14.1.9** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_charged_a6⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_charged_statement⟧, p. 646. *Statement as formalized*: let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact, whose object M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, and such that every object lies in a tame strong bundle chart. Let $\Lambda : W|\partial X \to \mathbb Q^+$ be structurable over $\partial X$ and charge every boundary fibre, $N$ an auxiliary norm (Definition 8.3.5), $\tilde U$ an open saturated set containing the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, and $f : X \to [0, \infty)$ a continuous functor with $\operatorname{cl}\{f \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U$ and $N(\Lambda)(x) < f(x)$ on the boundary domain support. Then there is a structurable sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda' : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ (Definition 13.3.6) with (1) $N(\Lambda')(x) \le f(x)$ for all $x$, (2) $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda') \subset \tilde U$, (3) $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. *Narrower*, by the two readings named in the decisions: the tame strong bundle charts at every object, the reading of "a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid" used for Proposition 14.1.4 (§XIV.3); and charging, the reading of the factor $|I_x|^{-1}$ of Definition 14.1.3 (3). Both are gap G.186 (§XIV.29). Two readings of the hypotheses on $f$: "supported in $\tilde U$" is read as $\operatorname{cl}\{f \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U$; and the text writes $N(\Lambda)(x) < f(x)$ "for $x \in \partial X$" in the theorem, while what is needed and assumed is the inequality on the boundary domain support (off it, $N(\Lambda) = 0$ and $f \ge 0$ would allow $f = 0$). The proof, the whole of §§14.2–14.5, is §XIV.25.

**Charging is necessary** ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.chargesBoundary_of_structurable_eq_a6⟧: if a structurable $\Lambda'$ on $W$ agrees with $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$, then $\Lambda$ charges every boundary fibre. *Proof*: a structurable $\Lambda'$ has local section structures at every point (Definition 13.2.1), whose local weights sum to $1$ on every fibre; so over each $x$ some $w$ has $\Lambda'(w) > 0$, and over $\partial X$ this is $\Lambda(w)$. Hence the exact form ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_iff_a6⟧: under the other hypotheses, a structurable $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ has an extension as in the theorem if and only if it charges every boundary fibre. For a structured tuple, charging is the same as non-empty index sets at all boundary points ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.nonempty_I_a6⟧ (§XIV.2).

*Remark: the uncharged Lean statement.* The Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 without the charging condition and without the tame strong bundle charts ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement⟧, whose hypotheses are jointly satisfiable ($\Lambda = 0$, $\tilde U = \emptyset$, $f = 0$) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement_hyp_witness⟧, does not hold when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.not_theorem_14_1_9_statement_a6⟧, for $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact and sc-smooth partitions of unity. Because the formal Definition 14.1.3 admits $I_x = \emptyset$, the function $\Lambda \equiv 0$ is structurable over $\partial X$ in the formal sense ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_zeroFun_a6⟧: on a good system from Theorem 14.1.6, with the empty index set at every boundary point ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.emptyBoundaryStructure_a6⟧ under the trivial action on the empty type ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.pemptyAction_a6⟧, and the unique correspondence between empty index sets ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.eq_of_isEmpty_a6⟧ ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.emptyTau_a6⟧, which satisfies (a)–(c) and (4) vacuously. Its boundary domain support is empty ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_zeroFun_a6⟧, so $\tilde U = \emptyset$ and $f = 0$ satisfy the hypotheses, with $N$ from Theorem 12.2.2; an extension would be structurable and $0$ over a boundary point, which necessity excludes. The statement holds when $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement_of_boundary_eq_empty_a6⟧. This is a property of that Lean statement and of the formal Definition 14.1.3, not of the text, whose $|I_x|^{-1}$ presumes $I_x \ne \emptyset$; the statement with charging above is the one proved. The forms derived from that statement are recorded where they occur (§§XIV.25, XIV.28).

**Remark 14.1.10** (2017: Remark 14.3), p. 646, says that the proof needs preparation and is lengthy; nothing to formalize.

### XIV.8 Lemmas 14.2.1, 14.2.2 and Proposition 14.2.3 (2017: the text before Lemma 14.1, Lemma 14.1, Proposition 14.2): a good structured representative

§14.2 fixes a representative $(\Lambda, \mathcal U^0, S^0, \tau^0)$ of a structured sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$; the text names its properties (P1) (the good system), (P2) (the structures) and (P3) (the correspondences), which are the fields of a structured tuple (§XIV.5). It then shrinks the good system so that the level sets of the correspondences acquire disjoint closures, property (P4), which §14.3 needs to separate them by open sets.

**Lemma 14.2.1** (same) ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_2_1⟧, p. 648. *Statement*: let $X$ be tame, $x \in \partial X$ and $V^0(x)$ a good neighbourhood, $U^0(x) = V^0(x) \cap \partial X$. There is a good neighbourhood $V(x) \le V^0(x)$ (same natural action, restricted) with $\operatorname{cl}_X V(x) \subset V^0(x)$, $\operatorname{cl}_X U(x) \subset U^0(x)$, and $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|U(x)| \subset |U^0(x)|$ (14.15). The text states (14.15) with the closure in $|\partial X|$; since $|\partial X| = \pi(\partial X)$ is closed in $|X|$ (§XIV.11), the closure in $|X|$ is the same. The faces, the connectedness and the invariance of $U(x)$ are those of a good neighbourhood (Definition 14.1.2).

*Proof.* 1. Choose a closed neighbourhood $C$ of $x$ with $C \subset V^0(x)$ (the object space is regular). 2. Apply Proposition 14.1.1 in its relative form inside the interior of $C$ (§XIV.1): this gives a good $V(x) \le V^0(x)$ with $V(x) \subset C$, so $\operatorname{cl}V(x) \subset C \subset V^0(x)$, and $\operatorname{cl}U(x) \subset \operatorname{cl}V(x) \cap \partial X \subset U^0(x)$ because $\partial X$ is closed. 3. For the orbit closure, Proposition 7.1.10 for the proper set $\operatorname{cl}V^0(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/Basic · proposition_7_1_10_of_isProperMap⟧ gives $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}\pi(A) = \pi(\operatorname{cl}_X A)$ for $A \subset V^0(x)$ with $\operatorname{cl}A$ inside; applied to $A = U(x)$ it gives (14.15). For all boundary points at once ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_2_1_system⟧: a good system $\mathcal U \le \mathcal U^0$ for $\partial X$ with these properties; the component condition passes to the smaller sets (§XIV.4).

**Lemma 14.2.2** (same) ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.lemma_14_2_2⟧, p. 648. *Statement*: let $\mathcal U$, $\mathcal U^0$ be good systems for $\partial X$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X U(x) \subset U^0(x)$ for all $x$, and let $\tau$ be locally constant on $\mathcal U^0(x, x')$. For $[d] \ne [d']$ the closures in the morphism space of $\tau^{-1}([d]) \cap \mathcal U(x, x')$ and $\tau^{-1}([d']) \cap \mathcal U(x, x')$ are disjoint. *Proof*: $\operatorname{cl}\mathcal U(x, x') \subset \mathcal U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.closure_mor_subset⟧, since $s$ and $t$ are continuous and $\operatorname{cl}U(x) \subset U^0(x)$. A common limit point $\varphi$ of the two sets therefore lies in $\mathcal U^0(x, x')$, where $\tau$ is locally constant; near $\varphi$ in $\mathcal U^0(x, x')$, $\tau$ is constant, and the two sets both meet that neighbourhood, so $[d] = \tau(\varphi) = [d']$. *A reading*: the text defines $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with $t(\varphi) \in U(x)$; presumably $U(x')$ is meant, as in (P3), and that is what is formalized.

**Restriction.** A decoration restricts to a smaller good system with the same actions ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.restrictTo⟧, the boundary morphism sets shrink ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.mor_mono⟧, and the correspondences restrict ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.Tau.restrict⟧: local constancy, finiteness of the values, (a)–(c) and (4) are inherited by subsets, and the bi-action is the same because the actions are. The restricted tuple ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.restrict⟧ is equivalent to the original ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equiv_restrict⟧, with $O(x)$ the smaller neighbourhoods.

**Proposition 14.2.3** (same) ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.proposition_14_2_3⟧, p. 649. *Statement*: for $X$ tame, every structured tuple $(\Lambda, \mathcal U, S, \tau)$ is equivalent to one with the same $\Lambda$, the same index sets and the same correspondences on a smaller good system with restricted actions, which has (P4) ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.HasP4⟧: for $[d] \ne [d']$ the closures of $\tau_{x,x'}^{-1}([d])$ and $\tau_{x,x'}^{-1}([d'])$ (preimages in $\mathcal U(x, x')$) are disjoint. *Proof*: Lemma 14.2.1 for the good system of the tuple, restriction to the smaller system, and Lemma 14.2.2 with $\mathcal U^0$ the original system, on which $\tau$ is locally constant by (2) of Definition 14.1.7. (P4) persists under further shrinking ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.HasP4.restrict⟧ (the text: "it will persist when we replace these sets by even smaller ones"), since the preimages only shrink. On classes ⟦Chapter14/GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.proposition_14_2_3_class⟧: every structured sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ of a tame $X$ has a representative with (P4). The hypotheses of Theorem 14.1.9 enter only as tameness.

### XIV.9 (P5) and Lemma 14.3.1 (2017: Lemma 14.2): open neighbourhoods of the level sets

**(P5)** ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds⟧, p. 649. Fix a tuple with (P1)–(P4). Neighbourhoods $\tilde U'(x)$, $x \in \partial X$, with (P5) are open sets of objects with (i) the natural $G_x$-action and $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U'(x))$, and (ii) $\tilde U'(x) \cap \partial X = U^0(x)$. *Reading*: "admits the natural $G_x$-action" is read as carrying the natural representation of the good system $\mathcal U^0$ itself, extended to $\tilde U'(x)$; this makes the bi-action on $\tilde U'(x, x') = \mathcal U(\tilde U'(x), \tilde U'(x'))$ (14.19) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.mor⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.isOpen_mor⟧, ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.biact⟧, agree with the bi-action of Definition 14.1.7 (c) on the boundary morphisms ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.biact_eq⟧, the natural bi-action depending only on the representations ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.biact_congr_rep_p3w4⟧. The bi-action preserves $\tilde U'(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.biact_mem⟧, and that of $\mathcal U^0$ preserves $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.biact_mem_mor_p3w4⟧. *Boundary morphisms* are those with source and target in $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.boundaryMor⟧; by (ii), the boundary morphisms of $\tilde U'(x, x')$ are exactly $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.mor_inter_boundaryMor⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.mor_subset⟧, and inversion maps $U^0(x, x')$ to $U^0(x', x)$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.inv_mem_mor_p3w4⟧. *Witness*: the open sets $V(x)$ of the good system itself ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.ofGood⟧, which have $V(x) \cap \partial X = U^0(x)$ by definition.

Two identities of the bi-actions are used: $(g' * [d] * g)^\sharp = g^{-1} * [d]^\sharp * g'^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swap_biact_p3w4⟧ for correspondences, and $(g' * \varphi * g)^{-1} = g^{-1} * \varphi^{-1} * g'^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.inv_biact_p3w4⟧ for morphisms (Definition 13.1.5).

**Lemma 14.3.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.lemma_14_3_1⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension⟧, p. 650. *Statement*: under (P1)–(P5), for all $x, x' \in \partial X$ and every $[d] \in J(x, x')$ there is an open $\tilde O_{x,x',[d]} \supset \tau^{0-1}([d])$ with (1) $\tilde O_{x,x',[d]} \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$; (2) pairwise disjoint closures for $[d] \ne [d']$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.disjoint⟧, so that a morphism lies in at most one of them ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.eq_of_mem⟧; (3) $h * \tilde O_{[d]} * g = \tilde O_{h * [d] * g}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.image_biact⟧; (4) the union $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ot⟧ meets $\partial X$ exactly in $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.iUnion_inter_boundaryMor⟧; and (14.20), $\tilde O_{[d]} \cap \partial X = \tau^{0-1}([d])$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.inter_boundaryMor⟧. *Stronger*: in addition, $\varphi \in \tilde O_{x,x',[d]}$ iff $\varphi^{-1} \in \tilde O_{x',x,[d]^\sharp}$. The printed form, (1)–(4) alone, is ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.lemma_14_3_1_book⟧.

*Proof*, the text's with one step added.

1. *Separation* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.exists_of_hasP4⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre⟧. Fix $x, x'$. The correspondence $\tau^0_{x,x'}$ has finitely many values (Definition 14.1.7 (2)), and by (P4) the closures of its level sets are pairwise disjoint closed sets. The morphism space is metrizable, hence normal, and in a normal space finitely many pairwise disjoint closed sets have open neighbourhoods with pairwise disjoint closures ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.exists_open_disjoint_closure⟧ (an induction on the finite set, the empty level sets getting the empty set). Intersecting with the open set $\tilde U'(x, x')$ gives open $\tilde O'_{x,x',[d]} \supset \tau^{0-1}([d])$ inside $\tilde U'(x, x')$ with disjoint closures. The level set lies in $\tilde U'(x, x')$ because $U^0(x, x') \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$.
2. *Invariance under the bi-action* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.biInv⟧. Replace $\tilde O'_{[d]}$ by $\bigcap_{h, g}(h * \cdot * g)^{-1}(\tilde O'_{h * [d] * g})$, the intersection over the finite group $G_{x'} \times G_x$ of the preimages under the bi-action, which is a homeomorphism of $\tilde U'(x, x')$. This is the text's $\bigcap h * \tilde O'_{[d']} * g$ over the $(h, [d'], g)$ with $h * [d'] * g = [d]$, written through preimages. The result is open, still contains $\tau^{0-1}([d])$ by the equivariance (c) of $\tau^0$ and the invariance of $U^0(x, x')$, keeps (1) and (2) (it is smaller), and satisfies $h * \varphi * g \in \tilde O_{h * [d] * g} \iff \varphi \in \tilde O_{[d]}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.biInv_biact_mem_iff⟧, which is (3).
3. *Symmetry under inversion* (added) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.symm⟧. Replace $\tilde O_{x,x',[d]}$ by $\tilde O_{x,x',[d]} \cap \iota^{-1}(\tilde O_{x',x,[d]^\sharp})$, $\iota$ the inversion. This is open, contains $\tau^{0-1}([d])$ by (a) of Definition 14.1.7, keeps (1) and (2), and has the symmetry ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.symm_inv_mem_iff⟧, since $[d]^{\sharp\sharp} = [d]$; it keeps (3) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.symm_biact_mem_iff⟧ by the two identities of the bi-actions above.
4. *(4) and (14.20).* A boundary morphism in $\tilde O_{[d]}$ lies in $U^0(x, x')$ by (1) and (P5) (ii), so it has some value $\tau^0(\varphi) = [d']$ and lies in $\tilde O_{[d']}$; by (2), $[d'] = [d]$. Conversely the level sets are inside.

The inversion symmetry is what makes the extended correspondences satisfy Definition 14.1.7 (a) (§XIV.10), which the z-loops of §14.4 need to be reversible. Only finitely many $[d]$ have non-empty sets.

### XIV.10 Definition 14.3.2, Lemma 14.3.3, Proposition 14.3.4 and Remark 14.3.5 (2017: the text before Lemma 14.3, Lemma 14.3, Proposition 14.3, Remark 14.4): the extended correspondences

**Definition 14.3.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat⟧, p. 651. $\hat O_{x,x'}$ is the union of the connected components of $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ that meet $\partial X$. For $\varphi \in \tilde O_{x,x'}$, $\hat\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)$ is the unique $[d]$ with $\varphi \in \tilde O_{x,x',[d]}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.mem_O_tauHat⟧; off $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ the value is irrelevant. $\hat O_{x,x',[d]} = \{\varphi \in \hat O_{x,x'} : \hat\tau(\varphi) = [d]\}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatD⟧. *Restated*: the text defines $[d]_\varphi = \tau^0(\psi)$ for a boundary morphism $\psi$ in the component of $\varphi$; the formal definition reads the value off the decomposition of Lemma 14.3.1, and the two agree:

1. $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ is open ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.isOpen_Ot⟧, lies in $\tilde U'(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ot_subset_mor⟧ and contains $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.mor_subset_Ot⟧.
2. The $\tilde O_{[d]}$ are pairwise disjoint open sets with union $\tilde O_{x,x'}$, so the component in the union of a point of one of them lies in it ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.connectedComponentIn_iUnion_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.component_subset⟧: the component is connected and the other sets separate it.
3. Hence $\hat\tau$ is constant on the components of $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq_of_mem_component⟧, and, by (14.20), $\hat\tau(\varphi) = \tau^0(\psi)$ for every boundary morphism $\psi$ in the component of $\varphi$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq_tau_of_mem_component_Ot⟧, which is the text's definition.

(14.23): $\hat O_{x,x'} \subset \tilde O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat_subset_Ot⟧, so $\hat O_{x,x'} \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat_subset_mor⟧; $U^0(x, x') \subset \hat O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.mor_subset_Ohat⟧, each of its points lying in a component that meets $\partial X$ at that point; and $\hat O_{x,x'} \cap \partial X = U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat_inter_boundaryMor⟧ by (4). The component in $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ of a point of $\hat O_{x,x'}$ lies in $\hat O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.component_subset_Ohat⟧, so $\hat O_{x,x'}$, a union of components of an open set in a locally connected space, is open ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.isOpen_Ohat⟧. And $\hat O_{[d]} = \hat O \cap \tilde O_{[d]}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatD_eq⟧, with $\hat O_{[d]} \cap \partial X = \tau^{0-1}([d])$ (14.24) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatD_inter_boundaryMor⟧.

**Lemma 14.3.3** (same) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.lemma_14_3_3⟧, p. 651: two boundary morphisms in one component of $\hat O_{x,x'}$ have the same $\tau^0$. *Proof*: a component of $\hat O_{x,x'}$ lies in a component of $\tilde O_{x,x'}$, which lies in one $\tilde O_{[d]}$ (item 2 above); by (14.20) both morphisms have $\tau^0 = [d]$. So $\varphi \mapsto [d]_\varphi$ is well defined, and $\hat\tau(\varphi) = \tau^0(\psi)$ for every boundary $\psi$ in the component of $\varphi$ in $\hat O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq_tau_of_mem_component⟧. Every component of $\hat O_{x,x'}$ contains a boundary morphism, indeed one in the component in $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.exists_boundary_mem_component⟧, by definition of $\hat O$.

**Proposition 14.3.4** (same) ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.proposition_14_3_4⟧, p. 652. *Statement*: under (P1)–(P5) there are open sets $\hat O_{x,x'}$ of morphisms with (1) $U^0(x, x') \subset \hat O_{x,x'} \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$ and $\hat O_{x,x'} \cap \partial X = U^0(x, x')$; (2) $\hat O_{x,x'}$ invariant under the bi-action of $G_{x'} \times G_x$; (3) a locally constant extension $\hat\tau_{x,x'}$ of $\tau^0_{x,x'}$ to $\hat O_{x,x'}$, unique among locally constant extensions, with $\hat\tau(g' * \varphi * g) = g' * \hat\tau(\varphi) * g$ and $\hat\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, y)) = \tau^0_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, z))$ for $y \in \tilde U'(x)$ with $\Gamma(g, y) \in \hat O_{x,x}$ and $z \in U^0(x)$; and the decomposition (14.24). *Proof.*

1. *(1)* is (14.23) above.
2. *Local constancy* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_locallyConstant⟧: near $\varphi \in \tilde O_{[d]}$ the open set $\tilde O_{[d]}$ is a neighbourhood on which $\hat\tau = [d]$.
3. *Extension* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq_tau⟧: on $U^0(x, x')$, $\varphi \in \tilde O_{\tau^0(\varphi)}$ because $\tilde O_{[d]} \supset \tau^{0-1}([d])$.
4. *Uniqueness* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_unique⟧: a function locally constant on $\hat O_{x,x'}$ is constant on its components ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.eq_of_mem_connectedComponentIn⟧; every component contains a boundary morphism $\psi$, where the function equals $\tau^0(\psi) = \hat\tau(\psi)$, and $\hat\tau$ is constant on the component too. The values of $\hat\tau$ on $\hat O$ are values of $\tau^0$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_image_subset⟧, hence finitely many ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.finite_tauHat⟧ (the text's "taking the same values as $\tau^0$").
5. *Equivariance and (2)* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_biact⟧: by (3) of Lemma 14.3.1, $\varphi \in \tilde O_{[d]}$ iff $h * \varphi * g \in \tilde O_{h * [d] * g}$. The bi-action maps $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ to itself ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.biact_mem_Ot⟧, and, being a homeomorphism preserving $\partial X$, maps components meeting $\partial X$ to components meeting $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.biact_mem_Ohat⟧.
6. *The diagonal property* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_Γ⟧: $\hat\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, y)) = [I_x \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_x \xrightarrow{g} I_x]$ for $y \in \tilde U'(x)$ with $\Gamma(g, y) \in \hat O_{x,x}$. The text states it without proof. *Sheets.* For a natural representation on $R$, every morphism $\varphi$ between points of $R$ is $\Gamma(g, s(\varphi))$ for exactly one $g$, its *sheet label* ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.sheetLabel_p3w4⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.Γ_sheetLabel_p3w4⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.sheetLabel_eq_p3w4⟧. The sheet $\{\Gamma(g, z)\}$ is open: if $\varphi_0 = \Gamma(g, s(\varphi_0))$, then $\varphi = \Gamma(g, s(\varphi))$ for all $\varphi$ near $\varphi_0$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.eventually_Γ_src_eq_p3w4⟧, because $s$ is a local homeomorphism and $z \mapsto \Gamma(g, z)$ is a continuous local inverse of $s$ through $\varphi_0$. So the sheet label is locally constant on the morphisms between points of $R$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.sheetLabel_locallyConstant_p3w4⟧. *The argument.* The component of $\Gamma(g, y)$ in $\tilde O_{x,x}$ meets $\partial X$ (as $\Gamma(g, y) \in \hat O$), say in $\psi$; the sheet label is constant on that component, so $\psi = \Gamma(g, s(\psi))$ with $s(\psi) \in U^0(x)$; then $\hat\tau(\Gamma(g, y)) = \hat\tau(\psi) = \tau^0(\psi) = [\mathrm{id}, g]$ by (b) of Definition 14.1.7.
7. *Inversion* (added): $\varphi \in \hat O_{x,x'}$ iff $\varphi^{-1} \in \hat O_{x',x}$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.inv_mem_Ohat⟧, inversion being a homeomorphism that preserves $\partial X$ and, by the symmetry of Lemma 14.3.1, maps $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ onto $\tilde O_{x',x}$; and $\hat\tau_{x',x}(\varphi^{-1}) = \hat\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)^\sharp$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_inv⟧, which is Definition 14.1.7 (a) for $\hat\tau$.

**Remark 14.3.5** (2017: Remark 14.4), p. 653, observes that $\hat O_{x,x'}$ need not be of the form $\tilde U(x, x')$ for neighbourhoods of objects; it states nothing to prove, and nothing formal depends on that form.

### XIV.11 Lemmas 14.3.6 and 14.3.7 (2017: Lemmas 14.4, 14.5): a locally finite cover of the boundary

The rest of §14.3 chooses the index set $A$ of the construction and the sets $\hat V_a$ on which the local extensions of §14.4 live. Both lemmas are formalized in an abstract setting that the objects of Chapter 14 instantiate (§XIV.12): the boundary is any set $B$ of objects (with $|B|$ closed for Lemma 14.3.6, saturated for Lemma 14.3.7), the neighbourhoods are natural neighbourhoods in the sense of §13.1 (Part XIII), and the sets $\hat O_{a,b}$ are any open sets of morphisms that contain the boundary morphisms $U'(a, b)$. The proofs use only these properties; isolating them makes visible which facts of §§14.1–14.3 the lemmas need.

**Closed saturated sets.** Four small facts about saturated sets are used throughout §§14.3–14.5. A saturated set contains the target of every morphism with source in it ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.IsSaturated.tgt_mem⟧ (that is the definition, read through the inverse morphism); the complement of a saturated set is saturated ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_compl⟧ (a morphism from the complement into the set would, inverted, leave the set); every preimage $\pi^{-1}(S)$ of a set of orbits is saturated ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_preimage_π⟧; and the saturation of an open set is open ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.isOpen_saturation⟧, which is Proposition 7.1.8 (Part VII). From these: *a closed saturated set $B$ has closed image $|B|$ in $|X|$* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.isClosed_π_image_of_isSaturated⟧. *Proof*: the complement of $|B|$ is $\pi(X \setminus B)$, because $B$ is saturated (an orbit meets $B$ iff it lies in $B$); $X \setminus B$ is open and saturated, so $\pi(X \setminus B)$ is open by Proposition 7.1.8. For $B = \partial X$: the degeneracy index is invariant under morphisms, so $\partial X$ is saturated ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_boundary_p3w4⟧, and it is closed; hence $|\partial X|$ is closed in $|X|$, which the text uses tacitly when it treats $|\partial X|$ as a closed subset.

**Lemma 14.3.6** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_6⟧, p. 654. *Statement*: let $|X|$ be paracompact, $B$ a set of objects with $|B|$ closed in $|X|$, and $\tilde U(x)$, for every object $x$, an open neighbourhood with the natural $G_x$-action. There are $A \subset B$ and nonempty open sets $\tilde V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, $a \in A$, with (1) $|\tilde V_a|$ open and $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\tilde V_a| \subset |\tilde U(a)|$, (2) $\tilde V_a$ invariant under the natural $G_a$-action, (3) $(|\tilde V_a|)_{a \in A}$ locally finite in $|X|$ and covering $|B|$. *Explicit*: the closedness of $|\partial X|$, which the text's proof uses, is a hypothesis here, discharged for $B = \partial X$ as above.

*Proof*, the text's.

1. *The cover.* The sets $|\tilde U(x)|$, $x \in B$, and $|X| \setminus |B|$ form an open cover of $|X|$, indexed by $B$ plus one extra index: $|\tilde U(x)| = \pi(\tilde U(x))$ is open by Proposition 7.1.8 (Part VII), and $|X| \setminus |B|$ is open because $|B|$ is closed. It covers: an orbit meeting $B$ at $x$ lies in $|\tilde U(x)|$.
2. *Refinement.* $|X|$ is paracompact, so the cover has a locally finite open refinement $(v_i)$ indexed by the same set, each $v_i$ inside the $i$-th member (precise refinement). A paracompact Hausdorff space is normal, and a point-finite open cover of a normal space can be shrunk to an open cover $(w_i)$ with $\operatorname{cl}w_i \subset v_i$; $(w_i)$ is again locally finite.
3. *The sets $\tilde V_a$.* For $a \in B$ put $\tilde V_a = \tilde U(a) \cap \pi^{-1}(w_a)$, and let $A$ be the set of $a \in B$ with $\tilde V_a \ne \emptyset$. Then $\tilde V_a$ is open, contained in $\tilde U(a)$, and invariant under the natural $G_a$-action, because $\tilde U(a)$ is and $\pi^{-1}(w_a)$ is saturated. Its image is $|\tilde V_a| = w_a$: $w_a \subset v_a \subset |\tilde U(a)|$, so every orbit in $w_a$ meets $\tilde U(a)$. So $|\tilde V_a|$ is open and $\operatorname{cl}|\tilde V_a| = \operatorname{cl}w_a \subset v_a \subset |\tilde U(a)|$.
4. *Local finiteness and cover.* $(|\tilde V_a|)_{a \in A}$ is a subfamily of $(w_i)$, re-indexed injectively, hence locally finite. A point $\pi(x)$ with $x \in B$ lies in some $w_i$; not in the extra one, since $\operatorname{cl}w_{\text{extra}} \subset |X| \setminus |B|$; so $\pi(x) \in w_a$ for some $a \in B$, and then $\tilde V_a \ne \emptyset$ and $a \in A$.

**Lemma 14.3.7** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_7⟧, p. 655. *Setting*: $B$ saturated; $a \in A$ fixed; $\tilde U'(a)$ a neighbourhood of $a$ with the natural $G_a$-action; for $b \in A$, $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b) \subset \tilde U'(b)$ and $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b)$ proper (Definition 7.1.13: $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b))$); the sets $\hat O_{a,b}$ open and containing every $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \tilde U'(a) \cap B$, $t(\varphi) \in \tilde U'(b) \cap B$; and $(|\tilde V_b|)_{b \in A}$ locally finite. *Statement*: every $y \in U'(a) = \tilde U'(a) \cap B$ has a finite $o(y) \subset A$ and an open $\tilde O(y) \ni y$ inside $\tilde U'(a)$ with (1) $|\tilde O(y)| \cap |\tilde V_b| \ne \emptyset$ only for $b \in o(y)$; (2) $g * \tilde O(y) = \tilde O(g * y)$ and $o(g * y) = o(y)$ for $g \in G_a$; (3) every $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \tilde O(y)$ and $t(\varphi) \in \tilde U(b)$, $b \in o(y)$, lies in $\hat O_{a,b}$. *Stronger*: the text asks (3) for $s(\varphi) \in \tilde O(y) \cap \tilde U(a)$; it holds without the intersection, at no cost.

*Proof*, the text's, in four steps.

0. *The domain.* $U'(a) = \tilde U'(a) \cap B$ is invariant under the natural action: $g * y$ is the target of $\Gamma(g, y)$, whose source $y$ lies in the saturated $B$.
1. *Finitely many $b$ near each orbit.* By local finiteness every orbit $p$ has an open $W(p) \ni p$ in $|X|$ meeting only finitely many $|\tilde V_b|$; let $F(p)$ be that finite set of $b$. Put $o(y) = F(|y|)$. It depends only on the orbit, so $o(g * y) = o(y)$, which is the second half of (2).
2. *Properness* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.exists_nhds_of_isProperSubset⟧. For $b \in o(y)$: every morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = y$ and $t(\varphi) \in \operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b)$ lies in $\hat O_{a,b}$, because $y \in \tilde U'(a) \cap B$, $t(\varphi) \in \operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b) \subset \tilde U'(b)$, and $t(\varphi) \in B$ by saturation ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.IsSaturated.tgt_mem⟧. The general lemma: if $Q$ is proper, $S$ open, and every $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = y$, $t(\varphi) \in Q$ lies in $S$, then the same holds for all $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi)$ in an open $W \ni y$. Its proof: the inverses of the bad morphisms, $\{\psi \in s^{-1}(Q) : \psi^{-1} \notin S\}$, form a closed subset $T$ of $s^{-1}(Q)$; by properness of $t$ on $s^{-1}(Q)$, $t(T)$ is closed; $y \notin t(T)$ by hypothesis; $W$ is the complement of $t(T)$. So each $b \in o(y)$ gives an open $W_b(y) \ni y$.
3. *$O_0(y)$.* $O_0(y) = \tilde U'(a) \cap \pi^{-1}(W(|y|)) \cap \bigcap_{b \in o(y)} W_b(y)$, a finite intersection of open sets containing $y$. It has (1), as $|O_0(y)| \subset W(|y|)$, and (3), by step 2 and $\tilde U(b) \subset \operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b)$.
4. *Symmetrization.* $\tilde O(y) = \bigcap_{g \in G_a}\{z \in \tilde U'(a) : g * z \in O_0(g * y)\}$. It is open (finite intersection, the actions continuous), contains $y$ (as $g * y \in O_0(g * y)$), lies in $O_0(y)$ (take $g = 1$), so keeps (1) and (3). For (2): $z \in \tilde O(y)$ iff $hz \in O_0(hy)$ for all $h$; then for $g * z$ and $g * y$, $h * (g * z) = (hg) * z \in O_0((hg) * y)$, so $g * \tilde O(y) \subset \tilde O(g * y)$, and the reverse inclusion is the same argument for $g^{-1}$, since $g^{-1} * (g * z) = z$ for the natural action.

*The $G_y$-invariance* ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_7_stab⟧: the text asks $\tilde O(y)$ to be $G_y$-invariant. It is read as invariance under the elements of $G_a$ fixing $y$, whose natural action near $y$ is that of $G_y$ (every morphism between points of $\tilde U'(a)$ is a $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$); by (2), $g * \tilde O(y) = \tilde O(g * y) = \tilde O(y)$ for such $g$.

The hypotheses of the setting are what the proof uses, named: $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b) \subset \tilde U'(b)$ and its properness come from (P6) (§XIV.12); $\hat O_{a,b}$ open with $U'(a, b) \subset \hat O_{a,b}$ is Proposition 14.3.4 (1); local finiteness is Lemma 14.3.6 (3); saturation of $\partial X$ is shown above.

### XIV.12 (P6) and Proposition 14.3.8 (2017: Proposition 14.4): the sets $\hat V_a$

**(P6)** ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds⟧, p. 653. Given (P5) neighbourhoods $\tilde U'(x)$, $x \in \partial X$, (P6) neighbourhoods are open $\tilde U(x) \ni x$ with (i) the natural $G_x$-action and the properness property, (ii) $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\tilde U(x)| \subset |\tilde U'(x)|$. *Reading*: "the natural $G_x$-action" is read as the restriction of that of $\tilde U'(x)$, the same representation with $\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$, so that the bi-actions and the sets $\hat O$ of §XIV.10 are the same for both. *The "obvious ramification"* ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds.closure_subset⟧: $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$. *Proof*: a point $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(x)$ has $|z| \in \operatorname{cl}|\tilde U(x)| \subset |\tilde U'(x)|$, so $z$ is isomorphic to a point of $\tilde U'(x)$; Lemma 13.1.1 (Part XIII), with the properness of $\tilde U'(x)$ from (P5) (i), says that a limit of points of $\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$ isomorphic to points of $\tilde U'(x)$ lies in $\tilde U'(x)$ itself. *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds.exists_⟧: for any (P5) data, without tameness: choose a closed neighbourhood $C$ of $x$ inside $\tilde U'(x)$ and an open neighbourhood with the properness property inside its interior (Proposition 7.1.10 and Corollary 7.1.17, Part VII), intersect over the finite group to make it invariant, and use Proposition 7.1.10 again for (ii).

Off $\partial X$ the neighbourhoods are extended by arbitrary natural neighbourhoods, irrelevant since $A \subset \partial X$; the sets $\hat O_{a,b}$ are extended by $\emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatObj⟧, so that the abstract lemmas, indexed by objects, apply.

**Proposition 14.3.8** (explicit), p. 656. *Abstract form* ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · EpGroupoid.proposition_14_3_8⟧. *Setting*: $B$ saturated; $\tilde U'(a)$, $\tilde U(a)$ natural neighbourhoods with the same representation, $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b) \subset \tilde U'(b)$ proper; $\tilde V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$ open and invariant, $(|\tilde V_a|)$ locally finite and covering $|B|$; $\hat O_{a,b}$ open with $U'(a, b) \subset \hat O_{a,b}$. *Statement*: the sets (14.32) $\hat V_a = (\bigcup_{y \in U'(a)}\tilde O(y)) \cap \tilde V_a$, with $\tilde O(y)$ from Lemma 14.3.7, satisfy (1) $\hat V_a$ open, $G_a$-invariant, $\hat V_a \subset \tilde V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$; (2) $\hat V_a \cap B = \tilde V_a \cap B$; (3) $(|\hat V_a|)$ a locally finite cover of $|B|$ by open subsets of $|X|$; (4) $\hat V_{a,a'} \subset \hat O_{a,a'}$, where $\hat V_{a,a'}$ is the set of morphisms from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_{a'}$. *Explicit*: the hypotheses are named.

*Proof.*

1. *(1).* $\hat V_a$ is a union of open sets intersected with an open set. Invariance: $g * \tilde O(y) = \tilde O(g * y)$ (Lemma 14.3.7 (2)) and $g * y \in U'(a)$, so the union is invariant, and $\tilde V_a$ is invariant.
2. *(2).* $\tilde U(a) \subset \tilde U'(a)$ (same representation and (P6)), so a point $y \in \tilde V_a \cap B$ lies in $U'(a)$ and in its own $\tilde O(y)$; hence $\tilde V_a \cap B \subset \hat V_a$.
3. *(3).* $|\hat V_a|$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8) and contained in $|\tilde V_a|$, so the family is locally finite; it covers $|B|$ because $(|\tilde V_a|)$ does and, by (2), $\hat V_a$ keeps the boundary points of $\tilde V_a$.
4. *(4)*, the text's argument. Let $\varphi$ go from $z \in \hat V_a$ to $z' \in \hat V_{a'}$, and $z \in \tilde O(y)$, $y \in U'(a)$. Then $|z| = |z'| \in |\tilde O(y)| \cap |\tilde V_{a'}|$, so $a' \in o(y)$ by Lemma 14.3.7 (1); and $t(\varphi) = z' \in \tilde V_{a'} \subset \tilde U(a')$, so $\varphi \in \hat O_{a,a'}$ by Lemma 14.3.7 (3). This is where the strengthening of (3) is convenient: $s(\varphi) \in \tilde O(y)$ suffices.

*Instantiated* ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.proposition_14_3_8⟧: for a representative with (P1)–(P4), (P5) neighbourhoods, the extension of Lemma 14.3.1, (P6) neighbourhoods, and $|X|$ paracompact, there are $A \subset \partial X$, $\tilde V_a$ with the conclusions of Lemma 14.3.6, and $\hat V_a$ with (1)–(4) for the $\hat O_{a,a'}$ of Definition 14.3.2. Every hypothesis of the abstract form is discharged: saturation of $\partial X$; closedness of $|\partial X|$; the closure and properness conditions by (P6); $U'(a, b) \subset \hat O_{a,b}$ by Proposition 14.3.4 (1). The text's summary (14.33)–(14.38) is contained in this statement.

**Definition 14.1.7 (a), (b) for $\hat\tau$ on $\hat V$.** §14.4 needs two properties of $\hat\tau$ on the sets $\hat V_a$, which Proposition 14.3.4 gives on $\hat O$: (b) $\hat\tau_{a,a}(\Gamma(g, w)) = [I_a \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_a \xrightarrow{g} I_a]$ for $w \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_Γ_of_VHat⟧, since $\Gamma(g, w)$ is a morphism of $\hat V_{a,a} \subset \hat O_{a,a}$ by (4) and invariance; and (a) $\hat\tau_{a',a}(\varphi) = \hat\tau_{a,a'}(\varphi^{-1})^\sharp$ on $\hat V_{a',a}$ ⟦Chapter14/CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_inv_of_VHat⟧, from step 7 of Proposition 14.3.4. They are the conditions *diag* and *swap* of the setting of §XIV.13.

### XIV.13 Remark 14.4.1 and the setting of §14.4 (2017: Remark 14.5, (14.33)–(14.38)): from the objects of §14.3

§14.4 works with the objects of §14.3 through a short list of their properties, (14.33)–(14.38). The formalization does the same: the results of §14.4 are proved in an abstract setting that carries exactly those properties, and the objects of §14.3 are then shown to form an instance of it. **Remark 14.4.1** (2017: Remark 14.5), p. 657, explains the plan of the section (the local extension near $\partial X$ must respect the identifications of indices forced by loops of morphisms) and has nothing to prove.

**The combinatorial setting** ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup⟧, p. 659: an index set $A$ of objects; for $a \in A$ an open neighbourhood $\tilde U(a)$ with the natural $G_a$-action, a $G_a$-invariant set $\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, and a finite index set $I_a$ with a $G_a$-action; and maps $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ from morphisms to correspondences $J(a, a')$ with two properties: *diag*, $\hat\tau_{a,a}(\Gamma(g, w)) = [I_a \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_a \xrightarrow{g} I_a]$ for $w \in \hat V_a$, and *swap*, $\hat\tau_{a',a}(\varphi) = \hat\tau_{a,a'}(\varphi^{-1})^\sharp$ for $\varphi$ from $\hat V_{a'}$ to $\hat V_a$. These are Definition 14.1.7 (a), (b) for the extended correspondences; the text uses them in the proof of Lemma 14.4.5 without naming them. *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.trivialSetup⟧: every ep-groupoid, with $A$ all objects, $\hat V_a = \tilde U(a)$ a neighbourhood with the natural action (Theorem 7.1.13, Part VII), one-point index sets and constant $\hat\tau$.

**The setting with topology** ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData⟧, pp. 657–664: the combinatorial setting together with the three facts of §14.3 that §14.4 uses: the $\hat V_a$ are open (Proposition 14.3.8 (1)); $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, which is (14.33); and $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ is locally constant at every morphism from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_{a'}$ (Proposition 14.3.4 through Proposition 14.3.8 (4)). *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.trivial⟧: the trivial setting with smaller $\hat V_a$, $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$ (two natural neighbourhoods one inside the other with the same action, by Proposition 7.1.10 and Theorem 7.1.13); in it every $a$ lies in its $\hat V_a$ and $i \sim_a i$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.trivial_zRel⟧.

**The boundary sections** ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZSections⟧, p. 665: over a setting with topology, sections $s^{0a}_i$, $i \in I_a$, with $P(s^{0a}_i(y)) = y$ and (14.45), $s^{0a}_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_i(y))$, on $U(a) = \tilde U(a) \cap \partial X$, and Definition 14.1.7 (4) for $\hat\tau$: $s^{0a'}_j(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, s^{0a}_i(s(\varphi)))$ whenever $(i, j)$ is a pair of $\hat\tau_{a,a'}(\varphi)$ and $\varphi$ is a morphism from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_{a'}$ with source in $\partial X$ (there $\hat\tau = \tau^0$). A morphism has source in $\partial X$ iff its target is ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.tgt_mem_boundary_iff_z4⟧, so such a $\varphi$ is a boundary morphism. *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZSections.zero⟧: the zero sections over the trivial setting.

**The objects of §14.3** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete⟧: for a tuple $T$ with (P4), (P5) neighbourhoods, an extension $E$ of the correspondences (Lemma 14.3.1) and (P6) neighbourhoods, the data of Proposition 14.3.8: the set $A \subset \partial X$, the sets $\tilde V_a$ with the conclusions of Lemma 14.3.6, the sets $\hat V_a$ with (1)–(4) of Proposition 14.3.8, and a base point $x_0 \in \partial X$ that fixes irrelevant values off $\partial X$. They exist when $|X|$ is paracompact and $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.exists_⟧, by the instantiated Proposition 14.3.8 (§XIV.12); the whole chain from (P4) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.exists_zConcrete_of_hasP4⟧: (P5) from the good system of $T$ (§XIV.9), the extension from Lemma 14.3.1, (P6) from its witness, and the data from Proposition 14.3.8; and for tame $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact and a boundary point, from the zero tuple with (P4) by Proposition 14.2.3 ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.exists_zConcrete_of_tame⟧, a nonvacuity check.

*Index transport.* The objects of §14.3 are indexed by boundary points (a subtype of the objects), those of §14.4 by objects. A retraction $r$ of the objects onto $\partial X$, the identity on $\partial X$ and $x_0$ elsewhere ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.bdryRetr_z5⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.bdryRetr_z5_of_mem⟧, with the homomorphism $G_a \to G_{r(a)}$ that is the identity on morphisms for $a \in \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.isoRetr_z5⟧, carries the index sets, actions and correspondences over without casts; the natural action at $r(a)$ through this homomorphism is that at $a$, and $[\mathrm{id}, g]$ is unchanged by the relabelling. The base point only fixes values at objects off $\partial X$, where no $a \in A$ lies.

*The instance.* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.toZData⟧: $\tilde U(a)$ the (P6) neighbourhood, $\hat V_a$ from Proposition 14.3.8, $I_a$ the index set of $T$ at $a$, and $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ the extended correspondence of Definition 14.3.2. Every field is a proved property: *diag* and *swap* are the last two properties of §XIV.12; $\hat V_a$ open and invariant is Proposition 14.3.8 (1); local constancy of $\hat\tau$ at the morphisms of $\hat V_{a,a'}$ is Proposition 14.3.4 with $\hat V_{a,a'} \subset \hat O_{a,a'}$; and $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.closure_Vh_subset⟧ comes from $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\tilde V_a| \subset |\tilde U(a)|$ (Lemma 14.3.6 (1)), Lemma 13.1.1 (Part XIII) and the properness of $\tilde U(a)$, exactly as the text derives (14.33). *The boundary sections* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.toZSections⟧ are those of $T$: (14.45) is Definition 14.1.3 (2); Definition 14.1.7 (4) for $\hat\tau$ along the boundary morphisms ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.compatNbhd⟧ holds because $\hat\tau = \tau^0$ on the boundary morphisms (Proposition 14.3.4 (3)) and $\tilde U(a) \cap \partial X \subset U^0(a)$, where the tuple's sections live. A pair of a correspondence satisfies every condition the correspondence satisfies, which is how Definition 14.1.7 (4), stated for all representatives, applies to a pair. *The facts used by the limit argument* (§XIV.16) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.toLimit⟧: the sets $\hat O_{b,c}$, which contain the boundary morphisms from $\tilde U(b)$ to $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(c)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.morBetween_subset_Ohat⟧ (since $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(c) \subset \tilde U'(c)$ by (P6) and $U'(b, c) \subset \hat O_{b,c}$); the properness of $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.isProper⟧; and the local finiteness of Proposition 14.3.8 (3).

*Verdict*: explicit. The setting is the text's; the identification of objects with boundary points and the three facts are named.

### XIV.14 Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4 and Lemma 14.4.5 (2017: Definitions 14.5–14.7, Lemma 14.6): z-loops and the relations $\sim_z$

**Pairs of a correspondence** ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.Pairs⟧: for a correspondence $\tau = [I \xleftarrow{\alpha} K \xrightarrow{\beta} I']$, $(i, j)$ is a pair if $(i, j) = (\alpha(k), \beta(k))$ for some $k$; this does not depend on the representative, since equivalent representatives differ by a bijection of $K$. The pairs of $\tau^\sharp$ are the reversed pairs of $\tau$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.pairs_swap⟧, and the pairs of $[\mathrm{id}, g]$ are the $(i, g(i))$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.pairs_ofPerm⟧.

**Definitions 14.4.2 and 14.4.3** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc⟧, pp. 659–660. The text: for $a \in A$ and $z \in \hat V_a$, a z-loop is a sequence $a = a_0, \dots, a_n = a$ in $A$ with composable morphisms $\varphi_j$ from $\hat V_{a_j}$ to $\hat V_{a_{j+1}}$, $s(\varphi_0) = z$, composing to $1_z$; a z-arc along it is a sequence of indices $i_j \in I_{a_j}$ with each $(i_j, i_{j+1})$ of the form $(\alpha_j(k_j), \beta_j(k_j))$ for a representative of $\hat\tau_{a_j,a_{j+1}}(\varphi_j)$. *As formalized*, loop and arc are one inductive predicate $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$: "there are $a = a_0, \dots, a_m = b$ in $A$, composable morphisms through the $\hat V_{a_j}$ with composite $\varphi$, and indices $i = i_0, \dots, i_m = j$ with $(i_j, i_{j+1})$ a pair of $\hat\tau_{a_j,a_{j+1}}(\varphi_j)$". It is generated by two rules: *start*, $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i, 1_z)$ for $a \in A$, $z \in \hat V_a$; and *append*, from $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$, a morphism $\psi$ with $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, $t(\psi) \in \hat V_c$, $c \in A$, and a pair $(j, k)$ of $\hat\tau_{b,c}(\psi)$, conclude $\mathrm{Arc}(a, c, i, k, \psi \circ \varphi)$. A z-loop with a z-arc from $i$ to $i'$ is $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i', 1_z)$: the composite $1_z$ fixes the start and the end at $z$. Every arc has $a, b \in A$, $s(\varphi) \in \hat V_a$ and $t(\varphi) \in \hat V_b$, by induction. *Restated*: the text's loop is a sequence and the arc a further sequence along it; the predicate records only what the later proofs use, the composite and the end indices.

*Concatenation* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc.trans⟧: from $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ and $\mathrm{Arc}(b, c, j, k, \psi)$ with $s(\psi) = t(\varphi)$, $\mathrm{Arc}(a, c, i, k, \psi \circ \varphi)$. *Proof*: induction on the second arc; its start $1_{t(\varphi)}$ composes to $\varphi$, and each appended step is appended to the concatenation, by associativity. *Reversal* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc.symm⟧: from $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$, $\mathrm{Arc}(b, a, j, i, \varphi^{-1})$. *Proof*: induction; for an appended step $\psi$ with pair $(j, k)$ of $\hat\tau_{b,c}(\psi)$, the reversed chain starts with $\psi^{-1}$ from $\hat V_c$ to $\hat V_b$, whose correspondence is $\hat\tau_{c,b}(\psi^{-1}) = \hat\tau_{b,c}(\psi)^\sharp$ by *swap*, with the reversed pair $(k, j)$; it is followed by the reversal of the rest, and $(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1} = \varphi^{-1} \circ \psi^{-1}$.

**Definition 14.4.4** (same) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.ZRel⟧, p. 660: $i \sim_z i'$ if there is a z-loop for $a$ with a z-arc from $i$ to $i'$, that is, $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i', 1_z)$; the class (14.43) is $[i]_{\sim_z} = \{i' : i' \sim_z i\}$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zClass⟧. $i \sim_z i'$ forces $z \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.ZRel.mem_V⟧. *$\sim_z$ is an equivalence relation* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_equivalence⟧ for $a \in A$, $z \in \hat V_a$, as the text calls it without proof: reflexivity is the start rule; symmetry is reversal, $1_z^{-1} = 1_z$; transitivity is concatenation, $1_z \circ 1_z = 1_z$.

*Loops of length zero.* The start rule gives loops with no morphism, which the text does not list. They add nothing ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_iff_unit_step⟧: $i \sim_z i'$ iff a loop with at least one step relates them. *Proof*: append the step $1_z = \Gamma(1, z)$ from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_a$, whose correspondence is $[\mathrm{id}, 1] = [\mathrm{id}]$ by *diag*, with pairs $(i', i')$; conversely a loop with a last step is a loop.

**Lemma 14.4.5** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.lemma_14_4_5⟧, p. 660. *Statement*: for $a \in A$, $z \in \hat V_a$, $i, i' \in I_a$ and $g \in G_a$, $i \sim_z i'$ iff $g(i) \sim_{g*z} g(i')$; hence $[g(i)]_{\sim_{g*z}} = g([i]_{\sim_z})$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.lemma_14_4_5_class⟧. *Explicit*: *diag* is a hypothesis of the setting. *Proof*, the text's ⟦Chapter14/ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_smul⟧. Let $w = g * z$, which lies in $\hat V_a$ by invariance.

1. *The first step.* $\Gamma(g^{-1}, w)$ is a morphism from $w$ to $g^{-1} * w = z$, between points of $\hat V_a$, with correspondence $[\mathrm{id}, g^{-1}]$ by *diag*; its pairs are $(k, g^{-1}(k))$, so $(g(i), i)$ is one. Start at $w$ with index $g(i)$ and append this step: $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, g(i), i, \Gamma(g^{-1}, w))$.
2. *The loop.* Concatenate the given $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i', 1_z)$: the composite is $\Gamma(g^{-1}, w)$ again.
3. *The last step.* Append $\Gamma(g, z)$ from $z$ to $w$, correspondence $[\mathrm{id}, g]$, pair $(i', g(i'))$. The composite is $\Gamma(g, z) \circ \Gamma(g^{-1}, w) = 1_w$, by the functoriality of the natural representation ($\Gamma(g, g^{-1} * w) \circ \Gamma(g^{-1}, w) = \Gamma(gg^{-1}, w)$). So $g(i) \sim_w g(i')$.
4. *The converse* applies this to $g^{-1}$ and $w$: $g^{-1}(g(i)) = i$, $g^{-1} * w = z$. The class identity follows from the equivalence at each $i'$.

### XIV.15 Proposition 14.4.6 (1) and Lemma 14.4.7 (2017: Proposition 14.5 (1), Lemma 14.7): deforming z-loops

**Proposition 14.4.6 (1)** (same) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.proposition_14_4_6_1⟧, p. 661. *Statement*: if $i \sim_{z_0} i'$, then $i \sim_z i'$ for all $z$ near $z_0$ (all of them in $\hat V_a$). Open-set form ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.proposition_14_4_6_1_open⟧: an open $O \ni z_0$, $O \subset \hat V_a$, with $i \sim_z i'$ on $O$. Class form ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.eventually_zClass_subset⟧: $[i]_{\sim_{z_0}} \subset [i]_{\sim_z}$ for $z$ near $z_0$, because $I_a$ is finite and finitely many "eventually" statements hold together.

*The text's proof* moves the morphisms of a $z_0$-loop along with $z$, using the finite natural representation of Lemma 14.4.7, and concludes by the local constancy of $\hat\tau$. *The Lean proof* moves them along sheets (Definition 7.1.4, Part VII), the open sets of morphisms on which $s$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto an open set, and does not need Lemma 14.4.7.

*Sheets.* For a sheet $\mathbf U$, the local inverse $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ is defined on the open set $s(\mathbf U)$ and continuous; $\mathbf U$ is open; $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(s(\varphi)) = \varphi$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf U$; and $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z) \to \varphi$ as $z \to s(\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.Sheet.tendsto_srcInv⟧. If $1_x \in \mathbf U$, then $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z) = 1_z$ for $z$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.Sheet.eventually_srcInv_eq_unit⟧: the unit map is continuous, so $1_z \in \mathbf U$ for $z$ near $x$, and $1_z$ has source $z$, where $s|\mathbf U$ is injective. Composition is continuous along composable pairs ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.tendsto_comp_of_eventually⟧: if $a_n \to a_0$, $b_n \to b_0$ and $a_n, b_n$ are eventually composable, then $a_n \circ b_n \to a_0 \circ b_0$, since the multiplication is continuous on the fibre product, which carries the subspace topology.

*Key step* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopDeform · EpGroupoid.ZData.Arc.eventually_srcInv⟧: if $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ and $\mathbf U \ni \varphi$ is a sheet, then $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, (s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z))$ for all $z$ near $s(\varphi)$. *Proof*, by induction on the arc.

1. *Start*: $\varphi = 1_{z_0}$, $z_0 \in \hat V_a$. For $z$ near $z_0$, $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z) = 1_z$ and $z \in \hat V_a$ ($\hat V_a$ open), so the start rule applies at $z$.
2. *Append*: $\varphi = \psi \circ \varphi_1$ with $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b', i, j', \varphi_1)$, $s(\psi) = t(\varphi_1)$, $t(\psi) \in \hat V_b$, $(j', j)$ a pair of $\hat\tau_{b',b}(\psi)$. Choose sheets $\mathbf U_1 \ni \varphi_1$ and $\mathbf U_2 \ni \psi$ (sheets cover the morphisms, $s$ being a local sc-diffeomorphism). For $z$ near $s(\varphi_1) = s(\varphi)$: $\varphi_1' = (s|\mathbf U_1)^{-1}(z)$ carries an arc from $i$ to $j'$, by induction, and is near $\varphi_1$; so $t(\varphi_1')$ is near $s(\psi)$ and $\psi' = (s|\mathbf U_2)^{-1}(t(\varphi_1'))$ is defined and near $\psi$.
3. *The step survives*: $t(\psi') \in \hat V_b$ for $\psi'$ near $\psi$ ($\hat V_b$ open, $t$ continuous); $\psi$ is a morphism from $\hat V_{b'}$ to $\hat V_b$ (its source is $t(\varphi_1) \in \hat V_{b'}$), where $\hat\tau_{b',b}$ is locally constant, so $\hat\tau_{b',b}(\psi') = \hat\tau_{b',b}(\psi)$ and $(j', j)$ is still a pair. Hence $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \psi' \circ \varphi_1')$.
4. *Identification*: $\psi' \circ \varphi_1' \to \psi \circ \varphi_1 = \varphi$ by continuity of composition, so it eventually lies in the open sheet $\mathbf U$; it has source $z$, so it equals $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z)$.

*Proof of (1).* $i \sim_{z_0} i'$ is $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i', 1_{z_0})$. Take a sheet $\mathbf U \ni 1_{z_0}$: by the key step, $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i', (s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z))$ for $z$ near $z_0$, and $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z) = 1_z$ for $z$ near $z_0$. So $i \sim_z i'$.

**Lemma 14.4.7** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_4_7⟧, pp. 661–662. The text restates Proposition 7.1.15 and Corollary 7.1.17 (Part VII) for a finite set $Y$ of isomorphic objects and open $Q(x) \ni x$. Part VII has the proposition as a structure (a natural representation of $Y$ inside one open set): open, connected, mutually disjoint $O(x)$, $x \in Y$, a functor $f$ from the morphisms between points of $Y$ to sc-diffeomorphisms $f(\psi) : O(s(\psi)) \to O(t(\psi))$, the morphisms between points of $O = \bigcup O(x)$ the disjoint union of components $\mathbf O(\psi)$, and items (1)–(3). The lemma adds:

1. *Per-object neighbourhoods and (7)* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRepFinite_subset⟧: $O(x) \subset Q(x)$, and each $\operatorname{cl}O(x)$ proper. *Proof*: choose pairwise disjoint open neighbourhoods of the finitely many points of $Y$ inside the $Q(x)$ with the properness property (Hausdorff, Corollary 7.1.17), apply Proposition 7.1.15 inside their union, and note that the connected $O(x) \ni x$ lies in the member containing $x$.
2. *(4)* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_isotropy⟧: for $g \in G_x$, $f(g)(z) = t(\Gamma(g, z)) = g * z$, with a natural representation of $G_x$ on $O(x)$: the restriction of the representation to the isotropy group is one.
3. *(5)* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_equivariant⟧: $f(\varphi)(g * z) = \gamma_\varphi(g) * f(\varphi)(z)$ with $\gamma_\varphi(g) = \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$: functoriality, $f(\varphi) \circ f(g) = f(\varphi g) = f(\gamma_\varphi(g) \varphi) = f(\gamma_\varphi(g)) \circ f(\varphi)$.
