4. *(6)*: the multiplication $\mathbf O(\psi) \times_{s,t} \mathbf O(\varphi) \to \mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi)$. *The key identity* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.comp_srcInv_eq⟧: for $\varphi' \in \mathbf O(\varphi)$, $(s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(t(\varphi')) \circ \varphi' = (s|\mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1}(s(\varphi'))$. *Proof* by connectedness: the map $\varphi' \mapsto (s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(t(\varphi')) \circ \varphi'$ is continuous on the connected $\mathbf O(\varphi)$ and takes $\varphi$ to $\psi \circ \varphi$; its image is connected and consists of morphisms between points of $O$, so it lies in one component, $\mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi)$; there $s$ is injective. *Bijection* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.bijOn_comp⟧: every pair $(\psi', \varphi')$ of the fibre product has $\psi' = (s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(t(\varphi'))$, so $m(\psi', \varphi') = (s|\mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1}(s(\varphi'))$, injective in $\varphi'$; surjectivity uses the inverse $\chi \mapsto (\ldots, (s|\mathbf O(\varphi))^{-1}(s(\chi)))$. *sc-diffeomorphism* ⟦Chapter14/FiniteRepresentation · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_comp⟧: parametrizing the fibre product by its second factor, the multiplication is $(s|\mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1} \circ s : \mathbf O(\varphi) \to \mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi)$, with inverse $(s|\mathbf O(\varphi))^{-1} \circ s$, both composites of sc-diffeomorphisms. *Restated*: the text's fibre product is an M-polyfold; the parametrization by the second factor avoids building that structure.

Lemma 14.4.7 is not used by the proof of Proposition 14.4.6 (1) above; it is used by the proof of (2) (§XIV.16).

### XIV.16 Proposition 14.4.6 (2) (2017: Proposition 14.5 (2)): limits of z-loops

**Transport along chains.** Over boundary sections (§XIV.13), the sections are transported along every arc that starts in $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZSections.arc_transport⟧: from $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ with $s(\varphi) \in \partial X$, $s^{0b}_j(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, s^{0a}_i(s(\varphi)))$. *Proof* by induction: at the start $\mu(1_z, w) = w$; for an appended $\psi$ with pair $(j', j)$ of $\hat\tau(\psi)$, the source $t(\varphi_1)$ of $\psi$ is in $\partial X$ by saturation, so Definition 14.1.7 (4) for $\hat\tau$ gives $s_j(t\psi) = \mu(\psi, s_{j'}(s\psi))$, and $\mu(\psi, \mu(\varphi_1, \cdot)) = \mu(\psi \circ \varphi_1, \cdot)$ (Definition 8.3.5, Part VIII). For a loop, $\varphi = 1_z$: if $i \sim_z i'$ with $z \in V_a = \hat V_a \cap \partial X$, then $s^{0a}_{i'}(z) = s^{0a}_i(z)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZSections.zRel_sections_eq⟧.

**Proposition 14.4.6 (2) at points of $V_a$** ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZSections.proposition_14_4_6_2_of_mem⟧: if $z_0 \in V_a$ and $i \sim_{z_0} i'$, then $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on a neighbourhood of $z_0$ in $\partial X$. *Proof*: by (1), $i \sim_z i'$ for $z$ near $z_0$, and at those $z$ in $\partial X$ the transport gives the equality.

**Proposition 14.4.6 (2)** (same, and stronger), p. 661. *The printed form* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_6_2_statement⟧: if $z_k \in V_a$, $i \sim_{z_k} i'$ and $z_k \to z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, then $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on a neighbourhood of $z_0$ in $U(a)$. The sequences are read as closure: $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}\{y \in V_a : i \sim_y i'\}$. *The form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.HasThetaLocalEq⟧: for $(i, i') \in \Theta_{z_0}$ (Definition 14.4.8, §XIV.17), that is, $z_k \in \hat V_a$, and $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, the same conclusion. It implies the printed form ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.HasThetaLocalEq.proposition_14_4_6_2⟧, since $V_a \subset \hat V_a$. *A reading*: Lemma 14.4.9 (3) cites (2) for the pairs of $\Theta_z$, whose sequences lie in $\hat V_a$, while (2) is printed for $z_k \in V_a$. The text's proof works for $z_k \in \hat V_a$, and that is the form proved.

*The setting of the proof* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting⟧, the facts of §14.3 it uses beyond the setting with topology: open sets $M_{b,c}$ of morphisms (the $\hat O_{b,c}$ of Proposition 14.3.4) on which $\hat\tau_{b,c}$ is locally constant and which contain every boundary morphism from $\tilde U(b)$ to $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(c)$; the properness of $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b)$ ((P6)); and the local finiteness of $(|\hat V_b|)_{b \in A}$ (Proposition 14.3.8 (3)). And Definition 14.1.7 (4) for $\hat\tau$ along the boundary morphisms from $\tilde U(b)$ to $\tilde U(c)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZSections.CompatNbhd⟧, slightly more than along those of $\hat V_{b,c}$, since the limit loop runs through the closures. All of these hold for the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.13).

*The general statement* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.sections_eq_of_theta_closure⟧ (stronger): for every $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ and $(i, i') \in \Theta_{z_0}$, $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on a neighbourhood of $z_0$ in $\partial X$. From it, the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.hasThetaLocalEq_of_limit⟧ ($\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a) \subset \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$, $\partial X$ being closed) and the printed form ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_6_2_of_limit⟧. *Stronger*: $z_k \in \hat V_a$ instead of $V_a$, and every $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ instead of $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$.

*Proof*, the text's, in Lean's order.

1. *The finite representation at $z_0$* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_limitRep⟧ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep⟧. (a) By local finiteness, a neighbourhood of $|z_0|$ meets only the $|\hat V_b|$ with $b$ in a finite set $o \subset A$. (b) $K = \bigcup_{b \in o}\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_b$ lies in the proper set $\bigcup_{b \in o}\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(b)$, a finite union of proper sets; so only finitely many objects of $K$ are isomorphic to $z_0$ (Lemma 7.1.11, Part VII); let $Y \ni z_0$ be that finite set. (c) For $y \in Y$ choose neighbourhoods $Q(y)$: for each pair $b, c \in o$ with $y \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_b \cap \partial X$, inside $\tilde U(b)$ and with every morphism from $Q(y)$ into $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(c)$ in $M_{b,c}$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_nbhd_near⟧ (by the properness step of Lemma 14.3.7, §XIV.11, since at $y$ itself all such morphisms are boundary morphisms from $\tilde U(b)$ to $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(c)$, which lie in $M_{b,c}$); for each $b \in o$ with $y \notin \operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$, disjoint from $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_nbhd_yb⟧; and the intersection over the finitely many conditions. (d) Lemma 14.4.7 on $Y$ inside the $Q(y)$ gives the sheets $\mathbf O(\psi)$. (e) Properness of $K$ gives a neighbourhood $W \subset O(z_0)$ of $z_0$ such that every morphism from $W$ into a $\hat V_c$ has $c \in o$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.mem_o_of_mem_W⟧ and ends in $\bigcup_y O(y)$: otherwise morphisms with sources tending to $z_0$ and targets in $K$ outside $\bigcup O(y)$ would have a convergent subsequence, with limit a morphism from $z_0$ to a point of $K$ isomorphic to $z_0$, so a point of $Y$, inside the open $O(y)$.
2. *Sheets and correspondences.* The morphisms between points of the $O(y)$ lie in sheets, and the sheet containing a given morphism is unique ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.eq_of_mem_sheet_z5⟧ (the sheets are disjoint components). For a morphism $\omega : y \to y'$ of $Y$ with $y \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$, $y' \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_c$, the sheet $\mathbf O(\omega)$ lies in $M_{b,c}$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.sheet_subset_M⟧, by the choice of $Q(y)$ (its morphisms go into $O(y') \subset \tilde U(c)$). A map locally constant at every point of a set is constant on every preconnected subset ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · EpGroupoid.eq_of_isPreconnected_z5⟧, so $\hat\tau_{b,c}$ is constant on the connected sheet $\mathbf O(\omega)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.tau_eq⟧.
3. *The limit loop* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.arc_transport⟧. Claim: for an arc $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ with $s(\varphi) \in W$ and $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$, there is a morphism $\psi : z_0 \to y$ of $Y$ with $y \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ and $\varphi \in \mathbf O(\psi)$, and along the deformed morphisms $(s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(y')$, $y' \in O(z_0) \cap \partial X$, the sections are transported: $s^{0b}_j(t((s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(y'))) = \mu((s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(y'), s^{0a}_i(y'))$. *Proof* by induction. At the start, $\varphi = 1_z$ with $z \in W \subset O(z_0)$ lies in the sheet of $1_{z_0}$, and the deformed morphisms are units. For an appended step $\chi$ (from $\hat V_{b'}$ to $\hat V_b$, pair $(j', j)$): by induction $\varphi_1 \in \mathbf O(\psi_1)$, $\psi_1 : z_0 \to y_1$; $\chi$ starts at $t(\varphi_1) \in O(y_1)$ and ends in $\hat V_b$, and the source of $\chi \circ \varphi_1$ is in $W$, so by 1 (e) it ends in some $O(y)$ and lies in a sheet $\mathbf O(\omega)$, $\omega : y_1 \to y$, with $y \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ (since $O(y)$ meets $\hat V_b$, and $O(y)$ misses the closures not containing $y$). By Lemma 14.4.7 (6), $\chi \circ \varphi_1 \in \mathbf O(\omega \circ \psi_1)$; put $\psi = \omega \circ \psi_1$. For $y' \in O(z_0) \cap \partial X$, the deformed $(s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}(y')$ is the composite of the deformed $\varphi_1$ and the morphism of $\mathbf O(\omega)$ from its target (the key identity of Lemma 14.4.7 (6)); the latter is a boundary morphism from $\tilde U(b')$ to $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b)$, its correspondence is $\hat\tau_{b',b}(\chi)$ by step 2, so $(j', j)$ is a pair of it, and Definition 14.1.7 (4) along it, composed with the induction hypothesis, gives the transport.
4. *Conclusion* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimits · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.sections_eq⟧. Let $(i, i') \in \Theta_{z_0}$: there is $z \in W \cap \hat V_a$ with $i \sim_z i'$, an arc with composite $1_z$. By 3, $1_z \in \mathbf O(\psi)$ for a morphism $\psi$ from $z_0$; the unit $1_z$ lies in the sheet of $1_{z_0}$ too, so $\psi = 1_{z_0}$ by uniqueness of the sheet, and the deformed morphisms are the units $1_{y'}$. The transport gives $s^{0a}_{i'}(y') = s^{0a}_i(y')$ for $y' \in O(z_0) \cap \partial X$.

*How Lean departs from the text.* The text builds the limit $z_0$-loop (the limits of the morphisms of the $z_k$-loops, which exist by properness) and deforms it along $\partial X$. Here each step of one $z_k$-loop, $k$ large (a $z \in W$), is located in a sheet of the finite representation directly; the limit loop is the chain of sheet centres $\psi$, and the identity of its composite is read off from the sheet of the unit. The two arguments use the same facts. Gap G.168 is closed by this proof. For the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.13), where every fact of the setting is proved, both forms hold with no hypothesis beyond the text's data: the printed one ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.proposition_14_4_6_2⟧ and the one with $z_k \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.hasThetaLocalEq⟧.

### XIV.17 Definition 14.4.8 and Lemma 14.4.9 (2017: Definition 14.8, Lemma 14.8): the relations $\approx_z$ on the closure

At points of $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ outside $\hat V_a$ there are no z-loops; the relation $\approx_z$ records which indices are identified by loops at nearby points.

**Definition 14.4.8** (restated), p. 663. *$\Theta_z$* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.Theta⟧: $(i, i') \in \Theta_z$ if $z \in \operatorname{cl}\{y : i \sim_y i'\}$. The text asks for a sequence $z_k \in \hat V_a$ with $i \sim_{z_k} i'$ and $z_k \to z$; the closure is the same in a Fréchet–Urysohn space ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.theta_iff_seq⟧, for instance a metrizable one, which the object space is. *$\approx_z$* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.Approx⟧: the reflexive-transitive closure of $\Theta_z$, that is, $i \approx_z i'$ if there is a chain $i = i_0, \dots, i_k = i'$ with $(i_p, i_{p+1}) \in \Theta_z$ (the text's last index is printed $i_p = i'$; $i_k = i'$ is meant). (14.44): $[i]_{\approx_z} = \{i' : i' \approx_z i\}$ ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.approxClass⟧. *Restated*: closure in place of sequences, and the reflexive closure included, so that $\approx_z$ is reflexive also where $\Theta_z$ is empty (off $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$, where nothing is asked).

*$\approx_z$ is an equivalence relation* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.approx_equivalence⟧, as the text calls it. $\Theta_z$ is symmetric ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.theta_symm⟧, because $\sim_y$ is (§XIV.14); so the reflexive-transitive closure is symmetric (reverse the chain), and it is reflexive and transitive by construction. On $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, $\Theta_z$ is itself reflexive ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.theta_refl⟧: $i \sim_y i$ for every $y \in \hat V_a$, so $z \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_a = \operatorname{cl}\{y : i \sim_y i\}$.

**Lemma 14.4.9** (same; (3) stronger), pp. 663–664.

*(1)* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.lemma_14_4_9_1⟧: for $z \in \hat V_a$, $i \sim_z i'$ implies $i \approx_z i'$. *Proof*: by Proposition 14.4.6 (1), $i \sim_y i'$ for $y$ near $z$, so $z$ is in the closure of that set and $(i, i') \in \Theta_z$.

*(2)* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.lemma_14_4_9_2⟧: $i \approx_z i'$ implies $g(i) \approx_{g*z} g(i')$. *Proof*: for a single step ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.theta_smul⟧, the set $\{y : g(i) \sim_y g(i')\}$ contains $g * \{y : i \sim_y i'\}$ by Lemma 14.4.5, and $z \mapsto g * z$ is continuous on $\tilde U(a)$, which contains $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$ (14.33); so $g * z$ is in the closure of the image. Chains map to chains. *Classes* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.lemma_14_4_9_2_class⟧: $[g(i)]_{\approx_{g*z}} = g([i]_{\approx_z})$ for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$; the reverse inclusion applies (2) to $g^{-1}$ and uses $g^{-1} * (g * z) = z$, valid on $\tilde U(a) \supset \operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$.

*(4)* ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.lemma_14_4_9_4⟧: for $i \in I_a$ and $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ there is an open $\tilde Q(z_0) \ni z_0$ in $\tilde U(a)$ with $[i]_{\sim_z} \subset [i]_{\approx_{z_0}}$ for $z \in \hat V_a \cap \tilde Q(z_0)$. *Proof*: for each of the finitely many $i' \notin [i]_{\approx_{z_0}}$, $(i', i) \notin \Theta_{z_0}$ (as $\Theta_{z_0} \subset {\approx_{z_0}}$), so $z_0$ has an open neighbourhood missing $\{y : i' \sim_y i\}$. Intersect these with $\tilde U(a)$. At $z$ in the intersection, every $i' \sim_z i$ is in $[i]_{\approx_{z_0}}$. For all $i$ at once ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.ZData.lemma_14_4_9_4_all⟧, intersect over the finite $I_a$. The text argues by contradiction with sequences; this is the same argument with neighbourhoods.

*(3)*, p. 663: for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ and $i \approx_z i'$, $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $U(a)$ near $z$. *Proof*, the text's: chain Proposition 14.4.6 (2), in the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, along the steps of $\Theta_z$, intersecting the finitely many neighbourhoods. With that form as a hypothesis ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_9_3_hyp⟧, and, the form being proved (§XIV.16), unconditionally and for every $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_9_3_of_limit⟧, from the general statement of §XIV.16. *Stronger*: $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$, which contains $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$.

### XIV.18 Proposition 14.4.10, Definition 14.4.11 and Remark 14.4.12 (2017: Proposition 14.6, Definition 14.9, Remark 14.6): coherent neighbourhood systems

**The natural action on open sets.** For a natural neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ and $O \subset N$: $g * O = N \cap \Phi_{g^{-1}}^{-1}(O)$, so $g * O$ is open when $O$ is ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.isOpen_image_Φ⟧, and $(gh) * O = g * (h * O)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.image_Φ_mul⟧. The action preserves $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.Φ_mem_boundary_z4⟧ (the degeneracy index is invariant) and maps $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ and $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ into themselves ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.mapsTo_Φ_closure_z4⟧ (continuity on $\tilde U(a) \supset \operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$).

**Equivariant shrinking** ⟦Chapter14/ZRelationClosure · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.exists_equivariant_nbhds⟧, the step of Proposition 14.4.10 (2) the text leaves to the reader. *Statement*: let $C \subset N$ be $G_x$-invariant and $P(z, O)$ a property of neighbourhoods of $z \in C$ that passes to smaller sets and is carried along by the action ($P(z, O) \Rightarrow P(g * z, g * O)$); if every $z \in C$ has an open $O \ni z$ with $P(z, O)$, there are open $O(z) \ni z$, $O(z) \subset N$, with $P(z, O(z))$, $O(g * z) = g * O(z)$, and $O(z) \cap O(g * z) = \emptyset$ whenever $g * z \ne z$. *Proof.*

1. *At one point $w \in C$.* Start from $O$ with $P(w, O)$, intersected with $N$. The finitely many points $g * w \ne w$ are distinct from $w$; the object space is Hausdorff, so shrink $O$ so that $O \cap g * O = \emptyset$ for each such $g$ (choose $O$ inside a neighbourhood $U_g$ of $w$ with $U_g \cap g * U_g = \emptyset$, which exists by continuity of the action and $g * w \ne w$). Then intersect over the stabilizer: $O_w = \bigcap_{h * w = w} h * O$. It is open, contains $w$, is smaller than $O$ (so $P(w, O_w)$ and the separation persist), and is invariant under the stabilizer.
2. *Transport from orbit representatives.* Choose one $w$ in each $G_x$-orbit of $C$ and put $O(g * w) = g * O_w$. This is well defined: if $g * w = g' * w$, then $g^{-1}g'$ fixes $w$ and $g' * O_w = g * (g^{-1}g') * O_w = g * O_w$. $P$ holds by the equivariance of $P$; $O(h * z) = h * O(z)$ by construction.
3. *Separation.* If $z = h * w$ and $g * z \ne z$, then $k = h^{-1}gh$ moves $w$, so $O_w \cap k * O_w = \emptyset$; applying $h$, $O(z) \cap O(g * z) = \emptyset$.

**Proposition 14.4.10** (same) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_10_hyp⟧, p. 664. *Statement*: for $a \in A$, every $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ has an open $\tilde O(z) \ni z$ with (1) $\tilde O(z) \subset \tilde U(a)$; (2) $\tilde O(g * z) = g * \tilde O(z)$, and $\tilde O(z) \cap \tilde O(g * z) = \emptyset$ if $g * z \ne z$; (3) $[i]_{\sim_y} \subset [i]_{\approx_z}$ for $y \in \tilde O(z) \cap \hat V_a$; (4) for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ and $i \approx_z i'$, $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $\tilde O(z) \cap U(a)$. *Proof.* The text calls it immediate from Lemma 14.4.9. Apply the equivariant shrinking with $C = \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ (invariant, inside $\tilde U(a)$ by (14.33)) and $P(z, O)$ the conjunction of (3) at $z$ and (4) at $z$.

1. *Existence at each $z$*: (3) holds on the $\tilde Q(z)$ of Lemma 14.4.9 (4) for all $i$; (4) holds on a neighbourhood by Lemma 14.4.9 (3), for each of the finitely many pairs $i \approx_z i'$; intersect.
2. *Shrinking*: both are statements about all points of $O$.
3. *Action*: (3) at $g * z$ on $g * O$: for $y \in O \cap \hat V_a$, $[i]_{\sim_{g*y}} = g([g^{-1}(i)]_{\sim_y}) \subset g([g^{-1}(i)]_{\approx_z}) = [i]_{\approx_{g*z}}$ by Lemma 14.4.5 and Lemma 14.4.9 (2), with $\hat V_a$ invariant. (4) at $g * z$: if $i \approx_{g*z} i'$, then $g^{-1}(i) \approx_z g^{-1}(i')$, so $s^{0a}_{g^{-1}(i)} = s^{0a}_{g^{-1}(i')}$ on $O \cap U(a)$; by (14.45), $s^{0a}_i(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_{g^{-1}(i)}(y))$, and the same for $i'$, so they agree on $g * (O \cap U(a)) = g * O \cap U(a)$, the action preserving $\partial X$.

The hypothesis of this form, Proposition 14.4.6 (2) with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, is used only in step 1 through Lemma 14.4.9 (3). Unconditionally ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_10_of_limit⟧, by §XIV.16; for the objects of §14.3, with no hypothesis beyond the text's data ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.proposition_14_4_10⟧.

**Definition 14.4.11** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZCoherentNbhdSystem⟧, p. 664. A coherent neighbourhood system for $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \subset \tilde U(a)$ (the 2017 text calls it a good neighbourhood system) is a family of open $\tilde O(z) \ni z$, $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, with (1), (2), (3) for $z \in \hat V_a$ as printed, and (4). *Existence*, "in view of Proposition 14.4.10": from the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_hyp⟧; unconditionally ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_of_limit⟧; for the objects of §14.3 ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem⟧. For the zero data the hypothesis holds trivially ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.hasThetaLocalEq_zero⟧, and a system exists ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_zero⟧.

*The abstract form used by Proposition 14.4.14.* The local extension is proved over data for one fixed $a$ ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.LocalExtensionBase⟧: $\tilde U(a)$ with the natural $G_a$-action, an open invariant $\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, a finite $I_a$ with a $G_a$-action, boundary sections face-wise sc⁺ on $U(a) = \tilde U(a) \cap \partial X$ with (14.45), relations $\sim_y$ with Lemma 14.4.5, and relations $\approx_z$ as parameters. Over them, a coherent neighbourhood system ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem⟧ has (1), (3) for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, and (4) as fields; (2) is a separate predicate ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.IsEquivariant⟧, since the proof of Proposition 14.4.14 below does not use it. *A reading*: (3) is printed for $z \in \hat V_a$; Proposition 14.4.10 (3) states it for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, and the proof of Proposition 14.4.14 uses it at points of the closure; we read $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, presumably what is meant. The data come from the setting of §XIV.13 ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.LocalExtensionBase.ofZSetup⟧, with $\sim_y$ the relation of Definition 14.4.4 and Lemma 14.4.5 discharged; and from the boundary sections ⟦Chapter14/ZDataLocalExtension · SBLocalization.ZSections.toLocalExtensionBase⟧, with $\approx_z$ that of Definition 14.4.8 and the face-wise sc⁺ condition of Definition 14.1.3 (1) as input. The system in this form, with (2), comes from Proposition 14.4.10 ⟦Chapter14/ZDataLocalExtension · SBLocalization.coherentNbhdSystem_hyp⟧, and unconditionally ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.coherentNbhdSystem_of_limit⟧. *Witness* of the abstract form at every boundary point of a tame $X$ ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.exists_coherentNbhdSystem_zero⟧: a good $V_0$ at $x$ contains a good $V$ with $\operatorname{cl}V \subset V_0$ (Lemma 14.2.1), and $\tilde U(x) = V_0$, $\hat V_x = V \ni x$ with zero sections, one index and trivial relations carry the system $\tilde O(z) = V_0$.

**Remark 14.4.12** (2017: Remark 14.6), p. 664, explains the meaning of the conditions (sections constant on the classes near $z$ can be extended compatibly) and has nothing to prove.

### XIV.19 Lemma 14.4.13 (2017: Lemma 14.9): the sections near an orbit

Fix a coherent neighbourhood system and $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ with orbit $[z] = G_a * z$. The text sets $\tilde O([z]) = \bigcup_{z' \in [z]}\tilde O(z')$, a disjoint union ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.ZCoherentNbhdSystem.disjoint_orbit⟧: distinct points of one orbit have disjoint neighbourhoods, by (2).

**Lemma 14.4.13** (narrower in (2)), p. 666. The $\approx_{z'}$-classes partition $I_a$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.approxClass_eq_or_disjoint⟧, $\approx_{z'}$ being an equivalence relation: two classes are equal or disjoint.

*(1)* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_1⟧: an element $g$ of the stabilizer $G_a(z')$ maps $[i]_{\approx_{z'}}$ onto $[g(i)]_{\approx_{z'}}$, so it permutes the classes. *Proof*: Lemma 14.4.9 (2) with $g * z' = z'$.

*(2)* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_2⟧: for $z' \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ and $g \in G_a(z')$ fixing the class $[i]_{\approx_{z'}}$, $s^{0a}_i(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_i(y))$ for $y \in \tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$. *Proof*: within one class the sections agree on $\tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_classSection⟧, by (4) of the system (the text recalls this as the definition of the sections $s^{z'}_j$ of the proof). $g(i)$ is in the class of $i$; by (14.45), $s^{0a}_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_i(y))$; and $g * y \in \tilde O(g * z') \cap \partial X = \tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$, where $s^{0a}_{g(i)} = s^{0a}_i$. *Narrower*: the text states (2) for every $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$. The proof uses Definition 14.4.11 (4), which covers only points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, and a point of $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ need not lie in $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$. Presumably $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ is meant; it is what Proposition 14.4.14 uses. The printed (2) at the other points would need a system with (4) there, which the stronger Lemma 14.4.9 (3) of §XIV.17 permits (about 90 lines, not done, not needed).

*(3)* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_3⟧: for $g \in G_a(z')$ and every $i$, $s^{0a}_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_i(y))$ for $y \in \tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$. This is (14.45) on $\tilde O(z') \cap \partial X \subset U(a)$; it relates the class of $i$ to the class $g([i]) = [g(i)]$ when they differ.

*(4)* ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopCoherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_4⟧: for $z'' = g * z'$, the sections over $\tilde O(z'') \cap \partial X$ are determined by those over $\tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$. *Proof*: every point of $\tilde O(z'') \cap \partial X = g * \tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$ is $g * y$ with $y \in \tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$, and there $s^{0a}_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_i(y))$ by (14.45).

The lemma serves the text's construction of Proposition 14.4.14 orbit by orbit. The Lean proof of Proposition 14.4.14 (§XIV.20) does not go orbit by orbit and uses none of (1)–(4); they are proved as printed (with the reading of (2)) for completeness.

### XIV.20 Proposition 14.4.14 (2017: Proposition 14.7): the local extension on $\hat V_a$

**Proposition 14.4.14** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14⟧, pp. 667–671. *Statement*: let every object lie in a tame strong bundle chart and let the object M-polyfold admit sc-smooth partitions of unity (the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4, §XIV.3). For the data of a fixed $a$ and a coherent neighbourhood system (abstract form, (1), (3), (4)) there are sc⁺-sections $\hat s^a_i$, $i \in I_a$, on $\hat V_a$ with $\hat s^a_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), \hat s^a_i(y))$ on $\hat V_a$, (1) $\hat s^a_i = s^{0a}_i$ on $V_a = \hat V_a \cap \partial X$, and (2) $\hat s^a_i(z) = \hat s^a_{i'}(z)$ whenever $i \sim_z i'$, $z \in \hat V_a$. *Restated*: "a local sc⁺ symmetric section structure on $\hat V_a$" is read as sc⁺-sections with the symmetry of Definition 13.2.5 (1) (Part XIII); the weights and the functor $\hat\Lambda_a$ are defined from them in §14.5.

*The text's proof* builds, on each $\tilde O([z])$, sections constant on the $\approx_{z'}$-classes and equivariant under $G_a$, class by class and orbit by orbit (using Lemma 14.4.13), and glues them with a $G_a$-invariant partition of unity subordinate to the $\tilde O([z])$. *The Lean proof* glues non-equivariant pieces with an ordinary partition of unity and then averages over $G_a$, as in Proposition 14.1.4.

1. *(4) for the equivalence closure* ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.eqvGen_s0⟧: for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, if $i$ and $i'$ are related by the equivalence relation generated by $\approx_z$, then $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $\tilde O(z) \cap U(a)$; equality is an equivalence relation, so (4) passes to the generated one. Thus $\approx_z$ need not be an equivalence relation for this proof.
2. *Local pieces* ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.exists_local_piece⟧: every object $y$ has an open $U \ni y$ with sc⁺-sections $\sigma_i$ of $P$ that equal $s^{0a}_i$ on $U \cap \hat V_a \cap \partial X$ and are constant on the $\sim_z$-classes at every $z \in U \cap \hat V_a$. Three cases.
   (a) $y \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$. Take an open $G \ni y$ with $\operatorname{cl}G \subset \tilde O(y)$ (regularity). Choose a representative $r(i)$ of the class of each $i$ under the equivalence relation generated by $\approx_y$. The section $s^{0a}_{r(i)}$ is face-wise sc⁺ on $\tilde O(y) \cap U(a)$, so it has an sc⁺ extension $\bar s_{r(i)}$ equal to it on $G \cap \partial X$ (the partition-of-unity step of Proposition 14.1.4, §XIV.3). Put $U = G$ and $\sigma_i = \bar s_{r(i)}$. On $G \cap \hat V_a \cap \partial X$, $\sigma_i = s^{0a}_{r(i)} = s^{0a}_i$ by step 1. At $z \in G \cap \hat V_a$, $i \sim_z i'$ implies $i' \in [i]_{\approx_y}$ by (3), so $r(i) = r(i')$ and $\sigma_i = \sigma_{i'}$.
   (b) $y \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \setminus \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$. $U = \tilde O(y) \setminus \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, $\sigma_i = 0$. $U \cap \hat V_a \cap \partial X \subset U \cap V_a = \emptyset$, so nothing is to be matched, and zero sections are constant on every class.
   (c) $y \notin \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$. $U$ the complement of $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$, $\sigma_i = 0$; nothing is asked.
3. *Gluing.* Choose an sc-smooth partition of unity $(\rho_k)$ subordinate to the cover by the sets $U$ of step 2, and put $\sigma_i = \sum_k \rho_k\sigma^k_i$, an sc⁺-section (a locally finite sum of products of sc-smooth functions with sc⁺-sections). On $\hat V_a \cap \partial X$ each piece with $\rho_k \ne 0$ equals $s^{0a}_i$, so the sum does. A glued section takes equal values for $i$, $i'$ wherever every piece with non-zero weight does ⟦Chapter14/CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.glueSection_congr_at⟧; so $\sigma_i(z) = \sigma_{i'}(z)$ when $i \sim_z i'$.
4. *Averaging over $G_a$.* $\hat s^a_i$ is the average of §XIV.3 applied to $(\sigma_i)$ on the invariant $\hat V_a$. It is sc⁺ and equivariant (§XIV.3, stage 2). It still extends $s^{0a}$, because $s^{0a}$ is equivariant on $V_a$ by (14.45), and the average of an equivariant family is itself. It still satisfies (2): if $i \sim_z i'$, then $g(i) \sim_{g*z} g(i')$ by Lemma 14.4.5, so each translate $\mu(\Gamma(g, z)^{-1}, \sigma_{g(i)}(g * z))$ agrees for $i$ and $i'$.

*Consequences of the departure.* Definition 14.4.11 (2) is not needed, nor Lemma 14.4.13, nor a $G_a$-invariant partition of unity; $\approx_z$ need not be an equivalence relation; and (4) is used only at points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, as printed, since the other points of $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ get neighbourhoods missing $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$.

*For the setting of §14.4.* With Proposition 14.4.6 (2) as a hypothesis ⟦Chapter14/ZDataLocalExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14_of_hyp⟧; unconditionally, from the facts of §14.3 and Definition 14.1.7 (4) ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopLimitExists · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14_of_limit⟧; and for the objects of §14.3 ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.proposition_14_4_14⟧, with $\hat s^a_i$ equal to the sections of the tuple on $\hat V_a \cap \partial X$, under the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4 only. There the boundary sections are face-wise sc⁺ on $U(a)$ ⟦Chapter14/ZLoopSetting · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.isFaceScPlus⟧, by Definition 14.1.3 (1) for the tuple, restricted to $\tilde U(a) \cap \partial X \subset U^0(a)$.

### XIV.21 Lemma 14.5.1 and (14.53) (2017: Lemma 14.10): the cut-offs

§14.5 transports the local extensions of §14.4 from the $\hat V_a$ to every $\hat V_b$, cut off by functors $\beta_a$, sums them, and assembles the result into a structurable multisection on $X$.

**Lemma 14.5.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_5_1⟧, p. 671. *Statement*: let $X$ admit sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definition 7.5.5, Part VII), $B$ a closed saturated set of objects, $A \subset B$, and $\hat V_a$, $a \in A$, open with $B \subset \bigcup_{a \in A}\pi^{-1}(\pi(\hat V_a))$. There are sc-smooth functors $\beta_a : X \to [0, 1]$ ($\beta_a(s\varphi) = \beta_a(t\varphi)$ for every morphism) with (1) $\operatorname{supp}\beta_a \subset \pi^{-1}(\pi(\hat V_a))$; (2) every object has a saturated open neighbourhood on which only finitely many $\beta_a$ are not identically $0$; (3) $\sum_{a \in A}\beta_a = 1$ on $B$. *Stronger*: the tameness of $X$, part of the text's setting, is not used.

*Proof*, the text's.

1. *The cover.* For each object $x$, let $U_x = \pi^{-1}(\pi(\hat V_x))$, the saturation of $\hat V_x$, if $x \in A$, and $U_x = X \setminus B$ otherwise. Each $U_x$ is open (the saturation of an open set is open, §XIV.11) and saturated (a preimage under $\pi$, resp. the complement of the saturated $B$). They cover $X$: a point of $B$ lies in some saturation by hypothesis, and a point off $B$ lies in $X \setminus B = U_y$ for any $y \notin A$, in particular for itself (it is not in $B \supset A$).
2. *The partition.* Definition 7.5.5 for ep-groupoids gives an sc-smooth partition of unity $(\rho_x)$ by functors, subordinate to a saturated open cover, locally finite on saturated open sets. Put $\beta_a = \rho_a$ for $a \in A$.
3. *(1)* is subordination. *(2)* is the local finiteness of $(\rho_x)$. *(3)*: at $y \in B$, every $\rho_x$ with $x \notin A$ vanishes, since its support lies in $X \setminus B$; so $\sum_{a \in A}\beta_a(y) = \sum_x\rho_x(y) = 1$.

**(14.53)**, p. 672: $\operatorname{cl}_X\{y \in \tilde U(a) : \beta_a(y) \ne 0\} \subset \hat V_a$. The text obtains it by shrinking the cover. For the objects of §14.3 no shrinking is needed: it follows from (1), by a property of natural neighbourhoods.

*Closure points of a natural neighbourhood* ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.tgt_mem_of_closure_a6⟧: for a natural neighbourhood $\tilde U(x)$ and an invariant $V \subset \tilde U(x)$, a morphism $\varphi$ from a point of $V$ to a point of $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(x)$ ends in $V$. *Proof*: $t$ is a local homeomorphism, hence open, so $\varphi$ is a limit of morphisms $\psi$ with $s(\psi) \in V$ (open condition near $\varphi$ along the sheet) and $t(\psi) \in \tilde U(x)$; such $\psi$ are $\Gamma(g_\psi, s(\psi))$ for some $g_\psi \in G_x$, by the naturality of the representation. $G_x$ is finite, so one $g$ occurs for $\psi$ arbitrarily close to $\varphi$. The condition $\Gamma(g, s(\psi)) = \psi$ is closed near $\varphi$ (both sides continuous, the morphism space Hausdorff), so $\varphi = \Gamma(g, s(\varphi))$, whose target $g * s(\varphi)$ lies in $V$ by invariance.

*(14.53) from (1)* ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.closure_support_subset_a6⟧: if $\operatorname{supp}\beta \subset \pi^{-1}(\pi(V))$ for an invariant open $V \subset \tilde U(x)$, then $\operatorname{cl}_X\{y \in \tilde U(x) : \beta(y) \ne 0\} \subset V$. *Proof*: a point $y$ of the closure lies in $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(x)$ and in $\operatorname{supp}\beta$, so it is the target of a morphism from a point of $V$ ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.exists_mor_of_ne_zero_a6⟧ (that is what $y \in \pi^{-1}(\pi(V))$ says); by the previous lemma, $y \in V$.

*For the objects of §14.3* ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.exists_betaSpec⟧: Lemma 14.5.1 with $B = \partial X$ (closed and saturated, §XIV.11), $A$ and the $\hat V_a$ of Proposition 14.3.8 (whose orbits cover $|\partial X|$ by (3)), and $\beta_a = 0$ for $a \notin A$, gives cut-offs with all the properties the transport needs ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.BetaSpec⟧: sc-smooth functors into $[0, 1]$, (1)–(3), and (14.53) for the $\hat V_a$ themselves, by the lemma above with $V = \hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$ invariant.

### XIV.22 Lemma 14.5.2 and Remark 14.5.3 (2017: Lemma 14.11, Remark 14.7): the cut-offs over $\partial X$

**Lemma 14.5.2**, p. 672, says that for $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ and the $\beta_a$ of Lemma 14.5.1, the family $(\beta_a|\partial X) \odot \Lambda$ is commensurable (Definition 13.3.11, Part XIII) and its sum is $\Lambda$. *As formalized* (narrower): the identity the proof of Theorem 14.1.9 uses, for the summed sections, $\tilde s^b_j = s^{0b}_j$ on $\hat V_b \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_boundary⟧, proved below once the summed sections are defined. The multisection form, the commensurable family over $\partial X$ and its sum, is not built: it needs the boundary analogue of the commensurability data of §13.3 (about 120 lines), and nothing uses it (gap G.172, §XIV.29).

**The data of §§14.3–14.5** ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput⟧, for $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$, as the assembly uses them: a setting of §14.4 with an input of Proposition 14.5.4 (§XIV.23) whose cut-offs satisfy Lemma 14.5.1 (1)–(3); the values of $\hat\tau$ finite in number and equivariant for the bi-action (Proposition 14.3.4); non-empty index sets $I_b$; the representation of $\Lambda$ by the boundary sections $s^{0b}$ on $\hat V_b \cap \partial X$ (Definition 14.1.3 (3)); and the functor property of $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$.

**A closed set off which everything vanishes.** $K_a = \operatorname{cl}\{y \in \tilde U(a) : \beta_a(y) \ne 0\} \subset \hat V_a$ (14.53), and $C = \bigcup_{a \in A} t(s^{-1}(K_a))$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.C⟧, the set of points isomorphic to a point where some cut-off is non-zero near its own $\hat V_a$. *$C$ is closed* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isClosed_C⟧: each $t(s^{-1}(K_a))$ is closed, $K_a$ being a closed subset of the proper $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(a)$ ((P6)), and the family is locally finite by Lemma 14.5.1 (2) (a saturated neighbourhood on which only finitely many $\beta_a$ are non-zero meets only finitely many of these saturated sets). *$C$ is saturated* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isSaturated_C⟧. *Every transported section vanishes off $C$* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.tsec_eq_zero_of_not_mem_C⟧: a value $\mu(\varphi, \beta_a(s\varphi)\hat s^a_i(s\varphi))$ with $t(\varphi) \notin C$ has $s(\varphi) \notin K_a$, so $\beta_a(s\varphi) = 0$. This is how the text's points $|x| \notin \bigcup_b|\hat V_b|$, where "all sections vanish", are handled.

**The sum** ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec⟧: $\tilde s^b_j(y) = \sum_{a \in A}\tilde s^a_{b,j}(y)$ in the fibre over $y$. *Locally finite* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.exists_finite_tsec⟧: every $y_0$ has an open $Q \ni y_0$ and a finite $F \subset A$ with $\tilde s^a_{b,j} = 0$ on $Q$ for $a \notin F$, by Lemma 14.5.1 (2) (if $\beta_a$ vanishes on a saturated neighbourhood, every transport of $\beta_a\hat s^a$ vanishes there). On $Q$ the sum is a finite section sum ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_eq_sectionSum⟧, so *sc⁺ on $\hat V_b$* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isScPlusSectionOn_usec⟧, a finite sum of sc⁺-sections (Proposition 14.5.4) being sc⁺. *Equivariant* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_equivariant⟧ and *compatible with $\hat\tau$* ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_compat⟧: $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is linear on the fibres and commutes with the finite sum, and each summand has the property by Proposition 14.5.4 (4) and the equivariance there.

*Proof of the sum identity* (Lemma 14.5.2 as used). For $y \in \hat V_b \cap \partial X$: $\tilde s^a_{b,j}(y) = \beta_a(y)s^{0b}_j(y)$ by Proposition 14.5.4 (3), so $\tilde s^b_j(y) = (\sum_a\beta_a(y))s^{0b}_j(y) = s^{0b}_j(y)$ by Lemma 14.5.1 (3).

*The cut-off of the size control*, folded into the sections: for an sc-smooth functor $\sigma$, $\sigma\tilde s^b_j$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportedSum · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.ssec⟧ is again sc⁺ on $\hat V_b$, equivariant and compatible with $\hat\tau$ ($\sigma$ is invariant under morphisms), and zero off $C$.

**Remark 14.5.3** (2017: Remark 14.7), p. 672, comments on the role of the cut-offs and states nothing to prove.

### XIV.23 Proposition 14.5.4 (2017: Proposition 14.8): the transport

**The input** ⟦Chapter14/TransportStatement · SBLocalization.TransportInput⟧, over a combinatorial setting of §14.4: the open sets $\hat V_a$; the properness of $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(a)$; $\hat\tau$ locally constant; cut-offs $\beta_a$, sc-smooth functors with (14.53); boundary sections $s^{0a}$ with Definition 14.1.7 (4) for $\hat\tau$ over $\partial X$; and local extensions $\hat s^a$, the output of Proposition 14.4.14: sc⁺ on $\hat V_a$, $G_a$-equivariant, equal to $s^{0a}$ on $V_a$, and equal on $\sim_z$-related indices.

**Proposition 14.5.4** (same) ⟦Chapter14/TransportStatement · SBLocalization.proposition_14_5_4_statement⟧, p. 673. *Statement*: for every $a \in A$ there are sections $\tilde s^a_{b,j}$, $b \in A$, $j \in I_b$, sc⁺ and $G_b$-equivariant on $\hat V_b$, with (1) $\tilde s^a_{a,i} = \beta_a\hat s^a_i$ on $\hat V_a$; (2) the support of $\tilde s^a_{a,i}$ closed in $X$ and contained in $\hat V_a$, read as: $\tilde s^a_{a,i}$ vanishes off a closed subset of $X$ contained in $\hat V_a$; (3) $\tilde s^a_{b,j} = \beta_a s^{0b}_j$ on $V_b = \hat V_b \cap \partial X$; (4) $\tilde s^a_{b',\beta(k)}(t\varphi) = \mu(\varphi, \tilde s^a_{b,\alpha(k)}(s\varphi))$ for $\varphi \in \hat V_{b,b'}$ and every representative $[I_b \xleftarrow{\alpha} K \xrightarrow{\beta} I_{b'}]$ of $\hat\tau_{b,b'}(\varphi)$. "Symmetric sc⁺-section structure on $\hat V_b$" is read as sc⁺ and $G_b$-equivariant (Definition 13.2.5 (1)). *The statement is consistent* ⟦Chapter14/TransportStatement · SBLocalization.proposition_14_5_4_statement_of_zero⟧: for vanishing data it holds with $\tilde s = 0$, multiples of zero sections being zero ⟦Chapter14/TransportStatement · SBLocalization.sectionSmul_fiberZero_gl⟧.

**Proved** ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.proposition_14_5_4⟧, for every input whose cut-offs satisfy Lemma 14.5.1 (1) ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.SuppInSat⟧: $\beta_a(y) \ne 0$ only if $y$ is the target of a morphism with source in $\hat V_a$. The input records Lemma 14.5.1 only through (14.53); (1) itself is needed for (3), at boundary points of $\hat V_b$ not reached from $\hat V_a$. The cut-offs of §XIV.21 have it; so does $\beta \equiv 0$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.suppInSat_of_zero⟧. Gap G.170 is closed by this proof.

*Proof*, the text's, with the transport defined through arcs.

1. *The cut-off local extensions.* $\beta_a\hat s^a_i$, extended by $0$ off $\hat V_a$, is a global section, sc⁺ on $\hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.isScPlusSectionOn_bsec⟧ (product of an sc-smooth function with an sc⁺-section).
2. *Definition* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec⟧: $\tilde s^a_{b,j}(y) = \mu(\varphi, \beta_a\hat s^a_i(s\varphi))$ for any arc $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ (§XIV.14) with $t(\varphi) = y$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_arc⟧, and $0_y$ if there is none ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_not⟧. A morphism from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_b$ with a pair $(i, j)$ of $\hat\tau_{a,b}(\varphi)$ is an arc of length one ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.arc_of_pairs⟧, so the definition agrees with the text's one-step form ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_pairs⟧; and the section vanishes at points of $\hat V_b$ that are targets of no morphism from $\hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_not_reach⟧. *Why arcs*: with arcs the equivariance and (4) are immediate (append a step); the text defines the value along one morphism and proves independence by z-loops, which is the next step.
3. *Independence of the arc* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.fibAct_bsec_eq⟧, the text's z-loop argument. Let $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i, j, \varphi)$ and $\mathrm{Arc}(a, b, i', j, \varphi')$ end at the same point. Concatenating the second with the reversal of the first gives $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i', i, \varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi')$, a chain from $s(\varphi') \in \hat V_a$ to $s(\varphi) \in \hat V_a$. Both ends lie in $\tilde U(a)$, so $\varphi^{-1} \circ \varphi' = \Gamma(g, s\varphi')$ for some $g \in G_a$. Append $\Gamma(g^{-1}, s\varphi)$, with pair $(i, g^{-1}(i))$ by *diag*: the composite is $1_{s\varphi'}$, a z-loop, so $i' \sim_{s\varphi'} g^{-1}(i)$. By Proposition 14.4.14 (2), $\hat s^a_{i'}(s\varphi') = \hat s^a_{g^{-1}(i)}(s\varphi')$; by equivariance, $\mu(\Gamma(g, s\varphi'), \hat s^a_{g^{-1}(i)}(s\varphi')) = \hat s^a_i(s\varphi)$; $\beta_a$ is invariant. Hence $\mu(\varphi^{-1}\circ\varphi', \beta_a\hat s^a_{i'}(s\varphi')) = \beta_a\hat s^a_i(s\varphi)$, and applying $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ gives the claim.
4. *sc⁺ on $\hat V_b$* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.isScPlusSectionOn_tsec⟧. Two cases at $y_0 \in \hat V_b$. (a) $y_0 = t(\varphi_0)$ for a morphism $\varphi_0$ with source in $\hat V_a$. Take a local sc-smooth inverse $\tau$ of $t$ through $\varphi_0$ (Definition 7.1.4), and $i$ with $(i, j)$ a pair of $\hat\tau_{a,b}(\varphi_0)$ (the right leg of a representative is onto). For $z$ near $y_0$: $\tau(z)$ goes from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_b$, and $\hat\tau_{a,b}(\tau(z)) = \hat\tau_{a,b}(\varphi_0)$ by local constancy, so $\tilde s^a_{b,j}(z) = \mu(\tau(z), \beta_a\hat s^a_i(s\tau(z)))$, the transport of an sc⁺-section along an sc-smooth family of morphisms, which is sc⁺ (Part XIII). (b) $y_0$ is not such a target. Then $y_0 \notin t(s^{-1}(K_a))$, $K_a = \operatorname{cl}\{y \in \tilde U(a) : \beta_a \ne 0\} \subset \hat V_a$, a closed set by the properness of $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(a)$; on the open complement intersected with $\hat V_b$, every arc ending there starts at a point with $\beta_a = 0$, so the section is $0$ near $y_0$.
5. *Equivariance* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_equivariant⟧: for $y \in \hat V_b$ and $g \in G_b$, append the step $\Gamma(g, y)$, with pair $(j, g(j))$ by *diag*, to an arc ending at $(y, j)$; if there is none at $(y, j)$, there is none at $(g * y, g(j))$ either (append $\Gamma(g^{-1}, g * y)$), and both values are zero.
6. *(4)* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_compat⟧: for $\varphi \in \hat V_{b,b'}$ and a pair $(j, j')$ of $\hat\tau_{b,b'}(\varphi)$, append $\varphi$ to an arc ending at $(s\varphi, j)$; if there is none, there is none at $(t\varphi, j')$ (append $\varphi^{-1}$, with the reversed pair by *swap*), and both sides are zero.
7. *(3)* ⟦Chapter14/TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_boundary⟧: for $y \in \hat V_b \cap \partial X$. If an arc from $(x, i)$, $x \in \hat V_a$, reaches $(y, j)$, then $x \in \partial X$ (saturation), $\hat s^a_i(x) = s^{0a}_i(x)$ by Proposition 14.4.14 (1), and Definition 14.1.7 (4) along the arc (§XIV.16) gives $\mu(\varphi, s^{0a}_i(x)) = s^{0b}_j(y)$; with the invariance of $\beta_a$, $\tilde s^a_{b,j}(y) = \beta_a(y)s^{0b}_j(y)$. If no arc reaches $(y, j)$, then no morphism from $\hat V_a$ reaches $y$ (with any pair, as the right leg is onto), so $\beta_a(y) = 0$ by Lemma 14.5.1 (1), and both sides are zero.
8. *(1)*: for $y \in \hat V_a$ the start arc $\mathrm{Arc}(a, a, i, i, 1_y)$ ends at $(y, i)$, so $\tilde s^a_{a,i}(y) = \mu(1_y, \beta_a\hat s^a_i(y)) = \beta_a(y)\hat s^a_i(y)$; by step 3 every other arc ending at $(y, i)$ gives the same value.
9. *(2)*: $\tilde s^a_{a,i}$ vanishes off $K_a \cap \hat V_a$, by (1) and the definition of $K_a$, and $K_a$ is closed in $X$ and contained in $\hat V_a$ by (14.53).

### XIV.24 Theorem 14.5.5 (2017: Theorem 14.3): a structurability criterion

**Theorem 14.5.5** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.theorem_14_5_5⟧, p. 678. *The data* ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData⟧, indexed by a type with points $\mathrm{pt}(a)$: (a) neighbourhoods $U(a)$ with the natural $G_a$-action; (b) invariant open $V_a \subset U(a)$; (c) $\bigcup_a|V_a| = |X|$; (d) symmetric sc⁺-section structures $(s^a_i)_{i \in I_a}$ on $V_a$ representing $\Lambda$; (e) correspondences $\tau_{a,a'}$ on $V(a, a') = \{\varphi : s\varphi \in V_a, t\varphi \in V_{a'}\}$. *Statement*: over an ep-groupoid with $|X|$ paracompact, an sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda$ with such data is structurable. With a good system in place of paracompactness ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.theorem_14_5_5_of_goodSystem⟧; paracompactness gives one by Theorem 13.1.8 (Part XIII). *Stronger*: the text's (a) also asks $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}U(a))$, and (b) asks $\operatorname{cl}|V_a| \subset |U(a)|$; neither is used, so neither is assumed. *A reading*: "correspondence" in (e) is read as in Definitions 13.3.4 and 13.3.6 (Part XIII): locally constant with finitely many values, equivariant for the bi-actions, relating the sections pointwise on $V(a, a')$, with $\tau_{a,a}(\Gamma(g, y)) = [\mathrm{id}, g]$ and $\tau_{a',a}(\varphi) = \tau_{a,a'}(\varphi^{-1})^\sharp$; the text's proof uses the first of the last two for $\tau_{a_x,a_x}$.

*The text's proof* restricts $\Lambda$ to the full subcategory on $V = \bigcup V_a$, an equivalence by Theorem 13.4.3 (Part XIII), chooses $a_x$ with $x \in V_{a_x}$ and small $Q(x) \subset V_{a_x}$, and restricts the data. *The Lean proof* does not pass through the restriction; it pulls the structures back along local transports, as in Theorem 13.5.3 (Part XIII).

1. *Local transports* ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.exists_transport⟧: every object $y$ has an index $a_y$, an open $O(y) \ni y$ and an sc-smooth $\tau_y : O(y) \to$ morphisms with $t(\tau_y(z)) = z$ and $s(\tau_y(z)) \in V_{a_y}$. By (c), $y$ is the target of a morphism $\varphi_0$ from some $V_a$; $t$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, and its local inverse through $\varphi_0$, restricted to where the source stays in the open $V_a$, is $\tau_y$. With a good system $\mathcal U_0$ these data form the structure of the proof ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.nonempty_transport⟧.
2. *Conjugation.* Put $\sigma_y(z) = s(\tau_y(z)) \in V_{a_y}$. For $\psi$ from $O(y)$ to $O(y')$, $\mathrm{conj}(\psi) = \tau_{y'}(t\psi)^{-1} \circ \psi \circ \tau_y(s\psi)$, a morphism from $\sigma_y(s\psi)$ to $\sigma_{y'}(t\psi)$, continuous in $\psi$ and functorial: $\mathrm{conj}(\psi_1 \circ \psi_2) = \mathrm{conj}(\psi_1) \circ \mathrm{conj}(\psi_2)$, $\mathrm{conj}(1_z) = 1_{\sigma_y(z)}$, $\mathrm{conj}(\psi^{-1}) = \mathrm{conj}(\psi)^{-1}$.
3. *The homomorphisms $\gamma_y : G_y \to G_{a_y}$.* For $\psi$ between points of $O(y)$ near the isotropy, $\mathrm{conj}(\psi)$ is a morphism between points of $V_{a_y} \subset U(a_y)$, hence $\Gamma(h, \sigma_y(s\psi))$ for a unique $h = H(\psi) \in G_{a_y}$, functorial in $\psi$. $\gamma_y(g) = H(\Gamma(g, y))$, with $\Gamma$ the representation of $\mathcal U_0$, is a homomorphism. *The good system*: inside $\mathcal U_0(y) \cap O(y)$, a neighbourhood with the restricted natural action on which $\mathrm{conj}(\Gamma(g, z)) = \Gamma_{a_y}(\gamma_y(g), \sigma_y(z))$, so $\sigma_y(g * z) = \gamma_y(g) * \sigma_y(z)$ (this holds near $y$ by continuity of $H$, which is locally constant).
4. *The structures.* At $y$: index set $I_{a_y}$, $G_y$ acting through $\gamma_y$, and sections $s^y_i(z) = \mu(\tau_y(z), s^{a_y}_i(\sigma_y(z)))$, sc⁺ as transports along an sc-smooth family. They are symmetric, by step 3 and the symmetry of $s^{a_y}$, and represent $\Lambda$, because $\Lambda$ is a functor and $s^{a_y}$ represents it at $\sigma_y(z)$.
5. *The correspondences* $\bar\tau_{y,y'}(\varphi) = \tau_{a_y,a_{y'}}(\mathrm{conj}(\varphi))$: locally constant (conj continuous, $\tau$ locally constant), finitely many values, equivariant because conj of the bi-action is the bi-action of conj through $\gamma_y$, $\gamma_{y'}$, and the bi-action of correspondences pulls back along homomorphisms ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_compHom_gl⟧; they relate the sections, because a relation $s^{a'}_j(t\chi) = \mu(\chi, s^a_i(s\chi))$ for $\chi = \mathrm{conj}(\psi)$ transports to $s^{y'}_j(t\psi) = \mu(\psi, s^y_i(s\psi))$; the diagonal and swap conditions follow from those of $\tau$.
6. *Conclusion* ⟦Chapter14/StructurabilityCriterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.Transport.isStructurable⟧: the decoration and the correspondences form a structured tuple (Definition 13.3.6), so $\Lambda$ is structurable.

*Use.* The assembly applies the criterion to $\Lambda'$ with the data built from the summed sections (§XIV.25).

### XIV.25 The proof of Theorem 14.1.9 (2017: Theorem 14.2), pp. 656–678

The statement is in §XIV.7. The Lean proof ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_charged_a6⟧ has three lines: the data of §§14.3–14.5 exist (step A); they give, for every saturated open set containing the boundary domain support, a structurable extension with domain support inside it (step B); and the size control turns such extensions into one with $N(\Lambda') \le f$ (step C). This is the text's proof, §§14.2–14.5 and the end of p. 677.

**Step A: the data exist** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.exists_assemblyInput_a6⟧. *Statement*: for $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact, sc-smooth partitions of unity on the objects, a tame strong bundle chart at every object, and $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ and charging every boundary fibre, there are data of §§14.3–14.5 for $\Lambda$ (§XIV.22). *Proof.*

1. *$\partial X = \emptyset$.* The empty data ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.emptyAssemblyInput⟧: $A = \emptyset$, $\beta \equiv 0$, zero sections; every condition is vacuous or about the empty boundary.
2. *A good representative.* $\Lambda$ is the functor of a structured tuple (§XIV.5, structurability), and by Proposition 14.2.3 the tuple may be taken with (P4) (§XIV.8).
3. *The objects of §14.3* from (P4) and a boundary point (§XIV.13): (P5) neighbourhoods from the good system, the extension of the correspondences of Lemma 14.3.1, (P6) neighbourhoods, and the cover of Proposition 14.3.8.
4. *The cut-offs*: Theorem 7.5.7 (Part VII) gives sc-smooth partitions of unity on $|X|$ from those of the objects and paracompactness; Lemma 14.5.1 for the cover of $\partial X$ by the $\hat V_a$, with (14.53) (§XIV.21).
5. *The local extensions*: Proposition 14.4.14 for the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.20), one choice $\hat s^a$ for each $a \in A$ and zero for $a \notin A$ ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.shA6⟧ ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.shA6_spec⟧.
6. *The input of Proposition 14.5.4* ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.transportInput_a6⟧: $\tilde U(a)$, $\hat V_a$ and $\hat\tau$ from the setting of §XIV.13, the boundary sections of the tuple, the properness of (P6), the local constancy of $\hat\tau$, the cut-offs of step 4 and the $\hat s^a$ of step 5. Lemma 14.5.1 (1) for these cut-offs is part of their specification.
7. *The data of §§14.3–14.5* ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.assemblyInput_a6⟧. The remaining fields: the values of $\hat\tau$ are finitely many (Proposition 14.3.4); the bi-action ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.biact_τ_a6⟧, from the equivariance of $\hat\tau$ in Proposition 14.3.4, through the identification of the bi-actions ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.biact_eq_a6⟧, since $\Gamma$ and the natural action of the setting at $a \in \partial X$ are those of the tuple's good system ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.Γ_eq_a6⟧ ⟦Chapter14/AssemblyInputInstance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.Φ_eq_a6⟧ (the retraction of §XIV.13 is the identity there); the representation of $\Lambda$ by the boundary sections and the functor property, from the tuple (Definition 14.1.3 (3)); and the non-empty index sets $I_a$, from charging (§XIV.2). *Explicit*: charging and the tame strong bundle charts are named.

**Step B: the extension** ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.extension⟧. *Statement*: for data of §§14.3–14.5, $|X|$ paracompact, sc-smooth partitions of unity, and a saturated open $\tilde U'$ containing the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, there is a structurable $\Lambda''$ on $W$ with $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda'') \subset \tilde U'$ and $\Lambda'' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. *Proof.*

1. *The cut-off* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.exists_cutoff⟧: an sc-smooth functor $\sigma : X \to [0, 1]$ with $\sigma = 1$ on the boundary domain support and $\operatorname{cl}\{\sigma \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U'$. The boundary domain support is closed and saturated (§XIV.7), so its image $K$ in $|X|$ is closed (§XIV.11), and $|\tilde U'|$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8). $|X|$ is paracompact Hausdorff, hence normal: choose an open $u$ with $K \subset u$, $\operatorname{cl}u \subset |\tilde U'|$. The sc-smooth Urysohn lemma on the orbit space ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn⟧ (Theorem 7.5.7, Part VII) gives $F : |X| \to [0, 1]$ sc-smooth, $F = 1$ on $K$, $F = 0$ off $u$; $\sigma = F \circ \pi$ is a functor, and its support lies in $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}u) \subset \tilde U'$, $\tilde U'$ being saturated.
2. *The functor $\Lambda'' = \Lambda'_\sigma$* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult⟧, with the cut-off folded into the sections (§XIV.22): for $w$ with a morphism $\varphi$ from $P(w)$ into some $\hat V_b$, $\Lambda''(w) = |I_b|^{-1}\#\{j : \sigma\tilde s^b_j(t\varphi) = \mu(\varphi, w)\}$; where there is no such $\varphi$, $\Lambda''(w) = 1$ if $w$ is the zero of its fibre and $0$ otherwise. *Independent of the chart* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult_eq⟧: for two charts $\varphi : P(w) \to \hat V_b$, $\varphi' : P(w) \to \hat V_{b'}$, the morphism $\chi = \varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}$ goes from $\hat V_b$ to $\hat V_{b'}$; the summed sections are compatible with $\hat\tau_{b,b'}(\chi)$ (§XIV.22), and a correspondence $[I_b \xleftarrow{\alpha} K \xrightarrow{\beta} I_{b'}]$ with bijective legs (Definition 13.3.1) matches the indices $j$ with $\sigma\tilde s^b_j(t\varphi) = \mu(\varphi, w)$ to the indices $j'$ with $\sigma\tilde s^{b'}_{j'}(t\varphi') = \mu(\varphi', w)$, and $|I_b| = |K| = |I_{b'}|$. Off $C$, $\Lambda''$ is the trivial functor (the sections vanish there). *A functor* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isWFunctor_mult⟧: a chart for $w$ composed with $\psi^{-1}$ is a chart for $\mu(\psi, w)$.
3. *Criterion data for $\Lambda''$* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.crit⟧, indexed by $A \sqcup X$. For $b \in A$: $\tilde U(b)$, $\hat V_b$, $I_b$, the sections $\sigma\tilde s^b_j$. For an object $x$: a natural neighbourhood of $x$ and inside it the invariant set of its points off $C$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.critV⟧ (open, since $C$ is closed, and invariant, since $C$ is saturated), with one index and the zero section. The correspondences are the text's: $\hat\tau_{b,b'}$; $[I_b \leftarrow I_b \to \{1\}]$ from $\hat V_b$ to a set off $C$, where all $\sigma\tilde s^b_j$ vanish, so they all relate to the zero section; its reverse; and $[\{1\} \leftarrow \{1\} \to \{1\}]$. The covering condition (c): a point of $C$ is isomorphic to a point of some $K_a \subset \hat V_a$, and a point $x$ off $C$ lies in its own set. The sections represent $\Lambda''$ on each set by the definition of $\Lambda''$ (resp. its triviality off $C$); the diagonal, swap and equivariance conditions for the correspondences involving $\{1\}$ are identities of correspondences with a one-point set.
4. *$\Lambda''$ is an sc⁺-multisection* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.CriterionData.hasLocalSectionStructure_t9⟧: criterion data with non-empty index sets for a functor give local section structures at every point, the structure of some set of the data transported by a local inverse of $t$ (as in step 1 of Theorem 14.5.5, §XIV.24). The non-empty index sets are where charging enters: the weights $|I_b|^{-1}$ must sum to $1$.
5. *Structurable* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isStructurable_mult⟧, by Theorem 14.5.5 (§XIV.24).
6. *$\Lambda'' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult_boundary⟧, when $\sigma = 1$ on the boundary domain support. A boundary point $y$ has a chart $\varphi$ into some $V_b$, by Proposition 14.3.8 (3) and (2). There $\sigma\tilde s^b_j = \sigma s^{0b}_j$ by the sum identity (§XIV.22); the boundary sections vanish off the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, so $\sigma s^{0b}_j = s^{0b}_j$ at all boundary points; and the count with the $s^{0b}_j$ is $\Lambda(\mu(\varphi, w)) = \Lambda(w)$, by Definition 14.1.3 (3) and the functor property of $\Lambda$.
7. *The domain support* ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.domSupp_mult_subset⟧: $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda'') \subset \operatorname{cl}\{\sigma \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U'$, since where $\sigma = 0$ every section is zero and $\Lambda''$ is trivial.

*How the assembly departs from the text.* The text forms $\Lambda'$ from the summed sections on the $\hat V_b$, gives the points $|x| \notin \bigcup|\hat V_b|$ a neighbourhood with the zero section, applies Theorem 14.5.5, and multiplies by the cut-off afterwards (Lemma 13.3.14). Here the cut-off $\sigma$, which only ensures the domain support lies in $\tilde U'$, is folded into the sections before Theorem 14.5.5 is applied, and the points off the closed set $C$ (which contains every point where some section is non-zero) are covered by sets around all objects. The size control (step C) multiplies by a second cut-off afterwards, as the text does.

**Step C: size control** ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.sizeControl_a6⟧, the end of p. 677. *Statement*: if for every saturated open $\tilde U' \supset$ the boundary domain support there is a structurable extension with domain support in $\tilde U'$, then, for $N$, $\tilde U$, $f$ as in Theorem 14.1.9, there is a structurable $\Lambda'$ with $N(\Lambda') \le f$, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda') \subset \tilde U$, $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. *Tools*: the pointwise norm $N(\Lambda)(x) = \max\{N(w) : \Lambda(w) > 0, P(w) = x\}$ (Definition 13.2.3) is non-negative ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_nonneg⟧ and a functor ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_tgt⟧ ($\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is an isometry for an auxiliary norm and preserves $\Lambda$); on the domain of an sc⁺-section $y \mapsto N(s(y))$ is continuous ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.continuousOn_normW⟧, so $\{N(\Lambda) < f\}$ is open ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.isOpen_pointwiseNorm_lt⟧ for continuous $f$, since on the domain of a local representation $N(\Lambda)(y) = \max_i N(s_i(y))$; $N(w) \le |a| N(\Lambda)(P(w))$ on the support of $a\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.normW_le_of_multisectionSmul_pos⟧ (Definition 13.2.10), hence $N(\beta \odot \Lambda) \le |\beta| N(\Lambda)$ ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_smulFun_le⟧ (Lemma 13.2.11); and $\beta \odot \Lambda = \Lambda$ where $\beta = 1$ ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.multisectionSmulFun_of_eq_one⟧. Saturation: $\partial X$ is saturated ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_boundary_gl⟧, and closures ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_closure_gl⟧ (saturations of open sets are open) and unions ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_union_gl⟧ of saturated sets are saturated. The zero multisection has empty domain support ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.domSupp_zeroMultisection_gl⟧. *Proof.*

1. *A smaller target.* $U' = \{f > 0\}$ is open, saturated ($f$ a functor), contains the boundary domain support (there $0 \le N(\Lambda) < f$), and lies in $\tilde U$ (as $\operatorname{cl}\{f \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U$). Take the extension $\Lambda''$ with $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda'') \subset U'$.
2. *The good set.* Put $h = N(\Lambda'')$ and $K = \operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda'') = \operatorname{cl}\{h > 0\}$ (Definition 13.2.14 through the norm); $h = 0$ off $K$. $G = \{h < f\} \cup (X \setminus K)$ is open and saturated ($h$, $f$ functors; $K$ the closure of a saturated set).
3. *$\partial X \subset G$.* Let $x \in \partial X \cap K$. Over $x$, $\Lambda''$ and $\Lambda$ have the same support. If $x$ is in the boundary domain support, $h(x) = N(\Lambda)(x) < f(x)$. If not, every $w$ over $x$ with $\Lambda(w) > 0$ is the zero (else $x$ would be in the boundary domain support), so $h(x) = 0$; and $f(x) > 0$ because $x \in K \subset U'$. Either way $x \in \{h < f\}$.
4. *The cut-off.* $|\partial X|$ and $|X \setminus G|$ are closed (closed saturated sets, §XIV.11) and disjoint (by 3 and saturation). The sc-smooth Urysohn lemma ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn⟧ gives $F : |X| \to [0, 1]$ with $F = 1$ on $|\partial X|$ and $F = 0$ on $|X \setminus G|$; $\sigma = F \circ \pi$ is an sc-smooth functor.
5. *$\Lambda' = \sigma \odot \Lambda''$* is structurable, by Lemma 13.3.14 (Part XIII) for functions.
6. *The bound.* $N(\Lambda') \le \sigma h$. On $\{h < f\}$: $\sigma h \le h < f$. On $X \setminus K$: $h = 0 \le f$. Off $G$: $\sigma = 0 \le f$.
7. *Domain support.* Where $N(\Lambda') > 0$, $\sigma h > 0$, so $h > 0$; hence $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda') \subset \operatorname{cl}\{h > 0\} = K \subset U' \subset \tilde U$.
8. *Over $\partial X$*, $\sigma = 1$, so $\Lambda' = \Lambda'' = \Lambda$.

*Readings in the size control*, as in the statement (§XIV.7): the text uses $N(\Lambda)(x) < f(x)$ for $x \in \partial X$; the hypothesis gives it on the boundary domain support. At boundary points outside it where $f = 0$, the argument needs $\Lambda''$ trivial nearby; asking the extension to have domain support in $\{f > 0\}$ (step 1), which step B allows, provides this.

**The chain, in the book's terms.** §14.2: Proposition 14.2.3 (§XIV.8). §14.3: Lemma 14.3.1, Proposition 14.3.4, Lemmas 14.3.6, 14.3.7 and Proposition 14.3.8 (§§XIV.9–XIV.12). §14.4: the setting from §14.3, Lemma 14.4.5, Proposition 14.4.6, Lemmas 14.4.7, 14.4.9, Proposition 14.4.10, Definition 14.4.11 and Proposition 14.4.14 (§§XIV.13–XIV.20). §14.5: Lemma 14.5.1 with (14.53), the sum identity of Lemma 14.5.2, Proposition 14.5.4, Theorem 14.5.5, the assembly and the size control (§§XIV.21–XIV.25). No step assumes a hypothesis beyond the theorem's, read with the tame strong bundle charts and charging.

*Remark on the superseded route.* The size control and the assembly were first proved for the Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 without charging (§XIV.7). That route has four statements, kept in the formalization as properties of that statement. (i) The extension statement ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement⟧ (for every $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ and saturated open $\tilde U$ containing its boundary domain support, a structurable extension with domain support in $\tilde U$) implies that statement ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_hyp⟧, by the size control above for all $\Lambda$ at once; it holds when $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧. (ii) The hypothesis that every $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ has the data of §§14.3–14.5 ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyHyp⟧ implies the extension statement ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_assembly⟧ and the uncharged statement ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_of_assembly⟧, and holds when $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/ExtensionAssembly · SBLocalization.assemblyHyp_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧. (iii) For $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact and partitions of unity, that hypothesis holds only when $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.boundary_eq_empty_of_assemblyHyp_a6⟧, since it implies the uncharged statement, which does not hold when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$; step A is its form with charging. The proof above uses none of (i)–(iii).

### XIV.26 A witness with boundary: the half-space bundle

The hypotheses of Theorem 14.1.9 are jointly satisfiable with $\partial X \ne \emptyset$, non-zero fibres and a non-trivial $\Lambda$; the theorem is applied to such data.

**The object** ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.halfSEP⟧: Part I's trivial strong bundle $H \times \mathbb R^k \to H$ over the half-space $H = [0, \infty) \times \mathbb R^m$, over the trivial ep-groupoid of $H$ (objects $H$, only identity morphisms) ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.epBundleW1⟧. *The hypotheses of the theorem*: $H$ is a tame quadrant, so the ep-groupoid is tame ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.isTame_halfSEP⟧; its orbit space, $H$ itself, is metrizable, hence paracompact ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_halfSEP⟧; it admits sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_halfSEP⟧, by Theorem 5.5.10 (Part V) with its one chart, whose model is finite-dimensional (Proposition 5.5.11); and Part I's re-centred charts are tame strong bundle charts at every object ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.hB_halfSEP⟧. *Non-degenerate*: $\partial H = \{x_1 = 0\}$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.mem_boundary_halfSEP_iff⟧ (degeneracy index $1$ there), which contains $0$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.zero_mem_boundary_halfSEP⟧; and the fibres $\mathbb R^k$ are non-zero for $k \ge 1$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.nontrivial_fibre_halfSEP⟧. All hypotheses hold jointly with the zero multisection, an auxiliary norm from Theorem 12.2.2 (Part XII), $\tilde U = X$ and $f \equiv 1$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_charged_hypotheses_halfSEP⟧, and the theorem applies ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_halfSEP⟧.

**A non-trivial $\Lambda$.** For $v \in \mathbb R^k$, $v \ne 0$, the constant section $x \mapsto (x, v)$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.constSec⟧ is sc⁺ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.isScPlusSectionOn_constSec⟧ (constant in a finite-dimensional fibre). The function $\Lambda_v(w) = 1$ if $w = (P(w), v)$ and $0$ otherwise ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.constMulti⟧ is structurable over $\partial H$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.isBoundaryStructurable_constMulti⟧: on a good system for $\partial H$, one index, the constant section ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.constStructure⟧, and the trivial correspondence ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.constTau⟧; Definition 14.1.3 (1) holds by the general lemma of §XIV.2 (an sc⁺-section on $X$ is face-wise sc⁺ on every set). It charges $\partial H$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.chargesBoundary_constMulti⟧; its boundary domain support contains $0$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.boundaryDomSupp_constMulti_nonempty⟧, since $v \ne 0$; and $N(\Lambda_v)(x) = N(x, v)$ ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.pointwiseNorm_constMulti⟧, a continuous function ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.continuous_normW_constSec⟧. *The theorem applied* ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceConstSection · HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_constSec⟧: with $\tilde U = X$ and $f(x) = N(x, v) + 1$ (a continuous functor, $> N(\Lambda_v)$ everywhere), there is a structurable $\Lambda'$ on the bundle with $N(\Lambda')(x) \le N(x, v) + 1$ and $\Lambda' = \Lambda_v$ over $\partial H$; every hypothesis is discharged.

*Scope of the witness*: the ep-groupoid has no isotropy and one chart, so it shows that the hypotheses are jointly satisfiable in a non-degenerate case, not that the isotropy part of the construction is exercised. The trivial bundle over $\mathbb R^n$, the witness of the tame strong bundle charts in §XIV.3, has $\partial X = \emptyset$ and so cannot serve here.

### XIV.27 §14.6 and Definitions 14.6.1, 14.6.2 (2017: §14.6, Definitions 14.10, 14.11): structured sc⁺-multisections on the faces

§14.6, pp. 680–682, assumes $X$ tame and face-structured. Each face $F$ is saturated and a sub-M-polyfold, hence an ep-groupoid with the morphisms between its points. One is given a structured sc⁺-multisection on each $W|F$, compatible on the intersections of faces, and Theorem 14.6.3 glues them into one over $\partial X$, which then extends to $W$ by Theorem 14.1.9. This subsection treats the preamble of p. 680 and the two definitions; the next one treats the theorem.

**Faces.** The faces of §14.6 are Part XI's ep-faces $X_\theta$ (Definition 11.1.3, Part XI): for a face $\theta$ of the orbit space, the set of objects whose orbit lies in $\theta$. They are closed and saturated, and tame ep-groupoids with the morphisms between their points (Proposition 11.1.6, Part XI). The proof of Theorem 14.6.3 uses five properties of them near a boundary point, each proved separately.

1. *Faces consist of boundary points* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.subset_boundary⟧. *Proof*: $X_\theta$ is the preimage of the closure of a component of $\{d = 1\}$ in $|X|$, and since the orbit map is open (Proposition 7.1.8, Part VII), the preimage of the closure is the closure of the preimage. Let $y$ be in that closure and suppose $d(y) = 0$. Near $y$ the degeneracy index is at most $d(y)$ (Lemma 2.4.3, Part II, upper semicontinuity), so a point $y'$ of the component close to $y$ has $1 = d(y') \le d(y) = 0$, which is impossible. Hence $d(y) \ge 1$.
2. *Every boundary point lies on a face* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.exists_isEpFace_mem⟧. *Proof*: face-structured means that $|x|$ lies on exactly $d_X(x)$ faces of $|X|$; for $x \in \partial X$ this number is at least $1$, so the set of faces through $|x|$ is non-empty, and the ep-face of any of them contains $x$. *And on finitely many* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.finite_isEpFace_mem⟧: the faces of $|X|$ through $|x|$ number $d_X(x)$, and every ep-face through $x$ is the image of one of them.
3. *Near $x$, every face through a point contains $x$* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.eventually_mem_of_isEpFace⟧. *Proof*: the degeneracy index of a tame M-polyfold is a corner index (Part II), so at $x$ there are local pieces: an open $B \ni x$ such that each face of $X$ through a point of $B$, read in $B$, is one of the $d(x)$ local pieces of $\{d = 1\}$ at $x$, each of which has $x$ in its closure (Proposition 2.7.5 (3), Part II). For $y \in B$ and $X_\theta \ni y$, the unique face of the object M-polyfold through $y$ inside $X_\theta$ is such a piece, so it contains $x$, and so does $X_\theta$.
4. *Faces are saturated* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.tgt_mem_iff⟧: $s(\varphi) \in F$ iff $t(\varphi) \in F$, because $s(\varphi)$ and $t(\varphi)$ have the same orbit. Hence a face is invariant under every natural action at its points ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.Φ_mem⟧: $\Phi(g)(y) = t(\Gamma(g, y))$ and $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y$. This is the text's $g * (F \cap U(x)) = F \cap U(x)$.
5. *A local face of a tame chart lies in one face* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.exists_isEpFace_germ⟧: in a tame chart $\varphi$, if $t_i(\varphi(y)) = 0$, there are $\varepsilon > 0$ and a face $X_\theta$ such that every point $e'$ of the retract within $\varepsilon$ of $\varphi(y)$ with $t_i(e') = 0$ has $\varphi^{-1}(e') \in X_\theta$. *Proof*: by Part I's local face structure, there are $\varepsilon$ and a point $p$ of $\{d_O = 1\}$ such that, within $\varepsilon$, the face $\{t_i = 0\}$ of the retract lies in the closure of the component $S$ of $\{d_O = 1\}$ through $p$. In a tame chart the degeneracy index of $X$ is that of the model, so $\varphi^{-1}(S) \subset \{d_X = 1\}$; it is preconnected, as a continuous image of a preconnected set, and therefore lies in the component of $\{d_X = 1\}$ through $q = \varphi^{-1}(p)$. Let $\theta$ be the face of $|X|$ through $|q|$. A point $e'$ as above lies in $\operatorname{cl}S$, so $\varphi^{-1}(e')$ lies in the closure of $\varphi^{-1}(S)$, by continuity of $\varphi^{-1}$ within $S$, hence in the face of the object M-polyfold through $q$, whose image in $|X|$ lies in $\theta$.

A sixth fact concerns natural actions, not faces: *two natural representations of $G_x$ agree near $x$* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Γ_eq⟧. For each $g$, $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ and $\Gamma'(g, \cdot)$ are continuous with value $g$ at $x$, so near $x$ both lie in an open set around $g$ on which $s$ is injective; there $s(\Gamma(g, y)) = y = s(\Gamma'(g, y))$ gives $\Gamma(g, y) = \Gamma'(g, y)$. The natural actions agree as well ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq⟧. This is why the text can speak of "the" natural action on $F \cap U(x)$: it does not depend on $U(x)$ near $x$.

**Sc⁺ relative to a face** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.IsFaceRelScPlusSectionOn⟧, p. 680.
