The text's sections of $W|F$ are sc⁺ for the induced M-polyfold structure of $F$. *As formalized*: $s$ is a section over $U \subset F$ with values in $W_{0,1}$, and in every tame strong bundle chart, at every $y \in U$, on every local face germ $\{t_i = 0\}$ at $\varphi(y)$ that lies in $F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.FaceGermIn⟧ (for some $\varepsilon > 0$, the points of the retract within $\varepsilon$ of $\varphi(y)$ with $t_i = 0$ map into $F$), the local representative is sc⁺ on that germ in the sense of Part I. *Reading*: the local face germs lying in $F$ are the local models of the sub-M-polyfold $F$ at its points (Theorem 2.5.17, Part II; Proposition 11.1.6, Part XI), so this is "$s|F$ is an sc⁺-section of $W|F$" read in the charts of $X$, as Definition 14.1.3 (1) is read (§XIV.2); only the values of $s$ on $F$ near $U$ enter. Definition 14.1.3 (1) implies it for every face ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.IsFaceScPlusSectionOn.isFaceRelScPlusSectionOn⟧, since it asks the same on every local face germ, whether in $F$ or not; the property passes to subsets of $U$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.IsFaceRelScPlusSectionOn.mono⟧. *Witness*: the zero section, on every $U \subset \partial X$ and for every face ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.isFaceRelScPlusSectionOn_fiberZero⟧.

*Locality.* Being sc⁺ on a face germ at a point depends only on the section near the point on the germ ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · IsScPlusOnFaceNear.congr_nhds⟧: if $s = s'$ on $O \cap N \cap \{t_i = 0\}$ for an open $N \ni x$, and $s$ is sc⁺ on the germ $O \cap V \cap \{t_i = 0\}$, then $s'$ is sc⁺ on $O \cap (V \cap N) \cap \{t_i = 0\}$: this set is an sc-retract, as an open subset of one (Proposition 2.3.1 (1), Part II), and $s'$ agrees there with the restriction of $s$. The local representative of a section at $z$ depends only on the section at $\varphi^{-1}(z)$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.localRepOne_congr⟧.

*The gluing criterion* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGerm · SBLocalization.isFaceScPlusSectionOn_of_local⟧. *Statement*: let $s$ be a section over $U$ with values in $W_{0,1}$ such that for every $y \in U$ and every face $F \ni y$ there are a section $\sigma$, sc⁺ relative to $F$ at $y$, and an open $N \ni y$ with $s = \sigma$ on $F \cap N$. Then $s$ satisfies Definition 14.1.3 (1) on $U$. *Proof*. 1. Fix a tame strong bundle chart, $y \in U$ in its domain, and $i$ with $t_i(\varphi(y)) = 0$. By fact 5, there are $\varepsilon$ and a face $F$ with the local face germ $\{t_i = 0\}$ at $\varphi(y)$, within $\varepsilon$, mapping into $F$; in particular $y \in F$ (take $e' = \varphi(y)$). 2. The hypothesis gives $\sigma$ and $N$; since the germ lies in $F$, $\sigma$ is sc⁺ on it at $\varphi(y)$. 3. The set of model points over $N$ is $N' \cap O$ for an open $N'$, by continuity of $\varphi^{-1}$ on $O$. On $O \cap (N' \cap B_\varepsilon) \cap \{t_i = 0\}$, a point $z$ has $\varphi^{-1}(z) \in F \cap N$, so $s(\varphi^{-1}(z)) = \sigma(\varphi^{-1}(z))$ and the local representatives agree at $z$. 4. Locality transfers sc⁺ from $\sigma$ to $s$ on the germ.

**Structured data over a set** ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple⟧. For $K$ a face or an intersection of faces, and an index family ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IndexFamily⟧ (finite sets $I_x$ with $G_x$-actions, one for every object), the data of a structured sc⁺-multisection over $K$ are:

- a function $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ that is a functor over $K$, $\Lambda(\mu(\varphi, w)) = \Lambda(w)$ for $s(\varphi) \in K$;
- for $x \in K$ a neighbourhood $U(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action of $X$, with $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}(U(x) \cap K))$, condition (1) of Definition 13.1.4 (Part XIII) for the trace on $K$;
- sections $s^x_i$, $i \in I_x$, over $U(x) \cap K$, equivariant under the natural action, $s^x_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^x_i(y))$, and representing $\Lambda$ on $U(x) \cap K$ by the counting formula of Definition 14.1.3 (3);
- correspondences $\tau_{x,x'}$ on the morphisms between $U(x) \cap K$ and $U(x') \cap K$, locally constant with finitely many values, with (a) inversion, (b) the diagonal, (c) the bi-action, and (4) the compatibility of the sections of Definition 14.1.7.

The regularity of the sections is not part of these data; it is added for faces below. The traces are written $U(x) \cap K$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.U⟧, and the morphism sets between them $\mathcal U(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.mor⟧.

*The equivalence* ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv⟧, "similar to the $X$-case" (Definition 13.3.8, Part XIII), in the form of §XIV.5: $T \sim T'$ if $\Lambda = \Lambda'$ over $K$ and there are open $O(x) \ni x$ with $O(x) \cap K \subset U(x) \cap U'(x)$, $I_x = I'_x$, and $\tau'_{x,x'} = \tau_{x,x'}$, transported along these equalities, on the morphisms between the $O(x) \cap K$. Reflexive ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv.refl⟧ with $O(x) = U(x)$; symmetric ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv.symm⟧ by reversing the equalities; transitive ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv.trans⟧ with $O(x) = O_1(x) \cap O_2(x)$, a morphism between these sets being one for both pairs. The classes are the structured multisections over $K$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelStructured⟧.

*Reading*: the text's "good neighbourhood $U_F(x) \subset F$" is read as it explains it on p. 680, $U(x) \cap F$ for a neighbourhood of $X$ with the natural action and the properness of Definition 13.1.4 (1). Since $F$ is closed, $\operatorname{cl}(U(x) \cap F)$ lies in $F$, and the properness in $X$ is the properness inside the face (shown below).

*Restriction to a smaller set* ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.restrictTo⟧, for $K' \subset K$: the same $\Lambda$, index sets, sections and correspondences, on the traces $U(x) \cap K'$ for $x \in K'$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.restrictTo_U⟧. Properness passes to the smaller closed set; the remaining conditions are inherited by subsets. Restriction respects the equivalence ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv.restrictTo⟧: the same open sets $O(x)$, for $x \in K'$, witness the equivalence of the restrictions, since $O(x) \cap K' \subset O(x) \cap K$. Restricting twice is restricting once ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.restrictTo_restrictTo_equiv⟧, by reflexivity, the two tuples being equal; this is the text's remark that $\tilde\Lambda_{F \cap F' \cap F''}$ can be formed for any number of faces. On classes ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelStructured.restrictTo⟧.

**A structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|F$** ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple⟧, p. 680: data over a face $F$ whose sections $s^x_i$ are sc⁺ relative to $F$ on $U(x) \cap F$. The equivalence is that of the underlying data ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.setoid⟧, and the classes ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredMultisection⟧ are the text's $\tilde\Lambda_F = [\Lambda_F, \mathcal U_F, S_F, \tau_F]$. *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.zero⟧: the zero multisection on any face, on the index family $I_x = \{*\}$ with the trivial action ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IndexFamily.unit⟧, with the zero section, the trivial correspondence $[\{*\} \leftarrow \{*\} \to \{*\}]$, and neighbourhoods with the properness property, which Part XIII supplies at every point.

**Definition 14.6.1** (same) ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.restrictFace⟧, p. 681: the restriction $\tilde\Lambda_F|F'$ to $W|(F \cap F')$ is the restriction of the data to $K' = F \cap F'$: it keeps $\Lambda_F$, the index sets, the sections and the correspondences, with neighbourhoods $U_F(x) \cap F \cap F'$ for $x \in F \cap F'$ and the correspondences restricted to the morphisms between them. Since restriction respects the equivalence, it is well defined on classes ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredMultisection.restrictFace⟧, as the text's "obtained by taking a representative" asks. The text's $\tilde\Lambda_{F'}|F$, whose base is $F' \cap F$, is read as a class over $F \cap F'$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredMultisection.restrictFace'⟧, the two sets being equal. The sections of the restriction are sc⁺ relative to $F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.restrictFace_isFaceRelScPlus⟧, being restrictions of such sections.

*Sc⁺ on the corner* (same). The definition says that $\tilde\Lambda_F|F'$ is a structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|(F \cap F')$, so its sections must be sc⁺ on the corner $F \cap F'$, not only relative to $F$. *Locally* ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · IsScPlusOnCornerNear⟧: near $x$, for an open $V \ni x$, the corner germ $O \cap V \cap \{t_i = 0\} \cap \{t_j = 0\}$ is an sc-retract and $s$ restricted to it is an sc⁺-section; the condition is symmetric in $i$ and $j$ ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · IsScPlusOnCornerNear.symm⟧, the two hyperplanes being intersected in either order. *From a face germ to a corner germ* ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · IsScPlusOnFaceNear.isScPlusOnCornerNear⟧: in a tame local model, sc⁺ on the face germ $\{t_i = 0\}$ at $x$ gives sc⁺ on every corner germ $\{t_i = t_j = 0\}$ at $x$. *Proof*: by Part I's corner retraction for the pair $\{i, j\}$ of a tame retraction, the corner germ is an sc-retract; it is a subset of the face germ, and an sc-smooth map on a retract restricts to an sc-smooth map on a sub-retract of its source; the fibre condition of an sc⁺-section is pointwise. *On $X$* ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · SBLocalization.IsCornerRelScPlusSectionOn⟧: the sc⁺-sections of $W|(F \cap F')$, read in the tame strong bundle charts of $X$ on the corner germs whose two face germs lie in $F$ and in $F'$. Sc⁺ relative to $F$ gives it ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · SBLocalization.IsFaceRelScPlusSectionOn.isCornerRelScPlusSectionOn⟧, by the local statement applied to the face germ in $F$ (relative to $F'$ it follows by the symmetry). The zero section has it ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · SBLocalization.isCornerRelScPlusSectionOn_fiberZero⟧. *Hence* ⟦Chapter14/CornerScPlus · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.restrictFace_isCornerRelScPlus⟧: the sections of $\tilde\Lambda_F|F'$ are sc⁺ on the corner $F \cap F'$, and the restriction is a structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|(F \cap F')$ in the sense of the definition. This closes gap G.184.

*The neighbourhoods $U_F(x)$ inside the face* (restated, up to equivalence). The text asks the $U_F(x)$ to be good neighbourhoods for the ep-groupoid $F$, that is, the conditions of Definitions 13.1.2 and 13.1.4 inside $F$. Three steps.

1. *Conditions (1) and (3) of Definition 13.1.4 pass from $X$ to a face.* Properness ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_face⟧: if $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}(U \cap X_\theta))$ in $X$, then it is proper on $s^{-1}$ of the closure of the trace in the face ep-groupoid. The proof is by ultrafilters: an ultrafilter of face morphisms with sources in the closure and targets converging to $z \in X_\theta$ is an ultrafilter of morphisms of $X$ with the same property, so it converges in $X$ to some $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \operatorname{cl}(U \cap X_\theta) \subset X_\theta$, the face being closed, and $t(\varphi) = z$; then $\varphi$ is a face morphism, and the ultrafilter converges to it in the face. Components ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · EpGroupoid.isDiffeoComponent_face⟧: if every component of the morphisms between $U$ and $U'$ in $X$ has $s$ and $t$ sc-diffeomorphisms onto open sets, so does every component of the face morphisms between $U \cap X_\theta$ and $U' \cap X_\theta$. A component $C$ of the face morphism set is preconnected in $X$, so it lies in the component of $X$ through any of its points; on that component $s$ and $t$ are injective, hence on $C$; and on an open set of morphisms of an ep-groupoid, injectivity of $s$ and $t$ is the component condition (the morphisms of the face form a sub-M-polyfold, with $s$, $t$ local sc-diffeomorphisms). So every good system of $X$ restricts to neighbourhoods of $X_\theta$ with (1) ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isProperSubset_face⟧ and (3) ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isDiffeoComponent_face⟧.
2. *Shrinking a tuple.* For open $W(x) \ni x$, the invariant core of $U(x) \cap W(x)$ under the natural action is an open neighbourhood of $x$ carrying the same action ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.shrink⟧. Replacing the neighbourhoods of a tuple by these cores, and keeping $\Lambda$, the sections and the correspondences, gives a tuple ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.RelTuple.shrink⟧ equivalent to the original ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.RelTuple.equiv_shrink⟧, with $O(x)$ the cores. Sections that were sc⁺ relative to $F$ stay so on the smaller sets ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.shrink⟧.
3. *Choosing the shrinking.* For $|X|$ paracompact, Theorem 13.1.8 (Part XIII) gives a good system $\mathcal G$ of $X$; shrinking inside its neighbourhoods $G(x)$ gives an equivalent tuple whose neighbourhoods satisfy (3) in $X$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.RelTuple.exists_equiv_isDiffeoComponent⟧, since (3) passes to smaller open sets (§XIV.4). By step 1, they satisfy (1) and (3) inside the face.

*Conclusion* ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.exists_equiv_faceGood⟧: for $X$ tame and face-structured with $|X|$ paracompact, every face tuple over $X_\theta$ is equivalent to one with the same $\Lambda$, index sets, sections and correspondences whose $U_F(x)$ satisfy (1) and (3) inside the face ep-groupoid and are invariant under the natural $G_x$-action of $X$, $\Phi(g)(U(x) \cap F) \subset U(x) \cap F$. On classes ⟦Chapter14/FaceGoodSystem · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredMultisection.exists_rep_faceGood⟧: every structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|F$ has such a representative. *Restated*: the text takes good neighbourhoods inside $F$ for every representative; the formalization shows that every class has a representative with them, which is all the gluing needs. *Not built*: condition (2) of Definition 13.1.4 inside the face, a natural representation of the ep-groupoid $F$ itself with a connected domain inside $F$ (Theorem 7.1.13, Part VII, for $F$). The natural action used is that of $X$ restricted to $U(x) \cap F$, which is how the text describes it on p. 680. Nothing in §14.6 uses (2) (gap G.185, §XIV.29).

**Definition 14.6.2** (same) ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment⟧, p. 681: an assignment $F \mapsto \tilde\Lambda_F$, one structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|F$ for each face, is compatible if $\tilde\Lambda_F|F' = \tilde\Lambda_{F'}|F$ as classes over $F \cap F'$ for all faces $F$, $F'$; the common class is the text's $\tilde\Lambda_{F \cap F'}$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.inter⟧. Equal classes have equivalent representatives ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.equiv⟧: the restrictions of the chosen representatives of $\tilde\Lambda_F$ and $\tilde\Lambda_{F'}$ to $F \cap F'$ are equivalent. The text draws two consequences, both proved from this: "$I^F_x = I^{F'}_x$" for $x \in F \cap F'$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.index_eq⟧, since equivalent tuples have equal index sets; and $\Lambda_F = \Lambda_{F'}$ on $W|(F \cap F')$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.Λ_eq⟧, since equivalent tuples have equal functors. What the equivalence does not give, the equality of the sections, is the subject of the next subsection. *Witness* ⟦Chapter14/FaceStructured · SBLocalization.isCompatibleAssignment_zero⟧: the zero multisection on every face, on any choice of neighbourhoods; all restrictions are the zero data over $F \cap F'$, equivalent with $O(x)$ the intersections of the two neighbourhoods.

### XIV.28 Theorem 14.6.3 (2017: Theorem 14.4): gluing the faces, and the extension

**Theorem 14.6.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.theorem_14_6_3_hyp⟧, p. 682. *Input* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData⟧, the chosen representatives of the text's proof:

- one index family $I_x$, the text's "$I_x := I^F_x$";
- for every face $F$ a face tuple $(\Lambda_F, \mathcal U_F, S_F, \tau_F)$ on this index family;
- $\Lambda_F = \Lambda_{F'}$ on $W|(F \cap F')$;
- $s^x_{F,i} = s^x_{F',i}$ on $U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x) \cap F \cap F'$, for $x \in F \cap F'$;
- $\tau_{F,x,x'} = \tau_{F',x,x'}$ on the morphisms between the sets $U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x) \cap F \cap F'$ and $U_F(x') \cap U_{F'}(x') \cap F \cap F'$.

Such data form a compatible assignment ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.isCompatibleAssignment⟧: the restrictions of the two tuples to $F \cap F'$ are equivalent, with $O(x) = U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x)$, equal index sets, and equal correspondences on the morphisms between these sets. *Statement*: for $X$ tame and face-structured with $|X|$ paracompact, the glued function $\Lambda(w) = \Lambda_F(w)$ for $P(w) \in F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.Λg⟧ is structurable over $\partial X$ and equals $\Lambda_F$ over each face $F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.Λg_eq⟧; its structure restricts to the given ones.

*Narrower*: the input is representatives that agree, not a compatible assignment of classes. The text says that the compatibility gives $s^x_{F,i} = s^x_{F',i}$ on $U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x)$. As we read Definition 14.6.2, this does not follow: the equivalence of Definition 13.3.8, and its analogue here, compares $\Lambda$, the index sets and the correspondences on smaller neighbourhoods, not the sections, so two equivalent tuples may have different sections at the same index. *An illustration* (not formalized): on a face with trivial isotropy along which the only morphisms are identities, take $I_x = \{1, 2\}$ at every point, sections $s^x_1$, $s^x_2$ that agree across the neighbourhoods but $s_1 \ne s_2$, and correspondences that pair each index with itself. Exchanging $s^x_1$ and $s^x_2$ at every $x$ gives a tuple with the same $\Lambda$ (the counting formula is symmetric in the indices), the same index sets, and the same correspondences, which still satisfy (4), since the pair $(i, i)$ now relates the exchanged sections, which again agree. The two tuples are equivalent, and their sections at the index $1$ differ. Over one face such a difference can be undone by relabelling; the text's step asks that it can be undone on all faces through $x$ at once, consistently with the correspondences. Presumably the text means that representatives can be chosen so that they agree; we neither prove this nor claim the contrary. The two routes to the class-level statement are gap G.173 (§XIV.29).

*Proof*, the text's, as the Lean proof goes.

1. *The glued functor.* $\Lambda(w) = \Lambda_F(w)$ for any face $F \ni P(w)$, and $0$ off $\partial X$. It is well defined by the agreement of the $\Lambda_F$ on $F \cap F'$, and defined on all of $W|\partial X$ because every boundary point lies on a face (fact 2 of §XIV.27). It is a functor over $\partial X$: for $s(\varphi) \in F$, also $t(\varphi) \in F$ (fact 4), and $\Lambda_F$ is a functor over $F$.
2. *A face selection.* For $x \in \partial X$ and objects $y$, $x'$, choose a face through $y$, $x$ and $x'$ if there is one, and otherwise any face through $x$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.faceSel⟧; when one exists, the chosen face contains all three ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.faceSel_spec⟧. The glued sections and correspondences are read from the selected face: $s^x_i(y) = s^x_{F,i}(y)$ with $F$ selected for $(x, y, x)$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.sg⟧, and $\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi) = \tau_{F,x,x'}(\varphi)$ with $F$ selected for $(x, s(\varphi), x')$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.τg⟧. That the choice does not matter is proved in step 4.
3. *An adapted good system* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.exists_adapted⟧, the text's choice of $V(x)$ with $U(x) \cap F \subset U_F(x)$. A good system $\mathcal W$ for $\partial X$ is *adapted* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.Adapted⟧ if for every $x \in \partial X$ and $y \in U(x)$: every face through $y$ contains $x$; and for every face $F \ni x$, $y \in U_F(x)$ and $\Gamma(g, y) = \Gamma_F(g, y)$ for all $g \in G_x$. *Construction*: (a) a good system $\mathcal U_0$ for $\partial X$ from Theorem 14.1.6 (§XIV.4); (b) at each $x$, an open $O(x) \ni x$ on which every face through a point contains $x$ (fact 3); (c) at each $x$, a neighbourhood $M(x) \subset O(x)$ with the natural action, below $U_0(x)$ and below each of the finitely many $U_F(x)$, $F \ni x$ (fact 2), with the restricted actions: the common refinement of finitely many natural neighbourhoods of $x$ (Part XIII); (d) a refinement of $\mathcal U_0$ inside the $M(x)$ (§XIV.4). The natural action on $V(x)$ is that of $U_0(x)$, which on $M(x)$ is that of $M(x)$, which is that of each $U_F(x)$. Two consequences: on $U(x)$ the natural actions of $V(x)$ and $V_F(x)$ agree ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.Φ_eq⟧, as targets of the same morphisms $\Gamma(g, y)$; and $U(x) \cap F \subset U_F(x)$ for the faces $F \ni x$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue_U_inter_subset⟧.
4. *The glued data agree with the face data.* On $U(x) \cap F$, $s^x_i = s^x_{F,i}$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.sg_eq⟧: for $y \in U(x) \cap F$, $F$ contains $x$ (adapted), so a face through $y$ and $x$ exists and the selected face $G$ contains both; $y \in U_G(x) \cap U_F(x) \cap G \cap F$ (adapted), where $s^x_{G,i} = s^x_{F,i}$ by the input. A morphism $\varphi$ between $U(x)$ and $U(x')$ with source on $F$ is one between $U_F(x) \cap F$ and $U_F(x') \cap F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.mem_mor_face⟧: $t(\varphi) \in F$ (saturation), $x, x' \in F$ (adapted), and the traces lie in $U_F$ (adapted). Hence on such morphisms $\tau_{x,x'} = \tau_{F,x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.τg_eq⟧, by the input's agreement of the correspondences for the selected face and $F$.
5. *The symmetric structure on $U(x)$* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.S⟧, with index set $I_x$ and sections $s^x_i$.
   - *Face-wise sc⁺* (Definition 14.1.3 (1)), by the gluing criterion of §XIV.27: the values lie in $W_{0,1}$ because at $y$, on a face $F \ni y$, $s^x_i(y) = s^x_{F,i}(y)$, which is sc⁺ relative to $F$; and near $y$, on each face $F \ni y$, $s^x_i$ agrees on $F \cap U(x)$ with $s^x_{F,i}$, which is sc⁺ relative to $F$ at $y$.
   - *Equivariant*: for $y \in U(x)$ on a face $F$, also $g * y \in F$ (fact 4); both sides are read in $F$ by step 4, the natural actions of $V(x)$ and $V_F(x)$ agree there by step 3, and $S_F$ is equivariant.
   - *Represents $\Lambda$*: for $P(w) \in U(x) \cap F$, $\Lambda(w) = \Lambda_F(w)$, which is $|I_x|^{-1}$ times the number of $i$ with $s^x_{F,i}(P(w)) = w$, the same as the number with $s^x_i(P(w)) = w$ by step 4.

   So the glued $\Lambda$ is an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.isBoundaryScPlusMultisection⟧, with the decoration $(\mathcal W, S)$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.dec⟧.
6. *The correspondences* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.tau⟧, $\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi) = \tau_{F,x,x'}(\varphi)$ for $s(\varphi) \in F$.
   - *Locally constant*. Near $\varphi$, every face through the source of a nearby morphism contains $s(\varphi)$ (fact 3, pulled back by the continuous $s$). For each of the finitely many faces $F \ni s(\varphi)$, $\tau_F$ is locally constant at $\varphi$. Intersecting these finitely many neighbourhoods, a nearby $\psi$ in the morphism set has its source on some face $G$, which contains $s(\varphi)$, and $\tau(\psi) = \tau_G(\psi) = \tau_G(\varphi) = \tau(\varphi)$ by step 4.
   - *Finitely many values*: every value is a value of some $\tau_F$ with $F$ through $x$ and $x'$, a finite union of finite sets.
   - *(a) Inversion*: $s(\varphi^{-1}) = t(\varphi) \in F$; read both sides in $F$.
   - *(b) The diagonal*: $\Gamma(g, z)$ has source $z$; for $z$ on $F$, $\Gamma(g, z) = \Gamma_F(g, z)$ by step 3, and $\tau_F$ has (b).
   - *(c) The bi-action*: the source of $g' * \varphi * g$ is $\Phi(g^{-1})(s(\varphi))$, on $F$ by fact 4. The bi-action computed with the natural actions of $V(x)$, $V(x')$ equals that computed with those of $V_F(x)$, $V_F(x')$, by step 3; then $\tau_F$ has (c).
   - *(4) Compatibility*: read in the face of $s(\varphi)$, with $s^{x'}_j(t(\varphi)) = s^{x'}_{F,j}(t(\varphi))$ and $s^x_i(s(\varphi)) = s^x_{F,i}(s(\varphi))$ by step 4.
7. *The structured tuple* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue⟧: $(\Lambda, \mathcal W, S, \tau)$, so $\Lambda$ is structurable over $\partial X$. It restricts to the face data: $s^x_i = s^x_{F,i}$ on $U(x) \cap F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue_s⟧, and $\tau_{x,x'} = \tau_{F,x,x'}$ on the morphisms of $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with source on $F$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue_τ⟧.

*Witness* ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.zero⟧: the zero multisection on every face, on the index family $I_x = \{*\}$; all agreements are equalities of zero data, and the glued $\Lambda$ is the zero multisection over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.zero_Λg⟧. It charges every boundary fibre (the zero vector has weight $1$), so it also satisfies the charging hypothesis of the extension part below. The witness is degenerate in the sections, all zero, but not in the boundary: tame face-structured ep-groupoids with $|X|$ paracompact and $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ exist (Part XI).

**The extension part** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.theorem_14_6_3_extension_a6⟧. *Statement*: let $X$ be face-structured (hence tame) with $|X|$ paracompact, with sc-smooth partitions of unity on the object M-polyfold and a tame strong bundle chart at every object, and let face data with agreeing representatives be given whose glued $\Lambda$ charges every boundary fibre. For $N$, $\tilde U$, $f$ as in Theorem 14.1.9 (with the boundary domain support of the glued $\Lambda$), there is a structurable $\Lambda'$ on $W$ with $N(\Lambda') \le f$, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda') \subset \tilde U$, and $\Lambda' = \Lambda_F$ over every face $F$. *Proof*: 1. The glued $\Lambda$ is structurable over $\partial X$ (above). 2. Theorem 14.1.9 with charging (§XIV.7, proved in §XIV.25) gives $\Lambda'$ with the size and support properties and $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. 3. For $P(w) \in F$, $P(w) \in \partial X$ (fact 1), so $\Lambda'(w) = \Lambda(w) = \Lambda_F(w)$. *Narrower*: the agreeing representatives, and the two readings of Theorem 14.1.9 (§XIV.7). Charging is necessary here too, since the conclusion makes $\Lambda$ the restriction of a structurable functor (§XIV.7).

*Remark: the form with the uncharged statement.* A form taking the uncharged Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 as a hypothesis ⟦Chapter14/FaceAssembly · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.theorem_14_6_3_extension_hyp⟧ remains in the formalization, with the same proof. That hypothesis holds only when $\partial X = \emptyset$ (§XIV.7), in which case there are no faces and the statement says nothing; the form above does not use it.

### XIV.29 What is not formalized

Every numbered statement of Chapter 14 is formalized, either as printed or in a form recorded in its subsection. What remains open is listed here by gap number, with what is missing and an estimate in lines of Lean. None of the open gaps lies on the path of Theorem 14.1.9: the theorem, with its two readings, is proved from the construction of §§14.2–14.5, and its extension part over the faces from Theorem 14.6.3 for agreeing representatives.

- **Gap G.172**, the multisection form of Lemma 14.5.2 (formalized in part, §XIV.22). *Formalized*: the identity for the summed sections, $\sum_a \tilde s^a_{b,j} = s^{0b}_j$ over $\partial X$, which is the only use the proof of Theorem 14.1.9 makes of the lemma. *Missing*: that the structured functors $\Lambda_a = (\beta_a|\partial X) \odot \Lambda$ form a commensurable, locally finite family over $\partial X$ whose sum is $\Lambda$. This is a boundary version of the commensurable sums of Part XIII (Definitions 13.3.11 and 13.4.5): the index sets and correspondences of $\Lambda$ would be carried to each $\Lambda_a$, the commensurability checked on the common good system of §XIV.21, and the sum computed fibrewise from the section identity. About 120 lines. Nothing formalized uses it. Remark 14.5.3, which explains the lemma, is prose.
- **Gap G.173**, Theorem 14.6.3 from a class-level compatible assignment (§XIV.28). *Formalized*: faces as Part XI's ep-faces with their local properties; sc⁺ relative to a face and on a corner; Definitions 14.6.1 and 14.6.2, with the two consequences the text draws; good systems on a face up to equivalence; Theorem 14.6.3 for face data whose chosen representatives agree on the intersections of faces; and its extension part, from Theorem 14.1.9 with charging. *Missing*: the passage from a compatible assignment of classes, $\tilde\Lambda_F|F' = \tilde\Lambda_{F'}|F$, to representatives that agree. The equivalence of structured multisections on a face compares $\Lambda$, the index sets and the correspondences on smaller neighbourhoods, not the sections, so two routes are open. (a) *A re-choice of representatives*: near each $x \in \partial X$, relabellings $I^{F'}_x \to I^F_x$ compatible with the correspondences and with the $G_x$-action, carrying the sections of $F'$ to those of $F$ on $F \cap F'$, chosen consistently over the finitely many faces through $x$ (at a corner of index $d$ the $d$ relabellings must commute) and locally constant in $x$; possibly with a hypothesis on the local constancy of the relabelling where two sections cross. About 350–550 lines. (b) *An example*: two equivalent representatives over a corner whose sections differ by an index swap, such that no re-choice agrees on two faces at once, which would show that the text's step needs the agreeing representatives as an assumption. About 150–250 lines. We do not know which of the two holds.
- **Gap G.185**, condition (2) of a good system on a face (formalized in part, §XIV.27). *Formalized*: every structured sc⁺-multisection on $W|F$ has a representative whose neighbourhoods $U_F(x)$ satisfy (1), the properness of $t$ over the closure, and (3), the component condition, inside the face ep-groupoid, and are invariant under the natural action of $X$ restricted to $U(x) \cap F$. *Missing*: condition (2) of Definition 13.1.4 in the strict sense, a natural representation of the ep-groupoid $F$ itself with a connected domain inside $F$ (Theorem 7.1.13, Part VII, applied to $F$), and its identification with the restricted action of $X$ near $x$. About 150–250 lines. Nothing in §14.6 uses it: the gluing of Theorem 14.6.3 reads the neighbourhoods $U_F(x)$ as $U(x) \cap F$, as the text explains them on p. 680.
- **Gap G.186**, the readings of the standing hypotheses of Theorem 14.1.9 (§§XIV.3, XIV.7, XIV.26). (a) *Non-empty index sets in the formal Definition 14.1.3.* The theorem is stated with charging, which for a structured $\Lambda$ is the same as $I_x \ne \emptyset$ at every boundary point, and which is necessary. Building $I_x \ne \emptyset$ into the definition itself is an edit of an existing definition, with about 20–60 lines of follow-up where structures with empty index sets serve as witnesses; charging would then follow from structurability. (b) *A witness with $\partial X \ne \emptyset$* in which all hypotheses of the theorem hold jointly, tame strong bundle charts included: done, the half-space bundle with a constant non-zero section (§XIV.26). (c) *The tame strong bundle charts at every object derived from the tameness of $X$*, if that holds: a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid would be shown to have, at every object, a strong bundle chart whose base retraction is tame, by Part I's construction of tame retractions applied to the base of a strong bundle retraction and lifted to the bundle. About 300–600 lines.
- **Lemma 14.4.13 (2) at every point of $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$** (§XIV.19). Proved for points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, which is what Proposition 14.4.14 uses. The printed range would need a coherent system with (4) at the other points, which the stronger Lemma 14.4.9 (3) of §XIV.17 permits. About 90 lines; not needed.
- **Prose.** Remarks 14.1.10, 14.3.5, 14.4.1, 14.4.12 and 14.5.3 are explanatory and have nothing to formalize beyond what their subsections record.

*Closed gaps*, for reference: G.164, Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$ (§XIV.6); G.165, the faces $\bar\theta_j$ as tame M-polyfolds (§XIV.1); G.168, Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in general (§XIV.16); G.169, the setting of §14.4 from the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.13); G.170, the proof of Proposition 14.5.4 (§XIV.23); G.171, the data of §§14.3–14.5 for every charging $\Lambda$ (§XIV.25); G.184, sc⁺ on the corners $F \cap F'$ (§XIV.27).

### XIV.30 What the formalization taught us

**No statement of Chapter 14 was found not to hold as we read it.** Two statements are proved with readings that are hypotheses of their Lean form (Theorem 14.1.9: tame strong bundle charts and charging; Theorem 14.6.3: agreeing representatives), and one has a printed range wider than its proof covers (Lemma 14.4.13 (2)). The rest is proved as printed, or in a stronger form.

**Two kinds of formal content.** Chapter 14 is the longest construction of the book, and what it needs splits in two.

The first kind is *local topology of the morphism space*: shrinking good neighbourhoods so that closures stay inside (Lemma 14.2.1, §XIV.8), separating the values of a locally constant correspondence by open sets (Lemma 14.3.1, §XIV.9), extending it by components (Proposition 14.3.4, §XIV.10), and choosing neighbourhoods compatible with the action and with local finiteness (Lemmas 14.3.6, 14.3.7, Proposition 14.4.10, §§XIV.11, XIV.18). All of it rests on three facts used again and again. First, $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}$ of the closure of a good neighbourhood, so a property of the morphisms from a point persists near it. Second, $s$ and $t$ are local homeomorphisms on sheets, so the sheet through a morphism is locally constant. Third, a locally constant function on an open set is constant on its components. The diagonal property of Proposition 14.3.4, for which the text gives no argument, is the second fact applied through sheet labels: the component of $\Gamma(g, y)$ stays in the sheet of $g$ and reaches the boundary there (§XIV.10). The inversion symmetry of the extended correspondences, which the text does not state, costs one more intersection in Lemma 14.3.1 and is what the z-loops of §14.4 need to be reversible (§§XIV.9, XIV.14).

The second kind is *combinatorics of index sets along chains of morphisms*. Encoding a z-loop together with its arc as one inductive predicate, built by appending one morphism and one index step at a time, made the equivalence-relation properties of $\sim_z$, which the text asserts, and Lemma 14.4.5 short (§XIV.14). It made Proposition 14.4.6 (1) a deformation of the chain along sheets, one morphism at a time, without Lemma 14.4.7 (§XIV.15). It carried the limit argument of Proposition 14.4.6 (2): with Lemma 14.4.7 around the finitely many isomorphs of the limit point, each step of a nearby loop moves along its own sheet to the boundary, so the text's limit loop need not be built, and the result holds for loops at points of $\hat V_a$, the form Lemma 14.4.9 (3) uses (§XIV.16). It also carried Proposition 14.5.4: defining the transported section through chains rather than single morphisms gives its equivariance and its compatibility with $\hat\tau$ directly, and its well-definedness is the text's closing of two chains into a loop (§XIV.23).

**Steps that needed less than printed.**

- *Theorem 14.5.5* needs neither its properness nor its closure condition: local transports into the sets $V_a$ and the conjugation homomorphisms of Theorem 13.5.3 (Part XIII) carry the structure (§XIV.24).
- *Lemma 14.5.1* does not use tameness, and (14.53) holds for the cover of §14.3 itself, without the shrinking the text performs: a morphism from an invariant subset of a natural neighbourhood to a point of its closure ends in that subset, because the isotropy group is finite and the morphism space Hausdorff (§XIV.21).
- *Lemma 14.5.2* enters the proof of Theorem 14.1.9 only through its identity for the summed sections; the commensurable family over $\partial X$ is not needed (§XIV.22, gap G.172).
- *Proposition 14.1.8* holds along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms and their classes without the paracompactness of the orbit spaces (§XIV.6).
- *Definition 14.4.11 (2)* is not needed once Proposition 14.4.14 is proved by averaging (§§XIV.18, XIV.20).
- *Proposition 14.4.6 (1)* does not need Lemma 14.4.7 (§XIV.15).

**Steps that needed more, or a different argument.**

- *Proposition 14.1.4.* The local extension cannot be glued with one partition of unity of $X$, because the boundary data on an open $V(x)$ may be unbounded near its frontier. An exhaustion of $V(x)$ by the sets at distance $> 1/n$ from its complement, glued by sc-smooth cut-offs, does it (§XIV.3).
- *Averaging.* Averaging over the whole isotropy group, $\bar s_j(y) = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_g \mu(\Gamma(g^{-1}, g * y), s_{g(j)}(g * y))$, replaces the text's average over a stabilizer together with transport along an orbit, both in Proposition 14.1.4 and in Proposition 14.4.14. In Proposition 14.4.14 it also replaces the class-by-class, orbit-by-orbit construction with an invariant partition of unity (§§XIV.3, XIV.20).
- *Theorem 14.1.6* is proved from tameness of $X$ and paracompactness of $|X|$, which its proof uses, in place of the paracompactness of $|\partial X|$ printed in the statement (§XIV.4).
- *The size control of Theorem 14.1.9* hides one choice: the extension must be taken with support in $\{f > 0\}$, not merely in $\tilde U$, or the cut-off cannot reach the boundary points where $f = 0$; and the inequality $N(\Lambda) < f$ is needed, and assumed, on the boundary domain support rather than on all of $\partial X$ (§§XIV.7, XIV.25).
- *Proposition 14.5.4* needs one property of the cut-offs that its statement does not list, that $\beta_a$ vanishes off the saturation of $\hat V_a$; Lemma 14.5.1 (1) gives it (§XIV.23).
- *Index sets on two domains.* The index sets of §14.1 live on boundary points and those of §14.4 on all objects; a map to boundary points that is the identity on $\partial X$, with the identity on morphisms as a homomorphism of isotropy groups, joins them (§XIV.13).
- *Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$* carries everything along except Definition 14.1.3 (1), which is read in every tame strong bundle chart; its transport needs that tame charts compose with local strong bundle isomorphisms, a fact Part I proved for Theorem 3.6.8 (§XIV.6).
- *Sc⁺ on corners.* The restriction of Definition 14.6.1 is sc⁺ on the corner $F \cap F'$ because, in a tame model, the corner germ $\{t_i = t_j = 0\}$ is itself an sc-retract by Part I's corner retraction, and an sc⁺ map on a face germ restricts to it (§XIV.27).

**Readings.** Each is recorded in its subsection; together:

- Lemma 14.2.2: the morphism sets $\mathcal U(x, x')$ are read with $t(\varphi) \in U(x')$, as in (P3), where the text prints $U(x)$ (§XIV.8).
- Definition 14.4.8: the last index of an $\approx_z$-chain is $i_k$ (§XIV.17).
- Proposition 14.4.6 (2): the loops are taken at points $z_k \in \hat V_a$ (§XIV.16).
- Definition 14.4.11 (3): read for the closure, as Lemma 14.4.9 provides it (§XIV.18).
- Lemma 14.4.13 (2): stated for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, the range Definition 14.4.11 (4) covers and Proposition 14.4.14 uses (§XIV.19).
- Definition 14.1.3 (1): "$s|\bar\theta_j$ is sc⁺" read through the tame strong bundle charts of $X$, on every local face germ (§XIV.2); likewise sc⁺ relative to a face and on a corner (§XIV.27).
- Theorem 14.1.9: "a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid" read as tame strong bundle charts at every object; the factor $|I_x|^{-1}$ read as charging; "supported in $\tilde U$" read as $\operatorname{cl}\{f \ne 0\} \subset \tilde U$ (§XIV.7).
- §14.6: "good neighbourhood $U_F(x) \subset F$" read as $U(x) \cap F$ with the restricted natural action (§XIV.27); Theorem 14.6.3 read with representatives that agree on $F \cap F'$ (§XIV.28).

**A property of our own formalization.** Definition 14.1.3 (3) writes $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\cdot\#\{i : s^x_i(P(w)) = w\}$, which presumes $I_x \ne \emptyset$. The formal definition does not ask for it, so the zero function, with empty index sets, counts as structurable over $\partial X$, and no structurable extension can vanish over a boundary fibre. A Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 without the charging condition, and every hypothesis that asks for its conclusion for all $\Lambda$, therefore holds only when $\partial X = \emptyset$ (§XIV.7); witnesses on spaces without boundary cannot reveal this, since every condition on $\partial X$ is then vacuous. Two lessons follow for the formalization rather than for the text. A witness on a space without boundary says nothing about a statement on $\partial X$; the half-space bundle (§XIV.26) is the witness that does. And a statement about structurable functors should be checked against the zero function with empty index sets, which the formal definitions admit and the printed formulas exclude. Stated with charging, the theorem is proved, and charging is necessary: the theorem is an equivalence (§XIV.7).

**§14.6.** The step from compatible classes to agreeing representatives is where the text is shortest. The equivalence of structured multisections compares $\Lambda$, the index sets and the correspondences, not the sections, so the text's identification $s^x_{F,i} = s^x_{F',i}$ is a choice of representatives, which Theorem 14.6.3 takes as its input (§XIV.28, gap G.173). Everything else in §14.6 is local: faces are closed and saturated, every boundary point lies on finitely many, near a point every face through a nearby point contains it, and a local face of a tame chart lies in one face (§XIV.27). These four facts, with the gluing criterion for sc⁺ on faces, are the whole proof of the gluing.

**How the chapter is used later.** Theorem 14.1.9 is the tool by which the transversality results of Chapter 15 and the cobordism results of Chapter 16 control a multisection near the boundary. Theorem 15.3.9 (Part XV) uses it in its charged form, with the same two readings, tame strong bundle charts at every object and charging; the cut-off step of its proof uses the extension of face-wise sc⁺ sections of Proposition 14.1.4 (§XIV.3) and Definition 14.1.3 (1) read through the charts (§XIV.2). Theorem 16.5.7 (Part XVI) uses it in one representative of a strong polyfold bundle, and the transport between representatives is Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$ (§XIV.6). In both places the remark of §XIV.7 has a counterpart: a Lean statement that takes the uncharged form of Theorem 14.1.9 as a hypothesis, or asks its conclusion for every structurable $\Lambda$, holds only without boundary, and the charged form replaces it. What these later chapters need from Chapter 14 is therefore exactly what is proved here: the charged theorem, its necessity, the transport over $\partial X$, and the half-space witness with boundary.

**A note on how the proof is organized.** The text proves Theorem 14.1.9 in one pass, introducing the objects of each section from those of the previous one. The formalization splits each step into an abstract statement over a structure that names its inputs, and an instance built from the objects of the construction (§§XIV.13, XIV.25). The split made three things visible. First, which properties of the previous objects each step actually uses: Theorem 14.5.5 uses neither properness nor closures, Lemma 14.5.1 not tameness, Proposition 14.4.14 not Definition 14.4.11 (2). Second, where a step uses a property its statement does not list: Proposition 14.5.4 and the support of the cut-offs. Third, where each standing hypothesis enters: paracompactness of $|X|$ through the good systems of Theorem 14.1.6 and Part XIII and through the size control; tameness through Proposition 14.1.1 and the faces; the sc-smooth partitions of unity and the tame strong bundle charts through the local extensions of Propositions 14.1.4 and 14.4.14, the charts also through Definition 14.1.3 (1) and its transport (§XIV.6). Each of these is named in the subsection where it is used.

## Part XV. Transversality and invariants (HWZ Chapter 15, §§15.1–15.4)

Chapter 15 (Springer 2021, pp. 683–703; the 2017 numbers in parentheses) is the perturbation theory of an sc-Fredholm section functor $f$ of a strong bundle $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid by sc⁺-multisections $\Lambda$, and the invariants obtained from the perturbed solution sets $\Lambda \circ f$. §15.1 defines the linearization $T(f, \Lambda)$ of $\Lambda \circ f$, a section functor with values in the formal sums $\mathrm{GrF}$ of sc-Fredholm operators, and proves that it is well defined through a separation argument for finitely many sections (Theorem 15.1.1, Remark 15.1.2, Proposition 15.1.3, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5, Remark 15.1.6, Definition 15.1.7 (2017: Theorem 15.1, Remark 15.1, Proposition 15.1, Lemmas 15.1, 15.2, Definition 15.1; Remark 15.1.6 is new in 2021)). §15.2 defines transversality and good position and describes the local solution sets, which make $\Lambda \circ f$ a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid (Definitions 15.2.1, 15.2.4, Theorems 15.2.2, 15.2.5, Remarks 15.2.3, 15.2.6). §15.3 controls compactness by an auxiliary norm, defines admissible perturbations and general position, and constructs perturbations: Theorem 15.3.7 (general position), Theorem 15.3.9 (transversal extension of boundary data) and Corollary 15.3.10 (regular perturbations exist, and any two are joined over the cylinder $[0, 1] \times X$). §15.4 orients $\Lambda \circ f$ by an orientation of $f$ (Theorem 15.4.1, Definition 15.4.2) and integrates sc-differential forms over it: Stokes' theorem (Theorem 15.4.3) and the invariant on de Rham cohomology (Corollary 15.4.4). This Part retells the formal proofs in the book's order: §15.1 in §§XV.1–XV.11, §15.2 in §§XV.12–XV.16, §15.3 in §§XV.17–XV.33 (the definitions in §§XV.17–XV.20, Theorem 15.3.7 in §§XV.21–XV.26, Theorem 15.3.9 in §§XV.27–XV.29, Corollary 15.3.10 in §§XV.30–XV.33), §15.4 in §§XV.34–XV.37; then what is not formalized (§XV.38) and what the formalization taught us (§XV.39).

**What is proved, and what is not.** *§15.1.* *Theorem 15.1.1* (narrower) is proved in its substance in a stronger form: the formal sum $\sum_{f(x) = s_i(x)}\sigma_i \cdot (f - s_i)'(x)$ does not depend on the local sc⁺-section structure or on the chart, at every level-$1$ point, for any sc-smooth $f$, with no use of positivity of the weights or of the functoriality of $\Lambda$ (§§XV.2, XV.7); the value $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is Definition 15.1.7 (§XV.8); the functor property $T(f, \Lambda)(t(\varphi)) = \varphi_*T(f, \Lambda)(s(\varphi))$ holds at all level-$1$ points, with no added hypothesis (§XV.9, gap G.144 closed). The row is narrower for one reason: the summands are proved sc-Fredholm in the chart reading and for $f$ with Part I's tame germ data (§XV.11, gap G.145 closed). *Remark 15.1.2* and *Definition 15.1.7* are restated (§§XV.2, XV.8). *Lemmas 15.1.4 and 15.1.5* are proved in a stronger, purely topological form (§§XV.4, XV.5), *Remark 15.1.6* with "slightly" made explicit (§XV.6). *Proposition 15.1.3* is proved with the added hypothesis that the base point is not isolated; at an isolated point, for instance for the one-point local model of a zero-dimensional $X$, it does not hold as we read it, since no sequence $x_k \ne x_0$ converges to $x_0$. The case is degenerate and does not reach Theorem 15.1.1, whose formal proof does not use the proposition (§§XV.3, XV.7). The proof of Theorem 15.1.1 is read in two places: the separation and the limit run in the level-$1$ topology, the "weak topology" being pointwise convergence of operators; and the final sum is presumably over the $i$ with $f(0) = s_i(0)$ (§XV.7).

*§15.2.* Definitions 15.2.1 and 15.2.4 are restated, the first with "nonzero" and "sc-Fredholm" automatic (§§XV.12, XV.15). Theorems 15.2.2, 15.2.5 and Remark 15.2.3 (narrower) are proved with Part I's tame germ data for $f$, inherited from Part I's Theorem 3.6.8, on which they rest; this is the only hypothesis they add. Their "tame" submanifolds and tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids (Definition 9.3.6) are proved (§§XV.14, XV.16, gap G.150 closed). "The ep-groupoid $U(x)$" of Remark 15.2.3 is read as the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$; on it the statements hold as printed, the paracompactness of the support included (§XV.14, gap G.152 closed). Their global forms on $X$ take a paracompact orbit space of the support, Definition 9.1.2 (1), which is new in 2021 and which the remarks do not address. The closing sentence of Theorem 15.2.5, under general position, is proved for tame $X$ (§XV.16, gap G.151 closed). Remark 15.2.6 is prose.

*§15.3.* The paragraph before Definition 15.3.1, Definition 15.3.3 with its example, and the first sentence of Remark 15.3.6 are proved as stated; Definitions 15.3.1 and 15.3.5 are restated (§§XV.17, XV.18, XV.20). The rest of Remark 15.3.6 is proved at every point of the support, not only on $\partial X$, with the inherited tame germ data and, for the branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, a paracompact support (§XV.20, gap G.161 closed). The products remark after Definition 15.3.3: product ep-groupoids, product strong bundles, products of sections and section functors and the auxiliary norm $\max(N, N')$ are formalized; $f \times f'$ sc-Fredholm and $\Lambda \times \Lambda'$ (Remark 15.3.4) are not (§XV.19, gap G.160, in part). *Theorem 15.3.7* (explicit) is proved with the text's hypotheses, the inherited tame germ data being the only one not printed, with no good system and no paracompactness of $|X|$, as Remark 15.3.8 says; the addendum "structurable" needs a good system, which is necessary for it and which exists for paracompact $|X|$; its "in particular" holds with "tame" (§§XV.21–XV.26; gap G.162 closed for Theorem 15.3.7). *Theorem 15.3.9* (narrower) is proved in the charged form, the boundary multisection having non-empty index sets, which the conclusion forces, from tame strong bundle charts and one open proposition, the relative local families of steps (c)–(d) (gap G.178); its face condition is asked for every sc⁺ extension (gap G.179); step (a) is proved (gap G.177 closed), step (b) is Theorem 14.1.9 in its charged form (Part XIV), and the Sard and compactness parts of steps (c)–(d) are proved (§§XV.27–XV.29). Its witnesses have no boundary and zero fibres. *Corollary 15.3.10* (1) follows from Theorem 15.3.7 for paracompact $|X|$, with bump functions and the tame germ data, the tameness of $X$ derived from $d_X \equiv 0$ (§§XV.30, XV.31, gap G.183 closed); (2) is proved with an explicit interpolated auxiliary norm (§XV.31); (3) is reduced to the charged Theorem 15.3.9 on $[0, 1] \times X$, with the partitions of unity of the cylinder proved from those of $X$ (gap G.181 closed), the structurability of the glued boundary data proved given that lifted sc⁺-sections are sc⁺ on the faces (gap G.193), and the face condition of the glued data and tame strong bundle charts on the cylinder as hypotheses (gaps G.180, G.189) (§§XV.32, XV.33). The last paragraph of the proof of the corollary is proved as printed (§XV.33). Remarks 15.3.2 and 15.3.11 are prose.

*§15.4.* Theorem 15.4.1 and Definition 15.4.2 (narrower) are proved at a single point, in Part I's chart reading: the operators $(f - s_i)'(y)$ lie in Part I's $\mathrm{Lin}(f, y)$, the canonical lift exists, has the text's formula, is unique and does not depend on the local structure, and the kernel orientations are defined; their assembly into an orientation of $\Lambda \circ f$ is open (§XV.34, gap G.159, in part). Theorem 15.4.3 (narrower) is proved with the orientation as data, by Part IX's Stokes theorem (§XV.35). Corollary 15.4.4 (narrower) is proved by the text's cobordism argument from oriented cobordisms between regular perturbations; on the cylinder the ends and the splitting of the boundary measure are proved, and the oriented end identities are a hypothesis (gaps G.182, G.190); the effective version adds the local unique continuation property on the cylinder (gap G.191) (§§XV.36, XV.37). Remark 15.4.5 is prose.

*Open:* G.159 and G.160 in part; G.162 for Theorem 15.3.9 and Corollary 15.3.10 (3); G.178–G.180, G.182, G.189–G.191, G.193 (§XV.38). *Closed:* G.144, G.145, G.150–G.152, G.161, G.177, G.181, G.183. Proposition 15.1.3 at an isolated point is the one statement of the chapter that does not hold as we read it, a degenerate case; no statement of §§15.2–15.4 was found not to hold as we read it.

**The decisions that shape the chapter.** (1) *Formal sums are finitely supported functions.* $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is the type of finitely supported functions from the linear maps $T_xX \to W_x$ to $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$, defined at every level-$1$ point ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.GrF⟧; that the operators are sc-Fredholm is proved for the operators that occur, not built into the type. On a strong bundle model the operators are $T_zO \to F_0$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.GrFModel⟧. (2) *The separation argument is pure topology.* Proposition 15.1.3, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5 and Remark 15.1.6 are proved for finitely many continuous maps into a Hausdorff space and applied on the level-$1$ subspace of the model, where the sections and their derivatives are continuous. (3) *Pairs, not operators.* The proof of Theorem 15.1.1 compares finite formal sums of pairs (value, derivative) over all branches, $\mathrm{wsum}(a, \sigma)(q) = \sum_{i : a_i = q}\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum⟧ with masses of sets ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass⟧ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass_eq_of_wsum_eq⟧; the sum of the theorem is the part with first entry $f(y)$. (4) *A branch is a section problem of Part I.* A local sc⁺-section $s_i$ on an open $O$ is a global sc⁺-section of the restricted bundle $W|_O$, and $(f - s_i)|_O$ is an sc-Fredholm section there (§XV.10); every analytic statement of §§15.2–15.4 is Part I's theorem applied branch by branch. The price is Part I's hypothesis: *tame germ data* for $f$, inherited from Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8, which are proved for it; with the untamed notion of 2021 Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it (Part III). (5) *Operators are read in charts.* $T_xX$ and $W_x$ carry no sc-structure in the project; "sc-Fredholm", "onto on $T^R_xX$" and "$\in \mathrm{Lin}(f, y)$" are read in a strong bundle chart, through the identifications that define the intrinsic operators, and shown independent of the chart where it matters. (6) *The cylinder is a product with Part I's cube.* $[0, 1] \times X$ is built as $[0, 1]^n \times X$ with $n = 1$, so that Part I's parametrized Fredholm theory applies to $\tilde f$ (§XV.30). (7) *Boundary data are charged.* A multisection over $\partial X$ is taken with non-empty index sets, as the text's "sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$" has them; Theorem 15.3.9 needs it, and the uncharged Lean statement does not hold when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ (§XV.27). (8) *Open steps are named propositions.* Where a theorem rests on a step that is not proved, the step is a named statement (for instance the relative local families of Theorem 15.3.9, the oriented end identities of Corollary 15.4.4), taken as a hypothesis with a witness, and the theorem is proved from it.

**Map.**

- *The linearization (§15.1).* `Chapter15/SeparationLemmas`: formal sums of points, Proposition 15.1.3 with its witness and the isolated point, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5, Remark 15.1.6, the limit step and the core lemma (§§XV.1, XV.3–XV.7). `LinearizationModel`: $\mathrm{GrF}$ on a strong bundle model, level-$1$ continuity and locality of derivatives, Theorem 15.1.1 and Remark 15.1.2 on the model (§§XV.2, XV.7). `Linearization`: principal parts and counts in a strong bundle chart, Theorem 15.1.1 in a chart, the chart form of Definition 15.1.7 (§§XV.7, XV.8). `LinearizationIntrinsic`: intrinsic operators, the change of chart, Theorem 15.1.1 with intrinsic operators, Definition 15.1.7 (§§XV.1, XV.7, XV.8). `LinearizationFunctor`: the action of morphisms on $\mathrm{GrF}$ and the functor property (§XV.9).
- *Branches as section problems, and §15.2.* `LocalScPlus`, `LocalIFT`: local sc⁺-sections on $W|_O$, the sections $f - s_i$, the chart linearization, local solution sets (§XV.10). `FredholmSummands`: the sc-Fredholm summands (§XV.11). `Transversality`: Definition 15.2.1, Theorem 15.2.2, Remark 15.2.3 (§§XV.12–XV.14). `BoundaryPerturbation`: Definition 15.2.4, Theorem 15.2.5 (§§XV.15, XV.16). `InteriorPerturbationWitness`, `GoodPositionWitness`, `TameWitness`: witnesses for §15.2. `TameBranched`: tame local solution sets and the tame forms of Remarks 15.2.3, 15.3.6, Theorems 15.2.5, 15.3.7 (§§XV.14, XV.16, XV.20, XV.21). `RestrictedEp`: the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$ and the statements on it (§§XV.14, XV.16). `GeneralPositionLocal`: general position at a point, its relation to good position and to Part I, Theorem 15.2.5 under general position (§XV.16).
- *Definitions of §15.3 and products.* `ControllingPairs`: Definitions 15.3.1, 15.3.3, 15.3.5, the paragraph before Definition 15.3.1, the example after Definition 15.3.3, the first sentence of Remark 15.3.6 (§§XV.17, XV.18, XV.20). `ProductEp`: product ep-groupoids (§XV.19). `ProductStrongBundle`, `ProductBundle`, `ProductBundleLevels`, `ProductBundleMap`, `ProductEpBundle`, `ProductAuxNorm`: product strong bundles, their levels and sections, the product over $X \times X'$, $\max(N, N')$ (§XV.19). `GoodPositionBranches`, `GeneralPositionBranched`: the rest of Remark 15.3.6, the statement of Theorem 15.3.7 and its "in particular" (§§XV.20, XV.21).
- *Theorem 15.3.7.* `ParamFamily`: linear families, (15.1), sums of families, norm and support bounds (§XV.22). `GeneralPositionAssembly`: the assembly from the local families and the parametric step (§XV.22). `ParamOntoTransport`, `LocalFamilies`, `LocalSeeds`: (15.1) with vectors and along morphisms, seeds, the local families (§XV.23). `ParamOntoBridge`: (15.1) and Part I's conditions (i)–(ii) (§XV.24). `LocalSlice`, `BranchChart`, `ParametricGeneralPosition`: the local Sard step, a branch as a Part I parametrized section, achieving global transversality (§XV.25). `GeneralPositionPointwise`, `GeneralPositionGoodSystem`, `GeneralPositionExistence`: the theorem with the text's hypotheses, the structurable form, Remark 15.3.8 (§XV.26).

Throughout, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ is a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor, and $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection with local sc⁺-section structures $(s_i, \sigma_i)$, the local representations of Definition 13.2.1 on open sets ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn⟧ (Part XIII). "Part I's" refers to Part I of the book (Chapters 1–6, M-polyfolds), whose statements Parts I–VI of this book retell.

### XV.1 The preamble of §15.1: $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ and finite formal sums

The text (p. 683) fixes, at a smooth point $x$, the set of sc-Fredholm operators $L : T_xX \to W_x$, and lets $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ consist of the finite formal sums $\sum\sigma_L \cdot L$ with non-negative rational coefficients; a morphism $\varphi : x \to y$ acts by $\varphi_*L \circ T\varphi = \mu(\varphi, L(\cdot))$, and $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$ becomes a category over $X$. Three objects of the formalization stand for this preamble.

**$\mathrm{GrF}(x)$** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.GrF⟧. For a level-$1$ point $x$, $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is the type of finitely supported functions from the linear maps $T_xX \to W_x$ to $\mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$, where $T_xX$ is the project's tangent fibre of the object M-polyfold (Part II of the book, with the linear structure of Chapter 2) and $W_x = P^{-1}(x)$ is the fibre with its vector space structure. Two departures from the text are deliberate. First, the point ranges over $X_1$, not only over $X_\infty$: the linearization of a section at a zero is defined at level-$1$ points already, and everything proved below holds there. Second, the operators are all linear maps, not only the sc-Fredholm ones. The sc-Fredholm property is a property of the operators that actually occur, proved for them in §XV.11; it is not built into the type, so that $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is a plain free commutative monoid on which sums, push-forwards and supports behave without side conditions. The text's $\mathrm{GrF}(X)$ and the category structure are not built as such; the action of morphisms is defined in §XV.9, where it is needed.

**On a strong bundle model** ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.GrFModel⟧. On a strong bundle model $U \triangleleft F$ with retraction $R$ and base retraction $r$, $O = r(U)$, the same object at a level-$1$ point $z$ is the type of finitely supported functions on the bounded operators $T_zO \to F_0$, where $T_zO = \operatorname{range} Dr(z)$ is the tangent space of the retract, as in Part I's linearization in a chart ⟦Chapter3/LinearizationCharts · linAt⟧. This is the form in which the analysis is done.

**Intrinsic operators from chart operators.** An operator of a strong bundle chart $c = (\varphi, \Phi)$ around $x$ becomes an element of $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ in two steps. First $L : E_0 \to F_0$ is read along $T_xX$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.chartOp⟧: $\alpha \mapsto L(T\varphi\,\alpha)$, where $T\varphi$ identifies $T_xX$ with the tangent space $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ of the model ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.chartOp_apply⟧. Then the values are pulled back to $W_x$ through the fibre part $\Phi_x : W_x \to F_0$ of the chart, which is linear and injective ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.toIntr⟧: if every value $L(T\varphi\,\alpha)$ lies in the range of $\Phi_x$, the operator is $\Phi_x^{-1} \circ L \circ T\varphi : T_xX \to W_x$, and otherwise it is $0$. The default value is never used: at a zero of a section that is sc-smooth in the chart, the chart derivative takes values in $\Phi_x(W_x)$ (§XV.7, step (f)), and then $\Phi_x \circ (\text{intrinsic operator}) = L \circ T\varphi$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.fiberLin_toIntr⟧.

**Finite formal sums of points.** The proof of Theorem 15.1.1 compares formal sums of *points*, not of operators, and the formalization makes these first-class. For finitely many points $a_i$ of a set $Q$ with weights $\sigma_i$ in a commutative monoid, the coefficient of $q$ in $\sum\sigma_i \cdot a_i$ is
$$\mathrm{wsum}(a, \sigma)(q) = \sum_{i : a_i = q}\sigma_i$$
⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum⟧, and the mass of a set $N \subseteq Q$ is $\mathrm{mass}(a, \sigma)(N) = \sum_{i : a_i \in N}\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass⟧. The mass is the sum of the coefficients over any finite set $S$ containing all $a_i$, restricted to $N$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass_eq_sum_wsum⟧ (exchange the two finite sums), so two families with the same coefficients have the same mass on every set: take $S$ the union of the two finite images ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass_eq_of_wsum_eq⟧. The coefficient of $q'$ in the image $\sum\sigma_i \cdot \psi(a_i)$ is the mass of $\psi^{-1}(q')$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_map⟧, so equal formal sums have equal images under every map ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_map_eq_of_wsum_eq⟧. This last remark is the formal content of "select the terms with $s_i(y) = f(y)$, then forget the value": both are images, and images respect equality.

### XV.2 Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1) and Remark 15.1.2 (2017: 15.1): the statements as formalized

**The text.** For a strong bundle $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid, an sc-Fredholm section $f$ and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$, there is a section functor $T(f, \Lambda)$ of $\mathrm{GrF}(X) \to X_\infty$, uniquely characterized by (1) $T(f, \Lambda)(x) = 0$ off $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$, and (2) for $x$ in the support and any local sc⁺-section structure $(s_i, \sigma_i)_{i \in I}$ describing $\Lambda$ around $x$, $T(f, \Lambda)(y) = \sum_{\{i : f(y) = s_i(y)\}}\sigma_i \cdot (f - s_i)'(y)$ at smooth $y$ near $x$ (p. 684). The substance is that the right side of (2) does not depend on the structure; existence and uniqueness then follow from the covering of $X$ by structures. A local sc⁺-section structure is the local representation of Definition 13.2.1 (Part XIII) on an open set: sc⁺-sections $s_1, \dots, s_k$ on $O$ with positive rational weights summing to $1$ such that $\Lambda(w) = \sum_{i : w = s_i(P(w))}\sigma_i$ for $w$ over $O$ ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn⟧, with $s_i$ an sc⁺-section on $O$ ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn⟧, and an sc⁺-multisection is a functor $W \to \mathbb Q^{\ge 0}$ with such a structure on the domain of a natural representation around every object ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection⟧.

The formalization states the theorem three times, on three levels of the reduction "without loss of generality $X = O$", and then once more for the value of Definition 15.1.7 (§XV.8) and for the functor property (§XV.9).

**On a strong bundle model** (stronger than the text's local statement) ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.theorem_15_1_1_model⟧. Let $U \triangleleft F$ be a strong bundle model ($U$ relatively open in a partial quadrant, $R$ a strong bundle retraction, $O = r(U)$), and let $\hat f$, $\hat s_1, \dots, \hat s_k$, $\hat t_1, \dots, \hat t_l$ be principal parts $E_0 \to F_0$ with $\hat f \circ r$, $\hat s_i \circ r$, $\hat t_j \circ r$ sc-smooth on $U$. The formal sum at a level-$1$ point $z$ is
$$\sum_{i : \hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)}\sigma_i \cdot (\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z) \in \mathrm{GrF}_{\mathrm{model}}(z),\qquad (\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z) = D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(z)|_{T_zO}$$
⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.linSumModel⟧, with its coefficient of an operator $\ell$ the sum of the $\sigma_i$ with $\hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)$ and $(\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z) = \ell$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.linSumModel_apply⟧. If the two structures give the same weighted count $\sum_{i : \hat s_i(y) = v}\sigma_i = \sum_{j : \hat t_j(y) = v}\tau_j$ of every value $v$ at every $y \in O \cap N$, $N$ open, then the two formal sums agree at every level-$1$ point of $O \cap N$. The same holds after replacing each operator $D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(z)$ by its image under any map $\psi$ of operators ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.linSumModelMap⟧ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.linSumModelMap_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.theorem_15_1_1_model_map⟧; the map that matters is the passage to intrinsic operators. The statement is stronger than what the proof of the text needs in two ways: all level-$1$ points instead of the smooth ones, and no condition on $\Lambda$ at all, only that the two structures have the same counts. Neither positivity of the weights nor functoriality is used.

**In a strong bundle chart** (stronger) ⟦Chapter15/Linearization · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1⟧. For an sc-Fredholm section functor $f$ and two local sc⁺-section structures $(s_i, \sigma_i)$ on $O$ and $(t_j, \tau_j)$ on $O'$ of the same $\Lambda$, the formal sums $\sum_{i : f(y) = s_i(y)}\sigma_i \cdot (f - s_i)'(y)$, read in a strong bundle chart $c$ with domain in $O \cap O'$ ⟦Chapter15/Linearization · SBLocalization.linSumChart⟧, agree at every level-$1$ point of the chart. The same holds for any sc-smooth section $f$ ⟦Chapter15/Linearization · SBLocalization.linSumChart_eq⟧; this is what the proof uses.

**With intrinsic operators** (narrower, as the row of the theorem; stronger in its substance) ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_intrinsic⟧. The formal sum in $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ through a chart $c$,
$$\sum_{i : f(x) = s_i(x)}\sigma_i \cdot (f - s_i)'(x),\qquad (f - s_i)'(x) = \Phi_x^{-1} \circ D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(\varphi(x)) \circ T\varphi$$
⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linSumIntr⟧, is the same for two structures of $\Lambda$ on open $O$, $O'$, computed through any chart $c$ with domain in $O$ and any chart $c'$ with domain in $O'$, at every $x \in X_1$ in both domains. This is the text's (2) with the operators in their intrinsic form, and the formulation in which Definition 15.1.7 is made.

*Why the row is narrower.* What Theorem 15.1.1 claims beyond the independence is (a) that $T(f, \Lambda)$ is a *section functor*, which is proved at all level-$1$ points in §XV.9, and (b) that its values lie in $\mathrm{GrF}$, i.e. that the summands are sc-Fredholm. (b) is proved in §XV.11 only in a chart reading, since $T_xX$ and $W_x$ carry no sc-structure of their own in the project, and only for $f$ with Part I's tame germ data, the hypothesis of Part I's implicit function theorem on which the proof rests. That inherited hypothesis is the only reason the row is narrower; the independence itself is proved in a stronger form. The text's "uniquely characterized" is the remark that (1) and (2) determine the value at every point, which in the formalization is Definition 15.1.7 with $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ equal to the sum of *any* local data (§XV.8).

**Remark 15.1.2** (restated). The text observes that $(f - s_i)'(y)$ is undefined where $f(y) \ne s_i(y)$ but is not counted, and that with the empty sum equal to $0$, (1) follows from (2). In the formalization the operator $(\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z)$ is defined for every $i$, and the sum is filtered by $\hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)$; so the first half of the remark is the definition of the formal sum. The second half is proved on each level. *On the model* ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.remark_15_1_2_model⟧: if the weights are positive and the weighted count of $\hat f(z)$ is $0$, then each term of that count is $0$, so no $i$ has $\hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)$ (a term with $\hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)$ would contribute $\sigma_i > 0$), every summand of the formal sum is the empty case, and the formal sum is $0$. The same counting gives the description of the support used by Definition 15.2.1: with positive weights an operator $\ell$ has a nonzero coefficient iff $\ell = (\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z)$ for some $i$ with $\hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationModel · Linearization15.mem_support_linSumModel_iff⟧. *In a chart* ⟦Chapter15/Linearization · SBLocalization.remark_15_1_2⟧: where $\Lambda(f(y)) = 0$, the weighted count of $\hat f(\varphi(y))$ in the chart is $\Lambda(\Phi^{-1}(\varphi(y), \hat f(\varphi(y)))) = \Lambda(f(y)) = 0$ (the count formula of §XV.7, step (e)), so the model remark applies. *Intrinsically*, Theorem 15.1.1 (1) ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero⟧: $T(f, \Lambda)(x) = 0$ where $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$, by the same count read through the data that define $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ (§XV.8).

### XV.3 Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1): separating sequences

**The separation property** at a point $z$ for a partition $e : I \to \{1, \dots, p\}$ of the index set ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.IsSeparatedAt⟧: (1) $s_i(z) = s_{i'}(z)$ iff $e(i) = e(i')$, and (2) if $e(i) = e(i')$ then $s_i = s_{i'}$ on a neighbourhood of $z$. This is the conclusion of the proposition at one point $x_k$.

**Statement** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp⟧. Let $Z$ be a first countable $T_1$ space, $s_i$, $i \in I$ finite, maps continuous on an open $V \ni x_0$ with values in a Hausdorff space, and suppose that $x_0$ is not isolated. Then there are $x_k \in V$ with $x_k \ne x_0$ and $x_k \to x_0$, and one surjective partition $e : I \to \{1, \dots, p\}$, such that the separation property holds at every $x_k$. The text states it on the local model $O$, with the metric of $E_0$, $x_0 = 0$ and the sections of a local sc⁺-section structure. The formal statement is more general in its setting (topological, no sc-structure, the maps only continuous) and narrower by one hypothesis.

**Proof.** *Step 1, points near $x_0$ where the maps are dichotomous.* Call $z$ *locally dichotomous* for the family if every pair of the maps either coincides on a neighbourhood of $z$ or differs at $z$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.IsLocDich⟧. Every nonempty open set on which the maps are continuous contains such a point ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_isLocDich_mem⟧: Lemma 15.1.5 in its topological form (§XV.5) gives a nonempty open $W$ inside it on which each pair either coincides or differs everywhere, and any point of $W$ will do (coincidence on $W$ is coincidence near the point, since $W$ is open). Now take a decreasing countable basis $(u_k)$ of neighbourhoods of $x_0$, which exists by first countability. For each $k$ the set $\operatorname{int}(u_k) \cap V \setminus \{x_0\}$ is open, because $Z$ is $T_1$ so that $\{x_0\}$ is closed; and it is nonempty, because it belongs to the punctured neighbourhood filter of $x_0$, which is not trivial since $x_0$ is not isolated. So it contains a locally dichotomous point $z_k$; $z_k \ne x_0$, $z_k \in V$, and $z_k \to x_0$ since $z_k \in u_k$ and the $u_k$ form a decreasing basis.

*Step 2, the subsequence* ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_isSeparatedAt_subseq⟧. At each $z_k$ the *pattern* of coincidences is the relation $\{(i, j) : s_i(z_k) = s_j(z_k)\}$ on $I \times I$. There are finitely many such relations, so one of them, $P$, occurs for infinitely many $k$ (a map from $\mathbb N$ to a finite set has an infinite fibre), and an extraction $k \mapsto \phi(k)$, strictly increasing, picks those $k$. The partition $e$ is taken from the values at $z_{\phi(0)}$: $e(i) = e(j)$ iff $s_i(z_{\phi(0)}) = s_j(z_{\phi(0)})$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_fin_partition⟧, the classes of equal values numbered by a finite set. Since the pattern is $P$ at every $z_{\phi(k)}$, (1) holds at every point of the subsequence. For (2): if $e(i) = e(j)$ then $s_i(z_{\phi(k)}) = s_j(z_{\phi(k)})$, and since $z_{\phi(k)}$ is locally dichotomous, the pair cannot differ there, so it coincides near $z_{\phi(k)}$. The sequence of the proposition is $x_k = z_{\phi(k)}$.

*How this departs from the text's proof.* The text picks $y_k \to 0$, $y_k \ne 0$, applies Lemma 15.1.5 on small balls around $y_k$ to get $z_k$ with partitions $I = I^k_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup I^k_{p_k}$, and then takes successive subsequences making $I^k_1$, $I^k_2$, … constant. The formal proof takes a single subsequence on which the whole pattern is constant, by the pigeonhole principle on the finite set of relations on $I$; the result is the same. The points come from a neighbourhood basis rather than from a sequence chosen in advance, so no metric is needed.

**The added hypothesis, and the isolated point.** That $x_0$ is not isolated is not derived from the text; it is what makes the punctured neighbourhoods nonempty in Step 1. Its witness is two maps $z \mapsto 0$ and $z \mapsto z$ on $\mathbb R$ at $0$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness⟧, where all hypotheses hold and the proposition applies. **At an isolated point, Proposition 15.1.3 does not hold as we read it.** If $\{x_0\}$ is open, no sequence $x_k \ne x_0$ converges to $x_0$: convergence would put some $x_k$ in the open set $\{x_0\}$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated⟧. This happens for the one-point local model $O = \{0\}$ of a zero-dimensional $X$ ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_point⟧. The case is degenerate, and nothing depends on it: the formal proof of Theorem 15.1.1 does not use the proposition, because its core lemma needs separated points in every neighbourhood of $x_0$, and $x_0$ itself may be one of them (§XV.7). At an isolated point the theorem therefore holds without change.

### XV.4 Lemma 15.1.4 (2017: 15.1): finite closed covers of a ball

**Statement** (stronger) ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4⟧. In any pseudo-metric space, if a ball $B_\varepsilon(y)$, $\varepsilon > 0$, is the union of finitely many sets $A_i$ that are closed in $B_\varepsilon(y)$, then one of the $A_i$ has nonempty interior. The text states it for $O$ with the metric of $E_0$ (p. 685); the formal statement holds in every pseudo-metric space.

**Proof.** *The topological core* ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.interior_biUnion_eq_empty⟧: in any topological space, a finite union of closed sets with empty interiors has empty interior. By induction over the finite index set: the empty union is empty; and if $A$ is closed with empty interior and $B$ (the union so far) has empty interior, then $A \cup B$ has empty interior, Mathlib's fact for the union of a closed set and a set with empty interior. *The cover form* ⟦Chapter15/SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover⟧: a nonempty open set $V$ covered by finitely many closed sets meets the interior of one of them. Otherwise all interiors are empty, so the union has empty interior by the core; but $V$ is open and contained in the union, so every point of $V$ lies in the interior of the union. *The lemma* is the cover form in the subspace $B_\varepsilon(y)$, which is nonempty (it contains $y$) and open in itself: the preimages of the $A_i$ in the subspace are closed by hypothesis and cover it, so one of them has a point $x$ in its interior in the subspace. The image of that interior under the inclusion is open in the ambient space, because the ball is open, and it lies in $A_i$; so $x$ lies in the interior of $A_i$.

*How this departs from the text's proof.* The text moves a point $z$ step by step, each step adding to the set of indices $i$ with $z \notin \Sigma_i$, until $z$ lies in the interior of some $\Sigma_i$. The formal proof is the induction on the index set above. Neither uses the Baire property, which a finite union does not need.
