- extend them to sc⁺-sections $s^1_j$ supported in an invariant $V(x)$ with closure in $U(x)$;
- symmetrize over $G_x$;
- take the atomic multisection;
- invoke the implicit function theorem for a neighbourhood $Q(x)$ on which the parametrized problem stays onto.

The formalization follows this order. It needs one more tool, the transport of (15.1) along morphisms, because the symmetrized branches are moved by the isotropy group, and because the text passes to saturations "by equivariance".

**(15.1) with given vectors** ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoVec⟧. At a level-$1$ point $x$ and for vectors $v_1, \dots, v_\ell \in W_x$: for every operator $L$ of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$, every chart presentation of $T^R_xX$ and every $w \in W_x$, there are $u \in T^R_xX$ and $\tau$ with $Lu + \sum_j\tau_jv_j = w$. (15.1) for a family at $x$ is this property for the values $s_{ij}(x)$ of every branch of a linear representation ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.isParamOntoAt_iff_vec⟧.

**Transport along morphisms** ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoVec.of_mor⟧. If $\varphi : x \to y$ and (15.1) holds at $x$ with $v_j$, it holds at $y$ with $\mu(\varphi, v_j)$.

*Proof.*
1. *The operators at $y$.* Every operator $L'$ of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(y)$ is the conjugate $\mu(\varphi, \cdot) \circ L \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$ of an operator $L$ of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$. This is the functor property of the linearization (§XV.9) ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_functor⟧, read on the support of the pushed-forward formal sum.
2. *The reduced tangent space at $y$.* Take a chart at $x$, restricted to the sheet of $\varphi$, and transport it along $\varphi$. Then $T\varphi$ maps $T^R_xX$ into the reduced tangent space at $y$ computed in the transported chart ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.tangentMorCLE_mem_reducedTangentFiber_transport⟧. By chart independence of $T^R$ (Part I) ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.reducedTangentFiber_eq⟧, this is the reduced tangent space of every chart presentation at $y$.
3. *Solving.* $\mu(\varphi, \cdot) : W_x \to W_y$ is a linear bijection with inverse $\mu(\varphi^{-1}, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.muLin_surjective⟧. Write $w = \mu(\varphi, w_0)$ and solve $Lu + \sum_j\tau_jv_j = w_0$ at $x$. Then $T\varphi\,u \in T^R_yX$ and
$$L'(T\varphi\,u) + \textstyle\sum_j\tau_j\mu(\varphi, v_j) = \mu(\varphi, Lu + \sum_j\tau_jv_j) = w.$$

*Linear representations are carried too* ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.exists_linearRep_of_mor⟧. Suppose $\Lambda_t$ is a functor for every $t$ and $(\sum_jt_js_{ij}, \sigma_i)$ represents it on $O \ni x$. Transport each section along the local diffeomorphism of $\varphi$; this gives sections on a neighbourhood of $y$ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.transSec_eq_muLin⟧. Since $\mu$ is fibrewise linear, the transported combinations are the combinations of the transported sections ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.paramSec_transSec_eqOn⟧. They represent $\Lambda_t$ there because $\Lambda_t$ is a functor. So (15.1) for a family passes along morphisms in both directions ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAt.of_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoTransport · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAt.of_mor_inv⟧.

**Saturation** ("the same assertion also holds for points … in the saturation of $Q(x)$").
- $S_f$ is saturated: if $\varphi : a \to z$ and $f(a) = 0$, then $f(z) = \mu(\varphi, 0) = 0$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.mem_solutionSet_tgt⟧.
- A family good on an open $V$ is good on the saturation of $V$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.GPFamily.saturate⟧ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionExistence · SBLocalization.ScPlusGPFamily.saturate⟧. For $z \in S_f$ in the saturation there are $a \in V$ and $\varphi : a \to z$. Then $a \in S_f$, so (15.1) holds at $a$ and passes to $z$ along $\varphi$.
- The saturation of an open set is open, because $\pi$ is open. So it suffices to produce, at each $x \in S_f$, an open $V \ni x$ carrying a good family ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.hasLocalGPFamilies_of_nhds⟧.

**Seed data** ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData⟧. Seed data consist of:
- a point $x$;
- a natural representation of $G_x$ on an open $U(x)$ with the properness property;
- an open $V(x) \ni x$ invariant under the action, with $\operatorname{cl}V(x) \subseteq U(x)$;
- sc⁺-sections $s_1, \dots, s_\ell$ of $W$ supported in $V(x)$.

Such $U(x)$, $V(x)$ exist inside any open neighbourhood of $x$ ⟦Chapter13/AtomicMultisection · SBLocalization.exists_atomicNbhd⟧ (Theorem 7.1.13 and the proof of Theorem 7.5.7).

**The atomic family** ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.Λ⟧. For each $t$, $\Lambda_t$ is Part XIII's atomic multisection generated by the seed $\sum_jt_js_j$. Its branches on $U(x)$ are the translates
$$(\textstyle\sum_jt_js_j)^g(y) = \mu\big(\Gamma(g, g^{-1} * y), \sum_jt_js_j(g^{-1} * y)\big), \qquad g \in G_x,$$
which is the text's $s^{x,g}_t$. Each $\Lambda_t$ is an sc⁺-multisection.
- *Linear branches on $U(x)$* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.isLocalRepOn_branch⟧. Since $\mu$ is linear on fibres, $(\sum_jt_js_j)^g = \sum_jt_js_j^g$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.natTerm_paramSec⟧. So on $U(x)$ the family has the linear representation with sections $s^g_j$ and weights $1/|G_x|$.
- *Away from the seed* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.isLocalRepOn_zero⟧. Off the saturation of $\operatorname{cl}V(x)$, $\Lambda_t$ is the trivial multisection, represented by the zero section.
- *Linear everywhere* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.isLinearFamily⟧. There are two cases for a point $x_0$.
  - If $x_0$ is the target of a morphism $\varphi$ from a point of $U(x)$, the representation on $U(x)$ is carried along $\varphi$ (`exists_linearRep_of_mor`).
  - Otherwise $x_0$ lies off the closed saturation of $\operatorname{cl}V(x)$, and the zero representation serves.
- *Structurable* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.isStructurable_Λ⟧. Given a good system, every $\Lambda_t$ is structurable: an atomic multisection is structurable (Theorem 13.5.3) ⟦Chapter13/AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_of_goodSystem⟧. This is the text's "for fixed $t$ it is structurable".
- *Domain support* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.domSupp_Λ_subset⟧. It lies in the saturation of $U(x)$.
- *Norm* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.norm_le⟧. If $N(s_j) \le c$ and $c \le h$ on the saturation of $U(x)$, then $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1h$.
  - At a point reached from $U(x)$, every branch value is $\mu(\Gamma, \sum_jt_js_j(\cdot))$. Its norm is at most $|t|_1c$, since $N$ is invariant under $\mu$ ⟦Chapter13/AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed_normW_le⟧ ⟦Chapter13/AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.AtomicData.pointwiseNorm_mult_le⟧. And $c \le h$ there.
  - At other points the pointwise norm is $0$.
- *(15.1)* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.isParamOntoAt⟧. Let $W \ni x$ be open such that the vectors $s_j(y)$ satisfy (15.1) at every point $y$ of $S_f \cap W$. Put
$$Q_0 = \bigcap_{g \in G_x}\big(U(x) \cap \Phi_g^{-1}(W)\big).$$
  This set is open (a finite intersection) and contains $x$. At $y \in Q_0 \cap S_f$, the branch $g$ takes the values $\mu(m, s_j(\operatorname{src}m))$, where $m = \Gamma(g, \Phi_{g^{-1}}(y))$ is a morphism from $\Phi_{g^{-1}}(y) \in W$ to $y$. Its source lies in $S_f$, since $S_f$ is saturated, and in $W$. So (15.1) holds there with $s_j$, and `IsParamOntoVec.of_mor` carries it to $y$ for the branch $g$. This is the text's "the linearization … at $(0, x)$ is also surjective for every $g$", extended from $x$ to the points of $S_f$ near $x$.
- *Together* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.SeedData.gpFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionExistence · SBLocalization.SeedData.scPlusGPFamily⟧. The atomic family is good on $Q_0$: structurable given a good system, and sc⁺ without one.

**Local families from local seeds** ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.hasLocalGPFamilies_of_seeds⟧ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionExistence · SBLocalization.exists_scPlusGPFamily_nhds⟧. The analytic input is named *local seeds* ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.HasLocalParamSeeds⟧. It says: at every $x \in S_f$, for every open $O \ni x$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$, there are
- finitely many sc⁺-sections $s_j$ supported in $O$ with $N(s_j) \le \varepsilon$, and
- an open $W \ni x$ such that the $s_j(y)$ satisfy (15.1) at every level-$1$ point $y$ of $S_f \cap W$.

Given local seeds, every $x \in S_f$ has an open neighbourhood carrying a good family.

*Proof.*
1. Put $c = h(x)/2 > 0$ and $W_1 = U \cap \{y : h(y) > c\}$, an open neighbourhood of $x$.
2. Choose $U(x) \subseteq W_1$ and $V(x)$ as above, and seeds with $O = V(x)$ and $\varepsilon = c$.
3. *$c \le h$ on the saturation of $U(x)$.* A point $y$ there is isomorphic to some $a \in U(x)$, and $h(y) = h(a) > c$ because $h$ is constant along morphisms.
4. *The saturation of $U(x)$ lies in $U$*, because $U$ is saturated.
5. So the atomic family has $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1h$, domain support in $U$, and (15.1) on $Q_0$.

The text asks $N(s^1_j(y)) \le \min\{1, h(y)\}$ on $U(x)$. The formalization takes the constant bound $h(x)/2$ and shrinks $U(x)$ so that $h > h(x)/2$ on it. This gives the bound on the saturation directly.

With local seeds, the structurable form is proved in one statement ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_hyp_seeds⟧ ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_seeds⟧. These are intermediate steps of the final proof.

**Seeds from two facts at single points** ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.hasLocalParamSeeds_of⟧. Local seeds follow from bump functions, the smoothness of the points of $S_f$, and two facts:
- *small vectors* ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.HasPointwiseParamOnto⟧: at every level-$1$ point $x \in S_f$ and for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there are smooth vectors $w_j \in W_x$ with $N(w_j) < \varepsilon$ satisfying (15.1) at $x$;
- *openness* ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.HasParamOntoOpen⟧: if the values of sc⁺-sections $s_j$ satisfy (15.1) at $x \in S_f$, there is an open $W \ni x$ such that they satisfy it at every level-$1$ point of $S_f \cap W$.

*Proof.*
1. At $x \in S_f$, take the small vectors with $N(w_j) < \varepsilon/2$.
2. Part I's Lemma 5.3.3, on the object M-polyfold with its bump functions (Theorem 12.3.2 (1)), extends each smooth $w_j$ to an sc⁺-section $s_j$ with $s_j(x) = w_j$, support in $O$, and $N(s_j) \le \varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · lemma_5_3_3⟧.
3. Then (15.1) holds at $x$ with the $s_j(x)$, and openness gives $W$.

Points of $S_f$ are smooth by the regularity that the tame germ data provide ⟦Chapter15/Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_eq⟧. The structurable form from the two facts and parametric general position ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_pointwise⟧ is the next intermediate step.

The two facts are the text's choice of the $w_j$ ("we can pick the $w_i$ as small as we wish") and its appeal to the implicit function theorem for $Q(x)$. Both are proved from the theorem's hypotheses in §XV.24.

*Departures from the text's local constructions.*
- The text's two cases, $d_X(x) = 0$ and $d_X(x) \ge 1$, are one construction, because (15.1) is stated on $T^R_xX$.
- The text's "(Interior)" and "(Boundary)" conclusions assert that the parametrized solution set over $\{|t| < \varepsilon_x\} \times Q(x)$ is a tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid. The formalization does not use this structure: what the assembly needs from $Q(x)$ is (15.1) at the points of $S_f \cap Q(x)$. The local structure of the parametrized solution set enters only in §XV.25, branch by branch, through Part I.

### XV.24 Proof of Theorem 15.3.7, III: (15.1) and Part I's conditions (i)–(ii)

The two facts of §XV.23 concern (15.1), stated on the ep-groupoid with reduced tangent spaces. Part I's proof of Theorem 5.3.10 works with conditions (i)–(ii) for a parametrized section in an M-polyfold chart, with the full tangent space. This subsection proves the two conditions equivalent at a zero of $f$, and then derives both facts from Part I.

**Part I's conditions** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP⟧. Take a strong bundle chart centred at $y$ (chart point $0$, retraction $r$, model fibre $K_0$) and a presentation $T$ of its partial quadrant, whose minimal subspace $E_0$ is the chart's reduced tangent space. Let $F(a, u) = \operatorname{Lin}_g(0)u + \sum_ia_i\hat t_i(0)$ be the linearization of $g + \sum_i\lambda_it_i$ at $(0, y)$. The conditions are:
- (i) $F$ maps $\mathbb R^m \times T_0O$ onto $K_0$;
- (ii) the kernel of $F$ is transversal to $\mathbb R^m \oplus T^R$: every $w \in T_0O$ is $u + e$ with $e \in E_0$ and $F(a, u) = 0$ for some $a$.

**The bridge** (extra) ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.isParamOntoVec_iff_isParamGP⟧. Let $x$ be a level-$1$ zero of $f$, let a strong bundle chart of $W$ be centred at $x$ with a presentation $T$, and let $s_j$ be sc⁺-sections. Then (15.1) at $x$ with the vectors $s_j(x)$ holds if and only if Part I's (i)–(ii) hold in that chart for $f + \sum_jt_js_j$.

*Proof.* Both sides are read in the chart.
1. *The operator.* At a zero of $f$, the only operator of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$ is the intrinsic form of the chart linearization $D((\hat f - \hat 0) \circ r)(0)$ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.mem_support_linearization_zero_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.linAt_principal_eq_subDeriv⟧. It is taken at the chart point of $x$, which is $0$ ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.levelLift_eq_zero_of_centred⟧.
2. *(15.1) in the chart* ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.onto_chart_iff⟧. (15.1) says that $(v, \tau) \mapsto D((\hat f - \hat 0) \circ r)(0)v + \sum_j\tau_j\hat s_j(0)$ maps $(T_0O \cap E_0) \times \mathbb R^\ell$ onto $K_0$. The fibre $W_x$ is $K_0$ read through the chart, and $T^R_xX$ is $T_0O \cap E_0$.
3. *(i)–(ii) are equivalent to this reading* ⟦Chapter15/ParamOntoBridge · SBLocalization.isParamGP_iff_onto_chart⟧. Write $L$ for the chart linearization and $\hat s_j$ for $\hat s_j(0)$.
   - *Forward.* Given $k \in K_0$, (i) gives $(a, u)$ with $Lu + \sum a_j\hat s_j = k$. Then (ii), applied to $u$, gives $(a', u')$ with $Lu' + \sum a'_j\hat s_j = 0$ and $u - u' \in E_0$. So $(a - a', u - u')$ hits $k$ with $u - u'$ reduced.
   - *Backward.* (i) is immediate. For (ii), take $w \in T_0O$. Then $Lw \in K_0$; solve $Lu + \sum\tau_j\hat s_j = Lw$ with $u$ reduced. The pair $(-\tau, w - u)$ is in the kernel, and $w - (w - u) = u \in E_0$.
4. *Every chart presentation.* (15.1) quantifies over all chart presentations, while the right side uses one. The two agree because the reduced tangent space does not depend on the chart (Part I) ⟦Chapter2/ReducedTangentIntrinsic · MPolyfold.reducedTangentFiber_eq⟧.

*Extra*: the text states (15.1) with $T^R_xX$, while Part I's proof of Theorem 5.3.10 uses (i)–(ii) with the full tangent space. The text presumably takes their equivalence for granted when it cites "the corresponding implicit function theorem".

Tame strong bundle charts centred at a point of $S_f$, with a presentation, exist by the tame germ data ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.exists_tameChart_centred⟧.

**Small vectors** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.hasPointwiseParamOnto⟧. With bump functions and the tame germ data, the small-vectors fact of §XV.23 holds.

*Proof.* Let $x \in S_f$ be a level-$1$ point and $\varepsilon > 0$.
1. Take a tame chart centred at $x$.
2. Part I's proof of Theorem 5.3.10 provides sc⁺-sections $s_j$ of the object M-polyfold bundle for which $f + \sum_jt_js_j$ satisfies (i)–(ii) in this chart. They can be chosen with norm at most $1$ for any given auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_sections_isParamGP⟧.
3. Apply this to the auxiliary norm $(2/\varepsilon)N$; a positive multiple of an auxiliary norm is one. This gives $N(s_j) \le \varepsilon/2 < \varepsilon$.
4. The bridge turns (i)–(ii) into (15.1) for the vectors $w_j = s_j(x)$.
5. The $w_j$ are smooth, because $x$ is smooth and sc⁺-sections map smooth points to smooth vectors.

*Explicit*: this is the text's choice of $w_1, \dots, w_\ell$ "as small as we wish", made in a chart.

**Openness** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.hasParamOntoOpen⟧. For tame $X$ and $f$ with tame germ data, the openness fact of §XV.23 holds.

*Proof.* Let sc⁺-sections $s_j$ satisfy (15.1) at $x \in S_f$.
1. The bridge, in a tame chart centred at $x$, gives (i)–(ii).
2. Part I turns (i)–(ii) into general position of $F(t, y) = f(y) + \sum_jt_js_j(y)$ on $\mathbb R^\ell \times X$ at $(0, x)$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP⟧.
3. $\mathbb R^\ell \times X$ is tame ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · prod_rn_isTame⟧ and $F$ is a tame sc-Fredholm section ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbationG · theorem_3_1_21_tame⟧. So general position at a zero spreads to the zeros in an open $W_0 \ni (0, x)$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_isOpen_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧.
4. Put $W = \{y : (0, y) \in W_0\}$. At a point $y \in S_f \cap W$, $(0, y)$ is a zero of $F$ in general position.
5. In a tame chart centred at $y$, Part I recovers (i)–(ii) ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isParamGP_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧, and the bridge at $y$ gives (15.1) there.

*Explicit*: this is the text's "from the local implicit function theorem we deduce", made precise as the openness of Part I's general position.

Both facts are needed only at points of $S_f$, which are smooth, so centred tame charts are available.

### XV.25 Proof of Theorem 15.3.7, IV: achieving global transversality

**Parametric general position** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPosition⟧. Suppose $X$ is tame, $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data, $|S_f|$ is compact, and $(N, U)$ controls compactness. Let $t \mapsto \Lambda_t$, $t \in \mathbb R^\ell$, be a family of sc⁺-multisections with:
- $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1$;
- domain supports in $U$;
- (15.1) at every level-$1$ point of $S_f$.

Then there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $(f, \Lambda_t)$ is in general position for almost every $t$ with $\|t\| < \varepsilon$. This is step (d) of §XV.22. The proof does not use that the family is linear everywhere (the linear representations inside (15.1) at the points of $S_f$ suffice), nor bump functions, nor $h$.

The text proves this in "Achieving global transversality":
- it uses Theorem 15.2.5 for an $\varepsilon$ below which the parametrized solution set is a tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid with surjective reduced linearizations;
- around each of its points $(t_0, x_0)$ it writes the branches as manifolds with corners $M_i$;
- it applies Sard's theorem to $F \cap M_i \to \mathbb R^{\bar\ell}$ for every intersection $F$ of local faces;
- it covers the set (15.3) by countably many, or by compactness finitely many, such neighbourhoods.

The formalization keeps the plan but makes three changes.
- It centres the local neighbourhoods only at points $(0, x)$ with $x \in S_f$. The form of (15.2) proved below shows that for small $t$ the support of $\Lambda_t \circ f$ stays near $S_f$.
- It works branch by branch, where each branch is a section of a strong bundle over an open subset of the object M-polyfold, so that Part I's results apply directly.
- Part I's Theorem 4.3.1 in local form carries the faces. This replaces the text's "obvious branched ep⁺-groupoid version of Theorem 4.3.1".

**(i) Part I's Sard step, locally** (extra) ⟦Chapter15/LocalSlice · StrongBundle.exists_null_isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSlice_near⟧. Let $X$ be a tame M-polyfold, $g$ a tame sc-Fredholm section, and $t_1, \dots, t_m$ sc⁺-sections. Suppose $F(\lambda, y) = g(y) + \sum_i\lambda_it_i(y)$ is in general position at a zero $z_0$. Then there are an open $W \ni z_0$ in $\mathbb R^m \times X$ and a null set $C \subseteq \mathbb R^m$ such that, for $\lambda \notin C$, the slice $F(\lambda, \cdot)$ is in general position at its zeros $y$ with $(\lambda, y) \in W$.

*Proof.*
1. $F$ is a tame sc-Fredholm section on the tame $\mathbb R^m \times X$ ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbationG · theorem_3_1_21_tame⟧ ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · prod_rn_isTame⟧.
2. General position at $z_0$ gives an open $W_0$ on which the zero set $A$ of $F$ is in general position ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_isOpen_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧.
3. *Faces.* Part I's Theorem 4.3.1 in local form gives a null set $C_1$ off which the fibres $\{y : (\lambda, y) \in A\}$ are submanifolds in general position to the faces ⟦Chapter4/Families · exists_local_family⟧.
4. *Surjectivity.* Part I's Sard step gives a null set $C_2$ off which the linearizations of the slice are onto at its zeros near $z_0$ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · exists_null_isLinSurjAt_paramSlice_near⟧.
5. *Assembling general position of the slice.*
   - The slice is a tame sc-Fredholm section ⟦Chapter3/TameGermsAddG · theorem_3_1_18_tame⟧.
   - Near a zero, its zero set is the fibre piece of $A$, a submanifold ⟦Chapter15/LocalSlice · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.exists_inter⟧.
   - Part I's characterization of general position by good position of a tame germ applies ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGoodPositionGermTame_of_isGeneralPositionAt⟧.
   - So the slice is in general position at every zero in $W$, with $C = C_1 \cup C_2$.

*Extra*: Part I's Theorem 5.3.10 is stated globally, under compactness ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_3_10_of_family⟧. The proof of Theorem 15.3.7 needs its Sard step near one point.

**(ii) A branch as a Part I section.** Let $(\sum_jt_js_{ij}, \sigma_i)$ be a linear representation of the family on $O$, and fix a branch $i$.
- *The parametrized section.* On the open subset $O$ of the object M-polyfold (tame, since an open subset of a tame M-polyfold is tame), take $g = (f - 0)|_O$, the section of $W|_O$ of §XV.10, and $t_j = (-s_{ij})|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.negRestrict⟧.
- *Its slices are the branches* ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.paramSlice_branch_eq⟧. The slice at $t$ of $g + \sum_jt_j(-s_{ij})|_O$ is $(f - \sum_jt_js_{ij})|_O$. Its zeros are the points where $f$ meets branch $i$ of $\Lambda_t$.
- *(15.1) gives Part I's (i)–(ii)* ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.isParamGP_restrictTo_of_onto⟧. Take a chart of $W$ centred at $x$ with domain in $O$, transported to $W|_O$. The chart operator of $g$ is the chart linearization of $f$ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.principal_eq_fiberLin⟧, and the principal part of $(-s)|_O$ is $-\hat s$ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.principal_restrictTo_negRestrict⟧.
  - For (i): solve with (15.1) and change the sign of $\tau$.
  - For (ii): for $w$, solve $Lv + \sum_j\tau_j\hat s_{ij} = Lw$ with $v$ reduced. Then $(\tau, w - v)$ is in the kernel and $w - (w - v) = v \in E_0$.

  This is the argument of the bridge (§XV.24), in the form needed here.
- *General position at $(0, y)$* ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_branchParam⟧. Suppose (15.1) holds at $y \in S_f \cap O$.
  1. $y$ is smooth ⟦Chapter15/Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_eq⟧.
  2. The tame germ data give a tame chart centred at $y$, restricted into $O$.
  3. The operator of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(y)$ is obtained from a local linearization datum of $\Lambda_0$.
  4. Then (15.1) gives (i)–(ii) for the branch, and Part I gives general position of the parametrized branch at $(0, y)$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP⟧.

  The $s_{ij}$ are sc⁺ on $O$, as the branches of $\Lambda_{e_j}$ ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_of_paramSec⟧.

**(iii) Local general position** ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_local_paramGP⟧. Suppose $X$ is tame, $f$ has tame germ data, the $\Lambda_t$ are sc⁺, $x_0 \in S_f$ is a level-$1$ point, and (15.1) holds at $x_0$. Then there are an open $V \ni x_0$, a $\delta > 0$ and a null set $C$ such that $(f, \Lambda_t)$ is in general position at every $y \in V$ with $\Lambda_t(f(y)) > 0$, whenever $\|t\| < \delta$ and $t \notin C$.

*Proof.*
1. Take the linear representation on $O \ni x_0$ from (15.1).
2. For each branch $i$, (ii) and (i), applied on $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$, give an open $W_i \ni (0, x_0)$ and a null set $C_i$.
3. Shrink each $W_i$ to a product $u_i \times v_i$. Take $\delta$ with the $\delta$-ball inside every $u_i$, put $v' = \bigcap_iv_i$, let $V$ be its image in $X$, and put $C = \bigcup_iC_i$.
4. *General position at the support points in $V$.* Let $y \in V$ with $\Lambda_t(f(y)) > 0$. The operators of $T(f, \Lambda_t)(y)$ are the linearizations at $y$ of $f - \sum_jt_js_{ij}$ over the branches through $f(y)$ (Definition 15.1.7, §XV.8). For each such branch, $y$ is a zero of the slice at $t$, so the slice is in general position at $y$.
5. In a chart at $y$ restricted to $O$, this gives the reduced surjectivity of that operator (§XV.16) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isReducedOntoAtLevel_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧. Hence general position at $y$ in the sense of Definition 15.3.5 at one point ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPositionAt⟧.

**(iv) Invariance under morphisms** (extra) ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPositionAt_of_mor⟧. General position at a point passes along morphisms: if $\varphi : y \to x$ and $(f, \Lambda)$ is in general position at $y$, it is so at $x$. The proof is that of the transport of (15.1) in §XV.23 without the parameters ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isReducedOntoAtLevel_of_mor⟧:
- the operators at $x$ are conjugates of those at $y$ (§XV.9);
- $T\varphi$ maps reduced tangent vectors to reduced tangent vectors;
- $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is onto.

*Extra*: the text uses this silently when it passes to saturations "by equivariance" ("the properties of $(\tilde f, \tilde\Lambda)$ at $(0, x')$ are the same as those of $(0, x)$").

**(v) The form of (15.2) the proof uses** (extra) ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_pos_auxLe_subset⟧. Suppose $f$ is an sc-Fredholm section functor, $(N, U)$ controls compactness, and $V \supseteq S_f$ is open and saturated. Then there is $\varepsilon > 0$ with $\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le \varepsilon\} \subseteq V$.

*Proof.* By contradiction.
1. Suppose that for every $n$ there is $x_n \in U \setminus V$ with $N(f(x_n)) \le 1/(n + 1)$. The orbits $\pi(x_n)$ lie in the compact closure that $(N, U)$ provides, so they have a cluster point $q = \pi(z)$.
2. The object space is metrizable, so $z$ has a decreasing neighbourhood basis $B_k$. Since $\pi$ is open and $q$ is a cluster point, there are $n_k \ge k$ and $y_k \in B_k$ with $\pi(y_k) = \pi(x_{n_k})$.
3. Because $U$ and $V$ are saturated, $y_k \in U \setminus V$.
4. $N(f(y_k)) \le 1/(k + 1)$, since $N \circ f$ is invariant along morphisms: $f(\operatorname{tgt}\varphi) = \mu(\varphi, f(\operatorname{src}\varphi))$, and $N$ is invariant under $\mu$.
5. So $y_k \to z$ and $N(f(y_k)) \to 0$. The third property of an auxiliary norm (Part I's Definition 5.1.1 (3)) gives $f(y_k) \to 0_z$.
6. Since $f$ is continuous, $f(z) = 0$. Then $z \in S_f \subseteq V$, and $V$ is open, so $y_k \in V$ for large $k$, a contradiction.

On the support of $\Lambda \circ f$, $N(f(x)) \le N(\Lambda)(x)$, and $x \in U$ once the domain support lies in $U$ ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.auxLe_of_pos⟧. This is the argument of step 4 of the "in particular" (§XV.21).

*Extra* in this form: the text states (15.2) as the compactness of $\{(t, x) : |t| \le \varepsilon_0, \Lambda_t(f(x)) > 0\}$. It uses that compactness to keep the parametrized solution set within finitely many local neighbourhoods. The formalization proves exactly that consequence.

**Proof of parametric general position.**
1. *Local neighbourhoods.* Every $z \in S_f$ is smooth, hence a level-$1$ point, and (15.1) holds there. So (iii) gives $V_z$, $\delta_z$, $C_z$.
2. *Finite cover.* The open sets $\pi(V_z)$ cover the compact $|S_f|$. Choose a finite set $T$ of such $z$, and let $V$ be the saturation of $\bigcup_{z \in T}V_z$. It is open, saturated, and contains $S_f$.
3. *Staying near $S_f$.* (v) gives $\varepsilon_0$ for this $V$. Choose $\varepsilon > 0$ so that $\|t\| < \varepsilon$ implies $\|t\| < \delta_z$ for $z \in T$ and $|t|_1 \le \varepsilon_0$ (recall $|t|_1 \le \ell\|t\|$).
4. *The null set* is $C = \bigcup_{z \in T}C_z$, a finite union.
5. *General position.* Let $\|t\| < \varepsilon$ and $t \notin C$. General position is checked point by point ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_iff_forall_at⟧. Let $\Lambda_t(f(x)) > 0$.
   - By `auxLe_of_pos` with $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1 \le \varepsilon_0$, $x \in U$ and $N(f(x)) \le \varepsilon_0$, so $x \in V$.
   - So there are $z \in T$, $y \in V_z$ and $\varphi : y \to x$.
   - $\Lambda_t(f(y)) = \Lambda_t(f(x)) > 0$, because $f$ and $\Lambda_t$ are functors.
   - So (iii) gives general position at $y$, and (iv) carries it to $x$.

*Explicit*: this is the step "Achieving global transversality", with four readings:
- Sard "on the intersections of faces" is read as Part I's local Theorem 4.3.1 with its Sard step, branch by branch on $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$;
- the passage to saturations is (iv);
- "using the compactness … a finite number of sets … suffices" is the finite cover of $|S_f|$ together with (v);
- the text's appeal to Theorem 15.2.5 for the structure of the parametrized solution set is replaced by Part I's results, through (ii) and (i).

With parametric general position, the structurable form follows from the local families alone ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_hyp_local⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_local⟧. These are intermediate steps of the final proof.

### XV.26 Theorem 15.3.7 with the text's hypotheses, the structurable addendum, and Remark 15.3.8

**Theorem 15.3.7, (1)–(4)** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionExistence · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_existence⟧. Under the hypotheses of §XV.21 there is an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with (1)–(4).

*Proof*, as the Lean proof goes.
1. $N$ is an auxiliary norm, being part of "$(N, U)$ controls compactness".
2. *Local seeds* (§XV.23) come from:
   - the bump functions;
   - the smoothness of the points of $S_f$;
   - the small-vectors fact (§XV.24);
   - the openness fact (§XV.24).
3. *Local families* (§XV.23). Each $x \in S_f$ has an open neighbourhood carrying a family of sc⁺-multisections good for $(N, U, h)$. This uses the continuity of $h$, its invariance along morphisms, and $h > 0$.
4. *One family* on a neighbourhood $Q$ of $S_f$, by saturation and the compactness of $|S_f|$ (§§XV.22–XV.23).
5. *Parametric general position* for this family (§XV.25), with the bound $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1h \le |t|_1$ (from $h \le 1$), domain supports in $U$, and (15.1) on $S_f \subseteq Q$. This gives $\varepsilon$.
6. *The choice of $t$* with $\|t\| < \min(\varepsilon, 1/(\ell + 1))$ (§XV.22). $\Lambda = \Lambda_t$ has (1)–(4).

*Explicit*: the hypotheses are the text's, plus the tame germ data inherited from §15.2.
- The tame germ data are used for the smoothness of the points of $S_f$, the tame charts of the bridge, and the branches as Part I sections.
- Tameness of $X$ is used in the openness fact and in the local Sard step.
- Bump functions are used for the seeds.
- No good system and no paracompactness of $|X|$ are used.

**The structurable addendum** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_goodSystem⟧. If $X$ has a good system, the structurable form of §XV.21 holds. The proof has the same five steps, with structurable families (§XV.22): the atomic families are structurable by Theorem 13.5.3, sums by Proposition 13.3.12, and the empty family with the good system. The last step is the intermediate statement from the two facts at single points (§XV.23). For paracompact $|X|$, Theorem 13.1.8 gives a good system ⟦Chapter13/GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_8⟧, so the structurable form holds ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_paracompact⟧.

*Narrower*: the good system is not in the text's hypotheses. It is necessary for this part, since a structurable multisection (Definition 13.3.6) carries a good system, so the conclusion implies the hypothesis. The text's proof opens with "We shall construct a structurable perturbation", and the step "for fixed $t$ it is structurable" is Theorem 13.5.3, which in the formalization needs a good system (Part XIII). The text presumably has in mind the paracompact situation that Remark 15.3.8 calls usual in applications.

**The theorem with its addendum** ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionExistence · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7⟧. (1)–(4) always, and $\Lambda$ structurable whenever a good system exists.

**The intermediate statements** are steps of these two proofs. Each one proves the structurable form from a hypothesis that another step of the proof discharges:
- `theorem_15_3_7_hyp` and `theorem_15_3_7_of_hyp` (local families and parametric general position; §XV.22);
- `theorem_15_3_7_hyp_seeds` and `theorem_15_3_7_of_seeds` (local seeds; §XV.23);
- `theorem_15_3_7_of_pointwise` (the two facts at single points; §XV.23);
- `theorem_15_3_7_hyp_local` and `theorem_15_3_7_of_local` (local families alone; §XV.25);
- the form from the two facts and a good system ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionPointwise · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_paramOnto⟧, which the structurable addendum specializes by proving the two facts.

Each has its hypotheses satisfied on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$:
- a good system there, by Theorem 13.1.8 on $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.nonempty_goodSystem_epSEP_zero⟧;
- local families with $\ell = 0$ for every $f$, $N$, $U$, $h$ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.hasLocalGPFamilies_epSEP_zero⟧;
- parametric general position, since every pair is in general position there ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero⟧;
- local seeds ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.hasLocalParamSeeds_epSEP_zero⟧;
- small vectors with $\ell = 0$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.hasPointwiseParamOnto_epSEP_zero⟧ and openness ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.hasParamOntoOpen_epSEP_zero⟧, both resting on (15.1) being automatic with zero fibres ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.isParamOntoVec_epSEP_zero⟧.

The conclusion holds there in each form:
- ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_hyp⟧
- ⟦Chapter15/LocalFamilies · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_seeds⟧
- ⟦Chapter15/LocalSeeds · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_pointwise⟧
- ⟦Chapter15/ParametricGeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_local⟧
- ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionPointwise · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_paramOnto⟧
- ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionGoodSystem · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_goodSystem⟧

These witnesses are weak: the fibres are zero and there is no boundary, so every pair is in general position. They show only that the intermediate statements are not vacuous. The final theorems need no such witness, since all their added hypotheses are discharged, except the inherited tame germ data and, for the addendum, the necessary good system.

**Remark 15.3.8** (nothing to formalize). The remark says the theorem does not assume a paracompact orbit space, only an auxiliary norm, and that constructing auxiliary norms usually needs paracompactness of $|X|$.
- In the formalization, (1)–(4) need neither paracompactness nor a good system. The auxiliary norm enters only through "$(N, U)$ controls compactness".
- The addendum "structurable" needs a good system. Paracompactness supplies one (Theorem 13.1.8), and so does any structurable multisection.

So the remark holds as read for (1)–(4). For the addendum, paracompactness, or at least a good system, does enter. The part of gap G.162 that concerns Theorem 15.3.7 is closed.

### XV.27 Theorem 15.3.9 (2017: 15.5): the statement, the face condition, and charging

Theorem 15.3.9, the Transversal Extension Theorem (p. 698), extends a perturbation given over the boundary to a perturbation over all of $X$ that is transversal, without changing it over $\partial X$. It is the tool for the cobordism part of Corollary 15.3.10 (§XV.33), where the boundary data are two regular perturbations sitting at the ends of the cylinder $[0, 1] \times X$. Its proof (pp. 698–699) has five steps: (a) a cut-off functor $h_0$ between $N(\Lambda)$ and $h$; (b) Theorem 14.1.9, which extends $\Lambda$ to a structurable $\Lambda_0$ with $N(\Lambda_0) \le h_0$; (c) transversality of $(f, \Lambda_0)$ near $\partial X$, from the hypothesis on the faces; (d) the argument of Theorem 15.3.7 away from $\partial X$, with families $\Lambda_t$ whose domain support avoids $\partial X$; (e) $\tilde\Lambda = \Lambda_t \oplus \Lambda_0$ for a small regular $t$. The formalization follows these steps in this order. This subsection gives the definitions, the statement as formalized and the property of the uncharged Lean statement; step (a) is §XV.28, steps (b)–(e) are §XV.29.

**General position at one point.** For a level-$1$ point $x$, $(f, \Lambda)$ is *reducedly onto at $x$* if every operator $L$ in the support of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ (Definition 15.1.7, §XV.8) restricts to a surjection $T^R_xX \to W_x$, the reduced tangent space $T^R_xX$ being read in every chart of $X$ around $x$ and every presentation of the partial quadrant of its model ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.IsReducedOntoAtPt⟧. This is Definition 15.3.5 at one point: $(f, \Lambda)$ is in general position iff it is reducedly onto at every level-$1$ point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$, by definition ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_iff_forall_reducedOntoAtPt⟧ (it is the same predicate as the pointwise general position of §XV.16, ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPositionAt⟧, there with the level-$1$ membership as a separate clause). In general position $(f, \Lambda)$ is transversal: every operator of the support is onto on the larger space $T_xX \supseteq T^R_xX$, and the support points are at level $1$ ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPosition.isTransversal⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ControllingPairs · SBLocalization.mem_levelSet_one_of_pos⟧.

**The boundary data.** Chapter 14's objects over $\partial X$ are used as Part XIV formalizes them. An *sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$* (Definition 14.1.3) is a function $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ of which only the values over $\partial X$ enter: it is a functor on $W|\partial X$, and every $x \in \partial X$ has a good neighbourhood $U(x) = V(x) \cap \partial X$ carrying a *symmetric sc⁺-section structure*, a finite index set $I_x$ with a $G_x$-action and sections $s_i$ that are sc⁺ on the faces (Definition 14.1.3 (1)), equivariant (2), and represent $\Lambda$ by $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i(P(w)) = w\}$ (3) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryScPlusMultisection⟧ ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.BoundarySymmetricStructure⟧. It is *structurable over $\partial X$* (Definition 14.1.7) if it carries in addition a decoration and a family of index correspondences ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryStructurable⟧. Its *boundary domain support* is the closure of the set of $x \in \partial X$ over which $\Lambda$ charges a non-zero vector ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp⟧. Finally, $\Lambda$ *charges $\partial X$* if over every $x \in \partial X$ some $w$ has $\Lambda(w) \ne 0$ ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.ChargesBoundary⟧. For a symmetric structure at a charged point the index set is not empty, because the formula (3) with $I_x = \emptyset$ gives $\Lambda = 0$ on the fibre ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.BoundarySymmetricStructure.nonempty_I_a6⟧. The formal Definition 14.1.3 admits $I_x = \emptyset$, while the text's $|I_x|^{-1}$ presumes $I_x \ne \emptyset$; charging is the reading of the text's definition that excludes the empty index sets (Theorem 14.1.9, Part XIV).

**The face condition** ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryFaceOnto⟧. The text asks that $T_{(f|\partial X, \Lambda)}(x)$ be "surjective with respect to intersections of local faces" at every smooth $x \in \partial X$. It is read as follows: for every sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda'$ on $W$ that agrees with $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$, and every smooth level-$1$ point $x \in \partial X$ with $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$, $(f, \Lambda')$ is reducedly onto at $x$. Two readings are in this. (i) The intersections of the tangent spaces of the local faces through $x$ form a family whose smallest member is $T^R_xX$ (Part I, Definition 2.5.8), and surjectivity on a subspace implies surjectivity on every larger one; so the condition for all intersections is the condition on $T^R_xX$, which is general position at $x$. (ii) $T(f|\partial X, \Lambda)$ is not defined by the text: $\Lambda$ lives only over $\partial X$, and its linearization needs local sections near $x$, not only on the faces. The restriction of $(f - s_i)'(x)$ to $T^R_xX$ sees only the values of $s_i$ on the faces through $x$, so it should not depend on how $\Lambda$ is extended; the formal condition is therefore asked for every sc⁺ extension $\Lambda'$. That it does not depend on the extension is not proved (gap G.179, §XV.38); in the proof the condition is used for exactly one extension, the $\Lambda_0$ of step (b) (§XV.29).

**Statement** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_statement⟧. Let $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ be a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid with $|X|$ paracompact, whose object M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, and every object of which lies in a tame strong bundle chart. Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section functor with Part I's tame germ data and compact $|S_f|$, and $(N, U)$ control compactness (Definition 15.3.1, §XV.17; $U$ open and saturated). Let $\Lambda$ be structurable over $\partial X$ and charge $\partial X$, with boundary domain support in $U$ and $N(\Lambda) \le 1$ on $\partial X$, and let $h : X \to (0, 1]$ be a continuous functor with $N(\Lambda)(x) < h(x)$ for $x \in \partial X$. Assume the face condition. Then there is a structurable sc⁺-multisection $\tilde\Lambda$ with

1. $\tilde\Lambda = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$;
2. domain support in $U$, $N(\tilde\Lambda) < h$ everywhere, and $\tilde\Lambda$ $(N, U)$-admissible (Definition 15.3.3, §XV.18);
3. $(f, \tilde\Lambda)$ transversal (Definition 15.2.1, §XV.12);

and $\tilde\Lambda \circ f$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid with compact support.

*Readings.* "$U$ a saturated subset" is read as open and saturated, which Definition 15.3.1 contains. "$\Lambda$ is $(U, N)$-admissible" over $\partial X$ is read as boundary domain support in $U$ and $N(\Lambda) \le 1$ on $\partial X$, the two parts of Definition 15.3.3 that make sense over $\partial X$. "Onto on $\operatorname{supp}(\tilde\Lambda \circ f)$" is transversality. The word "tame" of the "moreover" is not in the formal conclusion: the $\tilde\Lambda$ that the proof produces is in general position (§XV.29), and for such a $\tilde\Lambda$ the tame form of the "in particular" of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.21) gives a tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, but the statement as formalized exports only the text's (1)–(3) with "branched" and "compact".

*Narrower,* by four hypotheses, of which two are readings and two are open. **Tame strong bundle charts** at every object: the reading of "a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid" that Part XIV uses for Theorem 14.1.9; it is needed in step (a) (§XV.28), not derived from the text, and it has a witness with boundary and non-zero fibres, the trivial bundle $[0, \infty) \times \mathbb R^m \times \mathbb R^k \to [0, \infty) \times \mathbb R^m$ of Part XIV ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.hB_halfSEP⟧, as well as one without boundary ⟦Chapter14/OpenExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn⟧. **Charging** of $\partial X$ by $\Lambda$: the reading $I_x \ne \emptyset$ of "sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$". It is necessary: if a structurable $\tilde\Lambda$ agrees with $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$, then $\Lambda$ charges $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.chargesBoundary_of_theorem_15_3_9_r6⟧, because a local representation of $\tilde\Lambda$ at $x \in \partial X$ (Definition 13.2.1) has weights summing to $1$, so it has a branch $s_i$, and $\tilde\Lambda(s_i(x)) \ge \sigma_i > 0$ ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.chargesBoundary_of_structurable_eq_a6⟧. The zero multisection charges every fibre ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.chargesBoundary_zeroMultisection_a6⟧, and the boundary hypotheses of Theorem 14.1.9 with charging hold together on the half-space bundle, whose boundary is not empty ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.theorem_14_1_9_charged_hypotheses_halfSEP⟧. The **tame germ data** of $f$ are inherited from §15.2 and Part I's Theorem 3.6.8, as everywhere in this Part. The **face condition for every extension** is the reading (ii) above (gap G.179). Partitions of unity on the objects and the paracompactness of $|X|$ are the text's.

**The theorem** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_of_local_rel⟧. The charged statement holds for every strong bundle for which the *relative local families* exist ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.relative_local_families_statement⟧: under the hypotheses of steps (c)–(d), every point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)$ lies in a saturated open set carrying a parameter family with domain support in $U \setminus \partial X$, the bound $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1(h - N(\Lambda_0))$ and the relative form of (15.1) (§XV.29). This is the one analytic input of the proof that is not formalized, gap G.178: everything else, the cut-off, Theorem 14.1.9, the relative parametric transversality, the compactness and the assembly, is proved. *Witnesses*: the relative local families and the charged statement hold on the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.relative_local_families_statement_epSEP_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_statement_epSEP_zero⟧, where $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.boundary_epSEP_eq_empty⟧ and the fibres are zero, so every pair is in general position. These witnesses are **weak**: no strong bundle with boundary is known to satisfy the relative local families, and the theorem has no non-degenerate witness.

**Remark: the uncharged Lean statement.** The uncharged Lean statement ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_statement⟧ is the charged statement without the tame strong bundle charts and without charging; the charged statement follows from it ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_of_statement⟧. As a Lean statement it does not hold when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ and one sc-Fredholm $f$ with tame germ data, compact $|S_f|$ and a pair $(N, U)$ controlling compactness exists ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionCylinder · SBLocalization.not_theorem_15_3_9_statement_w2⟧. *Proof.* Take $\Lambda \equiv 0$. It is structurable over $\partial X$ in the formal sense, with empty index sets ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_zeroFun_a6⟧; its boundary domain support is empty ⟦Chapter14/EmptyIndex · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_zeroFun_a6⟧; its pointwise norm is $0$, its support over every point being empty ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionCylinder · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_zeroFun_w2⟧; with $h \equiv 1$ the norm conditions hold, and the face condition holds vacuously since $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$. The statement would give a structurable $\tilde\Lambda$ vanishing over $\partial X$, and no structurable multisection vanishes over a point (the necessity of charging above). On the cylinder $[0, 1] \times X$ of §XV.30, with $d_X \equiv 0$ and $X$ nonempty, the hypotheses of Corollary 15.3.10 provide all of this: the cylinder is tame since $X$ is (§XV.30), its orbit space is paracompact, $(0, x)$ lies on its boundary, $\tilde f$ is sc-Fredholm with tame germ data and compact solution set, and Corollary 15.3.10 (2) gives a controlling pair; so the uncharged statement fails on every such cylinder ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionCylinder · SBLocalization.not_theorem_15_3_9_statement_cube_w2⟧. This is a property of our formalization, not of the text, whose $\Lambda$ has non-empty index sets; it has the same source as the failure of the uncharged Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 (Part XIV). *Consequences.* The Lean forms that conclude the uncharged statement are correct implications whose hypotheses fail when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$; they are vacuous there and are used only as intermediate steps for $\partial X = \emptyset$: the reduction to Theorem 14.1.9 and two proof steps ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_hyp⟧, its form with step (a) proved ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_of_extension_ty⟧, and its forms with the relative parametric step proved ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_of_rel_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeParametric · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_of_local_rel⟧, which take the uncharged extension statement of Theorem 14.1.9 as a hypothesis. The forms of Corollary 15.3.10 (3) that take the uncharged statement on the cylinder are vacuous for nonempty $X$ (§XV.33). The charged statement, built on Theorem 14.1.9 in its charged form (Part XIV), replaces all of them, and the rest of this subsection and §§XV.28–XV.29 tell its proof. The uncharged statement does hold on the boundaryless example, where its three propositional inputs hold as well ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_statement_epSEP_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.lemma_15_3_9_cutoff_statement_epSEP_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_statement_epSEP_zero⟧: there $\Lambda_0 = 0$ has every conclusion, being in general position ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionBranched · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero⟧, and the boundary domain support is empty ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_epSEP⟧.

**The shape of the proof** ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_hyp⟧. The charged statement follows from the *relative statement*, the proposition that steps (c)–(d) produce ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_statement⟧: given a structurable $\Lambda_0$ with domain support in $U$, $N(\Lambda_0) < h$, and $(f, \Lambda_0)$ reducedly onto at the points of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f) \cap \partial X$, there is a structurable $\tilde\Lambda$ equal to $\Lambda_0$ over $\partial X$, with domain support in $U$, $N(\tilde\Lambda) < h$, transversal and in general position. The relative statement follows from the relative local families alone ⟦Chapter15/RelativeParametric · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_of_local⟧, the parametric step being proved. §XV.28 proves step (a); §XV.29 retells steps (b)–(e) and the proof of the relative statement.

### XV.28 Proof of Theorem 15.3.9, step (a): the cut-off functor $h_0$

**Statement** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.lemma_15_3_9_cutoff_hyp⟧. If every object lies in a tame strong bundle chart, then step (a) holds ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.lemma_15_3_9_cutoff_statement⟧: for $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact and sc-smooth partitions of unity, $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$, $N$ an auxiliary norm, $U$ open and saturated containing the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, and $h > 0$ a continuous functor with $N(\Lambda) < h$ on $\partial X$, there is a continuous functor $h_0 \ge 0$ with $\operatorname{tsupp}h_0 \subset U$, $h_0 < h$ everywhere, and $N(\Lambda) < h_0$ on the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$. These are the hypotheses that Theorem 14.1.9 asks of its function $f$ with $\tilde U = U$, and the margin $h_0 < h$ is used at the end of the proof.

*A reading.* The text asks for $h_0$ with $N(\Lambda)(x) < h_0(x) < h(x)$ for every $x \in \partial X$ and $h_0$ supported in $U$. Off the boundary domain support, over $\partial X$, the support of $\Lambda$ is the zero vector and $N(\Lambda) = 0$; at a point of $\partial X$ outside $U$ the two requirements would ask $0 < h_0 = 0$. So the strict lower bound is presumably meant on the domain support, which is what Theorem 14.1.9 asks; the formal statement says so. The text's $h_0 \le 1$ is not needed, $h_0 < h \le 1$ holding anyway in the application.

**Proof.** Write $C$ for the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$. Four facts about $\Lambda$ come first.

*The support over a boundary point.* If $S$ is a symmetric structure of $\Lambda$ on $V(x)$ and $y \in V(x) \cap \partial X$, then $w$ lies in the support of $\Lambda$ over $y$ iff $w = s_i(y)$ for some $i$ ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.BoundarySymmetricStructure.mem_suppAt_iff_ty⟧: by the representation formula (3), $\Lambda(w) > 0$ iff the count $\#\{i : s_i(y) = w\}$ is positive, the index set being non-empty as soon as it contains one $i$. In particular the support over $\partial X$ lies in $W_{0,1}$, each $s_i$ being sc⁺ on the faces ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryScPlusMultisection.suppAt_subset_oneSet_ty⟧, so the pointwise norm $N(\Lambda)(y) = \sup\{N(w) : \Lambda(w) > 0\}$ is the maximum of the finitely many $N(s_i(y))$.

*$N(\Lambda)$ is a functor on $\partial X$* ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_tgt_of_boundary_ty⟧. For a morphism $\varphi$ with source in $\partial X$, $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ carries the support over $s(\varphi)$ into the support over $t(\varphi)$, since $\Lambda$ is a functor on $W|\partial X$, and it preserves $N$, since an auxiliary norm is invariant under $\mu$ ⟦Chapter13/AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.normW_μ⟧; so the set of norms over $s(\varphi)$ lies in that over $t(\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.normW_image_suppAt_subset_ty⟧, and the inverse morphism, whose source again lies in the saturated set $\partial X$, gives the other inclusion.

*$C$ is saturated* ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.isSaturated_boundaryDomSupp_ty⟧. The set of $x \in \partial X$ over which $\Lambda$ charges a non-zero $w$ is saturated: $\mu(\varphi, w)$ is charged over $t(\varphi)$, and it is not zero, since $N(\mu(\varphi, w)) = N(w) > 0$, an auxiliary norm vanishing only at zero vectors. The closure of a saturated set is saturated. And $C \subset \partial X$, $\partial X$ being closed ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_subset_boundary_ty⟧.

*$N(\Lambda)$ is upper semicontinuous along $\partial X$* ⟦Chapter15/CutoffFunctor · SBLocalization.exists_nhds_pointwiseNorm_lt_ty⟧: for $x \in \partial X$ and $c > N(\Lambda)(x)$ there is an open $O \ni x$ with $N(\Lambda) < c$ on $O \cap \partial X$. Take a symmetric structure on $V(x)$. Its sections $s_i$ are sc⁺ only on the faces; with tame strong bundle charts at every object and sc-smooth partitions of unity, each extends to an sc⁺-section $\bar s_i$ on the open set $V(x)$ with $\bar s_i = s_i$ on $V(x) \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/OpenExtension · SBLocalization.exists_scPlusSectionOn_extension_of_face⟧ (the extension lemma of Part XIV behind Proposition 14.1.4). The functions $y \mapsto N(\bar s_i(y))$ are continuous on $V(x)$. With $c' = (N(\Lambda)(x) + c)/2$, the set $O = V(x) \cap \bigcap_i\{N \circ \bar s_i < c'\}$ is open, contains $x$ because $N(s_i(x)) \le N(\Lambda)(x) < c'$, and on $O \cap \partial X$ every norm $N(s_i(y)) = N(\bar s_i(y))$ is below $c'$, so $N(\Lambda)(y) \le c' < c$. This is the only place where the tame strong bundle charts enter. Without them Definition 14.1.3 (1) constrains the $s_i$ only face by face, and nothing prevents $N(\Lambda)$ from jumping up along $\partial X$; the text uses the semicontinuity without comment.

*Construction of $g$ on $|X|$.* The orbit space $|X|$ is paracompact and Hausdorff. For an orbit $q$ let
$$t(q) = \{y \ge 0 : y < h(x) \text{ and, if } x \in C, \ y > N(\Lambda)(x), \text{ for every } x \text{ with } \pi(x) = q\},$$
an intersection of intervals, hence convex. Since $h$ and $N(\Lambda)|_{\partial X}$ are constant on orbits and $C$ is saturated, $t(q)$ is described by any one $x$ over $q$. Each $q = \pi(x)$ has a constant $c$ that lies in $t(q')$ for all $q'$ near $q$. If $x \in C$, take $c = (N(\Lambda)(x) + h(x))/2$: by the upper semicontinuity there is an open $O \ni x$ with $N(\Lambda) < c$ on $O \cap \partial X$, and $h > c$ on an open neighbourhood by continuity; if $x \notin C$, take $c = h(x)/2$ on $(X \setminus C) \cap \{h > h(x)/2\}$, open since $C$ is closed. In both cases the open set maps to an open neighbourhood of $q$, the orbit map being open (Proposition 7.1.8) ⟦Chapter7/Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_8⟧, and the invariance of the data transfers the inequalities from the chosen representatives to all points of the orbits. Mathlib's selection lemma for convex-valued maps with local constant selections on a paracompact space ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/Convex/PartitionOfUnity · exists_continuous_forall_mem_convex_of_local_const⟧, a partition of unity argument, gives a continuous $g : |X| \to \mathbb R$ with $g(q) \in t(q)$ for all $q$: $0 \le g < h$, and $g > N(\Lambda)$ on $\pi(C)$.

*The Urysohn factor.* $\pi(C)$ is closed in $|X|$, $C$ being closed and saturated ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryCover · EpGroupoid.isClosed_π_image_of_isSaturated⟧, and $\pi(U)$ is open and contains it. By normality there is an open $V$ with $\pi(C) \subset V$ and $\operatorname{cl}V \subset \pi(U)$, and an Urysohn function $\psi : |X| \to [0, 1]$ with $\psi = 1$ on $\pi(C)$ and $\psi = 0$ off $V$.

*The functor.* $h_0 = (\psi g) \circ \pi$. It is continuous, non-negative, constant on orbits, hence a functor. Its topological support lies in $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}V) \subset \pi^{-1}(\pi(U)) = U$, $U$ being saturated. $h_0 \le g \circ \pi < h$, since $0 \le \psi \le 1$. On $C$, $\psi = 1$ and $h_0 = g \circ \pi > N(\Lambda)$. $\square$

*The added hypothesis*, tame strong bundle charts at every object, is not stated in the theorem; it is the reading of the standing assumption used for Theorem 14.1.9 in Part XIV. Witnesses: the trivial bundle over $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter14/OpenExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn⟧, with $\partial X = \emptyset$, and the half-space bundle, with boundary and non-zero fibres ⟦Chapter14/HalfSpaceBundle · HalfSpaceBundle.hB_halfSEP⟧. On $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0$ the cut-off statement holds trivially with $h_0 = 0$, the boundary domain support being empty ⟦Chapter15/TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.lemma_15_3_9_cutoff_statement_epSEP_zero⟧. Gap G.177 is closed.

### XV.29 Proof of Theorem 15.3.9, steps (b)–(e): relative general position and the assembly

This subsection follows the proof of the charged theorem ⟦Chapter15/ChargedExtensionFibres · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_charged_hyp⟧ after the cut-off of §XV.28, and then the proof of the relative statement that steps (c)–(d) supply.

**Step (b): the extension $\Lambda_0$.** Apply Theorem 14.1.9 in its charged form (Part XIV) ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_charged_a6⟧ to $\Lambda$, with $\tilde U = U$ and the function $h_0$ of step (a). Its hypotheses are those of Theorem 15.3.9 together with the properties of $h_0$: $X$ tame, $|X|$ paracompact, partitions of unity, tame strong bundle charts, $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ and charging $\partial X$, $N$ an auxiliary norm, $U$ open, saturated and containing the boundary domain support, $h_0 \ge 0$ a continuous functor with topological support in $U$, and $N(\Lambda) < h_0$ on the boundary domain support ⟦Chapter14/BoundaryExtensionTheorem · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_charged_statement⟧. It gives a structurable $\Lambda_0$ with $N(\Lambda_0) \le h_0$ everywhere, domain support in $U$, and $\Lambda_0 = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. In particular $N(\Lambda_0) \le h_0 < h$ everywhere. *A reading*: after applying Theorem 14.1.9 the text writes "$N(\Lambda_0)(x) \le h(x)$"; presumably $\le h_0(x)$ is meant, since the margin $h_0 < h$ is what makes the final $N(\tilde\Lambda) < h$ strict.

**Step (c): general position of $\Lambda_0$ on the boundary.** For a level-$1$ point $x \in \partial X$ with $\Lambda_0(f(x)) > 0$, $(f, \Lambda_0)$ is reducedly onto at $x$. Indeed $f(x)$ lies over $x \in \partial X$, where $\Lambda_0 = \Lambda$, so $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$; $x$ is a smooth point, every point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)$ being smooth under the tame germ data, since $f(x)$ is then the value of an sc⁺-section and $f - s$ is regularizing ⟦Chapter15/Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_pos⟧; and $\Lambda_0$ is an sc⁺-multisection on $W$ that agrees with $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$, so the face condition applies to it. The text says at this point that the boundary assumption gives, for every boundary point of the support, a neighbourhood $Q(x)$ on which the reduced linearization of $(f, \Lambda_0)$ is onto; the formal proof takes the condition at the boundary support points only and leaves the neighbourhood to the local families (below).

**Steps (c)–(d): the relative statement.** Its hypotheses hold for $\Lambda_0$: structurable, domain support in $U$, $N(\Lambda_0) < h$, reducedly onto at the boundary support points. It gives a structurable $\tilde\Lambda$ with $\tilde\Lambda = \Lambda_0$ over $\partial X$, domain support in $U$, $N(\tilde\Lambda) < h$, $(f, \tilde\Lambda)$ transversal and in general position. Its proof is the rest of this subsection.

**Step (e): the conclusions.** $\tilde\Lambda = \Lambda_0 = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. Since $h \le 1$, $N(\tilde\Lambda) \le 1$, and with the domain support in $U \supseteq S_f$ the example after Definition 15.3.3 (§XV.18) makes $\tilde\Lambda$ admissible ⟦Chapter15/ControllingPairs · SBLocalization.isAdmissible_of_domSupp_subset⟧. The "moreover": general position, $N(\tilde\Lambda) \le 1$ and domain support in $U$ are the hypotheses of the "in particular" of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.21) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionBranched · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_in_particular_hyp⟧, which gives a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid with compact support. $\square$

The proof of the relative statement is "argue as in Theorem 15.3.7" (p. 698), made precise. The text takes parameter families $\Lambda_t$ with domain support away from $\partial X$ and asks of $\Lambda_t \oplus \Lambda_0$ near $(0, x)$, $x$ in the support, that the reduced linearization of the parametrized problem be onto. The formalization reads this as (15.1) relative to the branches of $\Lambda_0$, and then repeats the three parts of the proof of Theorem 15.3.7 (§§XV.22–XV.25): the assembly of local families, the parametric transversality, and the choice of $t$.

**Relative (15.1)** ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAtRel⟧. Let $t \mapsto \Lambda_t$, $t \in \mathbb R^\ell$, be a family of sc⁺-multisections and $x$ a level-$1$ point. The family satisfies (15.1) relative to $\Lambda_0$ at $x$ if it has, on an open $O \ni x$, a linear local representation by the sections $\sum_jt_js_{ij}$ with weights $\sigma_i$ independent of $t$ (as in §XV.22, ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.paramSec⟧), and for every operator $L$ in the support of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$, every chart presentation of $T^R_xX$ and every branch $i$, the map
$$T^R_xX \times \mathbb R^\ell \to W_x, \quad (v, \tau) \mapsto Lv + \sum_j\tau_js_{ij}(x)$$
is onto. The operators of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$ are the $(f - s^0_a)'(x)$ for the branches $s^0_a$ of $\Lambda_0$ through $f(x)$ (§XV.12); the text's (15.1) has the operators of $T(f, 0)(x)$, which is the case $\Lambda_0 = 0$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.isParamOntoAtRel_zero_iff⟧. Two properties. *Where $(f, \Lambda_0)$ is already reducedly onto*, relative (15.1) holds for every linear family, with $\tau = 0$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAtRel.of_reducedOnto⟧; this is how step (c) feeds steps (c)–(d) at the boundary support points. *Sums*: if one summand satisfies relative (15.1) and the other is linear, the sum family $\Lambda_t \oplus \Lambda'_{t'}$ on $\mathbb R^{\ell + \ell'}$ does ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAtRel.famAdd_left⟧ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAtRel.famAdd_right⟧. The sum family is linear with the branches $\sum_jt_js_{ij} + \sum_kt'_ks'_{i'k}$ on the intersection of the two domains ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.famAdd⟧ ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.isLocalRepOn_famAdd⟧; given $(v, \tau)$ for the branch $i$ of the first family, $(v, (\tau, 0))$ serves for every branch $(i, i')$ of the sum.

**Relative families** ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.RelGPFamily⟧. For a function $g$ and a set $Q$: a linear family ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsLinearFamily⟧ of structurable sc⁺-multisections with $N(\Lambda_t)(x) \le |t|_1\,g(x)$, domain support in a given $U'$, and relative (15.1) at every level-$1$ point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f) \cap Q$. In the application $g = h - N(\Lambda_0)$ and $U' = U \setminus \partial X$. The family of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.22) is the case $\Lambda_0 = 0$, $g = h$. A family on $Q$ is one on every smaller set ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.RelGPFamily.mono⟧. Given a good system, the parameter-free family $\Lambda_t = 0$ ($\ell = 0$), which is linear ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.isLinearFamily_zero⟧ and structurable ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.isStructurable_zeroMultisection_of_goodSystem⟧, is a relative family on every set on which $(f, \Lambda_0)$ is reducedly onto at the support points ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.RelGPFamily.zeroOn⟧, in particular on $\emptyset$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.RelGPFamily.zero⟧. Two families on $Q$ and $Q'$ add to one on $Q \cup Q'$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.RelGPFamily.add⟧: the sum of structurable multisections is structurable (Proposition 13.3.12) ⟦Chapter13/StructurableMultisection · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_12⟧; the norm of a sum is at most the sum of the norms ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_multisectionAdd_le⟧, so $N \le (|t|_1 + |t'|_1)g = |(t, t')|_1\,g$; the domain support of a sum lies in the union ⟦Chapter15/ParamFamily · SBLocalization.domSupp_multisectionAdd_subset⟧; and relative (15.1) passes to sums from either summand.

**Off the domain support.** An sc⁺-multisection is the zero multisection over every point outside its domain support ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.eq_zeroMultisection_of_notMem_domSupp⟧: in a local representation at that point every branch passes through the zero vector, for otherwise the point would be in the domain support, so $\Lambda(0_x) = \sum_i\sigma_i = 1$ and $\Lambda = 0$ elsewhere on the fibre. Hence $\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda = \Lambda_0$ over every point outside the domain support of $\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeFamilies · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_eq_left_of_notMem_domSupp⟧, the zero multisection being neutral for $\oplus$ (Part XIII) ⟦Chapter13/MultisectionNoInverse · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_zeroMultisection⟧. This is what "domain support away from $\partial X$" achieves: $\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t = \Lambda_0$ over $\partial X$.

**The two analytic steps, relative to $\Lambda_0$**, as propositions. *The relative local families* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.HasLocalGPFamiliesRel⟧: every $x$ with $\Lambda_0(f(x)) > 0$ lies in an open saturated $Q$ carrying a relative family. *The relative parametric transversality* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.HasParametricGeneralPositionRel⟧: for every linear family of sc⁺-multisections with $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1(1 - N(\Lambda_0))$, domain support in $U$ and relative (15.1) at every point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)$, there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $(f, \Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t)$ is in general position for almost every $t$ with $\|t\| < \varepsilon$.

**The relative statement from the two steps** ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_hyp⟧. Let $\Lambda_0$ be structurable with domain support in $U$ and $N(\Lambda_0) < h \le 1$, and assume the relative local families with domain support in $U \setminus \partial X$ and $g = h - N(\Lambda_0)$, and the relative parametric transversality. *Step 1, a good system.* A structurable $\Lambda_0$ carries a decoration, whose good system is all that the empty family needs. *Step 2, compactness of the support.* $|\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)|$ is compact ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.isCompact_image_supp_comp⟧: with $N(\Lambda_0) \le 1$ and domain support in $U$ this is the compactness of the "in particular" of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.21) ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionBranched · SBLocalization.isCompact_orbitSupp_comp⟧, read as a statement about the image of $\{x : \Lambda_0(f(x)) > 0\}$ in $|X|$. *Step 3, from local to global* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.exists_relGPFamily_of_compact⟧. The images $\pi(Q_x)$ of the sets of the local families are open (Proposition 7.1.8) and cover the compact set of Step 2; finitely many suffice; the families on them add, by induction over the finite set starting from the empty family ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.nonempty_relGPFamily_biUnion⟧, to one relative family $F$ on a set $Q$ that contains $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)$, the $Q_x$ being saturated. *Step 4, a regular parameter.* $F$ satisfies the hypotheses of the relative parametric transversality: its domain support lies in $U \setminus \partial X \subset U$, and $|t|_1(h - N(\Lambda_0)) \le |t|_1(1 - N(\Lambda_0))$ since $h \le 1$. So for some $\varepsilon > 0$, almost every $t$ with $\|t\| < \varepsilon$ gives general position. A ball has positive measure, so there is such a $t$ with $\|t\| < \min(\varepsilon, 1/(\ell + 1))$ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.exists_norm_lt_of_ae⟧; in the sup norm of $\mathbb R^\ell$ this gives $|t|_1 < 1$ ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.sum_abs_lt_one⟧. *Step 5, the perturbation* $\tilde\Lambda = \Lambda_0 \oplus F_t$. It is structurable (Proposition 13.3.12). Over $\partial X$ it equals $\Lambda_0$: a point of $\partial X$ is not in the domain support of $F_t$, which lies in $U \setminus \partial X$. Its domain support lies in the union of the two, inside $U$. Its norm: with $m = h - N(\Lambda_0) > 0$ at $x$, $N(F_t)(x) \le |t|_1m < m$, so $N(\tilde\Lambda)(x) \le N(\Lambda_0)(x) + N(F_t)(x) < h(x)$, pointwise, without a uniform margin. It is in general position by the choice of $t$, hence transversal ⟦Chapter15/GeneralPositionAssembly · SBLocalization.isTransversal_of_isInGeneralPosition⟧. $\square$ Under the hypotheses of the relative statement the two steps give the relative statement ⟦Chapter15/RelativeReduction · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_of_hyp⟧; the relative parametric transversality is proved (below), so the relative local families alone suffice ⟦Chapter15/RelativeParametric · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_relative_of_local⟧.

*Readings.* "Supported away from $\partial X$" is domain support in $U \setminus \partial X$ ($\partial X$ is closed and saturated). The text bounds the family by the norm of the perturbation without saying by what; the bound $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1(h - N(\Lambda_0))$ is the one that keeps $N(\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t) < h$ for $|t|_1 < 1$ pointwise, and the parametric step needs only the weaker $|t|_1(1 - N(\Lambda_0))$. The text writes $\Lambda_t \oplus \Lambda_0$; the formalization adds in the other order, which changes nothing.

**The relative parametric transversality** (explicit) ⟦Chapter15/RelativeParametric · SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPositionRel⟧. For $X$ tame, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data, $(N, U)$ controlling compactness and $\Lambda_0$ an sc⁺-multisection with $N(\Lambda_0) \le 1$ and domain support in $U$, the relative parametric transversality holds. The compactness of $|S_f|$ is not used; that of $|\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda_0 \circ f)|$ comes from the control of compactness. The proof is that of the parametric transversality of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.25) with a branch $s^0_a$ of $\Lambda_0$ in place of the zero section, in four parts: one branch, the local step, the relative (15.2), and the assembly.

*One branch of $\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t$.* On a common open set $O$, local representations $(s^0_a, \sigma^0_a)$ of $\Lambda_0$ and $(s_i, \sigma_i)$ of $\Lambda$ give the representation of $\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda$ by the sections $s^0_a + s_i$ with the weights $\sigma^0_a\sigma_i$, reindexed by a finite type (Definition 13.2.9 (3)) ⟦Chapter15/RelativeBranch · SBLocalization.isLocalRepOn_multisectionAdd⟧: the sums are sc⁺ on $O$, the weights sum to $\sum_a\sigma^0_a\sum_i\sigma_i = 1$, and the count formula is that of the sum of Part XIII ⟦Chapter13/MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn⟧. For a linear family the branch through $s^0_a$ and $\sum_jt_js_{ij}$ is the slice at $t$ of Part I's parametrized section on $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$,
$$F_{a,i}(t, y) = (f - s^0_a)|_O(y) + \sum_jt_j(-s_{ij})|_O(y),$$
that is, the slice at $t$ is $(f - (s^0_a + \sum_jt_js_{ij}))|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/RelativeBranch · SBLocalization.paramSlice_branch_eq_rel⟧, a fibrewise identity in $W_y$ (the restricted sections being $f$ plus $(-1)$ times the section extended by zero off $O$).

*Relative (15.1) gives Part I's conditions (i)–(ii)* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeBranch · SBLocalization.isParamGP_restrictTo_of_onto_rel⟧. Let $c$ be a strong bundle chart of $W$ with domain in $O$, centred at $x$ ($c(x) = 0$), with $f(x) = s^0(x)$, $T$ a presentation of its model quadrant, and assume that $(v, \tau) \mapsto (f - s^0)'(x)v + \sum_j\tau_js_j(x)$ maps $T^R_xX \times \mathbb R^\ell$ onto $W_x$. Then in the transported chart of $W|_O$ the parametrized section $F$ has Part I's properties (i)–(ii) of the proof of Theorem 5.3.10 ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP⟧. The proof reads everything in the chart. The linearization at $0$ of the principal part of $(f - s^0)|_O$ in the transported chart is the chart derivative $D((\hat f - \hat s^0) \circ r)(0)$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalIFT · SBLocalization.scDeriv_restrictTo_subRestrict⟧; the principal part of $-s_j$ at $0$ is minus the chart image of $s_j(x)$ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.principal_eq_fiberLin⟧ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.principal_restrictTo_negRestrict⟧; and the chart image of the intrinsic operator applied to $v$ is the chart derivative applied to the chart vector of $v$ ⟦Chapter15/BranchChart · SBLocalization.fiberLin_toIntr_subDeriv⟧. So the hypothesis says: for every $w$ there are $v \in T^R_xX$ and $\tau$ with $D(v) + \sum_j\tau_j\hat s_j(0) = \hat w$. (i), $F'(0, x)$ onto: given $k$ with $(0, k) \in K$, write $k = \hat w$ and take $u = v$ and $a = -\tau$, the sign coming from the $-s_j$. (ii), the kernel of $F'(0, x)$ is transversal to $\mathbb R^\ell \oplus T^R$: given a tangent vector $w$ at $0$, apply the hypothesis to the image $D(w)$; it gives $v \in T^R$ and $\tau$ with $D(v) + \sum_j\tau_j\hat s_j(0) = D(w)$; then $u = w - v$ has $D(u) - \sum_j\tau_j\hat s_j(0) = 0$, so $(\tau, u)$ is in the kernel, and $w - u = v \in T^R$. These are the two lines of linear algebra of the bridge of §XV.24, with $s^0$ for $0$.

*The parametrized branch is in general position* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeBranch · SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_branchParam_rel⟧. Let $(s^0_a, \sigma^0_a)$ represent $\Lambda_0$ on $O$, $s^0_a(x) = f(x)$, and assume relative (15.1) at $x$ for the sections $s_j$. Then $F_{a}(t, y) = (f - s^0_a)|_O + \sum_jt_j(-s_j)|_O$ is in general position at $(0, x)$ (Definition 5.3.9 on $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$). *Proof.* $x$ is smooth, being a zero of $f - s^0_a$ ⟦Chapter15/Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_eq⟧, so the tame germ data give a tame strong bundle chart centred at $x$; restrict it to $O$, and take a presentation $T$ of its quadrant. With this chart and the local structure $(s^0, \sigma^0)$ as local data, the intrinsic operator $(f - s^0_a)'(x)$ lies in the support of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$ ⟦Chapter15/LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linearization_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter15/Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_support_linSumIntr_iff⟧, so relative (15.1) applies to it in this chart. The previous step gives (i)–(ii) in the transported chart; $(f - s^0_a)|_O$ is a tame sc-Fredholm section of $W|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.isScFredholmSectionTame_subRestrict⟧ vanishing at $x$; and Part I's lemma that (i)–(ii) at a zero give general position of the parametrized section ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP⟧ concludes.

*The local step* ⟦Chapter15/RelativeParametric · SBLocalization.exists_local_paramGP_rel⟧. Let $X$ be tame, $\Lambda_0$ an sc⁺-multisection, $\Lambda_t$ sc⁺-multisections with relative (15.1) at $x_0$. Then there are an open $V \ni x_0$, $\delta > 0$ and a Lebesgue null set $C_V \subset \mathbb R^\ell$ such that $(f, \Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t)$ is in general position at every $y \in V$ with $(\Lambda_0 \oplus \Lambda_t)(f(y)) > 0$, for $\|t\| < \delta$, $t \notin C_V$. *Proof.* Relative (15.1) provides a linear representation $\sum_jt_js_{ij}$ of the family on $O_1$; take a representation $(s^0_a, \sigma^0_a)$ of $\Lambda_0$ on $O_2$, its sections extended by zero, and $O = O_1 \cap O_2$; $O$ is a tame M-polyfold, an open subset of a tame one. For every pair $(a, i)$ there are an open $W_{a,i} \ni (0, x_0)$ in $\mathbb R^\ell \times O$ and a null set $C_{a,i}$ such that, for $(t, y) \in W_{a,i}$ with $f(y) = s^0_a(y) + \sum_jt_js_{ij}(y)$ and $t \notin C_{a,i}$, the branch $(f - (s^0_a + \sum_jt_js_{ij}))|_O$ is in Part I's general position at $y$. Two cases.
