Every class has a representative between any two given structures of $c$ and $d$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.exists_rep⟧: compose a representative $(f, \mathfrak f) : (X', \alpha') \to (Y', \beta')$ with the chosen isomorphisms $(X, \alpha) \to (X', \alpha')$ and $(Y', \beta') \to (Y, \beta)$ and use Step 3. *Step 5, Remark 16.1.9* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.toFun⟧: the continuous map of the class is $\beta \circ |\mathfrak f| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ for every representative, by Step 1 and Step 1 of PS. *Step 6, identities* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id_eq⟧: $1_{(Z,c)} = [(\mathrm{Id}_Z, [1_X])]$, the same class for every $(X, \alpha) \in c$, since two such representatives are related by the chosen isomorphism on both sides.

**Proof that the claim of Definition 16.1.10 does not hold as we read it.** *The claim in Lean:* if $(f, \mathfrak f) \sim (f', \mathfrak f')$ and $(g, \mathfrak g) \sim (g', \mathfrak g')$, and both pairs have a common middle structure, then the composites are equivalent. The example uses only the printed hypotheses: polyfold structures and morphisms of PS.

*Step 1, the structures.* $Z = W = V = \mathbb R$. $(X, \alpha) = (U, \gamma)$ is the polyfold structure $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action (§XVI.1), with $\gamma \circ \pi = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.z3_β_π⟧. $(Y, \beta)$ is $(\mathbb Z/3)^2 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, the action groupoid of the trivial action of $K = (\mathbb Z/3)^2$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.K2⟧ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2EpGroupoid⟧. As in §XVI.1, its orbit map is injective ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.injective_π_k2⟧ and a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.isHomeomorph_π_k2⟧, $|Y| \cong \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2OrbitHomeomorph⟧, it satisfies (ZHOU) ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.isZhou_k2⟧, and $(Y, \beta)$ is a polyfold structure ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2Structure⟧ with $\beta \circ \pi = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2Structure_β_π⟧. All continuous maps are the identity of $\mathbb R$.

*Step 2, the functors.* All are the identity on objects: $\iota : \mathbb Z/3 \to K$, $\iota(g) = (g, 1)$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι⟧; $\sigma : K \to K$, the swap of the two factors ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.σ⟧, with $\sigma \circ \sigma = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.σ_σ⟧; $\mathrm{pr}_1 : K \to \mathbb Z/3$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.pr₁⟧; and $T : \mathbb Z/3 \to \mathbb Z/3$, $T(g) = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.T⟧. The orbit map of the generalized map of a functor that is the identity on objects is the identity on orbits ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.orbitMap_map_π⟧, so every pair $(\mathrm{Id}, [\Phi])$ below is a morphism of PS.

*Step 3, two equivalent representatives of $\hat f$.* For $k \in \{1, \sigma\}$ let $a_k = (\mathrm{Id}, [\iota] \circ [k]) : (X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.a⟧, and $b = (\mathrm{Id}, [\mathrm{pr}_1]) : (Y, \beta) \to (U, \gamma)$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.b⟧. $[\sigma]$ is a generalized isomorphism, its own inverse ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.isGeneralizedIso_σ⟧, so $(\mathrm{Id}, [\sigma])$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.kσ⟧ is an isomorphism over the identity ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.kσ_isIdIso⟧. The square of Definition 16.1.6 with $h = 1$ and $k = [\sigma]$ commutes, so $a_1 \sim a_\sigma$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.a_equiv⟧.

*Step 4, the composites.* $b \circ a_1$ has generalized map $[\iota] \circ [\mathrm{pr}_1] = [\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \iota] = [1_X]$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι_pr₁⟧ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.gen_comp_one⟧, and $b \circ a_\sigma$ has $[\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \sigma \circ \iota] = [T]$, since $\mathrm{pr}_1(\sigma(g, 1)) = \mathrm{pr}_1(1, g) = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι_σ_pr₁⟧ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.gen_comp_σ⟧.

*Step 5, not equivalent* ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_equiv_comp⟧. Suppose $(\mathrm{Id}, [1_X]) \sim (\mathrm{Id}, [T])$ through $h$, $k$. Then $[T] \circ h = k \circ [1_X]$, so $[T] = k \circ h^{-1}$ is a generalized isomorphism (cancellation of isomorphisms in the localization). But $[T]$ is the class of a functor, and by Theorem 10.3.10 (Part X) the class of a functor is invertible iff the functor is an equivalence; $T$ is not, not being faithful: it sends the non-trivial isotropy elements to $1$ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isEquivalence_T⟧ ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isIso_T⟧.

*Step 6, on classes* ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_exists_comp⟧: no composition of sc-smooth maps agrees with the composite of representatives for all choices, since it would have to equal both classes of Step 5.

*The mechanism.* It is that of §XVI.2: in Definition 16.1.6 the isomorphism $(k, \mathrm{Id}_W)$ of the middle structure is not determined by $\mathrm{Id}_W$, because two generalized isomorphisms of $Y$ with the identity orbit map need not agree. The middle structure is not effective ⟦Chapter16/CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isEffective_k2⟧.

**Proof of the effective form.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective⟧. Let the middle structure $(Y', \beta')$ be effective, $a \sim a'$ through $(h, k)$ and $b \sim b'$ through $(k', l)$, where $k$ and $k'$ are isomorphisms over the identity $(Y, \beta) \to (Y', \beta')$. By the uniqueness for an effective target (§XVI.2), $k = k'$. Then the two squares paste to one square for the composites, with the outer isomorphisms $h$ and $l$. *Step 2, composites of representatives* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp⟧: for representatives $(f, \mathfrak f) : (X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$ and $(g, \mathfrak g) : (Y', \beta') \to (V, \gamma)$ whose middle structures differ, the composite is $(g \circ f, \mathfrak g \circ k \circ \mathfrak f)$ with the chosen isomorphism $k$ of Step 4 of PS. For an effective $d$ it respects the relation ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp_equiv⟧, by Step 1 and the uniqueness, which makes the chosen $k$ the only one. *Step 3, effectiveness on classes* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.IsEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.isEffective_iff⟧: a polyfold is effective if one structure is, and then every structure is, since effectiveness is invariant under equivalences of ep-groupoids ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEffective_iff⟧ (Remark 10.1.12, through the bijections of isotropy groups) and so under generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · EPLoc.isEffective_iff_of_isGeneralizedIso⟧. *Step 4, the composite of classes* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_mk⟧: for effective $d$, the lift of Step 2 to the quotients. *Step 5, the laws* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_assoc⟧: on representatives, with the chosen isomorphisms absorbed by Step 3 of Definition 16.1.6.

**Definition 16.1.11** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · EffPolyfold⟧. Objects are effective polyfolds, morphisms sc-smooth maps, identities $[(\mathrm{Id}_Z, [1_X])]$, and composition from Step 4. *Narrower* because, as we read Definition 16.1.10, the composition is not defined on all polyfolds. Presumably the text intends effective polyfolds, or morphisms carrying a chosen isomorphism of the middle structure; the formalization takes the first. Witness: the one-point polyfold ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldStructure.pointStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · EffPolyfold.point⟧, whose ep-groupoid has trivial isotropy and so is effective.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text gives Definitions 16.1.6–16.1.11 without proofs. Three points are made explicit. First, the laws of PS, which hold componentwise once the continuous map is seen to be determined by the generalized map. Second, the composite of two classes: the text composes representatives "with a common middle structure", which leaves open how two representatives are brought to a common middle structure; the formalization does it with a chosen isomorphism over the identity between the two middle structures, and it is exactly there that the choice matters, since another isomorphism over the identity can give an inequivalent composite. Third, the answer to the question "which polyfolds form a category": the effective ones, where Theorem 10.3.19 makes the isomorphism over the identity unique, so that the choice disappears. The counterexample is minimal in the sense that all continuous maps are the identity and all functors are the identity on objects; the only data that differ are the isotropy homomorphisms.

### XVI.5 Lemma 16.1.13 (2017: Lemma 16.1), Definitions 16.1.14, 16.1.17 (2017: 16.9, 16.11), Lemma 16.1.19 (2017: Lemma 16.2), Definition 16.1.20 (2017: 16.12), pp. 712–714

**Statement.** *The degeneracy index of a structure* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldStructure.degIndex⟧: $d_{(X,\beta)}(z) = d_{|X|}(\beta^{-1}(z))$. *Lemma 16.1.13* (p. 712, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_1_13⟧: equivalent structures have the same degeneracy index. *Definition 16.1.14* (p. 712, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.degIndex⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_1_14⟧: $d_Z(z) = d_X(x)$ for every $(X, \beta) \in c$ and $\beta(|x|) = z$. *Definition 16.1.17* (p. 713, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.boundary⟧: $\partial Z = \{z : d_Z(z) \ge 1\}$. *Lemma 16.1.19* (p. 714, stronger) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_1_19⟧: for equivalent structures, $X$ is tame iff $Y$ is; the text states one direction. *Definition 16.1.20* (p. 714, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.IsTame⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_1_20⟧: a polyfold is tame if one, and then every, structure in $c$ has $X$ tame.

**Proof of Lemma 16.1.13.** *Step 1, the index on the orbit space.* $d_{(X,\beta)}(z) = d_X(x)$ for any $x$ with $\beta(|x|) = z$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldStructure.degIndex_eq⟧, because $d_X$ is invariant under morphisms and so descends to $|X|$. *Step 2, invariance.* For a generalized isomorphism $f : X \to Y$, $d_{|Y|} \circ |f| = d_{|X|}$: Proposition 11.1.2 (Part XI), which reduces to the invariance of the degeneracy index under local sc-diffeomorphisms (Part IV) through the legs of a diagram. *Step 3.* If $(X, \alpha) \sim (Y, \beta)$ through $f$, then $|f| = \beta^{-1} \circ \alpha$ (§XVI.1), so $d_{|Y|}(\beta^{-1}(z)) = d_{|Y|}(|f|(\alpha^{-1}(z))) = d_{|X|}(\alpha^{-1}(z))$.

**Proof of Definitions 16.1.14 and 16.1.17.** The index of the class is that of its chosen structure, and by Lemma 16.1.13 that of every structure in $c$. $\partial Z$ is computed in any representative ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldStructure · PolyfoldClass.mem_boundary_iff⟧: $z \in \partial Z$ iff $x \in \partial X$ for one, or every, $x$ with $\beta(|x|) = z$, $\partial X$ being the objects of positive degeneracy index.

**Proof of Lemma 16.1.19 and Definition 16.1.20.** *Step 1.* Tameness of an ep-groupoid is invariant under equivalences in both directions (Chapter 11, Part XI): an equivalence is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, and tameness of an M-polyfold is local and invariant under sc-diffeomorphisms (Part II). *Step 2.* Along a diagram $X \leftarrow A \rightarrow Y$, $X$ tame iff $A$ tame iff $Y$ tame. The text states "if $X$ is tame then $Y$ is"; the other direction follows by symmetry of the relation, so the formal statement is the equivalence. *Step 3.* Definition 16.1.20 is "the chosen structure is tame", which by Step 2 is "some, equivalently every, structure is tame".

**Not formalized from §16.1.** Proposition 16.1.12 (the lifts $Z_i$ and their topology, which the raised polyfolds of §XVI.6 partly cover), Definition 16.1.15 and Remark 16.1.16 (subpolyfolds), Example 16.1.18, Definition 16.1.21 (faces of a polyfold) and Proposition 16.1.22 (§XVI.28).

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text proves Lemma 16.1.13 by the invariance of the degeneracy index under generalized isomorphisms, as here; the formalization makes the orbit-space form of the index explicit, $d_{|X|}$, because the structure map $\beta$ lives on $|X|$. For Lemma 16.1.19 the text proves one direction; the formal statement is an equivalence, which costs one application of the symmetry of Definition 16.1.2. Definition 16.1.17 is stated through the index as printed; the characterization of $\partial Z$ through any representative is a lemma, used in §§XVI.15, XVI.22 and XVI.26 to translate boundary conditions between $Z$ and a model.

### XVI.6 The raised polyfolds $(Z, c)^i$ (p. 715)

**Statement** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raise⟧. The text defines $(Z, c)^1$ as $Z_1$ with the structures $(X^1, \alpha|)$. The formalization: $(Z, c)^1$ is the space $|X_0^1|$ for the chosen structure $(X_0, \alpha_0)$ of $c$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.RaisedSpace⟧, with the polyfold class of the structures $(X^1, \alpha^1)$ for $(X, \alpha) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseStructure⟧, where $\alpha^1 : |X^1| \to |X_0^1|$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseMap⟧ is induced by the raise of a generalized isomorphism realizing $(X, \alpha) \sim (X_0, \alpha_0)$. An injective continuous map $(Z, c)^1 \to Z$ has image $Z_1 = \beta(|X|_1)$ for every $(X, \beta) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.range_raiseIncl⟧. $(Z, c)^i$ is the $i$-fold raise ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseN⟧. *Restated* because $(Z, c)^1$ is a space with an injection into $Z$, not the subspace $Z_1$: its topology is that of $|X^1|$, which is finer than the subspace topology. The text means the former (the structure of $X^1$ carries its own topology); the formalization makes that explicit.

**Proof.** *Step 1, raising functors.* The index raise $X \mapsto X^1$ of Chapter 7 is functorial on equivalences and functors ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.liftOne_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.liftOne_id⟧, and the orbit map of $\Phi^1$ is the restriction of that of $\Phi$ to $|X^1| \subseteq |X|$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.orbitIncl_orbitMap_liftOne⟧.

*Step 2, raising diagrams.* A diagram $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y$ raises to $X^1 \xleftarrow{F^1} A^1 \xrightarrow{\Phi^1} Y^1$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.liftOne⟧, the raise of an equivalence being an equivalence. Refinements raise to refinements ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.liftOne⟧, including the identity refinement and composites ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_liftOne_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_liftOne_comp⟧, because the weak fibre product of Chapter 10 commutes with the raise; so equivalent diagrams raise to equivalent diagrams ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.liftOne⟧, and the orbit maps restrict ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitIncl_orbitMap_liftOne⟧.

*Step 3, raising generalized maps* ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom⟧: by Step 2 the raise is well defined on the localization, with $1^1 = 1$ and $(\mathfrak g \circ \mathfrak f)^1 = \mathfrak g^1 \circ \mathfrak f^1$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom_comp⟧, so it keeps generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_liftOneHom⟧, and $|\mathfrak f^1| = |\mathfrak f|$ on $|X^1|$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitIncl_orbitMap_liftOneHom⟧. Two generalized maps with the same orbit map have raises with the same orbit map ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_liftOneHom_eq⟧, because $|X^1| \to |X|$ is injective.

*Step 4, the raised structure is a polyfold structure.* $X^1$ has a paracompact orbit space ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.liftOne_paracompact⟧: $|X^1|$ is metrizable by Proposition 7.5.3 (Part VII), since $X^1$ is again an ep-groupoid. $X^1$ satisfies (ZHOU) ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.liftOne_isZhou⟧, by Propositions 7.4.8 and 7.4.9 (Part VII): the natural representations of $X^1$ are restrictions of those of $X$, and the sets $\mathrm{Fix}$ and their interiors behave under the raise as the propositions state.

*Step 5, the maps $\alpha^1$.* For $(X, \alpha) \in c$, $\alpha^1 = |\mathfrak f^1|$ for a generalized isomorphism $\mathfrak f$ with $\alpha_0 \circ |\mathfrak f| = \alpha$; it does not depend on $\mathfrak f$ by Step 3 ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseMap_eq⟧, is compatible with composition ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseMap_comp⟧, and is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.isHomeomorph_raiseMap⟧ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseHomeomorph⟧, being the orbit map of a generalized isomorphism. So $(X^1, \alpha^1)$ is a polyfold structure on $(Z, c)^1$, and all of them are equivalent through the raised isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseStructure_equiv⟧; the class does not depend on the representative it is built from ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raise_eq⟧.

*Step 6, the inclusion.* $(Z, c)^1 \to Z$ is $\alpha_0 \circ \iota$ with $\iota : |X_0^1| \to |X_0|$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl⟧; it is injective ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl_injective⟧ (orbits of $X^1$ are orbits of $X$ through level-$1$ points) and continuous ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.continuous_raiseIncl⟧, it satisfies $\mathrm{incl} \circ \alpha^1 = \alpha \circ \iota$ for every structure ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl_raiseMap⟧, and its image is $Z_1$ by Step 3. *Step 7, iteration.* $(Z, c)^0 = (Z, c)$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseN_zero⟧ and $(Z, c)^{i+1} = ((Z, c)^i)^1$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseN_succ⟧, with the space and class carried together ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.PolyfoldPair⟧. The text's index notation $mI$ is not introduced; $Z_i = \alpha(|X_i|)$ for every structure.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text defines the raised polyfold by restricting each structure $(X, \alpha)$ to $X^1$ and gluing; that the restricted pairs are polyfold structures, and that they are equivalent, is left implicit. The formalization proves both: paracompactness through Proposition 7.5.3, (ZHOU) through Propositions 7.4.8 and 7.4.9, and the equivalence through the raise of generalized isomorphisms, which needs the raise to commute with weak fibre products so that refinements raise to refinements. The topology is the second point: the text writes $(Z, c)^1$ for a space whose underlying set is $Z_1$, and the formalization keeps the topology of $|X^1|$ rather than the subspace topology of $Z_1 \subseteq Z$, since only the former makes $\alpha^1$ a homeomorphism; the inclusion into $Z$ is continuous and injective but in general not an embedding.

### XVI.7 Lemma 16.2.1 (2017: Lemma 16.3), p. 716: isomorphisms of polyfold structures and their tangents

**Statement** (does not hold as we read it; its orbit form and its form for an effective target hold). The text: if two isomorphisms $(f, \mathfrak f), (g, \mathfrak g) : (X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$ of polyfold structures have $f = g$, then $\mathfrak f = \mathfrak g$ and $T\mathfrak f = T\mathfrak g$. Its proof: $|\mathfrak f| = |\mathfrak g|$, then Theorem 10.3.19. The statement in Lean ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.Lemma_16_2_1⟧: $f$, $g$ homeomorphisms, $\mathfrak f$, $\mathfrak g$ generalized isomorphisms with $f \circ \alpha = \beta \circ |\mathfrak f|$ and $g \circ \alpha = \beta \circ |\mathfrak g|$, and $f = g$; conclusion $\mathfrak f = \mathfrak g$ and $T\mathfrak f = T\mathfrak g$. It does not hold as we read it ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.not_lemma_16_2_1⟧. *The orbit form* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_2_1_orbit⟧, under exactly the text's hypotheses: $|\mathfrak f| = |\mathfrak g|$ and $|T\mathfrak f| = |T\mathfrak g|$. *The effective form* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective⟧: if $Y$ is effective, the text's conclusion holds.

**The tangent of a generalized map.** For $\mathfrak f = [X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$, $T\mathfrak f$ is the class of $[TX \xleftarrow{TF} TA \xrightarrow{T\Phi} TY]$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentHom⟧. *Step 1.* The tangent of an ep-groupoid (Theorem 8.1.1, Part VIII) is taken in any universe ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EP.tangentAny⟧, and agrees with Chapter 8's where both are defined. *Step 2.* The tangent of a diagram is a diagram, since the tangent of an equivalence is an equivalence (Theorem 10.1.7, Part X) ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.Diagram.tangentAny⟧. *Step 3.* Refinements go to refinements ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.tangentAny⟧, compatibly with composition of refinements ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_tangentAny_comp⟧, so equivalent diagrams have equivalent tangents ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.tangentAny⟧. *Step 4.* The result is a copy of Chapter 11's tangent functor on the localization ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentHom_eq_tangentFunctor_map⟧, compatible with identities and composition ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentHom_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentHom_comp⟧, and it preserves generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_tangentHom⟧.

**Proof that the lemma does not hold as we read it.** *The example* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_2_1_counterexample⟧ is the pair of §XVI.2. On the polyfold structure $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ of $\mathbb R$ with the trivial action, take $f = g = \mathrm{id}$, $\mathfrak f = [X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} X]$ and $\mathfrak g = [1_X]$. Both squares commute, since both orbit maps are the identity; the orbit space is paracompact; (ZHOU) holds; $f = g$; and $\mathfrak f \ne \mathfrak g$ (§XVI.2, Step 4). The last step of the text's proof is Theorem 10.3.19, which does not hold as we read it ⟦Chapter10/LocalizationLRCounterexample · LocalizationLRCounterexample.not_theorem_10_3_19⟧ (Part X). Whether $T\mathfrak f \ne T\mathfrak g$ in this example is not decided; their orbit maps agree, by the orbit form.

**Proof of the orbit form.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.orbitMap_eq_of_comp⟧: $|\mathfrak f| = \beta^{-1} \circ f \circ \alpha$, so $f = g$ gives $|\mathfrak f| = |\mathfrak g|$.

*Step 2, reduction to an automorphism* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentHom_eq⟧: if $X$ or $Y$ has (LR) and $|\mathfrak f| = |\mathfrak g|$, then $|T\mathfrak f| = |T\mathfrak g|$. With $\mathfrak g'$ an inverse of $\mathfrak f$, $e = \mathfrak g' \circ \mathfrak g$ is a generalized automorphism of $X$ with $|e| = |\mathfrak f|^{-1} \circ |\mathfrak g| = 1$ (Proposition 10.3.11), and $\mathfrak g = \mathfrak f \circ e$; since $T$ is a functor, $|T\mathfrak g| = |T\mathfrak f| \circ |Te|$, and it suffices that $|Te| = 1$. If only $Y$ has (LR), the same argument runs with $\mathfrak g \circ \mathfrak f^{-1}$, an automorphism of $Y$.

*Step 3, the automorphism* ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentHom_eq_id⟧. Represent $e$ by a diagram $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} X$ of equivalences; $|e| = 1$ says $|F| = |\Phi|$. $A$ has (LR) by Proposition 10.1.9 (Part X), being equivalent to $X$. By Proposition 10.1.10 (1), two functors $A \to X$ with the same orbit map from an ep-groupoid with (LR) are connected locally by families of morphisms, and by Proposition 10.1.10 (2) these give $|TF| = |T\Phi|$, that is $|Te| = 1$.

*Step 4.* (ZHOU) gives (LR) for $X$ (§XVI.1), so Steps 2–3 apply to every polyfold structure.

**Proof of the effective form.** If $Y$ is effective, then $\mathfrak f = \mathfrak g$ by Remark 16.1.7 for an effective target (§XVI.2), and so $T\mathfrak f = T\mathfrak g$. Its hypotheses are satisfiable ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective_hypotheses⟧: the point ep-groupoid is effective and satisfies (ZHOU).

*What the rest of §16.2 needs.* Only the orbit form: the gluing of $T(Z, c)$ uses the maps $|T\mathfrak f|$ (§XVI.8), and the remark before Definition 16.2.5 uses the analogous statement for forms (§XVI.10).

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text's proof has two steps: $|\mathfrak f| = |\mathfrak g|$, then Theorem 10.3.19 for $\mathfrak f = \mathfrak g$, from which $T\mathfrak f = T\mathfrak g$ is immediate. The formalization keeps the first step, replaces the second by Proposition 10.1.10 at the level of tangent orbit maps, and proves the conclusion on orbit spaces only. For the tangent conclusion this is a genuinely different route: it never compares $\mathfrak f$ with $\mathfrak g$, only their effect on orbits, and it needs only (LR), which (ZHOU) gives. The full conclusion is recovered for an effective target, through the effective Theorem 10.3.19.

### XVI.8 The tangent $T(Z, c)$, (16.5), Lemma 16.2.2, Definition 16.2.3 (2017: Lemma 16.4, Definition 16.14), and the projection $\tau_Z$, pp. 716–719

**Statement.** *The construction* (pp. 716–718, same, with a base structure in place of the gluing; decision (3)): $T(Z, c) = |TX_0|$ for the chosen structure $(X_0, \alpha_0)$ of $c$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.TangentSpace⟧, with the orbit space topology ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentSpaceTopology⟧; for $(X, \alpha) \in c$, $T\alpha = |T\mathfrak f| : |TX| \to T(Z, c)$ for a generalized isomorphism $\mathfrak f : X \to X_0$ with $\alpha_0 \circ |\mathfrak f| = \alpha$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentMap⟧. *(16.5)* (same) ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentMap_comp⟧: $T\beta \circ |Th| = T\alpha$ for every generalized isomorphism $h : X \to Y$ with $\beta \circ |h| = \alpha$. *Lemma 16.2.2* (p. 718, same) ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.lemma_16_2_2⟧: (1) every $T\alpha$ is a homeomorphism; (2) the topology of $T(Z, c)$ is the unique one for which one, and then every, $T\alpha$ is a homeomorphism; (3) $T(Z, c)$ is metrizable. *Definition 16.2.3* (p. 719, restated) ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangent⟧ ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_2_3⟧: the tangent $(T(Z, c), Tc)$ is the polyfold whose class contains every $(TX, T\alpha)$, $(X, \alpha) \in c$. *The projection* (p. 717, restated) ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentProj⟧: $\tau_Z : T(Z, c) \to (Z, c)^1$ with $\tau_Z \circ T\alpha = \alpha^1 \circ |\tau_X|$.

**Proof of the construction.** *Step 1, $T\alpha$ does not depend on $\mathfrak f$* ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentMap_eq⟧. Two generalized isomorphisms $\mathfrak f, \mathfrak f'$ with $\alpha_0 \circ |\mathfrak f| = \alpha = \alpha_0 \circ |\mathfrak f'|$ have the same orbit map $\alpha_0^{-1} \circ \alpha$, hence the same $|T\mathfrak f|$ by the orbit form of Lemma 16.2.1 (§XVI.7, Steps 2–3). The text says "the unique $\mathfrak f$"; $\mathfrak f$ need not be unique (§XVI.2), but $|T\mathfrak f|$ is, and it is all that the construction uses. *Step 2, (16.5).* Let $\mathfrak f_Y : Y \to X_0$ realize $(Y, \beta)$. Then $\mathfrak f_Y \circ h$ realizes $(X, \alpha)$, since $\alpha_0 \circ |\mathfrak f_Y| \circ |h| = \beta \circ |h| = \alpha$. By Step 1, $T\alpha = |T(\mathfrak f_Y \circ h)| = |T\mathfrak f_Y| \circ |Th| = T\beta \circ |Th|$, using that $T$ is a functor on the localization (§XVI.7). *Step 3, homeomorphisms* ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.isHomeomorph_tangentMap⟧ ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentHomeomorph⟧: the orbit map of a generalized isomorphism is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isHomeomorph_orbitMap_of_isGeneralizedIso⟧ (its inverse is the orbit map of the inverse, by Proposition 10.3.11), and $T\mathfrak f$ is a generalized isomorphism.

**Proof of Lemma 16.2.2.** (1) is Step 3. (2): if $\tau$ is a topology on the set $T(Z, c)$ for which some $T\alpha$ is a homeomorphism, then the open sets of $\tau$ are exactly the sets whose preimage under $T\alpha$ is open in $|TX|$; the same holds for the given topology by (1); so the two agree. Since all $T\alpha$ are homeomorphisms for the given topology, "one" and "every" agree. (3): Theorem 8.1.15 (Part VIII) makes $|TX_0|$ metrizable ⟦Chapter8/TangentOrbit · metrizableSpace_tangent_orbitSpace⟧.

**Proof of Definition 16.2.3.** *Step 1, $(TX, T\alpha)$ is a polyfold structure* ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentStructure⟧. $|TX|$ is paracompact by Theorem 8.1.15 ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.tangent_paracompact⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentOrbit · theorem_8_1_15⟧, and $TX$ satisfies (ZHOU) by Proposition 8.1.16 in its 2021 form ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.tangent_isZhou⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentZhouReflect2021 · proposition_8_1_16_2021⟧ (Part VIII). *Step 2, they are equivalent* ⟦Chapter16/TangentPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentStructure_equiv⟧: for $h : X \to Y$ with $\beta \circ |h| = \alpha$, $Th$ is a generalized isomorphism with $T\beta \circ |Th| = T\alpha$ by (16.5). *Step 3.* $Tc$ is the class of $(TX_0, T\alpha_0)$, and by Step 2 every $(TX, T\alpha)$ lies in it. *Readings.* $T(Z, c)$ lives one universe up, as $TX$ does in Chapter 8. "Restated" because the text defines $T(Z, c)$ as a disjoint union modulo identifications; the base structure gives a canonically homeomorphic space (Lemma 16.2.2 (2)).

**Proof of the projection $\tau_Z$.** *Step 1, naturality of $\tau$ for functors* ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.orbitMap_tangentProj_tangent⟧: for a functor $\Phi$, $|\tau_Y| \circ |T\Phi| = |\Phi^1| \circ |\tau_X|$, from the pointwise identity $\tau \circ T\Phi = \Phi^1 \circ \tau$ on objects. *Step 2, for diagrams and generalized maps* ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_tangentProj_tangentAny⟧ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentProj_tangentHom⟧: through both legs, with the raised generalized maps of §XVI.6. *Step 3, the definition*: $\tau_Z = |\tau_{X_0}| : |TX_0| \to |X_0^1|$; it is continuous ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.continuous_tangentProj⟧, and for every $(X, \alpha) \in c$, $\tau_Z \circ T\alpha = \alpha^1 \circ |\tau_X|$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentProj_tangentMap⟧ by Step 2 applied to a realizing $\mathfrak f$. Composed with the inclusion $(Z, c)^1 \to Z$, it is the text's square into $Z$ ⟦Chapter16/RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl_tangentProj_tangentMap⟧.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text constructs $T(Z, c)$ as the disjoint union of the $|TX|$ over all $(X, \alpha) \in c$, modulo the identifications by $|T\mathfrak f|$ for the unique $\mathfrak f$, and Lemma 16.2.2 then puts a topology on the quotient. The formalization takes one structure as base point and defines $T\alpha$ as a map into it; the identifications of the text become the identity (16.5), and Lemma 16.2.2 (2) shows that the base point does not matter topologically. The two constructions give canonically homeomorphic spaces. The uniqueness of $\mathfrak f$, which the text uses to make the identifications consistent, is replaced by the uniqueness of $|T\mathfrak f|$, which is what consistency of the identifications needs. The projection $\tau_Z$ is built the same way, as $|\tau_{X_0}|$ with a naturality square for every structure.

### XVI.9 Theorem 16.2.4 (2017: Theorem 16.1), p. 719: the tangent functor

**Statement** (narrower). *On PS* ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PSCat.tangentFunctor⟧: $(X, \alpha) \mapsto (TX, T\alpha)$ and $(f, \mathfrak f) \mapsto (Tf, T\mathfrak f)$ is a functor from PS to PS one universe up. *On sc-smooth maps* ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.theorem_16_2_4⟧: $T\hat f = [(Tf, T\mathfrak f)]$ is well defined for every sc-smooth map between any polyfolds, with $Tf \circ T\alpha = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f|$, and $T1 = 1$. *On effective polyfolds* ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · theorem_16_2_4_eff⟧: $T$ is a functor on the category of effective polyfolds ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · EffPolyfold.tangentFunctor⟧. *Narrower* because there is no category of all polyfolds as we read Definition 16.1.10 (§XVI.4); on effective polyfolds, where the composite is defined, it is the text's statement with no added hypothesis.

**Proof on PS.** *Step 1.* A generalized map alone determines a morphism of PS one universe up ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PSHom.ofGen'⟧, compatibly with composition ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PSHom.ofGen'_comp⟧: its continuous map is forced by Step 1 of PS (§XVI.4). *Step 2.* $T(X, \alpha)$ is the structure $(TX, T\alpha)$ on $|TX|$ itself, with $T\alpha$ the identity of $|TX|$ for the structure taken as its own base ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldStructure.tangentSelf⟧, and the functor laws are those of $T$ on the localization (§XVI.7). *Step 3.* Isomorphisms over the identity go to isomorphisms over the identity ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.tangent_isIdIso⟧, by (16.5).

**Proof on sc-smooth maps.** *Step 1, representatives* ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.tangent⟧: for a representative $(f, \mathfrak f) : (X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$, $(Tf, T\mathfrak f) : (TX, T\alpha) \to (TY, T\beta)$ with $Tf = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f| \circ (T\alpha)^{-1}$. *Step 2, well defined* ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.tangent_equiv⟧: a square $(f', \mathfrak f') \circ (h, \mathrm{Id}) = (k, \mathrm{Id}) \circ (f, \mathfrak f)$ goes under $T$ to a square with the isomorphisms over the identity $(Th, \mathrm{Id})$ and $(Tk, \mathrm{Id})$, by Step 3 on PS. No effectiveness is used, because Definition 16.1.6 carries $h$ and $k$ as data. *Step 3, the class* ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent⟧ with its map determined by $Tf \circ T\alpha = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f|$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_mk⟧. *Step 4.* $T1 = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_id⟧, since $T[1_X] = [1_{TX}]$; and the tangent of a composite of representatives is the composite of the tangents ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_mk_comp⟧. *Step 5, composites of classes.* For an effective middle polyfold $d$ whose tangent is effective, $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_comp⟧: the composite on the right is defined only if $Td$ is effective, which the next proof supplies.

**The tangent of an effective ep-groupoid with (ZHOU) is effective** ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_tangentEpGroupoid⟧. *Statement:* for $X$ effective with (ZHOU), the tangent ep-groupoid $TX$ (Theorem 8.1.1) is effective (Definition 7.2.1). This is not printed; the text uses it implicitly when it calls $T$ a functor on the polyfold category.

*Proof.* Suppose an isotropy element $g$ of $TX$ at a tangent vector $a$, $g \ne 1$, acts trivially near $a$: there is an open $W \ni a$ in the object space of $TX$ on which the local diffeomorphism of $g$ is the identity.

*Step 1, the base morphism is not a unit.* Let $\varphi \in X$ be the base morphism of $g$ (the morphism of $X$ under the tangent morphism $g$, which acts on $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ by $T\varphi$). If $\varphi$ were a unit, then $g$ would be a unit ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.tangent_isotropy_eq_one⟧, since a tangent morphism over a unit with the same source and target is the unit. So $\varphi \ne 1$.

*Step 2, separation.* The morphism space is Hausdorff, so choose disjoint open sets $A \ni \varphi$ and $B \ni 1_{s(\varphi)}$.

*Step 3, a sheet of the source map.* $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism at $\varphi$; let $\sigma$ be its local inverse on a neighbourhood $V$ of $s(\varphi)$, with $\sigma(s(\varphi)) = \varphi$, and $T\sigma$ its tangent.

*Step 4, an open set of tangent vectors.* Let $W_0 \subseteq W$ be the tangent vectors whose base morphism lies in $A$, in the sheet, and has source whose unit lies in $B$, and let $O$ be the set of tangent vectors $b$ over $V$ with $T\sigma(b) \in W_0$. $O$ is open in $TX$ and contains $a$.

*Step 5, a smooth point.* $O$ is open in $TX$, whose topology is that of level $1$; smooth points are dense, so pick $b \in O$ over a smooth point. Its base point $x = \tau(b)$ lies in $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.levelVal_tangentProj_mem_smoothSet⟧, because the projection $TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth and $(X^1)_\infty = X_\infty$.

*Step 6, the morphism at $x$.* Put $\psi = \sigma(x)$, a morphism of $X$ from $x$, lying in $A$. By the choice of $W_0$, the tangent morphism $T\psi$ acts as the identity on an open set of $T_xX$ around $b$, through the triviality of $g$'s action on $W$ transported along the sheet.

*Step 7, linearity.* $T\psi : T_xX \to T_{t(\psi)}X$ is linear and equals the identity on an open subset of the fibre, so $T\psi = \mathrm{id}$ on the whole fibre and $t(\psi) = x$ ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · linearMap_eq_self_of_eqOn_isOpen⟧.

*Step 8, (ZHOU) and effectiveness.* $\psi \in G_x$ with $T_x\psi = \mathrm{id}$ at the smooth point $x$; (ZHOU) says that then $\psi$ acts as the identity near $x$, and effectiveness of $X$ gives $\psi = 1_x$. But $\psi \in A$ and $1_x \in B$, with $A \cap B = \emptyset$. This contradiction shows $g = 1$.

*Why both hypotheses.* Effectiveness of $X$ is a statement at level $0$, while open sets of $TX$ see only level $1$; an isotropy element acting trivially near a tangent vector must first be moved to a smooth point, where (ZHOU) converts the triviality of the linearized action into triviality near the point. **For polyfolds** ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · PolyfoldClass.IsEffective.tangent⟧: the tangent of an effective polyfold is effective, since (ZHOU) is part of every polyfold structure (Definition 16.1.1 (2)); no hypothesis is added.

**Proof on effective polyfolds.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · EffPolyfold.tangent⟧: an effective polyfold has an effective tangent, an object of the category. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/TangentEffective · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_comp_of_isEffective⟧: $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ whenever the middle polyfold is effective, from Step 5 of the previous proof with the effectiveness of $Td$ supplied by the theorem above. *Step 3*: with $T1 = 1$ this is a functor, and with $Tf \circ T\alpha = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f|$ it is Theorem 16.2.4.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text states Theorem 16.2.4 for the polyfold category of Definition 16.1.11 and treats functoriality as evident from the functoriality of $T$ on generalized maps. The formalization proves it at three levels: on PS, where it is the functoriality on the localization; on sc-smooth maps of all polyfolds, where well-definedness needs only that Definition 16.1.6 carries its isomorphisms as data; and on the category of effective polyfolds, where composites are defined. At the third level a statement the text does not print is needed, that the tangent of an effective polyfold is effective, since otherwise the tangent of a morphism of effective polyfolds would not be a morphism of the category. Its proof is new, and it uses (ZHOU), part of every polyfold structure, in an essential way.

### XVI.10 The remark before Definition 16.2.5, Definition 16.2.5 and Theorem 16.2.6 (2017: Definition 16.15, Theorem 16.2), pp. 720–721: sc-differential forms

**Statement.** *The remark* (p. 720, same) ⟦Chapter16/FormsIndependence · EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush_eq_of_orbitMap_eq_or⟧: for generalized isomorphisms $h, h' : X \to Y$ with $|h| = |h'|$, $h_* = h'_*$ on $\Omega^k_{ep,\infty}$ if $X$ or $Y$ has (LR); likewise for pull-backs ⟦Chapter16/FormsIndependence · EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPullback_eq_of_orbitMap_eq_or⟧. *Definition 16.2.5* (p. 720, restated) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm⟧: $\Omega^k_{sc}(Z, c)$ is the set of classes of pairs $(\omega, (X, \alpha))$. *Theorem 16.2.6* (p. 721, same), in two parts: the complex ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.theorem_16_2_6_complex⟧ and the pull-back by sc-smooth maps ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.theorem_16_2_6_pullback⟧.

**Proof of the remark.** It is Proposition 11.2.9 (Part XI) ⟦Chapter11/OrbitForms · formsPush_eq_of_orbitMap_eq⟧, which takes (LR) on the source; with (LR) on the target, Proposition 10.3.16 moves it to the source, being invariant under equivalences. For polyfold structures (ZHOU) gives (LR) (§XVI.1), so $h_*\omega$ depends only on $\alpha$ and $\beta$, since $|h| = \beta^{-1} \circ \alpha$. The mechanism is that of §XVI.7: generalized isomorphisms with one orbit map differ by an automorphism with trivial orbit map, which acts trivially on forms by Proposition 10.1.10. Pull-back by a generalized isomorphism is push-forward by its inverse ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush_eq_formsPullback⟧.

**Proof of Definition 16.2.5.** *Step 1, representatives* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.FormRep⟧: pairs $(\omega, (X, \alpha))$ with $(X, \alpha) \in c$ and $\omega \in \Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X)$. *Step 2, the relation* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.FormRep.Rel⟧: $(\omega, (X, \alpha)) \sim (\omega', (Y, \beta))$ if $\omega' = h_*\omega$ for some, equivalently (by the remark) every, generalized isomorphism $h$ with $\beta \circ |h| = \alpha$. *Step 3, an equivalence relation*: reflexive by $1_* = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.FormRep.Rel.refl⟧ (Theorem 11.2.1 (3), Part XI), symmetric by $(h^{-1})_* = (h_*)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.FormRep.Rel.symm⟧, transitive by $(h' \circ h)_* = h'_* \circ h_*$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · EPLocalization.EPLoc.formsPush_comp⟧, with composites and identities of generalized isomorphisms again generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_id⟧. *Step 4, classes* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk⟧, injective on each structure ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk_injective⟧, and related through push-forward ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk_eq_mk_formsPush⟧. *Step 5, the representative on a structure* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructure⟧: for $(X, \alpha) \in c$ and a class $\tau$, the unique $\omega$ with $\tau = [(\omega, (X, \alpha))]$, obtained by pushing any representative along a realizing isomorphism ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.exists_iso⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.formsPush_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.repOn⟧. This gives a bijection $\Omega^k_{sc}(Z, c) \cong \Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.equivStructure⟧, and representatives on related structures are related by pull-back ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructure_eq_formsPullback⟧. *Step 6, the vector space structure.* It is transported from the chosen structure ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.outₗ⟧ and satisfies the text's formulas for every representative: $[(\omega, q)] + [(\omega', q)] = [(\omega + \omega', q)]$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk_add⟧ and $r[(\omega, q)] = [(r\omega, q)]$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk_smul⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.mk_add_smul⟧, because $h_*$ is linear. So each bijection of Step 5 is linear ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructureₗ⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.equivStructureₗ⟧. *Restated* because the text's representatives are written $(\omega, (X, \alpha))$ informally and the vector space operations on classes are defined by these formulas; the formalization defines them on one structure and proves the formulas.

**Proof of Theorem 16.2.6, the complex.** *Step 1, $d$ on representatives* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.dRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.dFun⟧: $d[(\omega, (X, \alpha))] = [(d\omega, (X, \alpha))]$. *Step 2, well defined* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.formsPush_d⟧: $h_*$ commutes with $d$ for a generalized isomorphism (Theorem 11.2.1, Part XI), so related representatives have related differentials. *Step 3, the operator* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.d⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.d_apply⟧ is linear, and the formula holds for every $(X, \alpha) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.d_mk⟧. *Step 4, $d \circ d = 0$* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.d_d⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldForms · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.d_comp_d⟧, from $d \circ d = 0$ on $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}(X)$ (Part XI). *Step 5.* $\omega \mapsto [(\omega, (X, \alpha))]$ is a linear isomorphism of complexes.

**Proof of Theorem 16.2.6, the pull-back.** *Statement:* an sc-smooth map $\hat f : (Z, c) \to (W, d)$ pulls back forms by $\hat f^*[(\omega', (Y, \beta))] = [(\mathfrak f^*\omega', (X, \alpha))]$ for a representative $(f, \mathfrak f) : (X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$ ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_mk⟧, linearly, commuting with $d$, functorially. *Step 1, on a representative* ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.pullback⟧: $\omega' \mapsto \mathfrak f^*\omega'$ through the representatives on the structures of the representative (Step 5 above), a linear map. *Step 2, independence of the representative* ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.pullback_eq_of_equiv⟧, with no effectiveness: for related representatives with the square $\mathfrak f' \circ h = k \circ \mathfrak f$, the key identity is $\mathfrak f = k^{-1} \circ \mathfrak f' \circ h$, and pull-back is contravariantly functorial on the localization (Theorem 11.2.1), so $\mathfrak f^* = h^* \circ \mathfrak f'^* \circ (k^{-1})^*$; but forms on a class are identified exactly along $h$ and $k$ (Definition 16.2.5), whichever $k$ the square uses. So the non-uniqueness of §XVI.4 does not reach pull-backs. *Step 3, $d$* ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.d_comp_pullback⟧: $d \circ \hat f^* = \hat f^* \circ d$, because generalized maps commute with $d$ (Theorem 11.2.1 (2), Part XI). *Step 4, functoriality.* $1^* = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_id⟧; $(\hat g \circ \hat f)^* = \hat f^* \circ \hat g^*$ on representatives ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_mk_comp⟧, and on classes for an effective middle polyfold, where the composite is defined ⟦Chapter16/FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_comp⟧. With the complex this is Theorem 16.2.6 in full.

**Not formalized from §16.2.** Remark 16.2.7 (§XVI.28).

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The remark before Definition 16.2.5 cites Proposition 11.2.9; the formalization states it with (LR) on either side, since in a polyfold both ep-groupoids have (LR) and the comparison is sometimes made from the target. Definition 16.2.5 is restated: the text defines the vector space operations on classes by the formulas $[(\omega, q)] + [(\omega', q)] = [(\omega + \omega', q)]$ and $r[(\omega, q)] = [(r\omega, q)]$, which presupposes that any two classes have representatives on a common structure and that the result does not depend on it; the formalization transports the structure from one structure of $c$ and proves the formulas for all. The pull-back half of Theorem 16.2.6 is printed with a one-line proof; the formalization isolates the one point that needs care, independence of the representative of $\hat f$, and shows it uses no effectiveness.

### XVI.11 Definitions 16.3.1, 16.3.3–16.3.5 and Lemma 16.3.2 (2017: Definitions 16.16–16.19), pp. 721–723: strong polyfold bundles

**Statement.** *Definition 16.3.1* (p. 721, same) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure⟧: a strong polyfold bundle structure for a continuous surjection $p : Y \to Z$ is a strong bundle $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid $X$ with (ZHOU), paracompact $|X|$ and the local regularity property of Definition 8.4.2, together with homeomorphisms $\Gamma : |W| \to Y$ and $\gamma : |X| \to Z$ with $p \circ \Gamma = \gamma \circ |P|$. *Lemma 16.3.2* (p. 722, same; new in 2021) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.lemma_16_3_2⟧: $Y$ and $Z$ are metrizable. *Definition 16.3.3* (p. 722, same) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv⟧: two structures are equivalent if a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $F$ covering a generalized isomorphism $f$ has $\gamma' \circ |f| = \gamma$ and $\Gamma' \circ |F| = \Gamma$. *The uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3* (p. 723, does not hold as we read it; holds for an effective target base) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Uniqueness_16_3_3⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.not_uniqueness_16_3_3⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.uniqueness_16_3_3_of_isEffective⟧. *The induced polyfold* (p. 723, same) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.toPolyfoldStructure⟧. *Definition 16.3.4* (p. 723, same) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle⟧: a strong polyfold bundle is $p$ with an equivalence class $\bar c$ of structures. *Definition 16.3.5* (p. 723, (1) same, (2)–(3) restated) ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsTame⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsWeaklyFaceStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsFaceStructured⟧: tame, weakly face-structured, face-structured.

**Proof of Definition 16.3.1's consequences.** *Step 1, $p$ is determined* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_eq⟧: $p = \gamma \circ |P| \circ \Gamma^{-1}$, and in orbit form $p(\Gamma|w|) = \gamma(|P(w)|)$ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_Γ⟧. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.continuous_p⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.surjective_p⟧: $p$ is continuous, as $|P|$ is (Part VIII), and surjective, as $P$ is surjective on objects. The text assumes both; they follow.

**Proof of Lemma 16.3.2.** *$Z$*: $|X|$ is paracompact, and Theorem 7.3.1 with Chapter 2's metrization theorem make it metrizable (§XVI.1); $\gamma$ is a homeomorphism. *$Y$*: Proposition 8.4.1 (Part VIII) shows that $|W|$ is paracompact and metrizable for a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space and the local regularity property, through the metrizability of orbit spaces ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.lemma_16_3_2⟧; $\Gamma$ is a homeomorphism.

**Proof that Definition 16.3.3 is an equivalence relation.** *Step 1, orbit maps of generalized strong bundle maps compose.* This is the strong bundle form of Proposition 10.3.11. On a diagram of strong bundle equivalences the orbit maps compose ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_comp'⟧, the proof running on the weak fibre product $W'' \times_{W'} V''$ of the middle bundles through the action $\mu$ of Chapter 10, and the identity diagram has the identity orbit map ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_id'⟧. So for generalized strong bundle maps ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_id⟧, also for inverses ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_inv_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_comp_inv⟧, and for the base maps ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.base_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.baseOrbitMap_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.baseOrbitMap_comp⟧. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.trans⟧: as in §XVI.1, by the identity, inverses and composites, with Step 1 for the two conditions. The quotient ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.setoid⟧ is the type of strong polyfold bundles for $p$. *Step 3, the base condition is redundant* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Γ_base⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.equiv_iff_exists_Γ⟧: $\Gamma' \circ |F| = \Gamma$ implies $\gamma' \circ |f| = \gamma$, because $\gamma \circ |P| = p \circ \Gamma = p \circ \Gamma' \circ |F| = \gamma' \circ |P'| \circ |F| = \gamma' \circ |f| \circ |P|$ and $|P|$ is surjective.

**Proof that the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3 does not hold as we read it.** The text says that for equivalent structures $f$ and $F$ are uniquely determined, by $|f| = \gamma'^{-1} \circ \gamma$, (ZHOU), Theorem 10.3.19 and Proposition 10.4.7. The claim in Lean: any two generalized strong bundle isomorphisms satisfying both conditions agree, on the bases and on the bundles. *Step 1, the example* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3Structure⟧: the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, with $\mathbb Z/3$ acting trivially on base and fibres, and $\Gamma = \gamma = \mathrm{id}$ after the identifications of §XVI.1. It satisfies (ZHOU), has a paracompact orbit space and the local regularity property ⟦Chapter10/LocalizationLRCounterexample · LocalizationLRCounterexample.isLR_z3EpBundle⟧, so it is a strong polyfold bundle structure in the exact sense of Definition 16.3.1; its class is a strong polyfold bundle ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3Bundle⟧. *Step 2, two isomorphisms.* The generalized strong bundle isomorphisms $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ of Remark 10.5.5 (Part X) induce the identity on both orbit spaces ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3_orbitMap_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3_baseOrbitMap_id⟧, so both satisfy the conditions of Definition 16.3.3. *Step 3, they differ, already on the bases* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.uniqueness_16_3_3_counterexample⟧: the base maps are the pair of §XVI.2. The base is not effective ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleUniqueness · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.not_isEffective_z3Structure⟧. This is the bundle form of §XVI.2.

**Proof of the effective form.** For an effective target base, $f$ is unique by Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target (§XVI.2), and $F$ is then unique by Theorem 10.5.7 for an effective base (Part X), which determines a generalized strong bundle isomorphism by its orbit map and base. Nothing later in §16.3 uses the uniqueness: the relations of §§16.3, 16.5 and 16.6 are proved independent of the isomorphisms (decision (5)).

**Proof of the induced polyfold and Definition 16.3.4.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.toPolyfoldStructure⟧: $(X, \gamma)$ is a polyfold structure on $Z$, its two conditions being part of Definition 16.3.1. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.toPolyfoldStructure_equiv⟧: equivalent bundle structures give equivalent polyfold structures, through the base $f$ of $F$ (Remark 10.5.3). *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.polyfold⟧: a strong polyfold bundle has a polyfold $(Z, c)$, the class of the bases of its structures.

**Proof of Definition 16.3.5.** (1) A strong polyfold bundle is tame if $(Z, c)$ is (Definition 16.1.20), equivalently if the base of every structure is tame ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isTame_iff⟧, by Lemma 16.1.19 (§XVI.5). (2), (3): through representatives ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.IsWeaklyFaceStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.IsFaceStructured⟧, since Definition 16.1.21 (faces of a polyfold) is not formalized. Face structure holds for one representative iff for all ⟦Chapter16/StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.isFaceStructured_iff⟧, by Remark 11.1.7 (Part XI); for weak face structure the invariance under generalized isomorphisms is not formalized, and "some representative" is the reading (§XVI.28).

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text lists the continuity and surjectivity of $p$ among the data; the formalization derives them from the structure. In Definition 16.3.3 the text imposes both $\gamma' \circ |f| = \gamma$ and $\Gamma' \circ |F| = \Gamma$; the second implies the first, which the formalization proves and then uses to state every class-level relation of §§16.3, 16.5, 16.6 through $\Gamma$ alone. For the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3, the text's argument (Theorem 10.3.19 for $f$, then Proposition 10.4.7 for $F$) is tested step by step, as in §XVI.2; the first step does not hold as we read it on the $\mathbb Z/3$ bundle, and the effective form uses Theorem 10.5.7 in place of the text's second step. Definition 16.3.5 (2), (3) are restated through representatives, because the faces of a polyfold (Definition 16.1.21) are not formalized.

### XVI.12 Definitions 16.3.6–16.3.8 (2017: Definitions 16.20–16.22), pp. 724–726: the category $\mathcal{SPBS}$ and strong polyfold bundle maps

**Statement** (same). *Definition 16.3.6* (p. 724) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS⟧: the category $\mathcal{SPBS}$ of strong polyfold bundle structures. A morphism ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom⟧ from $(W, \Gamma, \gamma)$ over $p$ to $(W', \Gamma', \gamma')$ over $p'$ is $(A, a, \mathfrak A, \mathfrak a)$ with continuous $A : Y \to Y'$, $a : Z \to Z'$, a generalized strong bundle map $\mathfrak A$ covering $\mathfrak a$, $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = A \circ \Gamma$ and $\gamma' \circ |\mathfrak a| = a \circ \gamma$. *Definition 16.3.7* (p. 725) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv⟧: two morphisms are equivalent if they differ by invertible morphisms of the special form $(\mathfrak H, \mathrm{Id}_Y)$ on both sides. *Definition 16.3.8* (p. 726) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap⟧: an sc-smooth strong polyfold bundle map is a class of morphisms between structures of $\bar c$ and $\bar c'$.

**Proof of Definition 16.3.6.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.p_comm⟧: $p' \circ A = a \circ p$ follows, since $p' \circ A \circ \Gamma = p' \circ \Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \gamma' \circ |P'| \circ |\mathfrak A| = \gamma' \circ |\mathfrak a| \circ |P| = a \circ \gamma \circ |P| = a \circ p \circ \Gamma$, and $\Gamma$ is surjective. The text lists it as a condition. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.category⟧: identities and componentwise composition, with Step 1 of §XVI.11 for the orbit maps; the laws hold componentwise. A constructor from the bundle data alone ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.mk'⟧ derives the base conditions. *Step 3, invertibility* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.IsInvertible⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.isIso_iff_isInvertible⟧: a morphism is invertible in the text's sense ($A$, $a$ homeomorphisms, $\mathfrak A$ a generalized strong bundle isomorphism) iff it is an isomorphism of the category, the inverse being $(A^{-1}, a^{-1}, \mathfrak A^{-1}, \mathfrak a^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.inv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.comp_inv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.inv_comp⟧. *Step 4, the text before Definition 16.3.7* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.exists_isInvertible_iff_equiv⟧: $\bar c$ consists of the structures related to a given one by an invertible morphism $(\mathfrak A, \mathrm{Id}_Y)$, and for such a morphism $A = \mathrm{id}$ forces $a = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.f_eq_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.inv_F_eq_id⟧, by Step 1 and the surjectivity of $p$.

**Proof of Definitions 16.3.7 and 16.3.8.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.F_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.f_eq⟧: equivalent morphisms have $A_1 = A_0$ and $a_1 = a_0$, comparing the continuous components of the square. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.trans⟧: an equivalence relation, by the identity, inverses and pasting squares, as for Definition 16.1.6. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorRep.Rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.MorRep.setoid⟧: representatives are morphisms between structures of $\bar c$ and $\bar c'$, and the maps are the quotient. *Step 4, the continuous maps* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.baseFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.continuous_toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.p_comm⟧: $A$ and $a$ are well defined on classes by Step 1, continuous, and commute with the projections. *Step 5* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.toFun_id⟧: the identity map. The composition of strong polyfold bundle maps on classes would meet the question of §XVI.4; the text does not define it, and it is not formalized.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text defines $\mathcal{SPBS}$, its equivalence of morphisms and the strong polyfold bundle maps without verifying the category laws or the relation; the formalization proves them, and derives the commutation $p' \circ A = a \circ p$ and the base condition $\gamma' \circ |\mathfrak a| = a \circ \gamma$ from the bundle conditions. The text's remark before Definition 16.3.7, that $\bar c$ consists of the structures related by invertible morphisms over the identity of $Y$, is proved as an equivalence with Definition 16.3.3. The text does not define the composition of strong polyfold bundle maps on classes; by the mechanism of §XVI.4 it would need an effective middle base, and it is not formalized.

### XVI.13 Definition 16.3.9 (2017: Definition 16.23), Proposition 16.3.10, Remark 16.3.11, p. 726: auxiliary norms

**Statement.** *Definition 16.3.9* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm⟧: a function $n : Y \to \mathbb R$ is an auxiliary norm for $\bar c$ if, for every structure of $\bar c$, the function $N(e) = n(\Gamma(|e|))$ on $W_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf⟧ is an auxiliary norm of $W$ in the sense of Definition 12.2.1 ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.IsAuxNormFor⟧. The text says one structure suffices ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.definition_16_3_9⟧. *(16.7)* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf_pull⟧: $N = [D]^*N'$ for related structures. *Proposition 16.3.10* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_10⟧: auxiliary norms exist. *Remark 16.3.11* (nothing to formalize): prose. *Restated* because the text's $n$ is a function on $Y_{0,1}$, the image of the level-$(0,1)$ part; the formalization takes a function on $Y$ whose values on $Y_{0,1}$ matter, so that no subtype of $Y$ needs a topology.

**Background: auxiliary norms on a strong bundle.** Over an ep-groupoid, an auxiliary norm of a strong bundle $P : W \to X$ (Definition 12.2.1, Part XII) is a continuous function $N : W_{0,1} \to [0, \infty)$ on the bi-level $(0,1)$ part, invariant under the action of the morphisms, whose restriction to every fibre is a complete norm on the level-$1$ fibre, and which has the compactness property: if $P(h_k) \to x$ and $N(h_k) \to 0$, then $h_k \to 0_x$ in $W[1]$. Invariance is what lets $N$ descend to $|W[1]|$ and hence, through $\Gamma$, to a function on $Y_{0,1}$; the compactness property is what Proposition 16.3.16 (1) reads on $Y$. Auxiliary norms are the device by which Chapter 12 makes sense of "small" perturbations of an sc-Fredholm section: a multisection is controlled if its pointwise norm $N(\Lambda)$ is at most $1$ (§XVI.26), and properness (Definition 12.4.1) is a compactness statement for sublevel sets of $N \circ F$. The polyfold definitions of §16.3 are these notions moved to $Y$ along the homeomorphisms $\Gamma$; the only substantive points are that the move does not depend on the structure, and that the reflexive variants of §XVI.14, whose definitions involve sequences and weak limits rather than pointwise values, move as well.

**The set $Y_{0,1}$.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Y01⟧: for a structure, $Y_{0,1} = \Gamma(|W_{0,1}|)$, with the map $|W[1]| \to Y$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.oneToY⟧. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Y01_subset_of_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Y01_eq_of_equiv⟧: it does not depend on the structure, since generalized strong bundle isomorphisms preserve the bi-level $(0,1)$ (Chapter 10) and commute with $\Gamma$. So $Y_{0,1}$ is defined for the bundle ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.Y01⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.Y01_eq⟧. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.oneToY_pull⟧: the maps $|W[1]| \to Y$ of related structures are compatible with the orbit map of the realizing isomorphism.

**Proof of Definition 16.3.9, "one structure suffices".** *Step 1, invariance of $N$* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isOneInvariant_normOf⟧: $N = n \circ \Gamma \circ \pi$ is invariant under the morphisms of $W$, since $\pi$ is. *Step 2, (16.7).* For related structures through $F$, $N = N' \circ F$ on orbits, from $\Gamma' \circ |F| = \Gamma$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf_pull⟧. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isAuxNormFor_of_equiv⟧: auxiliary norms pull back along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, Proposition 11.5.1 (Part XI). So if $N'$ is an auxiliary norm, so is $N$. *Step 4.* The definition quantifies over all structures; Step 3 gives the equivalence with one. *Continuity and nonnegativity.* The continuity of $n$ on $Y_{0,1}$ is read in the topology of $|W[1]|$ carried by $\Gamma$, where it is the continuity of the descended function ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOrbit⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.continuous_normOrbit⟧, and nonnegativity ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm.nonneg⟧ follows from that of $N$.

**Proof of Proposition 16.3.10.** *Step 1.* Take a structure of $\bar c$. Theorem 12.2.2 (Part XII) gives an auxiliary norm $N$ of $W$, using the paracompactness of $|X|$, which is part of Definition 16.3.1. *Step 2, descend* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.descend⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf_descend⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.descend_oneToY⟧: $N$ is invariant, so $n(\Gamma|e|) = N(e)$ defines $n$ on $Y_{0,1}$, extended by $0$, and $N$ is recovered as $n \circ \Gamma \circ \pi$. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isAuxNorm_descend⟧: $n$ is an auxiliary norm by Definition 16.3.9 for one structure.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text writes $n : Y_{0,1} \to [0, \infty)$; the formalization takes $n : Y \to \mathbb R$, with only its values on $Y_{0,1}$ entering the definition. This avoids giving the subset $Y_{0,1}$ its own topology: continuity is read in the topology of $|W[1]|$ carried by $\Gamma$, which is the topology the text intends (the bi-level $(0,1)$ topology). The text's reason that one structure suffices is (16.7); the formalization makes it Proposition 11.5.1 applied to a realizing isomorphism, (16.7) being the identity $N = [D]^*N'$ that the proposition uses. Proposition 16.3.10 is proved as printed, by Theorem 12.2.2 in a representative, with the paracompactness that Definition 16.3.1 now includes.

### XVI.14 Definitions 16.3.12–16.3.14 (2017: Definitions 16.24–16.26), p. 727: reflexive $1$-fibres, mixed convergence, reflexive auxiliary norms, and their independence of the model

**Statement.** *Definitions 16.3.12, 16.3.13, 16.3.14* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.HasReflexiveFibers⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MixedTendsto⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm⟧: $\bar c$ has reflexive $1$-fibres if some model of $\bar c$ has them (Definition 12.2.6, with compatible charts whose fibre $F_1$ is reflexive); $y_k \to y$ in the mixed sense if this holds in some model (Definition 12.2.8); $n$ is a reflexive auxiliary norm if it is represented in some model by a reflexive auxiliary norm (Definition 12.2.10). Mixed convergence in a given model ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MixedTendstoIn⟧. *The parenthetical of Definition 16.3.12* (same) ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · StrongPolyfoldBundle.hasReflexiveFibers_iff_forall⟧: then every model has reflexive $1$-fibres. *The model does not matter for mixed convergence* (same; the remark before Theorem 16.3.17) ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mixedTendsto_iff_forall⟧, *nor for reflexive auxiliary norms* (same) ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_iff_forall⟧.

**Proof, the pull direction for reflexive fibres.** *Step 1, charts* ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.exists_reflexive_chart⟧. Let $\Phi : W|U \to W'|U'$ be a local strong bundle isomorphism over $\phi$, and $x \in U$. A compatible chart of $W'$ at $\phi(x)$ whose fibre $F_1$ is reflexive gives one of $W$ at $x$: restrict the chart to $U'$, then transport it along $\Phi^{-1}$; the transported chart is compatible with the strong bundle structure of $W$ because $\Phi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism, and its fibre model is the same Banach space, so it is reflexive. *Step 2, bundles* ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePull · StrongBundle.hasReflexiveFibers_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn⟧: if the objects of $X$ are covered by the domains of such isomorphisms, reflexive $1$-fibres of $W'$ give reflexive $1$-fibres of $W$. *Step 3, equivalences* ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePull · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.hasReflexiveFibers_of⟧: for a strong bundle equivalence $W \to W'$ (Definition 10.4.1), the local isomorphisms covering the objects are part (2) of the definition, so reflexive $1$-fibres of $W'$ give those of $W$, with no hypothesis added.

**Proof, the push direction for reflexive fibres** ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.hasReflexiveFibers_push⟧. For a strong bundle equivalence $L : W \to W'$ over $\phi$ and reflexive $1$-fibres of $W$: *Step 1.* For $x' \in X'$ pick $x$ and a morphism $\sigma : \phi(x) \to x'$ of $X'$, which exist because $\phi$ is essentially surjective. *Step 2.* $L$ is a local strong bundle isomorphism near $x$; its inverse $L_0^{-1}$ and Step 1 of the pull direction give a reflexive chart of $W'$ at $\phi(x)$. *Step 3.* The action $\mu$ of $W'$ along $\sigma$ is a local strong bundle isomorphism from a neighbourhood of $\phi(x)$ to one of $x'$ (Chapter 10, the morphism form of the local isomorphisms of a strong bundle); Step 1 of the pull direction for its inverse moves the reflexive chart to $x'$. *Step 4, along generalized isomorphisms* ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.hasReflexiveFibers_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · SBLocalization.SDiagram.hasReflexiveFibers_of⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.hasReflexiveFibers_iff⟧: with both directions, reflexivity passes along the two legs of a diagram. *Step 5, structures and the class* ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.hasReflexiveFibers_of_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ReflexivePush · StrongPolyfoldBundle.HasReflexiveFibers.of_mem⟧: equivalent structures have reflexive $1$-fibres together, so "some model" and "every model" agree, which is the parenthetical.

**Proof for mixed convergence.** *Step 1, along a local strong bundle isomorphism* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.mixedTendsto⟧. Let $\Phi$ be a local strong bundle isomorphism into a bundle with reflexive fibres, and $w_k \to w$ in the mixed sense: the base points converge, $(w_k)$ is bounded on level $1$ in local charts, and $w_k \rightharpoonup w$ weakly. In charts, $\Phi$ is linear and bounded on the fibres, uniformly near the base point: Proposition 5.1.3 (Part V) gives the chart form, and a bound of the fibre norms of the image by a multiple of the auxiliary norm holds near the point. Bounded sequences stay bounded, and a bounded linear map preserves weak limits; the fibre seminorms compose ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isFiberSeminorm_comp⟧, and the property is stable under eventual equality ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongBundle.MixedTendsto.congr_eventually⟧. *Step 2, along a diagram* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_mixedTendsto_transfer⟧. For $W \xleftarrow{L} W'' \xrightarrow{L'} W'$ and $w_k \to w$ in $W$: move the sequence along a morphism $\sigma$ into the image of $L$ by the action, which is a local strong bundle isomorphism (with the identity $\mu(1, -)$ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.mk_actOne⟧); lift through a local inverse of $L$ at the base point; push through $L'$, a local isomorphism; Step 1 at each stage. The images represent the orbits of the images of $w_k$ and converge in the mixed sense. *Step 3, structures* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.mixedTendstoIn_of_equiv⟧: for equivalent structures, mixed convergence of $y_k \to y$ read in one gives it in the other, through a sequence patched to the representatives that Step 2 provides, compatible with the maps $|W[1]| \to Y$ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.oneToY_of_oneOrbitMap⟧. *Step 4* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mixedTendsto_iff_forall⟧: the model does not matter.

**Proof for reflexive auxiliary norms.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.SDiagram.isReflexiveAuxNorm_pullNorm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.SDiagram.isReflexiveAuxNorm_pushNorm⟧: along a diagram, a reflexive auxiliary norm pulls back and pushes forward to one. Reflexivity of a norm (Definition 12.2.10) is lower semicontinuity along mixed convergent sequences; by the mixed-convergence transfer of the previous proof, applied in both directions (the push direction through the inverse diagram), it moves with the norm. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isReflexiveAuxNorm_pullNorm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isReflexiveAuxNorm_pushNorm⟧: for generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, through representative diagrams. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isReflexiveAuxNorm_of_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.of_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_iff_forall⟧: for related structures, $N = [D]^*N'$ by (16.7), so $N$ is reflexive iff $N'$ is, and Definition 16.3.14 does not depend on the structure.

*Hypotheses.* The text's standing hypothesis in Definitions 16.3.13 and 16.3.14, reflexive $1$-fibres, is the context; no hypothesis is added. Gap G.166 is closed.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text asserts in a parenthesis that reflexivity of the $1$-fibres does not depend on the model, and before Theorem 16.3.17 that mixed convergence does not either; no proof is given. The formalization proves both, together with the independence of reflexive auxiliary norms, which the text uses implicitly when it speaks of a reflexive auxiliary norm of $\bar c$. The proofs are transports along the two legs of a diagram, with one asymmetry: along the leg that is an equivalence into the target, reflexivity pulls back by transporting a chart, while in the other direction it must also be moved along the morphisms of the target, through the action $\mu$. Mixed convergence additionally needs that a local strong bundle isomorphism is bounded and linear on the fibres, uniformly near a point, which the chart form of Proposition 5.1.3 provides.

### XVI.15 Theorem 16.3.15, Proposition 16.3.16, Theorem 16.3.17 (2017: Theorems 16.3, 16.4, Proposition 16.5), pp. 727–728
