**Statement.** *Theorem 16.3.15* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_15_one⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_15_two⟧: if $\bar c$ has reflexive $1$-fibres, (1) a reflexive auxiliary norm exists, and (2) every auxiliary norm $n$ admits reflexive auxiliary norms $n_1 \le n \le n_2$ on $Y_{0,1}$. *Proposition 16.3.16 (1)* (stronger) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_16_one⟧: if $p(y_k) \to z$ and $n(y_k) \to 0$, then $y_k \to 0_z$; the formal statement is for every auxiliary norm, with the convergence in $|W[1]|$ of a model, and does not use reflexivity. *Proposition 16.3.16 (2)* (same) ⟦Chapter16/MixedTransfer · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_16_two⟧: for a reflexive auxiliary norm $n$ and $y_k \to y$ in the mixed sense, $n(y) \le \liminf n(y_k)$. *Theorem 16.3.17 (1)* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_one⟧: over a tame polyfold, an auxiliary norm of $Y_{0,1}|\partial Z$ extends to an auxiliary norm. *Theorem 16.3.17 (2)* (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp⟧: if the boundary norm is reflexive, the extension can be taken reflexive, with the reflexive local step of Theorem 12.2.13 as an added hypothesis.

**Proof of Theorem 16.3.15.** *Step 1.* By the parenthetical of Definition 16.3.12 (§XVI.14), the chosen structure of $\bar c$ has reflexive $1$-fibres. *Step 2, (1).* Theorem 12.2.11 (Part XII) gives a reflexive auxiliary norm $N$ of $W$; descend it as in Proposition 16.3.10 (§XVI.13). *Step 3, (2).* For an auxiliary norm $n$, its representative $N$ on the structure is an auxiliary norm (Definition 16.3.9), and the sandwich form of Theorem 12.2.11 gives reflexive $N_1 \le N \le N_2$; they descend to $n_1 \le n \le n_2$ on $Y_{0,1}$, because the inequality is pointwise on orbits.

**Proof of Proposition 16.3.16 (1).** *Step 1, lift the sequence.* $p(y_k) \to z$ in $Z$; through the open quotient map $X \to |X| \to Z$, pick $x$ over $z$ and lift a tail of the sequence to objects $x_k \to x$, and $w_k$ over $x_k$ representing $y_k$ (via $\Gamma$ and the surjectivity of $W_{0,1} \to Y_{0,1}$ on orbits). *Step 2, align the representatives.* For each $k$ a morphism moves the chosen representative to one over $x_k$; the value of the action at level $1$ is the representative needed, so $N(w_k) = n(y_k) \to 0$ for $N$ the representative of $n$. *Step 3, the compactness property.* Theorem 12.2.2's auxiliary norm property, which holds for every auxiliary norm (Definition 12.2.1 (2)), states that $x_k \to x$ and $N(w_k) \to 0$ imply $w_k \to 0_x$ in $W[1]$. *Step 4.* Taking orbits and $\Gamma$, $y_k \to 0_z$ in the topology of $|W[1]|$ carried by $\Gamma$. *Stronger* because the text states it for reflexive auxiliary norms and the proof does not use reflexivity.

**Proof of Proposition 16.3.16 (2).** *Step 1, the same-model form* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_16_two_of_mem⟧: if the mixed convergence is read in the model in which $n$ is represented by a reflexive auxiliary norm $N$, the inequality is the reflexivity of $N$ (Definition 12.2.10): $N(w) \le \liminf N(w_k)$ for $w_k \to w$ in the mixed sense, read on representatives and transported by $\Gamma$. *Step 2, the text's form.* The mixed convergence may be given in any model, and $n$ reflexive in any model; by §XVI.14 both notions are independent of the model, so the mixed convergence holds in the model where $n$ is reflexive, and Step 1 applies.

**Proof of Theorem 16.3.17 (1).** *Step 1, the boundary norm* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNormBoundary⟧: an auxiliary norm of $Y_{0,1}|\partial Z$ is read as in Definition 16.3.9 over $\partial X$, in all models. The set $p^{-1}(\partial Z)$ corresponds to $W|\partial X$: $p(\Gamma|e|) \in \partial Z$ iff $P(e) \in \partial X$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mem_boundary_iff⟧, by the computation of $\partial Z$ in a representative (§XVI.5) and $p \circ \Gamma = \gamma \circ |P|$. *Step 2.* Over a tame base, Theorem 12.2.7 (Part XII) extends an auxiliary norm of $W|\partial X$ to one of $W$; apply it in the chosen structure, whose base is tame by Definition 16.3.5 (1). *Step 3.* Descend the extension (§XVI.13); it agrees with $n$ over $\partial Z$ because the representative of $n$ over $\partial X$ was extended.

**Proof of Theorem 16.3.17 (2).** *Step 1, the reading.* "$n$ reflexive over $\partial Z$" is read as reflexive $1$-fibres and a reflexive representative over $\partial X$ in one model. *Step 2.* Theorem 12.2.13 (Part XII), in the form that takes its reflexive local step as a hypothesis ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp⟧, gives a reflexive extension in that model, which descends. *The added hypothesis*, not derived from the text: the reflexive local step, that near every boundary point a reflexive auxiliary norm over the boundary has a reflexive local extension. *Witness* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp_witness⟧: on every bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres, for the boundary norm that is the restriction of a global reflexive auxiliary norm. **This witness covers only a degenerate case**: when $n$ is already the restriction of a global reflexive norm, the local step is satisfied by restricting that norm, and nothing is extended. The non-degenerate case is supplied by Part XII, which proves the reflexive local step over tame bases ⟦Chapter12/ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧; Theorem 16.3.17 assumes a tame base, so the unconditional form is a one-line corollary, not stated as a separate Lean declaration. Tameness is not otherwise used.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text proves Theorem 16.3.15, Proposition 16.3.16 and Theorem 16.3.17 by the corresponding statements of Chapter 12 in a representative, and the formalization follows this. Three differences. Proposition 16.3.16 (1) is proved for every auxiliary norm, since the Chapter 12 property it rests on holds for all of them. Proposition 16.3.16 (2) needs the independence of the model of §XVI.14, which the text takes for granted, to bring the mixed convergence into the model where $n$ is reflexive. Theorem 16.3.17 (2) takes the reflexive local step of Theorem 12.2.13 as a hypothesis, discharged over tame bases by Part XII; since Theorem 16.3.17 is stated over tame polyfolds, the text's statement holds, but the composite is not packaged as one declaration.

### XVI.16 Definitions 16.3.18, 16.3.19 (2017: Definitions 16.27, 16.28), pp. 728–729: sections, the zero of a fibre and the zero section

**Statement.** *The relation before Definition 16.3.18* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel⟧: a representative is $(f, \Gamma, W, F)$ with $f$ a continuous section of $p$ and $F$ an sc-smooth section functor of a structure with $\Gamma \circ |F| = f \circ \gamma$; two are related if $f = f'$ and a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\mathfrak A$ has $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma$ and $\mathfrak A_*F = F'$. *Definition 16.3.18* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection⟧: an sc-smooth section is a class. *Definition 16.3.19* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsScPlus⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusSection⟧: an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section whose functor in one, equivalently every, representative is sc⁺. *The zero of a fibre* (p. 728, same) ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroAt⟧: $0_z = \Gamma(|0_x|)$ for $\gamma(|x|) = z$. *The zero section* (p. 728, same) ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroSection⟧: $z \mapsto 0_z$ is an sc⁺-section.

**Proof that the relation is an equivalence relation and depends only on $f$.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.setoid⟧: by the identity, the inverse with $(\mathfrak A^{-1})_* = (\mathfrak A_*)^{-1}$, and composites with $(\mathfrak B \circ \mathfrak A)_* = \mathfrak B_* \circ \mathfrak A_*$ (Chapter 10). The text states "this defines an equivalence relation". *Step 2, the push-forward condition is redundant* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.pushforward_eq_of_Γ⟧. If $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma$ and $f = f'$, then $\mathfrak A_*F$ and $F'$ are section functors of $W'$ with the same orbit map $\Gamma'^{-1} \circ f \circ \gamma$; a section functor is determined by its values on orbits. Indeed, if $F_1(x)$ and $F_2(x)$ lie in one orbit of $W$, a morphism of $W$ joins them, lying over an isotropy element $g \in G_x$; then $F_2(x) = \mu(g, F_1(x))$, and $\mu(g, F_1(x)) = F_1(x)$ because $F_1$ is a functor, so $F_1(x) = F_2(x)$. The orbit of $(\mathfrak A_*F)(x)$ is computed from $|\mathfrak A|$ and $|F|$, which gives the equality of orbits. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.rel_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.rel_of_f_eq⟧: two representatives are related iff $f = f'$ and their structures are equivalent. So the non-uniqueness of §XVI.11 does not reach sections.

**Proof of Definitions 16.3.18 and 16.3.19.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.p_toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.continuous_toFun⟧: the section $f$ of a class is well defined, continuous, and a section of $p$. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.ext_toFun⟧: by Step 3 above, a section is determined by $f$ (two classes with the same $f$ have representatives with equivalent structures, hence related). *Step 3, sc⁺* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.isScPlus_iff⟧: being sc⁺ is invariant under push-forward by generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, Theorem 10.5.4 (Part X), so one representative is sc⁺ iff every one is. *Restated* because the text phrases Definition 16.3.19 through the continuity of $f$ into $Y_{0,1}$; in a representative that is the continuity of $F$ into $W_{0,1}$, which is what sc⁺ asks.

**Proof of the zero of a fibre.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.zeroAt⟧ ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.zeroAt_eq⟧: for a structure, $0_z = \Gamma(|0_x|)$ for any $x$ with $\gamma(|x|) = z$; it does not depend on $x$, because a morphism $x \to x'$ acts linearly on fibres and sends $0_x$ to $0_{x'}$ ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · SBLocalization.π_fiberZero_eq_of_π_eq⟧, and the action of a morphism moves a non-zero vector to a non-zero vector ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · SBLocalization.μ_ne_fiberZero⟧, so the orbits of zeros are exactly the zeros of orbits ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · SBLocalization.π_eq_fiberZero_iff⟧. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_zeroAt⟧ ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundle.p_zeroAt⟧: $p(0_z) = z$. *Step 3, independence of the structure* ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.zeroAt_eq_of_equiv⟧: diagrams and generalized strong bundle maps send orbits of zeros to orbits of zeros ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · SBLocalization.SDiagram.orbitMap_π_fiberZero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_π_fiberZero⟧, since each leg is linear on fibres. *Step 4* ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Γ_π_eq_zeroAt_iff⟧: $\Gamma(|w|) = 0_z$ iff $w$ is the zero of its fibre and lies over $z$. *Auxiliary norms extended by $0$* ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normY⟧: off $Y_{0,1}$ an auxiliary norm is set to $0$, and $n(\Gamma|w|) = N(w)$ for $w \in W_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter16/FibreZero · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normY_Γ⟧; this is the reading of $n(f(z))$ in Definition 16.6.3 (§XVI.24).

**Proof of the zero section.** *Step 1, continuity* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.continuous_fiberZero_W⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.continuous_zeroAt⟧: the zero section functor of a model is continuous; $z \mapsto 0_z$ is continuous because $x \mapsto \Gamma(|0_x|)$ is, and $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$ is a quotient map ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isQuotientMap_γπ⟧ (§XVI.21). *Step 2, a representative in every model* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroRepOf⟧: the zero functor of a structure, which is an sc-smooth (indeed sc⁺) section functor, with $\Gamma \circ |0| = 0_{(\cdot)} \circ \gamma$ by Step 1 of the zero of a fibre. *Step 3, the class* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroSection⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroSection_eq_mk⟧: all these representatives have the same map $f$, so they give one class (Step 3 of the relation). Its map is $z \mapsto 0_z$ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.toFun_zeroSection⟧. *Step 4* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isScPlus_zeroSection⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroPlusSection⟧: it is an sc⁺-section, since the zero functor is sc⁺. *Step 5* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.rep_F_eq_fiberZero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.eq_zeroSection_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.eq_zeroSection_iff_F⟧: a section is the zero section iff $f(z) = 0_z$ for all $z$, iff its functor is the zero functor in some, equivalently every, representative. *Step 6* ⟦Chapter16/ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.solutionSet_zeroSection⟧: the solution set of the zero section is $Z$. Gap G.167 is closed, and Definitions 16.3.18 and 16.3.19 have a witness on every strong polyfold bundle.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text states the relation on representatives of sections and calls it an equivalence relation; the formalization proves this and the stronger fact that the push-forward condition is implied by the others, so that a section is determined by its map $f$. This is what protects §§16.3–16.6 from the non-uniqueness of §XVI.11: whichever isomorphism realizes an equivalence of structures, it pushes a representative to the unique representative with the same map. The zero of a fibre is defined in the text by a representative; the formalization proves its independence of the representative and of the structure. The zero section is mentioned in the text as an example; the formalization builds it as an element of Definition 16.3.18, with representatives in every model, and characterizes it.

### XVI.17 Definitions 16.4.1 and 16.4.2 (2017: Definitions 16.29, 16.30), pp. 729–730: branched suborbifolds and their properties

**Statement.** *Definition 16.4.1* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold⟧: a branched suborbifold of $(Z, c)$ is a class $\theta = [\Theta, (X, \alpha)]$ of representatives $(\Theta, (X, \alpha))$ with $(X, \alpha) \in c$ and $\Theta$ a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $X$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep⟧, where $(\Theta, (X, \alpha)) \sim (\Theta', (X', \alpha'))$ if a generalized isomorphism $f : X \to X'$ has $\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$ and $f^*\Theta' = \Theta$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel⟧. The function $\theta = |\Theta| \circ \alpha^{-1} : Z \to \mathbb Q^+$ is well defined ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_1_wellDefined⟧. *Definition 16.4.2* (p. 730; (1)–(4) same, (5) same) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsClosed⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsCompact⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsManifoldType⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsOrbifoldType⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsTame⟧: $\theta$ is closed, compact, of manifold type, of orbifold type, or tame, if a representative $\Theta$ is; then every representative is ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_tame⟧. *Restated* for Definition 16.4.1 because the text's class notation is made into explicit pairs and the relation is proved to be an equivalence relation.

**Background: branched ep⁺-subgroupoids.** A branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $X$ (Definition 9.1.1, Part IX) is a functor $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$, with values in the nonnegative rationals and supported in $X_\infty$, that near every point of its support is described by a local branching structure: finitely many finite-dimensional submanifolds $M_1, \ldots, M_k$ of an open set $U$ invariant under the natural representation, with positive rational weights $\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_k$, such that $\Theta(y) = \sum_{i : y \in M_i} \sigma_i$ on $U$. It is of manifold type or of orbifold type when its support carries the corresponding structure of Proposition 9.1.9, and tame if the local branching structures can be chosen tame in the sense of Definition 9.3.6. An orientation $\hat T_\Theta$ (Chapter 11) is a choice of orientations of the tangent spaces of the branches, compatible with the weights. Pull-backs along functors are composition, and push-forwards along equivalences are read on orbits; Chapter 11 extends both to generalized isomorphisms, which is the operation $f^*$ of Definition 16.4.1. So a branched suborbifold of a polyfold is a rational-weighted, locally finitely branched, finite-dimensional subset of $Z$, presented in one structure and moved to any other by $f^*$.

**Pull-backs of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_eq_of_orbitMap⟧: for a generalized isomorphism $f$ and a functorial $\Theta'$, $(f^*\Theta')(x) = \Theta'(y)$ whenever $|f|(|x|) = |y|$. This is the text's $|f^*\Theta'| = |\Theta'| \circ |f|$ (p. 730). The proof goes through a representative diagram $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} X'$: $f^*\Theta'$ is the push-forward along $F$ of $\Phi^*\Theta'$, the pull-back along a functor is composition, and the push-forward along an equivalence of a functorial function is read on orbits. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pull_congr⟧: two generalized isomorphisms with the same orbit map pull back alike, by Step 1. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_id_of_isFunctorial⟧: $1^*\Theta = \Theta$ for functorial $\Theta$.

**Proof of Definition 16.4.1.** *Step 1, an equivalence relation.* Reflexive by Step 3 above ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel.refl⟧. Symmetric ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel.symm⟧: if $f^*\Theta' = \Theta$, then $(f^{-1})^*\Theta = \Theta'$, by Step 1 on orbits, since $|f^{-1}| = |f|^{-1}$. Transitive ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel.trans⟧: $(g \circ f)^* = f^* \circ g^*$ on functorial functions, again by Step 1. The quotient is the type of branched suborbifolds. *Step 2, the function on a representative* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.toFun_eq⟧: $z \mapsto \Theta(x)$ for any $x$ with $\alpha(|x|) = z$, well defined because $\Theta$ is functorial. *Step 3, related representatives give the same function* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.toFun_eq_of_rel⟧: for $z = \alpha(|x|) = \alpha'(|y|)$ with $|y| = |f|(|x|)$, $\Theta(x) = (f^*\Theta')(x) = \Theta'(y)$ by Step 1 of the pull-backs. So $\theta$ is defined on classes, with $\theta(\alpha(|x|)) = \Theta(x)$ for every representative and every $x$ (the well-definedness statement), and $\theta \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.toFun_nonneg⟧. *Step 4, $\theta$ determines the class* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.rel_of_toFun_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.toFun_injective⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.toFun_mk⟧: if two representatives have the same function, any generalized isomorphism $f$ with $\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$ (which exists, both structures being in $c$) has $f^*\Theta' = \Theta$, because both sides are read on orbits and the orbit values agree. So the non-uniqueness of §XVI.2 does not reach branched suborbifolds: the relation is "the functions agree".

**Proof of Definition 16.4.2 (1)–(4) and the dimension.** *Step 1, the pattern* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.HasRepProperty⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.hasRepProperty_iff⟧: a property holds for $\theta$ if it holds for some representative; for a property stable under pull-backs by generalized isomorphisms, some representative has it iff all have it, since any two representatives are related by a generalized isomorphism. *Step 2.* Closed, compact, of manifold type and of orbifold type are stable, by Theorem 11.3.3 (3)–(5) (Part XI), so they hold for every representative iff for one ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_closed⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_compact⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_manifold⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_orbifold⟧. *Step 3.* So is the dimension $n$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsNDimensional⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_nDim⟧, by Theorem 11.3.3 (6); it is used in Theorem 16.4.6.

**Proof of Definition 16.4.2 (5), tameness.** The text says on p. 729 that tameness of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids is preserved by $f_*$ and $f^*$. *Step 1, restriction* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.restrictRep⟧: a tame local branching structure of Definition 9.3.6 at $x$ restricts to any smaller natural representation at $x$. *Step 2, moving* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.move⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.mapU_eq⟧: it moves along an sc-diffeomorphism of open sets $W \to W'$ that intertwines the natural representations, the branches and the tame sets being carried with it, since tameness of a set (Part IV) is invariant under sc-diffeomorphisms. *Step 3, pull-back along an equivalence* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pullbackTheta⟧. For an equivalence $\Phi : X \to X'$, $x \in X$ and a tame $\Theta'$: take a transport chart of Theorem 11.4.1 at $x$ (Part XI), which identifies natural representations at $x$ and $\Phi(x)$ through local sc-diffeomorphisms; take a tame branching structure $D$ of $\Theta'$ at $\Phi(x)$ and a natural representation $R_0$ at $x$ with the properness property (Theorem 7.1.13, Part VII); push $R_0$ to a representation $R'$ inside $D$'s domain; restrict $D$ to $R'$ (Step 1) and move it back along the chart (Step 2). The branches of $\Phi^*\Theta'$ near $x$ are the pulled-back branches, so the moved structure is a tame branching structure of $\Phi^*\Theta'$. *Step 4, push-forward* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pushforwardTheta⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pullbackTheta_iff⟧: the same argument in the other direction, using that $\Phi_*\Phi^*\Theta' = \Theta'$ for functorial $\Theta'$; so $\Phi^*\Theta'$ is tame iff $\Theta'$ is. *Step 5, generalized isomorphisms* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isTameBranched_pullTheta⟧: through the two legs of a diagram. *Step 6* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_tame⟧: tameness is stable, so Step 1 of the pattern applies. Gap G.154 is closed.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text writes $|f^*\Theta'| = |\Theta'| \circ |f|$ and draws from it the well-definedness of $\theta$; the formalization proves the identity through a representative diagram and draws, besides well-definedness, the converse: the function $\theta$ determines the class. For Definition 16.4.2 the text states that the properties hold for one representative iff for all, citing Theorem 11.3.3 for (1)–(4) and the remark on p. 729 for tameness. For (1)–(4) the formalization follows the text. For tameness the remark on p. 729 is stated without proof; the formalization proves it through the transport charts of Theorem 11.4.1, with the restriction and the moving of tame branching structures as the two lemmas that the text's remark presupposes.

### XVI.18 Proposition 16.4.3 (2017: Proposition 16.4), p. 730: the structure on $\operatorname{supp}\theta$

**Statement** (same). For a branched suborbifold $\theta$ of manifold type (orbifold type), $\operatorname{supp}\theta = \{z : \theta(z) > 0\}$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.supp⟧ carries a natural manifold (orbifold) structure. In Lean, in three parts. *The set and the topology* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_supp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_homeomorph⟧: for every representative, $\operatorname{supp}\theta = \alpha(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$, and $\alpha$ restricts to a homeomorphism $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta| \cong \operatorname{supp}\theta$. *The structure on one representative* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_manifold⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_orbifold⟧: Proposition 9.1.9 (1), (2) on $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$. *Naturality* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality⟧: for any two representatives, and any structures induced by Proposition 9.1.9 (1) on their supports, the transition $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta| \to |\operatorname{supp}\Theta'|$ over $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_all⟧. The word "natural" of the text is read as this independence of the representative, the statement being ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_statement⟧. The formal form is stronger than needed in one respect: the induced structures need not be chosen, since any two give the same comparison.

**Proof of the set and the topology.** *Step 1.* $\theta(\alpha(|x|)) = \Theta(x)$ (§XVI.17), so $\theta(z) > 0$ iff $\Theta(x) > 0$ for one, equivalently every, $x$ over $z$; that is $z \in \alpha(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$. *Step 2.* $\alpha$ is a homeomorphism $|X| \to Z$, and $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ carries the subspace topology of $|X|$; so $\alpha$ restricts to a homeomorphism onto $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ with its subspace topology ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_homeomorph_apply⟧.

**Proof of the structure on one representative.** *Manifold type.* With Proposition 9.1.9 (1) (Part IX), $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ carries an M-polyfold structure, finite-dimensional, for which $\operatorname{supp}\Theta \to |\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$, $a \mapsto |a|$, is a local sc-diffeomorphism; it is carried to $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ by the homeomorphism above. *Orbifold type.* With Proposition 9.1.9 (2), $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ is the orbit space of the ep-groupoid that $X$ induces on $\operatorname{supp}\Theta$.

**Proof of naturality.** *Step 1, the transition* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition⟧ ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.β_suppTransition⟧ ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_eq_iff⟧: for two representatives $\Theta$, $\Theta'$ of $\theta$, the homeomorphism $t = \alpha'^{-1} \circ \alpha$ restricted to $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta| \to |\operatorname{supp}\Theta'|$, characterized by $\alpha' \circ t = \alpha$. *Step 2, the cocycle identities* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_self⟧ ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_trans⟧ ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_symm⟧: $t_{aa} = 1$, $t_{a'a''} \circ t_{aa'} = t_{aa''}$, $t_{a'a} = t_{aa'}^{-1}$. *Step 3, the induced structures* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsInducedSuppStructure⟧: a structure on $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ is induced if $a \mapsto |a|$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism from $\operatorname{supp}\Theta$ with its M-polyfold structure (Proposition 9.1.9 (1)). For one representative the transition is the identity, an sc-diffeomorphism between any two induced structures ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturalityStatement · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_self⟧. *Step 4, the transition through a diagram* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_orbitSuppProj⟧. For a generalized isomorphism $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} X'$ between the representatives ($\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$, $f^*\Theta' = \Theta$), the transition sends $|F(b)|$ to $|\Phi(b)|$ for every $b$ in the support of $\Phi^*\Theta'$. *Step 5, sc-smoothness* ⟦Chapter16/SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.isScSmoothOn_suppTransition⟧. The legs $F$ and $\Phi$ restrict to equivalences of the sub-ep-groupoids on the supports (the argument of Proposition 11.1.6, Part XI), which are local sc-diffeomorphisms of the finite-dimensional M-polyfolds $\operatorname{supp}$. Near $|F(b)|$, the transition is the composite $p' \circ \Phi|_{\operatorname{supp}} \circ (F|_{\operatorname{supp}})^{-1} \circ p^{-1}$, with $p$, $p'$ the local sc-diffeomorphisms $a \mapsto |a|$ of the induced structures and $(F|_{\operatorname{supp}})^{-1}$ a local inverse; so it is sc-smooth. Only $\Theta'$ of orbifold type is used, for the sub-ep-groupoid on the support of $\Phi^*\Theta'$; manifold type, the text's case, gives orbifold type. *Step 6, inverse.* By the cocycle identities the inverse is the transition in the other direction, sc-smooth by Step 5. Gap G.155 is closed.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text's proof of Proposition 16.4.3 is the reference to Proposition 9.1.9, which gives the structure on $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ for one representative; that the structure is natural, that is, independent of the representative, is in the word "natural". The formalization proves the independence explicitly through the transition maps between supports, and in a form stronger than a choice: any structures induced by Proposition 9.1.9 on the two supports are related by an sc-diffeomorphism. The proof needs the restriction of an equivalence to the sub-ep-groupoids on the supports, which is the argument of Proposition 11.1.6 in Part XI.

### XVI.19 Definitions 16.4.4 and 16.4.5 (2017: Definitions 16.31, 16.34), pp. 730–732: oriented branched suborbifolds and their integrals

**Statement.** *Definition 16.4.4* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold⟧: an oriented branched suborbifold is a class $\hat\theta = [(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha)]$ of representatives with $(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ an oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $X$ (Chapter 11) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep⟧, related by $f^*(\Theta', \hat T_{\Theta'}) = (\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ and $\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel⟧, with an underlying branched suborbifold ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.toBranched⟧. *Definition 16.4.5* (p. 731, same) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_4_5_wellDefined⟧: $\partial\hat\theta = [\partial(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha)]$ does not depend on the representative. *The integrals* (p. 732, same) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff⟧: $\int_{\hat\theta}\tau = \mu^{\hat\Theta}_\omega(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ and $\oint_{\hat\theta}\tau$, for a tame compact oriented class, equal to the integrals on every representative ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_eq⟧.

**Proof of Definition 16.4.4.** *Step 1, the normalization.* The text's $\hat T_\Theta$ lives over $X_\infty$, and $f^*$ only reads it there; the formalization makes $\hat T_\Theta$ zero off $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.mem_grHatSections⟧. Reflexivity needs it: $1^*\hat T = \hat T$ holds for such $\hat T$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullSection_id_of_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pull_id_of_mem⟧, and fails otherwise, since the pull-back is $0$ off $X_\infty$. Every pull-back of Chapter 11 has this property, so it is a normalization, not an added hypothesis. *Step 2, an equivalence relation* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.trans⟧: as in §XVI.17, with the pull-back of oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoids of Chapter 11 (Part XI), which is functorial on generalized isomorphisms. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.toBranchedRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.toBranchedRep⟧: forgetting the orientation respects the relations, which defines the underlying $\theta$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.toBranched_mk⟧.

**Proof of Definition 16.4.5.** *Step 1.* If two representatives are related through $f$, then $f^*\partial\Theta' = \partial\Theta$ and $f^*\hat T_{\partial\Theta'} = \hat T_{\partial\Theta}$, by Theorem 11.3.9 (Part XI) ⟦Chapter11/BoundaryOrientationEquiv · theorem_11_3_9_pull_boundaryOrientation⟧. So $\partial\hat\theta$ does not depend on the representative. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryFun_eq_of_rel⟧: the boundary function $\partial\theta = |\partial\Theta| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ does not either, so neither does $\partial S = \operatorname{supp}\partial\theta$. *Readings.* The compatibility holds without tameness, which the text assumes for $\partial\hat\theta$ to be a branched suborbifold. $\partial(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ is formalized componentwise, as in Chapter 11.

**Proof of the integrals.** *Step 1, on a representative.* A representative is tame of dimension $n$ in the sense of Chapter 9 if oriented tame structures describe $\hat T_\Theta$ at every point of $\operatorname{supp}\Theta$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.IsTameOriented⟧. For such a representative that is compact, $\int = \mu^{\hat\Theta}_\omega(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral⟧ and $\oint = \mu^{\hat\Theta, \mathrm{eff}}_\omega(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff⟧, with $\omega$ the representative of $\tau$ on $(X, \alpha)$ (§XVI.10). For the effective integral, (ZHOU) gives the local uniqueness condition (LUC) by Proposition 7.4.10 (Part VII). *Step 2, the boundary integrals on a representative* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEff⟧: the measures of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 (Part IX), with separate forms in dimension $1$, where the boundary is $0$-dimensional ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralDim1⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEffDim1⟧. *Step 3, independence of the representative* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral_eq_of_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff_eq_of_rel⟧: if two tame compact representatives are related through $f$, the representative of $\tau$ on the first structure is $f^*$ of that on the second ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructure_eq_formsPullback⟧, and the tame integrals are invariant under pull-back, Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2 with $K = |\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ (Part XI) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tameBranchedIntegral_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tameBranchedIntegralEff_pull⟧. *Step 4, tameness on classes.* Related oriented representatives are tame together ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.isTameOriented⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.isTameOriented_iff⟧: the oriented tame structures move along the transport charts as in §XVI.17, with the orientations pulled back. So tameness of an oriented class ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.IsTameOriented⟧ holds in every representative ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.isTameOriented_iff⟧, and compactness is that of any representative ⟦Chapter16/BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.isCompactBranched_of_mk⟧. *Step 5, on classes.* The integral of the class is computed on the chosen representative, and by Steps 3–4 equals the integral on every representative. *Step 6, the boundary integrals.* Their independence of the representative is obtained from Stokes' theorem (§XVI.20) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegral_eq_of_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEff_eq_of_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralDim1_eq_of_rel⟧: both sides equal the integral of $d\tau$, which is independent by Step 3. This needs the hypothesis of §XVI.20, sc-smooth partitions of unity. The boundary integrals are not wrapped as functions on classes (§XVI.28); they would follow from Step 6 as the interior integrals follow from Step 3.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text defines the integrals on p. 732 through a representative and says that they do not depend on the choice; for the interior integrals the formalization proves this through Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2, as the text intends. For the boundary integrals the direct route would be the boundary form of Theorem 11.4.1, which is not formalized; the formalization instead derives their independence from Stokes' theorem, which costs the hypothesis of sc-smooth partitions of unity. Definition 16.4.4 adds the normalization of $\hat T_\Theta$ off $X_\infty$, which the text does not need to state because it only ever reads $\hat T_\Theta$ on $X_\infty$, but which a formal reflexivity proof does need.

### XVI.20 Theorem 16.4.6 (2017: Theorem 16.5), p. 732: Stokes' theorem on polyfolds

**Statement** (with an added hypothesis) ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_hyp⟧. Let $(Z, c)$ admit sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definition 16.1.5), $\hat\theta = [(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha)]$ oriented, compact and tame of dimension $n = m + 1 \ge 2$, and $\tau \in \Omega^m_{sc}(Z, c)$. Then $\int_{\hat\theta} d\tau = \int_{\partial\hat\theta}\tau$. The effective form ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_eff_hyp⟧: $\oint_{\hat\theta} d\tau = \oint_{\partial\hat\theta}\tau$. Dimension $1$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_dim1_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_eff_dim1_hyp⟧. Both identities together ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_both_hyp⟧.

**Proof.** *Step 1, to the representative.* The representative of $d\tau$ on $(X, \alpha)$ is $d$ of the representative $\omega$ of $\tau$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.toStructure_d⟧ (§XVI.10, the formula $d[(\omega, (X, \alpha))] = [(d\omega, (X, \alpha))]$). So both sides are integrals over $\Theta$ on $X$: $\mu^{\hat\Theta}_{d\omega}(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ and the boundary measure of $\omega$. *Step 2, partitions of unity on $X$.* By Definition 16.1.5 (2) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldPartitions · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_1_5_two⟧ (§XVI.3), $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, since $(Z, c)$ does. *Step 3, Stokes on $X$.* Theorem 9.5.17 (Part IX) ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · theorem_9_5_17⟧ gives the identity on $X$; for the effective form, Theorem 9.5.18 ⟦Chapter9/StokesTextHypotheses · theorem_9_5_18⟧, with (LUC) from (ZHOU). In dimension $1$, the dimension-$1$ forms of both theorems. *Step 4.* By §XVI.19, Steps 3 and 6, the result does not depend on the representative.

*The added hypothesis.* Theorem 16.4.6 does not state that $(Z, c)$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, but its proof reduces to Theorem 9.5.17, which assumes them for $X$; the polyfold theorem is proved with the same hypothesis, in the form of Definition 16.1.5. It is not derived from the text. *Witness* ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness⟧: the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1 admits sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧. Without the hypothesis the theorem is gap G.153 (§XVI.28). *Reading.* "Tame" is Chapter 9's, on the representative used; by §XVI.19, Step 4, it holds on every representative.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* None in the argument: the text's proof is the reduction to Theorem 9.5.17 in a representative, and the formalization is that reduction with each translation step made explicit. The departure is in the statement, which carries the hypothesis of Theorem 9.5.17 that the polyfold statement does not print. Dimension $1$ is stated separately because there the boundary of $\hat\theta$ is a weighted finite set of points and the boundary measure of Chapter 9 is a weighted sum of values rather than an integral over a manifold; Theorems 9.5.17 and 9.5.18 have separate forms for it, and the polyfold theorem inherits the split. The four Lean statements together cover every dimension $n \ge 1$ and both integrals.

### XVI.21 Definitions 16.5.1, 16.5.2, Remark 16.5.3 and (16.8) (2017: Definitions 16.35, 16.36, Remark 16.5), p. 733: sc⁺-multisections and $n(\lambda)$

**Statement.** *Definition 16.5.1* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection⟧: an sc⁺-multisection $\lambda : Y \to \mathbb Q^+$ of a strong polyfold bundle is a class of representatives $(\lambda, \Gamma, W, \Lambda)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep⟧, $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection functor of a structure of $\bar c$ (Definition 13.1.4) with $\lambda(\Gamma|w|) = \Lambda(w)$; two are related if $\lambda = \lambda'$ and $\Lambda = \bar f^*\Lambda'$ for a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\bar f$ with $\Gamma' \circ |\bar f| = \Gamma$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.Rel⟧. *Definition 16.5.2* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSupp⟧: the domain support of $\lambda$ is the closure of the set of $z$ over which some $y \ne 0_z$ has $\lambda(y) > 0$. *Remark 16.5.3* (same, with $\gamma$ for the printed $\Gamma$) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.remark_16_5_3⟧: for a representative, $\gamma(|\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda|) = \operatorname{dom-supp}\lambda$. *(16.8)* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normLam⟧ ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.continuous_normLam⟧: for an auxiliary norm $n$, $n(\lambda)(z) = \max\{n(y) : p(y) = z, \lambda(y) \ne 0\}$ is a continuous function $Z \to [0, \infty)$.

**Background: sc⁺-multisection functors.** Over an ep-groupoid, an sc⁺-multisection functor (Definition 13.1.4, Part XIII) is a functor $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ which near every object $x$ has a local section structure: an invariant open neighbourhood $O$ of $x$, finitely many sc⁺-sections $s_1, \ldots, s_k$ of $P$ over $O$ and positive rational weights $\sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_k$ with $\sum_i \sigma_i = 1$, such that $\Lambda(w) = \sum_{i : s_i(P(w)) = w} \sigma_i$ for $w$ over $O$. Thus over every object the values of $\Lambda$ on the fibre are finitely many positive weights summing to $1$, carried by the values of the local sections, and $\Lambda$ vanishes elsewhere. The domain support (Definition 13.2.2) is the closure of the objects over which $\Lambda$ charges a non-zero vector, and for an auxiliary norm $N$ the pointwise norm $N(\Lambda)(x)$ (Definition 13.2.3) is the largest $N(w)$ over the charged vectors $w$ of the fibre. A multisection is structurable (Definition 13.3.6) if it admits local section structures that fit together under the morphisms, the condition under which the perturbation theory of Chapters 14 and 15 works. An sc⁺-multisection of a strong polyfold bundle is the function on $Y$ that such a functor induces through $\Gamma$.

**Proof of Definition 16.5.1.** *Step 1, the map $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.continuous_γπ⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.surjective_γπ⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isSaturated_preimage_γπ⟧: it is continuous, surjective, and preimages of sets of $Z$ are saturated; and $p(\Gamma(|w|)) = \gamma(|P(w)|)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_Γ_π⟧. These are the translations used throughout §§16.5–16.6. *Step 2, the relation does not depend on $\bar f$* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.pullMult_eq_of_Γ⟧. By §XVI.11 the isomorphism $\bar f$ need not be unique; but for every $\bar f$ with $\Gamma' \circ |\bar f| = \Gamma$ and every functor $\Lambda'$ represented by $\lambda$, $(\bar f^*\Lambda')(w) = \lambda(\Gamma|w|)$. The pull-back of a multisection functor along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism is read on orbits (Part XIII), $\Lambda'$ is $\lambda \circ \Gamma' \circ \pi$, and $\Gamma' \circ |\bar f| = \Gamma$. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.rel_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.rel_of_lam_eq⟧: so two representatives are related iff their functions agree and their structures are equivalent; and it is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.setoid⟧. *Step 4, the check on the $\mathbb Z/3$ example* ⟦Chapter16/RepresentativeChecks · StrongPolyfoldBundle.pullMult_z3_independent⟧: on the strong bundle of §XVI.11, the two generalized isomorphisms $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ pull every multisection functor back to the same functor, as Step 2 predicts. *Step 5, a multisection is its function* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.ext_toFun⟧. *Step 6, representatives in every structure* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_rep_of_mem⟧: every structure of $\bar c$ carries a representative of every $\lambda$, by pulling back a representative along a realizing isomorphism and Proposition 11.5.3 (Part XI), which keeps sc⁺-multisection functors. *Step 7* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ofFunctor⟧: an sc⁺-multisection functor in one structure of $\bar c$ defines an sc⁺-multisection. *Witness* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zero⟧: the trivial multisection, $\lambda = 1$ on the zero section and $0$ elsewhere.

**Proof of Definition 16.5.2 and Remark 16.5.3.** *Step 1, the printed set is all of $Z$* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSuppText⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSuppText_eq_univ⟧. As printed, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda)$ is the closure of $\{z : \exists y \in p^{-1}(z),\ \lambda(y) > 0\}$. Over every $z$ the weights of $\lambda$ sum to $1$ (Definition 13.1.4, through a representative), so some $y$ has $\lambda(y) > 0$, and the set is $Z$. With $y \ne 0_z$, as in Definition 13.2.2 (Part XIII), it is the intended set: the domain support of the ep-groupoid notion is defined with $w \ne 0$. *Step 2, the set before the closure* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.nzSet⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isSaturated_nzSet⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.image_nzSet⟧: in a representative, the set $\{x : \exists w \in W_x \setminus \{0\},\ \Lambda(w) > 0\}$ is saturated (because $\Lambda$ is a functor and morphisms act linearly on fibres, so they preserve non-zero vectors) and its image under $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$ is the set before the closure in Definition 16.5.2, using that $\Gamma(|w|) = 0_z$ iff $w$ is a zero (§XVI.16). *Step 3, Remark 16.5.3.* The image of the closure of a saturated set under the open quotient map $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$ is the closure of its image; with Step 2 this is $\gamma(|\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda|) = \operatorname{dom-supp}\lambda$. The text writes $\Gamma$; both sets lie in $|X|$ and $Z$, so we read $\gamma$.

**Proof of (16.8), the formula.** *Step 1, the definition* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normLam⟧: $n(\lambda)(z)$ is the supremum of $n(y)$ over $y$ with $p(y) = z$ and $\lambda(y) \ne 0$, where $n$ is extended by $0$ off $Y_{0,1}$ (§XVI.16). *Step 2, in a representative* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.image_normY_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normLam_eq⟧: the set of values $\{n(y)\}$ over $\gamma(|x|)$ equals the set $\{N(w) : w \in W_x,\ \Lambda(w) \ne 0\}$, because $\Gamma$ maps the fibre $W_x$ onto $p^{-1}(\gamma|x|)$ up to the isotropy action, which preserves $N$ and $\Lambda$. So $n(\lambda)(\gamma(|x|)) = N(\Lambda)(x)$, the function of Definition 13.2.3 (Part XIII). *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.isGreatest_normLam⟧: the maximum is attained, since $\Lambda$ has finitely many non-zero values over each $x$ (finitely many local sections in a local section structure). *Step 4* ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.normLam_nonneg⟧: $n(\lambda) \ge 0$, as $n$ is.

**Proof of (16.8), the continuity.** *Step 1, $N(\Lambda)$ is continuous on $X$* ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.continuous_pointwiseNorm⟧. Let $\Lambda$ be an sc⁺-multisection functor and $N$ continuous on $W_{0,1}$. Near each $x$ there is a local section structure: sc⁺-sections $s_1, \ldots, s_k$ on an open $O \ni x$ with weights $\sigma_i > 0$ summing to $1$, with $\Lambda(w) = \sum_{s_i(y) = w}\sigma_i$. On $O$, $N(\Lambda)(y) = \max_i N(s_i(y))$ ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.pointwiseNorm_eq⟧, over a non-empty index set ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.univ_nonempty⟧ (the weights sum to $1$); every $s_i$ is continuous into $W_{0,1}$, being sc⁺, so $N \circ s_i$ is continuous, and a finite maximum of continuous functions is continuous. *Step 2, a quotient map* ⟦Chapter16/NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isQuotientMap_γπ⟧: $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$ is a quotient map, $\pi$ being an open quotient map (Proposition 7.1.8, Part VII) and $\gamma$ a homeomorphism. *Step 3.* $n(\lambda) \circ \gamma \circ \pi = N(\Lambda)$ by the formula, with $N$ the representative of $n$ (continuous by Definition 16.3.9), so $n(\lambda)$ is continuous by Step 2. The text calls $n(\lambda)$ continuous; this is the proof. Gap G.174 is closed.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text defines sc⁺-multisections by representatives and their relation with a chosen $\bar f$; the formalization proves that the choice of $\bar f$ does not matter, which the text does not address, and which is needed because $\bar f$ is not unique (§XVI.11). The text asserts that $n(\lambda)$ is continuous; the formalization proves it, through the local section structures of Chapter 13 and a quotient map. Definition 16.5.2 is read with $y \ne 0_z$, and Remark 16.5.3 with $\gamma$.

### XVI.22 Definitions 16.5.4–16.5.6 (2017: Definitions 16.37–16.39), p. 734: structurable multisections, and multisections over $\partial Z$

**Statement.** *Definition 16.5.4* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.IsStructurable⟧: $\lambda$ is structurable if one representative is (Definition 13.3.6); "and therefore all" ⟦Chapter16/StructurablePullback · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.definition_16_5_4⟧. *Definition 16.5.5* (restated) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection⟧: sc⁺-multisections of $Y|\partial Z$, classes of representatives with $\Lambda$ a multisection functor on $W|\partial X$ (Definition 14.1.3) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep⟧. *Definition 16.5.6* (same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.IsStructurable⟧: $\lambda$ over $\partial Z$ is structurable if one representative is (Definition 14.1.7). The text writes $\lambda : Z \to \mathbb Q^+$ in Definition 16.5.4; we read $\lambda : Y \to \mathbb Q^+$, the domain of Definition 16.5.1.

**Proof of Definition 16.5.4.** *Step 1, the pull-back proposition* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StructurablePullback⟧: pull-backs of structurable sc⁺-multisection functors along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are structurable. *Step 2, from it the class statement* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.definition_16_5_4_hyp⟧: if one representative is structurable, every other is its pull-back along a realizing isomorphism, by Step 2 of §XVI.21, and so is structurable. *Step 3, the proposition holds* ⟦Chapter16/StructurablePullback · fnStructurablePullback⟧: by Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3 for generalized isomorphisms (Part XIII), which pull back structured representatives along the two legs of a diagram. So Definition 16.5.4 holds as printed ⟦Chapter16/StructurablePullback · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.definition_16_5_4⟧. *Witness* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zero_isStructurable⟧: the zero multisection is structurable.

**Proof of Definition 16.5.5.** *Step 1, the boundary* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mem_boundary_iff_obj⟧: $\gamma(|x|) \in \partial Z$ iff $x \in \partial X$ (§XVI.5). *Step 2, the relation* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep.Rel⟧: $\lambda = \lambda'$ over $\partial Z$, and a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\bar f$ with $\Gamma' \circ |\bar f| = \Gamma$ has $\Lambda(w) = \Lambda'(w')$ whenever $|\bar f|(|w|) = |w'|$ over $\partial X$. *Restated* because the pull-back of multisection functors over the boundary is read in this orbit form: a pull-back over $\partial X$ along generalized isomorphisms is part of the gap of Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$ (Part XIV). *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep.rel_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep.rel_of_lam_eq⟧: as for Definition 16.5.1, two representatives are related iff their functions agree over $p^{-1}(\partial Z)$ and their structures are equivalent. *Step 4, the function* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.toFun_mk_of_mem⟧: $\lambda$ on $Y|\partial Z$, read as $0$ off $p^{-1}(\partial Z)$, is well defined.

**Proof of Definition 16.5.6.** Structurability over $\partial Z$ is that of one representative, as printed. The domain support over $\partial Z$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.domSupp⟧ is Definition 16.5.2 read over $\partial Z$, as Theorem 16.5.7 uses it, and $|\partial\text{-}\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda)| \subseteq \partial\text{-}\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda)$ through $x \mapsto \gamma(|x|)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.boundaryDomSupp_subset⟧, the image of the closure lying in the closure of the image by continuity. The text adds no "and therefore all" here; the invariance would need the boundary pull-back of Step 2 above.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text's "and therefore all" in Definition 16.5.4 is left unproved; the formalization isolates the proposition it needs, that structurability pulls back along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms, and proves it from Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3. Definition 16.5.5 is restated, since the pull-back of multisection functors over the boundary along generalized isomorphisms is not available as formalized; its orbit form suffices for the relation, by the same argument as for Definition 16.5.1.

### XVI.23 Theorem 16.5.7 (2017: Theorem 16.6), p. 735: extension of sc⁺-multisections from the boundary

**Statement** (with added hypotheses) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBoundaryExtension · theorem_16_5_7_a6⟧. Let $p : Y \to Z$ be a tame strong polyfold bundle whose models admit sc-smooth partitions of unity on the objects and tame strong bundle charts at every object, $n$ an auxiliary norm, $\lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial Z$ that is structurable with non-empty index sets ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBoundaryExtension · BoundaryMultisection.IsStructurableNe⟧, $\tilde U$ an open set containing $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda)$, and $f : Z \to [0, \infty)$ continuous with closed support in $\tilde U$ and $n(\lambda) < f$ on $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda)$. Then there is a structurable sc⁺-multisection $\lambda'$ with (1) $n(\lambda') \le f$, (2) $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda') \subseteq \tilde U$, and (3) $\lambda' = \lambda$ over $\partial Z$.

*Readings and added hypotheses.* (a) *Non-empty index sets* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBoundaryExtension · BoundaryMultisection.IsStructurableNe⟧: $\lambda$ has a representative structurable over $\partial X$ whose $\Lambda$ charges every boundary fibre; this implies Definition 16.5.6 ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBoundaryExtension · BoundaryMultisection.IsStructurableNe.isStructurable⟧. The text's $\lambda$ is an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial Z$, whose local section structures have non-empty index sets (the weights sum to $1$ over each boundary fibre), so this is the text's notion, made explicit because Definition 14.1.3 as formalized admits empty index sets. (b) *Tame strong bundle charts* at every object of every model: an added hypothesis, not derived from the text; it is the reading of Theorem 14.1.9 in Part XIV, where the derivation of such charts from tameness is a gap of that Part. (c) *Partitions of unity* on the objects of every model, the form Theorem 14.1.9 uses; for a polyfold this is Definition 16.1.5 (2) in the object form. (d) "Support" is the closed support.

**Proof.** *Step 1, choose the model.* Take a representative $a = (\lambda, \Gamma, W, \Lambda)$ over $\partial X$ in a structure $S$ of $\bar c$, with $\Lambda$ structurable and charging every boundary fibre. Let $g = \gamma \circ \pi : X \to Z$; it is continuous (§XVI.21).

*Step 2, translate the hypotheses to $X$.* The open set $g^{-1}(\tilde U)$ is open and saturated ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isSaturated_preimage_γπ⟧. $f \circ g$ is continuous, nonnegative, invariant under morphisms (since $g$ is), and its closed support lies in $g^{-1}(\tilde U)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.tsupport_comp_subset_preimage'⟧, the closed support of a composite with a continuous map lying in the preimage of the closed support. The boundary domain support of $\Lambda$ maps into that of $\lambda$ (§XVI.22), hence lies in $g^{-1}(\tilde U)$. For $x$ in the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, $x \in \partial X$ (it lies in the closure of a set of boundary points, and $\partial X$ is closed), and $N(\Lambda)(x) = n(\lambda)(g(x))$ by (16.8) in the representative (§XVI.21), with the value of $\lambda$ over the boundary read through the representative: for $w$ over $x$, $p(\Gamma|w|) = g(x) \in \partial Z$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_Γ_π⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mem_boundary_iff_obj⟧, so $\lambda(\Gamma|w|) = \Lambda(w)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.toFun_mk_of_mem⟧. So $N(\Lambda) < f \circ g$ on the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$.

*Step 3, Theorem 14.1.9 in the model.* The charged form of Theorem 14.1.9 (Part XIV) applies in $S$: $X$ is tame (Definition 16.3.5 (1)), $|X|$ paracompact (Definition 16.3.1), partitions of unity and tame strong bundle charts by (b), (c), $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ and charging every boundary fibre by (a), $N$ an auxiliary norm by Definition 16.3.9, and the data of Step 2. It gives a structurable sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda'$ with $N(\Lambda') \le f \circ g$, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda') \subseteq g^{-1}(\tilde U)$ and $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$.

*Step 4, back to $Y$.* Let $\lambda'$ be the sc⁺-multisection of $\Lambda'$ (§XVI.21, Step 7); it is structurable by Definition 16.5.4. (1): every $z$ is $g(x)$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.surjective_γπ⟧, and $n(\lambda')(g(x)) = N(\Lambda')(x) \le f(g(x))$ by (16.8). (2): by Remark 16.5.3, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda') = g(\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda') \subseteq \tilde U$. (3): every $y$ over $\partial Z$ is $\Gamma(|w|)$ with $P(w) \in \partial X$, and $\lambda'(y) = \Lambda'(w) = \Lambda(w) = \lambda(y)$.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text's proof is "Theorem 14.1.9 in a representative"; the formalization carries the translation of each hypothesis and conclusion explicitly, through (16.8) and Remark 16.5.3.

**A remark on a superseded Lean statement.** The declaration ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_5_7_hyp⟧ proves the same conclusion with "Theorem 14.1.9 holds in every model of $\bar c$" as a hypothesis, where Theorem 14.1.9 is the Lean statement in which multisections over $\partial X$ may have empty index sets (Definition 14.1.3 as formalized admits them). That Lean statement of Theorem 14.1.9 does not hold when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ (Part XIV), so this declaration is vacuous for polyfolds with boundary, the case the theorem is about; its other hypotheses are jointly satisfiable on every tame bundle ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMultisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_5_7_hyp_witness⟧, with the zero multisection over $\partial Z$, $\tilde U = \emptyset$ and $f = 0$. The statement above, with non-empty index sets, is the one that formalizes Theorem 16.5.7.

*Witness of the hypotheses.* The ep-groupoid hypotheses of the charged Theorem 14.1.9 hold, with boundary and non-zero fibres, on the half-space bundle of Part XIV. No strong polyfold bundle is built on it, so at the level of polyfolds the tame strong bundle charts and the non-empty index sets have no witness of their own; the remaining hypotheses are witnessed as above, and partitions of unity by the polyfold $\mathbb R$ (§XVI.27).

### XVI.24 The claim before Definition 16.6.1, Definitions 16.6.1–16.6.3 and Theorem 16.6.4 (2017: Definitions 16.40, 16.41, Theorem 16.7), pp. 735–737: sc-Fredholm sections

**Statement.** *The claim* (pp. 735–736, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.isFredholm_iff⟧: if one representative of an sc-smooth section is an sc-Fredholm section functor (Definition 12.1.2), every other is; a section is sc-Fredholm if one representative is ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsFredholm⟧. *Definition 16.6.1* (p. 736, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.FredholmSection⟧: the sc-Fredholm sections. *Definition 16.6.2* (p. 736, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.HasCompactSolutionSet⟧: $f$ has a compact solution set if $S_f = \{z : f(z) = 0_z\}$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.solutionSet⟧ is compact. *Definition 16.6.3* (pp. 736–737, same; new in 2021) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsProper⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsProperLtInfty⟧: (1) $f$ is proper if for every auxiliary norm $n$ there is an open $U \supseteq S_f$ with $\{z \in U : n(f(z)) \le 1\}$ having compact closure; (2) $f$ is proper$<\infty$ if the same holds for every $C$ in place of $1$, with $U$ depending on $C$; $(n, U)$ controls compactness if $U$ works with $C = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.ControlsCompactness⟧. *Theorem 16.6.4* (p. 737, same) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_4⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section, a compact solution set, proper and proper$<\infty$ are equivalent.

**Proof of the claim and Definition 16.6.1.** *Step 1.* Two representatives are related by a generalized strong bundle isomorphism pushing one functor to the other (§XVI.16). *Step 2.* Theorem 10.5.4 (Part X): the push-forward of an sc-Fredholm section functor along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism is sc-Fredholm, since the legs are local strong bundle isomorphisms and the sc-Fredholm property is local and invariant under them (Part XII). *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.exists_rep_of_mem⟧: every structure of $\bar c$ carries a representative of every sc-smooth section, by pushing a representative along a realizing isomorphism. So the property is that of any representative in any structure.

**The dictionary between $Z$ and a representative.** For a representative $a = (f, \Gamma, W, F)$ write $g = \gamma \circ \pi : X \to Z$. *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isSection_F⟧: $P \circ F = \mathrm{id}$. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.Γ_mem_Y01_iff⟧: $\Gamma(|w|) \in Y_{0,1}$ iff $w \in W_{0,1}$. *Step 3, the solution set* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.solutionSet_eq⟧: $S_f = g(S_F)$, because $f(g(x)) = \Gamma(|F(x)|)$ and $\Gamma(|w|) = 0_z$ iff $w$ is a zero (§XVI.16). *Step 4, sublevel sets* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.sublevel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.sublevel_eq⟧: $\{z \in V : f(z) \in Y_{0,1},\ n(f(z)) \le C\} = g(\{x \in g^{-1}(V) : N(F(x)) \le C\})$ with $N$ the representative of $n$; the text's "$n(f(z)) \le C$" is read as $f(z) \in Y_{0,1}$ and $n(f(z)) \le C$, since $n$ is defined on $Y_{0,1}$. *Step 5, topology* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isOpen_g_image⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.preimage_g_image⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isCompact_closure_g_image_iff⟧: $g$ is open, a saturated set is the preimage of its image, and a saturated set has compact closure in $X$'s orbit space iff its image has compact closure in $Z$ (the image of a compact set under the continuous $g$ is compact; conversely, $\gamma$ is a homeomorphism, so compactness in $Z$ is compactness in $|X|$, which is the meaning of compact closure for saturated sets in Chapter 12). *Step 6, the $U$-conditions* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.forall_iff_of_saturated⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.forall_iff_of_open⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.solutionSet_subset_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.solutionSet_subset_preimage_iff⟧: an open $U \supseteq S_f$ in $Z$ corresponds to the saturated open $g^{-1}(U) \supseteq S_F$, and conversely a saturated open $U' \supseteq S_F$ to $g(U')$, with the sublevel conditions corresponding for each $C$. *Step 7, every auxiliary norm* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.forall_auxNorm_iff⟧: "for every auxiliary norm $n$ of $Y$" may be read as "for every auxiliary norm $N$ of $W$", since auxiliary norms correspond by descent and representation (§XVI.13).

**Proof of Definitions 16.6.2, 16.6.3 in a representative.** *Definition 16.6.2* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.hasCompactSolutionSet_iff⟧: $S_f$ is compact iff $|S_F|$ is, by Steps 3 and 5; that is Definition 12.4.1 (1). *Definition 16.6.3 (1)* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isProper_iff⟧: by Steps 4–7 it is Definition 12.4.1 (2). *Definition 16.6.3 (2)* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isProperLtInfty_iff⟧: Definition 12.4.1 (3). *Controlling compactness* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.controlsCompactness_iff⟧: $(n, U)$ controls compactness iff $(N, g^{-1}(U))$ does in the sense of Definition 15.3.1 (Part XV).

**Proof of Theorem 16.6.4.** Take a representative in any structure (Step 3 of the claim). By the translations above, the three conditions are those of Definition 12.4.1 for $F$, and Theorem 12.4.2 (Part XII) shows that they are equivalent for an sc-Fredholm section functor over an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space, which every structure of $\bar c$ has.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text proves the claim before Definition 16.6.1 by Theorem 10.5.4, and Theorem 16.6.4 by Theorem 12.4.2 in a representative; the formalization follows both. What it adds is the dictionary between conditions on $Z$, $Y$ and conditions on a model, which the text leaves implicit: solution sets, sublevel sets, open neighbourhoods of the solution set, compact closures and the quantifier over auxiliary norms. Each translation is a separate lemma, and together they show that every notion of Definitions 16.6.2 and 16.6.3 is, in every representative, the corresponding notion of Definition 12.4.1.

### XVI.25 Definition 16.6.5 (2017: Definition 16.42), p. 739: orientations of sc-Fredholm sections

**Statement** (narrower). *The definition* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.FredholmSection.IsOrientable⟧: an orientation of an sc-Fredholm section $f$ is an orientation of a representative $(W, F)$: sc⁺-sections through every point, a topology on the orientation bundle $O_F$ as in Theorem 12.5.3, and an orientation in the sense of Definition 12.5.4; $f$ is orientable if one exists. *The transport* ⟦Chapter16/OrientationTransport · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.transport_hyp⟧: an orientation of one representative gives one of every other representative, the text's "an orientation of one representative determines orientations of all". *Narrower* in two ways: the standing hypotheses of the M-polyfold theory (tameness, sc-smooth bump functions, tame sc-Fredholm germs) are taken on the bundles of the diagram along which the orientation is carried, as in Theorem 12.5.7; and that the carried orientation does not depend on the diagram is not formalized. Both are gap G.176, formalized in part (§XVI.28).

**Background: orientations of sc-Fredholm section functors.** For an sc-Fredholm section functor $F$ of a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, Chapter 12 attaches to every smooth point $x$ the set of linearizations of $F$ at $x$, which differ by sc⁺-operators, and to each linearization its determinant line; Theorem 12.5.3 shows that these lines form a bundle $O_F$ over the smooth points with a topology for which local sc⁺-sections through a point give continuous local trivializations. An orientation (Definition 12.5.4) is a choice of one of the two orientations of each determinant line that is continuous in this topology and invariant under the morphisms of $X$, which act on linearizations by conjugation with the local strong bundle isomorphisms of the action. Theorem 12.5.7 shows that a strong bundle equivalence transports orientations, because it identifies linearizations at corresponding points. On a polyfold an orientation is therefore an orientation of one representative together with the promise, made by the text and proved here in part, that the transports to every other representative are consistent.

**Proof of the transport along a diagram** ⟦Chapter16/OrientationTransport · SBLocalization.SDiagram.orientation_transport_hyp⟧. *Statement:* for a diagram $D = [W \xleftarrow{L} W'' \xrightarrow{L'} W']$ of strong bundle equivalences with $[D]_*F = F'$ and an orientation $o$ of $F$ in the sense of Definition 12.5.4, for any topology on $O_F$ as in Theorem 12.5.3, there is exactly one invariant orientation $o'$ of $F'$ compatible with $o$ over $W''$, and it satisfies Definition 12.5.4 for every topology on $O_{F'}$ as in Theorem 12.5.3. *Step 1, pull back along $L$.* Theorem 12.5.7 (Part XII) carries $o$ to an orientation of $L^*F$ on $W''$, the linearizations of $F$ and $L^*F$ being identified by the local strong bundle isomorphisms of $L$; the standing hypotheses on $W$ and $W''$ are those of Theorem 12.5.7. *Step 2, push forward along $L'$.* The same theorem in the other direction carries it to $F'$, using $[D]_*F = F'$, that is $L'_*L^*F = F'$ up to the identification of the middle. *Step 3, uniqueness and invariance.* An invariant orientation of $F'$ is determined on orbits, and over the image of $L'$ it is forced by compatibility; since $L'$ is essentially surjective, every orbit meets the image. *Step 4, continuity for every topology* ⟦Chapter16/OrientationTransport · SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_orientation_of_eq⟧: Theorem 12.5.3 allows several topologies on $O_F$, all with the same continuous sections in the sense used by Definition 12.5.4; Part XII identifies the two readings of continuity, and an orientation for every such topology carries over along an equality $F_1 = F_2$.

**Proof on classes.** *Step 1* ⟦Chapter16/OrientationTransport · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.exists_diagram⟧: for an orientation of a representative $(W, F)$ and any other representative $(W', F')$ of the same section, a diagram $D$ with $[D]_*F = F'$ exists, by §XVI.16 (related representatives are related by a generalized strong bundle isomorphism pushing one functor to the other) and a representative diagram of that isomorphism. *Step 2* ⟦Chapter16/OrientationTransport · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep.transport_hyp⟧: the transport along $D$ gives an orientation of $F'$.

*What is not formalized.* (i) Two diagrams give the same transported orientation; this needs a common refinement and the compatibility of the orientation maps of Theorem 12.5.7 with composition and with natural equivalences, which Part XII proves for the data of diagrams. (ii) The standing hypotheses on the middle bundle $W''$ of a diagram follow from those on $W$ and $W'$; this needs the transfer of tameness, bump functions and tame germ data along strong bundle equivalences. On the $\mathbb Z/3$ example the two isomorphisms of §XVI.11 are the identity on objects and transport alike; no example was found where the diagram matters.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text says that an orientation of one representative determines orientations of all, by Theorem 12.5.7, and defines the orientation of $f$ as the resulting class. The formalization proves the first half, the transport along any diagram, and stops short of the second: that the result does not depend on the diagram, which the text does not argue, and which would be needed for the orientation of $f$ to be a well-defined class rather than a choice on one representative. The formal Definition 16.6.5 therefore records the orientation on one representative, which is what Theorem 16.6.6 uses.

### XVI.26 Theorem 16.6.6 (2017: Theorem 16.8), p. 739: the invariant of an oriented sc-Fredholm section

**Statement** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_hyp⟧. The text: for $\partial Z = \emptyset$, $f$ an oriented sc-Fredholm section with compact solution set, $n$ an auxiliary norm and $U$ open with $(n, U)$ controlling compactness, there are structurable sc⁺-multisections $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$ in general position; $\lambda \circ f$ is a compact branched suborbifold with an orientation inherited from $(f, o)$, and $\Phi_{(f,o)}([\tau]) = \int_{(\lambda \circ f, o)}\tau$ defines a linear map on cohomology that does not depend on $\lambda$. *The statement in Lean* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_statement⟧, degree-wise in the dimension $m + 1$ of $\lambda \circ f$, with a parameter $\mathrm{IsInherited}$, a predicate on pairs of an orientation of $f$ and an oriented perturbation: under the text's hypotheses, for every orientation $o$ of $f$, (i) for every admissible oriented perturbation with the inherited orientation, $\int$ and $\oint$ depend only on $[\tau]$, and (ii) for closed $\tau$, any two such perturbations give the same $\int$ and the same $\oint$. *Proved* given sc-smooth partitions of unity on $Z$ and cobordisms between any two such perturbations. *Narrower*: "inherited from $(f, o)$" is a parameter; the cobordisms are a hypothesis; "general position" is read in one model; index $0$ is not covered.

**How the pieces fit.** Theorem 16.6.6 combines four ingredients, which the formalization keeps separate so that each can be checked against its source. The perturbation $\lambda$ comes from Theorem 15.3.7 in one model, transported to the polyfold by (16.8) and Remark 16.5.3. The branched suborbifold $\lambda \circ f$ comes from Theorem 15.4.3 in that model, transported by the fact that a branched suborbifold is its function. The integral of a form over it comes from Chapter 9 in that model, transported by Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2, and its dependence only on the cohomology class comes from Stokes' theorem on the polyfold. The independence of $\lambda$ comes from a cobordism, which Chapter 15 constructs on a cylinder over one model. Of these, the first three are proved here for the polyfold; the fourth and the orientation that it must respect are the open part.
