**Controlled multisections and admissible perturbations.** *Controlled* ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.IsControlledBy⟧: $\lambda$ is controlled by $(n, U)$ if $n(\lambda) \le 1$ and $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\lambda) \subseteq U$ (the example after Definition 15.3.3). *General position* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsInGeneralPositionWith⟧: $(f, \lambda)$ is in general position if, in some model, the representatives $(F, \Lambda)$ are (Definitions 15.2.1, 15.3.4). *An oriented perturbation of dimension $m + 1$* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientedPerturbation⟧: a tame compact oriented branched suborbifold whose function is $\lambda \circ f$ for an sc⁺-multisection $\lambda$; it is *admissible* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientedPerturbation.IsAdmissible⟧ if $\lambda$ is controlled by $(n, U)$ and $(f, \lambda)$ is in general position. The text's $Z_{0,1}$ for the domain of $n$ is read as $Y_{0,1}$.

**Proof, $\lambda \circ f$ as a branched suborbifold.** *Step 1, the function* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.perturbedFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsPerturbedSuborbifold⟧: $\theta = \lambda \circ f : Z \to \mathbb Q^+$; a branched suborbifold "is $\lambda \circ f$" if its function is. *Step 2, in a model* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.toPolyfoldStructure_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.lam_f_eq⟧: the base $(X, \gamma)$ of a model $S \in \bar c$ is a structure of $(Z, c)$, and $\lambda(f(\gamma|x|)) = \Lambda(F(x))$ for representatives $F$ of $f$ and $\Lambda$ of $\lambda$ in $S$. *Step 3, the representative* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.perturbedRep⟧: $(\Lambda \circ F, (X, \gamma))$, for $\Lambda \circ F$ a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, which every model admits since every model carries a functor representing $\lambda$ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_functor_rep⟧. Its function is $\lambda \circ f$ in every model ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.perturbedRep_toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.perturbedRep_toFun_ofFunctor⟧. *Step 4* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isPerturbedSuborbifold_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isPerturbedSuborbifold_unique⟧: since a branched suborbifold is determined by its function (§XVI.17), $\theta = \lambda \circ f$ iff $\theta$ is the class of $(\Lambda \circ F, (X, \gamma))$ in any model, and such $\theta$ is unique. *Step 5, existence* (explicit) ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedSuborbifold · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_isPerturbedSuborbifold_hyp⟧: for $\partial Z = \emptyset$, $f$ sc-Fredholm, $(n, U)$ controlling compactness and $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$ and in general position in some model, $\lambda \circ f$ is a compact branched suborbifold. In the model, Theorem 15.4.3 (Part XV) makes $\Lambda \circ F$ a compact branched ep⁺-subgroupoid; good position is vacuous without boundary. The tame germ data of the model are inherited as in Part XV.

**Proof, the reduction to a model** ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_reduction⟧. For $\partial Z = \emptyset$, $f$ sc-Fredholm with compact solution set, $(n, U)$ controlling compactness and $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$: in every structure of $\bar c$, the representatives $F$, $\Lambda$ satisfy the hypotheses of the ep-groupoid statements of §§15.3–15.4. *Step 1.* $\partial X = \emptyset$, since $\partial Z$ is computed in any representative (§XVI.5) ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.not_mem_boundary_of_eq_empty⟧. *Step 2.* $|S_F|$ is compact (§XVI.24). *Step 3.* $(N, g^{-1}(U))$ controls compactness (§XVI.24). *Step 4.* $\Lambda$ is controlled: $N(\Lambda) = n(\lambda) \circ g \le 1$ by (16.8), and $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda) \subseteq g^{-1}(U)$ by Remark 16.5.3.

**Proof, the choice of $\lambda$** ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldFredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_generalPosition_hyp⟧. From the statement of Theorem 15.3.7 in a representative, with its standing hypotheses (tameness, sc-smooth bump functions, tame germ data), there is a structurable $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$ with $n(\lambda) < 1$ whose representative is transversal and in general position. *Step 1.* By the reduction, the hypotheses of Theorem 15.3.7 hold in the model. *Step 2.* Theorem 15.3.7 gives $\Lambda$. *Step 3.* $\lambda$ is the multisection of $\Lambda$ (§XVI.21), structurable (§XVI.22), controlled by (16.8) and Remark 16.5.3. *The hypothesis.* Theorem 15.3.7 in the representative is not an assumption of the text; it is discharged by Part XV's proof of Theorem 15.3.7 for paracompact orbit spaces, which every strong polyfold bundle structure has (Definition 16.3.1). The unconditional form is a one-line corollary, not stated as a separate declaration.

**Proof, the integrals on the polyfold.** *Step 1, additivity* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructure_add⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.ScForm.toStructure_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral_add⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff_add⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral_add⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_add⟧: the representative of a sum is the sum of the representatives, and the branched integrals of Chapter 9 are additive in the form. *Step 2, exact forms* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral_d_eq_zero_of_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff_d_eq_zero_of_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral_d_eq_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_d_eq_zero⟧: for $\partial Z = \emptyset$ with sc-smooth partitions of unity, $\int_{\hat\theta} d\eta = 0$ and $\oint_{\hat\theta} d\eta = 0$ for every tame compact oriented branched suborbifold of dimension $m + 1 \ge 1$. By Stokes (§XVI.20), $\int_{\hat\theta} d\eta = \int_{\partial\hat\theta}\eta$, and $\partial\Theta = 0$ because no object lies in $\partial X$. *Step 3* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral_add_d⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_add_d⟧: so the integrals depend only on $[\tau]$. *Step 4, compact oriented suborbifolds* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.integral⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.integralEff⟧: tame compact oriented branched suborbifolds of dimension $m + 1$ bundled with their proofs; their integral is, in every model, the integral of Definition 9.5.6 ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.integral_mk_rep⟧ (§XVI.19).

**Proof, cobordisms.** *The notion* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.HasCobordism⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.HasCobordismEff⟧: $P_0$ and $P_1$ are joined by an oriented compact cobordism if there are an ep-groupoid $Y$ with sc-smooth partitions of unity (and, for the effective form, the local unique continuation property), a compact oriented tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoid $\tilde\Theta$ of $Y$ of dimension $m + 2$, and an sc-smooth $F$ from $Y$ into a model of $Z$, with $\int_{\partial\tilde\Theta}F^*\omega = \int_{P_1}\omega - \int_{P_0}\omega$ for every form $\omega$. This is the shape of the proof of Corollary 15.4.4 (Part XV). *Closed forms* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.integral_eq_of_hasCobordism⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_eq_of_hasCobordismEff⟧: for $d\omega = 0$, $\int_{P_1}\omega - \int_{P_0}\omega = \int_{\partial\tilde\Theta}F^*\omega = \int_{\tilde\Theta}dF^*\omega = \int_{\tilde\Theta}F^*d\omega = 0$, by Theorem 9.5.17 on $Y$ (Theorem 9.5.18 for the effective form) and the commutation of $d$ with pull-back. *Satisfiable* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.hasCobordism_refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · PolyfoldClass.CompactOrientedSuborbifold.hasCobordismEff_refl⟧: every $P$ is cobordant to itself, with $Y = X$ and $\tilde\Theta = 0$.

**Proof of Theorem 16.6.6.** Let $o$ be an orientation of $f$. (i) For an admissible perturbation with the inherited orientation, $\int_P(\tau + d\eta) = \int_P\tau$ and the same for $\oint$, by the integrals on the polyfold, Step 3. (ii) For two such perturbations $P_0$, $P_1$ and closed $\tau$, the cobordism hypothesis gives $\tilde\Theta$, and the closed-forms identity gives $\int_{P_0}\tau = \int_{P_1}\tau$, and likewise for $\oint$. The well-definedness of the integral on the class (§XVI.19) uses no cobordism.

*Added hypotheses and parameters.* (a) Sc-smooth partitions of unity on $Z$, the hypothesis of Stokes' theorem (§XVI.20); not derived from the text. Witness: the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1 (§XVI.27). (b) The cobordisms between any two admissible perturbations with the inherited orientation: Corollary 15.4.4 on the polyfold, which is gap G.175 in part. *Witness* ⟦Chapter16/PerturbedIntegralIndependence · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_hyp_hcob_witness⟧: for the predicate $\mathrm{IsInherited}$ that singles out one perturbation $P$, the cobordism hypotheses hold through the self-cobordism of $P$. **This witness covers only a degenerate case**: with one perturbation there is nothing to compare, and no strong polyfold bundle with an admissible oriented perturbation of non-empty support is built. (c) "Inherited from $(f, o)$" is a parameter, any predicate on oriented perturbations; its definition needs the canonical orientation of Theorem 15.4.1 on the polyfold (gap G.159 of Part XV and gap G.175 in part). (d) "Generic" is read as general position in some model; its independence of the model is gap G.187. (e) The degree is the dimension $m + 1 \ge 1$ of $\lambda \circ f$; index $0$, where the integral is a weighted count of points, is gap G.188, the branched integrals of Chapter 9 being defined in dimension at least $1$.

*Where Lean departs from the text.* The text's proof of Theorem 16.6.6 refers to Chapter 15 in a representative: Theorem 15.3.7 for the choice of $\lambda$, Theorem 15.4.1 for the orientation of $\lambda \circ f$, and Corollary 15.4.4 for the independence of $\lambda$. The formalization does the first unconditionally, and isolates the second and third: the orientation as a parameter, the cobordism as a hypothesis. It also separates what does not need Chapter 15 at all: that the integrals are defined on the polyfold and depend only on $[\tau]$ follows from Stokes' theorem alone, because $\partial Z = \emptyset$. The text's statement is in cohomological degree $k$; the formalization is degree-wise in the dimension $m + 1$ of $\lambda \circ f$, which equals the Fredholm index, and does not cover index $0$.

### XVI.27 Witnesses and the hypotheses

**Hypotheses taken, by section.** Each is named, is not derived from the text unless said, and has a witness.

- *§XVI.2, §XVI.7.* The effective forms of the uniqueness after Definition 16.1.2, Remark 16.1.7 and Lemma 16.2.1 take an effective target. Witness: the point ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter16/TangentLemma · PolyfoldStructure.lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective_hypotheses⟧. Without it the statements do not hold as we read them; the orbit form of Lemma 16.2.1 needs no added hypothesis.
- *§XVI.4.* An effective middle polyfold for the composition of sc-smooth maps and for Definition 16.1.11. The text claims the composition in general; as we read it, it does not hold without effectiveness. Witness: the one-point polyfold ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldMaps · EffPolyfold.point⟧.
- *§XVI.9.* The functor on effective polyfolds takes only effectiveness; (ZHOU), which the effectiveness of the tangent needs, is part of every polyfold structure. The form on classes with an effective middle polyfold whose tangent is effective has that second hypothesis discharged by the theorem that tangents of effective polyfolds are effective, so it holds whenever the composite is defined.
- *§XVI.10.* The pull-back of forms by a composite of classes takes an effective middle polyfold, where the composite is defined; the pull-back by one sc-smooth map takes nothing.
- *§XVI.11.* The effective form of the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3 takes an effective target base; satisfiable, since trivial ep-groupoids are effective (Chapter 7).
- *§XVI.15.* Theorem 16.3.17 (2): the reflexive local step of Theorem 12.2.13. Witness ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp_witness⟧ on every bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres, **degenerate**: the boundary norm is the restriction of a global reflexive norm. The non-degenerate case is Part XII's proof of the local step over tame bases, which Theorem 16.3.17 assumes.
- *§XVI.20.* Sc-smooth partitions of unity, in Theorem 16.4.6 and in the independence of the boundary integrals (§XVI.19). Witness: the polyfold $\mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter16/BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness⟧.
- *§XVI.23.* Tame strong bundle charts in every model, and sc-smooth partitions of unity on the objects of every model. The partitions of unity are witnessed on the polyfold $\mathbb R$; the ep-groupoid hypotheses of the charged Theorem 14.1.9 hold non-degenerately, with boundary and non-zero fibres, on the half-space bundle of Part XIV; at the level of polyfolds, the charts and the non-empty index sets have no witness of their own. The remaining hypotheses (structurable $\lambda$ over $\partial Z$, $\tilde U$, $f$) are jointly satisfiable on every tame bundle with the zero multisection, $\tilde U = \emptyset$, $f = 0$, which is degenerate.
- *§XVI.25.* The standing hypotheses of the M-polyfold theory on the three bundles of the diagram, as in Theorem 12.5.7; Part XII's witnesses for Theorem 12.5.7 apply.
- *§XVI.26.* Sc-smooth partitions of unity on $Z$ (witness: the polyfold $\mathbb R$); the cobordisms (witness **degenerate**: one perturbation, self-cobordism); the predicate "inherited" (a parameter, not a hypothesis on data); the inherited tame germ data in the existence of $\lambda \circ f$.

No hypothesis of this Part quantifies over all charts of a bundle, and none is unsatisfiable: each has a witness above, degenerate where said.

**Readings, not hypotheses.** Bump functions on the object M-polyfold (decision (2)); the normalization $\hat T_\Theta = 0$ off $X_\infty$ (§XVI.19); $y \ne 0_z$ in Definition 16.5.2 (§XVI.21); $\gamma$ for $\Gamma$ in Remark 16.5.3; $\lambda : Y \to \mathbb Q^+$ in Definition 16.5.4; $n(f(z)) \le C$ read with $f(z) \in Y_{0,1}$ in Definition 16.6.3; $Y_{0,1}$ for the printed $Z_{0,1}$ in Theorem 16.6.6; "$n$ reflexive" read in one model in Theorem 16.3.17 (2); the boundary pull-back in orbit form in Definition 16.5.5.

**Every definition has a witness.**

*Polyfolds* (on the polyfold $\mathbb R$ given by $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, §XVI.1). Polyfold structure and polyfold; tame ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_isTame⟧; admits sc-smooth bump functions ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_admitsBumpFunctions⟧ and sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧; degeneracy index $\equiv 0$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_degIndex⟧ and empty boundary ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_boundary⟧. The same polyfold is the example of §XVI.2, so the hypotheses of Definition 16.1.1 are satisfiable there in a non-effective way. Its tangent and its raised polyfolds are witnesses of Definition 16.2.3 and of $(Z, c)^i$, $\tau_Z$.

*Maps.* The identity sc-smooth map on every polyfold; the category PS, with identities; effective polyfolds, the one-point polyfold. *Forms.* $\Omega^k_{sc}(Z, c)$ is a vector space isomorphic to $\Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X)$ for every structure in $c$ (§XVI.10).

*Strong polyfold bundles* (on the $\mathbb Z/3$ bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$, §XVI.11, with non-trivial isotropy). Structure and bundle; tame ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_isTame⟧; an invertible morphism of $\mathcal{SPBS}$ ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3_id_isInvertible⟧; reflexive $1$-fibres ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_hasReflexiveFibers⟧, since $\mathbb R^k$ is reflexive; an auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_exists_auxNorm⟧ and a reflexive one ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_exists_reflexiveAuxNorm⟧; auxiliary norms over the boundary, by restriction ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm.isAuxNormBoundary⟧, and the hypotheses of Theorem 16.3.17 (1) ⟦Chapter16/PolyfoldBundleExamples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_one_witness⟧. *Sections.* The zero section on every strong polyfold bundle (§XVI.16), an sc⁺-section. *Multisections.* The zero multisection, structurable; over $\partial Z$, the zero multisection of the witness of §XVI.23. *Sc-Fredholm sections and their orientations* are not separately witnessed at the polyfold level; Part XII's examples of sc-Fredholm section functors and orientations give them in any model.

*Branched suborbifolds.* A class exists as soon as a representative does; $\lambda \circ f$ gives one in every model (§XVI.26). No separate polyfold-level example of a compact tame oriented one is built; the hemisphere of Part IX is the nearest ep-level example.

### XVI.29 What the formalization taught us

**(ZHOU) does not give uniqueness of isomorphisms.** A polyfold structure in the 2021 sense adds two conditions to the 2017 definition, paracompactness of $|X|$ and (ZHOU), and the text derives from (ZHOU) that the generalized isomorphism realizing an equivalence of structures is unique. Formalized, (ZHOU) gives (LR), and (LR) is the hypothesis of Theorem 10.3.19. But Theorem 10.3.19 does not hold as we read it (Part X), and its example, $\mathbb Z/3$ acting trivially on $\mathbb R$, satisfies (ZHOU) and has a paracompact orbit space. It is therefore a polyfold structure, and the two generalized isomorphisms $[1_X]$ and $[X \xleftarrow{1} X \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} X]$ both realize the identity of $\mathbb R$. Five statements of the chapter do not hold as we read them for this reason: the uniqueness after Definition 16.1.2, Remark 16.1.7 with the sentence on pp. 709–710, Lemma 16.2.1, the claim of Definition 16.1.10 and the uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3. All five hold for an effective target or middle structure, where Theorem 10.3.19 holds. The isotropy that acts trivially is exactly what (ZHOU) allows and effectiveness forbids.

**Where the uniqueness bites, and where it does not.** None of the definitions of §§16.1 and 16.3 uses the uniqueness: an equivalence of structures only asks that some generalized isomorphism exist. The polyfold category is where it bites. Definition 16.1.6 lets the isomorphism $(k, \mathrm{Id}_W)$ of the middle structure be any generalized isomorphism over $\mathrm{Id}_W$; when the middle structure has isotropy acting trivially, two equivalent representatives of $\hat f$ composed with one representative of $\hat g$ give inequivalent composites. Presumably the text intends effective polyfolds, or morphisms with a chosen isomorphism; the formalization builds the category of effective polyfolds, while the category PS of polyfold structures, the sc-smooth maps of all polyfolds, their tangents and the pull-back of forms need no restriction, because they are defined map by map and Definition 16.1.6 carries its isomorphisms as data.

**Canonical on orbit spaces is enough for §16.2.** The text glues $T(Z, c)$ along "the unique" $\mathfrak f$ with $\beta \circ |\mathfrak f| = \alpha$, and Lemma 16.2.1 is there to make the gluing maps canonical. What the gluing uses is only $|T\mathfrak f|$, and that is unique: (LR) gives, for functors with the same orbit map, local families of morphisms between them (Proposition 10.1.10 (1)), and these give the same tangent orbit maps (Proposition 10.1.10 (2)). So $T(Z, c)$, $T\alpha$, (16.5), Lemma 16.2.2 and Definition 16.2.3 go through as printed, with one structure of $c$ as base point instead of the gluing over all. The same argument, Proposition 11.2.9, makes $h_*\omega$ independent of $h$, which is the remark before Definition 16.2.5. The raised polyfolds follow the same pattern, through the raise of generalized maps.

**The tangent of an effective polyfold needs (ZHOU) too.** The tangent functor lives on effective polyfolds, because the tangent of an effective polyfold is effective. The proof uses (ZHOU) as well as effectiveness: effectiveness is a statement at level $0$, while the open sets of $TX$ see only level $1$, so an isotropy element acting trivially near a tangent vector is first moved to a smooth point, where (ZHOU) turns the triviality of the linearized action into triviality near the point.

**Invariance statements are statements about equivalences.** The invariance statements of §16.1 are statements about equivalences of ep-groupoids, transported to classes. Bump functions are local; partitions of unity are best read on $|X|$; and the text's "easy exercise" in Proposition 16.1.4 (2) is the descent of sc-smoothness along an equivalence. The metrizability of a polyfold follows from Theorem 7.3.1 and the metrization theorem for locally metrizable paracompact Hausdorff spaces, without the Nagata–Smirnov theorem.

**§16.4 is Chapters 9 and 11 on classes, with two implicit points.** An orientation $\hat T_\Theta$ is read only on $X_\infty$, so a representative fixes it to be $0$ elsewhere, without which $1^*\hat T = \hat T$ fails. And Theorem 16.4.6 reduces to Theorem 9.5.17, which is stated for ep-groupoids with sc-smooth partitions of unity; the polyfold version needs the same hypothesis, which by Definition 16.1.5 holds for every representative as soon as it holds for one. The tameness of branched ep⁺-subgroupoids moves along equivalences through the transport charts of Theorem 11.4.1, so the integrals live on classes. Proposition 16.4.3 is the same transport once more: the two legs of a generalized isomorphism restrict to equivalences of the sub-ep-groupoids on the supports, and the transition between the induced structures is, near each point, a composite of local sc-diffeomorphisms. The structures of Proposition 9.1.9, which are existential, need not be chosen, since any two give the same comparison.

**Functions on $Y$ and $Z$ determine the class-level objects.** §§16.3, 16.5 and 16.6 survive the non-uniqueness because their relations are determined by functions. Two representatives of a section are related as soon as their maps $f$ agree: the condition $\mathfrak A_*F = F'$ follows from $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma$, since a functor is determined on orbits. Likewise the pull-back of a multisection functor along any generalized strong bundle isomorphism compatible with $\Gamma$ is $\lambda \circ \Gamma$, whichever isomorphism is chosen; on the $\mathbb Z/3$ example both isomorphisms are checked to pull back every functor alike. A branched suborbifold is determined by its function $\theta$, which makes $\lambda \circ f$ a well-defined branched suborbifold. Several conditions the text lists are consequences: the continuity and surjectivity of $p$, $p' \circ A = a \circ p$ for morphisms, the base condition of Definition 16.3.3.

**Small readings.** Read literally, the domain support of Definition 16.5.2 is all of $Z$, since the weights over each fibre sum to $1$, so that some $y$ over every $z$ has $\lambda(y) > 0$; with $y \ne 0_z$, as in Definition 13.2.2, it is the intended set. The continuity of $n(\lambda)$ in (16.8) is local: in a local section structure $N(\Lambda)$ is the maximum of the continuous functions $N \circ s_i$, and it descends to $Z$ through a quotient map.

**Reflexivity is a transport too.** Reflexivity of the $1$-fibres pulls back along a local strong bundle isomorphism by transporting a chart, whose fibre model does not change; the push direction needs the same for the action $\mu$ along a morphism, which Chapter 10 provides. Mixed convergence moves along a local strong bundle isomorphism because the isomorphism is linear and bounded on the fibres, so bounded sequences stay bounded and weak limits are preserved; the independence of the model for the reflexive notions is again a transport.

**§16.6 is a transport, and what remains is ep-level.** Once the definitions are on classes, every notion of §16.6 equals the ep-groupoid notion in every representative, and Theorem 16.6.4 is Theorem 12.4.2 there. Theorem 16.5.7 follows from Theorem 14.1.9 in one model, provided the multisections over $\partial X$ have non-empty index sets, which the text's notion has: a Lean form of Theorem 14.1.9 without that condition fails with boundary, and a polyfold theorem built on it would be vacuous exactly in the case it is about. For Theorem 16.6.6 the integrals live on the polyfold and depend only on the class of the form by Stokes alone; what the independence of $\lambda$ needs is the canonical orientation and a cobordism between two perturbations, both ep-level statements of Chapter 15. Orientations of sc-Fredholm sections follow the same pattern: Theorem 12.5.7 carries one along any diagram, and what is left is that two diagrams carry it alike, for which Part XII's independence of the representative is the tool.
